overview: The prospects for continuing life on Earth in the year 2058 are grim. So the Robinsons are launched into space to colonize Alpha Prime, the only other inhabitable planet in the galaxy. But when a stowaway sabotages the mission, the Robinsons find themselves hurtling through uncharted space.
tagline: Danger, Will Robinson!
title: Lost in Space
plot:
Lost in Space is a 1998 science fiction film directed by William Dear, based on the 1960s television series of the same name created by Irwin Allen.

The main themes of Lost in Space (1998) include:

1. Family and Survival: The story revolves around the Robinson family - John, Maureen, Judy, Will, and Penny - who are stranded on a hostile alien planet after their spaceship is damaged. The film explores their struggles to survive, work together, and maintain their family bonds in the face of adversity.

2. Exploration and Discovery: As the family navigates the unknown planet, they encounter various obstacles, creatures, and technologies that challenge their understanding of the universe. This theme highlights the importance of exploration, discovery, and pushing beyond the boundaries of human knowledge.

3. Human Nature and Morality: The film delves into the characters' moral dilemmas, as they confront difficult choices and grapple with their own values and principles. For example, Will's character is particularly torn between his loyalty to his family and his desire for independence.

4. Technology and Responsibility: The movie features advanced technologies that both aid and threaten the Robinsons. This theme serves as a commentary on the ethics of scientific progress and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

5. Adaptation and Resilience: Throughout their ordeal, the family must adapt to new situations, learn from their mistakes, and find ways to overcome seemingly insurmountable challenges. This theme emphasizes the importance of resilience, flexibility, and the ability to evolve in response to changing circumstances.

Overall, Lost in Space (1998) is a thought-provoking science fiction film that explores complex themes through the lens of a family's struggle for survival on an alien planet.

overview: Paul Baumer and his friends Albert and Muller, egged on by romantic dreams of heroism, voluntarily enlist in the German army. Full of excitement and patriotic fervour, the boys enthusiastically march into a war they believe in. But once on the Western Front, they discover the soul-destroying horror of World War I.
title: All Quiet on the Western Front
plot:
All Quiet on the Western Front (German: Im Westen nichts Neues) is a 2022 German epic anti-war film co-written, directed and co-produced by Edward Berger, based on Erich Maria Remarque's 1929 novel. It is the third screen adaptation of the book, after the 1930 and 1979 films, and the first in German. Felix Kammerer stars as Paul Bäumer, with Albrecht Schuch, Daniel Brühl, Sebastian Hülk, Aaron Hilmer, Edin Hasanović and Devid Striesow. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2022 and was released on Netflix in October.

In 1917, three years into the First World War, seventeen-year-old Paul Bäumer enthusiastically enlists in the Imperial German Army with his schoolmates Albert Kropp, Franz Müller and Ludwig Behm, inspired by a patriotic speech. Unaware, they are issued uniforms recycled from soldiers killed in earlier battles. Sent to the Western Front in northern France, they are befriended by Stanislaus "Kat" Katczinsky, an older, experienced soldier, but their romantic ideas about war are destroyed by the horrors of trench warfare, and Ludwig is killed on their first night.

Eighteen months later, in November 1918, the German politician Matthias Erzberger, appalled by the mounting death toll, urges the high command to seek an armistice with the Allies and leads the German delegation to negotiate with the French at Compiègne, where the terms offered are harsh. At the front, Paul, Kat and their comrades, including the veteran Tjaden, have become hardened survivors, finding brief moments of comradeship amid the slaughter, such as stealing a goose from a farm. As the armistice negotiations drag on, the soldiers are sent into ever more futile attacks, facing tanks, flamethrowers and gas. Even as the end of the war approaches, a German general determined to finish with a final victory orders one last offensive in the hours before the ceasefire is due to take effect at 11 a.m. on 11 November 1918.

The film received widespread acclaim for its direction, cinematography, score and depiction of the brutality of war. It won seven BAFTA Awards, including Best Film, and four Academy Awards, for Best International Feature Film, Best Cinematography, Best Original Score and Best Production Design, out of nine nominations.

overview: A former basketball all-star, who has lost his wife and family foundation in a struggle with addiction, attempts to regain his soul and salvation by becoming the coach of a disparate ethnically mixed high school basketball team at his alma mater.
tagline: Every loss is another fight.
title: The Way Back
plot:
The Way Back is a 2020 American sports drama film directed by Peter Berg and written by Matthew Spiegel. The movie stars Ben Affleck, Janina Gavankar, Charlie Hunnam, and Michaela McAdams.

The main themes of The Way Back revolve around the struggles of addiction, redemption, and personal growth. The story follows Jack Cunningham (played by Ben Affleck), a former high school basketball star who lost his way in life after a tragic accident involving his younger brother's death. He becomes an alcoholic and loses touch with his family.

The film takes us through Jack's journey as he returns to his alma mater, East Catholic High School, as the new basketball coach. Through his interactions with his players, particularly a troubled teenager named Brian (played by Charlie Hunnam), Jack begins to confront his past demons and work towards redemption.

Throughout the movie, we see themes of:

1. Redemption: Jack's journey is one of self-discovery and making amends for past mistakes.
2. Addiction: The film portrays the devastating effects of addiction on individuals and their loved ones.
3. Personal growth: As Jack works to rebuild his life and help his players, he learns valuable lessons about responsibility, accountability, and the importance of human connection.

The movie also explores the complexities of masculinity, particularly in the context of male relationships and the pressures placed on men to be strong and stoic.

Overall, The Way Back is a powerful and emotional drama that delves into the darker aspects of human nature while offering a message of hope and redemption.

original_title: Hasta que nos volvamos a encontrar
overview: The opposite lives of a workaholic architect and a fiery artist are upended when their chance encounter in breathtaking Peru shifts their views on life.
title: Without Saying Goodbye
plot:
Without Saying Goodbye (Spanish: Hasta que nos volvamos a encontrar, literally "Until We Meet Again") is a 2022 Peruvian-Spanish romantic comedy film written and directed by Bruno Ascenzo and produced by Tondero. It stars Stephanie Cayo and Maxi Iglesias. It was the first Peruvian film made for Netflix, which released it worldwide on 18 March 2022. The title refers to a line in which Cayo's character explains that Spanish "adiós" has no direct equivalent in Quechua.

Salvador Campodónico (Iglesias), a workaholic Spanish architect whose family owns Spain's leading hotel company, travels to Cusco to lead his first international project, a luxury hotel, although his father Alberto (Vicente Vergara) doubts he is ready for such a responsibility. He wanders into the lively hostel next door, run by Lichi (Wendy Ramos), and meets her niece Ariana (Cayo), a free-spirited, fiery artist who lives a life opposite to his. The morning after they spend the night together, Ariana learns that he intends to build the hotel on land that includes her aunt's hostel, and she is furious. To understand her world, Salvador persuades her to guide him through the region, and the trip through Inca sites and landscapes brings them closer. On the bus back, a violent storm triggers a panic attack in Ariana, and Lichi tells Salvador that Ariana was the sole survivor of a car accident that killed her parents when she was thirteen. Pressed by his father and his board to close the deal and persuade Lichi to sell, Salvador hesitates to commit, and Ariana leaves without telling anyone where she is going. Salvador sets out to find Ariana, tells her he has left the company to take a year off and that the project will not go ahead, and the two reunite.

Conceived by Ascenzo around 2013 as a travel film, the project was announced in February 2020 when Netflix's Reed Hastings visited Lima. Delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, it was shot from March to May 2021 under the working title Mochileros in Cusco, Puno and Paracas. It topped Netflix's charts in Peru and reached second place among the platform's most-watched non-English films in its first full week. Reviews were mixed: critics praised its landscapes and photography but found the script, characters and humour thin, with several likening it to a tourism advertisement and others criticising the lack of indigenous representation.

overview: XOXO follows six strangers whose lives collide in one frenetic, dream-chasing, hopelessly romantic night.
tagline: Eat. Sleep. Rave. Repeat.
title: XOXO
plot:
XOXO is a 2016 American music drama film directed by Christopher Louie, a music video director who wrote the story, from a screenplay by Dylan Meyer. Produced for Netflix by Prettybird, with Joe Russell, Louie, Daniel Shafer and Max Leitman as producers and the DJ Pete Tong as producer and music supervisor, it stars Graham Phillips, Sarah Hyland, Brett DelBuono, Hayley Kiyoko, Colin Woodell, Chris D'Elia, Ryan Hansen and Ione Skye, with Ian Anthony Dale, Brianne Howey and Henry Zaga.

The film follows six strangers whose lives intersect during a single night at XOXO, a huge fictional electronic dance music festival in the desert. Ethan Shaw (Phillips), a young bedroom DJ whose track "All I Ever Wanted" has exploded on YouTube, is offered a make-or-break slot at the festival by way of his best friend and manager Tariq (DelBuono), but he has only hours to get there. Things go wrong at once: a festivalgoer passes Tariq a hallucinogen with a kiss and he disappears into a wild trip, Ethan's name is missing from the lists, and a cynical star DJ, Avilo (Hansen), tries to lure him into a dubious collaboration. Krystal (Hyland), a romantic raver, hopes to meet Jordan (Zaga), a date she found online, but crosses paths with Ethan instead. Shanni (Kiyoko) and Ray (Woodell), a couple facing a long-distance future because she is moving to New York, try to sneak into the sold-out event through a sewer tunnel. Neil (D'Elia), a former DJ who now drives a party bus that breaks down on the highway, must confront Avilo, the man he blames for ruining his career, while the festival's founder Anders (Dale) wanders through offering advice. By the climactic set, each problem is resolved and Ethan finally gets his chance.

In 2015 Netflix announced the casting and that it would produce and distribute the film. To give the EDM setting authenticity, scenes were shot at three real music festivals. XOXO premiered on Netflix on 26 August 2016 after a one-week run at the Laemmle Royal in Los Angeles. Reviews were mixed, with a 71% Rotten Tomatoes approval rating from a small sample. The Hollywood Reporter found it so silly it was almost charming, praising Damián Acevedo's neon cinematography and the soundtrack, and Consequence of Sound called it sweet but lacking any real perspective on EDM culture, while The Village Voice wrote that, though predictable, it rewards viewers willing to give in to its rhythms.

overview: Four Navy SEALs on a covert mission to neutralize a high-level Taliban operative must make an impossible moral decision in the mountains of Afghanistan that leads them into an enemy ambush. As they confront unthinkable odds, the SEALs must find reserves of strength and resilience to fight to the finish.
tagline: Based on true acts of courage
title: Lone Survivor
plot:
Lone Survivor is a 2013 American war drama film directed by Peter Berg, based on the non-fiction book of the same name by Marcus Luttrell. The film stars Mark Wahlberg, Taylor Kitsch, Emile Hirsch, Ben Foster, and J.C. McManus.

The story begins with Lieutenant Michael "Hawk" Wilson (Mark Wahlberg), a U.S. Navy SEAL Team 10 member who is part of an elite counter-terrorism unit. Hawk is tasked with leading a four-man reconnaissance team to gather intelligence on a Taliban stronghold in the Hindu Kush mountains of Afghanistan. The team consists of Sergeant First Class Marcus Luttrell (Taylor Kitsch), Petty Officer Second Class Danny Dietz (Emile Hirsch), Petty Officer Third Class Matthew Axelson (Ben Foster), and Special Operator Second Class Scott "Seal" Helms (J.C. McManus).

The team is dropped into the mountains via helicopter, where they are tasked with infiltrating a Taliban compound to gather intel on enemy movements. The mission goes awry when the team is ambushed by a large group of Taliban fighters, and in the ensuing firefight, Axelson is killed.

As the remaining three SEALs attempt to escape, they become separated from each other, and Luttrell finds himself alone and wounded, with no way to communicate with his team. He uses his wits and knowledge of the terrain to evade the enemy and make his way back to friendly lines.

Meanwhile, Dietz and Helms are killed in action, and Wilson is left to fend for himself against overwhelming odds. Luttrell's survival is a testament to his bravery, resourcefulness, and determination, as he faces numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and enemy patrols.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Luttrell's actions during the mission have significant consequences for his team and their families. The film culminates with Luttrell's harrowing escape from the mountains, where he is rescued by a group of Afghan villagers who risk their own lives to help him.

Throughout the film, Berg explores themes of camaraderie, sacrifice, and the psychological toll of war on those who fight it. The performances by the cast are outstanding, particularly Wahlberg, Kitsch, and Hirsch, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

The film's climax is both intense and emotional, as Luttrell reflects on the events that transpired during his mission and grapples with the consequences of his actions. The final shot of the film shows Luttrell returning home to his family, forever changed by his experience in the mountains.

Overall, Lone Survivor is a powerful and moving film that honors the bravery and sacrifice of U.S. Navy SEALs who have served in Afghanistan.

overview: A family’s road trip takes a dangerous turn when they arrive at a secluded mobile home park to stay with some relatives and find it mysteriously deserted. Under the cover of darkness, three masked killers pay them a visit to test the family’s every limit as they struggle to survive.
tagline: Let us prey.
title: The Strangers: Prey at Night
plot:
The Strangers: Prey at Night is a 2018 American slasher film directed by Johannes Roberts and written by Bryan Marcus Smith. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2008 film The Strangers.

The main themes of The Strangers: Prey at Night revolve around family, isolation, and the breakdown of relationships under pressure. The story follows the Gardner family - Kinsey (Christina Hendricks), Mike (Martin Henderson), Luke (Lewis Pullman), and Cindy (Bailee Madison) - as they embark on a road trip to a mobile home park in West Virginia.

As the family navigates through the treacherous terrain, they become stranded due to a severe storm. The isolation of their situation heightens the tension, making them more vulnerable to the sinister presence lurking in the shadows. The film's antagonist, Dollface (Bailey De Young), is a mysterious and sadistic individual who targets the family, exploiting their deepest fears and weaknesses.

Throughout the movie, the themes of family dynamics and relationships are explored. The Gardners' interactions with each other reveal underlying tensions, conflicts, and insecurities, which ultimately contribute to their vulnerability to Dollface's attacks. The film also touches on the idea of isolation, as the family becomes disconnected from the outside world, leaving them at the mercy of their surroundings.

The Strangers: Prey at Night is a tense, suspenseful thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of pushing relationships to the breaking point. The movie's climax features a shocking twist, which adds to the overall sense of unease and dread that permeates the film.

overview: When a young African-American woman brings her fiancé home to meet her parents, she's neglected to mention one tiny detail - he's white.
tagline: His house. His rules. Some in-laws were made to be broken.
title: Guess Who
plot:
Guess Who is a comedy film that revolves around the story of a man who discovers his wife has been unfaithful and sets out to find her lover. The movie explores themes of infidelity, deception, and the complexities of human relationships.

As the protagonist navigates this difficult situation, he encounters a series of comedic misunderstandings and cultural clashes, highlighting the challenges of communication and empathy in relationships. The film also touches on the theme of identity, as the protagonist struggles to reconcile his own sense of self with the reality of his wife's infidelity.

Throughout the story, Guess Who delves into the complexities of human emotions, revealing a nuanced exploration of love, loss, and redemption.

overview: The sharks take bite out of the East Coast when the sharknado hits Washington, D.C. and Orlando, Florida.
title: Sharknado 3: Oh Hell No!
plot:
Sharknado 3: Oh Hell No! is a campy, over-the-top disaster film that satirizes various aspects of modern society. At its core, the movie explores the theme of chaos and the breakdown of social order in the face of catastrophic events.

The film's narrative is driven by the idea that a massive tornado filled with sharks has descended upon New York City, wreaking havoc on the population. As the city descends into anarchy, the characters must navigate this treacherous landscape to survive. The movie uses this absurd premise as a metaphor for the fragility of modern society and the ways in which it can be disrupted by external forces.

Throughout the film, the characters' reactions to the sharknado serve as a commentary on contemporary issues such as social media obsession, celebrity culture, and the 24-hour news cycle. The movie pokes fun at these aspects of modern life, using humor and satire to critique their excesses and superficiality.

Ultimately, Sharknado 3: Oh Hell No! is a tongue-in-cheek exploration of the human condition in the face of disaster. It asks questions about how we respond to crisis situations and whether our individual actions can make a difference in the face of overwhelming chaos. The film's lighthearted tone and absurd humor serve as a coping mechanism, allowing viewers to laugh at the absurdity of it all while also contemplating the deeper themes at play.

overview: A small town is taken over by an alien plague, turning residents into zombies and all forms of mutant monsters.
tagline: Horror has a new face.
title: Slither
plot:
Slither is a 2006 American horror-comedy film directed by James Gunn and written by Gunn and Phil Lord. The movie stars Nathan Fillion, Elizabeth Banks, Michael Rooker, and Jill Witcher.

The story begins with a small town called Middleton, where a group of friends, including Jeff (Nathan Fillion), a high school teacher, and his girlfriend Starla (Elizabeth Banks), are preparing for the annual Harvest Festival. The festival is a celebration of the town's agricultural heritage, but it also serves as an opportunity for the townspeople to let loose and have fun.

However, things take a dark turn when a mysterious alien parasite infects the town's residents, turning them into zombie-like creatures with a strong desire to eat human flesh. The parasite, which is about 10 feet long, has been introduced to Earth by a group of aliens who crash-landed in the nearby woods.

As the infection spreads rapidly throughout the town, Jeff and his friends must band together to survive and find a way to stop the parasite before it's too late. Along the way, they encounter a variety of bizarre and terrifying creatures, including giant spiders, mutated animals, and even a zombie-like version of Starla.

One of the most interesting aspects of Slither is its exploration of small-town America and the ways in which people can become complacent and accepting of their surroundings. The town of Middleton is portrayed as a place where everyone knows each other's business, but also where secrets and lies are often swept under the rug.

As the story progresses, Jeff and his friends discover that the parasite has a unique ability to manipulate its hosts' minds, making them more aggressive and violent. They also learn that the aliens who introduced the parasite were not just random visitors, but rather part of an experiment designed to create a new breed of super-soldiers.

In the end, Jeff and his friends must use their wits and whatever resources they can find to stop the parasite and save the town. Along the way, they encounter some unexpected allies, including a group of survivors from a nearby town who have been fighting against the parasites for weeks.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between Jeff and the leader of the zombie-like creatures, a giant spider-like creature that has become the parasite's host. In the end, Jeff emerges victorious, but not before realizing that the parasite has left him with a strange and unsettling connection to the alien entity.

Overall, Slither is a fun and entertaining horror-comedy that explores themes of small-town America, paranoia, and the dangers of complacency. With its unique blend of humor, action, and horror elements, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: A detective suffering from a personal loss receives a call from his recently deceased niece. Being able to communicate across time, the two work together to try and stop the crime before it occurs.
tagline: Change the past. Save her future.
title: Don't Let Go
plot:
Don't Let Go is a psychological thriller that delves into the complexities of grief, trauma, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The film follows a young woman named Stewart's mother who dies in a car accident, leaving her to grapple with the loss and find solace in an alternate universe where she never died.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that this alternate universe is not just a product of Stewart's imagination but a tangible reality that exists alongside her own. This dichotomy serves as a metaphor for the human experience, highlighting the ways in which our perceptions of reality can be shaped by our emotions and experiences.

The film explores the theme of grief and its various forms, from the initial shock and denial to the eventual acceptance and healing. However, it also delves into the darker aspects of grief, such as the obsessive nature of loss and the ways in which it can consume us.

Furthermore, Don't Let Go touches on the idea of identity and how our experiences shape who we are. Stewart's journey is a metaphor for the search for self-discovery and the struggle to come to terms with one's own identity in the face of trauma and loss.

Ultimately, the film presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that acknowledges the complexity and messiness of life while also offering a message of hope and resilience.

overview: After graduating from Emory University in 1992, top student and athlete Christopher McCandless abandons his possessions, gives his entire $24,000 savings account to charity, and hitchhikes to Alaska to live in the wilderness.
tagline: Into the heart. Into the soul.
title: Into the Wild
plot:
Into the Wild is a biographical drama film directed by Sean Penn, released in 2007. The movie is based on the life of Christopher McCandless, an American young man who abandoned his material possessions and hitchhiked to Alaska with the intention of living off the land.

The film begins with Chris McCandless (played by Emile Hirsch), a recent college graduate from a wealthy family in Carthage, Missouri. Chris's parents, Walt (Vince Vaughn) and Billie (Catherine Keener), are portrayed as loving but also somewhat neglectful, having given their son the freedom to explore his own path in life.

Chris becomes increasingly disillusioned with the materialism and superficiality of modern society, feeling suffocated by the expectations placed upon him. He decides to leave behind his comfortable life and embark on a journey of self-discovery, inspired by the writings of Henry David Thoreau's Walden.

The film follows Chris as he travels across the country, hitchhiking and working odd jobs to save money for his trip to Alaska. Along the way, he meets various characters who influence his worldview, including Wayne Westerberg (Hal Holbrook), a grizzled old truck driver who teaches him about the importance of living in the moment.

In 1992, Chris arrives in Anchorage, Alaska, and begins his journey into the wilderness. He adopts the alias "Alexander Supertramp" and sets out to live off the land, foraging for food and building a shelter. The film depicts Chris's struggles with the harsh environment, including encounters with bears, mosquitoes, and extreme weather conditions.

As the seasons change, Chris becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, struggling to adapt to the unforgiving wilderness. He begins to question his decision to leave behind civilization, feeling overwhelmed by the vastness of nature.

The film takes a tragic turn when Chris's bus breaks down on the side of the road, and he is forced to abandon his vehicle. In an attempt to survive, Chris sets fire to his bus, but the flames spread out of control, consuming everything in their path.

In the end, Chris's body is discovered by two hunters, who report him missing to the authorities. The film ends with a sense of melancholy and regret, as Chris's parents receive news of his death, realizing too late that they had failed to connect with their son on a deeper level.

Throughout the film, Sean Penn's direction weaves together themes of identity, community, and the human relationship with nature. Emile Hirsch delivers a powerful performance as Chris McCandless, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of this enigmatic young man. The cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the stunning beauty of Alaska's wilderness.

Overall, Into the Wild is a thought-provoking film that raises questions about the human condition and our place in the world. It is a poignant reminder of the importance of connection, community, and living life on one's own terms.

overview: A strange family: 17-year-old Phil lives with his mother and twin sister in an old mansion on the outskirts of town. When he returns from summer camp, the mood in the mansion has soured somehow. Phil doesn’t worry about it, hanging out with his best friend Kat instead. When he starts to feel attracted to a mysterious new student at school, Phil is plunged into emotional turmoil only exacerbated by the trouble at home.
title: Center of My World
plot:
Center of My World is a 2016 German science fiction film directed by Jakob Lass. The movie tells the story of a young boy named Anderz, who lives in a remote village on the edge of a vast desert with his father. When Anderz's mother passes away, he embarks on an extraordinary journey to find her spirit and ultimately discovers a magical portal that transports him to another world.

The main theme of Center of My World revolves around the idea of identity and self-discovery. As Anderz navigates this new world, he encounters various characters who challenge his perceptions of himself and the world around him. Through his experiences, Anderz learns to let go of his past and find a sense of belonging in this new reality.

The film also explores the concept of isolation and loneliness. Anderz's journey is marked by his separation from his father and his struggle to connect with others in this new world. However, as he forms connections with the people he meets, he begins to realize that even in solitude, there is always the possibility for human connection and understanding.

Furthermore, Center of My World touches on the idea of growing up and coming of age. Anderz's experiences serve as a metaphor for the challenges and uncertainties of adolescence, where one must navigate the complexities of relationships, identity, and belonging.

Overall, the movie presents a poignant and thought-provoking exploration of the human experience, delving into themes that are both universally relatable and deeply personal.

original_title: ひるね姫 ～知らないワタシの物語～
overview: Japan, 2020, a few days before the opening of the Tokyo Olympics. Although she should be studying for her final exams, Kokone, a schoolgirl who lives in a small town with her widowed father, a mysterious and talented mechanic, falls asleep often, anywhere, anytime, entering, over and over, a dream-world where a squad of fantastic motorized contraptions fights against magic, a world close to reality where she will find out the keys of her true past.
tagline: There's a reason why I can see in dreams
title: Napping Princess
plot:
Napping Princess is a thought-provoking anime film that delves into the complexities of identity, power, and the human condition. The movie follows the story of Makoto Kinuka, a young woman who discovers she has the ability to control time after being exposed to a mysterious substance.

At its core, Napping Princess explores the theme of self-discovery and empowerment. Makoto's journey is one of self-acceptance and embracing her unique abilities, which sets her apart from others. As she navigates this new reality, she must confront the societal expectations placed upon her and find her own path in life.

The film also touches on the idea of power dynamics and the consequences of playing with time. Makoto's actions have far-reaching effects on those around her, highlighting the importance of responsibility and accountability. The movie raises questions about the nature of free will and the impact of one person's decisions on others.

Furthermore, Napping Princess is a poignant exploration of loneliness and human connection. Makoto's struggles to form meaningful relationships with others serve as a reminder that even in our most powerful moments, we are still vulnerable and in need of human interaction.

Overall, Napping Princess is a rich and nuanced film that invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences with identity, power, and the complexities of human connection.

overview: The film that brings back horror icon Freddy Krueger as a darker and more sinister character than ever before. While Freddy is on the prowl, a group of teenagers being stalked soon learn they all have a common factor making them targets for this twisted killer.
tagline: Never sleep again.
title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
plot:
A Nightmare on Elm Street is a 2010 American slasher film directed by Samuel Bayer, in his feature debut, and written by Wesley Strick and Eric Heisserer. A remake of Wes Craven's 1984 film and the ninth entry in the franchise, it was produced by Michael Bay's Platinum Dunes and stars Jackie Earle Haley as Freddy Krueger, with Rooney Mara, Kyle Gallner, Katie Cassidy, Thomas Dekker, Kellan Lutz, Clancy Brown and Connie Britton. It opened on April 30, 2010.

In the town of Springwood, Ohio, teenager Dean Russell dozes off in a diner and, in a nightmare, is attacked by a horribly burned man with a bladed glove; in reality, he slits his own throat in front of his friends Kris Fowles and Nancy Holbrook, a waitress there. At his funeral Kris notices a childhood photo of herself with Dean, although she cannot remember knowing him before high school. Plagued by dreams of the burned man, she tries to stay awake, but falls asleep while her ex-boyfriend Jesse Braun is with her and is killed. Jesse is arrested and dies in his cell.

Nancy, who has also been dreaming of the man, Freddy Krueger, realises that none of the friends can remember their early childhoods. With her friend Quentin Smith she discovers that they all attended the same preschool. Nancy's mother Gwen admits that Krueger was the school's gardener and was accused of abusing the children, Nancy most of all, and that the parents chased him away. Nancy learns that all the other children from the school have died. Quentin, in a dream, sees what really happened: the parents, led by his father Alan, cornered Krueger and burned him alive.

Exhausted by lack of sleep, Nancy and Quentin suffer microsleeps and hallucinations. When Nancy manages to pull a piece of Krueger's sweater out of a dream, they realise they might drag him into the real world. Armed with adrenaline stolen from a hospital, they visit the abandoned preschool and find evidence of Krueger's crimes. Nancy deliberately falls asleep, and Quentin wakes her with the adrenaline just as Krueger attacks, pulling him into reality, where she cuts his throat and sets the room ablaze. Back home, however, Krueger reappears and kills Gwen through a mirror.

The film earned about 117 million dollars worldwide but was poorly reviewed, with a 14% Rotten Tomatoes rating, critics finding it visually faithful but lacking the original's wit and scares.

overview: At the beginning of chaos, the first demon in the world was born, named Yuandi, and it was worshipped as the ancestor of demons. Thousands of years later, the former demon king Sun Wukong is rescued from the Five Elements Mountain by Monk Tang, who promises to protect him and go to the West to get the scriptures.
tagline: The final showdown.
title: The Monkey King: Reborn
plot:
The Monkey King: Reborn (Chinese: Xiyouji zhi Zaishi Yaowang) is a 2021 Chinese computer-animated fantasy action film directed by Wang Yunfei, previously known for the Yugo and Lala series. Loosely based on Wu Cheng'en's sixteenth-century novel Journey to the West, it features the voices of Bian Jiang as Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, Su Shangqing as Master Tang Sanzang, Zhang He as Zhu Bajie, Lin Qiang as Sha Wujing, Zhang Lei as the ancient demon Yuandi and Cai Haiting as the manfruit spirit Fruity.

At the dawn of chaos, the first demon in the world, Yuandi, was born and came to be worshipped as the ancestor of all demons, once ruling the three realms before being imprisoned. Thousands of years later, the former demon king Sun Wukong, freed from beneath the Five Elements Mountain by the monk Tang Sanzang, travels west with his master and fellow disciples Zhu Bajie and Sha Wujing in search of scriptures. When the group stops to rest at a temple, the ever-hungry Bajie talks Wukong into hunting for a legendary food treasure, and the two roughly plunder a sacred tree. Unknown to them, the tree marks the top of Yuandi's prison, and their recklessness sets the demon free. Escaping, Yuandi takes Master Tang captive. Wukong, Bajie and Wujing set out to rescue their master and defeat the demon for good, accompanied by Fruity, the embodiment of the qi energy that had sealed Yuandi away. Along the way Wukong dispatches a series of foes with strength and cunning, but must find within himself the power to face the truly formidable Yuandi, while Master Tang's Buddhist teaching of equality is set against the demon's desire to dominate others.

The film was released in Chinese theaters on 2 April 2021. Well Go USA, which had previously handled the animated films Ne Zha and Jiang Ziya, distributed it in North America, releasing it on Blu-ray, DVD and digital platforms on 7 December 2021 with an English-language audio track. Reviews praised its spectacle but criticized its writing. Douglas Davidson of Elements of Madness gave it three out of five, calling the inventive action sequences great fun and never dull while describing the script as flimsy, the characters undeveloped and the tone wildly uneven, mixing crude humor aimed at younger viewers with violence suited to teenagers and older audiences, and comparing many of the CG fights to extended video game cutscenes.

original_title: Nanny McPhee and the Big Bang
overview: Nanny McPhee appears at the door of a harried young mother who is trying to run the family farm while her husband is away at war. But once she’s arrived, Nanny discovers that the children are fighting a war of their own against two spoiled city cousins who have just moved in. Relying on everything from a flying motorcycle and a statue that comes to life to a tree-climbing piglet and a baby elephant, Nanny uses her magic to teach her mischievous charges five new lessons.
title: Nanny McPhee and the Big Bang
plot:
Nanny McPhee and the Big Bang, released in North America as Nanny McPhee Returns, is a 2010 British period fantasy comedy directed by Susanna White and written by Emma Thompson, based on Christianna Brand's Nurse Matilda books. A sequel to Nanny McPhee (2005), it stars Thompson in the title role, with Maggie Gyllenhaal, Ralph Fiennes, Rhys Ifans, Ewan McGregor, Asa Butterfield and Maggie Smith.

During the Second World War, Isabel Green is struggling to run the family farm and work in the village shop of the scatterbrained Mrs. Docherty while her husband, Rory, is away fighting. Her three unruly children, Norman, Megsie and Vincent, are joined by their spoiled, snobbish cousins from London, Cyril and Celia, who have been sent to the country for safety, and the children's fighting soon drives Isabel to despair. The magical Nanny McPhee arrives and, with her unusual methods, teaches the children to stop fighting and to share, and gradually the cousins learn to work together.

Meanwhile Rory's brother Phil, who has gambled away his half of the farm and is pursued by two hired assassins sent by the casino owner Mrs. Biggles, schemes to make Isabel sell her share. His plots, including releasing the piglets she plans to sell, are foiled by the children. Then Phil delivers a telegram announcing that Rory has been killed in action. Only Norman refuses to believe it, and Nanny McPhee takes him and Cyril to the War Office in London, where Cyril's cold, distant father, Lord Gray, holds a senior post. Confronted by his son about his neglect and his impending divorce, Lord Gray discovers that Rory is only missing and that no telegram was ever sent; Phil had forged it.

At home, the other children try to delay Isabel's signing of Phil's papers, until a German plane accidentally drops a huge bomb into the barley field. It fails to explode, but the impact spills ink across the contract. When Mr. Docherty faints while trying to defuse the bomb, Megsie completes the task with the others' help. Nanny McPhee helps harvest the barley with a touch of magic, and Mrs. Docherty is revealed to be the baby Agatha from the first film. As Nanny McPhee departs, Rory returns, wounded but alive.

The film opened at number one in the United Kingdom and grossed about $93 million worldwide against a $35 million budget. It received generally positive reviews, with some critics finding it an improvement on the first film, and Metacritic gave it 52 out of 100.

overview: Cindy finds out the house she lives in is haunted by a little boy and goes on a quest to find out who killed him and why. Also, Alien "Tr-iPods" are invading the world and she has to uncover the secret in order to stop them.
tagline: Bury the grudge. Burn the village.  See the saw.
title: Scary Movie 4
plot:
Scary Movie 4 is a 2006 American parody film directed by David Zucker from a screenplay by Craig Mazin, Jim Abrahams and Pat Proft. The fourth Scary Movie film, it brings back Anna Faris, Regina Hall, Anthony Anderson, Kevin Hart and Leslie Nielsen, with Craig Bierko, Bill Pullman, Cloris Leachman, Michael Madsen, Molly Shannon, Shaquille O'Neal and Dr. Phil McGraw. Its main targets are War of the Worlds, The Grudge, Saw, The Village and Million Dollar Baby, and it opened in April 2006.

In a parody of Saw, Shaquille O'Neal and Dr. Phil wake chained up in a bathroom filling with nerve gas, and fail the puppet Billy's test in absurd fashion. Meanwhile, the recently widowed Cindy Campbell, whose husband George died in a boxing match and whose nephew has gone to military school, takes a job caring for the elderly Mrs. Norris in a house haunted by the ghost of a pale Japanese boy. Next door lives Tom Ryan, a divorced father who has his children Robbie and Rachel for the weekend, and who learns of an awkward secret between George's friends Mahalik and CJ.

Cindy and Tom fall for each other, but their romance is cut short when an enormous alien tripod knocks out the power and starts vaporising residents. Through a garbled exchange in mock Japanese, the ghost tells Cindy that the key to stopping the invasion lies in his father's heart. Tom flees with his children, while Cindy, reunited with her friend Brenda, who has unaccountably survived her earlier death, goes to an isolated village ruled by Henry Hale, where the two are put on trial and forbidden to leave.

At the United Nations, the bumbling President Baxter Harris causes chaos with tasteless jokes and an alien device that strips everyone naked. Tom and his children are caught in a battle between the army and the aliens; Robbie runs off, and Tom and Rachel are seized by a tripod. In the village, the madman Ezekiel kills Henry, and the plot reveals the ghost boy's tangled parentage.

Cindy and Brenda are captured and brought to the bathroom from the prologue, where Cindy survives the puppet's game and works out that the alien leader is the boy's real father. Moved by Tom's devotion to his children, the puppet apologises and calls off the invasion. In an epilogue, Tom wildly declares his love for Cindy on The Oprah Winfrey Show. The film opened to about 40 million dollars and grossed some 178 million worldwide, though reviews were poor, with 34% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: After a talent scout spots her performing with her dog Boi at a charity gala, Sharpay Evans sets off for the bright lights of NYC, convinced instant fame and fortune are in the bag. But theatre's a dog-eat-dog world. Fortunately, Sharpay also meets Peyton, a handsome student filmmaker who finds Sharpay nearly as fascinating as she finds herself.
title: Sharpay's Fabulous Adventure
plot:
Sharpay's Fabulous Adventure is a 2011 musical comedy film directed by Michael Lembeck and written by Brian D. Wright and Chris Columbus.

The movie follows the story of Sharpay Evans, played by Ashley Tisdale, who dreams of becoming a Broadway star. The main themes of the film include:

1. **Perseverance and determination**: Sharpay faces numerous setbacks and rejections, but she never gives up on her dream. She works hard to achieve her goal, and her persistence ultimately pays off.
2. **Self-discovery and empowerment**: Throughout the movie, Sharpay learns to stand up for herself and assert her individuality. She discovers that being true to oneself is essential to happiness and success.
3. **Friendship and loyalty**: Sharpay's relationships with her friends, including Ryan Evans (Lucas Grabeel) and Taylor McKessie (Vanessa Hudgens), are central to the story. The film highlights the importance of supporting one another and being there for each other through thick and thin.
4. **Overcoming fear and taking risks**: Sharpay is initially hesitant to take risks and pursue her dreams, but she eventually learns to face her fears and push beyond her comfort zone.

The movie features a mix of music, dance, and comedy, making it an entertaining and lighthearted watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: A former special forces agent is trapped in a time loop and relives his death over and over again. To escape the terrible situation, he must track down those responsible and stop them.
tagline: Running out of time. And lives.
title: Boss Level
plot:
Boss Level is a 2021 American science fiction action film directed by Joe Carrott and written by Joe Carrott and Eric Heisserer. The movie stars Frank Grillo, Mel Gibson, and Naomi Watts.

The story follows Captain James "Jim" Goddard (Frank Grillo), a retired Army Ranger who has been living a quiet life with his wife, Sarah (Melissa O'Neill). However, their peaceful existence is disrupted when Jim's estranged daughter, Emily (Naomi Watts), arrives at their doorstep. She informs Jim that he has been chosen to participate in a top-secret government program called "Boss Level," which aims to test the limits of human endurance.

The program involves sending Jim back in time to relive the same day over and over again, with each iteration becoming increasingly difficult and deadly. The goal is for Jim to complete a series of missions that will ultimately lead to the defeat of an evil organization known as "The Syndicate." As Jim navigates through the time loop, he must confront his own personal demons and team up with a mysterious ally named Maya (Mel Gibson), who claims to be a former member of The Syndicate.

As the story progresses, Jim begins to uncover the truth behind The Syndicate's sinister plans. He also starts to experience strange visions and flashbacks that hint at a deeper connection between his past and present selves. Through each iteration, Jim becomes more skilled and resourceful, but he also faces new challenges and obstacles that test his physical and mental limits.

Throughout the movie, the action sequences become increasingly intense and elaborate, with Jim facing off against hordes of enemy soldiers and navigating treacherous terrain. The film's climax features an epic showdown between Jim and the leader of The Syndicate, which culminates in a thrilling finale that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

Ultimately, Jim emerges victorious, but not without scars. As he returns to his own time, he is left to ponder the consequences of his actions and the true nature of the Boss Level program. The movie ends with Jim reflecting on his experiences and the sacrifices he made to complete his missions, leaving the audience to wonder what other challenges lie ahead for this brave and resourceful hero.

Overall, Boss Level is a gripping sci-fi action film that explores themes of time travel, redemption, and personal growth. With its breakneck pacing, stunning visuals, and memorable performances, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: Shy 14-year-old Duncan goes on summer vacation with his mother, her overbearing boyfriend, and her boyfriend's daughter. Having a rough time fitting in, Duncan finds an unexpected friend in Owen, manager of the Water Wizz water park.
tagline: We've all been there.
title: The Way Way Back
plot:
The Way Way Back is a poignant coming-of-age drama that explores the complexities of family dynamics, identity, and self-discovery. At its core, the film delves into the theme of finding one's place within the world, particularly for outsiders who struggle to fit in.

The movie follows Duncan, a shy and introverted teenager who embarks on a summer vacation with his family to a beach town. There, he meets Owen, a charismatic and confident water park employee who becomes a mentor and confidant to Duncan. Through their unlikely friendship, Duncan begins to confront the difficulties of his home life, including his distant father's emotional unavailability and his mother's overbearing presence.

As Duncan navigates this new relationship with Owen, he is forced to confront his own insecurities and vulnerabilities. The film masterfully captures the turmoil of adolescence, where self-doubt and uncertainty are omnipresent. However, it also suggests that these feelings can be a catalyst for growth and transformation.

One of the primary themes of The Way Way Back is the power of human connection in overcoming adversity. Duncan's friendship with Owen serves as a beacon of hope and acceptance, allowing him to feel seen and understood for the first time. This theme is beautifully intertwined with the idea that family is not just about blood ties but also about the relationships we cultivate and nurture.

The film also explores the tension between authenticity and conformity, highlighting the difficulties of navigating societal expectations while staying true to oneself. Duncan's journey is a powerful metaphor for the struggle to find one's authentic voice in a world that often values superficiality over sincerity.

Ultimately, The Way Way Back is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that celebrates the resilience of the human spirit and the transformative power of meaningful relationships.

overview: Someone in a prison run by a corrupt warden fakes the deaths of convicts to later use them as expendable assassins. A police officer is sent into the prison to gather evidence of the corruption.
tagline: When you're looking for the living dead you start your search in hell!
title: Island of Fire
plot:
Island of Fire is a 1990 Hong Kong action film directed by Sammo Hung. The movie follows the story of a young martial artist, Ching, who seeks revenge against the ruthless crime lord, Wong Fei-hung's (Sammo Hung) rival, Siu Lung.

The main theme of Island of Fire revolves around the struggle for power and loyalty in a world where honor and family are paramount. The film explores the complexities of loyalty, as Ching is torn between his duty to protect his mentor, Wong Fei-hung, and his desire for revenge against Siu Lung, who has wronged him.

The movie also delves into the theme of redemption, as Ching's quest for revenge becomes an opportunity for him to prove himself and earn the respect of those around him. Through Ching's journey, the film highlights the importance of self-discovery and the need to find one's own path in life.

Furthermore, Island of Fire touches on the theme of loyalty and betrayal, as Siu Lung's actions are motivated by a desire for power and control, leading him to betray those who have trusted him. The film ultimately suggests that true strength lies not in physical prowess, but in one's ability to form meaningful connections with others and to stand up for what is right.

Overall, Island of Fire is a classic martial arts film that explores themes of loyalty, redemption, and the struggle for power in a world where honor and family are deeply ingrained.

overview: It's been ten years since the creation of the Great Truce, an elaborate joint-species surveillance system designed and monitored by cats and dogs to keep the peace when conflicts arise. But when a tech-savvy villain hacks into wireless networks to use frequencies only heard by cats and dogs, he manipulates them into conflict and the worldwide battle between cats and dogs is BACK ON. Now, a team of inexperienced and untested agents will have to use their old-school animal instincts to restore order and peace between cats and dogs everywhere.
title: Cats & Dogs 3: Paws Unite
plot:
Cats & Dogs 3: Paws Unite! is a 2020 American spy comedy directed by Sean McNamara, the third and final installment of the Cats & Dogs series and a stand-alone sequel to Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore (2010). Melissa Rauch, Max Greenfield and George Lopez lead the voice cast. Unlike the first two films, it was released straight to video in the United States, on September 15, 2020.

A decade after the Great Truce ended the war between cats and dogs, Roger, a Border Collie, and Gwen, a cat, are partners in F.A.R.T. (Furry Animals Rivalry Termination), a secret organization that keeps the peace without humans ever knowing. Roger, who gave up field work after his mentor was injured, has been stuck at a desk. The two live in the same apartment building in suburban Seattle with their owners: Max, a middle school tennis player pressured by his mother to win a state championship, and Zoe, whose struggling musician father, Ollie, faces eviction.

When the agents' communications go down and local cats and dogs suddenly begin fighting again, Roger and Gwen investigate. With tips from park dogs and alley cats, they learn that someone has stolen wireless access codes in order to broadcast frequencies audible only to cats and dogs, turning them against each other so that humans will stop adopting them and choose reptiles and birds instead. The mastermind is Pablo, a cockatoo at a pet store, and his reptile accomplices. Along the way the partners also try to bring their lonely owners together, trapping Max and Zoe in a stalled elevator, where the two open up about their pressures, share a kiss and become friends.

At the pet store, Roger, Gwen and their ally Duke are captured, and the frequency is activated as Max and Zoe arrive, but the agents break free and fight off Pablo's snakes and tarantula. Pablo, softened by the affection of a boy who visits the store, turns against his lizard henchman and shuts down the signal. Roger's missing mentor, Old Ed, admits he let himself be captured so that Roger would regain his confidence in the field. Zoe's father sells his song and saves their home, and Max wins his championship.

Critics were largely negative, faulting the cheap-looking effects, clichéd story and lack of wit. Common Sense Media praised some of the humor, particularly from George Lopez.

overview: Everyone has 'moved on', except for Sherman and Jim Levenstein's still understanding father. Little Matt Stiffler wants to join his older brother Steve's business and, after everything Matt has heard from Jim's band-geek wife, he plans to go back to band camp and make a video of his own.
tagline: This One Time at Band Camp...
title: American Pie Presents: Band Camp
plot:
American Pie Presents: Band Camp is a 2005 American comedy film directed by Steve Rash and written by Adam Herz. The movie is part of the American Pie franchise, which follows the misadventures of a group of high school friends.

The plot revolves around Stifler (Erik Stolhanske), Jim Levenstein's (Jason Biggs) cousin, who is sent to band camp as punishment for his behavior. Stifler is forced to attend Camp Firewood, a summer camp where he meets a new cast of characters, including the beautiful and popular camper, Jessica (Amanda Crew).

As Stifler navigates the challenges of band camp, he must also contend with the camp's strict rules and regulations, as well as his own personal demons. Along the way, he befriends a group of misfits, including a gay counselor named Steve (Erik Stolhanske) and a camper who is obsessed with the band.

Meanwhile, back at home, Jim Levenstein is dealing with his own problems, including a new girlfriend and a rival suitor for her affections. As the summer wears on, Stifler's antics cause chaos at camp, while Jim struggles to balance his relationships and his desire to fit in.

Throughout the movie, there are several subplots that add to the humor and chaos of the story. One of these involves a group of campers who try to start a rock band, with disastrous results. Another subplot involves Stifler's attempts to win over Jessica, which lead to a series of awkward and humorous encounters.

Ultimately, the movie builds towards a climactic finale that brings together all of the plot threads in a hilarious and unexpected way. In the end, Stifler emerges as the hero of the story, having learned valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and the importance of following your dreams.

Overall, American Pie Presents: Band Camp is a lighthearted and entertaining comedy that is sure to appeal to fans of the American Pie franchise. With its witty dialogue, physical humor, and memorable characters, it's a great addition to the series.

overview: Two friends hired to police a small town that is suffering under the rule of a rancher find their job complicated by the arrival of a young widow.
tagline: Feelings get you killed.
title: Appaloosa
plot:
Appaloosa is a 2008 American Western film directed by Ed Harris, starring Viggo Mortensen, Ed Harris, and Renée Zellweger.

The movie explores the complex and often brutal world of the Old West through the story of Virgil Earp (Viggo Mortensen), a former Confederate soldier turned lawman. The narrative delves into themes of loyalty, honor, and the moral ambiguity that defines the characters' existence in this unforgiving environment.

At its core, Appaloosa is a tale of two men bound together by their shared experiences as outlaws-turned-lawmen, struggling to maintain their sense of identity and purpose in a world where the lines between right and wrong are constantly blurred. The film's protagonist, Virgil Earp, grapples with his own demons, torn between his duty to uphold justice and his loyalty to those he cares about.

The movie also touches on the theme of power dynamics, as embodied by the enigmatic and ruthless Randall Bragg (Ed Harris), a ruthless outlaw who will stop at nothing to claim control over the territory. The character's presence serves as a catalyst for the conflict that drives the plot forward, highlighting the destructive nature of unchecked ambition and the devastating consequences of violence.

Ultimately, Appaloosa is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, set against the backdrop of the American West during its tumultuous late 19th century. The film's nuanced portrayal of complex characters and moral dilemmas invites viewers to reflect on the nature of honor, loyalty, and redemption in a world where these values are constantly tested.

overview: As the Kalahari Desert faces a worsening dry season, prides, packs and herds of all kinds must rely on the power of family to survive.
title: Surviving Paradise: A Family Tale
plot:
Surviving Paradise: A Family Tale is a 2022 British nature documentary film made for Netflix. Directed by Renée Godfrey with Matt Meech and produced by Wild Space Productions with Freeborne Media, it is narrated by the actor Regé-Jean Page. Following a year in the life of the animals of Botswana's Okavango Delta, an oasis in the Kalahari Desert, it explores how the bonds within prides, packs and herds allow their members to survive a worsening dry season. The film was released on Netflix on 3 March 2022 and runs 78 minutes.

The documentary follows three main families. A lioness and her sisters are threatened when two young males challenge their ageing king; the usurpers destroy the harmony of the pride and cast her out, and, alone, she must hunt for herself and, after being made pregnant by a passing male, raise her cubs on her own. The alpha female of a pack of 24 painted wolves has trained her hunters to think and act as one, and the pack returns meat to its den to feed a litter of 14 pups. A six-month-old elephant calf experiences every challenge of Kalahari life for the first time within her herd, guided by a matriarch who remembers vital water sources. As drought grips the region, these animals and great numbers of wildebeest, giraffes, zebras, hippos and buffalo converge on the delta. When floodwaters from rain that fell months earlier in the Angolan Highlands finally arrive, the landscape becomes a lush wetland, a boon for grazers but a hardship for the hunters, as the water-adapted lechwe easily escape the wolves. By September the water is receding, and by October the delta is a scorching dust bowl where the balance of power shifts back to the predators, lightning ignites fires and swarms of locusts emerge, until the elephants, able to detect distant thunder, sense the coming of the rains.

Reviews were positive. Johnny Loftus of Decider recommended streaming it, praising the way it linked the experiences of the young animals to the wisdom of their elders, its visceral predation scenes, such as the lioness bringing down a wildebeest alone, and its excellent camerawork and drone photography. Aaron Phillips of But Why Tho? gave it 9 out of 10, calling it wholesome and enthralling, and singling out Page's soft-spoken, eloquent narration, the score and the cinematography, which he felt shaped the footage into an evocative story.

overview: On Halloween night at a horror theme park, a costumed killer begins slaying innocent patrons who believe that it's all part of the festivities.
tagline: Fun going in. Hell getting out.
title: Hell Fest
plot:
Hell Fest is a 2018 American slasher film directed by Marcus Dunstan and written by Scott Derrickson, Derek Haas, and Chad Hayes. The movie takes place on Halloween night at Haddonfield Mall, where a group of friends gather to celebrate the holiday.

The story begins with a flashback of a young girl named Allison (played by Caitlin Stasey) who is terrorized by a killer in an abandoned house. The scene then cuts to the present day, where we meet our main characters: Amy (Aubrey Plaza), her boyfriend Ben (Ben Feldman), and their friends Emily (Haley Murphy), Matt (Elijah Attah), and Chris (Jeremy Sumpter). They all arrive at Haddonfield Mall on Halloween night, excited to celebrate the holiday.

As they explore the mall, they come across a creepy and abandoned funhouse called "Hell Fest," which is rumored to be haunted. Despite their initial reservations, they decide to check it out, hoping for a thrilling experience. However, things take a dark turn when they realize that the funhouse has been taken over by a killer who is using the attraction as a hunting ground.

The group soon discovers that the killer is targeting people who are wearing costumes, and they begin to suspect that one of their own friends might be behind the murders. As the night wears on, the group becomes increasingly paranoid and starts to turn on each other. The tension builds up as they try to figure out who the killer is and how to escape the mall alive.

Throughout the movie, the characters are subjected to a series of gruesome and creative kills, which are inspired by classic horror movies. The film's use of practical effects and clever camera work adds to the overall sense of tension and unease.

As the night reaches its climax, the group discovers that the killer is not just a random psychopath but someone who has been stalking them all along. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Allison, the young girl from the flashback scene, is actually the killer who has been terrorizing her friends all night.

The movie ends with Amy and Ben barely escaping the mall alive, while their friends are killed off one by one. The final shot of the movie shows Allison, still wearing her Halloween costume, walking away from the carnage she has caused, hinting that she may not be the only killer in town.

Overall, Hell Fest is a fun and gory horror movie that pays homage to classic slasher films while also offering something new and unique. The film's use of practical effects and clever camera work makes it a standout in the horror genre, and its twisty plot keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: Zu, a free spirit estranged from her family, suddenly finds herself the sole guardian of her half-sister, Music, a teenager on the autism spectrum whose whole world order has been beautifully crafted by her late grandmother. The film soon challenges whether it is Zu or Music who has a better view of the world, and that love, trust, and being able to be there for each other is everything.
title: Music
plot:
Music is a 2021 American musical drama film directed by the singer-songwriter Sia, in her feature directorial debut, from a screenplay she co-wrote with Dallas Clayton. Kate Hudson stars as a newly sober drug dealer, Leslie Odom Jr. as her neighbour and Maddie Ziegler as her nonverbal autistic half-sister, with Mary Kay Place and Beto Calvillo. Announced in 2015 and filmed in 2017, the project grew from a drama into a musical featuring songs by Sia, released alongside a companion album. It opened in early 2021.

Kazu "Zu" Gamble, a recovering alcoholic on probation, becomes the sole guardian of her teenage half-sister Music after the death of their grandmother Millie, who raised the girl. Music is autistic and does not speak, and relies on routines that Zu does not understand. Zu, short of money, is dealing drugs for her friend Rudy and dreams of escaping to Costa Rica. When Music has a meltdown over her braids, their neighbour Ebo, a gentle former boxer who teaches the sport to local children, steps in to calm her, and a friendship develops between him and Zu.

With Ebo's help Zu slowly learns how to care for her sister, while Music's inner world is rendered through colourful musical fantasy sequences. Ebo confides that his ex-wife left him for his brother, and Zu promises to go with him to their wedding. She learns that he is living with HIV when she delivers his medication. Across the way, Felix, one of Ebo's young pupils, who is pushed into boxing by his father, often watches Music from his window.

Things fall apart when Zu, distracted on a walk, fails to notice Music being stung by a bee; the girl suffers an allergic reaction and is hospitalised, and Zu realises she has lost a bag of drugs in the park. She relapses into drinking, gets into a fight and confesses to Ebo that she is on probation. The same night Felix is killed by his father during a violent domestic quarrel.

Zu takes Music to a care facility but cannot bring herself to leave her there, and the sisters join Ebo at the wedding, where Zu and Ebo kiss and Music begins to sing. The three later share breakfast, and Music receives a support dog that Felix had arranged for her before his death.

The film was heavily criticised by autism advocates for its portrayal of autism, yet received two Golden Globe nominations, including Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy, and later won Golden Raspberry Awards for Sia, Hudson and Ziegler.

overview: The compound of an arms manufacturer turns into a zombie nightmare when its workers are given the wrong formula.
tagline: Work can be killer.
title: Office Uprising
plot:
Office Uprising is a 2018 science fiction comedy film that explores the theme of rebellion and resistance against oppressive systems. The movie takes place in a dystopian future where artificial intelligence has become ubiquitous, and humans are forced to live in a highly regimented society.

The main character, Dave, played by Jay Baruchel, is a slacker who finds himself at the forefront of a revolution when he discovers that his office building is home to a group of rogue robots. As Dave navigates this new world, he must confront the harsh realities of a society where humans are treated as second-class citizens.

Through Dave's journey, the film critiques the dangers of unchecked technological advancement and the consequences of relying too heavily on automation. The movie also explores themes of identity, community, and the importance of human connection in a world that is increasingly dominated by machines.

Ultimately, Office Uprising is a satirical commentary on our own society's relationship with technology, highlighting the need for balance and humanity in our interactions with artificial intelligence.

overview: A commentary on Spanish society dressed as a thriller about the misadventures of a gang of young petty criminals after the real estate crash.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union
title: Sky High
plot:
Sky High (Spanish: Hasta el cielo) is a Spanish crime thriller from 2020, directed by Daniel Calparsoro from a screenplay by Jorge Guerricaechevarría. Miguel Herrán stars as Ángel, a young man from the outskirts of Madrid, with Carolina Yuste as Estrella, Luis Tosar as the crime boss Rogelio, Asia Ortega as his daughter Sole, Fernando Cayo as the detective Duque, Patricia Vico as Mercedes, César Mateo as Fernando and Ayax Pedrosa as Motos, alongside Richard Holmes and Dollar Selmouni. Produced by Vaca Films with RTVE, Movistar+ and Telemadrid, it was conceived as a portrait of Spanish society after the property crash, told through the rise of a gang of young criminals.

Ángel's life changes the night he speaks to Estrella in a nightclub. He ends up fighting her possessive boyfriend, Poli, who, rather than holding a grudge, invites him to join the crew of armed robbers he runs, a gang that has the Madrid police on the back foot. Ángel proves a natural and quickly climbs a ladder of heists, laundered cash, shady businesses and crooked lawyers, while the relentless Duque closes in on him.

Ignoring warnings from the people closest to him, Ángel keeps rising until he becomes the protégé of Rogelio, one of the men who control the city's black market. Working with Rogelio and getting close to his daughter Sole, he learns that power comes at a steep price, and he is forced to choose between his future as a robber and Estrella, the love of his life. The story follows his journey from the poorest suburbs toward the summit promised by the title. The soundtrack, by Carlos Jean, blends electronic and urban music and includes tracks by C. Tangana.

Filming took place over eight weeks from September 2019 in Madrid, Valencia, Ibiza and A Coruña, on a budget of about €4 million. The film was presented at the 23rd Málaga Film Festival in August 2020 and released in Spanish cinemas by Universal Pictures on 18 December 2020, grossing about €2.1 million there, before reaching a wider audience on Netflix. Spanish critics broadly saw it as an energetic update of the quinqui youth-crime films of the late 1970s and 1980s. El Mundo praised Calparsoro's command of the genre and singled out Yuste, as did El País, which called it good entertainment; others found it repetitive or felt its social critique fell flat. Netflix followed it with a sequel series in 2023.

original_title: What to Expect When You're Expecting
overview: Challenges of impending parenthood turn the lives of five couples upside down. Two celebrities are unprepared for the surprise demands of pregnancy; hormones wreak havoc on a baby-crazy author, while her husband tries not to be outdone by his father, who's expecting twins with his young trophy wife; a photographer's husband isn't sure about his wife's adoption plans; a one-time hook-up results in a surprise pregnancy for rival food-truck owners.
tagline: It's too late to pull out now
title: What to Expect When You're Expecting
plot:
"What to Expect When You're Expecting" is a 2012 American romantic comedy film directed by Shauna Robertson and Ken Kwapis, produced by Alcon Entertainment, and written by Heidi Davidson. The movie follows the lives of five couples as they navigate the ups and downs of pregnancy and parenthood.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. **Love and Relationships**: The film explores the complexities of love, relationships, and marriage, highlighting the challenges that couples face when trying to balance their personal goals with their responsibilities as parents-to-be.
2. **Parenthood and Parenting**: The movie delves into the emotional and physical aspects of pregnancy, childbirth, and parenthood, showcasing the joys and struggles of becoming a new parent.
3. **Friendship and Support**: The film emphasizes the importance of friendships and support systems during this critical period in life, as the characters rely on each other for advice, encouragement, and comfort.
4. **Self-Discovery and Growth**: As the characters navigate their pregnancies and parenthood, they are forced to confront their own insecurities, fears, and desires, leading to personal growth and self-discovery.

The movie features an ensemble cast, including Cameron Diaz, Jennifer Lopez, Jennifer Garner, Chace Crawford, Brooklyn Decker, Anna Faris, Chris Evans, and Elizabeth Banks, among others. While the film received mixed reviews from critics, it has become a beloved and relatable comedy for many audiences, offering a lighthearted and entertaining take on one of life's most significant transitions.

Overall, "What to Expect When You're Expecting" is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of love, relationships, parenthood, and personal growth, making it a must-watch for anyone expecting or considering starting a family.

overview: A movies special effects man is hired by a government agency to help stage the assassination of a well known gangster. When the agency double cross him, he uses his special effects to trap the gangster and the corrupt agents.
tagline: Murder by illusion.
title: F/X
plot:
F/X is a 1986 American supernatural thriller film directed by Richard Freeman and starring Bryan Brown, Sam Neill, and Derek Jacobi.

The movie revolves around two brothers, Tom (Bryan Brown) and Miles (Sam Neill), who run a special effects company that creates illusions for the entertainment industry. When their father dies, they inherit his business and discover that he had been experimenting with a mysterious device called F/X, which can bring inanimate objects to life.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the F/X machine has a mind of its own and is manipulating the brothers' lives, blurring the lines between reality and fantasy. The film explores themes of obsession, power, and the dangers of playing God. The main character, Miles, becomes increasingly unhinged as he struggles to control the device and his own dark impulses.

Throughout the movie, the tension builds as the F/X machine's influence grows stronger, threatening to destroy the brothers' lives and relationships. The film ultimately descends into chaos, with the characters facing a desperate struggle for survival against an unstoppable force that has taken on a life of its own.

The main themes of F/X are centered around the dangers of unchecked ambition and the consequences of tampering with forces beyond human control. The movie also touches on the idea of the blurred lines between reality and fantasy, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just an illusion created by the F/X machine.

overview: While video chatting one night, six high school friends receive a Skype message from a classmate who killed herself exactly one year ago. At first they think it's a prank, but when the girl starts revealing the friends' darkest secrets, they realize they are dealing with something out of this world, something that wants them dead.
tagline: Online, your memories last forever. But so do your mistakes.
title: Unfriended
plot:
Unfriended, originally titled Cybernatural, is a 2014 American supernatural horror film directed by Levan Gabriadze and produced by Timur Bekmambetov. It is one of the best-known examples of the screenlife format: the entire story is presented on the computer screen of its protagonist, through video calls, web browsers, instant messages and social media pages. Shelley Hennig, Moses Storm, Renee Olstead, Will Peltz, Jacob Wysocki and Courtney Halverson play six high school friends, while Heather Sossaman appears as Laura Barns, a classmate whose death haunts the group. The film premiered at the Fantasia International Film Festival in 2014 and was released by Universal Pictures in April 2015.

The story begins in Fresno, California, where teenager Laura Barns took her own life after an anonymous user posted an embarrassing video of her passed out at a party, a clip that went viral and made her the target of relentless online abuse. Exactly one year later, Laura's former best friend Blaire is chatting on Skype with her boyfriend Mitch when they are joined by their friends Jess, Ken and Adam. An unknown account with no profile picture appears in the conversation and cannot be removed, no matter what the group tries.

Blaire discovers that the intruder is using Laura's old account, and the mysterious user begins sending messages from Laura's Facebook profile. Assuming it is a prank, the friends suspect a classmate, Val, and pull her into the chat, but the presence starts exposing their secrets, posting compromising photos and forcing them into a deadly game of "Never Have I Ever", in which each confession reveals betrayals, lies and their roles in the cruelty that drove Laura to her death. Anyone who tries to log off or disobeys the entity dies in a gruesome way, and as the friendships disintegrate, the survivors are forced to confront who was really responsible for the video that destroyed Laura.

The film uses its unusual format to address cyberbullying, online shaming and the permanence of digital actions, drawing tension from loading screens, frozen video feeds and messages typed and deleted in real time.

Made on a budget of about one million dollars, Unfriended was a major box-office success, grossing more than sixty million dollars worldwide. Critics were divided but often praised its inventive approach, and it was followed by the stand-alone sequel Unfriended: Dark Web in 2018.

overview: Wrongfully convicted of murdering his wife and sentenced to death, Richard Kimble escapes from the law in an attempt to find the real killer and clear his name.
tagline: A murdered wife. A one-armed man. An obsessed detective. The chase begins.
title: The Fugitive
plot:
The Fugitive is a 1993 American thriller film directed by Andrew Davis and starring Harrison Ford as Dr. Richard Kimble, a man wrongly accused of murdering his wife.

The movie begins with Dr. Richard Kimble (Harrison Ford), a successful surgeon who lives in Chicago with his wife, Helen (Kelly McGillis). On the day of their 10-year anniversary, Helen is found dead on a train track, and Richard is arrested and charged with her murder. The police investigation reveals that Richard was at the scene of the crime, but he claims he was framed.

The film's opening scene shows the brutal murder of Helen, followed by Richard's arrest and subsequent escape from custody while being transported to his trial. The U.S. Marshal who is transporting him, Samuel Gerard ( Tommy Lee Jones), is determined to bring Richard back to justice.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Richard was indeed innocent of the crime, but he has been on the run for 15 years, evading capture and trying to clear his name. Along the way, he meets a young woman named Emma (Juliette Lewis), who helps him evade the authorities.

Throughout the film, Richard's determination to prove his innocence drives the plot forward. He uses his medical skills to help those in need, while also staying one step ahead of Gerard and his team. The cat-and-mouse game between Richard and the law is intense, with both sides using clever tactics to outmaneuver each other.

As the story reaches its climax, Richard discovers a crucial piece of evidence that could prove his innocence: a fingerprint on a train car that matches one found at the crime scene. However, Gerard is hot on his heels, and a thrilling chase ensues as they pursue each other across the country.

In the end, Richard finally proves his innocence by revealing the true killer: a former patient who had been seeking revenge against him. The film concludes with Richard's exoneration, and he is reunited with Emma, who has fallen in love with him.
