The third live-action Asterix film, following Asterix & Obelix: Mission Cleopatra (2002), it stars Clovis Cornillac, who replaced Christian Clavier as Asterix, and Gérard Depardieu, returning as Obelix, with Benoît Poelvoorde as Brutus and Alain Delon as Julius Caesar.

In the village of indomitable Gauls, the young and lovesick Lovesix is smitten with Irina, a Greek princess. But Irina has been promised to Brutus, the scheming son of Julius Caesar, who also wishes to marry her. To win her hand, Lovesix decides to compete against Brutus in the Olympic Games in Greece, and Asterix and Obelix, along with the druid Getafix, accompany him to help. The Gauls must face not only formidable athletes from across the known world but also the ruthless Brutus, who will stop at nothing, including cheating, sabotage and doping his own Roman team, to ensure victory. At the same time Brutus plots to get rid of his father and seize power. Complicating matters, the Gauls are forbidden from using their magic potion, the source of their superhuman strength, and must find other ways to triumph. The climax unfolds during a spectacular chariot race.

The film is a loose adaptation of the 1968 comic book Asterix at the Olympic Games. The love story between Lovesix and Irina was invented for the film, and Brutus, who plays a much larger role here than in the comics, serves as the comic villain. The film features cameo appearances by sports stars including Michael Schumacher as a charioteer, Zinedine Zidane, Tony Parker and Amélie Mauresmo. It was Alain Delon's last film role as an actor and the final film of Jean-Pierre Cassel, who played Getafix, and of Sim, who played Geriatrix. It was filmed in Alicante, Spain.

At the time of its release in January 2008, it was the most expensive French film and the most expensive non-English-language film ever made. Critics responded negatively, but the film was a commercial success in several European countries, topping the box office in France, Spain and Poland and grossing about $23 million in France in its opening weekend. It was followed by Asterix and Obelix: God Save Britannia in 2012.

overview: The story of a young boy in the Midwest is told simultaneously with a tale about a young girl in New York from fifty years ago as they both seek the same mysterious connection.
tagline: It's not what you look at that matters, it's what you see.
title: Wonderstruck
plot:
Wonderstruck is a 2017 American drama film directed by Todd Haynes. The story revolves around two young protagonists, Ben and Rose, who are connected through a mysterious letter that sets them on a journey to uncover the truth about their families' pasts.

The main theme of Wonderstruck is the power of storytelling and its ability to transcend time and space. Through the interconnected narratives of Ben and Rose, the film explores how stories can be passed down through generations, influencing our understanding of ourselves and our place in the world.

One of the central themes of the film is also the idea of identity and self-discovery. Both Ben and Rose are searching for answers about their families' pasts, which leads them to question their own identities and sense of belonging. As they navigate through their respective stories, they begin to uncover secrets that challenge their perceptions of themselves and their relationships with others.

Furthermore, Wonderstruck touches on the theme of love and connection across time and space. Despite being separated by decades, Ben and Rose form a deep bond through their shared experiences and the mysterious letter that brings them together. The film highlights the importance of human connections in our lives, even when we are physically far apart.

The film also explores the idea of nostalgia and its impact on our understanding of the past. Through the characters' stories, the film shows how nostalgia can be both a source of comfort and a hindrance to moving forward. As Ben and Rose navigate their respective narratives, they must confront the complexities of their families' pasts and the ways in which nostalgia can shape our perceptions of reality.

Overall, Wonderstruck is a poignant exploration of the human experience, delving into themes that are both deeply personal and universally relatable.

overview: Down-and-dirty musical love story set in the world of the working class. Nick is an ironworker who builds and repairs bridges. He's married to Kitty, a dressmaker, a strong and gentle woman with whom he has three daughters. He is carrying on a torrid affair with a redheaded woman named Tula. Nick is basically a good, hardworking man driven forward by will and blinded by his urges.
title: Romance & Cigarettes
plot:
Romance & Cigarettes is a 2005 musical romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and human connection in a world where people are often disconnected from each other. The movie delves into the theme of loneliness and isolation, showcasing how individuals struggle to form meaningful connections with others.

The film also touches on the idea of escapism, as characters seek solace in music, cigarettes, and romantic fantasies to temporarily escape their mundane lives. However, these escapes are often fleeting, and the characters are ultimately forced to confront the harsh realities of their own desires and relationships.

Furthermore, Romance & Cigarettes critiques societal expectations and norms surrounding love, relationships, and identity. The movie presents a nuanced portrayal of human desire, highlighting both the beauty and the pain that can come with it.

Through its unique blend of music, dance, and drama, the film offers a poignant commentary on the human experience, encouraging viewers to reflect on their own desires, connections, and sense of belonging.

overview: When an unknown military force invades Bushwick, a Brooklyn neighborhood, young student Lucy and war veteran Stupe must rely on each other to escape and survive.
tagline: Fight for your city, block by block
title: Bushwick
plot:
Bushwick is a 2017 American action thriller film directed by Jonathan Milott and Cary Murnion. The movie follows the story of Lucy Hill (played by Brittany Snow), an American woman who finds herself in the middle of a war between Russian and Ukrainian forces in Brooklyn's Bushwick neighborhood.

The main themes of Bushwick include:

1. **Survival**: The film focuses on Lucy's struggle to survive amidst the chaos and violence that surrounds her. She must use her wits, resourcefulness, and determination to stay alive.
2. **Identity**: As a foreigner in an unfamiliar environment, Lucy is forced to confront her own identity and sense of belonging. Her experiences in Bushwick challenge her perceptions of herself and her place in the world.
3. **Human Connection**: Despite the dire circumstances, the film highlights the importance of human connection and community. Lucy forms bonds with the people around her, including a Ukrainian man named Viktor (played by Dave Bautista), who helps her navigate the treacherous situation.
4. **War and its Consequences**: Bushwick portrays the devastating effects of war on civilians, particularly women. The film sheds light on the human cost of conflict and the need for empathy and understanding in times of crisis.

Overall, Bushwick is a tense, action-packed thriller that explores themes of survival, identity, human connection, and the consequences of war.

overview: In the late 21st century, a subculture of humans have emerged who have been modified genetically by a vampire-like disease, giving them enhanced speed, incredible stamina and acute intelligence. As they are set apart from "normal" and "healthy" humans, the world is pushed to the brink of worldwide civil war  aimed at the destruction of the "diseased" population. In the middle of this crossed-fire is - an infected woman - Ultraviolet, who finds herself protecting a nine-year-old boy who has been marked for death by the human government as he is believed to be a threat to humans.
tagline: The blood war is on.
title: Ultraviolet
plot:
Ultraviolet is a 2006 science fiction film directed by Vincenzo Natali, starring MJ Nutter, Jamie King, and Kevin Zegers.

The main themes of Ultraviolet can be broken down into several key areas:

1. **Identity Crisis**: The protagonist, Violet (MJ Nutter), struggles with her identity after being exposed to a mysterious energy source that alters her DNA. This transformation leads to a series of events that challenge her sense of self and force her to confront the darker aspects of her personality.

2. **Trauma and PTSD**: Violet's experiences are marked by trauma, violence, and abuse, which have left her with emotional scars. As she navigates this new reality, she must come to terms with her past and find ways to cope with the aftermath of these traumatic events.

3. **Corruption and Decay**: The film explores the theme of corruption and decay through its depiction of a dystopian future where corporations and governments have become increasingly powerful and oppressive. This serves as a commentary on the dangers of unchecked power and the erosion of individual freedoms.

4. **Rebirth and Redemption**: Throughout the story, Violet undergoes a process of transformation, both physically and emotionally. As she confronts her past and the forces that seek to control her, she begins to find a sense of purpose and redemption, ultimately emerging as a stronger and more resilient individual.

5. **Existentialism and Free Will**: The film raises questions about the nature of free will and whether individuals have agency in shaping their own destinies. Violet's journey is marked by choices that challenge her understanding of herself and the world around her, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of these decisions.

Overall, Ultraviolet is a thought-provoking sci-fi thriller that explores complex themes and ideas through its narrative and characters.

overview: The Blind Man has been hiding out for several years in an isolated cabin and has taken in and raised a young girl orphaned from a devastating house fire. Their quiet life together is shattered when a group of criminals kidnap the girl, forcing the Blind Man to leave his safe haven to save her.
tagline: Bad things happen to bad people.
title: Don't Breathe 2
plot:
Don't Breathe 2 is a 2021 American horror thriller directed by Rodo Sayagues, in his directorial debut, who co-wrote it with Fede Álvarez, director of the original film. The sequel to Don't Breathe (2016), it brings back Stephen Lang as the blind former Navy SEAL Norman Nordstrom, with Brendan Sexton III and Madelyn Grace. Shot in Belgrade, Serbia, in 2020, it was released by Sony Pictures in the United States on August 13, 2021.

Eight years after the events of the first film, Norman lives in seclusion near Detroit with an eleven-year-old girl, Phoenix, whom he presents as his daughter and trains in survival skills, and his rottweiler, Shadow. He tells her that her mother died in a house fire. His friend Hernandez, a former Army Ranger, persuades him to let Phoenix come into town with her, and takes the girl to visit her mother's memorial at the burnt-out house. There a man named Raylan tries to grab Phoenix, but is driven off by the dog.

Raylan's gang follows them home, murders Hernandez, kills Shadow, and breaks into Norman's house to seize Phoenix. During the struggle Raylan reveals that he is the girl's real father, pointing to the matching streak of white in their hair. Phoenix learns that her home burned down after a meth lab exploded, that Raylan spent years in prison, and that Norman had found her unconscious in the ruins and taken her to replace the daughter he had lost. The gang sets fire to the house and leaves Norman for dead, but he escapes with Raylan's own dog, which leads him to the gang's hideout.

There Raylan introduces Phoenix, whose real name is Tara, to her mother Josephine, who survived the explosion but is dying from organ damage caused by the fumes. The couple intend to have the girl's compatible heart transplanted into her mother in a makeshift operation. Norman arrives, cuts the power and picks off the gang one by one in the dark; the surgeon is killed and a stray bullet kills Josephine. Norman blinds Raylan and, badly wounded, confesses his past crimes to Tara. When Raylan returns and stabs Norman, Tara kills him. Norman appears to die, and Tara walks to a children's home, introducing herself as Phoenix.

The film grossed about 53.8 million dollars worldwide and received mixed to negative reviews, with critics questioning its attempt to make Norman sympathetic.

overview: High school graduation just wouldn’t be complete without an un-chaperoned, uninhibited and unforgettable final holiday. At least that’s what Will, Jay, Simon and Neil think when they book a two-week stay on an exotic Greek island. As their dreams of sun-drenched days and booze-filled nights are left hopelessly unfulfilled, the lads fight their way into the party scene with hilariously humiliating results in this smash hit UK raunchy comedy.
tagline: Out of school. Out of their league.
title: The Inbetweeners Movie
plot:
The Inbetweeners Movie, known in North America simply as The Inbetweeners, is a 2011 British coming-of-age comedy based on the E4 sitcom The Inbetweeners. Written by series creators Damon Beesley and Iain Morris and directed by Ben Palmer, it was intended as the conclusion of the television series and stars Simon Bird, Joe Thomas, James Buckley and Blake Harrison, reprising their roles, with Emily Head, Laura Haddock, Tamla Kari and Lydia Rose Bewley. It was released in the United Kingdom and Ireland on 17 August 2011 by Entertainment Film Distributors.

Will McKenzie, Simon Cooper, Jay Cartwright and Neil Sutherland finish their A-levels and leave Rudge Park Comprehensive. Jay's grandfather has died and Simon has been dumped by his long-time crush and girlfriend, Carli. To celebrate the end of school and cheer up their friends, the four boys book a holiday in the party resort of Malia, on the Greek island of Crete. After a coach ride shared with chanting football supporters, they discover that their hotel is a rundown dump and head out into Malia's nightlife.

Tricked into visiting a deserted bar, the boys meet four girls on holiday: Alison, Lucy, Lisa and Jane. Will and Alison connect over their shared sense of humor, Simon frustrates Lucy by talking endlessly about Carli, Neil and Lisa sit in awkward silence, and Jay is annoyed when Jane takes an interest in him. Their first encounter goes badly, but the boys keep running into the girls over the course of the week. The holiday becomes a series of humiliating misadventures, as the friends fail to fit in at the resort's clubs, quarrel among themselves and wrestle with their own insecurities. Simon's obsession with Carli, who is also holidaying in Malia, threatens his chance with Lucy, while Jay must decide whether to stop boasting and admit his real feelings, and Will tries to win over Alison. By the end of the trip, the four friends come to appreciate each other and the girls they have met.

The film was a huge commercial success in the United Kingdom, becoming one of the highest-grossing comedies in British box-office history, and it received generally favorable reviews there, though its later release in the United States was greeted less warmly. It was followed by The Inbetweeners 2 in 2014.

overview: A young, lonely woman is consumed by her deepest and darkest desires after tragedy strikes her quiet country life.
title: The Eyes of My Mother
plot:
The Eyes of My Mother is a 2016 American black-and-white psychological horror film written and directed by Nicolas Pesce. The movie tells the story of Francisca, a young woman who was raised by her mother after her father's death, and her subsequent descent into madness and violence.

At its core, The Eyes of My Mother explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the destructive power of unchecked emotions. Francisca's life is marked by a deep sense of disconnection from the world around her, as she is raised in a sterile and loveless environment that stifles her emotional development. As she grows older, her desire for human connection and intimacy becomes increasingly distorted, leading her to commit heinous acts of violence.

The film also delves into the idea of the "monstrous other," where Francisca's actions are seen as a manifestation of her own inner turmoil and the societal expectations placed upon her. Her relationship with her mother is particularly significant, as it highlights the ways in which trauma can be passed down through generations and the devastating consequences of unaddressed emotional pain.

Furthermore, The Eyes of My Mother critiques the notion of romantic love and the idea that it can be a redemptive force in one's life. Francisca's obsession with her mother is portrayed as a twisted form of devotion, rather than a healthy expression of love or attachment. This serves to underscore the film's central theme of the corrosive effects of unrequited desire and the dangers of allowing emotions to consume us.

Overall, The Eyes of My Mother is a haunting and unsettling exploration of the human psyche, one that probes the darkest recesses of the human heart and reveals the devastating consequences of unchecked emotions.

overview: As a wild stallion travels across the frontiers of the Old West, he befriends a young human and finds true love with a mare.
tagline: Leader. Hero. Legend.
title: Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron
plot:
Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron is a 2002 American animated Western drama film produced by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the journey of a wild mustang stallion named Spirit, who embarks on an epic quest to find his place in the world.

The film begins with Spirit (voiced by Matt Damon) as a young foal, born and raised in the Cimarron Valley. He is a spirited and adventurous horse, always eager to explore and discover new things. As he grows up, Spirit becomes increasingly restless, feeling confined by the limitations of his herd's routine.

One day, Spirit meets a beautiful mare named Rain (voiced by Gina Philips), who shares his sense of wanderlust. Together, they set out on an adventure across the American West, facing numerous challenges and dangers along the way. They encounter fierce storms, treacherous terrain, and hostile humans, but their bond grows stronger with each passing day.

As Spirit and Rain journey through the wilderness, they meet a wise old stallion named Thunder (voiced by Michael Jeter), who teaches them about the importance of freedom and self-discovery. However, their happiness is short-lived, as they are captured by a ruthless horse trader named Colonel Hart (voiced by James Cromwell) and his men.

Spirit is sold to a cavalry unit, where he meets a young soldier named Little Creek (voiced by Paul Williams), who befriends him and helps him escape. Together, they embark on a perilous journey back to the Cimarron Valley, facing numerous obstacles and dangers along the way.

As Spirit returns home, he is reunited with Rain, and together they face off against Colonel Hart in an epic showdown. With his newfound courage and determination, Spirit defeats the colonel and his men, securing his freedom and proving himself as a true leader among his herd.

Throughout the film, the animation is stunning, with beautifully rendered landscapes and characters that bring the American West to life. The voice cast delivers strong performances, bringing depth and emotion to their respective roles. The music, composed by Hans Zimmer and John Powell, is equally impressive, perfectly capturing the spirit (pun intended) of the wild mustang.

Overall, Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron is a timeless tale of self-discovery, courage, and the power of the human (and equine) spirit. With its stunning animation, memorable characters, and epic storyline, it's no wonder this film has become a beloved classic among both children and adults alike.

overview: Ajin is a live-action adaptation of a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Gamon Sakurai. Kei Nagai dies in a car accident, but realises he is a type of immortal known as Ajin (demi-human). Hunted by humans, Ajin is eventually found by the government and used as a subject in cruel experiments. He finds fellow demi-humans along the way as he escapes and goes on the run.
title: Ajin: Demi-Human
plot:
Ajin: Demi-Human is a thought-provoking anime series that delves into complex and mature themes. At its core, the story revolves around the concept of humanity and what it truly means to be alive.

The series explores the idea of identity and how it can be manipulated and distorted. The main character, Kei, is an Ajin, a being with extraordinary abilities, but also struggles with his own existence and sense of self. He grapples with the fact that he is not like other humans, and this perceived difference makes him question his place in society.

The show also delves into the theme of prejudice and how it can be used to control and oppress certain groups. The Ajin are shunned and feared by society, leading to a cycle of violence and mistrust. This serves as a commentary on how fear and misunderstanding can lead to the marginalization of those who are different.

Furthermore, Ajin: Demi-Human touches on the idea of morality and the gray areas that exist between right and wrong. The characters are often faced with difficult choices, and their actions have consequences that ripple throughout the story. This moral ambiguity adds depth to the narrative and encourages viewers to think critically about the themes presented.

Lastly, the series explores the concept of loneliness and isolation. Many characters in the show struggle with feelings of disconnection and loneliness, highlighting the importance of human connection and empathy in a world where individuals are often forced to hide their true selves.

Overall, Ajin: Demi-Human is a thought-provoking series that challenges viewers to confront complex themes and questions about what it means to be human.

overview: A group of young explorers discover a secret area hidden from all maps and GPS devices. When they reach the center of the lake, they discover an abandoned facility that houses one of the largest, and deadliest apex-predators known to man.
title: Lake Placid: Legacy
plot:
Lake Placid: Legacy is an action-adventure film that revolves around the theme of family and legacy. The movie follows the story of a young woman, who returns to her hometown in Maine to confront her troubled past and protect her loved ones from a monstrous creature. As she navigates through the treacherous terrain of her family's history and the dangers posed by the lake monster, she must also come to terms with her own identity and the weight of her family's legacy.

The film explores the idea that our past can shape us in profound ways, often leaving scars that we may not even realize are there. The main character's journey is a metaphor for the struggle to break free from the shackles of one's heritage and forge a new path, while still honoring the memories and lessons of those who came before her.

Throughout the movie, the theme of family is woven throughout, highlighting the complexities and tensions that can arise when different generations and personalities clash. The film also touches on the idea of legacy, suggesting that our actions have consequences that can be passed down to future generations, often in unexpected ways.

Ultimately, Lake Placid: Legacy is a story about self-discovery, redemption, and the power of love and sacrifice to overcome even the most daunting challenges.

overview: Rising executive Tim Conrad works for a boss who hosts a monthly dinner in which the guest who brings the biggest buffoon gets a career-boost. Tim plans on not attending until he meets Barry, a man who builds dioramas using stuffed mice. Barry's blundering but good intentions send Tim's life into a downward spiral, threatening a major business deal and possibly scuttling Tim's engagement to his fiancee.
tagline: Takes One To Know One.
title: Dinner for Schmucks
plot:
Dinner for Schmucks is a 2010 American comedy film directed by Jay Roach and starring Steve Carell, Paul Rudd, and Keira Knightley.

The movie revolves around Barry Speck (played by Steve Carell), an eccentric and awkward employee who wins a contest to attend a dinner party hosted by his boss, Tim Conrad (played by Paul Rudd). The story takes a turn when Barry's coworker, Greta Spangenberg (played by Keira Knightley), is invited to the same dinner party, and their lives become intertwined.

The main themes of Dinner for Schmucks include:

1. Social awkwardness: The film explores the struggles of social interactions, particularly in professional settings, through Barry's character.
2. Class differences: The movie highlights the contrast between the wealthy and influential guests at the dinner party and the more down-to-earth, yet equally eccentric, characters like Barry and Greta.
3. Unlikely friendships: Despite their initial awkwardness, Barry and Greta form an unlikely bond, which serves as a catalyst for personal growth and self-discovery.
4. Self-acceptance: As the story unfolds, both Barry and Greta learn to accept themselves and find their place in the world, rather than trying to conform to societal expectations.

Throughout the film, Roach uses humor, satire, and wit to poke fun at social norms, class differences, and the human tendency to try to fit in. The movie ultimately becomes a heartwarming exploration of friendship, self-acceptance, and finding one's place in the world.

overview: It is the story of an average, popular American teenager named Wendy Wu who discovers that in order to win the coveted crown she must first learn the way of the warrior. Wendy Wu has a one track mind, and that track leads directly to the title of homecoming queen -- no unscheduled stops, and no unnecessary detours. When a mysterious Chinese monk named Shen arrives to mold Wendy into a fearless kung fu warrior, however, her royal aspirations suddenly jump the track as she desperately attempts to juggle her boyfriend, her homework, and of course, the fierce competition to become homecoming queen. Now, as Wendy begins to train her mind, body, and spirit in the ancient tradition of the martial arts and her inner warrior gradually begins to emerge, the girl who once obsessed over popularity finally begins to put that popularity into perspective as she gradually realizes what truly matters in life.
tagline: Pretty. Tough.
title: Wendy Wu: Homecoming Warrior
plot: It is the story of an average, popular American teenager named Wendy Wu who discovers that in order to win the coveted crown she must first learn the way of the warrior. Wendy Wu has a one track mind, and that track leads directly to the title of homecoming queen -- no unscheduled stops, and no unnecessary detours. When a mysterious Chinese monk named Shen arrives to mold Wendy into a fearless kung fu warrior, however, her royal aspirations suddenly jump the track as she desperately attempts to juggle her boyfriend, her homework, and of course, the fierce competition to become homecoming queen. Now, as Wendy begins to train her mind, body, and spirit in the ancient tradition of the martial arts and her inner warrior gradually begins to emerge, the girl who once obsessed over popularity finally begins to put that popularity into perspective as she gradually realizes what truly matters in life.

overview: After years in the limelight, Selena Gomez achieves unimaginable stardom. But just as she reaches a new peak, an unexpected turn pulls her into darkness. This uniquely raw and intimate documentary spans her six-year journey into a new light.
tagline: Every breath, a breakthrough.
title: Selena Gomez: My Mind & Me
plot:
Selena Gomez: My Mind & Me is a 2022 American documentary film directed by Alek Keshishian that follows the singer and actress Selena Gomez over a period of six years. Produced by Lighthouse Management + Media and Interscope Films, it documents her struggles with her physical and mental health following her diagnoses of lupus and bipolar disorder, and features Gomez herself along with her close friend of more than a decade, Raquell Stevens.

The project began around 2015, after Keshishian directed the music video for Gomez's song "Hands to Myself". He has said that he had no interest in making a traditional pop documentary and wanted to show something more authentic, a goal Gomez shared, and that he had no idea at the outset that the film would become a six-year labor of love.

The documentary opens at a moment when Gomez has achieved enormous fame. Behind the glamour of concerts, tours and publicity, however, she is suffering from exhaustion, anxiety and depression, and an unexpected turn pulls her into darkness. Shot in an intimate, diary-like style, the film follows her through periods of crisis and recovery: the cancellation of a world tour, her treatment, her efforts to understand her illnesses and the slow process of learning to live with them. It shows her returning to her roots in Texas, revisiting people and places from her childhood, and travelling to Kenya for a charitable project, while she reflects on the pressures of growing up in the public eye. Much of the film is narrated through Gomez's own words, including passages from her journals, presenting an unvarnished portrait of a star trying to reconcile her public image with her private reality.

Critics noted that, unlike many music documentaries designed to burnish a celebrity image, the film operates in a rawer register, with Gomez trying to communicate honestly rather than perfectly, and it was praised for its transparency about mental health.

My Mind & Me premiered on the opening night of AFI Fest at the TCL Chinese Theatre in Hollywood on November 2, 2022, and was released on Apple TV+ and in select theaters two days later. Its trailer debuted on World Mental Health Day, and the song "My Mind & Me", heard over the end credits, was released as a single. It received positive reviews, with 97 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 68; The New York Times called it an honest portrait of stardom and mental illness.

overview: The lives of several couples and singles in New York intertwine over the course of New Year's Eve.
tagline: The one night anything is possible.
title: New Year's Eve
plot:
New Year's Eve is a 2011 romantic comedy film directed by Garry Marshall, produced by New Line Cinema, and written by Katherine Heigl, Josh Duhamel, and others. The movie follows the interconnected love stories of multiple couples in the five years leading up to New Year's Eve.

The main themes of New Year's Eve include:

1. Love and relationships: The film explores various aspects of love, including romance, friendship, and family relationships. It highlights the ups and downs of relationships and how people grow and change over time.
2. Self-discovery: Many characters in the movie are on a journey of self-discovery, trying to figure out who they are, what they want, and where they're going in life. This theme is particularly evident in the storylines of Rachel (Halle Berry) and Marcus (Eugene Levy).
3. Friendship: The film emphasizes the importance of friendships and how they can provide support, comfort, and a sense of belonging. Characters like Emma (Jessica Biel), Sam (Ashton Kutcher), and Oleg (Armie Hammer) form strong bonds with each other.
4. Nostalgia: New Year's Eve is a celebration of memories and the passing of time. The movie takes viewers on a journey through the past, highlighting moments that shape who we are today.
5. Hope and renewal: As the characters look to the future, they also reflect on their past experiences and the lessons they've learned. This theme is reflected in the storylines of Emma and Sam, as well as Rachel and Marcus.

Throughout the film, these themes are intertwined, creating a rich tapestry of stories that explore the complexities of human relationships and personal growth.

overview: Frank and Lindsay—two emotionally-broken strangers—meet on the way to a destination wedding. Over the course of the weekend and against all odds, they find themselves drawn together even though they are initially repulsed by one another.
tagline: Check your baggage.
title: Destination Wedding
plot:
Destination Wedding is a 2018 American romantic comedy-drama written and directed by Victor Levin. Winona Ryder and Keanu Reeves star as two cynical strangers attending the same wedding in Paso Robles, California, marking their fourth film together; the story is told almost entirely through their conversations, with other characters barely heard. It was released in the United States on August 31, 2018.

At the airport, two middle-aged travellers, Frank and Lindsay, bicker before boarding and are dismayed to find themselves seated next to each other on a tiny commuter plane, then even more so when they realise they are bound for the same destination wedding. They know of each other already: the groom, Keith, is Frank's estranged half-brother and Lindsay's former fiancé, who left her six years earlier, and they suspect they have been deliberately put together. On arrival they discover they have adjoining rooms at the inn.

Frank admits he has no wish to attend, while Lindsay says she is going in search of closure. Frank, who works in marketing, and Lindsay, a lawyer, mock each other's careers. Seated together and apart from the other guests at the rehearsal dinner, they trade acid remarks about everyone present, and Frank unloads his bitterness about his family. The next day they skip the planned activities, such as a wine tasting, and keep talking instead. Lindsay confesses that she still loves Keith, while Frank insists that love is pointless and that his family history has ruined his life, and Lindsay tells him to move on.

The two keep up their running commentary through the wedding, then slip away from the dancing for a walk in the countryside, where a mountain lion appears and Frank scares it off. Falling to the ground as they run, they kiss and then have sex, before retreating to Frank's room to talk, drink and watch television. Lindsay tells him she wants a relationship, but Frank refuses, convinced it could never work, and they argue before falling asleep side by side.

On the flight home Lindsay keeps arguing that their unlikely connection is a small miracle worth pursuing, while Frank insists that he prefers to be alone. They agree not to swap contact details, but Lindsay calls out her address as her taxi pulls away. That night her doorbell rings, and she opens the door to find Frank standing there. Reviews were mixed, with critics praising the stars' chemistry while finding the relentless banter wearing.

overview: A teenage girl lives with her grandmother and worries she will be removed by social services. She sets off to get adopted by someone she admires more than anything, one of the most powerful women in the world.
title: Hawa
plot:
Hawa is a 2022 French comedy-drama directed by Maïmouna Doucouré, her second feature after Cuties, written by Doucouré with Alain-Michel Blanc and Zangro, who also produced it through Bien ou Bien Productions for Amazon Prime Video. Newcomer Sania Halifa, discovered through an open casting call, plays the title role, with the Malian singer Oumou Sangaré as her grandmother Maminata, Titouan Gerbier as Erwan and Jérôme Pouly as Jackie; the singer Yseult and the astronaut Thomas Pesquet appear as themselves. According to Doucouré, the story is about wanting to rise above one's social class.

Hawa is a fifteen-year-old Parisian girl with albinism, thick glasses and a blonde afro, who is often bullied for her looks but never backs down. She lives with Maminata, a griot who sings stories in the oral tradition and hopes to pass that art on to her. The grandmother is terminally ill and is searching for a family to take Hawa in, while the girl, who earns money at a corner grocery, rejects every candidate and faces the prospect of a foster home. After reading that Michelle Obama is in Paris promoting her memoir Becoming, Hawa decides that the former First Lady, whose daughters have left home, would be the ideal adoptive mother. Riding her scooter across the city with help from her shy friend Erwan, she slips backstage at a rehearsal for a concert by Yseult, who is charmed by her nerve, steals an invitation to a gala, sneaks into a children's hospital to pitch herself to Obama, wins the support of Thomas Pesquet and finally makes her way through the luggage area of Charles de Gaulle Airport toward Obama's plane, while at home Maminata's health keeps declining.

Hawa premiered in the Platform section of the Toronto International Film Festival on 13 September 2022, also screened at the Calgary International Film Festival, and was released on Prime Video on 9 December 2022. Critics responded warmly. In Variety, Tomris Laffly called it a big-hearted, crowd-pleasing contemporary fable with a disarming sense of humor, praising Halifa's lived-in performance, Sangaré's screen presence and the tight structure. Decider's John Serba recommended it as an understated neo-fairy tale that skirts magical realism and ends on a moving finale, though he admitted its set pieces defy logic. French press reviews were positive, averaging 3.2 out of 5 on AlloCiné.

overview: A mouthy and feisty taxicab driver has hot tips for a green and inept cop set on solving a string of New York City bank robberies committed by a quartet of female Brazilian bank robbers.
tagline: Take a Ride on the Wild Side.
title: Taxi
plot:
Taxi is a 2004 French drama film directed by Gérard Pirès. The movie follows the story of François Pignon (played by Samy Naceri), a young man who becomes involved in organized crime after his brother's death.

The main themes of Taxi include:

1. **Family and Loyalty**: The film explores the importance of family ties and loyalty, particularly in the context of organized crime. François is driven by a desire to protect his family and provide for them, which leads him down a path of involvement with the mafia.
2. **Identity and Belonging**: As François navigates the world of organized crime, he struggles to find his place within it. He must confront his own identity and decide whether to conform to the expectations of those around him or forge his own path.
3. **Redemption and Guilt**: Throughout the film, François grapples with feelings of guilt and regret over his brother's death. His journey is one of seeking redemption and making amends for past mistakes.
4. **The Corrupting Influence of Power**: The movie highlights the corrupting influence of power and the dangers of getting caught up in a world of organized crime. François's involvement with the mafia ultimately leads to chaos and destruction.

Overall, Taxi is a gripping drama that explores complex themes and characters, offering a nuanced portrayal of the human condition.

overview: Seventeen-year-old Shirley is a good student who works as a babysitter in order to make money for college. One night Michael, a father Shirley works for, confesses he's unhappy with married life. Shirley has a crush on Michael, and seizes this moment to kiss him. Michael is so happy he presents Shirley with a big tip, which gives her an idea. Shirley plans to make extra money by setting up her teenage friends with other unhappy fathers.
tagline: These girls mean business.
title: The Babysitters
plot:
The Babysitters is a 2007 American drama written and directed by David Ross. Katherine Waterston, in one of her first leading roles, stars as Shirley Lyner, a teenager who turns her babysitting service into a prostitution ring for married men, with John Leguizamo as Michael Beltran, Cynthia Nixon as his wife Gail, Andy Comeau and Denis O'Hare. The independent film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2007 and was released in the United States on 9 May 2008 by Peace Arch Releasing.

Narrating in voice-over, Shirley introduces her unusual "babysitting service" before a flashback shows how it began. Michael, a frustrated husband and father, picks Shirley up for an ordinary babysitting job and afterwards they share a meal and flirt; he is unhappy in his marriage, and she finds boys her own age immature. Michael and Gail meet his friend Jerry, who offers Michael a business opportunity that Gail does not want him to accept. Driving Shirley home one night, Michael stops at an abandoned train yard and the two share a kiss. Although they agree it cannot happen again, Michael pays her extra.

When Shirley's friend Melissa learns the truth about these outings and Michael tells Jerry, Michael asks whether any of Shirley's friends might also "babysit." Melissa volunteers, agreeing to give Shirley a twenty percent cut, and the girls recruit their friend Brenda, eventually running an organized business complete with printed cards and a growing clientele of suburban fathers. Michael becomes jealous when he learns that Shirley is seeing other men. Trouble begins when Brenda brings in her rough, aggressive stepsister Nadine without consulting Shirley, sparking a rivalry that threatens the enterprise, and as Shirley's control over the business grows, so do the risks to the girls and the men involved, along with the lies that keep their double lives hidden.

The Babysitters received negative reviews from critics, many of whom found its treatment of its provocative subject matter uneven and its tone confused. Some reviewers nonetheless singled out Waterston's poised performance, and she went on to more prominent roles in the following decade.

keywords.name: based on magazine, newspaper or article

overview: The remarkable true story of how retiree Jerry Selbee discovers a mathematical loophole in the Massachusetts lottery and, with the help of his wife, Marge, wins $27 million dollars and uses the money to revive their small Michigan town.
tagline: It's never too late to risk it all.
title: Jerry & Marge Go Large
plot:
Jerry & Marge Go Large is a 2022 American comedy-drama directed by David Frankel and written by Brad Copeland, based on Jason Fagone's 2018 HuffPost article about a real-life retired couple who legally exploited a loophole in a state lottery. Bryan Cranston and Annette Bening star, with Rainn Wilson, Larry Wilmore and Michael McKean. It premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on June 15, 2022, and was released on Paramount+ two days later.

In the struggling small town of Evart, Michigan, Jerry Selbee is pushed into retirement after 42 years at a factory. A gifted mathematician with time on his hands, he discovers a statistical loophole in the state lottery game WinFall: when the jackpot reaches $2 million without a winner, the money "rolls down" to lower prize tiers, and anyone buying enough tickets is virtually guaranteed a profit. Testing the theory in secret, he first loses money, then buys far more tickets and turns a profit. When his wife, Marge, finds out, she is thrilled and wants to join in. After Michigan's WinFall is discontinued, the couple begin driving to Massachusetts, where a similar game exists, buying tickets at a store in Sunderland.

To increase their stakes, they form a corporation and sell shares to friends and neighbors. Their winnings grow, and the dividends help revive Evart, as shuttered businesses reopen and plans are made to bring back the town's jazz festival. Their success attracts the attention of Tyler, an arrogant Harvard student running his own WinFall syndicate, who discovers their operation and demands that they stop, threatening to hack their accounts. Jerry nearly gives up, but with the encouragement of his son and the town, he keeps playing. When Tyler manipulates the game to trigger a roll-down early, cutting the Selbees out, Jerry confronts him in front of his fellow students, who abandon him, and persuades the lottery commission to announce roll-downs publicly to level the playing field.

A Boston Globe report on the loophole leads to the game's cancellation. The Selbees decide to sit out the final roll-down, but their investors secretly travel to Massachusetts to buy tickets across the state for one last big win. At the revived jazz festival, Jerry and Marge are celebrated as the heroes who brought their town back to life, having won around $27 million over the years.

Reviews were mixed to positive. Rotten Tomatoes reported 67% approval, and Metacritic gave it 52 out of 100.

overview: A father is without the means to pay for his daughter's medical treatment. As a last resort, he partners with a greedy co-worker to rob a casino. When things go awry they're forced to hijack a city bus.
tagline: Never make a bet you can't afford to lose.
title: Heist
plot:
Heist, also released as Bus 657, is a 2015 American action thriller directed by Scott Mann and written by Stephen Cyrus Sepher and Max Adams from an original story by Sepher. It stars Jeffrey Dean Morgan as Luke Vaughn, Robert De Niro as the casino owner known as the Pope, Dave Bautista as Cox and Gina Carano as police officer Kris Bajos, with Kate Bosworth, Morris Chestnut and Sepher. The story follows a desperate father whose casino robbery turns into a hostage crisis aboard a city bus.

Luke Vaughn works at a casino in the American South run by Francis Silva, a ruthless boss nicknamed the Pope. Vaughn's young daughter is seriously ill and needs an operation costing 300,000 dollars. When he asks the Pope for a loan, he is refused, fired and beaten by Silva's enforcer, Dog. A security guard named Cox then tells Vaughn that the casino launders money for the mob and proposes a robbery. Because Vaughn knows the vault codes, he agrees to join Cox's crew, and they steal the cash.

The getaway goes wrong when Dog's men intercept the thieves, a gunfight leaves one of the crew wounded and their driver abandons them. The robbers hijack a city bus full of passengers, pursued by Officer Bajos, and soon the police set up roadblocks. Vaughn tries to keep the hostages safe and negotiates with Bajos through a pregnant passenger's phone, while the volatile Cox threatens to kill people if the police do not back off. As the bus races along the highway and runs low on fuel, Detective Marconi and a SWAT team prepare to intervene, while the Pope sends Dog to recover his money at any cost. Vaughn must keep everyone alive, outwit both the police and the mob and find a way to get the money to his daughter.

The film combines a heist story with the confined, high-speed tension of a bus hijacking, setting a father's desperation against the brutality of organized crime.

Heist was released by Lionsgate Premiere on November 13, 2015. It received negative reviews, with 30 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that its all-star cast was dealt a poor hand by a humorless potboiler, and a Metacritic score of 37.

overview: Ten years after he first ventured into the Further, Josh Lambert heads east to drop his son Dalton off at an idyllic, ivy-covered university. However, Dalton's college dream becomes a nightmare when the repressed demons of his past suddenly resurface.
title: Insidious: Fear the Dark
plot:
Insidious: The Red Door is a 2023 American supernatural horror film directed by Patrick Wilson in his directorial debut, from a screenplay by Scott Teems based on a story by Leigh Whannell and Teems. The fifth Insidious film and a direct sequel to Insidious: Chapter 2 (2013), it reunites Wilson, Ty Simpkins, Rose Byrne and Lin Shaye, with Sinclair Daniel and Hiam Abbass joining the cast.

Nine years after the Lambert family's ordeal, Josh and his son Dalton have had their memories of the Further, the realm of the dead visited through astral projection, suppressed through hypnosis. Josh and Renai have since divorced, and Josh, struggling with lapses of memory, has grown distant from his children. After the funeral of Josh's mother, Josh drives Dalton to college, where the young man is studying art, but their relationship remains strained. Dalton befriends his roommate, Chris, and in an art class he is encouraged to delve into his subconscious, producing a painting of a red door that awakens buried memories and his dormant abilities.

Experimenting with astral projection, Dalton is confronted by the red-faced demon that tormented him as a child, which also attacks Chris. His brother Foster recalls a recurring nightmare in which their possessed father tried to kill them, and Dalton completes his painting, depicting Josh in front of the red door. Pulled back into the Further, Dalton relives Josh's possession and becomes trapped in the demon's lair. Meanwhile, Josh investigates his own father, who died in a psychiatric hospital, and learns from Renai the truth about their family's past and that his father also had the gift of astral projection but believed his visions were madness.

With Renai's help, Josh re-enters the Further to rescue his son as the demon takes control of Dalton's body and tries to kill Chris. Josh frees Dalton and holds the red door shut against the demon so that his son can escape, and Dalton seals the door by painting over his canvas in black. Guided home by the spirit of his own father, Josh returns to the living, reconciles with his family and visits Dalton, who shows him a painting of Josh carrying his young son out of the Further.

Released in the United States by Sony Pictures Releasing on July 7, 2023, the film received mixed reviews; Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called it a disappointing conclusion to a once-frightening franchise, and Metacritic gave it 45 out of 100. It grossed over $189 million, the highest of the series.

overview: A bet pits a British inventor, a Chinese thief and a French artist on a worldwide adventure that they can circle the globe in 80 days.
tagline: Let your imagination soar.
title: Around the World in 80 Days
plot:
Around the World in 80 Days is a 2004 action adventure comedy directed by Frank Coraci from a script by David Titcher, David Benullo and David Goldstein. Loosely based on Jules Verne's 1873 novel, it deliberately departs from the book for comic effect and includes many anachronisms. It stars Jackie Chan as Passepartout, Steve Coogan as Phileas Fogg, Cécile de France as Monique La Roche and Jim Broadbent as Lord Kelvin, with Ewen Bremner, Ian McNeice and cameo appearances by Arnold Schwarzenegger, Owen Wilson, Luke Wilson and others.

In Victorian London, a Chinese thief named Lau Xing steals a jade Buddha from the Bank of England. The statue had been given to Lord Kelvin, head of the Royal Academy of Science, by the Black Scorpions, a violent criminal group, in exchange for his support. Hiding from the police, Lau Xing takes refuge in the home of the eccentric inventor Phileas Fogg and, calling himself Passepartout, becomes his valet and helps test his inventions. When Fogg claims that it is possible to travel around the world in eighty days, the arrogant Kelvin, who despises innovation, wagers that if Fogg succeeds he will give up his position, but if he fails Fogg must abandon science forever.

Passepartout sees the journey as a way to return the Buddha to his village in China. Pursued by agents sent by Kelvin, Fogg and Passepartout travel to Paris, where they are joined by Monique, an aspiring impressionist painter. Their adventures take them by balloon, train and ship through Turkey, where a vain prince wants Monique for his harem, India and China, where Fogg learns Passepartout's true identity and helps defend his village. Crossing the Pacific to America, they meet the Wright brothers before racing back to London. Despite Kelvin's attempts to sabotage the journey, the travelers fight to arrive in time to win the bet and expose the corrupt lord.

The film emphasizes Chan's martial arts comedy over Verne's original story, transforming Passepartout into the central character.

Around the World in 80 Days premiered at the El Capitan Theatre on 13 June 2004 and opened in the United States three days later. It was a box-office bomb, earning about 72.6 million dollars worldwide against a 110 million dollar budget. Reviews were mixed to negative, with 32 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 49.

overview: An adaptation of the successful stage musical based on Victor Hugo's classic novel set in 19th-century France, in which a paroled prisoner named Jean Valjean seeks redemption.
tagline: Fight. Dream. Hope. Love.
title: Les Misérables
plot:
Les Misérables is a musical drama film directed by Tom Hooper, released in 2012 by Universal Pictures. The film is based on the novel of the same name by Victor Hugo and features an all-star cast, including Hugh Jackman, Anne Hathaway, Eddie Redmayne, Amanda Seyfried, and Samantha Barks.

The story begins in 1815, six months after the June Rebellion in Paris. Jean Valjean (Hugh Jackman), a former prisoner who was released from prison after serving nineteen years for stealing a loaf of bread to feed his sister's seven children, is pursued by the ruthless police inspector Javert (Russell Crowe). Valjean seeks redemption and a new life, but Javert is determined to capture him.

Valjean meets Bishop Myriel (Mark Addy), who shows him kindness and compassion, teaching him the value of humanity. Valjean vows to use his newfound wealth and influence for good, and he becomes a successful businessman and mayor of Montreuil-sur-Mer.

However, Javert's obsession with capturing Valjean continues, and he eventually tracks him down in Paris. Valjean is forced to flee, but not before he rescues a young girl named Fantine (Anne Hathaway), who is forced into prostitution to support her daughter Cosette.

Valjean promises to care for Cosette after Fantine's death, and he raises her as his own. As Cosette grows up, she falls in love with Marius Pontmercy (Eddie Redmayne), a young revolutionary who joins the student-led uprising against the French government.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Javert is killed by Valjean during a confrontation at the barricades during the June Rebellion. Meanwhile, Cosette and Marius are separated from each other, and Cosette becomes ill with tuberculosis.

In the end, Marius finds Cosette again, and they reunite. The film ends with the characters coming together to mourn the loss of Javert and to celebrate their newfound freedom and love for one another.

Throughout the film, the music plays a crucial role in conveying the emotions and themes of the story. The iconic songs, such as "I Dreamed a Dream," "Do You Hear the People Sing?," and "One Day More," bring depth and complexity to the characters and their struggles.

The film received widespread critical acclaim for its performances, direction, and music. Anne Hathaway's powerful performance in "I Dreamed a Dream" earned her an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress.

overview: Pu Songling, a legendary demon hunter, is asked to investigate the mysterious disappearances of young girls from a small village. When he discovers evil forces are kidnapping the girls to feast on their souls, he sets out to save humanity from the inhuman invasion journeying through hidden worlds and colorful dimensions.
title: The Knight of Shadows: Between Yin and Yang
plot:
The Knight of Shadows: Between Yin and Yang is a 2019 Chinese fantasy adventure film directed by Stephen Chow. 

The movie revolves around the story of a young orphan named Lin Xiao, who discovers he has magical powers that allow him to harness the energy of yin and yang. He becomes embroiled in a battle between good and evil forces vying for control over the world.

One of the main themes of The Knight of Shadows: Between Yin and Yang is the struggle between balance and chaos. Lin Xiao's journey represents the quest for balance within oneself, as he learns to harness his powers and navigate the complexities of the world around him. This theme is reflected in the film's use of yin and yang symbolism, which represents the harmonious interplay between opposing forces.

Another significant theme is the power of friendship and loyalty. Lin Xiao forms strong bonds with a group of allies who help him on his quest, demonstrating the importance of supportive relationships in overcoming adversity.

The movie also explores the idea of identity and self-discovery. As Lin Xiao navigates his newfound powers and confronts the challenges of the world, he must come to terms with his own sense of purpose and belonging.

Finally, The Knight of Shadows: Between Yin and Yang touches on the theme of good vs. evil, highlighting the complexities of moral ambiguity and the gray areas that exist between right and wrong.

Overall, the film offers a rich tapestry of themes and ideas, exploring the complexities of balance, friendship, identity, and morality in a fantastical and action-packed adventure.

overview: Starship C57D travels to planet Altair 4 in search of the crew of spaceship "Bellerophon," a scientific expedition that has been missing for 20 years, only to find themselves unwelcome by the expedition's lone survivor and warned of destruction by an invisible force if they don't turn back immediately.
tagline: Earthmen on a fabulous, peril-journey into outer space!
title: Forbidden Planet
plot:
Forbidden Planet is a science fiction film directed by Fred M. Wilcox, produced by Charles H. Schneer, and released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) in 1956.

The story begins with the crew of the spaceship C57D, led by Captain John J. Adams, receiving a distress signal from the planet Altair IV. The crew is sent to investigate and rescue any survivors. Upon arrival, they discover that the planet's surface is uninhabitable due to a toxic atmosphere. However, they soon realize that the real challenge lies within the planet's interior.

As the crew explores the planet, they come across an ancient temple dedicated to the goddess Caliban, who was once worshipped by the native inhabitants of Altair IV. The crew discovers a strange energy field surrounding the temple and decides to investigate further. They soon learn that the energy field is connected to the planet's unique properties and is believed to be the source of its deadly radiation.

The crew encounters various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, toxic gas, and malfunctioning equipment. As they delve deeper into the planet's interior, they begin to experience strange visions and hallucinations, which are later revealed to be caused by the energy field's effects on their minds.

One of the crew members, Dr. Edward Morbius, begins to exhibit unusual behavior, suggesting that he may have been affected by the energy field in a more profound way than initially thought. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Morbius has become possessed by the spirit of Caliban, who is seeking revenge against humanity for its treatment of her people.

The crew soon realizes that they must find a way to stop Morbius and escape the planet before it's too late. They discover that the only way to neutralize the energy field is to destroy the temple and sever the connection between the planet and Caliban's spirit.

In the climactic final act, the crew faces off against Morbius, who has become a vessel for Caliban's wrath. The captain and his crew must use all their skills and ingenuity to defeat Morbius and shatter the energy field, allowing them to escape the planet.

The film ends with the crew returning to Earth, where they are hailed as heroes for their bravery and ingenuity in overcoming the challenges of Altair IV. However, the ending also leaves room for interpretation, as some viewers may wonder if the crew truly escaped the planet's influence or if Morbius's spirit still lingers, waiting to be unleashed once again.

Overall, Forbidden Planet is a thought-provoking science fiction film that explores themes of identity, humanity, and the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control. The film's blend of adventure, suspense, and philosophical introspection has made it a classic of the genre, continuing to captivate audiences to this day.

original_title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
overview: This English-language adaptation of the Swedish novel by Stieg Larsson follows a disgraced journalist, Mikael Blomkvist, as he investigates the disappearance of a weary patriarch's niece from 40 years ago. He is aided by the pierced, tattooed, punk computer hacker named Lisbeth Salander. As they work together in the investigation, Blomkvist and Salander uncover immense corruption beyond anything they have ever imagined.
tagline: Evil shall with evil be expelled.
title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
plot:
The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is a 2011 psychological thriller film directed by David Fincher, based on the bestselling novel of the same name by Stieg Larsson. The movie stars Daniel Craig as Mikael Blomkvist, a journalist, and Rooney Mara as Lisbeth Salander, a young hacker.

The story begins with Mikael Blomkvist, a successful but troubled journalist who has lost his job due to an article he wrote that was deemed too critical of the wealthy elite. He is approached by Henrik Vanger, the patriarch of a wealthy family in Sweden, who hires him to investigate the disappearance of his niece, Harriet, 40 years ago.

Henrik believes that Harriet's disappearance is connected to an ancient family curse and asks Blomkvist to uncover the truth. As Blomkvist delves deeper into the case, he meets Lisbeth Salander, a brilliant but troubled young hacker who has been institutionalized for her mental health issues. Despite their initial reluctance, they form an unlikely partnership to solve the mystery.

As they dig deeper, they uncover a web of dark secrets and corruption within the Vanger family, including a possible murder that may be connected to Harriet's disappearance. Lisbeth's hacking skills prove invaluable in uncovering evidence that Blomkvist would have otherwise missed.

Throughout their investigation, Blomkvist and Lisbeth develop a complex and intense relationship, with Lisbeth's troubled past slowly revealed. They face numerous obstacles, including the family's attempts to silence them and Lisbeth's own demons.

As they get closer to the truth, they discover that Harriet was not just any ordinary victim but had been involved in some shady dealings within the family. The investigation leads them to a shocking revelation: Harriet's disappearance is linked to an ancient ritual that has been passed down through generations of Vangers.

In the climactic final act, Blomkvist and Lisbeth confront the mastermind behind the ritual, who is revealed to be Henrik himself. In a stunning twist, it is revealed that Henrik had orchestrated Harriet's murder to cover up his own dark secrets and protect the family's reputation.

The film ends with Blomkvist and Lisbeth finally solving the mystery, but not without scars. Lisbeth has found a sense of purpose and belonging with Blomkvist, while he has gained a new appreciation for her unique skills and perspective. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, with Lisbeth finally finding some measure of peace and acceptance.

Overall, The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is a gripping thriller that explores themes of corruption, power, and redemption. With its complex characters, intricate plot, and Fincher's masterful direction, it's no wonder this film has become a modern classic in the world of cinema.

overview: A journalist and podcaster from New York City travels to West Texas in order to report on the death of a girl he was hooking up with.
tagline: Find the story before it finds you.
title: Vengeance
plot:
Vengeance is a 2022 American black comedy thriller written and directed by B. J. Novak in his feature directorial debut. A neo-Western and neo-noir, it stars Novak as Ben Manalowitz, Boyd Holbrook as Ty Shaw, J. Smith-Cameron as Sharon Shaw, Lio Tipton as Abilene, Dove Cameron as Kansas City Shaw, Issa Rae as podcast producer Eloise and Ashton Kutcher as the record producer Quentin Sellers.

Ben Manalowitz is a New York journalist and aspiring podcaster who has had many casual relationships. One night he receives a call from a stranger, Ty Shaw, who tells him that Abilene "Abby" Shaw, a young woman Ben had briefly been involved with, has died of an apparent opioid overdose. Ty believes that Ben was Abby's boyfriend and insists that he come to the funeral in West Texas. Out of guilt and curiosity, Ben flies to the small town, where he meets Abby's warm and eccentric family: her mother Sharon, her sisters Paris and Kansas City, her younger brother and her grandmother.

Ty is convinced that Abby, who he claims never took drugs, was murdered, and asks Ben to help him find the killer and take revenge. Seeing an opportunity, Ben persuades his producer Eloise that the story could become a hit podcast about grief, conspiracy theories and the divide between urban and rural America. As he investigates, he meets local figures including a drug dealer suspected of involvement and Quentin Sellers, a philosophical record producer who gives Ben recordings of Abby's songs. Ben gradually grows attached to the family and begins to question his own condescension toward them, while he discovers that the truth about Abby's life and death is more complicated than either he or Ty expected.

The film satirizes the culture of true-crime podcasts and the mutual misunderstanding between coastal elites and small-town America, blending comedy with a genuine murder mystery.

Vengeance premiered at the Tribeca Festival on June 12, 2022, and was released in the United States by Focus Features on July 29, 2022. It received generally favorable reviews, with 81 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 65, and critics praised Novak's direction and screenplay.

original_title: In the Land of Blood and Honey
overview: During the Bosnian War, Danijel, a soldier fighting for the Serbs, re-encounters Ajla, a Bosnian who's now a captive in his camp he oversees. Their once promising connection has become ambiguous as their motives have changed.
tagline: Love can change what we want… war can change who we are
title: In the Land of Blood and Honey
plot:
In the Land of Blood and Honey is a 2011 war drama film that explores the complexities of human nature during times of conflict. The movie delves into the theme of love amidst war, highlighting the resilience of the human spirit in the face of unimaginable violence.

The story revolves around two characters, Danica (played by Zana Marjanovic), a Bosnian Serb woman, and Ajla (played by Goran Kostic), a Bosniak man. Their relationship is forbidden due to their conflicting ethnic backgrounds, yet they find solace in each other's company amidst the chaos of war.

The film critiques the senseless violence and brutality that often accompanies conflict, particularly in the context of the Bosnian War. It portrays the devastating effects of war on civilians, including women and children, who are often caught in the crossfire.

Through Danica and Ajla's story, the movie sheds light on the human cost of war, where individuals are reduced to mere pawns in a larger game of politics and power struggles. The film also touches upon themes of identity, loyalty, and survival, as characters navigate the treacherous landscape of war-torn Bosnia.

Ultimately, In the Land of Blood and Honey is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the harsh realities of war and its impact on individuals and communities.

overview: Trying to put her life back together after the death of her husband, Libby and her children move to her estranged Aunt's goat farm in central Texas.
tagline: It's never too late to find yourself.
title: The Lost Husband
plot:
The Lost Husband is a 2020 American romantic drama written and directed by Vicky Wight, based on Katherine Center's 2013 novel of the same name. Leslie Bibb stars as Libby, a widowed mother, with Josh Duhamel as the farm manager James O'Connor, Nora Dunn as her Aunt Jean, Herizen F. Guardiola and Kevin Alejandro. Quiver Distribution and Redbox Entertainment released it on video on demand on 10 April 2020.

After the death of her husband in a car accident, Libby, a single mother with two children, Abby and Tank, moves to her eccentric Aunt Jean's goat farm in central Texas in search of a fresh start. Jean puts her to work and asks James, her laconic farm manager, to teach Libby the ropes. Libby is reluctant, but she needs the job and accepts. Little by little, she and the children adjust to rural life. Libby learns to milk goats and run the farm, and despite their early friction she begins to bond with James, who also becomes a friend to the children, playing with Tank and teaching Abby to defend herself against a bully who mocks the limp she has had since the accident that killed her father.

When Abby is suspended for punching the boy, Libby is angry with James for teaching her karate, but she realizes that her daughter confided in him because she was afraid of adding to her mother's stress. The family also gets to know Jean's boyfriend, Russ, and his granddaughter Sunshine, who takes Libby to an abandoned house that once belonged to Jean and her late husband, Frank, and encourages her to try to communicate with her own dead husband. As Libby gradually confronts her grief and the unresolved feelings about her marriage, her relationship with James deepens, and she must also face difficult truths in her family, and decides whether she is ready to open her heart again and build a new life in Texas.

The film received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes 55 percent of 22 reviews were positive, with a consensus saying it would not set hearts aflutter for anyone but dedicated romantics, though audiences in the mood for love might enjoy it. Tara McNamara of Common Sense Media gave it three stars out of five, and Brian Tallerico of RogerEbert.com gave it two and a half stars, with critics generally praising the chemistry between Bibb and Duhamel.

overview: On a cold Christmas Eve, selfish miser Ebenezer Scrooge has one night left to face his past — and change the future — before time runs out.
title: Scrooge: A Christmas Carol
plot:
Scrooge: A Christmas Carol is a 2022 animated musical fantasy film directed by Stephen Donnelly and produced by Timeless Films, an animated reimagining of the 1970 musical Scrooge by Leslie Bricusse, itself based on Charles Dickens's 1843 novella A Christmas Carol. Luke Evans voices Ebenezer Scrooge, with Olivia Colman, Jessie Buckley, Jonathan Pryce, Johnny Flynn, Fra Fee, James Cosmo and Trevor Dion Nicholas. Dedicated to Bricusse, who died in 2021, it opened in select cinemas on November 18, 2022, before reaching Netflix on December 2.

On Christmas Eve 1843 in London, the miserly moneylender Scrooge, accompanied by his friendly mastiff Prudence, dodges his cheerful nephew Harry, refuses a donation to charity and adds to the debt of the toy-shop owner Tom Jenkins, who borrowed to pay for his mother's medical care. Scrooge resents Harry because his beloved sister Jen died giving birth to him. He grudgingly gives his underpaid clerk, Bob Cratchit, Christmas Day off; the Cratchits live in poverty, and their youngest son, Tiny Tim, is seriously ill and cannot afford treatment.

At home Scrooge is visited by the ghost of his late partner Jacob Marley, Prudence's former owner, who taught him to be ruthless and now drags the chains of his misdeeds. Marley warns Scrooge of the same fate and announces three visitors. The first, Past, a shifting, wax-like spirit, shows Scrooge how his father's imprisonment for debt forced him to support his mother and sister, his happy years working for the kindly Mr. Fezziwig, and his engagement to Fezziwig's daughter Isabel, which ended after Scrooge joined Marley and helped close the bakery that was Bob's childhood home.

The second spirit, the joyful giant Present, shows Harry's affection for his uncle and the Cratchits' grateful celebration in their cramped home. The third, Yet to Come, shows Tom leading a celebration that Scrooge first takes as praise, until he learns it is a reaction to his own death, that Tiny Tim has died and that almost no one mourns him. Glimpsing the afterlife that awaits him, Scrooge vows to change.

Waking on Christmas morning, he makes peace with Isabel's new life and throws a party, cancelling Tom's debt, giving to the charity, presenting Harry with a Father Christmas doll made by Jen and making Bob his business partner. Critics were divided, with 40% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and criticism of the animation and songs.

overview: A psychological, heart-wrenching love story that provides a unique and inside look at Charles Darwin. Torn between faith and science, he struggles to finish his legendary book "On the Origin of the Species," which goes on to become the foundation for evolutionary biology.
title: Creation
plot:
Creation is a 2009 biographical drama film directed by Jonny Lee Miller, based on the life of Scottish biologist James Watson and his role in discovering the structure of DNA.

The main themes of Creation include:

1. The ethics of scientific discovery: The film explores the moral implications of Watson's discovery, particularly with regards to its potential impact on humanity. Watson's character grapples with the consequences of his work, including the possibility that it could be used for destructive purposes.
2. The complexities of human relationships: The film delves into the complex and often tumultuous relationship between Watson and his wife, Frances (played by Miranda Richardson). Their marriage is portrayed as a troubled one, with both partners struggling to connect on an emotional level.
3. The tension between scientific curiosity and personal responsibility: Watson's character is driven by a desire to understand the fundamental nature of life, but this obsession comes at a cost to his relationships and overall well-being. The film suggests that scientists must balance their pursuit of knowledge with a sense of responsibility towards others.
4. The struggle for recognition and respect: Watson's discovery is initially met with skepticism and dismissal by some in the scientific community, highlighting the challenges faced by individuals who challenge conventional wisdom.

Overall, Creation offers a nuanced portrayal of James Watson's life, exploring the complexities of his character and the moral dilemmas he faces as a result of his groundbreaking work.

original_title: Scooby-Doo! & Batman: The Brave and the Bold
overview: Scooby-Doo and the Mystery Inc. gang meet up with Batman and other friends to defeat evil villains and save the day.
title: Scooby-Doo! & Batman: The Brave and the Bold
plot:
Scooby-Doo! & Batman: The Brave and the Bold is an animated television series that brings together two beloved franchises, Scooby-Doo and Batman. At its core, this show explores the idea of unlikely friendships and partnerships between characters from different worlds.

The main theme of the series revolves around the concept of teamwork and collaboration. The show's protagonists, Fred Jones (Scooby-Doo), Daphne Blake, Velma Dinkley, Shaggy Rogers, and Scooby-Doo, team up with Batman and his allies to solve mysteries and defeat villains. This partnership allows for a unique blend of humor, action, and detective work.

The series also delves into the idea of embracing one's true identity and finding belonging. The characters from both franchises often struggle with their own identities and find themselves in situations where they must navigate unfamiliar worlds and meet new people. Through these experiences, they learn to accept and appreciate each other's differences, ultimately forming strong bonds and friendships.

Furthermore, the show touches on themes of trust, loyalty, and responsibility. As the characters work together to solve mysteries, they must also rely on each other to stay safe and overcome challenges. This emphasis on teamwork and mutual support creates a sense of camaraderie among the characters, making their adventures all the more exciting and engaging.

Overall, Scooby-Doo! & Batman: The Brave and the Bold is a heartwarming and entertaining series that celebrates the power of friendship, collaboration, and embracing one's true identity.

overview: A summer fling born under the Sicilian sun quickly develops into a heartbreaking love story that forces a boy and girl to grow up too quickly.
title: Caught by a Wave
plot:
Caught by a Wave (Italian: Sulla stessa onda) is a 2021 Italian coming-of-age romantic drama directed by Massimiliano Camaiti in his directorial debut, from a screenplay he wrote with Claudia Bottino. Produced by Cinemaundici with Mediaset, it was one of five Italian films announced in October 2019 under a production agreement between Mediaset and Netflix. Elvira Camarrone and Christian Roberto star as Sara and Lorenzo, with Donatella Finocchiaro as Susanna, Corrado Invernizzi as Boris, Vincenzo Amato as Antonio and Manuela Ventura as Tuccia.

During a summer sailing course in Sicily, sixteen-year-old Sara, a talented sailor with a promising future, meets seventeen-year-old Lorenzo, one of the instructors, and the two quickly fall in love. During a sailing session, however, Sara's muscles go numb: she suffers from muscular dystrophy, a degenerative disease that is rapidly getting worse, and what begins as a leg cramp soon turns into a full rehabilitation program. Unwilling to be pitied or to spoil their summer romance, she hides her illness from Lorenzo, but the truth eventually comes out. After a perceived betrayal, a painful breakup and a reconciliation, the young couple struggles to cope with the pain while keeping their love alive, winning over Sara's initially wary parents along the way. A death among the patients in Sara's rehab program brings home the seriousness of her condition. Meanwhile, the sailing school prepares for an upcoming regatta, and despite the risk to her health, Sara insists on competing with Lorenzo; their boat capsizes during the race, but they still finish third. A coda set months later suggests that Sara has died, as Lorenzo receives her necklace and mourns her.

Filming lasted six weeks in Sicily, between San Vito Lo Capo, near Monte Cofano, and Palermo, including its historic center and the port area of La Cala. The trailer was released on 24 February 2021, and the film premiered on Netflix on 25 March 2021, with an English dub featuring Anne Yatco and Josh Zuckerman. Reviews were modest. Ready Steady Cut called it a pleasant, low-risk teen romance, refreshingly understated and resistant to emotional manipulation, with likable and natural young leads, but found the relationship rushed by the pacing and editing and the regatta subplot tacked on, while noting the story was reportedly drawn in part from the director's own life. Other critics also found it gentle but underdeveloped.

overview: A group of career criminals finds itself trapped in a warehouse with the law – and an Attack Dog named DeNiro closing in.
title: Bullet Head
plot:
Bullet Head is a 2017 American action thriller film directed by Paul McGuigan. The movie follows three prisoners - Frank, Jimmy, and Turk - who are brought together to participate in a prison's "Bullet Head" program, where they must work together to solve a murder mystery.
