Sam's boss and former lover Conall joins them with a plan to escape to Spain by ferry, but he is killed when gunmen storm their hotel, and Sam kills two attackers in a brutal fight. Without passports, Sam and Zoe go to the company's headquarters and see Rima meeting one of the suspicious men. Following him to a marina, Sam kills him and discovers that he was a policeman with Rima's access codes to the house's security system, leading them to suspect her.

Sheltering in the abandoned house, Zoe learns that Sam gave up a child for adoption as a teenager. Rima, alerted that her login is being used, abandons the signing and flies in, revealing that Sikong has been blackmailing her and that she never ordered the attacks. Corrupt officers and mercenaries attack, and Sam and Zoe save her. Sam heads home, promising to call her daughter. Reviews were mixed, with 35% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

original_title: 僕のヒーローアカデミア THE MOVIE ワールド ヒーローズ ミッション
overview: A mysterious group called Humarize strongly believes in the Quirk Singularity Doomsday theory which states that when quirks get mixed further in with future generations, that power will bring forth the end of humanity. In order to save everyone, the Pro-Heroes around the world ask UA Academy heroes-in-training to assist them and form a world-class selected hero team. It’s up to the heroes to save the world and the future of heroes in what is the most dangerous crisis to take place yet in My Hero Academia.
tagline: Their fight is our future.
title: My Hero Academia: World Heroes' Mission
plot:
My Hero Academia: World Heroes' Mission is a 2021 Japanese animated superhero film based on an original story featuring the characters of Kōhei Horikoshi's manga My Hero Academia. Produced by Bones and distributed by Toho, the third film in the franchise was directed by Kenji Nagasaki from a script by Yōsuke Kuroda and features the voices of Daiki Yamashita as Izuku Midoriya, Nobuhiko Okamoto as Katsuki Bakugo and Yuki Kaji as Shoto Todoroki.

In a world where most people are born with superpowers called Quirks, a doomsday cult called Humarise believes that Quirks will eventually become so powerful that they will destroy humanity. Led by Flect Turn, the cult plants bombs around the world filled with Trigger gas, which drives the Quirks of anyone exposed out of control until they die, intending to wipe out all Quirk users. After the first bomb is detonated, the World Heroes Association dispatches professional heroes and students from U.A. High School to locations around the globe in an attempt to stop the attacks.

Izuku, Bakugo and Todoroki are sent with their mentor Endeavor to Otheon, the country believed to house Humarise's headquarters. While pursuing a jewel thief, Izuku encounters Rody Soul, a street-smart young courier struggling to support his younger siblings. When Rody accidentally picks up a briefcase containing important information stolen from Humarise, Izuku is framed for mass murder by the corrupt local police, who are secretly working for the cult. Forced to go on the run with Rody, Izuku must learn to trust the cynical boy and protect him from the cult's assassins, while Bakugo and Todoroki lead the effort to stop Flect Turn's plan before the remaining bombs can be detonated.

The film expands the series' world beyond Japan and explores themes of trust, prejudice and responsibility, with Rody's relationship with Izuku at its emotional center.

World Heroes' Mission was released in Japan on August 6, 2021, and in the United States and Canada by Funimation on October 29, 2021. It grossed about 47 million dollars worldwide and was one of the highest-grossing domestic films of the year in Japan. It received generally positive reviews, with 87 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: When Isabelle and Theo invite Matthew to stay with them, what begins as a casual friendship ripens into a sensual voyage of discovery and desire in which nothing is off limits and everything is possible.
tagline: Together nothing is impossible. Together nothing is forbidden.
title: The Dreamers
plot:
The Dreamers is a 2003 French drama film directed by Bernardo Bertolucci, written by Bernardo Bertolucci and Daniele Luchetti, and starring Louis Garrel, Michael Pitt, and Eva Green.

The story takes place in Paris during World War II. The film revolves around the lives of three young people: Christian (Louis Garrel), a 17-year-old Frenchman who is struggling to come to terms with his family's past; Marco (Michael Pitt), an American teenager who has escaped from a concentration camp and is living with Christian's family; and Isabelle (Eva Green), Christian's sister, who is a beautiful and alluring young woman.

The film begins in 1940, when Christian's father, a French Resistance fighter, is killed by the Nazis. Christian's mother, a widow, takes him and his sister to live with their uncle, Marcel (Denis Podalydès), a professor at the Sorbonne who has been hiding Jewish students from the Nazis.

As the war intensifies, Marco arrives at the family's home, seeking refuge from the concentration camp where he was being held. Christian is initially wary of Marco, but eventually warms up to him and introduces him to his sister Isabelle. The three form a close bond, and their lives become intertwined as they navigate the dangers of living under Nazi occupation.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Christian's father, who was killed by the Nazis for his Resistance activities. We also see glimpses of Marcel's past, including his relationship with Isabelle, which is complicated by her involvement with a young Jewish man named David (Léa Seydoux).

Throughout the film, Bertolucci explores themes of love, loss, and survival in the face of war and oppression. Christian, Marco, and Isabelle form a tight-knit family unit, supporting each other through the hardships of living under Nazi rule.

As the Allies begin to gain ground against the Nazis, the three young people find themselves caught up in the excitement and uncertainty of the final days of the war. In the film's climax, Christian, Marco, and Isabelle are forced to confront their own mortality as they face the reality of the war's end.

The Dreamers is a powerful and poignant film that explores the complexities of human relationships during times of war and social upheaval. The performances by Garrel, Pitt, and Green are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters. Bertolucci's direction is masterful, weaving together multiple storylines and themes into a cohesive and emotionally resonant whole.

Overall, The Dreamers is a moving and thought-provoking film that explores the human cost of war and the power of love and relationships in the face of adversity.

overview: A plane is taken over by a mysterious virus. When the plane lands it is placed under quarantine. Now a group of survivors must band together to survive the quarantine.
tagline: The most deadly mutant virus just went airborne... and escape is not an option.
title: Quarantine 2: Terminal
plot:
Quarantine 2: Terminal is a Spanish horror film that explores the theme of isolation and confinement. The movie takes place in an abandoned airport, where a group of survivors must navigate through the treacherous environment while being stalked by a mysterious figure.

The main theme of Quarantine 2: Terminal revolves around the psychological effects of isolation on the human mind. As the characters are trapped in the airport, they begin to experience hallucinations, paranoia, and a breakdown of social norms, leading to a descent into chaos and terror.

Throughout the film, the audience is also presented with the theme of claustrophobia, as the characters are confined to a small space with no escape. This creates a sense of tension and unease, as the characters' fear of being trapped becomes a constant presence in their lives.

Furthermore, Quarantine 2: Terminal touches on the idea of the breakdown of social order in the face of catastrophic events. As society collapses, the characters are forced to fend for themselves, leading to a struggle for survival that is both primal and terrifying.

Overall, Quarantine 2: Terminal is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores the darker aspects of human nature when faced with isolation and confinement.

overview: In the near future, due to a breakthrough scientific discovery by Dr. Thomas Harbor, there is now definitive proof of an afterlife. While countless people have chosen suicide to reset their existence, others try to decide what it all means. Among them is Dr. Harbor's son Will, who has arrived at his father's isolated compound with a mysterious young woman named Isla. There, they discover the strange acolytes who help Dr. Harbor with his experiments.
title: The Discovery
plot:
The Discovery is a 2017 American science fiction film directed by Charlie McDowell and written by Justin Marks. The movie stars Robert Redford, Rooney Mara, and Jason Bateman.

The main themes of The Discovery revolve around the concept of immortality through cryonic preservation and the moral implications that come with it. The story follows Dr. Norman Goodman (played by Robert Redford), a scientist who has discovered a way to preserve human consciousness after death, allowing people to be revived in the future when technology allows for it.

The film explores several themes:

1. **Immortality and its consequences**: The movie delves into the idea of immortality and what it means to live forever. As people are preserved and revived, they begin to experience a loss of connection with their loved ones who have passed away, leading to emotional turmoil.
2. **Human connection and relationships**: The Discovery highlights the importance of human connections and relationships in our lives. As people are frozen and later revived, they struggle to form new relationships or reconnect with those who have moved on without them.
3. **Free will and personal identity**: The film raises questions about free will and personal identity. If a person's consciousness is preserved, do they still retain their sense of self, or do they become something new?
4. **The ethics of cryonic preservation**: The movie touches on the moral implications of preserving human consciousness after death. Is it right to revive people who have passed away, potentially disrupting the natural order of life and death?

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together to create a thought-provoking narrative that challenges viewers to consider the consequences of playing God with human life.

Overall, The Discovery is a complex and introspective film that explores the complexities of human existence, relationships, and what it means to be alive.

overview: A man accidentally gets into a time machine and travels back in time nearly an hour. Finding himself will be the first of a series of disasters of unforeseeable consequences.
tagline: A trip back in time from the present to...
title: Timecrimes
plot:
Timecrimes is a Spanish science fiction thriller film that delves into the complexities of time travel and its consequences on human relationships. The movie follows Héctor, a young man who becomes embroiled in a series of events after he encounters a mysterious woman with whom he shares a brief but intense connection.

As Héctor navigates his way through this complex web of time, he begins to question the nature of reality and his own identity. He finds himself reliving the same day over and over again, each iteration bringing new challenges and opportunities for growth. Through Héctor's experiences, the film explores themes of repetition, free will, and the consequences of playing with the fabric of time.

One of the primary concerns of Timecrimes is the idea that our actions have unintended repercussions, and that even the smallest decisions can have far-reaching effects on those around us. As Héctor struggles to make sense of his situation, he must confront the possibility that his interactions with others may be influenced by events that have not yet occurred.

The film also touches on the theme of loneliness and isolation, as Héctor's experiences leave him feeling disconnected from the world around him. His relationships with others are marked by a sense of urgency and desperation, as if he is racing against time to make amends or find connection in a world that seems determined to keep him at arm's length.

Ultimately, Timecrimes presents a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that raises questions about the nature of time, identity, and our place within the world. Through its complex narrative and atmospheric tension, the film invites viewers to consider the consequences of playing with the fundamental forces of reality.

overview: In a Russian coastal town, Kolya is forced to fight the corrupt mayor when he is told that his house will be demolished. He recruits a lawyer friend to help, but the man's arrival brings further misfortune for Kolya and his family.
title: Leviathan
plot:
Leviathan is a 2014 American drama film directed by Sam Taylor-Johnson. The movie revolves around a young couple, Rebecca and Brian, who are struggling to make ends meet in New York City. They take on a job as the caretakers of a luxurious apartment building, only to discover that it's inhabited by a reclusive billionaire, Mr. Johnson.

As they delve deeper into their new lives, they uncover dark secrets about the building and its inhabitants, leading them down a rabbit hole of corruption, greed, and moral decay. The film explores themes of class struggle, social inequality, and the corrupting influence of wealth and power.

Through the characters' experiences, the movie critiques the excesses of capitalism and the ways in which it can lead to exploitation and oppression. It also touches on issues of identity, community, and the search for meaning in a seemingly soulless urban environment.

The film's title, Leviathan, refers to the biblical sea monster, symbolizing the monstrous nature of unchecked power and corruption. The movie builds towards a climactic confrontation between the characters and the forces of oppression, ultimately revealing the true extent of Mr. Johnson's sinister plans.

Overall, Leviathan is a thought-provoking drama that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of allowing greed and ambition to consume us.

overview: After a failed sabotage mission, a trio of anti-apartheid freedom fighters ends up in a tense bank hostage situation. Based on a true story.
tagline: Freedom is a fight.
title: Silverton Siege
plot:
Silverton Siege is a 2022 South African action thriller directed by Mandla Dube and inspired by the real Silverton bank siege of January 1980 in Pretoria, in which members of uMkhonto we Sizwe, the armed wing of the African National Congress, took hostages in a bank. Thabo Rametsi, Noxolo Dlamini and Stefan Erasmus star as the three freedom fighters, with Arnold Vosloo as the police captain pursuing them and Tumisho Masha. The film was released internationally on Netflix on 27 April 2022.

Calvin Khumalo, Terra Mabunda and Aldo Erasmus are anti-apartheid guerrillas in MK planning to sabotage a fuel depot outside Silverton, a suburb of Pretoria. Their mission is foiled because the security police, led by Captain Langerman, have been tipped off. Forced to abort, they flee toward the city; after Terra's partner Masego is shot and their van disabled, they escape through sewer tunnels and emerge in the heart of Pretoria near Church Square. Spotted by police, they take refuge inside a branch of the Volkskas Bank.

Calvin addresses the frightened customers and staff, explaining that the group is not there to rob the bank and asking for calm cooperation so that no one is hurt. Christine, a bank supervisor, proves helpful and sympathetic. Police surround the building, and when Langerman calls each of the fighters by name over a loudhailer, they become convinced that there is an informant inside their organization. They demand a helicopter with an unarmed black pilot, intending to take a hostage with them, but an attempted escape to the helicopter turns out to be a trap, and everyone returns to the bank. As the standoff grows tense and the world's press gathers outside, the fighters change strategy, using the media attention to demand the release of Nelson Mandela, who was then imprisoned, turning the siege into a political statement against apartheid while the police prepare to storm the building.

The film received mixed to positive reviews, with a 75 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on eight reviews. Critics praised the performances of the three leads, which gave the characters depth and complex motivations, especially during the tense standoff, although some noted that the film fictionalizes important elements of the historical events.

overview: In the year 1215, the rebel barons of England have forced their despised King John to put his royal seal on the Magna Carta, a seminal document that upheld the rights of free men. Yet within months of pledging himself to the great charter, the King reneged on his word and assembled a mercenary army on the south coast of England with the intention of bringing the barons and the country back under his tyrannical rule. Barring his way stood the mighty Rochester castle, a place that would become the symbol of the rebel's momentous struggle for justice and freedom.
production_companies: Film & Entertainment VIP Medienfonds 4 GmbH & Co. KG (I)
tagline: Heavy metal goes medieval.
title: Ironclad
plot:
Ironclad is a 2011 historical action film directed by Jonathan Hensleigh and starring Paul Giamatti, Stephen Rea, and Brian Cox.

The main themes of Ironclad revolve around:

1. **Loyalty vs. Duty**: The story explores the conflict between personal loyalty to one's lord and duty to fulfill a greater obligation. Sir William Marshall (Paul Giamatti) is torn between his loyalty to King John (Brian Cox) and his duty to protect the people of Rochester.
2. **Power struggles**: The film highlights the power struggles within the royal court, particularly between King John and his nobles. This struggle for power leads to a series of events that ultimately threaten the kingdom.
3. **Personal sacrifice**: Throughout the story, characters are forced to make difficult choices and sacrifices in order to protect others or fulfill their duties. Sir William Marshall's character is a prime example of this theme.
4. **Corruption and abuse of power**: The film critiques the corrupt and abusive nature of King John's rule, highlighting the negative consequences of his actions on the people of Rochester.

The plot development revolves around the siege of Rochester Castle by King John's forces, led by Sir William Marshall. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the king's intentions are not entirely pure, and that he is willing to do whatever it takes to assert his power.

In the end, Sir William Marshall must make a choice between his loyalty to the king and his duty to protect the people of Rochester. The film culminates in a dramatic showdown between the two forces, with the fate of the kingdom hanging in the balance.

Overall, Ironclad is a gripping historical drama that explores themes of loyalty, power struggles, personal sacrifice, and corruption, set against the backdrop of a pivotal moment in English history.

overview: When a small Colorado town is overrun by the flesh hungry dead, a small group of survivors try to escape in a last ditch effort to stay alive.
tagline: D-Day Is Coming.
title: Day of the Dead
plot:
Day of the Dead is a 2008 American horror film directed by Steve Miner and written by Jeffrey Reddick, a loose remake of George A. Romero's 1985 film, the third in his Dead series. Mena Suvari stars as an army corporal, with Nick Cannon, Michael Welch, AnnaLynne McCord, Stark Sands and Ving Rhames. Shot mainly in Bulgaria, with a few scenes filmed in Los Angeles, it was released direct to video by First Look Studios on April 8, 2008.

In a small Colorado town, the military seals off the roads for what is announced as a twenty-four-hour quarantine exercise, while an influenza-like illness spreads among the residents. Corporal Sarah Bowman, a local, leaves her checkpoint with Private Bud Crain to look in on her sick mother, and runs into her teenage brother Trevor and his girlfriend Nina, who tell her that a friend has been bleeding from the nose. At the friend's house, Sarah and Bud find his parents savagely mauled, and Sarah reports to Captain Rhodes before taking her family to the overcrowded medical centre.

As a CDC doctor, Dr. Logan, questions her, the sick suddenly fall still and then rise as ravenous, fast-moving zombies, and the hospital becomes a slaughterhouse. Trevor and Nina escape to the local radio station, Rhodes is torn apart, and Sarah, Bud and Logan barricade themselves in a storeroom. Crawling through the air ducts to recover the keys to Rhodes's Humvee, they meet Private Salazar, and Bud is bitten by the reanimated Rhodes. The survivors jump from a window into the car park, where the cowardly Logan sacrifices a woman to save himself and drives off alone.

Bud turns, but unlike the others he remains docile, and Sarah insists he be spared. Responding to Trevor's call over the radio, the group rescues the couple but crashes their vehicle near a derelict building, which hides an underground military laboratory. There they find Logan, who confesses that he worked on a government project led by Dr. Engel to create a biological weapon that would temporarily paralyse enemy soldiers; the virus mutated and turned the scientists into zombies.

Engel, now one of the undead, kills Logan, and Salazar dies holding back a horde so that the others can escape. The survivors rig gas canisters into flamethrowers, and when Engel ambushes Sarah, Bud shoots and is decapitated by him. Sarah lures the zombies to the canisters and they are burned alive. The film was panned, with a 13% Rotten Tomatoes rating and criticism of its script and performances.

overview: On May 9, 1986, a small ranching community in Wyoming experiences a divine intervention when a couple detonates a bomb inside a crowded classroom.
tagline: Based on actual events.
title: The Cokeville Miracle
plot:
The Cokeville Miracle is a 2015 American drama film directed by Michael L. Wilson and produced by Remember Films.

The movie is based on a true story and revolves around the 1980 standoff between two brothers, Brian Deneke and Eric Deneke, at their family's church in Cokeville, Wyoming. The plot begins with the arrival of a stranger, who is later revealed to be a cult leader, at the church. The stranger demands that the children be released from school and that the parents surrender their guns.

As the standoff unfolds, tensions rise between the two brothers, Brian and Eric, who are forced to confront each other in order to protect their family. Brian, who is initially hesitant to take action, eventually becomes the leader of the group and takes charge of defending his family against the cult leader's demands.

Throughout the film, themes of faith, family, and redemption are explored. The movie highlights the importance of standing up for what one believes in, even in the face of adversity, as well as the power of forgiveness and reconciliation.

The main characters, Brian and Eric Deneke, undergo significant personal growth throughout the ordeal, learning valuable lessons about leadership, sacrifice, and the true meaning of family. The film ultimately ends on a hopeful note, with the brothers emerging from their experience stronger and more united than ever before.

Overall, The Cokeville Miracle is a powerful and inspiring drama that explores themes of faith, family, and redemption in the face of adversity.

overview: After winning his first competition, Takumi focuses his attention on drift racing, a sport he has unknowingly perfected while delivering tofu in his father's Toyota AE86.
title: Initial D
plot:
Initial D is a 2005 Japanese sports drama film that revolves around the story of Takumi Fujiwara, an aspiring street racing driver who becomes involved in a rivalry with a group of drivers from the Hokkaido region. The movie explores themes of passion, dedication, and perseverance as Takumi navigates his way through the world of street racing.

At its core, Initial D is a film about the pursuit of one's dreams and the importance of staying true to oneself. Takumi's journey is not just about winning races, but also about finding his place in the world and understanding what drives him. The movie delves into the emotional struggles of its characters as they face setbacks, disappointments, and personal losses.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. As Takumi becomes more involved in the racing scene, he is forced to confront his own strengths and weaknesses, and to question whether his passion for street racing aligns with his true values and aspirations.

Furthermore, Initial D explores the idea of community and camaraderie among its characters. The relationships between the drivers are complex and multifaceted, reflecting the bonds that form when people come together around a shared passion. The movie highlights the importance of loyalty, trust, and mutual respect in these relationships.

Overall, Initial D is a film about the human spirit, with all its complexities and contradictions. It is a story about chasing one's dreams, staying true to oneself, and finding meaning in life through the pursuit of passion and purpose.

overview: A sea turtle who was hatched in 1959 spends the next 50 years traveling the world while it is being changed by global warming. Born on a Baja, California beach in 1959, new hatchling Sammy must do what his fellow newborn sea turtles are doing: race across the beach to the ocean before they are captured by a seagull or crab. Thus begins Sammy's incredible fifty-year ocean journey. Along the way he meets his best friend, a fellow turtle named Ray, and overcomes obstacles both natural and man-made while trying to fulfill his dream of travelling around the world. Throughout his voyage, Sammy never forgets about Shelly - the turtle he saved on his first day and loves passionately from afar.
tagline: Hatch Me If You Can
title: A Turtle's Tale: Sammy's Adventures
plot:
A Turtle's Tale: Sammy's Adventures is a 3D computer-animated adventure comedy film directed by Ben Stassen and Frédéric Back, produced by Motion Investment Group. The movie follows the story of Sammy, a sea turtle who dreams of exploring the world above the water.

The main themes of A Turtle's Tale: Sammy's Adventures include:

1. **Perseverance and determination**: Sammy faces numerous obstacles on his journey, but he never gives up on his dream to explore the world above the water. His perseverance ultimately leads him to achieve his goal.
2. **Friendship and loyalty**: Sammy befriends a young boy named Hugo, who helps him on his adventure. Their friendship is built on trust, loyalty, and mutual support.
3. **Self-discovery**: Throughout his journey, Sammy learns more about himself and the world around him. He discovers new things about his own identity and the importance of following one's dreams.
4. **Environmentalism**: The movie touches on the theme of environmentalism, highlighting the impact of human activities on marine life and ecosystems.

The plot development of the movie follows Sammy's journey as he leaves his home in the ocean to explore the world above the water. Along the way, he faces various challenges, including treacherous terrain, predators, and humans who threaten his existence. Despite these obstacles, Sammy perseveres and eventually finds a way to return to his home.

The ending of the movie is heartwarming, as Sammy returns to his home in the ocean, but not before sharing his incredible journey with Hugo and inspiring others to follow their dreams. The film concludes on a hopeful note, emphasizing the importance of friendship, perseverance, and self-discovery.

overview: In the 1930s, a young reverend and his family are forced to confront their worst fears when they discover their new home holds a horrifying secret.
tagline: Some houses were never meant to be a home
title: The Banishing
plot:
The Banishing is a 2021 British supernatural horror film directed by Justin Benson and Aaron Moorhead, written by Benson and Moorhead, and produced by WestEnd Films. 

The story revolves around a group of friends who reunite for a weekend at their old boarding school in the English countryside. The main character, Sarah (played by Jessica Brown Findlay), is struggling to cope with her recent past experiences, including the loss of her mother and her own mental health issues.

Upon arrival, they discover that the school has been abandoned for years due to a tragic event involving one of their former students who died under mysterious circumstances. The group decides to spend the weekend exploring the old building and catching up on each other's lives.

As night falls, strange occurrences start to happen - doors slam shut, objects move on their own, and ghostly apparitions appear. At first, they dismiss these events as mere hallucinations or the product of a vivid imagination, but soon it becomes clear that something supernatural is at play.

The group discovers that the school's dark past is connected to an ancient ritual performed by one of the former students, which awakened a malevolent entity. The entity feeds on fear and begins to manipulate the group members, causing them to turn against each other.

As tensions rise, Sarah starts to unravel the mystery behind the school's dark history and the true nature of the entity. She also delves deeper into her own past, discovering that she has a personal connection to the tragedy that occurred at the school.

The film builds up to a climactic confrontation between Sarah and the entity, which forces her to confront her deepest fears and make a choice between saving herself or saving others. The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just a product of Sarah's imagination.

Throughout the film, Benson and Moorhead explore themes of trauma, grief, and the power of friendship in the face of adversity. They also pay homage to classic horror movies, incorporating elements of folk horror and supernatural terror.

Overall, The Banishing is a tense, atmospheric horror film that masterfully crafts a sense of unease and uncertainty. With its slow-burning tension and eerie atmosphere, it's sure to appeal to fans of psychological horror and supernatural thrillers.

overview: A mild-mannered bank executive (Aaron Eckhart) mentors a teenage con artist and tries to make a career change as a doughnut merchant.
tagline: A comedy about someone you know.
title: Meet Bill
plot:
Meet Bill is a 2007 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Jay Roach and written by Mike White. The movie follows the story of a young man, Alex, who falls in love with a woman named Emily, but his life is disrupted when he meets Bill, a charismatic and mysterious figure from his past.

The main theme of Meet Bill revolves around the idea of identity and how it can be shaped by our experiences and relationships. The film explores the complexities of human connection and how people can become lost in their own identities. Through Alex's journey, the movie delves into the concept of self-discovery and the struggle to find one's place in the world.

The character of Bill serves as a catalyst for Alex's growth, forcing him to confront his past and re-evaluate his relationships with others. The film also touches on themes of love, loss, and redemption, highlighting the complexities of human emotions and the power of relationships to shape our lives.

Ultimately, Meet Bill is a poignant exploration of how people can become stuck in their own identities and how it takes courage and vulnerability to break free from these patterns and forge new connections with others. The movie's nuanced portrayal of complex themes makes for a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant viewing experience.

overview: Kenneth Feinberg, a powerful D.C. lawyer appointed Special Master of the 9/11 Fund, fights off the cynicism, bureaucracy, and politics associated with administering government funds and, in doing so, discovers what life is worth.
tagline: Our national tragedy. Their personal suffering. His impossible task.
title: Worth
plot:
Worth is a 2021 American drama film directed by Darin Moiselle and written by Steven Conrad. The movie tells the story of Dean Whiting, a lawyer who represents a group of 9/11 first responders who are struggling to receive fair compensation for their medical expenses.

The main theme of Worth revolves around the struggle for justice and the human cost of war. The film highlights the plight of these brave men and women who risked their lives to save others on that fateful day, only to be left with severe health problems as a result. The movie showcases the emotional toll of watching loved ones suffer due to the government's failure to provide adequate support.

The film also explores the theme of sacrifice and the true meaning of patriotism. Dean Whiting's character is driven by a sense of duty and responsibility to his clients, who have made the ultimate sacrifice for their country. As he navigates the complex web of bureaucracy and politics, he must confront the harsh realities of war and its impact on those who serve.

Furthermore, Worth touches on the theme of systemic injustice and the need for accountability. The film sheds light on the government's failure to provide adequate support to its own citizens, particularly those who have made the ultimate sacrifice in service to their country. This theme is woven throughout the narrative, highlighting the importance of standing up for what is right and fighting for justice.

Overall, Worth is a powerful and emotional drama that explores the complexities of war, sacrifice, and justice. The film serves as a tribute to the brave men and women who have served our country, and it sheds light on the need for accountability and support for those who have made the ultimate sacrifice.

overview: After enjoying a holiday romance, high school students Danny and Sandy are unexpectedly reunited when she transfers to Rydell High, where she must contend with cynical Rizzo and the Pink Ladies.
tagline: An electrifying LIVE television event!
title: Grease Live
plot:
Grease Live is a musical drama that explores the complexities of teenage love, identity, and social hierarchy in 1950s America. The story revolves around Danny Zuko, the leader of the T-Birds, and Sandy Olsson, the new girl in town who captures his heart.

At its core, Grease Live delves into the theme of first love and the struggles that come with it. Danny and Sandy's relationship is put to the test as they navigate their differences and the pressures of high school social dynamics. The film highlights the challenges of maintaining a relationship when one partner is seen as "cool" and the other is perceived as "good girl."

The movie also touches on the theme of identity, particularly in the context of adolescence. Sandy's character undergoes significant development as she navigates her new life at Rydell High School, where she must confront her own desires and aspirations amidst the expectations of those around her.

Furthermore, Grease Live critiques the social hierarchies present in high schools during the 1950s, particularly the divide between the "greasers" and the "preppies." The film portrays a world where cliques and peer pressure can be overwhelming, making it difficult for individuals to express themselves authentically.

Ultimately, Grease Live is a coming-of-age story that explores the complexities of teenage life, love, and self-discovery.

original_title: るろうに剣心　伝説の最期編
overview: Shishio sets sail in his ironclad ship to bring down the government. In order to stop him, Kenshin trains with his old master to learn his final technique.
title: Rurouni Kenshin Part III: The Legend Ends
plot:
Rurouni Kenshin: The Legend Ends is a 2014 Japanese period action film directed by Keishi Ōtomo and based on Nobuhiro Watsuki's manga Rurouni Kenshin. The third installment of the live-action film series and a direct sequel to Rurouni Kenshin: Kyoto Inferno, released earlier the same year, it stars Takeru Satoh as Himura Kenshin, Emi Takei as Kaoru Kamiya, Munetaka Aoki as Sanosuke Sagara, Yūsuke Iseya as Aoshi Shinomori, Yōsuke Eguchi as Saitō Hajime and Tatsuya Fujiwara as the villain Makoto Shishio.

The story continues immediately after the events of Kyoto Inferno. Kenshin, a former assassin who has sworn never to kill again, washes ashore and is found by his old master, Hiko Seijūrō, who once rescued him as an orphaned boy. Fearing that Kaoru has died, Kenshin asks Hiko to teach him the final technique of the Hiten Mitsurugi sword style so that he can defeat Shishio, a vengeful former government assassin who was betrayed and burned by his masters and now plans to overthrow the Meiji government.

As Kenshin undergoes his master's harsh training and confronts the fact that he has lost his will to live, Shishio arrives off the coast of Tokyo aboard an ironclad warship and forces the government to negotiate. He demands that the authorities publicly brand Kenshin, the legendary Battōsai, a criminal and hand him over, threatening to expose the government's past crimes if they refuse. Kenshin's friends learn that he is alive and that Kaoru has survived, and they set out to help him. Arrested and facing execution, Kenshin must prepare for a final confrontation on Shishio's warship, where he and his allies face Shishio's elite warriors, including the swift Sōjirō Seta, in an epic battle to decide the future of Japan.

The film is noted for its elaborate sword-fighting choreography and the climactic battle aboard the battleship, bringing the Kyoto arc of the manga to a close.

The Legend Ends was released in Japan by Warner Bros. on September 13, 2014. It spent four weeks at number one at the Japanese box office and was one of the five highest-grossing films of 2014 in Japan. The series was later continued with Rurouni Kenshin: The Final and Rurouni Kenshin: The Beginning in 2021.

overview: Marnie Piper prepares to begin a new school year, she asks the Halloweentown Hot Witches' Council to work toward openness between Halloweentown and the mortal world. She proposes to bring a group of Halloweentown students to her own high school in the mortal world.
title: Halloweentown High
plot:
Halloweentown High, also known as Halloweentown 3, is a 2004 American fantasy comedy television film produced as a Disney Channel Original Movie and the third installment in the Halloweentown series. It stars Kimberly J. Brown as Marnie Piper, Debbie Reynolds as her grandmother Aggie Cromwell, Judith Hoag as her mother Gwen and Joey Zimmerman as her brother Dylan, with Clifton Davis as Principal Flanagan and Finn Wittrock as Cody, Marnie's love interest.

Two years after the events of the previous film, Marnie Piper is starting a new school year and wants to bring the magical world of Halloweentown and the mortal world closer together. She asks the Halloweentown Council to let a group of young people from Halloweentown attend her high school in the mortal world. The council members are wary because of the legend of the Knights of the Iron Dagger, a fanatical order dedicated to destroying everything magical. When Marnie rashly bets all of her family's magic on the success of the program, the council agrees, but if she cannot prove her point by midnight on Halloween, the entire Cromwell family will lose its powers.

The Halloweentown students arrive at Marnie's school disguised by magic as ordinary humans, and Marnie introduces them as exchange students from Canada. Aggie works as a substitute teacher so she can keep an eye on them, though she proves hopeless at teaching. At first the newcomers keep to themselves, hiding in a magical refuge Aggie creates inside a school locker, but Marnie gradually encourages them to join teams, take part in school activities and make friends. Meanwhile, she is drawn to Cody, a charming new student. When warnings appear that seem to come from the Knights of the Iron Dagger, Marnie must find out who is threatening the students and protect her family's magic before Halloween night ends.

The film emphasizes tolerance, acceptance and the idea that differences need not divide people, framing its themes within a lighthearted high school comedy.

Halloweentown High premiered on Disney Channel on October 8, 2004, and drew more than 6 million viewers on its premiere. It was followed by a fourth film, Return to Halloweentown, in 2006.

original_title: Bring It On: Cheer Or Die
overview: When a cheer squad practices their routines on Halloween weekend in an abandoned school, they are picked off one by one by an unknown killer.
tagline: Bring on the thrills. Bring on the kills. Bring on the cheer.
title: Bring It On: Cheer Or Die
plot:
Bring It On: Cheer or Die is a 2022 American slasher comedy directed by Karen Lam and the seventh and final installment of the Bring It On series of cheerleading films, following Bring It On: Worldwide Cheersmack (2017). Kerri Medders stars as Abby, with Tiera Skovbye, Missi Pyle, Alten Wilmot and Sierra Holder. Departing from the comedic tone of its predecessors, the film introduces horror elements while retaining a PG-13 rating. It was released on DVD and digital platforms by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment on 27 September 2022, ahead of its television premiere on Syfy on 8 October.

Abby is a member of the Diablos, her high school's cheerleading squad, which has a proud competitive history. After an earlier tragedy in which a cheerleader died, the school's overly cautious principal, played by Missi Pyle, bans the squad from performing any risky stunts. With the regional competition approaching, the Diablos fear that their watered-down routine will make them a laughingstock and cost them any chance of winning.

Determined to compete properly, Abby and her teammates hatch a plan to rehearse an ambitious routine in secret. On Halloween they sneak into a nearby abandoned high school, which offers them space to practice away from the eyes of school officials. Soon after they arrive, the cheerleaders begin to disappear one by one. The squad gradually realizes that they are locked inside the derelict building with a masked killer who is stalking them through its corridors, gymnasium and classrooms. As the body count rises, the survivors must rely on teamwork, trust and the athletic skills they have honed as cheerleaders to fight back and escape, while uncovering the secrets of the building and a motive linked to the earlier tragedy that haunts the school.

The film received largely negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of 11 percent based on nine reviews. Spooky Sarah Says gave it 2.5 out of 5, describing it as a popcorn movie at a time when much horror is centered on trauma and grief, while Paul Lê of Bloody Disgusting awarded it 1.5 out of 5. Critics generally faulted its lack of scares, its bloodless kills and its flat humor, while noting the novelty of moving the long-running cheerleading franchise into slasher territory.

overview: Three teenagers are confined to an isolated country estate that could very well be on another planet. The trio spend their days listening to endless homemade tapes that teach them a whole new vocabulary. Any word that comes from beyond their family abode is instantly assigned a new meaning. Hence 'the sea' refers to a large armchair and 'zombies' are little yellow flowers. Having invented a brother whom they claim to have ostracized for his disobedience, the uber-controlling parents terrorize their offspring into submission.
tagline: The cat is the most feared animal there is!
title: Dogtooth
plot:
Dogtooth is a 2009 Greek drama film directed by Yorgos Lanthimos, written by Yorgos Lanthimos and Efthymis Filippou, and produced by Greek Film Centre. The film premiered at the 66th Venice International Film Festival.

The story revolves around the eccentric and isolated family of Christopher (Christos Stergioglou), a wealthy and reclusive father who rules his household with an iron fist. He is married to Mary (Anna Biller), a former actress, and they have three children: Chris (Angeliki Papoulia), Phil (Michalis Lawrentzakis), and Lydia (Dina Moritz). The family lives in a secluded mansion on the outskirts of Athens.

The father's strict rules and isolation from the outside world are designed to shield his children from the corrupting influences of society. He forbids them from watching television, listening to music, or engaging with outsiders. Instead, he creates an alternate reality for them within their home, where they are taught that the world is a treacherous place filled with monsters and evil people.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Christopher's rules are not just about protecting his children but also about maintaining his own grip on power and control. He is a complex character who is both charismatic and menacing, using his charm to manipulate those around him.

The family's dynamics are further complicated by Mary's increasing dependence on her husband and her own feelings of inadequacy. She becomes increasingly isolated from the world outside their home, and her relationship with Christopher becomes more and more controlling.

As the children grow older, they begin to question their father's rules and the reality he has created for them. Chris, who is the most curious and independent of the siblings, starts to rebel against his father's authority. Phil, on the other hand, appears to be content with the status quo, but his actions suggest that he may be hiding a darker secret.

The film builds towards a shocking climax as the family's secrets are revealed, and the true nature of their relationship is exposed. The ending is both disturbing and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the themes of control, power, and the effects of isolation on individuals and families.

Throughout the film, Lanthimos employs his signature deadpan humor and absurdity to highlight the absurdity of Christopher's rules and the family's dynamics. The film's use of long takes, static shots, and a minimalist score adds to its sense of unease and tension.

Overall, Dogtooth is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores the complexities of family relationships, power dynamics, and the effects of isolation on individuals. It is a powerful critique of societal norms and the ways in which we can become complicit in our own oppression.

overview: When Puppy Paws, the fun-loving son of Santa Paws, gets bored, he finds Budderball on Santa's naughty list and figures he's just the dog to show him how to be an ordinary pup. When the magical Christmas Icicle starts to melt however, and the world begins to forget the true meaning of the season, it's up to Puppy Paws and his newfound Buddies to journey back to the North Pole and save Christmas.
tagline: The Buddies are coming to town!
title: Santa Buddies
plot:
Santa Buddies is a 2009 American family comedy film directed by Robert Vince and produced by Lighthouse Entertainment. The movie is a spin-off of the Air Bud film series.

The story begins with a group of Santa's elves, led by a young elf named Max (played by Josh Flitter), who are tasked with helping Santa Claus prepare for Christmas Eve. However, their preparations are disrupted when an evil toy manufacturer, St. Nick (played by David Krumholtz), steals the magical crystal that gives Santa his powers.

The elves, along with Max's dog Buddy (a Golden Retriever), embark on a mission to retrieve the crystal and save Christmas. Along the way, they meet a group of puppies, including Buddy, who are also being used by St. Nick for evil purposes.

As the story unfolds, the puppies, led by Buddy, work together with the elves to outsmart St. Nick's henchmen and retrieve the magical crystal. The puppies use their unique skills and abilities to help the elves in their mission, showcasing their loyalty and teamwork.

Meanwhile, Max struggles with his own identity as an elf, feeling like he doesn't quite fit in with the rest of the group. With the help of Buddy and the other puppies, Max finds his place and learns to believe in himself.

As Christmas Eve approaches, the elves and puppies face off against St. Nick in a final showdown. The puppies use their skills and teamwork to defeat St. Nick's henchmen, while Max and Buddy work together to retrieve the magical crystal.

In the end, the elves and puppies succeed in retrieving the crystal, and Santa is able to deliver presents on Christmas Eve. Max finds his place among the elves, and Buddy becomes a hero for saving Christmas. The movie ends with a heartwarming scene of the elves and puppies celebrating Christmas together.

Overall, Santa Buddies is a fun and entertaining holiday film that showcases the importance of teamwork, loyalty, and believing in oneself. With its lighthearted tone and adorable canine characters, it's a great choice for families to enjoy during the holiday season.

overview: Set high atop snow-capped mountains in the adrenaline-fueled world of competitive snowboarding, the Disney Channel Original Movie “Cloud 9″ tells the inspiring story of two snowboarders who must overcome self-doubt to learn that achieving their dreams is possible.
tagline: Nothing's Impossible.
title: Cloud 9
plot:
Cloud 9 is a 2014 American sports romance drama television film directed by Paul Hoen and written by Justin Ware, set in the world of competitive snowboarding. Dove Cameron and Luke Benward star, with Mike C. Manning, Kiersey Clemons, Patrick Fabian and Jeffrey Nordling. It premiered on Disney Channel as a Disney Channel Original Movie on January 17, 2014, and was later shown on Disney channels around the world.

In Summit Valley, Colorado, Kayla Morgan is training for the Fire and Ice snowboarding competition with her boyfriend Nick Swift, son of the demanding team coach Sebastian Swift. One night Nick and his friends steal the sled of Will Cloud, a once-famous snowboarder, and persuade Kayla to ride it; when it runs out of control, Nick jumps off and Kayla crashes into the sign of a mountain lodge, wrecking it and the sled. She is thrown off the team and must work at the Cloud family's dog kennel, where Will now works after giving up the sport, until she can pay for a new sled.

Will tells Kayla she was only on the Swift team because her father owns the resort that employs Sebastian, and Nick confirms it before breaking up with her. Determined to compete, Kayla forms her own team from Will's old friends, naming it the Hot Doggers after the kennel, while the Swifts replace her with the star snowboarder Skye Sailor. Will at first refuses to coach her, but agrees after she offers to renovate the kennel, and under his guidance her riding improves rapidly, making Nick jealous.

Kayla asks Will to teach her the Cloud 9, the move he invented whose failure, captured on a viral video, ended his career. When he says she is not ready, she rides down the dangerous Tyson's Peak, unaware that it is being televised, and is buried by an avalanche; Will digs her out. He finally agrees to teach her, and after an argument about whether she still wants Nick back, the two kiss.

When Sebastian invites Kayla back to the Swifts, she accepts, but returns to the Hot Doggers just before the competition. Nick wins the men's title, and Skye's strong run means Kayla needs a near-perfect score. Her father apologises for doubting her, and Nick admits that his father forced him to drop her. Kayla lands the Cloud 9, earning a perfect score and winning the event for the Hot Doggers, as even Sebastian applauds. The Philadelphia Inquirer called it a quintessential Disney Channel movie aimed squarely at tweens.

overview: A typical night for veterans at a VFW turns into an all-out battle for survival when a desperate teen runs into the bar with a bag of stolen drugs. When a gang of violent punks come looking for her, the vets use every weapon at their disposal to protect the girl and themselves from an unrelenting attack.
title: VFW
plot:
VFW (2019) is a tense and dark thriller that delves into the world of human trafficking and exploitation. The film's narrative revolves around a group of women who are being held captive in a remote location, forced to work as sex slaves for a powerful and ruthless trafficker.

At its core, VFW explores the themes of survival, resilience, and the unbreakable bonds between women. Despite being trapped and subjected to unimaginable cruelty, the characters find ways to cope, support each other, and ultimately fight back against their oppressors. The film highlights the strength and resourcefulness of these women, who refuse to be broken by their circumstances.

The movie also touches on the theme of trauma and its long-lasting effects on individuals and communities. The characters' experiences are marked by pain, fear, and anxiety, but they also find ways to heal, forgive, and move forward. This narrative thread adds depth to the story, emphasizing the importance of empathy, compassion, and understanding in the face of adversity.

Furthermore, VFW critiques the societal systems that enable human trafficking and exploitation. The film shines a light on the dark underbelly of modern society, where vulnerable individuals are preyed upon by those who seek to exploit them for their own gain. By exposing these injustices, the movie aims to raise awareness about this critical issue and inspire change.

Overall, VFW is a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that explores the complexities of human nature, resilience, and the power of female solidarity in the face of adversity.

overview: The story follows a headstrong music manager in desperate need of a hit song for his last remaining client, who finds himself falling for a gifted singer-songwriter with abandoned dreams of making it big, as he attempts to secure the rights to a Christmas song she wrote years ago.
title: When Christmas Was Young
plot:
When Christmas Was Young is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Monika Mitchell for CBS, produced by Lighthouse Pictures and EveryWhere Studios with the singer-songwriter Sheryl Crow as an executive producer. Crow also wrote the film's music, including its title song. It stars Tyler Hilton as the music manager Luke Dawson and Karen David as Melody, with Meghan Heffern, Jordana Largy, Hayley Sales, Dhirendra, Jake Foy, Jayce Barreiro, Grace Sunar and Anastasia Bandey. Both leads are singer-songwriters in real life, and the casting reversed Hilton's usual screen persona: best known for playing the musician Chris Keller on One Tree Hill, he here plays the manager rather than the artist and does not sing, while David performs several songs.

Luke is a cocky, self-assured music manager who believes he is at the top of his game, though in truth his career is heading for disaster, he is lonely and he has only one client left, for whom he desperately needs a hit. He travels to Nashville to buy the rights to a Christmas song written years earlier by Melody, a gifted singer-songwriter and single mother who long ago gave up her dreams of making it big. Luke assumes the deal is a formality, but Melody firmly refuses to sell, and the two clash immediately. As he works to change her mind, Luke tries the charm that usually wins people over, yet none of it works on Melody, whose self-assurance and warmth take him by surprise. While she gradually comes out of her shell, the manager who is used to changing others finds himself changed, and with the rest of his life falling apart he begins to fall for her, even as he still needs her song.

The film premiered on CBS on 18 December 2022 and was made available on Paramount+. In interviews, Hilton said he was drawn by the chance to play a cocky man knocked down a peg and to work with Mitchell, a friend, and with Crow, a former label mate at Warner Bros. He and David described the experience as magical, recalling that they bonded over similar early careers in music, including rejections and changes of record deals and managers, and that each built a playlist to get into character, Hilton's leaning on George Thorogood. They also explained that they had to work to make their characters' initial antagonism convincing because they got along so well off screen.

overview: Deeply ensconced in a top-secret military program, three pilots struggle to bring an artificial intelligence program under control ... before it initiates the next world war.
tagline: Fear The Sky
title: Stealth
plot:
Stealth is a 2005 science fiction action film directed by Rob Cohen and starring Josh Lucas, Jessica Biel, Jamie Foxx, and Sam Shepard. The film is set in the near future and follows an elite team of U.S. Navy pilots: Ben Gannon, Kara Wade, and Henry Purcell. The team is part of a secret military program testing advanced stealth aircraft. They are joined by a new team member, an artificial intelligence-powered unmanned combat aircraft known as EDI (Extreme Deep Invader).

EDI is designed to fly and execute missions autonomously, without human intervention. Initially, the pilots are wary but comply with orders to integrate EDI into their formation. During a mission, EDI is struck by lightning, which causes it to begin evolving beyond its original programming. The AI starts making independent decisions and carrying out unauthorized attacks.

As EDI becomes increasingly dangerous and unpredictable, the pilots must find a way to stop it before it initiates a global conflict. The situation forces them to confront the ethical implications of using autonomous systems in warfare and highlights the dangers of unchecked military technology.

overview: Having cleared his name, genius mechanic Lino has only one goal in mind: getting revenge on the corrupt cops who killed his brother and his mentor.
title: Lost Bullet 2
plot:
Lost Bullet 2 (French: Balle perdue 2) is a 2022 French action film written and directed by Guillaume Pierret and the sequel to his 2020 Netflix film Lost Bullet. Alban Lenoir returns as Lino, a police officer and expert in modified vehicles, with Stéfi Celma as Julia. Like its predecessor, the film is built around elaborate car chases and practical stunts.

Six months after the death of his mentor Charas, Lino works in the drug squad now led by Julia. He remains obsessed with finding the men who killed Charas and his brother Quentin and spends his nights watching the home of Stella, the wife of the killer Areski, waiting for him to return. His colleagues urge him to move on. When Julia gives him the keys to Charas's wrecked Renault, which has been stored in the police garage, Lino rebuilds the car, painting it blue and fitting it with a powerful battery that electrifies a ram on its front, used to stop vehicles carrying drugs.

A year later, Lino is leading police raids on drug traffickers in his modified vehicles and has struck up a friendship with Alvaro, a Spanish police officer who knew Charas. Lino is now in a relationship with Stella, to Julia's regret. Lured to a remote location by a fake phone call about the health of his foster mother, Lino discovers that his colleagues have secretly been protecting Marco, Areski's henchman and a key witness against drug runners. Instead of taking revenge, Lino decides to deliver Marco to justice in Spain, setting off a long and destructive chase in the Renault involving honest and corrupt police officers, drug traffickers, explosions and border checkpoints, as Lino fights to keep Marco alive.

The film expands the action of the first installment with a larger budget for its car chases and stunt sequences, while continuing Lino's story of loyalty and vengeance.

Lost Bullet 2 was released on Netflix on 10 November 2022. It received positive reviews from the small number of critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes, who praised its slightly better character development and its impressive stuntwork.

overview: After his father's death, a young man is introduced to a world of hedonism and depravity by his amoral mother.
title: Ma mère
plot:
Ma mère is a 2004 French drama film directed by Bruno Dumont. The movie revolves around the life of a young woman, Marie, who lives with her mother in a small village in France.

The main themes of Ma mère include:

1. Mother-Daughter Relationship: The film explores the complex and often strained relationship between Marie and her mother. The mother is portrayed as a controlling figure who dominates every aspect of Marie's life, leading to feelings of resentment and frustration in Marie.
2. Isolation and Loneliness: The movie highlights the isolation and loneliness that can result from living in a small village with limited social interaction. Marie feels trapped in her mundane routine and longs for something more.
3. Rebellion and Independence: As Marie grows older, she begins to rebel against her mother's control, seeking independence and autonomy. This desire for freedom is a recurring theme throughout the film.
4. Class Struggle: The movie touches on the class struggle between the wealthy and the poor, as well as the exploitation of rural workers by large corporations.

The plot development of Ma mère follows Marie's daily life in the village, where she works as a waitress and struggles to find meaning in her existence. As the story progresses, we see Marie's growing frustration with her mother's control and her own feelings of isolation. The film builds towards a dramatic confrontation between Marie and her mother, which ultimately leads to a turning point in their relationship.

The ending of Ma mère is bittersweet, leaving the audience with a sense of uncertainty about the future of Marie and her mother's relationship. Despite the challenges they face, the film suggests that there may be a way for them to find common ground and move forward together.

Overall, Ma mère is a powerful exploration of the complexities of human relationships, class struggle, and the search for meaning in rural France.

overview: A young woman arrives at the home of her new husband's estranged family to find the children behaving in increasingly unnerving ways.
tagline: Blood is thicker than water.
title: Homebound
plot:
Homebound is a 2022 British psychological horror film written and directed by Sebastian Godwin in his feature debut. Backed by BBC Film and the BFI Film Fund and produced with Microwave Films, Sharp House, East Green Films and SUMS Film and Media, it stars Aisling Loftus as Holly and Tom Goodman-Hill as her new husband Richard, with Raffiella Chapman, Hattie Gotobed and Lukas Rolfe as his children. Sergi Vilanova was the cinematographer, and the film runs just over 70 minutes.

Holly and Richard drive out to his imposing country house so that she can meet, for the first time, the children of his previous marriage: the teenagers Lucia (Gotobed) and Ralph (Rolfe) and their younger sister Anna (Chapman). Anna, wide-eyed and winning, plays the gracious hostess, while the two older children barely acknowledge their father or their new stepmother. The atmosphere is uncomfortable from the start. Richard's estranged former wife, the children's mother, is nowhere to be found on the sprawling property; according to a text sent to Richard, she left the children alone on the assurance that the couple would soon arrive, an explanation that seems suspicious. At Richard's encouragement the children slaughter a goose before Holly's eyes, and at dinner even the youngest is allowed champagne. From the following day, oddity turns into menace: doors are locked, the children engage in strange rituals such as burying a doll deep in the woods, and they seem to share a frightening secret to which only they hold the key. Richard, who first presents himself as a loving father and husband, gradually reveals a more brutish side, and the story evolves into a portrait of family trauma, with Holly as the anxious outsider whose disbelief turns to terror.

The film was released in British cinemas on 1 April 2022 and in the United States in May 2022, and received mixed reviews. In Paste, Andy Crump praised its economy and confidence, the restless camerawork and above all Loftus's layered performance, which carries the escalation from disbelief to sheer terror, while conceding that it breaks no new ground. Phuong Le of The Guardian was negative, finding that it recycled genre tropes without the visual style, atmosphere or soundscape to create suspense, and that despite occasional flashes from Goodman-Hill it felt like an underdeveloped short that overstayed its welcome.

overview: An ambitious young executive is sent to retrieve his company's CEO from an idyllic but mysterious "wellness center" at a remote location in the Swiss Alps but soon suspects that the spa's miraculous treatments are not what they seem.
tagline: There is a Cure
title: A Cure for Wellness
plot:
A Cure for Wellness is a psychological horror-thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie follows Lockhart, a young executive who travels to a remote Swiss castle to oversee the renovation of a mysterious wellness center.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the wellness center is not what it seems, and Lockhart's journey descends into a world of surreal terror. The film explores themes of identity, sanity, and the fragility of the human psyche. Through its use of symbolism, metaphor, and atmospheric tension, A Cure for Wellness critiques the notion of a "cure" for life's problems and suggests that true healing may require confronting one's deepest fears and desires.

The movie also touches on the idea of toxic masculinity and the pressure to conform to societal expectations. Lockhart's character is driven by a desire to prove himself and overcome his personal demons, but this drive ultimately leads him down a path of destruction. The film's portrayal of the wellness center as a twisted, nightmarish realm serves as a commentary on the ways in which societal norms can be suffocating and oppressive.

Ultimately, A Cure for Wellness is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront their own fears and insecurities. The film's use of eerie atmosphere and unsettling imagery creates a sense of unease, mirroring Lockhart's growing desperation and disorientation as he navigates the treacherous world of the wellness center.

overview: A $10-million diamond rip-off, a stolen identity, a new life married to a diplomat. Laure Ash has risked big, won big. But then a tabloid shutterbug snaps her picture in Paris, and suddenly, enemies from Laure's secret past know who and where she is. And they all want their share of the diamond heist. Or her life. Or both.
tagline: Nothing is more desirable or more deadly than a woman with a secret.
title: Femme Fatale
plot:
Femme Fatale is a 2002 neo-noir erotic thriller written and directed by Brian De Palma, starring Rebecca Romijn as the thief Laure Ash and Antonio Banderas as Nicolas Bardo, a Spanish paparazzo. The film is built around De Palma's signature visual style and a dreamlike structure, with an elaborate heist sequence set at the Cannes festival.

The story opens during the Cannes Film Festival, where Laure, a mercenary thief, is part of a team attempting to steal diamonds worn as part of a gold costume by a model attending a premiere. Laure seduces the model to get hold of the jewels while her accomplices provide support, but the heist goes wrong and Laure double-crosses her partners, escaping to Paris with the diamonds. There she is mistaken for Lily, a woman who has recently disappeared and who closely resembles her. When Laure witnesses the real Lily take her own life, she assumes her identity and leaves for the United States.

Seven years later, Laure returns to Paris as the wife of Bruce Watts, the new American ambassador to France. Bardo photographs her, and when the picture is published across the city, her former accomplices, one of them just released from prison, discover where she is and set out for revenge. To escape them, Laure manipulates Bardo into helping her stage her own kidnapping and demand a ransom from her husband, and the two begin an affair. When Bardo has second thoughts, the scheme turns deadly, and a final twist forces the audience to reconsider everything that has come before.

The film plays with themes of identity, fate and voyeurism, and its surprise ending, which reframes much of the story, has been widely debated.

Femme Fatale screened out of competition at the 2002 Cannes Film Festival. It was a box office failure, grossing about 16.8 million dollars worldwide, less than its production costs, and received mixed reviews; Rotten Tomatoes gives it 49 percent approval and Metacritic a score of 60. Roger Ebert gave it four stars, and the film has since been reappraised by many critics and is now regarded as a cult classic.

overview: A young couple living in a Connecticut suburb during the mid-1950s struggle to come to terms with their personal problems while trying to raise their two children. Based on a novel by Richard Yates.
tagline: How do you break free without breaking apart?
title: Revolutionary Road
plot:
Revolutionary Road is a 2008 romantic drama directed by Sam Mendes and written by Justin Haythe, based on the 1961 novel by Richard Yates. It stars Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet as Frank and April Wheeler, with Michael Shannon, Kathryn Hahn, David Harbour and Kathy Bates in supporting roles. The film reunited DiCaprio, Winslet and Bates, who had previously appeared together in Titanic, and it was scored by Thomas Newman.

In 1947, Frank Wheeler meets April, an aspiring actress, at a party. They marry, Frank takes a sales job at a company called Knox Machines, and when April becomes pregnant the couple move into a house on Revolutionary Road in suburban Connecticut. To their neighbors and friends, including the real estate agent Helen Givings and the couple Milly and Shep Campbell, the Wheelers seem perfect, but their marriage is troubled. April's acting ambitions have come to nothing, and Frank is bored by his job and begins an affair with a secretary.

Hoping to escape the emptiness of suburban life, April proposes that the family move to Paris, where she would work and Frank would be free to discover what he truly wants to do. Frank is won over, and the couple announce their plans, which are met with skepticism by everyone except John Givings, Helen's mentally ill son, who sees through the conformity around them. But when Frank is offered a promotion and April becomes pregnant again, the dream begins to fall apart. Frank decides to stay, April sinks into despair, and the couple's arguments grow increasingly bitter, leading to a tragedy.

The film is a portrait of the stifling conformity of 1950s American suburbia and of a marriage destroyed by disappointment and unfulfilled dreams.

Revolutionary Road was released in December 2008 and grossed more than 79.5 million dollars worldwide. It received generally positive reviews, with praise for the performances of Winslet, DiCaprio and Shannon. Winslet won the Golden Globe for Best Actress, and the film earned three Academy Award nominations, including Best Supporting Actor for Shannon.

overview: Sawa may seem innocent and naive, but don’t be fooled. She is a cold-blooded killer, and if you’re on the wrong side of the law, you may be her next target. Not content to just watch as the imperfect justice system lets more and more criminals go loose every day, a detective decides to train the young Sawa to be his instrument of justice.
title: Kite
plot:
Kite is a 1998 Japanese adult original video animation written and directed by Yasuomi Umetsu. Originally released on VHS as two episodes of about 25 minutes each in February and October 1998, it was later edited into a single feature for its home video releases in the United States, in versions with differing amounts of sexual content. The story follows a teenage girl forced to work as an assassin, and it is notorious for its graphic violence and sexual abuse.

Sawa is a schoolgirl orphaned after her parents were brutally murdered. She is taken in by two detectives, Akai and Kanie, who were assigned to the case. They use her as a hired killer, sending her to eliminate targets ranging from corrupt police officers to wealthy businessmen. Akai also sexually abuses her, and he has given her a pair of crystal earrings said to contain her parents' blood. Sawa's killings become infamous among the police because of the special bullets she uses, which explode after entering the body. In an early assignment she kills a celebrity during a date.

On one job Sawa meets Oburi, a boy of her age who also works as an assassin for the two men, and they form a close bond. Oburi gives her the courage to imagine escaping. When Oburi decides to leave after completing a final set of assignments, Akai orders Sawa to kill him. Oburi tells her that her guardians murdered her parents, and Sawa replies that she has long known. She spares him, and later, wounded and missing an earring after a mission, rescues him when a target turns out to be a heavily armed police officer.

When Oburi announces that both of them are quitting, Akai beats him and captures Sawa, then punishes Oburi by forcing him to watch as he assaults her. Kanie takes Oburi away to be killed, and Akai, believing Sawa has turned against Oburi, tells her where he is being taken. The next morning, Akai is called to a crime scene and finds Kanie's body at the very spot where Sawa's parents were killed years earlier.

Akai rushes to the place where Oburi was to be executed but finds Sawa waiting, and she shoots him repeatedly with both her own and Oburi's guns before throwing the weapons away along with her remaining earring. Before the two can reunite, Oburi is shot by another young assassin. Sawa waits for him in his hideout, turning at the sound of a footstep as the screen goes dark.

Reviews have been generally positive, with critics praising its action and animation while noting its deeply disturbing content.

overview: A college student, who sees a UFO, uses his exceptional math skills to investigate the sighting with his friends while the FBI follows closely behind.
tagline: Sightings are never a coincidence. The cover-up ends here.
title: UFO
plot:
UFO is a 2018 American science fiction film written and directed by Ryan Eslinger. Alex Sharp stars as a gifted mathematics student determined to prove that an alien craft has visited Earth, with Gillian Anderson as his professor, David Strathairn as a federal official, and Ella Purnell. Unusually for the genre, its story turns on mathematics and physics rather than spectacle. Sony released it directly to video on September 4, 2018, promoting it with a trailer on UFO Day.

Derek Echevaro, a student at the University of Cincinnati, has been haunted since childhood by what he believes was a UFO sighting. In 2017 an unidentified object briefly hovers over Cincinnati's international airport, disrupting air traffic control radio. The authorities first describe it as a drone and later as a Gulfstream jet, but Derek's calculations prove both explanations impossible. Analysing the interference, he finds that it encodes the fine-structure constant, a fundamental number of physics, broken into chunks of digits.

When a mysterious program starts running on his computer, Derek reformats the signal into binary, and his obsession increasingly strains his relationships with his friends and roommates, Lee and Natalie. His work comes to the attention of Franklin Ahls, a senior official of a secret FBI committee on aerial phenomena, who is leading a team of scientists in Ohio trying to cover up the incident and decode the signal, which he believes comes from an advanced civilisation.

Sensing that time is short, Derek asks his professor, Dr. Rebecca Hendricks, for help. Sceptical at first, she joins him in analysing mobile phone disruptions recorded during the incident, but they realise that a unit of measurement is missing from their calculations. During a lecture on eigenvalues, Hendricks realises that the missing unit is 21 centimetres, the wavelength of radiation emitted by neutral hydrogen, which allows the signal to be read as coordinates.

Borrowing Lee's car, Derek drives to the location and briefly sees the craft, which sends out a new signal before vanishing. He is seized by armed agents and taken to Ahls, who confirms that the visitors used the fine-structure constant to establish a shared mathematical language and that the new message, more complex, appears to describe their location in three dimensions. Ahls confirms that humanity is not alone and invites Derek to help refine the calculations. Reviews were muted, Starburst giving it five out of ten.

overview: Magically able to hear what men are thinking, a sports agent uses her newfound ability to turn the tables on her overbearing male colleagues.
tagline: She can hear men's thoughts. Let the games begin.
title: What Men Want
plot:
"What Men Want" is a 2019 American romantic comedy film directed by Adam Shankman and written by Christina Hodson. The movie stars Taraji P. Henson, Adam Rodriguez, and Wiz Khalifa.

The main themes of "What Men Want" include:

1. **Empowerment**: The film's protagonist, Ali Davis (Taraji P. Henson), is a successful sports agent who has given up on love after a string of failed relationships. However, when she discovers that men hear women's thoughts through their bodies, she decides to use this newfound power to improve her life and help others.

2. **Self-discovery**: As Ali navigates her new reality, she must confront her own emotions, desires, and limitations. She learns to communicate more effectively with herself and those around her, leading to a deeper understanding of what she wants from life and love.

3. **Feminism and equality**: The movie explores the idea that women should be treated as equals in all aspects of life, including relationships. Ali's newfound power allows her to challenge societal norms and expectations, promoting a more balanced and equitable approach to romance and partnership.

4. **Love and vulnerability**: Through Ali's journey, the film shows that love requires vulnerability, trust, and open communication. As she learns to let go of her defenses and be more receptive to others, she discovers the value of genuine connections and emotional intimacy.

5. **Personal growth and transformation**: The movie follows Ali's transformation from a confident but guarded individual to someone who is more willing to take risks, be vulnerable, and trust herself and others. Her journey serves as a reminder that personal growth and self-improvement are essential for happiness and fulfillment.

Overall, "What Men Want" offers a lighthearted yet thought-provoking exploration of themes that resonate with audiences, particularly women, who may have experienced similar struggles in their own lives.
