overview: Follows a woman desperate to escape her town, she meets a stranger who promises a romantic escape, but it results in deceit, mistrust, and violence.
tagline: At sea, there are no boundaries.
title: Into the Deep
plot:
Into the Deep is a 2022 British-American psychological thriller film directed by Kate Cox from a screenplay and story by David Beton. Produced by Tea Shop & Film Company with Signature Films and Capstone Studios, it stars Ella-Rae Smith, Matthew Daddario and Jessica Alexander as three people trapped together on a boat, with Nikkita Chadha, Jack Morris, Andrew Steele and Michael Workeye in supporting roles. Lionsgate released the film in theatres, on demand and on digital platforms in the United States on 26 August 2022. It is rated R for sexual content and nudity, drug use, violence and language, and runs about 90 minutes.

Jess (Smith) is still haunted by the drowning of her mother a decade earlier, and her memories of near-drownings recur throughout the film. Estranged from her father, whom she resents for starting a new relationship, and desperate to escape her small seaside town, she sets out to party with friends and meets Ben (Daddario), a charming, attractive visitor who promises a romantic escape and who, like her, has lost a parent. After a whirlwind night together, Jess wakes up on Ben's boat to find that he has taken them out to sea. Despite her initial misgivings, she embraces the carefree domestic life he seems to offer. The idyll unravels when a stranger, Lexie (Alexander), crashes her jet ski into the side of the boat and comes aboard. Lexie and Ben accuse each other of vicious lies and dark secrets, and in the cramped, claustrophobic quarters of the boat a dangerous cat-and-mouse game develops, forcing Jess to decide whom to believe as deceit, mistrust and violence escalate and she must fight for her own survival.

Critical reception was negative. Rachel LaBonte of Screen Rant gave the film two out of five stars, finding that it showed moments of promise and created a genuine mystery once Lexie's motives emerged, with the boat setting used to claustrophobic effect and capable performances from the three leads, but that it lacked suspense, asked viewers to forgive implausible behaviour and ended with a twist that strained credulity. Alan French of Sunshine State Cineplex rated it three out of ten, criticising poorly written exchanges, wooden performances and an unsympathetic heroine, and objecting that the film flirted with troubling ideas about guilt and trauma before backtracking on them in the final act.

overview: When strange lights descend on the city of Los Angeles, people are drawn outside like moths to a flame where an extraterrestrial force threatens to swallow the entire human population off the face of the Earth. Now the band of survivors must fight for their lives as the world unravels around them.
tagline: Don't look up
title: Skyline
plot:
Skyline is a 2010 American science fiction disaster film directed by the brothers Greg and Colin Strause and co-produced and written by Liam O'Donnell. It stars Eric Balfour as Jarrod, Scottie Thompson as his girlfriend Elaine, Donald Faison as his friend Terry, Brittany Daniel, Crystal Reed and David Zayas as a group of people trapped in a Los Angeles apartment building during an alien invasion.

Jarrod and Elaine travel to Los Angeles to celebrate the birthday of Jarrod's best friend Terry, joining Terry's girlfriend Candice and his assistant Denise. During an argument, Elaine reveals that she is pregnant. Early the next morning, mysterious blue lights descend from the sky, hypnotizing anyone who looks at them and drawing them upward into enormous alien ships hovering over the city. Jarrod is nearly taken but is saved by Terry, and the survivors realize that the aliens are harvesting humans on a massive scale.

Trapped in the building, the group tries to escape by car, but monstrous aliens of various sizes block every route, and one by one the survivors are killed or abducted. The building's concierge, Oliver, joins the remaining survivors, who hide in an apartment and watch as the United States military launches a counterattack, including a nuclear strike against one of the ships, which manages to repair itself. Jarrod, who was briefly exposed to the light, begins to undergo strange physical changes. As the situation becomes hopeless, Jarrod and Elaine are finally pulled into the mothership, where they discover the horrifying purpose of the invasion: the aliens are harvesting human brains to power their own creatures.

The film was produced on a modest budget, with its visual effects created by the Strause brothers' own effects company, Hydraulx, which was responsible for most of the film's spectacle.

Skyline was released in the United States on November 12, 2010. It was panned by critics, receiving 15 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but grossed 68.3 million dollars worldwide against a budget estimated between 10 and 20 million dollars. It launched a film series that continued with Beyond Skyline (2017), Skylines (2020) and Skyline: Warpath (2025).

overview: Max imagines running away from his mom and sailing to a far-off land where large talking beasts—Ira, Carol, Douglas, the Bull, Judith and Alexander—crown him as their king, play rumpus, build forts and discover secret hideaways.
tagline: There's one in all of us.
title: Where the Wild Things Are
plot:
Where the Wild Things Are is a 2009 fantasy adventure drama directed by Spike Jonze, who co-wrote the screenplay with Dave Eggers, adapted from Maurice Sendak's 1963 picture book. Combining live action with performers in costumes, animatronics and computer-generated facial animation, it stars Max Records, Catherine Keener and Mark Ruffalo, with the voices of James Gandolfini, Lauren Ambrose, Chris Cooper, Catherine O'Hara and Forest Whitaker. It was filmed principally in Melbourne, Australia.

Max is an imaginative, emotional eight-year-old living with his divorced mother, Connie, and his teenage sister, Claire. When Claire's friends wreck his snow fort with him inside and she does nothing to stop them, Max trashes her room. That evening, feeling neglected when his mother entertains her boyfriend, he throws a tantrum in his wolf costume, bites her and runs away from home. At the water's edge he finds a small boat and sails across the sea to a distant island.

The island is inhabited by huge, shaggy creatures called the Wild Things: the volatile, sensitive Carol, who is wrecking their huts in anguish because his friend KW has drifted away, as well as Ira, Judith, Alexander, Douglas, KW and the silent Bull. When they threaten to eat Max, he convinces them that he is a king with magical powers who can keep everyone happy, and they crown him. Max declares a "wild rumpus," and they romp through the forest. Inspired by a model of an ideal island that Carol has built, Max orders the construction of a giant fort where they can all live together.

But the harmony is fragile. Tensions arise when KW brings two owl friends, whom Carol resents as outsiders, and a dirt-clod war that Max organizes to let off steam ends with Alexander hurt and KW leaving again. Alexander confides that he knows Max is no real king, and when Carol learns the truth amid a breakdown over the collapsing fort, he chases Max furiously until KW protects him. Max begins to understand what his mother goes through and decides to go home. He leaves Carol a gift and apologizes, and as he sails away, Carol runs to the shore, and they howl farewell to each other. At home, Max's relieved mother embraces him and gives him dinner.

Released by Warner Bros. on October 16, 2009, the film received generally positive reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes' consensus calling it as beautiful as it is uncompromising despite its dark tone and slender story. It grossed about $100 million worldwide.

original_title: 名探偵コナン １１人目のストライカー
overview: Kogoro's detective agency receives a mysterious phone call. Someone on the other end warns about a bomb and leaves behind a code, "The Boy in Blue and The Blue Zebra, the rain from above ..." If Conan can decipher the riddle, he can stop the bomb. An adventure begins for Conan and the Detective Boys, taking place at a soccer match between Hideo Akagi of the Tokyo Spirits and Ryusuke Higo of Big Osaka
title: Detective Conan: The Eleventh Striker
plot:
Detective Conan: The Eleventh Striker is a thrilling mystery film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between good and evil. The story revolves around a series of mysterious events that unfold in the city, where a series of murders takes place, all connected to an ancient legend.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of obsession and the destructive power it can have on individuals. The main character, Kogoro's rival, is driven by an unrelenting passion for solving the mystery, which ultimately consumes him, leading him down a path of darkness. This serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of becoming too fixated on a goal, losing sight of one's values and morals in the process.

The film also touches upon the theme of deception and the ease with which people can be manipulated by those who hide behind masks of innocence or authority. The intricate web of lies and half-truths that are woven throughout the story serves as a commentary on how easily people can become entangled in their own deceptions, leading to devastating consequences.

Furthermore, the movie delves into the theme of justice and the true meaning of righteousness. As the mystery unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems, and the lines between right and wrong are constantly blurred. This serves as a commentary on how our perceptions of justice can be skewed by our own biases and assumptions.

Overall, Detective Conan: The Eleventh Striker is a gripping mystery film that explores the complexities of human nature, the dangers of obsession, and the nuances of justice.

overview: A thief with a unique code of professional ethics is double-crossed by his crew and left for dead. Assuming a new disguise and forming an unlikely alliance with a woman on the inside, he looks to hijack the score of the crew's latest heist.
tagline: To get away clean, you have to play dirty.
title: Parker
plot:
Parker is a 2013 American action thriller directed by Taylor Hackford and written by John J. McLaughlin, adapted from Flashfire, the 19th novel in Donald E. Westlake's series about the professional thief Parker, written under the pen name Richard Stark. Jason Statham stars in the title role and Jennifer Lopez as a Palm Beach real estate agent, with Michael Chiklis, Wendell Pierce, Clifton Collins Jr., Emma Booth and Nick Nolte.

Parker is a career criminal who lives by a strict code: he steals only from those who can afford it and harms no one who does not deserve it. At the request of his mentor, Hurley, he leads a robbery of the Ohio State Fair with a crew he does not know, led by Melander. The heist succeeds, but one member's carelessness causes a fire that kills a bystander. When Parker refuses to roll his share into the crew's next, bigger job, they shoot him and leave him for dead by the roadside. Rescued by a farming family and taken to hospital, he escapes and sets out for revenge, while protecting his girlfriend Claire, Hurley's daughter, from a hitman sent by a Chicago mob boss connected to the gang.

Tracking the crew to Palm Beach, Florida, Parker poses as a wealthy Texan named Daniel Parmitt looking for a luxury home. The real estate agent Leslie Rodgers, a recently divorced woman struggling financially and living with her mother, shows him around and soon discovers that his identity is false. Seeing a way out of her troubles, she offers to help him in exchange for a share of the loot. The gang is planning to steal millions in jewels from a high-society auction. After a brutal fight with the hitman in his hotel, Parker, badly wounded, seeks shelter with Leslie, who deflects the police.

As the crew carries out the jewel heist, disguising themselves as firefighters, Parker waits at their hideout, having sabotaged their weapons in advance. When Leslie unexpectedly arrives and is taken hostage, the two fight their way out, killing the entire crew. Parker entrusts the jewels to Leslie, later eliminates the mob boss in Chicago, and eventually sends Leslie her share and rewards the family who saved his life.

Parker grossed about $46 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes reported 42% approval, its consensus calling it generic and convoluted, though critics found Statham well suited to the role and enjoyed Lopez's comic touches.

overview: When he suddenly finds himself without his long-standing blue-collar job, Larry Crowne enrolls at his local college to start over. There, he becomes part of an eclectic community of students and develops a crush on his teacher.
tagline: Rediscover life and love.
title: Larry Crowne
plot:
Larry Crowne is a 2011 American comedy-drama film directed by Tom Hanks and written by Will McCormack. The movie follows the story of Larry Crowne, a middle-aged man who decides to go back to college after being laid off from his job.

The main theme of Larry Crowne revolves around the idea of self-discovery and personal growth. Larry, played by Tom Hanks, is a complex character who struggles to find his place in the world. He feels unfulfilled with his life and seeks a new sense of purpose through education. As he navigates college, he meets various characters who challenge his perspectives and help him discover new aspects of himself.

The film also explores themes of identity, community, and the importance of human connection. Larry's experiences in college force him to confront his own biases and assumptions, leading to a deeper understanding of himself and those around him. Through his relationships with his classmates and professors, he learns to let go of his preconceptions and embrace the uncertainty of life.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the idea that it's never too late to pursue one's passions and make a change in life. Larry's decision to return to college is not taken lightly, but he finds a sense of freedom and empowerment through his newfound education. The film suggests that with hard work and determination, anyone can overcome obstacles and achieve their goals.

Overall, Larry Crowne is a heartwarming story about finding one's way in life, embracing change, and the importance of human connection in our personal journeys.

original_title: To All the Boys I've Loved Before
overview: Lara Jean's love life goes from imaginary to out of control when her secret letters to every boy she's ever fallen for are mysteriously mailed out.
tagline: The letters are out.
title: To All the Boys I've Loved Before
plot:
To All the Boys I've Loved Before is a romantic comedy film released in 2018, produced by Susan Johnson and Matt Tyler. The movie follows the story of Lara Jean Covey, played by Lana Condor, a high school student who writes letters to all the boys she's ever had a crush on, but never intends to send them.

The story begins with Lara Jean, who lives with her single mother, Margot (Janel Parrish), and her older sister, Kitty (Anna Cathcart). After their father's death, the sisters are left to navigate high school life together. Lara Jean's life is turned upside down when she accidentally sends out the letters to all the boys on her list, including Josh Sanderson (Jordan Fisher), Peter Kavinsky (Noah Centineo), and Chris Evans (Israel Broussard).

To avoid awkwardness and potential relationships with these boys, Lara Jean tries to convince them that the letters were never meant to be sent. However, things become complicated when Josh, who is now interested in her, asks her out on a date. Meanwhile, Peter, who is also charming and popular, offers to pretend to be Josh's boyfriend in exchange for Lara Jean's help with his college applications.

As Lara Jean navigates her relationships with these two boys, she must confront her own feelings and learn to prioritize her own happiness. Along the way, she discovers that she has more in common with Peter than she initially thought, despite their initial differences. The movie takes a romantic turn as Lara Jean finds herself falling for both Josh and Peter.

Throughout the film, the characters face various challenges, including family drama, peer pressure, and self-discovery. Lara Jean's relationships with her sisters and mother are also explored, highlighting the importance of female friendships and support.

The movie ends on a heartwarming note as Lara Jean finds love and acceptance in unexpected ways. With its lighthearted tone, witty dialogue, and charming performances, To All the Boys I've Loved Before has become a beloved favorite among audiences worldwide.

Overall, To All the Boys I've Loved Before is a delightful romantic comedy that explores themes of identity, relationships, and self-discovery. The film's relatable characters, engaging storyline, and sweet romance make it a must-watch for fans of the genre.

overview: A Los Angeles journalist befriends a homeless Juilliard-trained musician, while looking for a new article for the paper.
tagline: Life has a mind of its own
title: The Soloist
plot:
The Soloist is a 2009 biographical drama directed by Joe Wright, starring Jamie Foxx as Nathaniel Ayers and Robert Downey Jr. as the journalist Steve Lopez. It is based on the true story of Ayers, a gifted musician who developed schizophrenia and became homeless, and of Lopez, the Los Angeles Times columnist who wrote about him and befriended him.

In 2005, Steve Lopez is a columnist for the Los Angeles Times, divorced and working for his ex-wife Mary, an editor at the paper. One day he hears a homeless man playing a two-string violin beautifully on the streets of downtown Los Angeles. The man, Nathaniel Ayers, tells him that he once attended the Juilliard School. Intrigued, Lopez investigates and learns from Ayers's sister that he was a cello prodigy who began showing symptoms of schizophrenia while at Juilliard, dropped out and eventually ended up living on the streets.

Lopez writes a column about Ayers, and a moved reader sends him a cello. Lopez gives the instrument to Ayers and tries to improve his life, persuading him to keep it at a shelter for homeless people and arranging lessons with a professional cellist. He also tries to convince Ayers to accept an apartment and psychiatric help, but Ayers resists, and his growing attachment to Lopez strains their relationship. When Lopez pushes too hard, Ayers turns against him. Through their difficult friendship, Lopez comes to realize that Ayers has changed his life as much as he has changed Ayers's, and the two eventually reconcile.

The film depicts the realities of homelessness and mental illness in Los Angeles, and it ends by noting that Ayers remained a member of the LAMP Community, a nonprofit organization that helps people living with severe mental illness.

Originally scheduled for release in November 2008, The Soloist was released by Paramount Pictures on April 24, 2009. It grossed about 38 million dollars against a budget of 60 million dollars and received mixed reviews, with 57 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised the lead performances but faulted a lack of narrative focus, and a Metacritic score of 61.

overview: Several people start receiving voice-mails from their future selves -- messages which include the date, time, and some of the details of their deaths.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG IV
tagline: What will it sound like when you die?
title: One Missed Call
plot:
One Missed Call is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of one's actions. The film revolves around a mysterious phone call that foretells the exact time and manner of a person's death, leaving them with no choice but to try and prevent their own demise.

At its core, One Missed Call explores the theme of mortality and the inevitability of fate. The main character, Koichi Sakakibara, is forced to confront his own mortality after receiving the ominous phone call, which sets him on a desperate quest to uncover the truth behind the mysterious calls. As he delves deeper into the mystery, he begins to realize that the caller's intentions are far more sinister than he initially thought.

The film also touches upon the theme of guilt and redemption. Koichi is haunted by his own past mistakes and feels compelled to make amends before it's too late. His journey becomes a metaphor for the human desire to atone for past wrongs and find forgiveness, even in the face of impending doom.

Furthermore, One Missed Call examines the concept of fate versus free will, leaving the audience questioning whether our lives are predetermined or if we have control over our own destinies. The film's twisty plot keeps viewers on the edge of their seats, as they try to unravel the mystery alongside Koichi.

Overall, One Missed Call is a gripping thriller that delves into the complexities of human psychology, mortality, and the consequences of one's actions, leaving a lasting impact on its audience.

overview: The universe of the Halo video game series is expanded in seven short animated films from Japan's greatest anime directors and studios.
tagline: Seven stories from the heart of the Halo universe.
title: Halo Legends
plot:
Halo Legends is a 2010 adult animated military science fiction anthology film set in the universe of the Halo video game franchise and produced by 343 Industries, the Microsoft division created to oversee the Halo brand. It compiles seven animated short films, ranging from about ten to twenty minutes each, that detail the backstory of the Halo universe and offer side stories expanding it. The shorts were made by six Japanese anime houses, Bee Train, Bones, Casio Entertainment, Production I.G, Studio 4°C and Toei Animation, with directors including Mamoru Oshii, Hideki Futamura and Hiroshi Yamazaki, while Shinji Aramaki, the creator of Appleseed, served as creative adviser. The idea had its origins in the 2006 Marvel tie-in The Halo Graphic Novel; 343's creative director Frank O'Connor supplied story outlines or finished scripts, felt that the Japanese style of narrative suited the stories, and gave the studios access to Halo's story bible and art assets along with wide latitude in visual style.

The two-part Origins, set after the events of Halo 3, has the artificial intelligence Cortana recount the history of the universe to the Master Chief in cryogenic sleep, from the Forerunners' struggle against the Flood to humanity's war with the alien Covenant, while reflecting on whether war will ever end. The Duel, rendered with a filter that makes each frame resemble a watercolour painting, tells the tragic story of an Arbiter on the Elite home world who defies the Prophets. Homecoming centres on the final mission of a Spartan, Odd One Out follows the clumsy Spartan 1337, Prototype tells the story of an elite soldier called Ghost, The Babysitter depicts an infiltration mission by a squad of ODST troopers and a Spartan, and The Package follows five Spartans who must recover a "package" from a Covenant fleet.

Warner Bros. released Halo Legends on DVD and Blu-ray on 16 February 2010, a week later than planned, after a United States premiere at the AMC Metreon in San Francisco. Reception was mostly positive. IGN UK's Orlando Parfit called it a successful if uneven attempt to fuse Halo with anime, essential viewing for dedicated fans, and IGN US found the shorts surprisingly accessible to science fiction fans in general, while Game Informer felt it would appeal to fans interested in the story rather than multiplayer. It ranked second in US Blu-ray sales in its first week, and its DVD sales eventually grossed about 11 million dollars in the United States.

overview: When reporter Rachel Armstrong writes a story that reveals the identity of a covert CIA operative, the government demands that Rachel reveal her source. She defies the special prosecutor and is thrown in jail. Meanwhile, her attorney, Albert Burnside argues her case all the way to the U.S. Supreme Court.
tagline: Don't Reveal the Source.
title: Nothing But the Truth
plot:
Nothing But the Truth is a 2008 American political drama written and directed by Rod Lurie. Kate Beckinsale stars as a reporter jailed for refusing to reveal a source, with Matt Dillon, Angela Bassett, Alan Alda, Vera Farmiga, David Schwimmer and Noah Wyle. Lurie took inspiration from the case of Judith Miller, the journalist jailed in 2005 during the investigation into the leak of CIA officer Valerie Plame's identity, but the story is fictional. It premiered at the 2008 Toronto International Film Festival.

After an assassination attempt on President Lyman, the United States bombs Venezuela, which it blames for the attack. Rachel Armstrong, an ambitious reporter for the Washington paper Capital Sun-Times, discovers that a CIA report had found no Venezuelan involvement and that the administration ignored it. Her story also reveals that the author of the report is a covert CIA officer, Erica Van Doren, whose daughter attends the same school as Rachel's son Timmy. When Rachel confronts her at a school football match, Erica refuses to comment but betrays herself with an angry outburst. With the backing of her editor and the paper's lawyer, Rachel publishes, and the story makes front-page news.

Because revealing a covert officer's identity is a serious crime, special prosecutor Patton Dubois convenes a grand jury to find Rachel's source, but she refuses to answer. Despite the confidence of her prominent lawyer, Albert Burnside, she is jailed for contempt of court. Weeks turn into months. She is assaulted by fellow inmates, her husband Ray grows distant, her son is hurt by her absence, and the newspaper is crippled by fines. Meanwhile Van Doren is shot dead outside her home by a fanatic, which only strengthens Rachel's resolve that her source must never be exposed.

Burnside takes the case to the Supreme Court, arguing that a free press depends on the protection of sources, but loses five to four on grounds of national security. Eventually the judge accepts that Rachel will never talk and releases her, but Dubois immediately has her arrested for obstruction of justice, and she accepts a plea deal of two years in prison.

On her way to prison, Rachel recalls a school field trip on which Van Doren's young daughter innocently mentioned that her mother worked for the government and had just been to Venezuela, revealing that the child was her source. Distribution problems left it with almost no American theatrical release, though it opened abroad.

overview: The film centers on two estranged sisters who, along with their friends, become entrenched in a 48 hour whirlwind of violence after a traumatic experience at an underground music festival.
tagline: Get ready for a killer night out.
title: Dreamcatcher
plot: The film centers on two estranged sisters who, along with their friends, become entrenched in a 48 hour whirlwind of violence after a traumatic experience at an underground music festival.

overview: Two brothers return to the cult they fled from years ago to discover that the group's beliefs may be more sane than they once thought.
title: The Endless
plot:
The Endless is a 2017 American science fiction horror film directed and produced by Justin Benson and Aaron Moorhead, who also star in it. Benson wrote the screenplay and Moorhead shot it, with Callie Hernandez, Tate Ellington, Lew Temple and James Jordan co-starring. The film shares its universe and some characters with the duo's earlier films Resolution (2012) and Spring (2014).

Brothers Justin and Aaron Smith, who as children belonged to a commune called Camp Arcadia, receive a mysterious videotape from the group. Their memories of the place differ: Aaron remembers a friendly, harmless community, while Justin insists it was a UFO death cult whose talk of "ascension" hinted at mass suicide. Struggling with dead-end jobs and lonely lives, the brothers agree to return for a single day. At the camp in the hills outside San Diego, they are warmly welcomed, and none of the members seem to have aged in the decade since they left. Aaron is charmed by the place, while Justin keeps his distance. The group's leader, Hal, shows Justin an equation he cannot explain.

Strange events multiply. In one ritual, members compete in a tug-of-war against a rope that disappears into the night sky, and Justin senses an invisible presence watching him in the woods, which leaves him a photograph of a buoy. Hal admits that he understands no more than anyone else, explaining that two moons in the sky reveal the truth and that the third will bring ascension. Diving beneath the buoy, Justin recovers a tape on which he and Aaron are heard describing the camp to outsiders, and a furious argument reveals that Justin spread lurid stories about Camp Arcadia to the press, leaving Aaron feeling deceived.

Searching for help, Justin discovers that the area is a trap controlled by an unseen entity, in which people are caught in endlessly repeating time loops, many ending in violent deaths. He finds Aaron and tries to convince him to leave, but Aaron argues that an eternal life among people who care for him is better than the empty existence that awaits them outside. Only when Justin acknowledges that he has always forced his brother to follow his lead does Aaron agree to go, and the brothers escape just as the entity appears.

The Endless premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2017 and was released in April 2018. Critics praised its grounded approach to an increasingly bizarre story, and Metacritic gave it 80 out of 100.

overview: Ishaan Awasthi is an eight-year-old whose world is filled with wonders that no one else seems to appreciate. Colours, fish, dogs, and kites don't seem important to the adults, who are much more interested in things like homework, marks, and neatness. Ishaan cannot seem to get anything right in class; he is then sent to boarding school, where his life changes forever.
tagline: Every Child Is Special.
title: Like Stars on Earth
plot:
Like Stars on Earth is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, and the passage of time. The movie delves into the life of a young boy named Ishaan, who struggles to find his place in the world after being diagnosed with a rare eye disorder.

Through Ishaan's journey, the film sheds light on the fragility of childhood innocence and the challenges that come with growing up. It also touches upon the theme of unrequited love, as Ishaan navigates his feelings for a girl named Mitra, who is struggling to cope with her own personal demons.

One of the primary themes of Like Stars on Earth is the power of human connection and the importance of empathy in breaking down social barriers. The film highlights the struggles faced by people from different walks of life, including those with disabilities, and shows how even small acts of kindness can have a profound impact on someone's life.

The movie also explores the theme of nostalgia and the bittersweet nature of childhood memories. Ishaan's experiences are intertwined with his love for cricket, which serves as a metaphor for the fleeting nature of youth and the importance of holding onto cherished moments.

Overall, Like Stars on Earth is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that celebrates the beauty of human relationships and the resilience of the human spirit.

overview: The King of Far Far Away has died and Shrek and Fiona are to become King & Queen. However, Shrek wants to return to his cozy swamp and live in peace and quiet, so when he finds out there is another heir to the throne, they set off to bring him back to rule the kingdom.
tagline: He’s in for the Royal Treatment.
title: Shrek the Third
plot:
Shrek the Third is a 2007 American computer-animated fantasy comedy produced by DreamWorks Animation and loosely based on William Steig's 1990 picture book Shrek!. Directed by Chris Miller, co-directed by Raman Hui and written by Jeffrey Price, Peter S. Seaman, Miller and Aron Warner, it is the third installment in the Shrek series. Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy, Cameron Diaz, Antonio Banderas, Rupert Everett, Julie Andrews and John Cleese return to their voice roles, joined by Justin Timberlake as Arthur Pendragon and Eric Idle as Merlin.

Shrek and Princess Fiona are next in line to succeed Fiona's father, King Harold, but Shrek's attempts to stand in for the ailing king end in disaster, since he has no interest in ruling Far Far Away. On his deathbed Harold reveals that there is another heir: Fiona's cousin Arthur, known as Artie. Meanwhile, Prince Charming, seeking revenge for the death of his mother, the Fairy Godmother, rallies fairy-tale villains at the Poison Apple tavern, persuading them to fight for their own "happily ever after" and help him seize the kingdom.

Shrek sets sail with Donkey and Puss in Boots to find Artie. As they depart, Fiona tells Shrek that she is pregnant, and he is terrified at the prospect of fatherhood. At Worcestershire Academy, a medieval boarding school, they find Artie to be a scrawny teenage outcast. He is thrilled to learn he will be king until Donkey and Puss scare him with talk of the job's responsibilities, and he tries to turn the ship around, causing it to crash on an island where they meet Artie's eccentric former teacher, the wizard Merlin. Back in Far Far Away, Charming's villains storm the castle during Fiona's baby shower, and Fiona, Queen Lillian and the fairy-tale princesses, including Snow White, Cinderella, Sleeping Beauty and Rapunzel, must fight back. Shrek and Artie return to confront Charming, who plans to stage a theatrical show ending with Shrek's death.

Shrek the Third received mixed reviews, with critics finding it less inventive and funny than its predecessors, though its animation and voice cast were praised. It was a major commercial success, grossing over $800 million worldwide, and was followed by Shrek Forever After in 2010.

overview: A woman with a mysterious illness is forced into action when a group of terrorists attempt to hijack a transatlantic overnight flight. In order to protect her son she will have to reveal a dark secret, and unleash the inner monster she has fought to hide.
title: Blood Red Sky
plot:
Blood Red Sky is a 2021 German action thriller film directed by Ceri Thomas and written by Thomas and Michael Petroni. The movie stars Helen Mirren, Alex Rees, and Patrick Malahide.

The story begins with a group of young girls from different countries who are invited to attend an elite boarding school in Germany called the "Höhere Schule für Mädchen" (Higher School for Girls). Unbeknownst to them, this is actually a front for a secret organization that trains young women as assassins and spies.

The main character, Lena (played by Alex Rees), is a 16-year-old girl from England who is struggling to cope with the loss of her mother. She is recruited by the school's headmistress, Frau Müller (played by Helen Mirren), who reveals that she has been chosen for this special program.

As Lena begins her training at the school, she discovers that the other girls are also being trained in various skills such as marksmanship, hand-to-hand combat, and espionage. The girls are taught to be ruthless and efficient killers, with no regard for human life.

However, things take a dark turn when Lena discovers that Frau Müller's true intentions are not what they seem. She is revealed to be working for a powerful organization that uses the school as a recruitment tool for their assassins. The girls are forced to carry out missions on behalf of this organization, often with devastating consequences.

As Lena delves deeper into the truth, she must confront her own demons and make difficult choices between loyalty to Frau Müller and doing what is right. Along the way, she forms alliances with some of the other girls, including a rebellious student named Anna (played by Hanna Alström).

The plot thickens as Lena uncovers more about the organization's true purpose and the extent of their operations. She must use all her skills and training to take down Frau Müller and the organization, while also trying to escape the school and its deadly traps.

In the end, Lena emerges victorious but scarred by her experiences at the school. She manages to destroy the organization's headquarters and bring Frau Müller to justice, but not before she exacts a personal revenge on her former mentor.

Throughout the movie, Helen Mirren delivers a chilling performance as the ruthless and cunning headmistress, bringing depth and nuance to a character that could have easily been one-dimensional. The film's action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, making for a thrilling ride from start to finish.

Overall, Blood Red Sky is a gripping and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of loyalty, power, and the exploitation of young women. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and high-octane action, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

original_title: Dawn of the Planet of the Apes
overview: A group of scientists in San Francisco struggle to stay alive in the aftermath of a plague that is wiping out humanity, while Caesar tries to maintain dominance over his community of intelligent apes.
tagline: One last chance for peace.
title: Dawn of the Planet of the Apes
plot:
Dawn of the Planet of the Apes is a 2014 American science fiction action film directed by Matt Reeves, and produced by Peter Chernin, Dylan Clark, and Tim Burton. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2001 film Planet of the Apes and is set in an alternate timeline.

The story begins with Caesar (Andy Serkis), the intelligent and empathetic leader of the apes, living in a hidden sanctuary in the San Francisco Bay Area. After a devastating virus wipes out most of humanity, Caesar's group has been working to rebuild their community and find a way to coexist with humans.

Meanwhile, a human survivor named Malcolm (Jason Clarke) is struggling to cope with the loss of his family and the trauma he experienced during the outbreak. He joins a group of survivors led by Dreyfuss (Karl Urban), who are on a mission to find a cure for the virus.

As tensions rise between humans and apes, Caesar's group discovers that a human settlement is being established nearby. The apes decide to send an envoy to meet with the humans, hoping to establish communication and prevent further conflict.

Caesar sends his trusted advisor, Maurice (Frank Dillane), along with a small group of apes to negotiate with the humans. However, things quickly go awry when the human settlement is attacked by a group of rogue apes who are infected with the virus.

Malcolm, who has been struggling with PTSD, becomes embroiled in the conflict and forms an unlikely bond with Caesar's group. As the situation escalates, Malcolm and Caesar must work together to prevent all-out war between humans and apes.

Throughout the film, Reeves explores themes of empathy, compassion, and coexistence. The movie delves into the complexities of human nature and the consequences of playing with fire when it comes to advanced technology.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the virus is not just a simple disease, but a complex tool created by humans to control and manipulate apes. Caesar's group discovers that the virus was designed to make apes more aggressive and submissive, and that it has been used to create an army of super-soldiers.

In the climactic final act, Malcolm and Caesar lead a joint human-ape force against the rogue apes and their human creators. The battle is intense and emotional, with both sides suffering heavy losses.

Ultimately, the film ends on a hopeful note, with Caesar's group emerging victorious but scarred. Malcolm has found a new sense of purpose and belonging among the apes, while Caesar has come to realize that his people are not just victims of circumstance, but also capable of great kindness and compassion.

The movie concludes with a poignant moment between Caesar and Malcolm, as they share a moment of understanding and connection. The camera pans out to reveal the ruins of San Francisco, a symbol of the devastation and destruction caused by human conflict.

Overall, Dawn of the Planet of the Apes is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores complex themes and characters. With its stunning visuals, gripping storyline, and outstanding performances from Andy Serkis and Jason Clarke, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction and action movies.

overview: With computer genius Luther Stickell at his side and a beautiful thief on his mind, agent Ethan Hunt races across Australia and Spain to stop a former IMF agent from unleashing a genetically engineered biological weapon called Chimera. This mission, should Hunt choose to accept it, plunges him into the center of an international crisis of terrifying magnitude.
tagline: Expect the impossible again.
title: Mission: Impossible II
plot:
Mission: Impossible II is a 2000 action spy film directed by John Woo and starring Tom Cruise as Ethan Hunt. The movie takes place two years after the events of the first film.

The story begins with Ethan Hunt, who has been presumed dead after his last mission went awry. However, he is revealed to be alive and working undercover in the Middle East, where he infiltrates a terrorist organization known as the Syndicate. The Syndicate is led by a ruthless woman named Nyah Nordoff-Hall (Thandie Newton), who is also Ethan's love interest.

As Ethan delves deeper into the Syndicate, he discovers that they are planning to sell a deadly virus called the "Chimera" to the highest bidder. The Chimera is a genetically engineered virus that can kill millions of people and has the potential to wipe out entire cities.

Ethan soon realizes that the true mastermind behind the Syndicate is Sean Ambrose (Dougray Scott), a former CIA operative who was thought to be dead. Ambrose has been working with Nyah, who is revealed to be his sister, and together they plan to sell the Chimera virus to the highest bidder.

As Ethan navigates through the complex web of intrigue, he must also contend with the IMF (Impossible Mission Force), which is now led by Jim Phelps (Jon Voight). However, it soon becomes clear that Phelps has been compromised by Ambrose and is working against Ethan's interests.

The plot thickens as Ethan discovers that Nyah is being manipulated by her brother and that she is not what she seems. In a thrilling twist, Ethan and Nyah team up to take down the Syndicate and prevent the sale of the Chimera virus.

In the climactic final act, Ethan faces off against Ambrose in a high-stakes battle at a nightclub. The two engage in an intense fight, with Ethan using his wits and agility to outmaneuver Ambrose's henchmen.

As the dust settles, Ethan emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. Nyah is revealed to be a double agent who was working to take down her brother from within. In the end, Ethan and Nyah share a moment of tenderness, suggesting that their relationship may have a future.

The movie concludes with Ethan returning to the IMF, where he is welcomed back as a hero. However, the film ends on a somber note, hinting that there are still many more missions ahead for Ethan Hunt.

Overall, Mission: Impossible II is an action-packed thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane excitement and espionage intrigue. Tom Cruise's performance as Ethan Hunt is as charismatic as ever, and the movie's twists and turns keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: A man awakes-- without memory -- in a pit full of bodies and must figure out if the people who rescued him are the killers, or if he is the murderer.
tagline: The moment you wake up, the nightmare begins.
title: Open Grave
plot:
Open Grave is a 2013 American horror film directed by Juan Martinez and written by Travis Ziehm. The movie follows a man who discovers his girlfriend's body in their backyard, leading him to question his own sanity and morality.

The main theme of Open Grave revolves around the exploration of grief, guilt, and the human condition. As the protagonist navigates the aftermath of his girlfriend's death, he is forced to confront the darker aspects of his own psyche and the true nature of his relationship with her. The film delves into the complexities of human emotions, particularly the intense feelings of sadness, anger, and desperation that can arise in the face of loss.

Throughout the movie, the protagonist's perception of reality becomes increasingly distorted, blurring the lines between fantasy and reality. This serves as a metaphor for the way grief can warp our perceptions of the world and ourselves, leading us to question what is real and what is just a product of our own imagination.

The film also touches on themes of existentialism, exploring the idea that life has no inherent meaning or purpose, and that it is up to each individual to create their own sense of significance. The protagonist's actions become increasingly erratic and violent as he struggles to come to terms with his loss, highlighting the destructive potential of unchecked emotions.

Ultimately, Open Grave presents a bleak and unsettling portrayal of the human experience, one that is both haunting and thought-provoking.

overview: Brigitte has escaped the confines of Bailey Downs but she's not alone. Another werewolf is tailing her closely and her sister's specter haunts her. An overdose of Monkshood - the poison that is keeping her transformation at bay - leads to her being incarcerated in a rehabilitation clinic for drug addicts where her only friend is an eccentric young girl by the name of Ghost.
tagline: It only dies if you do.
title: Ginger Snaps 2: Unleashed
plot:
Ginger Snaps 2: Unleashed is a horror-comedy film that explores the theme of female empowerment and self-discovery, particularly in the context of adolescence. The movie delves into the complexities of sisterly relationships, as Ginger's transformation into a werewolf forces her to confront her own identity and assert her independence from her family.

The film also touches on the idea of societal expectations and conformity, as Ginger struggles to balance her desire for individuality with the pressures of living up to traditional feminine norms. Through Ginger's journey, the movie critiques the notion that women must conform to certain standards of beauty and behavior, instead embracing a more authentic and empowered expression of femininity.

Furthermore, Unleashed explores themes of family dynamics and the challenges of sibling relationships, particularly in the context of Ginger's transformation into a werewolf. The film highlights the complexities of sisterly love and loyalty, as well as the difficulties of navigating complex family relationships during adolescence.

Overall, Ginger Snaps 2: Unleashed is a movie that celebrates female empowerment, self-discovery, and individuality, while also exploring the complexities of adolescent life and the challenges of growing up.

overview: A group of friends take refuge in a deserted sanatorium after they are left stranded in a snowstorm. Later, the place becomes a death trap when man-eating cannibals surround them.
tagline: Frost Is Not The Only Thing That Bites In the Snow!
title: Wrong Turn 4: Bloody Beginnings
plot:
Wrong Turn 4: Bloody Beginnings is a 2011 slasher film written and directed by Declan O'Brien. It is the fourth installment of the Wrong Turn series and the first part of a prequel story to the original 2003 film, exploring the origins of the deformed cannibal brothers Saw Tooth, One Eye and Three Finger. The cast includes Jennifer Pudavick, Tenika Davis, Kaitlyn Wong and Terra Vnesa.

In 1974, at the Glenville Sanatorium in West Virginia, the head doctor shows a new colleague around the building, including the cell where the young Hillicker brothers, three cannibalistic patients, are held. After the doctors leave, the brothers escape, kill a guard and release the other inmates, starting a riot in which the staff are massacred.

In 2003, a group of college students set out on a winter break snowmobiling trip to a friend's cabin in the mountains. Caught in a snowstorm, they take shelter in the abandoned Glenville Sanatorium, unaware that the Hillicker brothers still live there. One of the students tells the others stories about the asylum and its cannibals, but her friends dismiss them. During the night, one of the group goes exploring and is killed, and the next day the students discover the cannibals butchering their missing friend's body. When they try to leave, they find that the brothers have sabotaged their snowmobiles. One student sets off on skis to find help while the others remain trapped in the building, and the brothers hunt them down one by one in a series of increasingly gruesome killings, as the survivors try to fight back and escape through the snow.

The film follows the series' formula of isolated victims and graphic violence, moving the setting to a snowbound asylum and offering a glimpse of the cannibals' early years.

Wrong Turn 4: Bloody Beginnings was released directly to DVD and Blu-ray by 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment on October 25, 2011. It received mixed reviews; Dread Central called it an objectively bad film that is still enjoyable to watch, while Little White Lies found the characters interchangeable and the plot derivative. It was followed by Wrong Turn 5: Bloodlines in 2012.

overview: A troubled hedge fund magnate, desperate to complete the sale of his trading empire, makes an error that forces him to turn to an unlikely person for help.
tagline: Power is the best alibi.
title: Arbitrage
plot:
Arbitrage is a 2012 American drama film directed by Nicholas Jarecki. The movie revolves around Robert Miller, a successful hedge fund manager who appears to have it all - wealth, power, and influence. However, beneath the surface of his polished facade lies a complex web of deceit and corruption.

One of the main themes of Arbitrage is the corrupting influence of wealth and power. As Robert navigates the treacherous waters of high finance, he becomes increasingly ruthless in his pursuit of success, sacrificing his relationships and integrity along the way. The film raises questions about the morality of those who accumulate vast wealth through questionable means, highlighting the tension between personal gain and social responsibility.

Another significant theme in Arbitrage is the fragility of identity. As Robert's world begins to unravel, he finds himself struggling to maintain a sense of self amidst the chaos. His carefully constructed persona is revealed to be a facade, hiding a complex tapestry of insecurities and vulnerabilities. This theme speaks to the human desire for authenticity and connection, as well as the ease with which our identities can become distorted by external pressures.

The film also explores the theme of class and social status, highlighting the stark contrasts between Robert's luxurious lifestyle and the lives of those around him. Through his relationships with his family, colleagues, and acquaintances, we see the ways in which wealth and privilege can both unite and isolate individuals, creating a sense of disconnection and disillusionment.

Ultimately, Arbitrage is a thought-provoking exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the cracks that can form beneath even the most polished exteriors.

overview: One year after his young son disappeared during a Halloween carnival, Mike Cole is haunted by eerie images and terrifying messages he can’t explain. Together with his estranged wife, he will stop at nothing to unravel the mystery and find their son—and, in doing so, he unearths a legend that refuses to remain buried in the past.
tagline: Evil walks among us.
title: Pay the Ghost
plot:
Pay the Ghost is a supernatural horror film that delves into the complexities of grief, guilt, and redemption. The story revolves around Michael Pettigrew, a former soldier who returns home to care for his young daughter after being severely injured in combat.

As Michael struggles to cope with his physical limitations and emotional trauma, he begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences that seem to be connected to an antique music box. The film's narrative is layered with themes of guilt and responsibility, as Michael grapples with the consequences of his past actions and the weight of his own mortality.

Throughout the movie, the main character's journey is marked by a sense of desperation and longing for redemption. His relationship with his daughter serves as a catalyst for his emotional growth, forcing him to confront the darkness within himself and find a way to make amends.

The film also explores the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and their loved ones. Michael's experiences in combat have left him with physical and emotional scars, which he struggles to overcome. The supernatural elements that permeate the story serve as a metaphor for the overwhelming nature of his emotions, highlighting the blurred lines between reality and the unknown.

Ultimately, Pay the Ghost is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, delving into the complexities of grief, guilt, and redemption in a way that is both haunting and emotionally resonant.

overview: British tennis player Peter clutches to an embarrassingly low position on the tennis-ranking ladder. Handed a wild card for Wimbledon, he expects it to be his final bow.
tagline: She's the golden girl. He's the longshot. It's a match made in...
title: Wimbledon
plot:
Wimbledon is a 2004 romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of love, identity, and social class. The story revolves around Amanda Woods, a talented but struggling tennis player who disguises herself as a man to compete in the Wimbledon tournament.

At its core, Wimbledon delves into the theme of self-discovery and the struggle for authenticity. Amanda's decision to disguise herself as a man is a metaphor for her desire to break free from the constraints of societal expectations and forge her own path. As she navigates the world of professional tennis, she must confront her own identity and learn to accept herself for who she truly is.

The film also touches on the theme of social class and the privileged world of Wimbledon's upper echelons. Amanda's experiences as a working-class woman in a predominantly affluent environment serve as a commentary on the disparities between wealth and privilege, highlighting the tension between those who are born into luxury and those who must fight for their place.

Furthermore, Wimbledon explores the theme of love and relationships, particularly in the context of same-sex attraction. The film's portrayal of Amanda's romance with her doubles partner, Tom, is a tender and nuanced exploration of first love and vulnerability.

Ultimately, Wimbledon is a heartwarming and humorous tale that celebrates individuality, self-acceptance, and the power of love to bring people together despite their differences.

overview: Even though he's 35, Alex acts more like he's 13, spending his days as the world's oldest video game tester and his evenings developing the next big Xbox game. But when he gets kicked out of his apartment, he's forced to move in with his grandmother.
tagline: A movie that proves you're never too old to come of age.
title: Grandma's Boy
plot:
Grandma's Boy is a comedy film that explores the complexities of male relationships and the struggles of growing up. The movie delves into the theme of masculinity, as the protagonist, Barry Egan, navigates his way through adulthood while still clinging to his childhood fantasies.

The film also touches on the idea of identity crisis, as Barry's attempts to fit in with a group of older men lead him to question his own sense of self. This is further complicated by his relationships with women, particularly his crush on a woman named Sarah, who represents a more mature and independent version of himself.

Moreover, Grandma's Boy critiques the societal expectations placed on men, particularly those in their 20s and 30s, to be successful, confident, and emotionally stoic. The movie pokes fun at these stereotypes, highlighting the absurdity and vulnerability that lies beneath.

Ultimately, the film is a coming-of-age story about self-discovery, as Barry learns to let go of his childish insecurities and find his place in the world. Through its lighthearted humor and relatable characters, Grandma's Boy offers a nuanced exploration of male adolescence, making it a memorable and entertaining watch.

overview: A unique horror film told from the first-person perspective of Grace - a naive, virginal college freshman trying to deal with campus culture and her outgoing roommate as an evil entity takes over her body and unleashes chaos.
tagline: Innocence ends in blood
title: Grace
plot:
Grace, released on home video as Grace: The Possession, is a 2014 Canadian-American supernatural horror film and the feature debut of director Jeff Chan. Produced by Automatik Entertainment and Colony Pictures and distributed on DVD by Sony Pictures, it stands out for its point of view: roughly ninety percent of the film is seen through the eyes of its title character, or of the evil force that has taken hold of her, without the found-footage device. Alexia Fast stars as Grace, with Lin Shaye as her grandmother Helen, Alexis Knapp as her roommate Jessica, Brett Dier as Brad, Alan Dale as Father John and Joel David Moore as a kindly young man about to be ordained a priest; Clarke Peters, Madeleine Arthur and John Emmet Tracy also appear.

Grace, an eighteen-year-old raised in a small town, has lived a sheltered life under the suspicious eye of her devout and domineering grandmother. Helen never recovered from the fall of Grace's mother, who left the Church, became pregnant and died giving birth to her daughter, so Grace has grown up with a Bible in her hand. Going away to college is her first chance to see more of the world. She is unsure about her outgoing roommate Jessica but drawn to Brad, a handsome classmate. However, she has started seeing strange visions and feeling unwell, with symptoms resembling the psychosis her mother seemed to suffer before her death. After a party where she has a few drinks with Brad and Jessica, an episode lands her in hospital, and Helen takes her home, forcing her back into a strict Catholic routine. There Grace uncovers secrets about her mother's death while her grandmother becomes convinced that the Devil is trying to claim her. As the entity inside her grows stronger and acts through her body, the stoic Father John attempts an exorcism, leading to a violent finale.

The film was released on DVD in the United States on 28 October 2014. Reviewers generally found the story thin and derivative of The Exorcist but credited the first-person approach. DVD Talk praised how Chan conveyed Fast's performance though she is rarely seen, and Shaye's turn as the repressed grandmother, but felt the director did not push his style far enough, calling the film a rental. Flickering Myth considered it a brave attempt to refresh a limited subgenre, admiring Shaye and Dale while criticizing the cheap computer effects and the demonic voice, and found that the film gains energy once Grace returns home.

overview: A group of friends must confront their most terrifying fears when they awaken the dark powers of an ancient spirit board.
tagline: Keep telling yourself it's just a game.
title: Ouija
plot:
Ouija is a supernatural horror film directed by Stiles White and written by Mike Flanagan and Chad Hayes. The movie was released on October 24, 2014, by Universal Pictures.

The story begins with a group of teenagers who are friends since childhood, consisting of Olivia (Shelley Hennig), Andrea (Anika Noni Rose), Nora (Haley Murphy), and Lindsey (Liana Liberato). They have been inseparable since they met in kindergarten, but their friendship has started to fray due to the pressures of high school life.

One day, while exploring an abandoned house on a dare from Olivia's boyfriend, Peter (Benjamin Walker), the group stumbles upon an antique Ouija board. Despite initial reservations, they decide to use it for fun and ask questions about the future. However, their actions inadvertently awaken a malevolent spirit that has been trapped in the board.

As the night wears on, the group starts experiencing strange and terrifying occurrences, which they initially dismiss as mere coincidence or pranks gone wrong. However, when they start receiving ominous messages from an unknown entity, they realize that something is seriously amiss.

The group soon discovers that the Ouija board has become a portal to the spirit world, allowing them to communicate with a malevolent entity known only as "Zoey." Zoey claims to be a victim of a brutal murder and demands that the group help her find peace by solving a series of puzzles and riddles.

As the night descends into chaos, the group realizes that they are trapped in the house with no way out. The lines between reality and fantasy blur, and the group starts to turn on each other as paranoia sets in.

The movie takes a dark and unexpected turn when it is revealed that Peter's family has been hiding a sinister secret: his father, Paul (Doug Jones), was involved in a cult that performed human sacrifices, including Zoey. The group soon discovers that they are trapped in the house with a vengeful spirit who will stop at nothing to claim their souls.

In the climactic final act, the group must work together to outsmart Zoey and escape the house before it's too late. However, as the night wears on, it becomes clear that some of them may not make it out alive.

The movie ends with a haunting twist: Olivia is left alone in the house, but she soon realizes that she has become trapped in her own nightmare. The camera pans out to reveal that Olivia is now standing in front of the Ouija board, ready to continue the ritual and invite more spirits into her world.

Overall, Ouija is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores the dangers of meddling with forces beyond human control. With its creepy atmosphere, well-developed characters, and shocking plot twists, it's no wonder why this movie has become a cult classic among horror fans.

overview: A professional thief with $40 million in debt and his family's life on the line must commit one final heist - rob a futuristic airborne casino filled with the world's most dangerous criminals.
tagline: The heist of the century.
title: Money Plane
plot:
Money Plane is a 2020 American action film directed by Andrew Lawrence, who co-wrote the screenplay with Tim Schaaf from a story they developed with the producers Tyler W. Konney and Richard Switzer. The former professional wrestler Adam Copeland stars, with Kelsey Grammer, Thomas Jane, Denise Richards, Katrina Norman and Patrick Lamont Jr., and the director's brothers Joey and Matthew Lawrence. It was released on video-on-demand platforms by Quiver Distribution on July 10, 2020.

Jack Reese, a professional thief and former gambler, attempts to steal a valuable painting from an art museum with his crew, Isabella, Trey and the hacker Iggy, but finds the painting gone and the job compromised. Already in debt to the notorious crime boss Darius Grouch III, known as "the Rumble," who commissioned the theft, Jack is forced to accept one last job under threat to his family. He must board the "Money Plane," a luxurious airborne casino for the world's most dangerous criminals, and steal its fortune in cash and cryptocurrency. Before leaving, Jack asks his best friend, Harry, to watch over his wife and children and to find out how the museum job went wrong.

Jack and Trey board the plane posing as human traffickers, while Isabella works undercover as a flight attendant. The guests indulge in high-stakes gambling that includes poker, Russian roulette and wagers on a fight between a man and a cobra. While Trey keeps up appearances at the tables, Jack takes control of the cockpit, Isabella fights her way to the vault, and Iggy prepares to transfer the cryptocurrency from the ground. Harry discovers that the painting already belonged to the Rumble, and that the crew has been set up to fail.

Pressing on, the team fends off suspicious guests while Iggy survives an attack by assassins with the help of a gun-equipped drone operated by Harry, and the damaged servers force them to copy the cryptocurrency onto a drive. Assassins sent to Jack's home are killed by Harry. The crew decides to give the money to charities, particularly those helping victims of the plane's guests, and Jack exposes the Rumble's betrayal by broadcasting his recorded words to the passengers before the team escapes from the plane, letting the cash scatter into the sky.

The film received generally negative reviews, with a 23% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. The Daily Beast called it the dumbest movie of 2020, and it was later mocked on the RiffTrax podcast.

overview: A husband-and-wife team play detective, but not in the traditional sense. Instead, the happy duo helps others solve their existential issues, the kind that keep you up at night, wondering what it all means.
production_companies: N1 European Film Produktions GmbH & Co. KG
tagline: An existential comedy
title: I ♥ Huckabees
plot:
I ♥ Huckabees is a thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the search for meaning in life. The movie delves into the theme of existentialism, where the protagonist, Donny Vito (played by Dustin Hoffman), embarks on a journey to find his purpose and belonging.

The film also touches upon the idea of consumerism and the commodification of happiness, as embodied by the character of Jack (played by Jason Schwartzman). His relentless pursuit of material possessions and superficial relationships serves as a commentary on the emptiness of modern life. Through Jack's character, the movie highlights the tension between authenticity and artificiality, as well as the consequences of prioritizing external validation over genuine human connections.

Furthermore, I ♥ Huckabees explores the concept of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and societal expectations. The character of Thomas (played by Mark Wahlberg) serves as a foil to Jack's superficiality, representing a more authentic and vulnerable approach to life. Their interactions and conversations serve as a catalyst for Jack's transformation, forcing him to confront his own insecurities and desires.

The movie also features a unique narrative structure, where the story is presented through a series of surreal and fantastical sequences, blurring the lines between reality and fantasy. This non-linear storytelling style adds to the film's sense of wonder and curiosity, inviting the audience to ponder the complexities of human existence.

Ultimately, I ♥ Huckabees presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, encouraging viewers to question their own values, desires, and relationships. The movie's themes of existentialism, consumerism, identity, and authenticity serve as a reminder that true fulfillment can only be achieved through genuine connections with others and a deeper understanding of oneself.

overview: The teenagers of Disney's most infamous villains return to the Isle of the Lost to recruit a new batch of villainous offspring to join them at Auradon Prep.
tagline: You didn't think this was the end of the story, did you?
title: Descendants 3
plot: The teenagers of Disney's most infamous villains return to the Isle of the Lost to recruit a new batch of villainous offspring to join them at Auradon Prep.

overview: Dragon Tiger Gate is a 2006 Hong Kong martial arts-action film directed by Wilson Yip and featuring fight choreography by Donnie Yen, who also stars in the film. The film is based on the popular Hong Kong manhua, Oriental Heroes, which bears the same Chinese name as the movie.
title: Dragon Tiger Gate
plot:
Dragon Tiger Gate is a 2006 Hong Kong martial arts fantasy film directed by Wilson Yip and based on the long-running manhua Oriental Heroes, which shares its Chinese title. Donnie Yen stars as Dragon Wong and also choreographed the fight scenes, with Nicholas Tse as his half-brother Tiger Wong and Shawn Yue as the stick fighter Turbo Shek, alongside Dong Jie, Li Xiaoran, Yu Kang, Chen Kuan-tai and Yuen Wah.

Dragon Tiger Gate is a martial arts academy founded to train fighters to uphold justice against the triads and to shelter children orphaned by gang violence. Dragon and Tiger are half-brothers, the sons of one of the academy's founders, separated as children. Dragon's mother gave him half of a jade pendant, telling him that Tiger has the other half. After her death, Dragon was taken in by the triad boss Ma Kun and grew up to become his bodyguard, while Tiger was raised at the academy by his uncle. Ma Kun's gang operates under the Luocha Cult, a powerful drug-trafficking organization led by the formidable martial artist Shibumi.

Years later, Tiger clashes with Ma Kun's men in a restaurant and steals a plaque that symbolizes authority within the Luocha Cult, leading to a fight with Dragon. With the help of Turbo, an arrogant young fighter who later joins the academy, the brothers recognize each other through the jade pendant. When Ma Kun decides to return the plaque and retire, Shibumi takes it as an insult and has him killed. Shibumi then attacks Dragon Tiger Gate, killing Master Wong and leaving Tiger and Turbo badly wounded. The young men retreat to the mountains to train under a new master, while Dragon, haunted by guilt, prepares to face Shibumi in a final battle at his headquarters.

The film combines martial arts action with the fantastical style of its comic source, culminating in a final duel in which Dragon defeats Shibumi with a powerful palm technique.

Dragon Tiger Gate was released in Hong Kong on July 27, 2006, with The Weinstein Company handling its release in English-speaking territories. Its reception was lukewarm: the South China Morning Post criticized its plodding plot and weak script and noted that its cartoonish feel divided reviewers.

overview: At the height of the First World War, two young British soldiers must cross enemy territory and deliver a message that will stop a deadly attack on hundreds of soldiers.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
tagline: Time is the enemy
plot:
1917 is a 2019 British war film directed and produced by Sam Mendes, who co-wrote it with Krysty Wilson-Cairns, partly inspired by his grandfather's stories of the First World War. George MacKay and Dean-Charles Chapman star as two young British soldiers, with Mark Strong, Andrew Scott, Richard Madden, Claire Duburcq, Colin Firth and Benedict Cumberbatch in supporting roles. Cinematographer Roger Deakins and editor Lee Smith designed the film to appear as two continuous shots.

On April 6, 1917, after the German army's apparent withdrawal to the Hindenburg Line, Lance Corporals Tom Blake and William Schofield are summoned by General Erinmore. Aerial reconnaissance has shown that the retreat is a trap, and a battalion of the Devonshire Regiment is set to attack the following morning, straight into the German defenses. With telephone lines cut, the two men must carry a written order across enemy territory calling off the assault and saving 1,600 men, among them Blake's older brother, Joseph.

Crossing no man's land, they enter the abandoned German trenches, where a booby-trapped bunker collapses and nearly kills Schofield before Blake pulls him free. At a deserted farmhouse, they rescue a German pilot from his burning plane, but he fatally stabs Blake. Schofield promises the dying Blake that he will complete the mission, and continues alone, briefly traveling with a passing British unit. At the shattered town of Écoust-Saint-Mein, he is knocked unconscious in a firefight with a sniper. Waking at night, he moves through the burning ruins, meets a French woman sheltering an infant and gives them food, then escapes German soldiers by leaping into a river and being swept over a waterfall.

Downstream, Schofield reaches the Devons as the final wave prepares to attack. Unable to push through the crowded trenches in time, he sprints across the open battlefield as the first troops go over the top and delivers the order to Colonel Mackenzie, who wearily calls off the attack. Schofield finds Joseph alive, tells him of his brother's death and hands over Tom's belongings, then rests beneath a tree, looking at photographs of his own family.

1917 premiered in London in December 2019 and was released by Universal Pictures. It was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $446 million worldwide, and won three of its ten Academy Award nominations, for cinematography, sound mixing and visual effects, along with the Golden Globe and BAFTA for Best Film.

overview: Malasaña neighborhood, Madrid, Spain, 1976. While political turmoil ravages the streets all over the country, the Olmedo family arrives in the big city and settles into their new apartment. They soon discover that they are not the only ones roaming its corridors.
tagline: Meet your new neighbours
title: 32 Malasana Street
plot:
32 Malasana Street (Spanish: Malasaña 32) is a 2020 Spanish supernatural horror film directed by Albert Pintó and written by Ramón Campos, Gema R. Neira, Salvador S. Molina and David Orea. Produced by Bambú Producciones with Atresmedia Cine and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures España, it stars Begoña Vargas, Iván Marcos, Bea Segura, Sergio Castellanos and José Luis de Madariaga, with Javier Botet, María Ballesteros and Concha Velasco. It was released in Spain on 17 January 2020.

In 1976, during Spain's transition to democracy after Franco, the Olmedo family moves from the countryside to a large, cheap, old-fashioned apartment at number 32 on Manuela Malasaña Street in Madrid. The household includes Manolo and Candela, her children Pepe, a young man with a stutter, and seventeen-year-old Amparo, five-year-old Rafael and the children's elderly grandfather Fermín, who suffers from dementia. The family hides a secret: Manolo is actually the brother of Candela's husband, who abandoned them, and the couple must conceal their relationship from the conservative society of the time.

While Manolo and Candela start new jobs, the children stay at home, and strange events begin from the first night. One morning, while Rafael is alone, the television switches on by itself and a puppet in the shape of an old woman invites him to play, and the boy vanishes. The police show little interest in the case. Amparo suffers persistent nausea, Pepe exchanges notes across the courtyard with a mysterious woman named Clara, and a terrifying presence, a long-haired old woman, begins to show itself throughout the apartment. After Amparo rescues her traumatized brother from inside a clock, the family flees to a hotel, while Candela seeks the help of a medium. Investigating a clue, Amparo tracks down an elderly woman who once lived in the building and learns the tragic story of its former resident, whose family kept her hidden away because of who she was, and whose restless spirit has developed an obsession with motherhood that now threatens Amparo.

Critical reception was mixed. Pablo Vázquez of Fotogramas gave it three stars, calling it an honest collection of scares, while Eulàlia Iglesias of El Confidencial found it relied on cheap frights. Several reviewers compared it to James Wan's films and to Paco Plaza's Verónica. Made for about 3 million euros, it was released theatrically in Spain by Warner Bros. and later reached international audiences through streaming.

overview: FBI informant Jim Hoffman lures troubled automobile magnate John DeLorean to an undercover sting for cocaine trafficking.
tagline: How a lemon became a legend.
title: Driven
plot:
Driven is a 2018 biographical comedy thriller directed by Nick Hamm and written by Colin Bateman. It stars Jason Sudeikis as Jim Hoffman, a pilot and FBI informant, and Lee Pace as the car designer John DeLorean, with Judy Greer as Hoffman's wife Ellen, Corey Stoll as FBI agent Benedict Tisa, Michael Cudlitz as drug smuggler Morgan Hetrick, Isabel Arraiza and Erin Moriarty. The film dramatizes the events leading up to DeLorean's arrest in an FBI sting.

Pilot Jim Hoffman is caught by the FBI flying a load of cocaine into the United States. To avoid prison, he agrees to become an informant, and the FBI relocates him and his family to San Diego, where agent Benedict Tisa pressures him to help bring down his former boss, the trafficker Morgan Hetrick. Hoffman soon discovers that his new next-door neighbor is John DeLorean, the famous automobile executive, who is trying to build his dream car. The two families become friends, and the charming, flamboyant DeLorean draws Hoffman into his glamorous world.

DeLorean is deeply in debt and struggling to raise money for his company, and when he asks Hoffman to help him find investors, Hoffman sees an opportunity. Under pressure from the FBI and eager to free himself from his obligations as an informant, Hoffman arranges a meeting between DeLorean, Hetrick and Tisa, who poses as a drug dealer offering to finance a cocaine deal. When the money falls short, Hoffman even persuades the FBI to lend DeLorean the funds. DeLorean is arrested in a hotel room after completing the deal, and the story is interwoven with scenes of Hoffman testifying at his trial, where his uncertain testimony about who proposed the deal becomes decisive.

The film portrays the case as a darkly comic tale of ambition, vanity and deception, focusing on the unusual friendship between the two men.

Driven premiered at the 75th Venice International Film Festival on September 8, 2018, and screened at the Toronto International Film Festival before its release in the United States in August 2019. It received mixed to positive reviews, with 63 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised the outstanding cast, and a Metacritic score of 55.

overview: In war-torn Japan, the Tokugawa Shogun, desperate to restore peace to his people, orders the assassination of the hostile warlords. A beautiful young woman is raised from birth with nine other orphans, to become an assassin. Her name is Azumi, the ultimate assassin.
tagline: From The Ravages of War Raises An Assassin.
title: Azumi
plot:
Azumi is a 2003 Japanese action film directed by Ryuhei Kitamura. The story revolves around Azumi, a young and deadly assassin who is trained from a young age to eliminate her targets with precision and stealth.

The main theme of the movie is the struggle for identity and self-discovery in a world where one's purpose is defined by their profession. Azumi, as an assassin, is forced to conform to her role and follow orders without question, but deep down she longs for freedom and autonomy. As she navigates through the complex web of intrigue and deception, Azumi begins to question the morality of her actions and the true nature of her existence.
