The film also explores the theme of loyalty and betrayal, as Azumi forms connections with those around her, including a young boy who becomes her ally, and a mysterious woman who seems to hold secrets about her past. Through these relationships, Azumi is forced to confront the harsh realities of her world and make difficult choices that challenge her values and loyalties.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the theme of redemption and the possibility of escape from one's predetermined path. As Azumi faces off against her enemies and confronts the darkness within herself, she begins to see a glimmer of hope for a different future, one where she can forge her own destiny and create her own identity.

Overall, Azumi is a gripping and intense action film that explores complex themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption in a world of espionage and deception.

overview: Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson find themselves in 1890s London in this holiday special.
tagline: Welcome to Sherlock 1895!
title: Sherlock: The Abominable Bride
plot:
Sherlock: The Abominable Bride is a 2016 British television episode written by Mark Gatiss and Steven Moffat, and directed by Paul McGuigan. It is the third episode of the second series of the BBC's modern adaptation of the Sherlock Holmes stories.

The story begins with Sherlock Holmes (played by Benedict Cumberbatch) and Dr. John Watson (played by Martin Freeman) investigating a mysterious case involving a woman who has been found dead in her home, with no signs of forced entry or struggle. As they delve deeper into the case, they discover that the victim was a woman named Eurus Holmes, who is revealed to be Sherlock's long-lost sister.

As the investigation unfolds, it becomes clear that Eurus was not just any ordinary person, but rather a master manipulator who had been using her intelligence and cunning to play a complex game of cat and mouse with her brother. The case takes a surprising turn when Sherlock discovers that he has a twin sister, Eurus, who is alive and well.

The plot thickens as Sherlock becomes increasingly obsessed with finding his long-lost sister, and the two engage in a series of mind games and intellectual battles. Meanwhile, Mrs. Hudson (played by Una Stubbs) becomes suspicious of Sherlock's behavior and begins to investigate her own past, which leads her to a surprising revelation about her own connection to the Holmes family.

As the story reaches its climax, it is revealed that Eurus was not just any ordinary person, but rather a highly intelligent and skilled individual who had been using her abilities to manipulate those around her. In the end, Sherlock finally tracks down his sister, only to discover that she has been playing him all along, using their intellectual battles as a way to keep herself entertained.

The episode ends with Sherlock realizing that he has been outsmarted by his own sister, and that he must confront the fact that he is not as intelligent or capable as he thought. The final scene shows Sherlock sitting in his armchair, looking defeated and humbled, while Eurus watches him from afar, a hint of a smile on her face.

Overall, Sherlock: The Abominable Bride is a clever and engaging episode that explores the complexities of the Holmes family dynamics and the intellectual battles between Sherlock and his sister.

overview: An uptight documentary filmmaker and his wife find their lives loosened up a bit after befriending a free-spirited younger couple.
tagline: Life Never Gets Old.
title: While We're Young
plot:
While We're Young is a 2014 film, not 2015, directed by Noah Baumbach and produced by Scott Rudin Productions.

The movie explores the complexities of relationships, identity, and the challenges of growing older. The story revolves around Jamie (Adam Driver), a young filmmaker who becomes involved with a couple, Naomi (Amanda Seyfried) and Max (Peter Glaser), in their 30s. As Jamie navigates his new relationship, he is forced to confront his own insecurities and the pressures of adulthood.

Through Jamie's character, the film delves into themes of youthful idealism versus the harsh realities of growing older. The movie also examines the complexities of relationships, particularly those between people of different ages and backgrounds. As Jamie becomes more entrenched in Naomi and Max's lives, he is drawn into their conflicts and insecurities, leading to a deeper understanding of himself and his place in the world.

The film ultimately poses questions about the nature of identity, love, and belonging, leaving the audience to ponder the complexities of human relationships and the challenges of navigating adulthood.

overview: Air Bud finds that he has the uncanny ability to play volleyball.
tagline: He's The Coolest Player Under The Sun!
title: Air Bud: Spikes Back
plot:
Air Bud: Spikes Back is a heartwarming film that explores several themes that resonate with audiences of all ages. At its core, the movie delves into the transformative power of friendship and loyalty.

The story revolves around Josh Framm, a young boy who forms an unbreakable bond with his dog, Spikes, a talented golden retriever with a passion for basketball. As Josh navigates the challenges of growing up, he learns valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and believing in oneself.

One of the primary themes of Air Bud: Spikes Back is the importance of mentorship and guidance. Josh's relationship with his father, who has passed away, serves as a source of inspiration and motivation for him to pursue his dreams. The film also highlights the significance of having positive role models in one's life, as embodied by Coach Morgan, a wise and experienced basketball coach who helps Josh develop his skills.

The movie also touches on the theme of overcoming adversity and learning from failure. Josh faces numerous setbacks and disappointments throughout the story, but he never gives up on his passion for basketball. Instead, he uses these experiences to learn and grow, ultimately emerging stronger and more determined than ever.

Furthermore, Air Bud: Spikes Back celebrates the joy and companionship that pets bring to our lives. The film showcases the special bond between Josh and Spikes, highlighting the ways in which animals can provide comfort, support, and unconditional love.

Overall, Air Bud: Spikes Back is a feel-good movie that explores themes of friendship, perseverance, mentorship, and the transformative power of relationships.

overview: Spain, 1939. In the last days of the Spanish Civil War, the young Carlos arrives at the Santa Lucía orphanage, where he will make friends and enemies as he follows the quiet footsteps of a mysterious presence eager for revenge.
tagline: What is a ghost?
title: The Devil's Backbone
plot:
The Devil's Backbone is a 2001 Spanish horror film directed by Guillermo del Toro, produced by El Deseo, and written by Guillermo del Toro and David Benioff. The film is set during the Spanish Civil War (1936-1939) and tells the story of a young boy named Carlos, who is sent to an orphanage called San Miguel de Allende.

The story begins with Carlos, a 10-year-old boy, being forced to leave his home in Madrid due to the war. He is sent to the orphanage, where he meets a mysterious and ghostly presence that seems to be connected to the death of a fellow student, Santi. As Carlos tries to adjust to his new life at the orphanage, he begins to experience strange occurrences, including finding Santi's belongings in different parts of the building.

Carlos soon discovers that the orphanage is haunted by the ghost of Santi, who died under mysterious circumstances. The ghost is believed to be a manifestation of the guilt and trauma experienced by the orphanage's caretaker, Captain Cánovas, who was responsible for Santi's death. As Carlos delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a dark secret about the orphanage's past and the true identity of the ghost.

Throughout the film, Carlos forms a close bond with his friend Jacinta, an older girl who is also living at the orphanage. Together, they try to uncover the truth behind Santi's death and the haunting of the orphanage. Along the way, they encounter various characters, including Captain Cánovas, who becomes increasingly unhinged as the story unfolds.

As the story progresses, Carlos learns that Santi was killed by Captain Cánovas in a fit of rage after discovering that he had been hiding a Jewish girl, Jacinta's sister, at the orphanage. The ghostly presence is revealed to be Santi's spirit, who is trapped between the world of the living and the dead.

In the climax of the film, Carlos confronts Captain Cánovas, who has become increasingly unhinged due to his guilt and paranoia. In a dramatic confrontation, Carlos exposes the truth about Santi's death and the haunting of the orphanage. The ghostly presence is finally laid to rest, and Carlos is able to find closure and move on from his experiences.

The Devil's Backbone is a haunting and atmospheric film that explores themes of trauma, guilt, and redemption. The film features stunning visuals and a powerful performance from Fernando Tielve as Carlos. The film's use of practical effects and set design creates a sense of realism and immersion, drawing the viewer into the world of the orphanage.

Overall, The Devil's Backbone is a masterful horror film that tells a haunting and atmospheric story about trauma, guilt, and redemption.

overview: In 1950s Pittsburgh, a frustrated African-American father struggles with the constraints of poverty, racism, and his own inner demons as he tries to raise a family.
tagline: Some people build fences to keep people out, and other people build fences to keep people in.
title: Fences
plot:
Fences is a 2016 American drama film directed by Denzel Washington, based on the Pulitzer Prize-winning play of the same name by August Wilson. The film stars Denzel Washington, Viola Davis, and Jovan Adepo.

The story takes place in 1957 Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, during the Civil Rights Movement. Troy Maxson (Denzel Washington), a former baseball player, is a complex and troubled man struggling to find his place in the world. He works as a bus driver for the Pittsburgh Transit Authority and lives with his wife, Rose (Viola Davis), and their son, Cory (Jovan Adepo).

Troy's life is marked by regret and unfulfilled dreams. He was once a promising baseball player but was cut from the Negro Leagues due to racism. This experience has left him bitter and resentful towards society. Troy's relationships with his family are strained, particularly with his son Cory, who he feels is not living up to his expectations.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Troy's past experiences have shaped his present. He struggles to connect with his son, who is trying to find his own way in life. Troy's wife Rose tries to hold their family together, but her efforts are often thwarted by Troy's anger and bitterness.

Meanwhile, Troy's friend and coworker, Bono (Mykelti Williamson), provides a different perspective on life. Bono is a more optimistic character who encourages Troy to let go of his past and find peace. However, Troy's inability to forgive himself and others holds him back from moving forward.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Cory announces that he wants to leave home and pursue a career in baseball. This news sets off a chain reaction of events that forces Troy to confront his own demons and re-evaluate his relationships with those around him.

In the end, Troy's past comes back to haunt him, and he is forced to face the consequences of his actions. The film concludes on a bittersweet note, as Troy finally begins to find some measure of peace and forgiveness, but not before realizing that it may be too late for some things.

Throughout the film, Denzel Washington delivers a powerful performance as Troy Maxson, bringing depth and nuance to the character. Viola Davis also shines in her supporting role as Rose, capturing the complexity and resilience of a woman who has been holding her family together for years.

Overall, Fences is a powerful exploration of the human condition, tackling themes of regret, forgiveness, and redemption. The film features outstanding performances from its cast and is a testament to Denzel Washington's skill as an actor and director.

original_title: ポケモン・ザ・ムービーXY 光輪の超魔神 フーパ
overview: Ash, Pikachu, and their friends come to a desert city by the sea. Here they meet the Mythical Pokémon Hoopa, which has the ability to summon things—including people and Pokémon—through its magic rings. After a scary incident, they learn of a story about a brave hero who stopped the rampage of a terrifying Pokémon long ago. Now, the threat that has been bottled up for years is in danger of breaking loose again.
tagline: A power unbound. A battle of legends.
title: Pokémon the Movie: Hoopa and the Clash of Ages
plot:
Pokémon the Movie: Hoopa and the Clash of Ages is a 2015 Japanese animated science fantasy adventure film produced by OLM, Inc. and directed by Masamitsu Hidaka.

The movie begins with Ash Ketchum and his friends, Misty and Brock, visiting Professor Sycamore's laboratory in Pallet Town. They are there to participate in the Pokémon World Tournament, a prestigious tournament that takes place every five years where trainers from all over the world compete against each other. However, things take an unexpected turn when Ash and his friends discover a mysterious entity known as Hoopa, who is capable of manipulating time and space.

Hoopa is revealed to be a powerful Pokémon from another dimension, and it has been awakened by the disturbance caused by the tournament. The movie then shifts to a parallel storyline where a young boy named Ryo is struggling with his own personal demons, including a traumatic event in his past that has left him feeling lost and alone.

As Ash and his friends try to find a way to stop Hoopa from causing chaos in the world, they also learn more about Ryo's story and how it is connected to Hoopa. Along the way, they meet new characters, including a mysterious woman named Mallow who becomes an ally in their quest.

The plot thickens as Ash and his friends discover that Hoopa is actually a manifestation of Ryo's own subconscious mind, created by his traumatic experiences. They also learn that Hoopa has the power to bring people from different dimensions together, but at a great cost.

As the story unfolds, Ash and his friends must navigate through multiple timelines and dimensions to stop Hoopa from causing destruction on a massive scale. Along the way, they encounter various Pokémon and characters from different worlds, including some familiar faces from previous movies.

In the climactic final battle, Ash and his friends face off against Hoopa in an epic showdown that takes them across multiple dimensions. With the help of their new allies, including Mallow and Ryo, they are able to defeat Hoopa and restore balance to the world.

The movie ends with Ash and his friends reflecting on what they have learned about themselves and each other. They realize that even though they come from different worlds and backgrounds, they can still work together and support one another in times of need. The final scene shows Ryo finally finding closure and moving forward from his traumatic experiences, thanks to the help of Ash and his friends.

Overall, Pokémon the Movie: Hoopa and the Clash of Ages is a thrilling adventure that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and personal growth. With its unique blend of science fiction and fantasy elements, it offers something new and exciting for fans of the Pokémon franchise.

overview: A hyper-repressed and schlubby accountant (Jonas Chernick) strikes a deal with a worldly but disorganized stripper (Emily Hampshire): he'll help her with her crushing debt if she helps him become a better lover.
title: My Awkward Sexual Adventure
plot:
My Awkward Sexual Adventure is a 2012 American coming-of-age comedy-drama film that explores the complexities and challenges of adolescence, particularly in regards to sex, identity, and relationships. The movie delves into the life of a young girl named Aimee, who is struggling to navigate her own desires, boundaries, and sense of self.

At its core, My Awkward Sexual Adventure is a poignant and humorous exploration of the awkwardness and uncertainty that often accompanies adolescence. The film tackles themes of first love, peer pressure, and the struggle to find one's place in the world. Through Aimee's journey, the movie sheds light on the difficulties of growing up and the importance of self-discovery.

One of the main themes of the film is the exploration of female identity and the societal expectations placed upon young women. Aimee's experiences are marked by a desire for independence and autonomy, as she navigates the complexities of relationships and her own desires. The movie raises important questions about consent, boundaries, and the importance of prioritizing one's own needs and desires.

The film also touches on themes of family dynamics and the impact of parental relationships on adolescent development. Aimee's home life is marked by tension and conflict, which serves as a backdrop for her own struggles with identity and self-discovery.

Ultimately, My Awkward Sexual Adventure is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of the challenges and triumphs of adolescence. The movie offers a nuanced and relatable portrayal of growing up, one that is both authentic and endearing.

overview: Set in a future-world vision of Tokyo where the police have been privatized and bitter self-mutilation is so casual that advertising is often specially geared to the cutter demographic, this is the story of samurai-sword-wielding Ruka and her mission to avenge her father’s assassination. Ruka is a cop from a squad whose mission is to destroy homicidal mutants known as engineers possessing the ability to transform any injury into a weapon.
tagline: Tokyo Is Burning.
title: Tokyo Gore Police
plot:
Tokyo Gore Police is a 2008 Japanese horror film directed by Yoshiaki Kawajiri, not Nikkatsu Corporation. The movie is known for its dark and twisted take on the traditional yakuza genre.

The main theme of Tokyo Gore Police revolves around the exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, particularly in the context of organized crime and violence. The film delves into the world of a corrupt and violent yakuza syndicate, exposing the brutal and sadistic tendencies of its members. Through the lens of this dark underworld, the movie critiques the societal norms and values that enable such behavior.

The film also touches on themes of existentialism and nihilism, as the characters navigate a world devoid of moral boundaries or empathy. The graphic violence and gore in the movie serve to underscore the senselessness and randomness of human suffering, leaving the viewer with a feeling of unease and discomfort.

Furthermore, Tokyo Gore Police can be seen as a commentary on the societal pressures and expectations that drive individuals to engage in violent behavior. The film's portrayal of a yakuza syndicate as a microcosm of Japanese society highlights the ways in which conformity and loyalty can lead to a breakdown in individual moral compasses.

Overall, Tokyo Gore Police is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that challenges its viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the societal norms that enable such behavior.

overview: A pastor preoccupied with writing the perfect sermon fails to realize that his wife is having an affair and his children are up to no good.
tagline: Some family secrets are best kept...buried.
title: Keeping Mum
plot:
Keeping Mum is a 2005 British black comedy directed by Niall Johnson, who co-wrote the screenplay. Rowan Atkinson stars as a distracted village vicar, with Kristin Scott Thomas as his frustrated wife, Maggie Smith as their new housekeeper and Patrick Swayze as an American golf instructor. Entertainment Film Distributors released it in the United Kingdom on December 2, 2005.

The film opens decades earlier, when a young pregnant woman named Rosie Jones boards a train with a large trunk that begins leaking blood. Inside are the bodies of her unfaithful husband and his lover. Found guilty of manslaughter on grounds of diminished responsibility, she is committed to an institution for the criminally insane.

Forty-three years later, in the sleepy village of Little Wallop, the Reverend Walter Goodfellow is so absorbed in writing the perfect sermon for an upcoming church convention that he fails to notice his family falling apart. His neglected wife, Gloria, has begun an affair with her lecherous golf instructor, Lance; their teenage daughter, Holly, goes through boyfriends at an alarming rate; and their young son, Petey, is tormented by bullies at school. Into this household comes Grace Hawkins, a sweet, elderly new housekeeper. Grace quietly sets about solving the family's problems in her own lethal way. She disposes of a neighbor's constantly barking dog, and its owner, sabotages the bullies' bicycles and dispatches Lance, hiding the bodies in the vicarage pond. She also gently helps Walter reconnect with his wife, suggesting he add humor to his sermons and pointing out the romance in the Song of Solomon.

As harmony seems to return, Walter leaves for his convention. Gloria and Holly then see a news report about the release of an elderly woman convicted of murder and realize that Grace is Rosie Jones, Gloria's long-lost mother. Gloria insists that you cannot simply kill people who cause you problems, a point on which, Grace admits, she and her doctors never agreed. The women resolve to keep the secret from Walter and Petey. After an interfering parishioner dies of shock during a misunderstanding, Grace slips away from the family. When two workmen inform Walter that the pond must be drained, Gloria smiles tightly and offers them tea, and a final shot reveals their bodies in the pond alongside the others.

Reviews were mixed; Rotten Tomatoes' consensus praised its strong cast but found the black comedy uneven, and Metacritic gave it 53 out of 100.

overview: On a mission deep in the Bolivian jungle, a team of elite commandos finds itself on the receiving end of a lethal betrayal. Now presumed dead, the men join forces with a mysterious operative named Aisha to hunt down their enemy and even the score.
tagline: Anyone Else Would Be Dead By Now.
title: The Losers
plot:
The Losers is a 2010 action-comedy film directed by Sylvain White and written by Andy Diggle and Stephen Levenson, based on the comic book series of the same name by Robert Venditti.

The movie begins with a group of mercenaries, known as The Losers, who are hired for various missions. They consist of Jake (Jeffrey Dean Morgan), Aimee (Zoe Saldana), Ms. Bishop (Isla Fisher), and Chip (Chris Evans). However, their latest mission goes awry when they discover that the target is a group of innocent civilians.

The team manages to escape with their lives but not without being betrayed by their employer, Max (Idris Elba). The Losers are left with no choice but to take revenge on Max and his organization. They hatch a plan to infiltrate Max's headquarters and gather evidence of his wrongdoing.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Jake's troubled past, which is revealed to be connected to his relationship with Aimee. The team faces numerous challenges as they work together to complete their mission. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including henchmen, traps, and double-crosses.

Throughout the film, the characters' personalities are showcased through their interactions and banter. Ms. Bishop's sarcastic wit and Chip's awkwardness provide comedic relief, while Aimee's tough exterior hides a vulnerable side. Jake's leadership is put to the test as he tries to keep his team together and focused on their goal.

As the final showdown approaches, The Losers face off against Max and his henchmen in an intense battle. The film culminates with a thrilling sequence of action and suspense, where the team uses their skills and teamwork to take down their enemies.

In the end, The Losers succeed in their mission, but not without sacrifices. Jake's past is revealed to be connected to Max's organization, and Aimee's true loyalties are called into question. The film concludes with a sense of closure for the characters, as they part ways, forever changed by their experiences.

Overall, The Losers is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of loyalty, trust, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the comic book series and action movies will likely enjoy this thrilling ride.

overview: England, early 20th century. The future writer and philologist John Ronald Reuel Tolkien (1892-1973) and three of his schoolmates create a strong bond between them as they share the same passion for literature and art, a true fellowship that strengthens as they grow up, but the outbreak of World War I threatens to shatter it.
tagline: A Life of Love, Courage & Fellowship.
title: Tolkien
plot:
Tolkien is a 2019 biographical drama film directed by Domee Shi and David Yates, focusing on the life of J.R.R. Tolkien, the author of The Lord of the Rings.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. **Trauma and PTSD**: The film explores Tolkien's experiences during World War I, where he was a soldier in the British Army and witnessed the horrors of trench warfare. This traumatic event had a lasting impact on his life and influenced his writing.
2. **Love and relationships**: The movie highlights Tolkien's complex relationships with his wife, Edith, and his close friendship with C.S. Lewis. These relationships played a significant role in shaping his writing and worldview.
3. **Faith and spirituality**: As a devout Catholic, Tolkien's faith is deeply intertwined with his writing. The film explores how his Christian beliefs influenced the creation of Middle-earth and its inhabitants.
4. **Creative process and inspiration**: The movie delves into Tolkien's creative process, showcasing his love for languages, mythology, and world-building. His experiences as a soldier and scholar are woven together to inspire the creation of Middle-earth.
5. **Identity and legacy**: As Tolkien navigates his post-war life, he grapples with finding his place in the world and leaving a lasting legacy through his writing.

The film's narrative is structured around key events in Tolkien's life, including:

* His time at Oxford University, where he developed his love for languages and mythology.
* His experiences during World War I, which had a profound impact on his writing.
* His romance with Edith and their marriage.
* The creation of Middle-earth and the writing of The Lord of the Rings.

Overall, Tolkien (2019) is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of J.R.R. Tolkien's life and creative process.

overview: Seduced by the challenge of an impossible case, the driven Dr. Carl Jung takes the unbalanced yet beautiful Sabina Spielrein as his patient. Jung’s weapon is the method of his master, the renowned Sigmund Freud. Both men fall under Sabina’s spell.
tagline: Why deny what you desire the most.
title: A Dangerous Method
plot:
A Dangerous Method is a 2011 psychological drama film directed by David Cronenberg, based on the book "The Three of Us" by Thomas Mann.

The movie revolves around the complex relationships between three influential figures: Carl Jung (played by Michael Fassbender), Sigmund Freud (played by Viggo Mortensen), and Sabina Spielrein (played by Keira Knightley).

The main themes of A Dangerous Method include:

1. **The Power Dynamics of Mentorship**: The film explores the intricate power dynamics between Jung, Freud, and Spielrein, highlighting the complexities of mentorship, obsession, and the blurring of professional boundaries.
2. **The Nature of Madness**: Through Sabina's character, the movie delves into the concept of madness, exploring the blurred lines between sanity and insanity. This theme is also reflected in Jung's theories on the collective unconscious and the process of individuation.
3. **The Tension between Reason and Emotion**: The film portrays the intellectual and emotional struggles of its characters, particularly Freud and Jung, as they grapple with their own desires, fears, and insecurities. This tension ultimately leads to a confrontation that challenges the very foundations of their professional relationships.
4. **The Impact of Trauma**: Sabina's traumatic experiences serve as a catalyst for the events in the film, highlighting the lasting effects of trauma on individuals and their relationships.

Throughout the movie, Cronenberg masterfully weaves together these themes, creating a complex and thought-provoking narrative that explores the darker aspects of human psychology.

overview: Dazzling doll sisters Queen Bee and Royal Bee make their first movie with help from their fashionable friends in this one-of-a-kind magical adventure.
title: L.O.L. Surprise! The Movie
plot:
L.O.L. Surprise! The Movie is a 2021 American animated family film based on MGA Entertainment's L.O.L. Surprise! line of collectable fashion dolls. Directed by Alex Kamb and Lauren Ciaravalli from a script by Julia Prescott and animated by Pixel Zoo, it combines a live-action framing story with an animated doll world. The voice and live-action cast includes Ayla Rae Neal, Paris Anderson, Sonya Krueger, Ashley Angione, Tickwanya Jones, Sabrina Fest, Sarah J. Bartholomew, Tommi Rose, Frankie Kevich and Jessica Ruth Bell. The film was released on Netflix on 8 October 2021. Rated TV-G, it runs 47 minutes.

Ava (Neal), a young girl, is unhappy because she is packing up her room ahead of a move to a new home that she does not want. As she talks to her L.O.L. Surprise! dolls, light glints through a pair of 3-D glasses and floods the room with colour. When the curious girl puts the glasses on, she is transported into a digital world where her dolls come to life, and she herself becomes a baby doll named Queen Bee, the little sister of the glamorous star Royal Bee (Anderson). Royal Bee and her fashionable friends are making their first movie, which is due to premiere that same evening; with no fixed script, they shoot four different endings and plan to choose their favourite before the premiere. Queen Bee helps her big sister finish the film, taking on her own movie debut with the encouragement of the older dolls, while the crew, in roles ranging from director and actress to special-effects coordinator, faces a car chase filmed against a green screen and a spooky figure in the fog who turns out to be friendly. Through the experience Ava learns to be brave and to accept that change can be good, giving her the courage to face the move in the real world.

Critics writing for parents saw the film chiefly as a promotional vehicle. Common Sense Media rated it suitable for ages seven and up, crediting its predominantly female cast, its diverse range of dolls and its messages of teamwork and encouragement, but warning that these came wrapped in heavy branding for the toy line's dolls, accessories and toys, and that some characters wore short, revealing outfits. Kirsten Hawkes of Parent Previews gave it a C-, calling the animation poor and the script lazy and objecting that, beyond its overt lessons about courage, it suggested to young viewers that girl power came from clothes, cosmetics and celebrity.

overview: An oil platform dramatically goes down on the Norwegian coast, and researchers try to find out what happened when they realize this is just the start of something even more serious.
tagline: The biggest disaster lies ahead of us.
title: The Burning Sea
plot:
The Burning Sea (Norwegian: Nordsjøen; also released as The North Sea) is a 2021 Norwegian disaster thriller directed by John Andreas Andersen from a screenplay by Harald Rosenløw-Eeg and Lars Gudmestad. Produced by Therese Bøhn for Fantefilm, with backing from partners including Film i Väst, Zefyr Media Fund, the Nordisk Film & TV Fond and the Norwegian Film Institute, it is set among the oil platforms off the Norwegian coast. The music is by Johannes Ringen and Johan Söderqvist and the cinematography by Pål Ulvik Rokseth. The film premiered at the Rome Film Festival in October 2021 before opening in Norway later that month.

Kristine Kujath Thorp stars as Sofia, a young researcher working on an underwater search drone, who lives with oil worker Stian (Henrik Bjelland) and his young son Odin (Nils Elias Olsen). When a platform suddenly sinks, Sofia and her colleague Arthur (Rolf Kristian Larsen) are sent to the site, where their drone finds bodies and a lone survivor trapped in an air pocket. Before he can be rescued, gas bursts from a crack in the seabed and a violent explosion destroys the platform, wounding Sofia. Reviewing the footage, Arthur discovers that the official explanation is wrong: a gigantic fault is opening on the floor of the North Sea, threatening every installation in the area and a catastrophic oil spill. The operator begins an emergency evacuation and orders all wells sealed, but on Stian's platform one valve fails to close automatically, and he volunteers to shut it by hand. The last helicopter leaves without him and he is presumed dead. Refusing to accept this, Sofia studies the surveillance footage, concludes he may have survived, and flies out to the stricken platform unofficially with Arthur to find him, just as the authorities decide to ignite the spreading slick from the air. Anders Baasmo Christiansen, Bjørn Floberg and Anneke von der Lippe play key roles.

Rather than relying chiefly on spectacle, the film devotes much of its attention to how the Norwegian authorities handle the crisis. It received seven nominations at the 2022 Amanda Awards, Norway's national film prizes, including Best Norwegian Film, and won the award for Best Visual Effects. Writing for Film.ru, Konstantin Myshkin gave it seven out of ten, observing that the oppressive mood Andersen creates lingers past the end credits, since the individual characters may be saved but humanity's relationship with nature seemingly cannot.

original_title: Frequently Asked Questions About Time Travel
overview: Follows three social outcasts -- two geeks and a cynic -- as they attempt to navigate a time-travel conundrum in the middle of a British pub. Faris plays a girl from the future who sets the adventure in motion.
tagline: Three guys. One pub. Too much time on their hands.
title: Frequently Asked Questions About Time Travel
plot:
Frequently Asked Questions About Time Travel, stylized as FAQ About Time Travel, is a 2009 British science fiction comedy directed by Gareth Carrivick from a screenplay by Jamie Mathieson. Chris O'Dowd, Marc Wootton and Dean Lennox Kelly star as three friends who find themselves caught up in a time-travel conundrum in a pub, with Anna Faris as a mysterious woman from the future and Meredith MacNeill. It was released in the United Kingdom and Ireland on 24 April 2009.

Ray, a science fiction enthusiast who has just been fired from his job as a theme park guide, spends the evening with his friends Pete, a fellow fan, and Toby, a cynical would-be ladies' man. After a trip to the cinema they settle into their local pub, where they compose a sarcastic "Letter to Hollywood" listing their complaints about bad films, written on a page torn from Toby's notebook. Ray then meets Cassie, a woman who claims to be a time traveler sent to repair "time leaks," and who warns him about the Editors, agents from the future who eliminate creative people at the peak of their careers. Ray assumes his friends have set up a prank, while they believe he has invented the encounter.

Soon Pete has a disturbing vision of a massacre in the pub involving a bearded version of himself, and the friends discover a time leak in the men's toilet that sends them half an hour into the past, where they meet earlier versions of themselves. Although Cassie claims to have repaired the leak, the anomalies multiply. The trio find themselves in a post-apocalyptic version of the pub, and Pete briefly vanishes into the leak, returning disheveled and shaken. Trying desperately to avoid paradoxes, they attend a party in the pub themed around their own future selves and meet Millie, who claims to be Cassie's mentor but is in fact an Editor sent to kill them at the moment of their greatest potential. Suspecting that their Letter to Hollywood is the source of their future fame, the friends race to protect it and escape the Editors.

Critical reception was mixed, with a 35 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Empire called it quirky and engaging, with a script that keeps viewers on the ride, while the Daily Mirror felt it resembled a stretched-out television pilot but praised it as a nicely made comedy with enough laughs.

overview: Found at a Catholic hospital filthy and ferocious, feral teenager Darlin’ is whisked off to a care home run by The Bishop and his obedient nuns, where she’s to be rehabilitated into a "good girl" as an example of the miraculous work of the church. But Darlin’ holds a secret darker than the "sins" she is threatened with, and she is not traveling alone. The Woman who raised her, equally fierce and feral, is ever present in the shadows of Darlin’s psyche and is determined to come for her no matter who tries to get in her way.
tagline: Don't mess with mother's nature.
title: Darlin'
plot:
Darlin' is a 2019 American horror film written and directed by Pollyanna McIntosh, in her directorial debut, who calls it a social issue horror film. It is the third, standalone part of a loose trilogy following Offspring (2009) and Lucky McKee's The Woman (2011), in which McIntosh played the feral title character, a role she reprises here. Lauryn Canny stars as the teenage girl raised in the wild, with Bryan Batt, Nora-Jane Noone and Cooper Andrews.

At the end of The Woman, the young Darlin' Cleek and her siblings left their abusive family to live in the wilderness with the feral Woman. Years later, Darlin', now a teenager, has become wild herself and roams the wintry forest with her adoptive mother. At the Woman's urging, she goes to a hospital, where she is struck by an ambulance. After treatment she is sent to St. Philomena's, a Catholic boarding school, where nuns and pupils try to civilise her. Tony, a kind gay nurse who first befriended her, tries to keep watch over her, but the school turns him away.

Unable at first to speak, she is called Darlin' after the name on her bracelet. Gradually she relearns language, makes friends with other girls, especially the rebellious tomboy Billy, and struggles to adapt, while the school's teachings about the Devil disturb her. The ambitious bishop who oversees the school hopes to exploit her as a miracle for publicity and money. Meanwhile the Woman makes her way through the city to reclaim her daughter, killing those who stand in her way, while befriending a group of homeless sex workers; Tony helps her find Darlin'.

The bishop, a paedophile who once abused Sister Jennifer when she was a child, approaches Darlin' and discovers that she is pregnant. Darlin' reveals that her sister Peggy died in childbirth and that the Woman sent her to the city to give birth safely. Terrified that she is carrying the Devil, she drinks bleach before her First Communion, but only falls ill. During the ceremony Sister Jennifer plays a recording of the bishop confessing his crimes, and as Darlin' goes into labour, the Woman storms the church and kills him.

Tony, his partner, Sister Jennifer and Billy deliver Darlin's baby daughter, and as sirens approach, Darlin' asks the Woman to take the child far away, and she carries the infant out of the church. Reviews were mixed to positive, with a 69% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes; the Los Angeles Times found it equal parts disgusting and grandiose.

overview: Belgian sleuth Hercule Poirot boards a glamorous river steamer with enough champagne to fill the Nile. But his Egyptian vacation turns into a thrilling search for a murderer when a picture-perfect couple’s idyllic honeymoon is tragically cut short.
tagline: Murder was just the beginning.
title: Death on the Nile
plot:
Death on the Nile is a 2022 mystery film directed by Kenneth Branagh from a screenplay by Michael Green, based on Agatha Christie's 1937 novel. The second big-screen adaptation of the book after the 1978 film, it is a sequel to Murder on the Orient Express (2017) and the second installment in Branagh's Hercule Poirot series. Branagh and Tom Bateman reprise their roles as Poirot and his friend Bouc, alongside an ensemble including Annette Bening, Russell Brand, Ali Fazal, Dawn French, Gal Gadot, Armie Hammer, Rose Leslie, Emma Mackey, Sophie Okonedo and Jennifer Saunders. After several delays, including those caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, it was released in February 2022.

A prologue set in Belgium in 1914 shows the young soldier Poirot devising a plan that saves his unit, only to be scarred when his captain triggers a booby trap; his fiancée Katherine suggests he grow a moustache to hide his injuries. In 1937, in a London nightclub where the blues singer Salome Otterbourne is performing, Poirot watches Jacqueline "Jackie" de Bellefort introduce her fiancé, Simon Doyle, to her wealthy childhood friend, the heiress Linnet Ridgeway.

Six weeks later, in Egypt, Poirot runs into Bouc and his mother, Euphemia, who are among the guests celebrating Linnet's marriage to Simon. The wedding party includes Linnet's maid Louise Bourget, Salome and her niece and manager Rosalie, Linnet's godmother Marie Van Schuyler and her nurse Mrs. Bowers, Linnet's cousin and financial manager Andrew Katchadourian, and her former fiancé Dr. Linus Windlesham. Jackie, bitter at being jilted, has followed the couple to Egypt. To escape her, the group boards the river steamer Karnak for a cruise along the Nile. Linnet asks Poirot to protect her, confiding that she distrusts many of the people around her. When Linnet is found shot dead in her cabin, Poirot must unravel a web of jealousy, greed and deception among the passengers, each of whom has a motive, before the killer strikes again.

The film received mixed reviews; critics praised its lavish production design, cinematography and Branagh's performance but found it overlong and less engaging than the novel's previous adaptation. Its release was overshadowed by controversy surrounding some cast members, and it grossed about $137 million worldwide, less than its predecessor. A third installment, A Haunting in Venice, followed in 2023.

overview: In 200,000 years of existence, man has upset the balance on which the Earth had lived for 4 billion years. Global warming, resource depletion, species extinction: man has endangered his own home. But it is too late to be pessimistic: humanity has barely ten years left to reverse the trend, become aware of its excessive exploitation of the Earth's riches, and change its consumption pattern.
tagline: A stunning visual portrayal of Earth
title: Home
plot:
Home is a 2009 French documentary directed by the photographer Yann Arthus-Bertrand and produced by Luc Besson, Denis Carot and François-Henri Pinault, with music by Armand Amar. Inspired by the director's photography book Earth from Above, the film is built almost entirely from aerial footage combined with a voice-over, and it is conceived as a travel journal about the bond between humanity and the planet. Its narrators varied by language: Glenn Close read the English version, Salma Hayek the Spanish, Isabella Rossellini the Italian and Zhou Xun the Chinese, while Jacques Gamblin voiced the French theatrical cut and Arthus-Bertrand himself the French television version.

The film begins with the formation of the Earth and the emergence of life, then traces how human societies spread across continents and, especially in the past few decades, began to reshape the planet at unprecedented speed. Sweeping images of deserts, forests, ice caps, farmland and megacities illustrate its central themes: water shortages, deforestation, melting ice, the depletion of natural resources and the impact of human activity on climate change. Rather than presenting a disaster film, Arthus-Bertrand frames it as a message of hope, arguing that humanity still has roughly ten years to change course.

The shoot took about eighteen months, with the director, a cameraman, a camera engineer and a pilot flying a small helicopter over more than fifty countries on every continent, including Antarctica. Stabilized high-definition Cineflex cameras mounted beneath the helicopter gave the footage its smooth, crane-like quality, and nearly 500 hours of raw material were recorded. With a budget of about 12 million euros, largely funded by the PPR group (later Kering), Home was released on World Environment Day, 5 June 2009, simultaneously in cinemas, on television, on DVD and free on YouTube in 181 countries, and it was screened outdoors on the Champ de Mars in Paris. It drew more than 8 million viewers on France 2 and tens of millions of views online. Critics praised its imagery but questioned its preachy narration and the contrast between its message and its luxury-goods sponsor. It was nominated for the César Award for Best Documentary.

overview: In order to save an assassinated scientist, a submarine and its crew are shrunk to microscopic size and injected into his bloodstream.
tagline: A Fantastic and Spectacular Voyage... Through the Human Body... Into the Brain.
title: Fantastic Voyage
plot:
Fantastic Voyage is a science fiction film that explores the human condition through its thought-provoking narrative. The movie delves into the complexities of life, death, and the nature of existence.

At its core, Fantastic Voyage is a story about the fragility and beauty of human life. The film's protagonist, Dr. Mike MacDougall (played by Raoul Lufon), finds himself miniaturized and injected into the bloodstream to save his wife's life. As he navigates the inner workings of the human body, he confronts the harsh realities of mortality and the impermanence of life.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. MacDougall's journey through the body forces him to reevaluate his own sense of purpose and meaning in life. He must come to terms with his own limitations and vulnerabilities, ultimately emerging with a newfound appreciation for the complexities of human existence.

Furthermore, Fantastic Voyage explores the tension between technology and humanity. The film's use of advanced medical technology raises questions about the ethics of scientific progress and its impact on human relationships. As MacDougall navigates the inner body, he begins to realize that even the most sophisticated technologies can be both a blessing and a curse.

Ultimately, Fantastic Voyage is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront their own mortality and the complexities of existence. The film's themes of identity, self-discovery, and the intersection of technology and humanity continue to resonate with audiences today.

overview: After making a harrowing escape from war-torn South Sudan, a young refugee couple struggle to adjust to their new life in a small English town that has an unspeakable evil lurking beneath the surface.
tagline: When ghosts follow, they never leave.
title: His House
plot:
His House is a 2020 British supernatural horror film directed by Remi Hasél and written by Jack Thorne. The movie follows the story of Fadi, a Sudanese refugee who, along with his wife Ugandan-born woman Ayanna, are struggling to cope with their new life in London.

The main themes of His House revolve around the struggles faced by refugees and asylum seekers, particularly those from war-torn countries like South Sudan. The film sheds light on the trauma, displacement, and cultural dislocation that many refugees experience when they are forced to flee their homes.

Throughout the movie, Fadi's experiences with PTSD and his attempts to rebuild a sense of identity and belonging in a new country serve as a powerful metaphor for the refugee experience. His House also explores themes of grief, loss, and the struggle to find hope and healing in the face of trauma.

The film's use of supernatural elements serves as a powerful allegory for the psychological toll that displacement can take on individuals. The "house" itself becomes a symbol of Fadi's inner turmoil and his struggles to reconcile his past with his present.

Ultimately, His House is a thought-provoking and deeply unsettling exploration of the human cost of war, displacement, and trauma.

overview: A man who suffers visions of an apocalyptic deluge takes measures to protect his family from the coming flood.
tagline: The end of the world is just the beginning.
title: Noah
plot:
Noah is a 2014 American epic drama directed by Darren Aronofsky, who co-wrote the screenplay with Ari Handel. Inspired by the biblical story of Noah's Ark in the Book of Genesis and drawing on the Book of Enoch, it stars Russell Crowe as Noah, with Jennifer Connelly, Ray Winstone, Emma Watson, Logan Lerman and Anthony Hopkins. Paramount Pictures released it in North America on 28 March 2014, in 2D and IMAX, with a 3D conversion in other countries.

As a boy, Noah witnesses the murder of his father, Lamech, by Tubal-cain, a descendant of Cain who covets their land. Years later, Noah lives quietly with his wife Naameh and their sons Shem, Ham and Japheth. After a vision of a great flood, he takes his family to seek the counsel of his grandfather, Methuselah. On the way they find a massacred village and adopt its sole survivor, a young girl named Ila, whose wound leaves her unable to bear children. Pursued by the killers, they flee into the land of the Watchers, fallen angels who were turned into giant stone creatures as punishment for helping Adam and Eve after their banishment from Eden.

Methuselah helps Noah interpret his visions and gives him a seed from the Garden of Eden. When Noah plants it, water springs up and a forest grows instantly, convincing the Watchers that he is doing the Creator's work, and they help him build an enormous ark. Years later, as birds, snakes and other animals stream toward the nearly completed vessel, Tubal-cain and his army arrive to claim it. Noah defies him, declaring that there is no escape for the descendants of Cain, and the Watchers defend the ark. As the rains begin and Tubal-cain launches a desperate assault, Noah comes to believe that the Creator intends humanity, including his own family, to perish after the animals have been saved. His grim conviction tears his family apart, particularly when Ila, now married to Shem, unexpectedly becomes pregnant, and Noah must choose between obedience to what he believes is divine will and mercy.

Noah received generally positive reviews, with praise for its ambition, visuals and performances, although it drew criticism and controversy from some religious groups over its departures from scripture and was banned in several countries. It grossed over $359 million worldwide, making it Aronofsky's highest-grossing film.

original_title: The Wizards Return: Alex vs. Alex
overview: While visiting Italy with her family, a young wizard accidentally creates an evil version of herself.
tagline: Everything is not what it seems.
title: The Wizards Return: Alex vs. Alex
plot:
The Wizards Return: Alex vs. Alex is a 2013 American television special based on the Disney Channel Original Series Wizards of Waverly Place, directed by Victor Gonzalez. Selena Gomez stars as Alex Russo, with Jake T. Austin, Jennifer Stone, Maria Canals-Barrera and David DeLuise reprising their roles from the series; David Henrie, who played Alex's brother Justin, does not appear, although the character is mentioned. Filmed mainly at Disney's studios in late 2012, the special premiered on the Disney Channel in the United States on 15 March 2013.

The Russo family, Alex's best friend Harper and Alex's werewolf boyfriend Mason throw a celebration for Justin, who has taken over as headmaster of the wizard school WizTech. Dominic, a WizTech student, arrives to explain that Justin is too busy to attend and flirts with Alex, making Mason jealous. Alex's father, Jerry, announces a family reunion in Tuscany. Alex magically creates a portal linking the family's Italian villa with their New York loft to save on travel, but Jerry scolds her for her selfishness and immaturity.

Hoping to prove that she is no longer the irresponsible wizard she once was, Alex casts a spell to rid herself of the negative parts of her personality, but it backfires and creates an evil double who emerges from a mirror and escapes to Italy. Meanwhile, Alex's brother Max chases after an Italian girl, unaware that she is his cousin, and their parents, Jerry and Theresa, follow him, starting the reunion early. Evil Alex, aided by a mysterious wizard, shrinks and imprisons Max, Jerry and Theresa. The accomplice is revealed to be Dominic, nephew of Gorog, the former leader of the Angels of Darkness. Following the trail to the Leaning Tower of Pisa, where Harper is also captured, Alex discovers that Dominic plans to use a spell replicator at the top of the tower to trap all mortals in tiny beads and take over the world, and he needs Alex's power to do it. Alex must face her evil reflection and defeat Dominic to save her family and the world.

The special drew 5.9 million viewers on its premiere in the United States. In the United Kingdom it attracted 575,000 viewers, making it at the time Disney Channel UK's third most-watched broadcast. It served as a reunion of the series, which had ended in 2012 after four seasons.

original_title: Barbie Fairytopia: Magic of the Rainbow
overview: Elina goes to a fairy school to learn dancing and fairy magic. The spring of the fairy land is soon threatened by evil Laverna who intends to prevent fairies from performing the annual vital rainbow dance. Elina must stop quarreling with her fellow students and unite them to save the first bud of the spring.
title: Barbie Fairytopia: Magic of the Rainbow
plot:
Barbie Fairytopia: Magic of the Rainbow, also known as Barbie: Magic of the Rainbow, is a 2007 computer-animated fantasy film directed by William Lau and written by Elise Allen. The tenth film in the Barbie series and the third and final installment of the Fairytopia trilogy, it features Kelly Sheridan as the voice of Elina, with Lee Tockar, Kathleen Barr, Christopher Gaze and Tabitha St. Germain. It was released direct-to-video in March 2007 and distributed internationally by Universal Pictures Video.

Elina, now celebrated for twice defeating the wicked Laverna, is invited to become an apprentice of the guardian fairy Azura at the Crystal Palace, where she will learn the Flight of Spring, the annual ritual that brings the season's first rainbow to life. She meets six fellow apprentices: Linden, a fairy who can talk to animals; Shimmer, a tiny and arrogant pixie; Lumina, a moon fairy who can glimpse the future; Sunburst, a sparkle fairy who resents Elina's fame; the vain Faben; and Glee, a cheerful wood nymph who becomes Elina's best friend. Glee's puffball, Dizzle, falls for Elina's companion Bibble.

Unknown to the apprentices, Laverna, the jealous sister of the Enchantress, is plotting to disrupt the Flight of Spring and plunge Fairytopia into a winter lasting ten years. Elina excels in her early lessons, which increases Sunburst's hostility, and a quarrel between the two gets them both reprimanded by Azura. Escaping her exile, Laverna disguises herself as an enchanted frog, tricking Elina and Linden into breaking the spell and freeing her. The guardians refuse to believe their warning, since Laverna has left a decoy in her place in the bogs, although Azura takes it seriously. Laverna then captures Sunburst and assumes her appearance to slip into the palace, where she poisons all the guardians and leaves them in a deep sleep. With the guardians helpless, the Enchantress calls on the young apprentices to perform the ritual themselves, and Elina and her companions must learn to trust each other and work together to create the rainbow and defeat Laverna.

The film won two Leo Awards in 2007, for best animation program or series and best overall sound in an animation program or series, and William Lau was nominated for best direction. It concluded the Fairytopia storyline begun with Barbie: Fairytopia (2005) and Barbie: Mermaidia (2006).

overview: The life of a teenage boy is forever altered by a chance encounter with cutting edge military technology.
tagline: Man's best friend has evolved
title: A-X-L
plot:
A-X-L is a 2018 American science fiction action film directed by Michael Bay and written by Art Marcum and Matt Holloway. The movie stars Dwayne Johnson, Woody Harrelson, and Carla Gugino.

The story begins with Alex Hitchens (Dwayne Johnson), a former Army Ranger who has lost his way after the death of his wife in combat. He is haunted by flashbacks of his time in Afghanistan and struggles to connect with his 8-year-old son, Christian (Max Thieriot). To cope with his emotions, Alex turns to extreme sports, including big wave surfing.

One day, while surfing, Alex is attacked by a massive shark that kills him. However, instead of dying, he is rescued by a team of scientists who have been studying the effects of a mysterious virus on humans and animals. The virus, known as "Project A-X-L," has the ability to transfer human consciousness into an alien creature's body.

The scientists, led by Dr. Emma Russell (Carla Gugino), believe that Alex's consciousness can be transferred into the body of an alien creature, allowing him to survive his injuries and potentially find a way to communicate with humans again. The team uses advanced technology to transfer Alex's consciousness into the body of an A-X-L, a massive, intelligent, and deadly alien creature.

As Alex navigates his new surroundings, he begins to form a bond with Christian, who is struggling to cope with his father's death. With the help of Dr. Russell and her team, Alex learns to control his newfound powers and work together with them to take down a group of rogue mercenaries who are seeking to exploit the A-X-L for their own gain.

Throughout the movie, Alex struggles to reconcile his human emotions with his new alien form, leading to some intense and emotional moments. He also begins to uncover the truth about Project A-X-L and the motivations of Dr. Russell and her team.

As the story unfolds, Alex and Christian work together to take down the mercenaries and prevent them from using the A-X-L for their own purposes. Along the way, Alex must confront his own demons and learn to trust himself and those around him.

The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between Alex and the mercenaries, with Alex using his newfound powers to protect Christian and defeat his enemies. In the end, Alex is able to find a sense of peace and closure, and he begins to rebuild his relationship with Christian.

Overall, A-X-L is a thrilling and emotionally resonant sci-fi action film that explores themes of grief, redemption, and the power of human connection.

overview: An American woman is stranded in Tokyo after breaking up with her boyfriend. Searching for direction in life, she trains to be a râmen chef under a tyrannical Japanese master.
tagline: Her romance is on pins and noodles.
title: The Ramen Girl
plot:
The Ramen Girl is a 2008 romantic comedy-drama directed by Robert Allan Ackerman and starring Brittany Murphy, who also co-produced, as an American woman who learns to make ramen in Tokyo. Toshiyuki Nishida plays her demanding teacher and Kimiko Yo his wife, with Sohee Park, Tammy Blanchard, Gabriel Mann and Tsutomu Yamazaki, star of the noodle comedy Tampopo (1985). Much of the dialogue is in Japanese.

Abby has moved to Tokyo to be with her boyfriend Ethan, who soon dumps her and leaves for Osaka. Heartbroken, she wanders into a small ramen shop near her apartment, run by the gruff chef Maezumi and his wife Reiko, neither of whom speaks English. Maezumi serves her a bowl of noodles that leaves her strangely moved; she imagines the shop's beckoning cat waving at her, and the couple refuse her money. Returning, she helps out when Reiko is injured, and decides she wants to learn the art of ramen.

Maezumi reluctantly agrees to teach her but treats her harshly and gives her menial work in the hope that she will give up. Abby perseveres, wins over the customers as a waitress and meets Toshi Iwamoto, a young businessman with whom she bonds over the unexpected turns their lives have taken. When Maezumi's rival Udagawa boasts that a Grand Master will soon judge whether his son is worthy to carry on his ramen tradition, Maezumi drunkenly promises that Abby will be tested too. Abby learns from Reiko that Maezumi has not spoken in years to their son Shintaro, who left to become a chef in Paris.

Toshi is transferred to Shanghai and asks Abby to go with him, but she stays. Insisting that her ramen has no soul, Maezumi takes her to his mother, who tells her she must cook from the heart. Abby makes her broth in tears, and the customers who taste it are moved to tears themselves. The Grand Master enjoys her unconventional creation but withholds his blessing, saying she needs more restraint. Maezumi nonetheless names her his true successor before closing his shop after forty-five years, and gives her the lantern from its door.

A year later Abby runs her own ramen shop in New York, where Toshi, who has quit his job to make music, finds her. Reviews were mixed, with critics describing it as a gentle but slight mix of The Karate Kid and Tampopo.

overview: An interpol agent and an attorney are determined to bring one of the world's most powerful banks to justice. Uncovering money laundering, arms trading, and conspiracy to destabilize world governments, their investigation takes them from Berlin, Milan, New York and Istanbul. Finding themselves in a chase across the globe, their relentless tenacity puts their own lives at risk.
tagline: Is your money making a killing?
title: The International
plot:
The International is an action thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of global politics and corruption. The story revolves around a secret organization within the United Nations, known as the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID), which harbors a sinister agenda.

At its core, The International explores the theme of power and control, highlighting how those in positions of authority will stop at nothing to maintain their grip on power. The film's protagonist, Narrator (played by Clive Owen), is a skilled operative who becomes embroiled in a complex web of deceit and corruption.

The movie also touches upon the theme of globalization and its consequences. The ICSID organization serves as a microcosm for the corrupting influence of power and money, demonstrating how institutions meant to promote international cooperation can be co-opted by those seeking personal gain.

Furthermore, The International critiques the notion of moral relativism, suggesting that even in the most seemingly neutral or humanitarian contexts, there exists a gray area where right and wrong become blurred. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, as the protagonist navigates a world where allegiances are constantly shifting and the lines between good and evil are intentionally obscured.

Overall, The International presents a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the corrupting influence of power.

overview: When a daughter becomes concerned about her mother's well-being in a retirement home, private investigator Romulo hires Sergio, an 83-year-old man who becomes a new resident—and a mole inside the home, who struggles to balance his assignment with becoming increasingly involved in the lives of several residents.
tagline: It's never too late to become a spy.
title: The Mole Agent
plot:
The Mole Agent is a 2020 documentary film that explores the life of an undercover agent who infiltrated the Japanese government's intelligence agency in the 1970s and 1980s. 

At its core, The Mole Agent delves into themes of deception, loyalty, and identity. It raises questions about the nature of truth and how it can be manipulated by those in power. The film also touches on the complexities of cultural exchange and the blurred lines between espionage and diplomacy.

Through the story of this undercover agent, who was tasked with gathering intelligence while pretending to be a loyal Japanese citizen, the documentary sheds light on the moral dilemmas that arise when individuals are forced to navigate multiple identities and allegiances. The film ultimately poses profound questions about the human condition, encouraging viewers to consider the consequences of deception and the importance of authenticity in our personal and professional lives.

The Mole Agent is a thought-provoking exploration of the gray areas between loyalty, duty, and self-preservation, leaving audiences with a deeper understanding of the complexities of espionage and the human cost of secrecy.

overview: Harry Sanborn is an aged music industry exec with a fondness for younger women like Marin, his latest trophy girlfriend. Things get a little awkward when Harry suffers a heart attack at the home of Marin's mother, Erica. Left in the care of Erica and his doctor, a love triangle starts to take shape.
tagline: Schmucks are people too.
title: Something's Gotta Give
plot:
Something's Gotta Give is a 2003 American romantic comedy film directed by Nancy Meyers, starring Jack Nicholson and Diane Keaton.

The movie revolves around Erica Barry (Diane Keaton), a successful author in her late 50s who has given up on love after a string of failed relationships. She is a self-centered, yet lovable woman who has built walls around herself to protect her heart.

Enter Harry Sanborn (Jack Nicholson), a wealthy and charming bachelor who becomes Erica's patient and confidant. As they spend more time together, Harry finds himself falling for Erica, but struggles with his own feelings of inadequacy and fear of commitment.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Love and vulnerability: The film explores the idea that love requires vulnerability and openness, which can be challenging for people like Erica who have built walls around themselves.
2. Self-discovery: As Erica and Harry navigate their relationship, they both undergo a journey of self-discovery, learning to let go of their past fears and insecurities.
3. Ageism: The movie tackles the theme of ageism, highlighting how society often perceives older people as being over the hill or no longer desirable. However, it shows that love can cross age boundaries and that people like Erica are still capable of experiencing deep connections.
4. Friendship: The film also explores the importance of friendship and the power of relationships in our lives.

The movie's plot development is driven by the slow-burning romance between Erica and Harry, as they navigate their feelings for each other amidst a backdrop of witty banter, comedic misunderstandings, and heartfelt moments.

Ultimately, the ending of the movie is a heartwarming one, as Erica and Harry find love in each other's arms, proving that it's never too late to experience true connection.

overview: Reincarnated 30 years after being killed in a suspicious on-set fire, a small-time actor is determined to punish the person who ignited the blaze.
tagline: For some dreams, one lifetime is not enough.
title: Om Shanti Om
plot:
Om Shanti Om is a 2007 Indian musical comedy film that explores the theme of reincarnation and the power of love. The movie delves into the idea of an eternal soul, which is reborn in different bodies, and how this concept can be used to understand human relationships.

The film's narrative revolves around the story of Om Kapoor (Shah Rukh Khan), a Bollywood actor who dies in a car accident and is reincarnated as a woman named Shanti. As Shanti, she falls in love with a young man named Virman (Salman Khan), but their love is threatened by the villainous character, Aryan (Vivek Oberoi).

Throughout the movie, the theme of reincarnation is woven into the narrative, as Om/Shanti's past and present lives become intertwined. The film also explores the idea of karma and how an individual's actions in one life can affect their future incarnations.

The main theme of Om Shanti Om is ultimately about the transformative power of love and the human spirit. Despite the complexities and challenges that come with reincarnation, the movie suggests that true love can conquer all, even death itself. The film's use of music, dance, and drama adds to its emotional impact, making it a memorable and engaging cinematic experience.

The movie also touches upon the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences and relationships. As Om/Shanti navigates her different lives, she must confront her own sense of self and learn to let go of her past in order to move forward.

Overall, Om Shanti Om is a film that celebrates the human spirit's capacity for love, forgiveness, and transformation, making it a timeless and captivating watch.

overview: Two couples meet for a painful and raw conversation in the aftermath of a violent tragedy.
title: Mass
plot:
Mass is a 2021 American drama film written and directed by Fran Kranz in his directorial debut. Reed Birney, Ann Dowd, Jason Isaacs and Martha Plimpton star as two couples who meet years after a school shooting in which the son of one couple killed the son of the other. Set almost entirely in one room, it premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 30, 2021, and was released by Bleecker Street on October 8, 2021.

Six years after a high school shooting, Jay and Gail Perry, whose son Evan was among those killed, agree to meet Richard and Linda, the parents of the teenage gunman, Hayden, who killed himself after the attack. Their meeting is arranged in a quiet back room of an Episcopal church, with a church worker nervously preparing the space. The couples have met before, during the legal proceedings that followed the shooting, when Jay and Gail spoke harshly to the other parents, and Jay has since become a public advocate for gun control.

After awkward small talk and memories of their sons as young children, the conversation turns to how the tragedy happened. Jay and Gail press for details of Hayden's upbringing beyond what the public already knows. Richard and Linda describe his growing depression after the family moved, his isolation, and the bullying he suffered, and they argue briefly over the influence of violent video games. While noting that schools and therapists failed to act on warning signs, they acknowledge their own guilt at not seeing what their son was becoming.

The talk grows heated. Jay and Gail admit they wanted Richard and Linda to suffer as much as the victims' families did. When the other couple reveal that Hayden had friends who were also bullied, one of whom had access to guns, Jay explodes, suggesting that Hayden was simply a psychopath, before breaking down as he describes how Evan died. Linda tells them about a notebook in which Hayden planned the attack, and explains that she and Richard held a funeral to mourn the boy they had loved before his crime.

When Linda asks to hear about Evan, Gail shares a happy memory of him at twelve and finally forgives Hayden and his parents, and the four hold hands in silence. As they leave, Linda returns to tell Gail how afraid she once was of Hayden. Jay is overcome by the sound of a choir rehearsing nearby. The film was acclaimed for its acting and writing, with 95% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and Dowd received a BAFTA nomination for Best Supporting Actress.

overview: After proving himself on the field of battle in the French and Indian War, Benjamin Martin wants nothing more to do with such things, preferring the simple life of a farmer. But when his son Gabriel enlists in the army to defend their new nation, America, against the British, Benjamin reluctantly returns to his old life to protect his son.
tagline: Some things are worth fighting for.
title: The Patriot
plot:
The Patriot is a historical drama film directed by Roland Emmerich, released in 2000 by Columbia Pictures.

The movie takes place during the American Revolutionary War and follows the story of Benjamin Martin (played by Mel Gibson), a widowed farmer who lives on his plantation in South Carolina with his two sons, Gabriel (Heath Ledger) and William (Jason Isaacs). The family is struggling to survive due to the British occupation of their land.

When the British army arrives at the Martin farm, they demand that Benjamin's sons join the British Army as loyalists. However, Benjamin refuses to send his sons, citing his loyalty to the American cause. Gabriel, who has been trained in combat by Benjamin, is particularly resistant to joining the British Army and instead decides to fight for the Americans.

As tensions rise between the British and the Americans, Benjamin's farm becomes a target for British raids. The family is forced to flee their home, and Benjamin's sons are captured by the British. Gabriel is eventually killed in battle, while William is taken prisoner and later executed by the British for his involvement with the American resistance.

Consumed by grief and anger, Benjamin sets out on a mission of revenge against the British army that killed his son. He joins the Continental Army and becomes a key figure in the war effort, using his knowledge of the land and his combat skills to help the Americans defeat the British.

As the war rages on, Benjamin's actions become increasingly radicalized, leading him to take drastic measures to protect his fellow soldiers and avenge his son's death. The movie culminates with a dramatic battle between the Continental Army and the British at Cowpens, where Benjamin plays a crucial role in the American victory.

Throughout the film, Mel Gibson delivers a powerful performance as Benjamin Martin, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Jason Isaacs and Miranda Richardson, also deliver strong performances that add to the overall tension and drama of the movie.

Overall, The Patriot is a gripping historical drama that explores themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and revenge in the context of the American Revolutionary War. With its stunning action sequences, memorable characters, and epic scope, it's no wonder that this film has become a classic of the genre.

overview: After a tragic accident, six friends reunite for a caving expedition. Their adventure soon goes horribly wrong when a collapse traps them deep underground and they find themselves pursued by bloodthirsty creatures. As their friendships deteriorate, they find themselves in a desperate struggle to survive the creatures and each other.
tagline: Scream your last breath.
title: The Descent
plot:
The Descent is a 2005 British horror film directed by Neil Marshall and produced by Celador Films. The movie follows a group of six women who embark on a caving expedition in the Appalachian Mountains, only to find themselves trapped and hunted by subterranean creatures.

The story begins with Sarah (Shauna Macdonald), a former rock climber who has lost her sense of purpose after a tragic accident that killed her friends. She joins an all-female caving expedition led by Juno (Natalie Mendoza) to the Appalachian Mountains, where they plan to explore an abandoned cave system.

The group consists of Sarah's friend Rebecca (Saskia Mulder), Juno, Beth (Alex Reid), Chris (Nikki Graham), and Holly (Jenny McAlpine). As they venture deeper into the caves, they discover a hidden underground chamber filled with ancient fossils and strange rock formations. However, their excitement is short-lived, as they soon realize that they are not alone in the cave.

The group begins to experience strange occurrences, including hearing eerie sounds and finding signs of recent habitation. They soon discover that the creatures are humanoid in appearance, but have been mutated by some unknown force to live in the dark depths of the cave system.

As the group tries to find a way out of the caves, they realize that one of their own members has been infected with the creatures' venom, which is slowly turning her into one of them. The group's dynamics begin to deteriorate as tensions rise and paranoia sets in.

The creatures, known as "crawlers," are fast-moving and deadly, using their sharp claws and teeth to attack their prey. The group soon realizes that they must work together to survive, but their efforts are hindered by the claustrophobic environment of the cave system.

As the body count rises, Sarah becomes increasingly determined to find a way out of the caves and rescue her friends. She leads the group on a perilous journey through the tunnels, facing numerous challenges and terrifying encounters with the creatures.

In the end, only two members of the group manage to escape the caves: Sarah and Juno. They emerge from the cave system, battered and traumatized, but alive. The movie ends with Sarah reflecting on her experience, realizing that she has found a new sense of purpose in life and a deeper appreciation for the beauty and danger of the natural world.

Overall, The Descent is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of female empowerment, friendship, and survival in the face of overwhelming odds.

overview: Surly, a curmudgeon, independent squirrel is banished from his park and forced to survive in the city. Lucky for him, he stumbles on the one thing that may be able to save his life, and the rest of park community, as they gear up for winter - Maury's Nut Store.
tagline: Let's Get Nuts!
title: The Nut Job
plot:
The Nut Job is an animated comedy film that revolves around the story of Surly, a grumpy but lovable squirrel who lives in a park filled with anthropomorphic animals. The movie explores several themes, primarily centered around friendship and community.

At its core, The Nut Job is a heartwarming tale about the power of unlikely friendships and the importance of coming together to overcome adversity. Surly, initially portrayed as an outcast due to his gruff demeanor, finds common ground with a group of misfit animals who share his disdain for the park's tyrannical leader, Rancid Rabbit.

Through their adventures, the characters learn valuable lessons about acceptance, empathy, and the value of having friends by your side. The film also touches on themes of loneliness and isolation, as Surly struggles to connect with others due to his prickly exterior.

Furthermore, The Nut Job features a narrative that critiques consumerism and materialism, particularly in the character of Rancid Rabbit, who seeks to exploit the park's resources for personal gain. This serves as a commentary on the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of preserving natural habitats.

Overall, The Nut Job is a lighthearted, entertaining film that celebrates the beauty of friendship and community, while also offering a subtle critique of societal issues.
