overview: A young nurse, Alma, is put in charge of Elisabeth Vogler: an actress who is seemingly healthy in all respects, but will not talk. As they spend time together, Alma speaks to Elisabeth constantly, never receiving any answer. The time they spend together only strengthens the crushing realization that one does not exist.
title: Persona
plot:
Persona is a 1966 Swedish psychological drama written, directed and produced by Ingmar Bergman. Bibi Andersson stars as the young nurse Alma and Liv Ullmann as Elisabet Vogler, a celebrated actress who has suddenly stopped speaking, with Margaretha Krook, Gunnar Björnstrand and Jörgen Lindström. A landmark of modernist cinema, its exploration of identity, duality and the act of filmmaking itself has been the subject of extensive critical debate, and it is often ranked among the greatest films ever made.

The film opens with a rapid montage as a projector starts up, including images of a crucifixion, a spider and the slaughter of a lamb, before a boy wakes in what looks like a hospital or morgue and reaches towards a blurred image of two women's faces. Elisabet Vogler fell silent in the middle of a performance of Electra, and doctors conclude that her muteness is an act of will rather than illness. Alma is assigned to care for her. In the hospital Elisabet is horrified by television footage of a monk burning himself in protest during the Vietnam War, and she tears up a photograph of her son sent by her husband.

The doctor sends the two women to her seaside cottage to recover. There Alma, flattered by Elisabet's attentive silence, talks freely about herself, her fiancé Karl-Henrik and, in a long confession, an erotic encounter on a beach with another woman and two boys, which left her pregnant and led to an abortion she still regrets.

When Alma reads a letter Elisabet has written, she discovers that the actress has been studying her and repeating her secrets. Hurt and angry, Alma turns on her, almost scalding her with boiling water, which makes Elisabet cry out. The film itself appears to tear and burn before resuming. The women's identities increasingly blur: Elisabet's husband arrives and, addressing Alma as his wife, sleeps with her. Alma recounts Elisabet's own story, of how she longed to be a mother, tried to end her pregnancy and came to despise the son who craves her love, and as she speaks their faces merge into a single image.

Alma insists that she is not Elisabet, coaxes her to say the word "nothing", and leaves the cottage, as a film crew is glimpsed and the projector winds down. Persona received favourable reviews on release and is now regarded as one of Bergman's masterpieces.

overview: Five people travelling by camper crash into a tree. When they recover, the road they were driving on has been replaced by an impenetrable forest and a wooden house.
title: A Classic Horror Story
plot:
A Classic Horror Story is a 2021 Italian horror film directed by Roberto De Feo and Paolo Strippoli, who wrote it with Lucio Besana, David Bellini and Milo Tissone. It stars Matilda Lutz, Francesco Russo, Peppino Mazzotta, Will Merrick and Yuliia Sobol. Netflix released the film worldwide on 14 July 2021.

Elisa, a young woman uncertain about her decision to end a pregnancy, arranges a ride-share to her family's home in Calabria, where she is scheduled to have an abortion. She joins a camper van driven by Fabrizio, a film-obsessed travel blogger, along with Riccardo, a doctor, and Sofia and Mark, an outgoing couple. When Elisa's morning sickness forces them to pull over, Mark takes the wheel. That night, drinking as he drives, he swerves to avoid a dead animal in the road and crashes into a tree.

When Elisa wakes the next morning, the others are treating Mark's broken leg, and the group realizes that the road has vanished: they are now in a clearing surrounded by dense forest, with no explanation of how they got there. In the clearing stands a rustic wooden house. Exploring nearby, Fabrizio and Riccardo find a grotesque altar with three crucified, pig-headed figures, while inside the house Elisa discovers a mural depicting three figures from local legend, Osso, Mastrosso and Carcagnosso, venerated by a secret society that offers human sacrifices in exchange for prosperity. That night, screams from the house draw most of the group inside, where they find a girl imprisoned in a cocoon of straw, her tongue cut out. As masked figures emerge from the woods and the travelers are subjected to brutal rituals one by one, Elisa fights to survive and uncovers a twist that reframes everything that has happened, with the film commenting on horror conventions and Italian society.

The film received mixed reviews from critics, with a 58 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on twelve reviews. Reviewers praised its visual style and atmosphere, which draw openly on folk horror and on familiar genre classics, while some found its self-aware ending divisive. In July 2021, The New York Times included it among its top five horror films to stream.

overview: It’s the dawn of a new age of heroes, and Metropolis has just met its first. But as Daily Planet intern Clark Kent – working alongside reporter Lois Lane – secretly wields his alien powers of flight, super-strength and x-ray vision in the battle for good, there’s even greater trouble on the horizon.
tagline: Before he was the Man of Steel, he was the Man of Tomorrow.
title: Superman: Man of Tomorrow
plot:
Superman: Man of Tomorrow is a 2020 animated superhero film based on the DC Comics character Superman. The movie follows Kal-El, an alien from the planet Krypton who is sent to Earth as an infant and adopted by Jonathan and Martha Kent.

The main themes of Superman: Man of Tomorrow include:

1. Coming of Age: The movie explores Kal's journey from a young boy to a young man, as he navigates his powers, identity, and responsibilities.
2. Identity Crisis: Kal struggles with his dual identity as an alien and a human, leading to feelings of isolation and disconnection from those around him.
3. Family and Belonging: The movie highlights the importance of family and finding one's place in the world. Kal's relationships with his adoptive parents and later with Lois Lane are central to the story.
4. Power and Responsibility: As Kal discovers his powers, he must learn to control them and use them for the greater good, rather than letting them consume him.
5. Self-Discovery: Throughout the movie, Kal grapples with questions of who he is, where he comes from, and what his purpose is.

The film's narrative is driven by Kal's growth and self-discovery, as he learns to balance his Kryptonian heritage with his human upbringing and values. The movie features a mix of action, adventure, and coming-of-age themes, making it a unique take on the Superman character.

Overall, Superman: Man of Tomorrow offers a fresh and exciting interpretation of the iconic superhero, exploring themes that are both timeless and timely.

overview: When a husband and wife move to a small town, a home invasion leaves the wife traumatized and suspicious that those around her might not be who they seem.
tagline: The quietest towns hide the darkest secrets.
title: Intrusion
plot:
Intrusion is a 2021 American psychological thriller directed by Adam Salky and written by Christopher Sparling, starring Freida Pinto as Meera Parsons and Logan Marshall-Green as her husband Henry, with Robert John Burke as Detective Stephen Morse. The film follows a couple whose new life in the New Mexico desert is shattered by a violent home invasion.

Seeking a quieter life away from Boston, Meera, a therapist, and Henry, an architect, move into an isolated, ultramodern house that Henry designed and built in Corrales, New Mexico. Shortly after their arrival, their home is burglarized, though only a laptop and their phones are stolen. A few nights later, masked intruders return, tie up Meera and pursue the couple through the house, until Henry uses a handgun he had secretly kept to kill two of the men. The third is critically wounded and taken to the hospital.

The police tell the couple that the intruders belonged to a family with a criminal history and are suspected in the disappearance of a young relative, college student Christine Cobb, a case that may never be solved unless the surviving man recovers. Meera, a cancer survivor, is deeply traumatized, while Henry urges her to move on. When the surviving intruder dies and Meera notices that Henry lied about where he went that night, her suspicions grow. Investigating on her own, she discovers that the intruders had worked on the construction of the house, and Henry offers an explanation involving financial fraud and blackmail. A videotape recorded by one of the intruders, however, leads Meera to a terrible secret hidden within the house itself, and she discovers that the man she married is far more dangerous than the strangers who broke in.

The film explores trust, trauma and the idea of the home as a place of hidden danger, building toward a final confrontation between husband and wife.

Intrusion was released by Netflix on September 22, 2021. It received negative reviews, with 23 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 39.

overview: This film, adapted from a work of fiction by author Tracy Chevalier, tells a story about the events surrounding the creation of the painting "Girl With A Pearl Earring" by 17th century Dutch master Johannes Vermeer. A young peasant maid working in the house of painter Johannes Vermeer becomes his talented assistant and the model for one of his most famous works.
tagline: Discover the mystery behind the legend.
title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
plot:
"Girl with a Pearl Earring" (2003) is a historical drama film directed by Peter Webber, produced by Wild B bear Films, and based on the novel of the same name by Tracy Chevalier.

The main themes of "Girl with a Pearl Earring" include:

1. **Beauty and Identity**: The film explores the concept of beauty and how it can be both captivating and suffocating. The protagonist, Griet (played by Scarlett Johansson), is a young Dutch girl who becomes a model for Johannes Vermeer's paintings, including the famous "Girl with a Pearl Earring." As she navigates her new role, she must confront the tension between her own identity and the idealized image of beauty imposed upon her.

2. **Social Class and Status**: The film highlights the social hierarchy of 17th-century Holland, where the wealthy elite held power and influence. Vermeer's studio is a microcosm of this class system, with Griet representing the lower-class servant who becomes embroiled in the lives of the aristocratic family.

3. **Art and Creativity**: The movie celebrates the artistic process and the creative relationship between the artist (Vermeer) and his subject (Griet). Through Vermeer's paintings, the film explores the themes of beauty, light, and shadow, as well as the emotional connections between the artist and his models.

4. **Forbidden Love and Desire**: As Griet becomes more deeply involved with Vermeer, she begins to experience forbidden desires that threaten her relationships with those around her. The film's portrayal of their complex and nuanced relationship raises questions about the nature of love, desire, and power dynamics in a patriarchal society.

5. **Feminism and Empowerment**: Through Griet's character, the film offers a feminist perspective on the experiences of women in 17th-century Holland. As she navigates her role as a model and a servant, Griet begins to assert her own agency and desires, challenging the societal norms that restrict her.

Overall, "Girl with a Pearl Earring" is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of beauty, identity, social class, art, desire, and feminism in 17th-century Holland.

original_title: LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace
overview: Master Yoda must go retrieve secret battle plans. However, things become a little more complicated when a class of younglings join the mission.
tagline: Star Wars and The LEGO Group join forces.
title: LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace
plot:
LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace is an animated adventure that delves into the world of young Jedi Knights, particularly Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi. At its core, this film explores the complexities of friendship, loyalty, and the struggle between good and evil.

The movie highlights the strong bond between Anakin and Obi-Wan, showcasing their camaraderie as they navigate the challenges of being young Jedi. Their relationship is built on trust, mutual respect, and a deep understanding of one another's strengths and weaknesses. This dynamic is beautifully captured in the film, allowing viewers to witness the early stages of their iconic partnership.

As Anakin navigates his journey from Padawan to Knight, he faces numerous trials that test his resolve and force him to confront the harsh realities of being a hero. The film masterfully conveys the sense of vulnerability and self-doubt that often accompanies growth and development, making Anakin's character arc both relatable and compelling.

The movie also explores the theme of mentorship, as Obi-Wan serves as a guiding light for Anakin, teaching him valuable lessons about discipline, responsibility, and the importance of following one's conscience. This dynamic is particularly noteworthy, as it sets the stage for their later relationship in the Star Wars saga.

Furthermore, The Padawan Menace touches on the idea of identity and self-discovery. As Anakin grapples with his own destiny and the expectations placed upon him, he must come to terms with who he is and what he wants to become. This internal conflict is skillfully woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and nuance to the story.

Ultimately, LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace is a heartwarming and action-packed adventure that celebrates the power of friendship, loyalty, and personal growth. By exploring these themes through the eyes of Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi, the film provides a unique perspective on the Star Wars universe, one that is both nostalgic and endearing.

overview: When dictator Joseph Stalin dies, his parasitic cronies square off in a frantic power struggle to become the next Soviet leader. As they bumble, brawl and back-stab their way to the top, the question remains — just who is running the government?
tagline: In the Kremlin, no one can hear you scheme
title: The Death of Stalin
plot:
The Death of Stalin is a dark comedy that delves into the power struggle and paranoia that ensued after the death of Soviet leader Joseph Stalin in 1953. The film masterfully weaves together the intricate web of relationships between Stalin's inner circle, exposing their ruthless ambition, deceit, and desperation to maintain control.

At its core, the movie is a scathing critique of totalitarianism, exploring the themes of power, corruption, and the dangers of unchecked ambition. As the characters navigate the treacherous landscape of Stalin's death, they reveal their true selves, showcasing the depths of human depravity and the lengths to which people will go to achieve power.

The film also touches on the theme of identity, as the characters struggle to define themselves in a world where loyalty is a luxury few can afford. The movie's use of satire and absurdity serves to highlight the absurdity of the situation, making it difficult for the viewer not to laugh at the sheer audacity of these characters.

Furthermore, The Death of Stalin explores the theme of mortality, as the characters confront their own mortality and the fragility of life. This is particularly evident in the character of Nikita Khrushchev, who must navigate the treacherous waters of Stalin's death to emerge as a viable successor.

Overall, The Death of Stalin is a masterful exploration of the human condition, offering a darkly comedic commentary on the dangers of unchecked power and the corrupting influence it can have on individuals.

overview: Irresponsible party girl, Maggie is kicked out of her father's and stepmother's home—where she lives for free—and is taken in by her hard-working sister, Philadelphia lawyer, Rose. After Maggie's disruptive ways ruin her sister's love life, Rose turns her out as well. But when their grandmother, who they never knew existed, comes into their lives, the sisters face some complicated truths about themselves and their family.
tagline: Friends. Rivals. Sisters.
title: In Her Shoes
plot:
In Her Shoes is a poignant and heartwarming drama that explores the complexities of family relationships, identity, and self-discovery. The film delves into the intricate web of emotions between two sisters, Maggie (played by Toni Collette) and Rose (played by Shirley MacLaine), as they navigate their way through life's challenges.

At its core, In Her Shoes is a story about the unbreakable bond between sisters, despite their differences. The film masterfully portrays the complexities of sibling relationships, where love, resentment, and forgiveness are intertwined like the threads of a rich tapestry. As Maggie struggles to come to terms with her own identity and find her place in the world, she finds solace in Rose's unconventional wisdom and unwavering support.

The movie also explores themes of grief, loss, and healing, as both sisters grapple with their own personal demons. Through their journey, the film sheds light on the importance of embracing vulnerability, letting go of past hurts, and finding the courage to be true to oneself.

One of the most striking aspects of In Her Shoes is its nuanced portrayal of mother-daughter relationships. The complex dynamics between Maggie's mother (played by Allison Janney) and her own daughter are expertly woven into the narrative, adding depth and richness to the story.

Ultimately, In Her Shoes is a film about finding one's own path in life, embracing imperfection, and discovering the power of love and forgiveness. With its talented ensemble cast, witty dialogue, and poignant storytelling, this movie has become a beloved classic that continues to resonate with audiences today.

overview: South Africa, 1978. Tim Jenkin and Stephen Lee, two white political activists from the African National Congress imprisoned by the apartheid regime, put a plan in motion to escape from the infamous Pretoria Prison.
tagline: Survival is key
title: Escape from Pretoria
plot:
Escape from Pretoria is a 2020 South African biographical drama film directed by Rilett van der Ryst, based on the memoir "No Place to Hide" by Tim Jenkin. The movie tells the true story of Tim Jenkin (played by Daniel Radcliffe), a white South African anti-apartheid activist who was arrested and imprisoned in Pretoria Maximum Security Prison in 1979.

The film begins with Tim Jenkin, a young and idealistic anti-apartheid activist, who is part of the Black Consciousness Movement. He becomes involved in a plot to escape from prison, which is led by his fellow inmate, Nelson Mandela (played by John Cusack). The plan involves digging a tunnel using makeshift tools, such as a spoon and a piece of metal.

As the story unfolds, Tim Jenkin's character faces numerous challenges, including the harsh conditions of the prison, the corruption of some of the guards, and the skepticism of his fellow inmates. Despite these obstacles, he perseveres and eventually becomes an expert tunnel digger.

The plot development is tense and suspenseful, as Tim Jenkin navigates the complexities of prison life while trying to stay one step ahead of the authorities. The film also explores the themes of hope, resilience, and the power of the human spirit in the face of oppression.

As the escape plan nears its climax, Tim Jenkin's character faces a series of setbacks, including the discovery of his tunnel by the prison guards. However, he refuses to give up and continues to work on the tunnel, using his skills and ingenuity to overcome the obstacles.

The ending is both thrilling and emotional, as Tim Jenkin finally escapes from prison, but not without consequences. The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as Tim Jenkin looks towards a future where he can continue to fight against apartheid.

Overall, Escape from Pretoria is a gripping and inspiring true story that highlights the bravery and determination of Tim Jenkin and other anti-apartheid activists who risked everything to fight for their freedom. The film features strong performances from its cast, particularly Daniel Radcliffe as Tim Jenkin, and is directed with skill and sensitivity by Rilett van der Ryst.

[No additional information available]

overview: Gang leader Tony pulls off a major diamond heist with his crew, but cop-turned-criminal Ling knows who has the loot and responds by kidnapping Tony's daughter and holding her for ransom. Unfortunately, Tony's lost the diamonds as well. As he frantically searches for his daughter and the jewels, Tony pairs with a high-kicking government agent who once worked with Ling and seeks revenge on him.
tagline: Mortal enemies make dangerous friends.
title: Cradle 2 the Grave
plot:
Cradle 2 the Grave is an action-adventure film released in 2003, directed by Andrzej Bartkowiak and starring Jet Li, DMX, and Gabrielle Union.

The main themes of Cradle 2 the Grave revolve around:

1. Family: The movie explores the theme of family, particularly the bond between a father and daughter. Nick (Jet Li) is a former Special Forces operative who must protect his daughter, Sophie (Gina Lee), from her mother's ruthless ex-boyfriend, Verona (DMX).
2. Loyalty and Betrayal: Throughout the film, characters are forced to confront their loyalties and make difficult choices between personal relationships and professional obligations.
3. Redemption: Nick's character arc is centered around redemption, as he seeks to atone for past mistakes and protect those he cares about.
4. Power and Corruption: The villainous Verona (DMX) serves as a symbol of the corrupting influence of power, highlighting the dangers of unchecked ambition and greed.

The plot follows Nick, who is hired by Sophie's mother to retrieve a valuable artifact from Verona, who has stolen it. As the story unfolds, Nick must navigate a complex web of loyalty, deception, and betrayal to protect his daughter and uncover the truth about her past.

Overall, Cradle 2 the Grave is an action-packed film with a strong emphasis on family, loyalty, and redemption, set against a backdrop of corruption and power struggles.

overview: A young woman quits her teaching job to be a private tutor for two wealthy young kids, but soon starts to suspect there’s more to their house than what meets the eye.
tagline: Watch the children with care.
title: The Turning
plot:
The Turning is a 2020 American gothic supernatural horror film directed by Floria Sigismondi and written by Carey W. Hayes and Chad Hayes, a modern adaptation of Henry James's 1898 novella The Turn of the Screw. Mackenzie Davis stars as a young governess, with Finn Wolfhard and Brooklynn Prince as her charges and Joely Richardson as her mother. It was filmed at Killruddery House in Ireland.

In 1994, after the previous tutor, Miss Jessel, has left, Kate Mandell takes a job as live-in governess to seven-year-old Flora Fairchild, an orphan who lives on a vast, isolated estate after witnessing her parents' deaths in a car accident. Before leaving, Kate visits her mother, Darla, an artist confined to a psychiatric institution. At the estate, the stern housekeeper Mrs. Grose explains that Flora is a "special case" who never leaves the grounds, and Flora begs Kate never to abandon her. Soon Flora's older brother, Miles, returns after being expelled from boarding school for violently attacking another boy. The children's pranks unsettle Kate.

Strange noises and apparitions begin to haunt Kate at night. She learns that the riding instructor, Peter Quint, died in a fall from his horse shortly after Miss Jessel left, and she finds Miss Jessel's diary, which describes Quint's obsession with her and how he photographed her as she slept. Kate becomes convinced that the ghosts of Quint and Miss Jessel walk the house, and her fear grows into paranoia. After receiving a package of her mother's artwork and hearing Mrs. Grose hope that Darla's condition is not hereditary, Kate discovers Miss Jessel's body in a pond and has a vision of Quint murdering her. When Quint's ghost appears to kill Mrs. Grose, Kate flees with the children.

This escape, however, is revealed to have been a vision. Kate insists that she and Flora have seen Quint, but Miles calls her delusional. The film ends abruptly as Kate, in her mind, walks into her mother's institution and approaches a figure whose face is never shown, screaming as it turns toward her, leaving open whether the haunting was real or a sign of inherited madness.

Released by Universal Pictures on January 24, 2020, The Turning was panned by critics, who criticized its muddled, ambiguous ending; Rotten Tomatoes reported 12% approval, and audiences gave it a rare "F" CinemaScore. It grossed about $19 million worldwide against a $14 million budget.

original_title: るろうに剣心 最終章 The Beginning
overview: Before he was a protector, Kenshin was a fearsome assassin known as Battosai. But when he meets gentle Tomoe Yukishiro, a beautiful young woman who carries a huge burden in her heart, his life will change forever.
title: Rurouni Kenshin: The Beginning
plot:
Rurouni Kenshin: The Beginning (Japanese: るろうに剣心 最終章 The Beginning) is a 2021 Japanese jidaigeki action film written and directed by Keishi Ōtomo and based on Nobuhiro Watsuki's manga Rurouni Kenshin. The fifth and final installment of the live-action film series and a prequel to the earlier films, it depicts Himura Kenshin's origins as the feared assassin known as Hitokiri Battōsai and his relationship with Yukishiro Tomoe. Takeru Satoh stars as Kenshin, with Kasumi Arimura as Tomoe, Issey Takahashi, Nijiro Murakami and Masanobu Ando. Produced alongside Rurouni Kenshin: The Final, which opened two months earlier, it was released in Japan by Warner Bros. Pictures on 4 June 2021 and later streamed internationally on Netflix.

In Kyoto during the Bakumatsu period, as revolutionary forces seek to overthrow the Tokugawa shogunate, the young swordsman Himura Kenshin serves the Chōshū clan as an assassin under its leader, Katsura Kogorō, working with the clan's agent Iizuka. During one killing, a dying bodyguard leaves a cross-shaped scar on Kenshin's cheek. One evening at a tavern, Kenshin intervenes when self-proclaimed revolutionaries harass a woman named Yukishiro Tomoe. He is then attacked by an assassin, whom he kills, and finds Tomoe watching him in the aftermath.

Kenshin takes Tomoe back to the inn that serves as a hideout for Chōshū revolutionaries, where she decides to stay and work. Her quiet questions about why he kills unsettle his convictions, and Katsura wonders how she will affect him. During the Ikedaya incident of 1864, when the Shinsengumi police raid a gathering of rebels, Kenshin rushes to rescue Katsura but is delayed by the Shinsengumi captain Okita Sōji. With the Chōshū forced into hiding, Kenshin and Tomoe retreat to a farmhouse in the countryside, posing as a married couple, and gradually fall in love. Tomoe, however, hides a painful connection to one of the men Kenshin has killed, and the shogunate's secret agents are closing in, setting Kenshin on a tragic path that explains the scar he bears and his later vow never to kill again.

The film opened at number one at the Japanese box office, with Rurouni Kenshin: The Final in second place, making it the first franchise to hold the top two spots in the same weekend. It grossed over $21 million in Japan and was praised by critics, including Anime News Network, for its action choreography and emotional weight.

overview: Kubo mesmerizes the people in his village with his magical gift for spinning wild tales with origami. When he accidentally summons an evil spirit seeking vengeance, Kubo is forced to go on a quest to solve the mystery of his fallen samurai father and his mystical weaponry, as well as discover his own magical powers.
tagline: The quest begins
title: Kubo and the Two Strings
plot:
Kubo and the Two Strings is a stop-motion animated fantasy adventure film directed by Travis Knight and produced by Laika Entertainment, Aardman Animations, and Legendary Pictures. The movie was released in 2016 to critical acclaim.

In ancient Japan, Kubo (voiced by Art Parkinson) is a young boy who possesses supernatural abilities passed down from his father, the samurai Beetle (voiced by Ralph Fiennes). After his father's death at the hands of the evil Moon King (voiced by Matthew McConaughey), Kubo sets out on a journey to find the legendary Sword of Daito, which will allow him to defeat the Moon King and bring peace back to his village.

Kubo's quest is fraught with danger as he encounters various creatures from Japanese mythology, including the Wind Spirit (voiced by Rooney Mara) and the Beetle Sisters (voiced by Brenda Vaccaro and Tilda Swinton). Along the way, Kubo meets a group of bumbling but lovable warriors known as the Beetle Brothers, who are on a mission to find the Sword of Daito.

As Kubo navigates this treacherous landscape, he must confront his own identity and the secrets of his family's past. The film features stunning animation, with intricate details and textures that bring the world of Japanese mythology to life.

Throughout the movie, Kubo faces numerous challenges as he battles against the Moon King's minions and uncovers the truth about his father's death. Along the way, he discovers that the Sword of Daito is not just a simple weapon, but a powerful symbol of hope and redemption.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Kubo and the Moon King, with Kubo using all of his skills and abilities to defeat the villainous Moon King. In the end, Kubo emerges victorious, but not without scars, both physical and emotional.

One of the standout aspects of Kubo and the Two Strings is its thoughtful exploration of themes such as identity, family, and redemption. The film features a richly detailed world that draws heavily from Japanese mythology, while also incorporating elements of Western fantasy.

Overall, Kubo and the Two Strings is a beautifully crafted film that combines stunning animation with a compelling narrative. With its richly detailed world and memorable characters, it's no wonder that this movie has become a modern classic in the world of stop-motion animation.

overview: The evil Queen Bavmorda hunts the newborn princess Elora Danan, a child prophesied to bring about her downfall. When the royal infant is found by Willow, a timid farmer and aspiring sorcerer, he's entrusted with delivering her from evil.
tagline: Adventure doesn't come any bigger than this.
title: Willow
plot:
Willow is a 1988 American high fantasy film directed by Ron Howard, produced by George Lucas, and written by Bob Dolman.

In a mystical realm, a young farmer named Willow Ufgood lives on the outskirts of a village with his adoptive family. Willow's life takes an unexpected turn when a sorceress named Madmartigan arrives at their doorstep, seeking refuge from the evil Queen Bavmorda, who is determined to destroy all newborns with magical abilities.

The queen believes that the child will grow up to be a powerful sorcerer and use his powers for evil. Willow's adoptive mother dies soon after giving birth to her son, and Willow takes on the responsibility of caring for him. However, when Madmartigan arrives, he convinces Willow to take the infant to the safety of the Sorceress Elora Danan, who is said to be able to protect the child from the queen's wrath.

As they embark on their perilous journey, Willow and Madmartigan encounter various obstacles, including fierce creatures, treacherous landscapes, and rival sorcerers. Along the way, Willow discovers his own hidden potential as a sorcerer and forms an unlikely bond with Elora Danan, who becomes a mentor to him.

Throughout their quest, Willow must confront his own identity and the true nature of his destiny. He learns that he is not just a simple farmer but a chosen one, destined to wield great power and protect the child from those who seek to harm him.

The film features a richly detailed world, memorable characters, and a narrative that explores themes of friendship, sacrifice, and self-discovery. The special effects, although dated by today's standards, still hold up remarkably well, bringing the fantastical creatures and landscapes to life in a way that immerses the viewer in the world of Willow.

Overall, Willow is a classic fantasy film that has captivated audiences for decades with its engaging story, memorable characters, and stunning visuals.

overview: A reporter on the trail of a sinister cult wakes up in a morgue to find herself a member of the undead. She goes on a personal vendetta for a group a cultists that are responsible for her death.
tagline: They didn't leave her alive. They left her UNDEAD.
title: Rise: Blood Hunter
plot:
Rise: Blood Hunter is an action-horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the struggle between good and evil. The movie follows a vampire hunter, Dr. Linda Weatherly, who must confront her own demons as she battles against a powerful and ancient bloodsucker.

At its core, Rise: Blood Hunter explores the theme of redemption and personal growth. Dr. Weatherly's character arc is one of self-discovery and transformation, as she grapples with her past mistakes and learns to come to terms with her true nature. This internal struggle serves as a metaphor for the human condition, where individuals must confront their own flaws and weaknesses in order to become better versions of themselves.

The film also touches on the idea of obsession and fixation. Dr. Weatherly's singular focus on hunting vampires becomes an all-consuming passion that drives her to take risks and push herself to the limit. This obsessive behavior serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of single-minded dedication, highlighting the importance of balance and moderation in life.

Furthermore, Rise: Blood Hunter features a rich tapestry of themes related to immortality, power, and corruption. The vampire's existence is portrayed as a curse that brings both benefits and drawbacks, serving as a commentary on the human desire for eternal life and the corrupting influence it can have on individuals.

overview: A young man raised by scientists on Mars returns to Earth to find his father.
tagline: What's your favorite thing about Earth?
title: The Space Between Us
plot:
The Space Between Us is a 2017 American romantic science fiction film directed by Peter Chelsom and written by Matt Sazama and Burk Sharpless. The movie stars Asa Butterfield, Britt Robertson, and Natalie Dormer.

The main themes of The Space Between Us revolve around love, identity, class differences, and the human condition. Here's a brief overview:

**Beginning:** The film opens with Miguel (Asa Butterfield), a young man living on Mars Colony Alpha, where he was born to a wealthy family. He dreams of visiting Earth, which is forbidden due to its toxic environment.

**Plot Development:** Miguel travels to Earth and meets Ava (Britt Robertson), a free-spirited woman who challenges his privileged upbringing. As they fall in love, Miguel must confront the harsh realities of his new life on Earth and the consequences of his family's wealth and influence.

**Ending:** The movie culminates with Miguel and Ava facing the challenges of their relationship, including the class differences between them. Ultimately, they find a way to be together, but not without sacrifices. The film ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that love can conquer even the most daunting obstacles.

Throughout the movie, the themes of identity, class, and social inequality are explored through Miguel's journey from his privileged Martian upbringing to his experiences on Earth. The film also touches on the idea of what it means to be human in a world where technology has created new forms of life and society.

Overall, The Space Between Us is a romantic drama that explores complex themes and emotions, with a unique blend of science fiction and social commentary.

overview: Set in the futuristic landscape of Los Angeles on July 4, 2008, as it stands on the brink of social, economic and environmental disaster. Boxer Santaros is an action star who's stricken with amnesia. His life intertwines with Krysta Now, an adult film star developing her own reality television project, and Ronald Taverner, a Hermosa Beach police officer who holds the key to a vast conspiracy.
tagline: Have a nice apocalypse.
title: Southland Tales
plot:
Southland Tales is a 2006 dystopian black comedy thriller written and directed by Richard Kelly, with an ensemble cast including Dwayne Johnson, Seann William Scott, Sarah Michelle Gellar, Mandy Moore, Justin Timberlake, Will Sasso and Wallace Shawn, and music by Moby. Set in the then-near future of 2008, it is a sprawling satirical portrait of Los Angeles and a commentary on the military-industrial complex, surveillance and the infotainment industry.

On July 4, 2005, nuclear attacks destroy the Texas cities of El Paso and Abilene, plunging the world into a third world war. The United States reinstates the draft and creates US-IDENT, a vast surveillance agency. Amid a fuel crisis, the company Treer unveils Fluid Karma, a seemingly limitless energy source generated by ocean currents, while its scientist Baron von Westphalen harbors grander ambitions.

In Los Angeles in 2008, the action star Boxer Santaros, married to the daughter of a Republican vice-presidential candidate, wakes up with amnesia in the desert and begins an affair with Krysta Now, a former adult film star turned would-be talk show host. Together they have written a screenplay that seems to predict the apocalypse. A cell of neo-Marxist radicals plots to discredit the government by staging a fake act of police brutality, involving Boxer and the police officer Roland Taverner, whose apparent twin brother Ronald is to be dressed in his uniform. But a rogue officer turns the staged killing into a real one, and the leaked footage ignites riots across the city.

As Los Angeles erupts, the elite gather aboard von Westphalen's giant zeppelin to celebrate the launch of Fluid Karma. Boxer learns that Treer's experiments have torn a rift in time, that he is a future version of himself who traveled back an instant, and that contact between two versions of the same person could bring about the apocalypse. Roland and Ronald are likewise the same man from two timelines. When they finally clasp hands, they rise into the air as a rift opens in the sky, and a missile destroys the zeppelin with Boxer aboard. The narrator, Iraq war veteran Pilot Abilene, describes the dawning of a new age.

The film premiered in competition at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival, where it was poorly received, and was re-edited before its US release on November 14, 2007. Critics were divided by its length and chaotic structure despite its intriguing vision; it grossed under $400,000 but has since developed a cult following.

overview: A documentary about World War I with never-before-seen footage to commemorate the centennial of Armistice Day, and the end of the war.
title: They Shall Not Grow Old
plot:
They Shall Not Grow Old is a documentary film that explores the lives of British soldiers during World War I, presented in a unique and powerful way through archival footage and interviews with veterans. The film delves into the harsh realities of war, the psychological toll it takes on soldiers, and the long-lasting impact it has on individuals and society.

At its core, the film is a poignant exploration of the human cost of conflict, shedding light on the experiences of ordinary men who were thrust into extraordinary circumstances. It highlights the camaraderie and bonds that formed among soldiers in the trenches, as well as the trauma and PTSD that many struggled with upon their return home.

The film also touches on themes of nostalgia, memory, and the passage of time, as the veterans' recollections serve as a window into a bygone era. The archival footage, which has been meticulously restored and presented in a cinematic format, adds to the sense of immediacy and intimacy, drawing the viewer into the world of the soldiers.

Ultimately, They Shall Not Grow Old is a powerful tribute to the men who served during World War I, and a reminder of the enduring impact that their experiences have had on our collective understanding of war and its effects on individuals.

overview: The true story of Richard Kuklinski, the notorious contract killer and family man.
tagline: Loving husband. Devoted father. Ruthless killer.
title: The Iceman
plot:
The Iceman is a 2012 American biographical crime thriller film directed by Ariel Vromen and written by Michael Brandt and Daniel Gaberman. The movie is based on the life of Richard Kuklinski, also known as "The Iceman," a serial killer who claimed to have killed over 100 people during the 1960s and 1970s.

The main themes of The Iceman revolve around the complexities of human nature, the blurred lines between good and evil, and the consequences of violence. Here's a breakdown of the film's plot development and ending:

Beginning: The movie opens with Richard Kuklinski (played by Michael Shannon) as an adult, reflecting on his life and crimes. We see flashbacks of his childhood, where he was raised in a troubled home with an abusive father. This sets the tone for Kuklinski's later life, marked by violence and a lack of empathy.

Plot Development: As the film progresses, we witness Kuklinski's transformation into a serial killer. He begins targeting people who are vulnerable or have wronged him in some way. The movie explores his modus operandi, which involves using ice picks to kill his victims, often leaving no signs of struggle or evidence behind.

Throughout the film, there are also flashbacks to Kuklinski's relationships with his family and friends, particularly his wife Carol (played by Winona Ryder). These scenes humanize him, making it harder for the audience to categorize him as purely evil. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Kuklinski's actions are driven by a desire for control and power.

Ending: The film concludes with Kuklinski being arrested in 1986, after his wife reports him to the police. As he sits in prison, reflecting on his life, we see glimpses of his victims' families, who have been left to pick up the pieces. The movie ends with a sense of unease, leaving the audience to ponder the nature of evil and whether people can truly change.

Overall, The Iceman is a thought-provoking film that challenges the audience to consider the complexities of human behavior. By exploring Kuklinski's backstory and motivations, the movie raises questions about the consequences of violence and the blurred lines between good and evil.

overview: Inspired by the 2005 riots in Paris, Stéphane, a recent transplant to the impoverished suburb of Montfermeil, joins the local anti-crime squad. Working alongside his unscrupulous colleagues Chris and Gwada, Stéphane struggles to maintain order amidst the mounting tensions between local gangs. When an arrest turns unexpectedly violent, the three officers must reckon with the aftermath and keep the neighborhood from spiraling out of control.
title: Les Misérables
plot:
Les Misérables is a 2019 French crime drama directed by Ladj Ly in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Ly, Giordano Gederlini and Alexis Manenti, expanded from Ly's 2017 short film of the same name. Damien Bonnard, Alexis Manenti and Djebril Zonga star as police officers, with Issa Percia and Al-Hassan Ly. Inspired by an incident of police violence that Ly witnessed and filmed in 2008, it takes its title from Victor Hugo's novel, part of which is set in Montfermeil.

In the summer of 2018, as France celebrates its World Cup victory, police officer Stéphane Ruiz, newly transferred from Cherbourg, joins an anti-crime squad patrolling Montfermeil, a deprived suburb east of Paris. His partners are the aggressive squad leader Chris and the more measured Gwada, who has grown up in the area. Stéphane is disturbed by the way Chris intimidates and humiliates local youths, but he does not intervene. Tensions rise when a lion cub is stolen from a traveling circus, and its furious owner threatens violence against the neighborhood unless it is returned. The officers are pressured to find the cub before the conflict explodes.

A photo posted online identifies the thief as Issa, a troubled boy. When the officers catch him, his friends attack them, and in the chaos Gwada fires a flash-ball round into Issa's face at close range, wounding him badly. Realizing the incident has been filmed by a drone belonging to a local boy named Buzz, Chris and Gwada refuse Stéphane's demand to take Issa to a hospital and instead hunt for the footage. The search draws in the neighborhood's power brokers, including a figure known as the Mayor and Salah, a respected former gang member turned restaurant owner and Muslim community leader, before Stéphane persuades Salah to hand over the memory card. The cub is returned, Issa is warned to keep quiet, and that evening Stéphane confronts Gwada about what he did.

The next day, Issa leads the neighborhood's children in an ambush of the police officers in a housing block stairwell. The film ends in an unresolved standoff, with Issa holding a Molotov cocktail and Stéphane aiming his gun, followed by a quotation from Hugo about bad cultivators rather than bad men.

The film premiered at the 2019 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Jury Prize. It received critical acclaim, won four César Awards including Best Film, and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best International Feature.

overview: A young woman left her family for an unspecified reason. The husband determines to find out the truth and starts following his wife. At first, he suspects that a man is involved. But gradually, he finds out more and more strange behaviors and bizarre incidents that indicate something more than a possessed love affair.
tagline: Inhuman ecstasy fulfilled.
title: Possession
plot:
Possession is a 1981 psychological horror drama written and directed by Andrzej Żuławski, starring Sam Neill as Mark, a spy, and Isabelle Adjani as his wife Anna, with Heinz Bennent as Anna's lover Heinrich. A French and West German co-production, it is Żuławski's only English-language feature. He wrote the screenplay in the emotional aftermath of his divorce from the actress Małgorzata Braunek and his exile from Poland, and the film was shot in West Berlin in 1980, largely near the Berlin Wall, on a budget of about 2.4 million dollars.

Mark returns home to West Berlin after a mission to find that Anna wants to separate from him and is seeing another man. He gives up their apartment and custody of their young son Bob, but after a long drinking binge he returns to find the boy neglected and decides to care for him himself. Bob's teacher, Helen, turns out to look exactly like Anna, except for her lighter hair and green eyes. Mark confronts Heinrich, an eccentric lover who easily overpowers him, but soon realizes that Anna has been seeing someone, or something, else entirely.

As the couple's encounters turn into scenes of hysterical violence and self-harm, Mark hires a private detective to follow Anna, who has been living in a derelict apartment. There the detective discovers a monstrous tentacled creature that Anna has been nurturing, and she kills him. As more people disappear, Mark is drawn into Anna's madness, killing and covering up crimes to protect her, while the creature gradually transforms, leading to an apocalyptic and deeply ambiguous ending.

The film uses horror to depict the disintegration of a marriage, with themes of jealousy, faith, chance and doubles. Adjani's frenzied performance, including a scene in which Anna suffers a violent miscarriage in the subway, is often singled out as the film's most memorable element. The creature effects were created by Carlo Rambaldi.

Possession premiered at the 34th Cannes Film Festival, where Adjani won the award for Best Actress. It received a lukewarm response on its initial release and was released in a heavily cut version in the United States. In later years the film acquired cult status and has been reappraised as a major work of art-house horror; it holds a Metacritic score of 75.

overview: Ollie Trinke is a young, suave music publicist who seems to have it all, with a new wife and a baby on the way. But life deals him a bum hand when he's suddenly faced with single fatherhood, a defunct career and having to move in with his father. To bounce back, it takes a new love and the courage instilled in him by his daughter.
tagline: He wanted it all...but he got more than he bargained for.
title: Jersey Girl
plot:
Jersey Girl is a 2004 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Kevin Smith. The movie follows the story of Ollie Trinko (played by Ben Affleck), a successful businessman who returns to his hometown in New Jersey after the death of his wife, Laura (played by Liv Tyler).

The main themes of Jersey Girl include:

1. Grief and Loss: The film explores Ollie's journey as he navigates the grieving process after losing his wife. He must come to terms with the fact that she is no longer with him and find a way to move on.

2. Family and Relationships: The movie highlights the importance of family and relationships in our lives. Ollie's interactions with his mother (played by Jennifer Lopez), sister (played by Rachel Weisz), and friends serve as a reminder of the significance of these bonds.

3. Identity and Self-Discovery: As Ollie returns to his hometown, he is forced to confront his past and re-evaluate his priorities. He begins to question his identity and find new meaning in life after losing his wife.

4. Nostalgia and Small-Town Life: The film celebrates the charm of small-town New Jersey and the nostalgia that comes with it. Ollie's experiences serve as a reminder of the beauty of simplicity and community.

5. Love and Redemption: Ultimately, the movie is about love and redemption. Ollie finds new love with a woman named Elizabeth (played by Raquel Welch), and through their relationship, he learns to heal and find happiness again.

Overall, Jersey Girl is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of life's complexities, love, and relationships.

overview: A deaf man and his girlfriend resort to desperate measures in order to fund a kidney transplant for his sister. Things go horribly wrong, and the situation spirals rapidly into a cycle of violence and revenge.
tagline: Revenge Was Never This Sweet
title: Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance
plot:
Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance is a 2002 South Korean psychological thriller film directed by Park Chan-wook, produced by CJ Entertainment and CJ Entertainment's subsidiary, CJ Entertainment & Media.

The story revolves around the character of Lee Gu (played by Song Kang-ho), an ordinary man who works as a delivery driver in Seoul. He lives a simple life with his wife, Yoo-jin (played by Kim Rye-won), and their young daughter, Soo-yeon (played by Park Hae-il). However, their lives take a drastic turn when they receive a ransom demand from the kidnapper of their daughter.

The kidnapper, Mr. Vengeance (played by Choi Min-sik), demands 10 million won in exchange for Soo-yeon's safe return. The family is shocked and devastated by this news, but Gu decides to take matters into his own hands to rescue his daughter. He embarks on a perilous journey to track down Mr. Vengeance and save Soo-yeon.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Mr. Vengeance has a personal vendetta against the wealthy and influential Kim family, who are responsible for the death of Gu's brother in a car accident several years ago. The kidnapper's true intention is to exact revenge on the Kim family by using their own daughter as leverage.

Throughout the film, Park Chan-wook masterfully weaves together themes of revenge, redemption, and the cyclical nature of violence. The title "Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance" refers to the audience's emotional investment in both Gu's quest to rescue his daughter and Mr. Vengeance's motivations for kidnapping her.

As the plot thickens, Gu becomes increasingly entangled in a web of deceit and betrayal. He discovers that the Kim family is hiding secrets about their past and their connection to the car accident that killed his brother. The film builds towards a shocking climax as Gu confronts the mastermind behind the kidnapping and ultimately exacts revenge on those responsible.

The ending is both haunting and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the consequences of violence and the cyclical nature of revenge. Despite its dark themes, Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance is a gripping and intense thriller that explores the complexities of human nature and the devastating effects of trauma.

Overall, Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance is a masterful film that showcases Park Chan-wook's unique storytelling style and his ability to craft complex, thought-provoking narratives.

overview: When a young boy contracts a mysterious illness, his mother must decide how far she will go to protect him from terrifying forces in her past.
tagline: You can't outrun a family secret.
title: Son
plot:
Son is a 2021 Irish-American horror thriller written and directed by Ivan Kavanagh. Andi Matichak stars as Laura, a woman who escaped from a cult, with Emile Hirsch as the police detective Paul, Luke David Blumm as her son David, Cranston Johnson and Blaine Maye. It was released in March 2021.

While fleeing a cult by car, Laura goes into labor and gives birth to a boy at the side of the road. Eight years later she lives a quiet life in a small town with her son, David. One night, checking on him, she sees a group of strangers standing around his bed before the door slams shut and locks. She runs to her neighbor Susan for help, but when she returns the intruders have vanished and David lies in bed, looking ill. Two police officers respond: Paul is sympathetic, while his partner Steve suspects that Laura is delusional. Paul gives her his card and asks her to call if anything else happens.

That night David vomits blood and is rushed to the hospital, where doctors cannot identify the cause of his illness and warn that he may not survive. Laura has dreams about her past with the cult, including a banner reading "He Is Coming." When she wakes, David has suddenly recovered. Back home, she tells Paul that she plans to sell the house and leave town; he urges her to stay, and they grow close, until David is seized by violent convulsions. Readmitted to hospital, David is again failing, and after overhearing a suspicious conversation among the doctors, Laura takes him and flees. On the run, she discovers that the only thing that can keep her son alive is human flesh and blood, and she is forced to commit terrible acts to sustain him while Paul, torn between his duty and his feelings, tries to find them, and the cult closes in.

Son received generally positive reviews, with a 79 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a horror story with unexpected emotional resonance that uses its familial focus to counter a certain queasy familiarity. On Metacritic it scored 54. Critics praised Matichak's committed performance, while Common Sense Media's Jeffrey M. Anderson was less impressed, rating it two out of five.

overview: Sayra, a Honduran teen, hungers for a better life. Her chance for one comes when she is reunited with her long-estranged father, who intends to emigrate to Mexico and then enter the United States. Sayra's life collides with a pair of Mexican gangmembers who have boarded the same American-bound train.
tagline: The greatest sin of all is risking nothing.
title: Sin Nombre
plot:
Sin Nombre is a 2009 American drama film directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga, written by Fukunaga and Eric Warren Singer, and starring Diego Luna, Jeremy Renner, and Woody Harrelson.

The movie follows the story of Elmer Escalante (Diego Luna), a young Guatemalan migrant who is traveling north through Mexico with his cousin, Valentina (Paola Mendoza). They are part of a large group of migrants attempting to reach the United States in search of a better life. The group faces numerous challenges and dangers along the way, including corrupt border patrol agents, ruthless coyotes (human smugglers), and treacherous terrain.

As Elmer navigates this perilous journey, he meets Alejandro (Jeremy Renner), a seasoned migrant who has been traveling for years. Alejandro is initially portrayed as a tough, no-nonsense individual who is driven by a desire to reach the United States and start anew. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that Alejandro's motivations are more complex, and he is haunted by his past.

Throughout the film, Elmer forms a bond with Alejandro, who becomes a sort of mentor to him. As they face various challenges together, Elmer learns valuable lessons about resilience, courage, and the importance of human connection in the face of adversity.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Alejandro's past is marked by tragedy and loss. He has been searching for his sister, who disappeared during a previous migration attempt. This personal quest drives much of Alejandro's actions throughout the film, as he hopes to find her and bring closure to his own emotional scars.

The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Elmer and Alejandro, as they are forced to make a difficult decision about their future. Ultimately, Elmer decides to continue on his journey, while Alejandro chooses to turn back and return to Mexico.

The movie ends with Elmer standing alone at the border, looking out at the vast expanse of the United States. He is filled with a mix of emotions - hope, fear, and uncertainty about what lies ahead. The camera lingers on his face, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of this young migrant's journey.

Throughout Sin Nombre, Fukunaga explores themes of migration, identity, and the human cost of globalization. The film offers a powerful and unflinching portrayal of the challenges faced by migrants, as well as the resilience and determination that defines them.

overview: Dangerously ill with a rare blood disorder, and determined to save others suffering his same fate, Dr. Michael Morbius attempts a desperate gamble. What at first appears to be a radical success soon reveals itself to be a remedy potentially worse than the disease.
tagline: A new Marvel legend arrives.
title: Morbius
plot:
Morbius is a 2022 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character, produced by Columbia Pictures and distributed by Sony as the third film in Sony's Spider-Man Universe. Directed by Daniel Espinosa and written by Matt Sazama and Burk Sharpless, it stars Jared Leto as Dr. Michael Morbius, alongside Matt Smith as Milo, Adria Arjona as Martine Bancroft, Jared Harris as Dr. Emil Nicholas, Al Madrigal and Tyrese Gibson as FBI agents.

As a boy in a Greek hospital, Michael Morbius befriends another child, whom he names Milo; both suffer from a rare blood disease and dream of being normal. Their adoptive father, the hospital's director, sends the gifted Michael to study medicine in New York. Twenty-five years later, Michael is a renowned scientist who has declined a Nobel Prize for his work on artificial blood. Secretly, he has captured vampire bats in Costa Rica, hoping to splice their genes with his own to cure his condition.

With money from the wealthy Milo, Michael conducts his experiment aboard a ship in international waters. The treatment cures him but turns him into a vampire-like creature with superhuman strength, speed and echolocation, and he kills the ship's crew in a frenzy of bloodlust. Back in New York, he tries to control his hunger with artificial blood while FBI agents investigate the killings. When Milo discovers the cure, he takes it himself and embraces his new powers, killing without remorse. Michael, who refuses to give in to his thirst for human blood, develops an antibody to stop his brother, leading to a final confrontation after Milo kills those closest to him. In mid-credits scenes, the Spider-Man villain Adrian Toomes arrives in Michael's universe.

After being delayed several times from its original July 2020 date, mainly because of the COVID-19 pandemic, Morbius was released in the United States on April 1, 2022.

The film grossed 167.5 million dollars worldwide and suffered one of the steepest second-weekend drops ever for a superhero film. Critics panned its writing, visual effects and post-credits scenes, giving it 15 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 35. It became the subject of mocking internet memes, which led Sony to re-release it in June 2022, again with poor results. At the Golden Raspberry Awards, Leto won Worst Actor and Arjona Worst Supporting Actress.

overview: A group of adult film cast and crew members must discover what is causing their fellow stars to rabidly attack them.
tagline: They want to eat you...
title: Porn Star Zombies
plot:
Porn Star Zombies is a 2009 American independent horror comedy written and directed by Keith Emerson (not the keyboardist of Emerson, Lake & Palmer) and produced by SFZ Productions. Shot in black and white on a micro-budget of around $10,000, it runs just under an hour. Emerson developed it from his own screenplay, which had been a semifinalist in the 2007 Slamdance Film Festival screenplay competition, and he raised the money to produce and direct it himself.

The story is set on the low-budget shoot of an adult film. As production gets under way, a mysterious, sexually transmitted infection begins spreading through the cast, turning the performers one after another into rabid, flesh-eating zombies who turn on their colleagues. The remaining cast and crew members, trapped together on the job, must work out what is causing their fellow stars to attack them and find a way to survive before they too are infected or devoured. Despite the title and the setting, the film contains relatively little sexual content, drawing most of its humour from dirty jokes, innuendo and the banter of its characters.

The cast includes Joshua Cameron as Gavin, alongside Alicia Oberle, Kevin Cazier, Kira Ratterman and Vivi Wreen. The gore effects were made cheaply, with one reviewer suspecting chocolate syrup and spare meat.

After its completion the film was marketed for distribution with a brief theatrical run and some exposure around the 2012 Cannes Film Festival, and it was then released on DVD by R-Squared Films. Reviews were limited and mixed. ML Miller compared it less to David Cronenberg's early sexually transmitted horror films Shivers and Rabid than to Kevin Smith's Clerks, citing its monochrome photography, sometimes witty dialogue and amateur performances. He felt the dialogue often sounded like actors reading someone else's distinctive writing rather than natural conversation and that it was more comedy than horror, but found it frequently funny, credited Emerson with getting a lot out of very little and concluded that it was worth a few laughs. Other reviewers and viewers were less forgiving, describing it as crude and amateurish, with weak acting and effects.

original_title: ONE PIECE 〜アドベンチャー オブ ネブランディア〜
overview: Kōmei devises a plan where Zoro and Sanji take part in an eating contest, and the two eat a strange "good-for-nothing-only" mushroom that turns them into good-for-nothing men. The two are then locked in a jail cell. When the rest of the Straw Hat Pirates chase after their imprisoned crew, they land on the island of Nebulandia, which features a mysterious fog made from sea water, and it has the same effects as seastone. The Straw Hat Pirates' arrival on Nebulandia is also a part of Kōmei's plan.
title: One Piece: Adventure of Nebulandia
plot:
One Piece: Adventure of Nebulandia is a 2015 Japanese animated television special based on the One Piece manga and anime and produced by Toei Animation. Directed by Konosuke Uda, the original series director of the One Piece anime, from a screenplay by Atsuhiro Tomioka, it was broadcast on 19 December 2015 in the Saturday Premium slot as the sixth One Piece special in that slot, following Episode of Sabo earlier that year. Unlike specials that retell manga arcs, it is an original story, and it brings back the Foxy Pirates, the crew the Straw Hats defeated in the anime's Davy Back Fight arc, with new members. It was released on Blu-ray and DVD in March 2016.

Sailing in the New World, Monkey D. Luffy and the Straw Hat Pirates are challenged by Captain Foxy to a Davy Back Fight rematch. The contest is a trap devised by Kōmei, a brilliant strategist who has recently joined Foxy's crew. During an eating contest, Zoro and Sanji consume a strange mushroom that saps their strength and turns them into good-for-nothings, and the pair are captured and carried away. Chasing their friends, the Straw Hats reach Nebulandia, an island shrouded in a mist formed from sea water that, like seastone, neutralises the powers of Devil Fruit users. Their arrival is exactly what Kōmei planned.

Kōmei is in fact a vice admiral of the Navy and a special operations strategist who infiltrated the Foxy Pirates by deliberately losing to them. Having lost his home town to pirates as a child, he despises them and dreams of proving that ordinary people without powers can defeat Devil Fruit users through cunning, thereby changing the Navy itself. Luffy is forced into an uneasy alliance with his old Davy Back rival Foxy for the rescue. Using the island's terrain and a series of traps, especially the pitfalls he favours, Kōmei captures Robin, Franky and Usopp, but Brook and Chopper, searching for an antidote to the mushroom, foil his attempt to seize Luffy. In the final battle, Kōmei floods his base with sea water to weaken Luffy, but Foxy's Slow-Slow Beam and a pitfall turn the tables, and Luffy defeats him with a decisive blow.

The regular voice cast returns, led by Mayumi Tanaka as Luffy, Kazuya Nakai as Zoro and Hiroaki Hirata as Sanji, with Toshio Shimada as Foxy. Ichikawa Ennosuke voices Kōmei, a role he modelled on the Three Kingdoms strategist Zhuge Liang, while Hoka Kinoshita plays another new crew member who is secretly a Navy officer.

overview: A trio of guys try and make up for missed opportunities in childhood by forming a three-player baseball team to compete against standard little league squads.
tagline: Get off the bench and get into the game.
title: The Benchwarmers
plot:
The Benchwarmers is a 2006 American sports comedy film directed by Dennis Dugan and starring Adam Sandler, David Spade, and Rob Schneider. The movie follows the story of three friends who were once part of a high school baseball team that was known for its exceptional skills.

The film begins with the main characters, Lane (Rob Schneider), Earl (David Spade), and Kenny (Adam Sandler), all in their mid-30s, struggling to find their place in life. They are all overweight, unemployed, and living with their parents. The three friends were once part of a high school baseball team that was known for its exceptional skills, but they never won the championship.

The story takes a turn when Lane's mother passes away, leaving him her house and a large sum of money. However, there is one condition: he must find his estranged father, who abandoned him as a child. The three friends decide to embark on a road trip to find Lane's father, who they believe lives in the Midwest.

Along the way, they face various challenges, including run-ins with eccentric characters, wild animals, and their own personal demons. As they journey through the country, they also reflect on their past and the reasons why they never won the championship.

The Benchwarmers is a comedy that relies heavily on slapstick humor, witty one-liners, and absurd situations. The movie features many memorable scenes, including a fight between Lane and his father's new wife, as well as a hilarious sequence where Earl tries to impress a woman by pretending to be a professional baseball player.

As the story unfolds, the three friends finally find their father, who is played by Peter Dante. However, they soon discover that he has changed significantly since they last saw him. He is now a successful businessman with a family of his own.

The movie takes a heartwarming turn when Lane and his friends learn about the importance of forgiveness and moving on from past mistakes. They also come to terms with their own personal struggles and find a new sense of purpose in life.

In the end, the three friends return home, where they are welcomed back by their families. The movie ends on a positive note, with Lane and his friends finally finding happiness and fulfillment in their lives.

Overall, The Benchwarmers is a lighthearted comedy that explores themes of friendship, forgiveness, and redemption. While it may not be the most sophisticated or nuanced film, it features many memorable moments and performances from its cast.

overview: When a deadly airborne virus threatens to wipe out the northeastern United States, teacher Elliott Moore and his wife Alma flee from contaminated cities into the countryside in a fight to discover the truth. Is it terrorism, the accidental release of some toxic military bio weapon -- or something even more sinister?
tagline: We've Sensed It. We've Seen The Signs. Now... It's Happening.
title: The Happening
plot:
The Happening is a 2008 science fiction thriller produced, written and directed by M. Night Shyamalan. Mark Wahlberg stars as a high school science teacher fleeing an inexplicable natural disaster that drives people to kill themselves, with Zooey Deschanel, John Leguizamo, Ashlyn Sanchez and Betty Buckley. 20th Century Fox released it on June 13, 2008. It was Shyamalan's first film with an R rating.

In Central Park, people suddenly freeze, become disoriented and begin to take their own lives, and the phenomenon soon spreads across the north-east of the United States. It is first thought to be a terrorist attack using an airborne toxin. In Philadelphia, the teacher Elliot Moore and his wife Alma, whose marriage is strained, are persuaded by Elliot's colleague Julian, a maths teacher, to take a train out of the city with his young daughter Jess. When the train stops in a small town after losing contact, Julian leaves Jess with the Moores to look for his wife in Princeton, where he is caught in the event and dies.

Elliot, Alma and Jess get a ride with the owners of a plant nursery, who suggest that plants have developed a defence against humanity, releasing a toxin that triggers people to kill themselves. As the survivors flee across the countryside, avoiding towns, larger groups are struck down, and Elliot concludes that the plants are targeting crowds. He splits the survivors into small groups, but two teenagers walking with them are shot dead by armed residents of a barricaded house.

The trio find refuge at the isolated home of Mrs. Jones, a suspicious and eccentric elderly woman, who agrees to let them stay the night but turns against them in the morning. When she goes outside she falls victim to the toxin, showing that it is now targeting even individuals. Trapped in separate buildings, Elliot and Alma, reconciled and unwilling to die apart, step outside to embrace, only to find that the event has ended as suddenly as it began.

Three months later, the couple are raising Jess, and Alma learns she is pregnant. An expert on television compares the event to a red tide and warns it may be a warning of worse to come, as the phenomenon begins again in a park in Paris. Critics were scathing, giving it a 17% Rotten Tomatoes approval, but the film grossed 163 million dollars worldwide and has since been reappraised by some as unintentional camp.

overview: Ray Breslin manages an elite team of security specialists trained in the art of breaking people out of the world's most impenetrable prisons. When his most trusted operative, Shu Ren, is kidnapped and disappears inside the most elaborate prison ever built, Ray must track him down with the help of some of his former friends.
tagline: He's back.
title: Escape Plan 2: Hades
plot:
Escape Plan 2: Hades is a 2018 American action thriller film directed by Tim Lee and written by Miles Chapman. The movie stars Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, and Adrienne Palicki.

The story begins with Emil Rottmayer (Adrienne Palicki), an inmate in the maximum-security prison of Hades, who is determined to escape. She befriends a fellow inmate, Sofia (Daniella Alonso), and together they devise a plan to break free from their confinement.

Meanwhile, Emil's past comes back to haunt her as she is pursued by a ruthless mercenary named Victor Vex (Jesse Metcalfe). Victor is hired by the prison's corrupt governor, who wants to keep Emil contained for his own gain.

Emil and Sofia put their plan into action, using their skills and cunning to evade the guards and make their way through the prison. Along the way, they encounter a group of fellow inmates who are also seeking freedom.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Victor is working with the governor to capture Emil and use her as leverage to gain control over the prison's lucrative black market. The stakes are raised when Emil discovers that Sofia has been secretly working for Victor all along, adding an element of betrayal to the plot.

Sylvester Stallone plays Ray Breslin, a seasoned prisoner who has spent years perfecting his escape techniques. He is initially hesitant to get involved with Emil and Sofia's plan but eventually joins forces with them to take down Victor and the corrupt governor.

The action-packed climax features an intense showdown between Emil, Ray, and Victor in the prison's maximum-security wing. The trio uses their skills and ingenuity to outsmart the guards and make a daring escape from Hades.

Throughout the movie, Stallone and Schwarzenegger deliver their signature one-liners and perform impressive stunts, showcasing their action hero credentials. While the plot may not be as complex or original as some of their previous collaborations, Escape Plan 2: Hades delivers on its promise of high-octane action and thrills.

Ultimately, Emil and Ray succeed in their mission to escape from Hades, but not without sacrifices. The movie concludes with a sense of closure for the characters, as they look towards a brighter future outside the prison walls.

Overall, Escape Plan 2: Hades is an entertaining, if predictable, action thriller that delivers on its promise of non-stop excitement and suspense.

overview: Dead bodies begin to turn up all over the city, each meeting their demise in a variety of grisly ways. All investigations begin to point the finger at deceased killer John Kramer.
tagline: A new game begins.
title: Jigsaw
plot:
Jigsaw is a 2017 American psychological horror film directed by the Spierig Brothers and written by Josh Stolberg and Peter Goldfinger. The movie serves as a sequel to the Saw franchise, ignoring the events of the previous films.

The story begins with Evelyn Johnson (Hannah Emily Anderson), the daughter of John Kramer's (Tobin Bell) former apprentice, who is now an old man living in a nursing home. Evelyn has been searching for her father and his legacy, hoping to understand why he was so obsessed with testing people's will to live.

Evelyn discovers that she is the target of Jigsaw's next game, which is designed to test her own will to survive. She receives a mysterious phone call from Jigsaw, who reveals that he has been watching her and knows about her father's past. Jigsaw claims that Evelyn must prove herself worthy to carry on his legacy by completing three challenges.

The first challenge takes Evelyn to an abandoned warehouse, where she finds a series of puzzles and traps designed to test her physical and mental limits. As she navigates the warehouse, Evelyn is forced to confront her own mortality and the consequences of her father's actions.

As Evelyn progresses through the game, she begins to uncover more about Jigsaw's motivations and the true nature of his tests. She also meets a new character, Logan (Matt Passmore), who becomes her ally in the game.

The second challenge takes Evelyn to a hospital, where she must navigate a series of medical puzzles and confront her own fears and weaknesses. Meanwhile, Logan is revealed to be working for a mysterious organization that seeks to exploit Jigsaw's technology for their own gain.

The final challenge takes Evelyn to an abandoned asylum, where she must face off against a group of ruthless mercenaries who are also seeking to claim Jigsaw's legacy for themselves. In the end, Evelyn emerges victorious, but not without scars and a newfound understanding of her father's complex legacy.

Throughout the movie, the Spierig Brothers explore themes of grief, redemption, and the consequences of playing god. The film features plenty of twists and turns, keeping viewers on the edge of their seats as they try to piece together the puzzle alongside Evelyn.

Overall, Jigsaw is a tense and thought-provoking thriller that expands on the Saw franchise while maintaining its signature style and suspense.

overview: Finley, a talented aspiring violinist, meets Beckett, a famous young movie star, on the way to her college semester abroad program in a small coastal village in Ireland. An unexpected romance emerges as the heartthrob Beckett leads the uptight Finley on an adventurous reawakening, and she emboldens him to take charge of his future, until the pressures of his stardom get in the way.
tagline: Trust the journey.
title: Finding You
plot:
Finding You is a 2021 American coming-of-age romantic comedy written and directed by Brian Baugh, based on Jenny B. Jones's 2011 young adult novel There You'll Find Me. Rose Reid stars as an aspiring violinist and Jedidiah Goodacre as a film star, with Katherine McNamara, Tom Everett Scott and Vanessa Redgrave. Roadside Attractions released it in American cinemas on May 14, 2021.

After failing an audition for a New York music conservatory, violinist Finley Sinclair joins a study abroad programme in a small Irish village, the same programme her late brother Alex once attended. On the flight she is upgraded and falls asleep on the shoulder of Beckett Rush, the arrogant-seeming star of the Dawn of the Dragon fantasy franchise, who is heading to Ireland to shoot the next film. Finley stays with Alex's former host family, the Callaghans, whose daughter Emma is a devoted Beckett fan, and discovers that he is staying at their bed and breakfast too.

Nora Callaghan gives Finley Alex's notebook of sketches, and she resolves to find the place in the last, unfinished drawing: a broken Celtic cross in a churchyard, labelled with her name. Beckett, pressured by his manager father Montgomery to keep the studio happy so he can land a multi-film deal, makes a bargain with Finley: she will help him rehearse and he will help her search. For a class project, Finley must also spend time with Cathleen Sweeney, a cantankerous elderly woman rumoured to have married her sister Fiona's sweetheart for money.
