Six months later, the plague has killed about ninety percent of the population of the United States.

Near Los Angeles, three survivors, Ramona, Billie and Kevin, are searching an auto repair shop for supplies when the noise draws a horde of zombies. Kevin is bitten before another group of survivors, Henry, Julian, Cassie and Mack, arrives to fight off the attackers; Cassie kills Kevin as he begins to turn. The two groups join forces, and Mack reveals that they are heading for Catalina Island, where a survivor camp is said to await anyone who can reach the ferry. On the way, they scavenge a surf shop, are attacked by a fast-moving "runner" zombie, and are forced to kill a stray dog that becomes infected. A supposed safe zone at a high school turns out to be abandoned, and when the gym is suddenly flooded with zombies, Billie is bitten.

The group is split apart in a burning neighborhood. Mack, Julian and Ramona are rescued by a band of archers, Brockton, Myrah and Sarah, while Henry and Cassie continue on alone. Julian is bitten when a zombie bursts out of a portable toilet, and before he can sacrifice himself as a distraction he begins to turn, forcing Mack to kill him. Henry and Cassie collect grenades from an abandoned army post, and an explosion they set off helps the others escape. The groups reunite on the rooftops and fight their way to the docks, where they find supplies and quarantine instructions, but also a pair of infected tigers. Brockton is killed and Henry is bitten, and Cassie grants his request to end his life. In the final scene, the remaining survivors watch as the ferry approaches.

Reviews were mixed to negative. The A.V. Club dismissed it as a dull riff on The Walking Dead, and Dread Central and DVD Talk found it routine, while Starburst considered it a cheap and cheerful genre film with enough good ideas and performances to entertain.

original_title: Have a Good Trip: Adventures in Psychedelics
overview: Celebrities recall their most mind-bending trips via animations, reenactments and more in this comedic documentary exploring the story of psychedelics.
title: Have a Good Trip: Adventures in Psychedelics
plot:
Have a Good Trip: Adventures in Psychedelics is a 2020 American comedic documentary written and directed by the Emmy-winning writer and producer Donick Cary and hosted by Nick Offerman. Mixing interviews with animation and comic re-enactments, it gathers celebrities who recount their most memorable experiences with hallucinogenic drugs, told with humor and candor, while also touching on the history of psychedelics and their potential role in treating conditions like depression and anxiety.

The interviewees include Sarah Silverman, Adam Scott, Rosie Perez, Adam Horovitz, A$AP Rocky, Anthony Bourdain, Ben Stiller, Bill Kreutzmann, Carrie Fisher, Natasha Lyonne, Lewis Black, Nick Kroll, Reggie Watts, Shepard Fairey, Sting and Deepak Chopra, alongside Paul Scheer, Rob Corddry, Will Forte, Haley Joel Osment, Thomas Lennon and David Cross. The stories range from euphoric to frightening and absurd, and many are brought to life through animated sequences and staged re-creations. The film is among the final screen appearances of Fred Willard, Anthony Bourdain and Carrie Fisher, whose Beverly Hills home, which she called the "acid house", served as one of the locations.

Cary conceived the project in 2009 at the Nantucket Film Festival, where he, Stiller and Fisher Stevens swapped stories about hallucinogens over dinner and agreed to make a film that would combine anecdotes with re-enactments and animation. What began as a collection of funny stories grew into a work aiming to open a serious and balanced conversation about psychedelics. Over eleven years, fitting around celebrities' schedules, Cary conducted more than a hundred interviews, far more than made the final cut. The film was financed by Mike Rosenstein's Sunset Rose Pictures and Cary's Sugarshack 2000, with support from Stiller's Red Hour, and its score was provided by the indie rock band Yo La Tengo.

It was set to premiere at South by Southwest in March 2020, but the festival was canceled because of the COVID-19 pandemic, and the film instead debuted on Netflix on 11 May 2020, remaining in the service's top ten for over a month. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes reported a 58% approval rating, with critics finding it entertaining but shallow, and Metacritic gave it 44 out of 100. Some reviewers valued its attention to medical research into psychedelics, while others felt its comic approach undercut the subject.

overview: Teenager Cleo's school science project goes quite awry, causing her popular older sister Molly to go invisible.
tagline: What you see is only half the story
title: Invisible Sister
plot:
Invisible Sister is a 2015 American science fiction comedy television film directed by Paul Hoen and loosely based on the book My Invisible Sister by Beatrice Colin and Sara Pinto. Rowan Blanchard stars as a brilliant but overlooked teenager and Paris Berelc as her popular older sister, with Karan Brar, Rachel Crow, Will Meyers and Alex Désert. The Disney Channel Original Movie premiered on October 9, 2015, drawing 4.03 million viewers.

Cleo Eastman, a gifted but introverted and sarcastic student in New Orleans, lives in the shadow of her older sister Molly, a lacrosse star whom everyone at school adores. Cleo's science teacher, Mr. Perkins, sets her a special challenge: to identify a mystery substance and turn it into crystals. While she works on it at home during a dinner Molly is hosting for her team, a moth distracts her and she spills extra chemicals into her mixture. The vapour turns the moth invisible, and it escapes.

That night the invisible moth flies into the bathroom light, falls into a glass of water and antacid that Molly is about to drink, and she swallows it. In the morning Molly is horrified to find that she is completely invisible. It is Halloween and the day of the season-opening lacrosse match, which college scouts will be watching, so Cleo is forced to dress in Molly's costume and impersonate her at school, while the invisible Molly steals a microscope so Cleo can investigate. Molly also secretly secures Cleo a date with Carter, the boy Cleo likes, while Cleo's friend George discovers the secret.

With Molly's help, Cleo leads the team to victory. Studying Molly's cells, Cleo and George realise that her invisibility will become permanent unless they create an antidote by midnight. Catching another moth in a cemetery, the sisters argue and then open up: Cleo admits she has always envied Molly's spark, while Molly confesses she envies Cleo's intelligence, knowing that popularity fades.

Getting into the school with help from the invisible Molly, Cleo and George repeat the experiment but need Carter's help to interpret the results, and find him at a Halloween party. Joined by Molly's boyfriend Coug, they race to produce the antidote, but it fails until Cleo adds the antacid Molly drank the night before, and Molly becomes visible again. Impressed, Mr. Perkins invites Cleo to present her findings to a scientific association, and Cleo comes to appreciate the line between being seen and unseen.

overview: Like the original film, the sequel is set in a near future where all drinking and drugs are banned except for on one glorious day known as The Binge. This year, that day happens to miraculously land on Christmas.
tagline: It's the most wonderful high of the year.
title: It's a Wonderful Binge
plot:
It's a Wonderful Binge (originally titled The Binge 2: It's a Wonderful Binge) is a 2022 American Christmas comedy film written and directed by Jordan VanDina. A sequel to the 2020 Hulu film The Binge, itself a comic riff on The Purge, it stars Dexter Darden and Eduardo Franco, with Zainne Saleh, Marta Piekarz, Tim Meadows, Kaitlin Olson, Danny Trejo, Nick Swardson, Tony Cavalero, Patty Guggenheim, Paul Scheer and Karen Maruyama. Produced by LD Entertainment and American High, it was shot mainly in Syracuse, New York, in February 2022, and was released on Hulu on 9 December 2022 with a TV-MA rating.

In a near future where drink and drugs are banned on every day but one, known as the Binge, the authorities move the annual day of indulgence from spring to Christmas Eve. Friends Hags (Darden) and Andrew (Franco) are fired from their jobs as costumed mascots at a children's fun centre. Hags plans to propose to his girlfriend Sarah (Saleh), whose father Keegan (Meadows) is overprotective, and must then recover the engagement ring her grandmother (Maruyama) gave him after it is accidentally donated to an orphanage. Andrew, overwhelmed by his loud, dysfunctional family, wanders through town wondering what the world would be like had he never been born, until an "Angel" (Trejo) shows him alternative realities, in sequences that turn to black and white in homage to It's a Wonderful Life. Meanwhile Kimmi (Piekarz), Andrew's love interest, is sent by her mother, Mayor Spengler (Olson), who is trying to keep the Binge out of her tidy Christmas party, to catch her Christmas owl after it escapes and eats a bag of drugs, while her uncle Kris (Swardson) turns up unannounced, having broken out of jail in a stolen police car. Scheer plays a newscaster whose live reports grow stranger as the night goes on, and Cavalero returns as Pompano Mike. The film features several original songs, including the carollers' "Worst/Best Christmas Ever".

Like its predecessor, the film received generally negative reviews, holding a 25% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from twelve reviews. Alex Maidy of JoBlo called it a bad movie and an even worse comedy, and John Serba of Decider found it sloppy, though he enjoyed Trejo and the claymation homage. Alex Reif of Laughing Place was more positive, calling it a funny, edgy adults-only alternative to typical holiday fare, and Bill Goodykoontz of The Arizona Republic gave it two and a half stars.

overview: Major Bill Cage is an officer who has never seen a day of combat when he is unceremoniously demoted and dropped into combat. Cage is killed within minutes, managing to take an alpha alien down with him. He awakens back at the beginning of the same day and is forced to fight and die again... and again - as physical contact with the alien has thrown him into a time loop.
tagline: Live. Die. Repeat.
title: Edge of Tomorrow
plot:
Edge of Tomorrow is a science fiction action film directed by Doug Liman, released in 2014. The movie stars Tom Cruise and Emily Blunt as the main characters.

The story begins with Major William Cage (Tom Cruise), a PR officer who is sent to cover the military's response to an alien invasion on Earth. Cage is not a soldier and has no experience in combat, but he is given a chance to prove himself when he is forced to join the fight against the extraterrestrial threat.

During his first deployment, Cage meets Sergeant Rita Vrataski (Emily Blunt), a skilled soldier who has been fighting the aliens for months. Despite their initial differences, they form an unlikely alliance as they try to survive the alien attacks and uncover the secrets behind the enemy's powers.

As the battle rages on, Cage discovers that he is able to relive the same day over and over again due to a mysterious phenomenon known as "the Loop." Each time he dies, he wakes up to the same day, with no memory of what happened before. Vrataski reveals that she has also experienced this phenomenon, but her memories of past loops are fragmented.

As Cage and Vrataski work together, they develop a strong bond and learn to rely on each other's strengths. They use their unique abilities to outsmart the aliens and gather information about their weaknesses. Along the way, Cage learns to appreciate Vrataski's skills as a soldier and her unwavering dedication to protecting humanity.

As the stakes grow higher, Cage and Vrataski discover that the aliens are not just mindless monsters but are actually a highly advanced species with a complex social hierarchy. They also learn that the Loop is a result of an alien technology that allows them to manipulate time and space.

In the climactic final battle, Cage and Vrataski face off against the alien leader, known as "Scary Mary," who has been using her powers to create the Loop. With their combined strength and knowledge, they manage to defeat Scary Mary and shatter the Loop, freeing humanity from its grasp.

Throughout the movie, the action is fast-paced and intense, with a mix of sci-fi elements and humor. The chemistry between Cruise and Blunt is undeniable, making their characters' relationship feel authentic and believable. The film's climax is both thrilling and emotionally satisfying, as Cage and Vrataski finally find a way to break free from the Loop and start anew.

Overall, Edge of Tomorrow is an entertaining and thought-provoking sci-fi action film that explores themes of time, memory, and human connection in the face of overwhelming odds.

original_title: ドラゴンボールZ 龍拳爆発!!悟空がやらねば誰がやる
overview: The Z Warriors discover an unopenable music box and are told to open it with the Dragon Balls. The contents turn out to be a warrior named Tapion who had sealed himself inside along with a monster called Hildegarn. Goku must now perfect a new technique to defeat the evil monster.
title: Dragon Ball Z: Wrath of the Dragon
plot:
Dragon Ball Z: Wrath of the Dragon is a 1995 Japanese animated science fantasy martial arts film produced by Toei Animation, based on the Dragon Ball Z manga series created by Akira Toriyama. The movie takes place after the events of the Androids Arc in the Dragon Ball Z anime series.

The story begins with a mysterious and powerful being known as Janemba, who is said to be the reincarnation of the demon king Piccolo Jr.'s evil spirit. Janemba is awakened from his slumber by the evil wizard Babidi, who seeks to use him to destroy Goku and take over the Earth.

Babidi's plan involves using a magical ritual to merge with Janemba's body, creating an even more powerful being known as Majin Buu. However, the ritual goes awry, and instead of merging with Janemba, Babidi is consumed by his own evil energy.

Meanwhile, Goku and his friends are unaware of the impending threat and continue their daily lives. However, when a series of mysterious events occur, they begin to suspect that something is amiss. They soon discover that Janemba has been awakened and is wreaking havoc on the Earth.

As the story unfolds, Goku and his allies, including Trunks, Goten, and Piccolo, band together to stop Janemba and Babidi. Along the way, they encounter a number of powerful foes, including the evil wizard's minions and a group of powerful warriors known as the "Warriors of Destruction."

The final battle takes place in the city of Capsule Corp., where Goku and his friends face off against Janemba and Babidi. In the end, Goku is able to defeat Janemba using the Spirit Bomb technique, while Trunks and Goten work together to defeat Babidi.

Throughout the movie, there are several themes that are explored, including the nature of evil and the power of friendship and teamwork. The film also features a number of action-packed sequences, showcasing the martial arts skills of the Dragon Ball Z characters.

Overall, Dragon Ball Z: Wrath of the Dragon is an exciting and entertaining addition to the Dragon Ball Z franchise, offering fans a thrilling adventure filled with intense battles and memorable moments.

belongs_to_collection.name: My Big Fat Greek Wedding Collection

overview: A young Greek woman falls in love with a non-Greek and struggles to get her family to accept him while she comes to terms with her heritage and cultural identity.
tagline: Love is here to stay... so is her family.
title: My Big Fat Greek Wedding
plot:
My Big Fat Greek Wedding is a 2002 romantic comedy directed by Joel Zwick and written by Nia Vardalos, adapted from her one-woman stage show. Vardalos stars as Toula Portokalos, with John Corbett, Lainie Kazan, Michael Constantine, Gia Carides, Louis Mandylor, Andrea Martin and Joey Fatone. Produced in part by Tom Hanks, Rita Wilson and Gary Goetzman, the American and Canadian co-production premiered at the American Film Market in February 2002 and was released in the United States by IFC Films on 19 April 2002.

In Chicago, thirty-year-old Fotoula "Toula" Portokalos belongs to a large, loud and overbearing Greek-American family. Her father, Gus, is desperate for her to marry a Greek man and start a family, and he is fond of tracing every word in English back to Greek. Toula works as a hostess at the family's restaurant, Dancing Zorba's, and longs for independence. One day she is smitten with Ian Miller, a high-school teacher who comes to the restaurant. With the help of her mother, Maria, she persuades Gus to let her take computer classes at a local college.

As her confidence grows, Toula changes her appearance, trading her thick glasses for contact lenses and adopting a brighter style. She takes a job at her aunt Voula's travel agency, where Ian notices her and asks her out. Their romance blossoms, but Toula keeps it secret, knowing her father will object to her dating a non-Greek. When the family finds out, Gus is furious, but Ian, a gentle vegetarian from a reserved and very small family, is determined to win them over. He agrees to be baptized into the Greek Orthodox Church and endures the boisterous affection of Toula's countless relatives. As the wedding approaches, the clash between the exuberant Portokalos clan and Ian's bewildered parents provides comedy, while Toula comes to accept both her heritage and the life she wants.

Made for about $5 million, the film became a surprise phenomenon through word of mouth, grossing over $368 million worldwide and becoming one of the most profitable independent films ever. It received positive reviews, and Vardalos was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay. Sequels followed in 2016 and 2023.

original_title: 좋은 놈, 나쁜 놈, 이상한 놈
overview: The story of three Korean outlaws in 1930s Manchuria and their dealings with the Japanese army and Chinese and Russian bandits. The Good (a bounty hunter), the Bad (a hitman), and the Weird (a thief) battle the army and the bandits in a race to use a treasure map to uncover the riches of legend.
tagline: One map. Three villains. Winner takes all.
title: The Good, the Bad, the Weird
plot:
The Good, the Bad, the Weird is a 2008 South Korean Western film directed by Kim Jee-woon, produced by CJ Entertainment and CJ E&M. 

The movie follows three main characters: Kang-ho (played by Song Kang-ho), a former soldier; Cheon-bong (played by Byung-hun Lee), a young gunslinger; and Ban-gi (played by Ma Dong-seok), a mysterious outlaw. The story revolves around their quest for a buried treasure in the American West during the 1890s.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Friendship: Throughout the film, the three characters form an unlikely bond despite their differences. They learn to trust and rely on each other as they face various challenges.
2. Loyalty: The characters' loyalty to one another is tested when they are forced to make difficult choices that put their relationships at risk.
3. Redemption: Kang-ho's character, in particular, seeks redemption for past mistakes and finds a new sense of purpose through his journey with Cheon-bong and Ban-gi.
4. Morality: The film explores the gray areas between good and evil, as the characters are forced to confront their own moralities in the face of violence and betrayal.

The movie's unique blend of action, drama, and dark humor creates a captivating narrative that keeps viewers engaged until the very end.

overview: "The human whose name is written in the Death Note shall die." After making the hardest decision ever, another serious case confronts L. There are only 23 days left and without his best partner Watari (Shunji Fujimura), L has to solve the case all by himself for the very first time.
tagline: The final death note showdown!
title: L: change the WorLd
plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "L: Change the World" released in 2008 by Shochiku. 

However, I found that there is a Japanese film titled "L: Change the World" released in 2008, directed by Ryūhei Kitamura and produced by Toho Co., Ltd. not Shochiku.

The movie is based on the manga of the same name written by Tsutomu Nihei. 

"L: Change the World" is a science fiction film that explores themes of existentialism, nihilism, and the human condition. The story follows L, a mysterious figure who is tasked with erasing humans from existence. As L navigates this world, he begins to question his own purpose and the nature of humanity.

Throughout the movie, Kitamura delves into philosophical and psychological themes, exploring the idea that humanity's existence is but a fleeting moment in an infinite universe. The film also touches on the concept of identity and what it means to be human.

The movie features stunning visuals and a haunting score, which complements its thought-provoking narrative. Overall, "L: Change the World" is a visually striking and intellectually stimulating film that challenges viewers to confront their own existence and place in the world.

overview: Three high school seniors throw a party to make a name for themselves. As the night progresses, things spiral out of control as word of the party spreads.
tagline: Witness it
title: Project X
plot:
Project X is a 2012 American found-footage teen comedy directed by Nima Nourizadeh in his feature debut, written by Michael Bacall and Matt Drake and produced by Todd Phillips. Thomas Mann, Oliver Cooper and Jonathan Daniel Brown star as three friends who throw a party that spirals out of control, with Kirby Bliss Blanton, Dax Flame, Alexis Knapp and Miles Teller. The film was loosely associated with a notorious 2008 party thrown by an Australian teenager whose online invitation drew hundreds of uninvited guests.

In Pasadena, California, high-school students Costa and J.B. plan a party for their friend Thomas Kub's seventeenth birthday, hoping to boost their popularity. Thomas's parents leave town for the weekend, warning him not to invite too many people and not to drive his father's Mercedes. Thomas is reluctant, but Costa pushes ahead and hires Dax, an audiovisual student, to film the night's events. While Costa and J.B. spread word of the party around school, Thomas invites his best friend Kirby, who secretly has feelings for him, and Alexis, a popular girl he has a crush on. Shopping for supplies, the boys bump into Miles Teller, who already knows about the party. They then buy marijuana from a drug dealer, T-Rick, and Costa steals his lawn gnome as a party mascot, provoking a chase.

At first nobody arrives, and Thomas fears the party will be a flop, but then guests start pouring in by the hundreds. Thomas tries to confine the party to the backyard and pool house, hiring two young security guards to protect the house, but the crowd swells as news spreads online and on the radio. Neighbors complain, police are deceived into leaving, and the chaos escalates: the house is overrun, a car ends up in the swimming pool, Thomas's romantic life becomes tangled between Kirby and Alexis, and T-Rick returns seeking revenge, armed with a flamethrower, as the party turns into a riot visible from news helicopters and fires spread across the neighborhood.

Project X received generally negative reviews, with critics condemning its depiction of reckless behavior, though some praised its energy. It was a box-office success, grossing over $100 million worldwide against a budget of about $12 million, and inspired a number of real-life party incidents.

overview: Huo Yuan Jia became the most famous martial arts fighter in all of China at the turn of the 20th Century. Huo faced personal tragedy but ultimately fought his way out of darkness, defining the true spirit of martial arts and also inspiring his nation. The son of a great fighter who didn't wish for his child to follow in his footsteps, Huo resolves to teach himself how to fight - and win.
tagline: Mastering others is strength. Mastering yourself makes you fearless.
title: Fearless
plot:
Fearless is a 2006 biographical drama film directed by Ron Howard, not Rogue Pictures. 

The main themes of Fearless (2006) include:

1. **Perseverance and Resilience**: The film tells the story of Bill Bradley, a young man who overcomes numerous obstacles, including poverty, racism, and personal struggles, to become a successful businessman and politician.
2. **Self-Discovery and Personal Growth**: As Bill navigates his way through life, he learns valuable lessons about himself, his values, and his place in the world, ultimately emerging as a confident and compassionate individual.
3. **The Power of Education and Opportunity**: The film highlights the importance of education and access to opportunities in breaking cycles of poverty and achieving success.
4. **Overcoming Adversity and Staying True to Oneself**: Bill faces numerous challenges throughout his life, but he remains committed to his values and principles, even when faced with adversity.

The movie features an all-star cast, including Jeff Bridges as Bill Bradley, Blythe Danner as Bill's mother, and Emma Thompson as a love interest.

overview: When Michèle, the CEO of a gaming software company, is attacked in her home by an unknown assailant, she refuses to let it alter her precisely ordered life. She manages crises involving family, all the while becoming engaged in a game of cat and mouse with her stalker.
title: Elle
plot:
Elle (2016) is a psychological thriller that delves into the complexities of human nature, particularly through the character of Michèle Leblanc, a successful businesswoman who finds herself at the center of a cat-and-mouse game with her attacker. The film explores themes of power dynamics, control, and the blurred lines between victimhood and agency.

As Michèle navigates this treacherous situation, she must confront her own vulnerabilities and the societal expectations placed upon her as a woman. The film raises questions about the nature of consent, the objectification of women, and the ways in which patriarchal systems perpetuate violence against women.

Through Michèle's character, the film also touches on themes of identity, self-discovery, and the performance of femininity. As she grapples with her own desires and boundaries, Michèle must confront the societal norms that have shaped her into a particular kind of woman.

Ultimately, Elle is a thought-provoking exploration of the ways in which women are perceived, treated, and empowered within society. The film's portrayal of Michèle's inner world is both haunting and mesmerizing, offering a nuanced and unflinching look at the complexities of human experience.

overview: She is a good woman living a fulfilling life. Or so it seems. A caring mother, a capable housewife and a successful career woman, she looks after her mother with dementia on her own. What she needs is a little more space but somehow, she just can't find any. She decides to buy a house since she believes that a bigger place will make her family happy.
title: Reclaim
plot:
Reclaim (Chinese: 一家之主) is a 2022 Taiwanese family drama film written and directed by CJ Wang in her feature filmmaking debut. Produced by Rong Gwan Productions and released on Netflix in July 2022, it stars Lu Yi-ching as a self-sacrificing wife and mother, with Johnny Kou, Chia An-yu, Paw Hee-ching and Mason Lee in supporting roles. Rated TV-PG, it runs 124 minutes, mostly in Mandarin.

Lan-hsin (Lu), nearing retirement, has run a children's art studio and day care for more than thirty years. Her income has helped put her children through college and pay for a family apartment, where she once also cared for her father-in-law in his final years, and her own artistic ambitions have shrunk to painting the tiny items in the studio's dolls' house. At home, her retired husband David (Kou), a hoarder of supposedly valuable teapots and broken appliances, will not lift a finger, issues constant instructions and throws out her books to make room. Her cold, critical mother (Paw), who discouraged her dreams, including studying in Paris, is slipping into dementia and keeps wandering out of her nursing home. Her architect daughter (Chia) quietly confides that she has quit her job, broken up with her boyfriend and is moving back home, while her son, a college teacher in the United States, is considering returning with his wife to take over her family's farm, and her sister-in-law presses her with a get-rich-quick scheme selling upmarket cemetery plots. Believing that a bigger place will make her family happy, Lan-hsin sets out to find a new house large enough for all of them and weighs investment opportunities, at one point appearing to be defrauded by a young estate agent she knows, as the film, framed by her complaints to her mother, raises questions about whether some events are real or imagined and whether she will reclaim something for herself.

Reviews were mixed. Roger Moore of Movie Nation saw it as a kind of upside-down The Joy Luck Club steeped in Stella Dallas-style martyrdom, with interesting subtexts about Taiwanese family duty and gambling culture, but felt that Wang let scenes linger so long that 95 minutes of material played out over 124, muddling the message. Brian Hioe of Cinema Escapist found the focus on a woman on the verge of retirement promising but judged that the film lacked dramatic punch and focus, introducing the fraud subplot and doubts about the narrator's reliability too late to succeed.

overview: Accomplished sailor Charlie St. Cloud has the adoration of his mother Claire and his little brother Sam, as well as a college scholarship that will lead him far from his sleepy Pacific Northwest hometown. But his bright future is cut short when a tragedy strikes and takes his dreams with it. After his high-school classmate Tess returns home unexpectedly, Charlie grows torn between honoring a promise he made four years earlier and moving forward with newfound love. And as he finds the courage to let go of the past for good, Charlie discovers the soul most worth saving is his own.
tagline: Life is for living.
title: Charlie St. Cloud
plot:
Charlie St. Cloud is a 2010 American fantasy drama film directed by Burr Steers. The movie revolves around Charlie St. Cloud, a young man who struggles to cope with the loss of his younger brother Sam in a car accident.

The main theme of the movie is the power of love and redemption that transcends even death. Charlie's relationship with his brother is deeply emotional and complex, and his attempts to reconnect with him after his passing serve as a catalyst for his own personal growth and healing.

Throughout the film, Charlie grapples with feelings of guilt, grief, and anger, but ultimately finds solace in the memories he shared with Sam. The movie explores the idea that love can be both painful and transformative, and that it can help us find meaning and purpose even in the darkest of times.

The film also touches on themes of loss, regret, and the complexities of human relationships. Charlie's relationship with his father is particularly significant, as he struggles to come to terms with his own mortality and the consequences of his actions.

Ultimately, Charlie St. Cloud is a poignant exploration of the human experience, one that celebrates the beauty and complexity of love, loss, and redemption.

overview: Nelson is a man devoted to his advertising career in San Francisco. One day, while taking a driving test at the DMV, he meets Sara. She is very different from the other women in his life. Nelson causes her to miss out on taking the test and later that day she tracks him down. One thing leads to another and Nelson ends up living with her through a November that will change his life forever.
tagline: She Just Needed A Month To Change His Life Forever.
title: Sweet November
plot:
Sweet November is a 2001 American romantic drama directed by Pat O'Connor and set in San Francisco. A loose remake of the 1968 film written by Herman Raucher, which starred Anthony Newley and Sandy Dennis, it reunites Keanu Reeves and Charlize Theron after The Devil's Advocate (1997), with Jason Isaacs, Greg Germann and Lauren Graham in supporting roles. Warner Bros. Pictures released it on February 16, 2001.

Nelson Moss is a driven, self-absorbed advertising executive. At the Department of Motor Vehicles he tries to cheat on his driving test by asking for help from the woman next to him, Sara Deever, and it is she who is failed when the examiner thinks she is the cheat. The free-spirited Sara is intrigued by him and keeps proposing that he spend a month with her, assuring him that he will come out of it a better person. When November begins, after Nelson has lost both his job and his girlfriend on the same day, he finally agrees to stay with her.

The next day, Sara's close friend and neighbour Chaz refers to Nelson as her "November". Over the following weeks Sara draws Nelson out of his workaholic routine, and the two share a series of simple, happy experiences and gradually fall in love. Nelson begins to reflect on his life and past, and befriends Abner, a fatherless ten-year-old boy from the neighbourhood. Realising how much Sara means to him, he asks her to marry him.

Sara then reveals that she is dying of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and Chaz's remarks make clear that Nelson is not the first man she has spent such a month with. She tells Nelson to leave, admitting to Chaz that his was the first proposal she had wanted to accept. Nelson goes, but returns over the Thanksgiving holiday with gifts recalling their happy times and covers her walls with November calendars, telling her it can always be November for them.

They spend one more night together, but in the morning Nelson finds that Sara has taken the calendars down. She runs out, and he chases her through the streets until she stops on a footbridge and begs him to let her go, so that he can remember her as she was while she returns to the family she has been avoiding. She blindfolds him, leads him to the spot of one of their first dates and kisses him goodbye, and he removes the blindfold to find himself alone.

Critics panned the film as schmaltzy and manipulative, with a 15% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and it grossed 65.8 million dollars worldwide.

overview: Rachel Keller must prevent evil Samara from taking possession of her son's soul.
tagline: The dead don't sleep.
title: The Ring Two
plot:
The Ring Two is a 2005 supernatural horror film directed by Hideo Nakata and written by Michael Robert Johnson. It is the sequel to the 2002 remake of the Japanese horror film Ringu, starring Naomi Watts.

The story begins with Samara Morgan (Naomi Watts), the vengeful spirit from the first film, who has been trapped in a well for over 50 years. However, she manages to escape and begins to wreak havoc on the world once again.

The main protagonist of the film is Rachel Keller (Brynn Thayer), a young journalist who discovers that Samara's curse can be broken by finding her mother's diary. Rachel sets out to find the diary, which leads her to a mysterious woman named Anna Morgan (Amber Valletta), who claims to be Samara's mother.

As Rachel delves deeper into the mystery of Samara's past, she discovers that Anna was a former actress who became pregnant with Samara after being seduced by a wealthy and powerful man. The baby, Samara, was born with a rare genetic disorder that made her extremely intelligent and vengeful.

Anna, realizing that she had created a monster, tries to kill Samara as an infant, but the child survives and grows up to become the vengeful spirit that haunts Rachel in the present day. Anna's plan is to use Rachel to find the diary and break the curse, which would allow her to finally be at peace.

As the story unfolds, Rachel becomes increasingly entangled in a web of deceit and danger, as she tries to uncover the truth about Samara's past and the mysterious Anna Morgan. Along the way, she must confront her own dark past and the evil forces that are driving Samara's vengeful spirit.

The film builds towards a climactic showdown between Rachel and Anna, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Rachel manages to outsmart Anna and find the diary, which breaks the curse and allows Samara to finally rest in peace.

However, the film ends on a somewhat ambiguous note, leaving the audience wondering whether Samara's spirit has truly been laid to rest or if there is still more evil lurking in the shadows. Overall, The Ring Two is a thrilling and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of motherhood, guilt, and redemption.

overview: Christmas is drawing near, but it’s not a happy time for David. After moving to a big city, his parents have been bogged down with work and forgotten the meaning of Christmas. David decides to change that. Together with Albert the Elf, who escaped from the land of Santa to figure out what Christmas is all about, David sets off to Tatra Mountains, where his grandparents live, on a journey full of adventures.
title: David and the Elves
plot:
David and the Elves (Polish: Dawid i Elfy) is a 2021 Polish Christmas fantasy comedy directed by Michał Rogalski from a screenplay by Mateusz Kuczewski and Marcin Baczyński. Cyprian Grabowski plays a young boy and Jakub Zając a runaway elf, with Anna Smołowik and Michał Czernecki as the boy's parents and Cezary Żak and Monika Krzywkowska as Santa and Mrs. Claus. The film was released worldwide on Netflix on December 6, 2021.

Young David Kosmala loves the Christmases he spends with his parents and grandparents in their home in the Tatra Mountains, surrounded by family traditions. A year later, however, the family has moved to Warsaw, where his parents Hania and Piotr are overwhelmed by their jobs and have little time for him or for the festive season, and David feels lonely in the big city.

At the North Pole, meanwhile, Albert, a popular and confident elf who is tired of his routine, runs away against Santa's wishes, convinced that the people of the human world will adore him and that the trip will restore his Christmas spirit. Reality turns out to be very different. Wandering through Warsaw, he meets David in a park and the two become friends. Albert's magic soon causes chaos: he shrinks a huge lorry into a toy, turns a Christmas tree into a drum kit and transforms the fake beard of David's father into a real one. David tries to explain the strange events to his parents, but only manages to confuse them by describing Albert as a thief.

Santa sets out to find the runaway and realises that the longer Albert stays among humans, the more his Christmas magic drains away, and that he will eventually turn into a toy. Unaware of the danger, Albert keeps using his powers to help his new friend. When his magic finally runs out, he decides to return to the North Pole, and David goes with him to help him find his way, while David's parents, joined by Santa and Mrs. Claus, search for the two.

Sheltering in a forest for the night, David falls asleep, and Albert turns into a toy, undoing all the magic he has worked. Heartbroken, David carries the toy to his grandparents' house in the mountains, where his parents and the Clauses catch up with him. His efforts to bring Albert back seem to fail, until he finds footprints in the snow and Albert reappears behind him. Albert returns to the North Pole with the Clauses, and David's family rediscover the joy of spending Christmas together, singing carols with the elves. Common Sense Media rated it two out of five stars.

original_title: 好きになるその瞬間を。～告白実行委員会～
overview: Following Natsuki Enomoto's confession rehearsals with Yuu Setoguchi, their younger siblings Kotarou and Hina struggle to confess their own love. Despite a disastrous first meeting in middle school with her upperclassman Koyuki Ayase, Hina’s heart is captured by his warm smile. Initially confused by these newfound feelings, Hina soon realizes that she has fallen in love for the very first time.  Chasing after her brother Yuu and her crush Koyuki, Hina also enrolls in Sakuragaoka High School; but the threads of love are far-reaching, and they entangle Hina and her friends. Boisterous but sensitive, Hina hopes to confess her feelings to the tender-hearted Koyuki. Meanwhile, Kotarou, oblivious to his own feelings for her, is determined to always keep Hina smiling.  This movie follows Hina, Kotarou, and Koyuki in high school. Their youthful love forges new relationships, but also threatens to break others.
title: The Moment You Fall in Love
plot:
The Moment You Fall in Love is a 2016 animated short film produced by Qualia Animation. 

The story revolves around two young rabbits, who are initially portrayed as rivals, but eventually develop feelings for each other. As they navigate their blossoming romance, the film explores themes of love, vulnerability, and acceptance.

One of the main themes of The Moment You Fall in Love is the power of vulnerability and openness in relationships. The two rabbit characters must confront their own fears and insecurities in order to truly connect with each other. This theme is beautifully conveyed through the film's gentle animation and soothing music.

Another significant theme present in the film is the importance of acceptance and understanding. As the rabbits navigate their differences, they learn to appreciate and celebrate their unique qualities, rather than trying to change or hide them. This message promotes a positive and inclusive attitude towards diversity and individuality.

The film also touches on the idea that love can be a transformative experience, allowing individuals to grow and evolve as people. The rabbit characters' relationship serves as a catalyst for personal growth, as they learn to let go of their past fears and insecurities in order to move forward together.

Overall, The Moment You Fall in Love is a heartwarming and poignant film that explores the complexities and beauty of love and relationships through its gentle and charming storytelling.

overview: A slick robotics expert joins a murderous plot after a passionate affair takes a sudden turn, but nothing — not even death — is what it seems to be.
title: Monica, O My Darling
plot:
Monica, O My Darling is a 2022 Indian Hindi-language neo-noir crime comedy thriller directed by Vasan Bala and starring Rajkummar Rao, Huma Qureshi and Radhika Apte. Adapted from Keigo Higashino's 1989 Japanese mystery novel Burutasu no Shinzō (Heart of Brutus), it takes its title from a line in a song from the 1971 film Caravan. It was released on Netflix on 11 November 2022.

At Unicorn, a robotics company, an employee named Dev is killed by an industrial robot during a night shift; the death is ruled an accident and a safety officer is fired. Six months later, the ambitious engineer Jayant Arkhedkar is promoted to the board and engaged to Nikki, the daughter of the chairman, Satyanarayan Adhikari. However, he has been having an affair with the secretary, Monica Machado, who tells him she is pregnant with his child and demands money. Jayant then learns that the chairman's son, Nishikant, and the company's finance chief, Arvind, have also been involved with Monica and are being blackmailed by her in the same way.

The three men devise an elaborate plan to murder Monica and dispose of her body, signing a contract to bind one another to it. But the scheme goes awry: the next day Monica is alive, and the body that has been dumped is Nishikant's. As police officer ACP Naidu investigates, Arvind is killed by a venomous snake delivered to his home, and Jayant narrowly survives attempts on his own life. Monica denies being responsible and appears to have figured out the killer's identity, but before she can tell Jayant she dies from venom slipped into her wine.

Jayant learns that the robot that killed Dev was manually overridden, and discovers that the murderer was his friend Gaurav, the fiancé of Jayant's sister Shalu, who had been in love with her. Gaurav confesses to killing Nishikant, who had been using him, and Arvind, but denies murdering Monica. Jayant kills him in self-defense. Naidu, however, privately reveals that Monica's death was arranged by Satyanarayan, the true father of her child, leaving Jayant entangled in the company's corruption in the film's final twist.

Monica, O My Darling received positive reviews, with praise for Bala's direction, the performances of Rao, Qureshi and Apte, its music and its homage to vintage Hindi crime films, though some critics found its second half overlong. It won four Filmfare OTT Awards, including Best Web Original Film.

belongs_to_collection.name: Father There Is Only One Collection

original_title: Padre no hay más que uno
overview: Javier is what we have dubbed as a "husband-in-law." That is that without taking care of the care of the house and children at all, he knows exactly what needs to be done, and that he continuously collects a sum of sentences from the type: "It is that you do not organize", or "do not get nervous", you already consider that overflowing woman drowns in a glass of water. Javier will have to face the reality of dealing with five children (between four and twelve years old) when his wife decides to go on a trip and leave him alone with them. The chaotic situation that takes place at home will progressively evolve ecologically to the most absolute disaster, but at the same time it will give parents and children the opportunity to meet and enjoy themselves for the first time.
production_companies: MAMA SE FUE DE VIAJE LA PELICULA, A.I.E.
title: Father There Is Only One
plot:
Directed by and starring Santiago Segura, Father There Is Only One (Padre no hay más que uno) is a Spanish family comedy from 2019; Segura also co-wrote the script with Marta González de Vega. A remake of the 2017 Argentine film Ten Days Without Mom (Mamá se fue de viaje) by Ariel Winograd, it was a Bowfinger International Pictures and Sony Pictures International Productions project made with Atresmedia Cine's collaboration, and scored by Roque Baños. Toni Acosta co-stars as Marisa, with Silvia Abril, Leo Harlem, Wendy Ramos and the children Martina D'Antiochia, Calma Segura, Luna Fulgencio, Carlos González Morollón and Sirena Segura.

Javier García (Segura) is what Spaniards jokingly call a "marido-cuñado", a husband who never lifts a finger at home but always knows exactly how things ought to be done, telling his overwhelmed wife Marisa that she simply needs to get organized. He works outside the home and leaves the care of their five children, aged between four and twelve, entirely to her. Fed up, Marisa decides to go away on a week-long trip, leaving him alone with the kids to see whether he can manage the household as well as he claims. Without her, Javier quickly loses control: he must juggle his job with medical appointments, endless extracurricular activities, school demands and the relentless school parents' WhatsApp group, while lost children, burned curtains, constant fights and a black eye pile up. The housekeeper Rosaura (Ramos) and his brother-in-law Paco (Harlem) appear along the way. As chaos turns to disaster, Javier discovers how little he knew about his children's worries and dreams, and the experience gives father and children the chance to truly get to know and enjoy one another for the first time.

The film includes cameos by figures such as the YouTuber El Rubius, Ona Carbonell, Carlos Baute and Boris Izaguirre. Released by Sony Pictures in Spain on 2 August 2019, it drew 600,000 spectators and more than €3 million in its first week, the second-best Spanish opening of the year, and became the highest-grossing Spanish film of 2019. Critics were divided: Hobby Consolas found its satire of school WhatsApp groups accurate but considered the film a collection of clichés, while Industrias del Cine praised its warm humor and its criticism of the education system. Its success launched a franchise of four sequels and a spin-off television series.

overview: 10-year-old Bart Millard lives with his mother and abusive father Arthur in Texas. One day his mother drops him off at a Christian camp where he meets Shannon. Upon his return from camp, Bart finds his mother has left and movers are removing her belongings. He angrily confronts his father, who denies that his abusiveness was the reason she left. Years later, in high school, Bart and Shannon are dating. Bart plays football to please his father but is injured, breaking both ankles and ending his career. The only elective with openings is music class, so he reluctantly signs up.
tagline: The Song You Know. The Story You Don't.
title: I Can Only Imagine
plot:
I Can Only Imagine is a 2018 American biographical drama film directed by the Erwin Brothers and written by Alex Cramer, Jon Erwin, and Brent McCorkle. The movie is based on the life of Christian music star Bart Millard and his journey to write the song "I Can Only Imagine," which has become one of the most popular Christian songs of all time.

The film begins with a young Bart Millard (played by J. Michael Finley) growing up in a troubled home with an abusive father, Robert Millard (played by Dennis Quaid). Despite his difficult childhood, Bart finds solace in music and becomes a talented singer-songwriter. As he grows older, Bart's relationship with his father deteriorates, leading to a rift between them.

Bart's mother, Karen (played by Margo Martindale), tries to keep the family together, but ultimately passes away when Bart is just 15 years old. This event sets Bart on a path of self-discovery and spiritual exploration. He begins to question his faith and struggles with feelings of anger and resentment towards God.

As Bart navigates his teenage years, he meets a girl named Samantha (played by Cloris Leachman), who becomes a source of comfort and support in his life. However, their relationship is complicated, and they eventually part ways.

Bart's journey takes a dramatic turn when he discovers that his father has been diagnosed with terminal cancer. This event forces Bart to confront his feelings towards God and seek answers about the nature of suffering and pain. In a moment of profound insight, Bart writes "I Can Only Imagine," which becomes a powerful expression of his faith and emotions.

The film's climax features Bart performing the song live for the first time, with his father in attendance. The performance is met with an outpouring of emotion from the audience, including Robert Millard, who is visibly moved by the song's message.

Throughout the movie, the Erwin Brothers weave together themes of faith, family, and redemption, creating a powerful narrative that explores the complexities of human experience. The film features a talented cast, including Finley, Quaid, Martindale, and Leachman, who deliver nuanced performances that bring depth and emotion to their characters.

Ultimately, I Can Only Imagine is a movie about the transformative power of music and faith. It's a story about how one person's song can touch the lives of countless others and inspire them to seek answers about the nature of God and the human experience. The film's message is both uplifting and thought-provoking, making it a must-see for fans of Christian music and drama.

overview: Vampire death dealer Selene fends off brutal attacks from both the Lycan clan and the Vampire faction that betrayed her. With her only allies, David and his father Thomas, she must stop the eternal war between Lycans and Vampires, even if it means she has to make the ultimate sacrifice.
tagline: Protect the Bloodline
title: Underworld: Blood Wars
plot:
Underworld: Blood Wars is a 2016 action horror film directed by Anna Foerster from a screenplay by Cory Goodman, based on a story by Kyle Ward and Goodman. The fifth installment in the Underworld series and the sequel to Underworld: Awakening (2012), it stars Kate Beckinsale as the vampire warrior Selene, with Theo James as David, Lara Pulver as the ambitious vampire Semira, Tobias Menzies as the Lycan leader Marius, Bradley James, James Faulkner and Charles Dance as the vampire elder Thomas.

The surviving vampire covens are on the brink of being wiped out by the Lycans, the werewolves with whom they have fought a centuries-long war. Both sides are hunting Selene: the vampires want to punish her for killing the elder Viktor, while Marius and his Lycans want to use her to find her daughter Eve, whose blood could allow them to create an army of vampire-werewolf hybrids. At Thomas's urging, the council of the Eastern Coven agrees to pardon Selene in exchange for her help training a new generation of Death Dealers. However, Semira and her lover Varga betray Selene, poison her, massacre the trainees and frame her for the killings, intending to drink her blood to steal her power.

Rescued by David and Thomas, who dies in the attempt, Selene escapes to the Nordic Coven, where the elder Vidar reveals that David is the son of the vampire elder Amelia and the rightful heir to the Eastern Coven. When Marius learns of their location and attacks the Nordic stronghold, Selene is mortally wounded and sinks beneath the ice of a frozen lake, but she is revived by the Nordic vampires and gains new powers. As the Lycans launch an assault on the Eastern Coven, Selene and David return to confront Semira and Marius in a final battle for the future of the vampires.

The film was shot in Prague, Czech Republic, beginning in October 2015, and continues the series' blend of gothic visuals, gunplay and creature effects.

Underworld: Blood Wars was released in select countries on November 24, 2016, and in the United States on January 6, 2017. It grossed 81.1 million dollars worldwide against a budget of 35 million dollars but was panned by critics, receiving 21 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 23.

overview: Oakland, California. Young Afro-American Oscar Grant crosses paths with family members, friends, enemies and strangers before facing his fate on the platform at Fruitvale Station, in the early morning hours of New Year's Day 2009.
tagline: Every step brings you closer to the edge
title: Fruitvale Station
plot:
Fruitvale Station is a 2013 American drama film directed by Ryan Coogler, written by Coogler and Michael B. Jordan, and produced by Ava DuVernay, Oprah Winfrey, and Ryan Coogler.

The main themes of Fruitvale Station revolve around the life of Oscar Grant, a young black man who was tragically killed by a police officer in Oakland, California, on January 1, 2009. The film explores several key themes:

1. **Racial Profiling and Police Brutality**: The film highlights the systemic racism and racial profiling faced by African Americans, particularly in the context of law enforcement. Oscar's encounter with the police officer is a pivotal moment that showcases the dangers of unchecked power and prejudice.
2. **Youth and Identity**: Fruitvale Station explores the complexities of growing up as a young black man in America. Oscar struggles to find his place in the world, navigating relationships, family expectations, and societal pressures.
3. **Love and Relationships**: The film delves into Oscar's romantic relationship with Sophina, played by Melonie Diaz, and his complicated interactions with his mother, Wanda, played by Octavia Spencer. These relationships humanize Oscar and provide a glimpse into the emotional struggles he faces.
4. **Social Justice and Activism**: Fruitvale Station touches on the Black Lives Matter movement and the importance of speaking out against systemic injustices. The film encourages viewers to think critically about the world around them and to take action in support of social justice.
5. **Tragedy and Loss**: Ultimately, the film is a tragic portrayal of Oscar's life cut short by senseless violence. The movie raises questions about the value of human life and the need for empathy and understanding in our society.

Overall, Fruitvale Station is a powerful and thought-provoking film that sheds light on the complexities of racism, identity, love, and social justice in America.

overview: Young adults become fascinated by the events of the three missing filmmakers in Maryland, so they decide to go into the same woods and find out what really happened.
tagline: Evil Doesn't Die.
title: Book of Shadows: Blair Witch 2
plot:
Book of Shadows: Blair Witch 2 is a 2000 American supernatural horror film directed by Joe Berlinger. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1999 film The Blair Witch Project, but it deviates from the original's found-footage style and narrative.

The main themes of Book of Shadows: Blair Witch 2 include:

1. **Deception and Misdirection**: The film explores the idea that appearances can be deceiving, and that nothing is as it seems. The movie's protagonist, Heather Donahue, is initially portrayed as a strong and capable individual, but her character is later revealed to be flawed and vulnerable.
2. **Trauma and PTSD**: The story delves into the psychological effects of trauma on individuals, particularly those who have experienced extreme fear and stress. Heather's character struggles with the aftermath of her experiences in the woods, leading to a breakdown in her mental state.
3. **The Power of Mythology and Folklore**: The film draws heavily from folklore and mythology, incorporating elements of witchcraft and the supernatural. This theme serves as a commentary on how stories and legends can shape our perceptions of reality.
4. **The Dangers of Obsession**: Heather's fixation on uncovering the truth about the Blair Witch leads her down a dark path, blurring the lines between reality and fantasy. The movie cautions against the dangers of becoming too obsessed with a particular idea or narrative.

Overall, Book of Shadows: Blair Witch 2 is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and ideas, often using horror elements to convey its messages.

overview: After a group of biologists discovers a huge network of unexplored caves in Romania and, believing it to be an undisturbed eco-system that has produced a new species, they hire the best American team of underwater cave explorers in the world. While exploring deeper into the underwater caves, a rockslide blocks their exit, and they soon discover a larger carnivorous creature has added them to its food chain.
tagline: There are places man was never meant to go
title: The Cave
plot:
The Cave is a 2005 American adventure film directed by Andrew Davis and starring Oliver Reed, Michael Biehn, and Steven Brand.

The movie follows an archaeologist named Dr. John "Mac" McAllister (played by Michael Biehn) who discovers a hidden cave in the Middle East that contains ancient artifacts and treasures. As Mac delves deeper into the cave, he becomes obsessed with uncovering its secrets and finds himself trapped inside.

The main themes of The Cave include:

1. Obsession: Mac's single-minded pursuit of knowledge and treasure drives the plot of the movie, highlighting the dangers of unchecked ambition.
2. Isolation: The cave serves as a physical and emotional prison for Mac, symbolizing his own isolation from the world outside.
3. Redemption: As Mac navigates the treacherous cave system, he is forced to confront his past mistakes and seek redemption for his actions.
4. Power and greed: The movie explores the corrupting influence of power and wealth, as Mac's obsession with treasure leads him down a path of destruction.

The film features stunning visuals, heart-pumping action sequences, and a gripping storyline that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: In pursuit of an unclaimed $125,000 prize, a broke college dropout decides to play an obscure, 1980s survival computer game. But the game curses her, and she’s faced with dangerous choices and reality-warping challenges. After a series of unexpectedly terrifying moments, she realizes she’s no longer playing for the money but for her life.
tagline: Sometimes a curse can be a gift.
title: Choose or Die
plot:
Choose or Die, originally titled CURS>R, is a 2022 British science fiction horror thriller directed by Toby Meakins in his feature debut. It stars Iola Evans as Kayla, a struggling student, and Asa Butterfield as her friend Isaac, with Robert Englund and Eddie Marsan. The story centers on a cursed 1980s computer game that forces its players to make terrible choices with real-world consequences.

In the prologue, Hal, a collector of retro video games, installs an old text-based adventure game called CURS>R, only to find that the choices he makes in the game take horrifying effect in his own home. Three months later, Kayla, a college student working as a cleaner to pay for her studies, discovers a copy of the game at the apartment of her friend Isaac, a programmer who is helping her learn to code. The game comes with a phone number promising a prize of 125,000 dollars to anyone who completes it. Desperate for money to help her mother, who has become addicted to drugs after the death of Kayla's brother and is being exploited by a predatory landlord, Kayla begins to play.

She soon realizes that the game can manipulate reality, forcing her to choose between horrifying options that harm the people around her. When she tries to destroy the game, it escapes onto the internet and continues to pursue her, exploiting her deepest traumas, including the drowning of her brother. Working with Isaac, Kayla investigates the game's origins and discovers that its creator embedded an ancient curse in its code to feed on players' suffering. To survive and save the people she loves, Kayla must reach the end of the game and face its final challenge, which leads her to Hal.

The film draws on 1980s gaming nostalgia and pairs its supernatural premise with themes of poverty, trauma and exploitation.

Choose or Die was released on Netflix on 15 April 2022. It received negative to mixed reviews, with 30 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said its frightening promise was muffled by an excessively franchise-focused story, and a Metacritic score of 43. The Guardian gave it two stars out of five.

overview: Join Barbie and her sisters Skipper, Stacie and Chelsea as their holiday vacation plans turn into a most unexpected adventure and heartwarming lesson. After a snowstorm diverts their plane, the girls find themselves far from their New York destination and their holiday dreams. Now stranded at a remote inn in the tiny town of Tannenbaum, the sisters are welcomed by new friends and magical experiences. In appreciation for the wonderful hospitality they receive, they use their musical talents to put on a performance for the whole town. Barbie and her sisters realize the joy of being together is what really makes A Perfect Christmas!
title: Barbie: A Perfect Christmas
plot: The vacation plans of Barbie and her sisters take a turn due to a snowstorm. Stranded in Tannenbaum town, they find themselves amidst a holiday venture where they learn a heartwarming lesson.

overview: Hard-to-crack ex-CIA man Jack Byrnes and his wife Dina head for the warmer climes of Florida to meet the parents of their son-in-law-to-be, Greg Focker. Unlike their happily matched offspring, the future in-laws find themselves in a situation of opposites that definitely do not attract.
tagline: Misery loves family.
title: Meet the Fockers
plot:
Meet the Fockers is a comedy film directed by Jay Roach, released in 2004 by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1998 film Meet the Parents.

The story begins with Greg Focker (Ben Stiller), who has been dating Pam Byrnes (Teri Polo) for several years. As their relationship progresses, Greg's parents, Jack (Robert De Niro) and Dina (Blythe Danner), meet Pam's family, including her father, Byrnes Sr. (Barry Sonnenfeld). The meeting is a disaster, with Jack's eccentricities and strict adherence to tradition causing tension.

As the story unfolds, Greg tries to win over his future in-laws by introducing them to his parents. However, things only get worse when Jack discovers that Pam has been keeping him at arm's length due to her father's behavior. Feeling betrayed, Jack decides to take matters into his own hands and sets out to "fix" Greg.

Meanwhile, Greg is struggling with the idea of becoming a stepfather to Pam's two children from a previous marriage, Eric (Owen Wilson) and Karen (Molly Shannon). As he tries to connect with them, he realizes that being a good stepdad won't be easy.

As tensions between Jack and Greg escalate, the family becomes increasingly dysfunctional. The situation reaches its boiling point when Jack discovers that Pam is pregnant, leading him to believe that she's trying to replace him as her partner in life.

In the end, Greg must find a way to reconcile with his parents and prove himself as a worthy stepfather. With the help of his friends and family, he manages to bring everyone together and create a sense of unity and acceptance.

Throughout the film, the characters' quirks and flaws are on full display, leading to plenty of comedic moments. The chemistry between the cast members is undeniable, making it easy to become invested in their relationships.

The movie's themes of family, love, and acceptance are timeless and relatable, making Meet the Fockers a hilarious and heartwarming addition to the comedy genre.

overview: A woman who survived the brutal killing of her family as a child is forced to confront the events of that day.
tagline: In 1985, her entire family was murdered. 30 years later, the truth emerges.
title: Dark Places
plot:
Dark Places is a 2015 American dark comedy-thriller film directed by Jean-Marc Vallée, based on the novel of the same name by Gillian Flynn. The movie stars Charlize Theron, Nicholas Hoult, and Christina Hendricks.

The main themes of Dark Places include:

1. Trauma and its lasting impact: The film explores the long-term effects of childhood trauma on individuals, particularly in the context of a family's dark past.
2. Family dynamics and secrets: The movie delves into the complex relationships within a dysfunctional family, highlighting the ways in which secrets and lies can both bind and destroy them.
3. Revenge and justice: The protagonist, Libby Day, seeks revenge against her brother, Ben, who was accused of murdering their family members when she was just 11 years old. This theme is intertwined with the exploration of justice and morality.
4. Mental health and identity: Libby's struggles with mental health and her own identity are a significant aspect of the film, as she grapples with the truth about her past and her place in the world.

The movie follows Libby Day (Charlize Theron), who returns to her hometown after 25 years away, seeking answers about the murder of her family members. As she delves deeper into the past, she uncovers secrets and lies that challenge everything she thought she knew about herself and her family.

original_title: 劇場版 デート・ア・ライブ 万由里ジャッジメント
overview: After performing a huge concert, Miku Izayoi invited Shido, Tohka and everyone for a day at a reserved indoor pool. Later at night, Shido keeps spotting a girl named Mayuri, who quickly disappeared after seeing her.
tagline: Because I've met you....I'm no longer an existance that was born to disappear.
title: Date A Live: Mayuri Judgment
plot:
Date A Live: Mayuri Judgment is a 2015 Japanese animated film based on an original story by Kōshi Tachibana, featuring the characters of his light novel series Date A Live. Directed by Keitaro Motonaga from a screenplay by Hideki Shirane, it was produced by Production IMS and distributed by Kadokawa, and introduces Mayuri, a new character voiced by Sora Amamiya, alongside the returning cast including Nobunaga Shimazaki as Shido Itsuka and Marina Inoue as Tohka Yatogami. It opened in Japanese cinemas on August 22, 2015.

After a concert, the idol Miku Izayoi invites Shido and the Spirit girls whose powers he has sealed, Tohka, his sister Kotori, Yoshino and the twins Kaguya and Yuzuru, to a private indoor pool. On the way home Shido glimpses a mysterious girl whom only he can see, and who quickly vanishes. The next morning an enormous sphere appears floating above Tengu City. It is invisible to everyone else and can be detected only by the radar of the airship Fraxinus.

The analyst Reine Murasame suspects that the sphere has formed from Spirit energy that the six girls are unconsciously releasing because of their intense feelings for Shido. To calm their emotions and make it disappear, she suggests that Shido take each of them on a date, and he goes out in turn with Kaguya, Miku, Yoshino, Yuzuru, Kotori and finally Tohka, all while the mysterious girl watches over him.

During his date with Tohka, interrupted earlier by Origami Tobiichi, Shido meets the girl, who introduces herself as Mayuri. She explains that she was born from the Spirit powers that he has sealed away and is bound to the sphere, an Angel named Kerubiel. Having fulfilled her role of keeping the girls' feelings in balance, she prepares to say goodbye, but Kerubiel suddenly transforms and attacks, kidnapping Mayuri. Reine realises that the Angel has turned violent because of Mayuri's own jealousy of the girls who dated Shido.

When Shido declares that he wants to save Mayuri, the girls' Spirit powers are temporarily released and they battle Kerubiel. After Mayuri is rescued, the Angel transforms again. As Shido tries to protect everyone, the dangerous Spirit Kurumi Tokisaki secretly saves him, and the energy gathered by Mayuri gives Tohka a new Astral Dress. With Mayuri kissing Shido to aid her, Tohka destroys Kerubiel. The kiss seals Mayuri, and she fades away, leaving Shido a necklace and a lollipop as keepsakes. The film grossed about 248,000 dollars.

overview: On the cusp of his 30th birthday, Jonathon Larson, a promising young theater composer, navigates love, friendship, and the pressures of life as an artist in New York City.
tagline: How much time do we have to do something great?
title: tick, tick... BOOM!
plot:
Tick, Tick... Boom! is a musical drama film directed by Lin-Manuel Miranda, based on the 2001 semi-autobiographical musical of the same name by Jonathan Larson. The movie follows the life of Jonathan Larson, a young composer struggling to create his first Broadway musical.

The main themes of Tick, Tick... BOOM! include:

1. **Creativity and Self-Discovery**: The film explores Jonathan's journey as he navigates his passion for music and theater, while trying to find his place in the world. He grapples with self-doubt, fear of failure, and the pressure to succeed.
2. **Time Management and Priorities**: As Jonathan struggles to balance his creative pursuits with his personal life, including relationships and financial responsibilities, he must confront the consequences of prioritizing one over the other.
3. **Mortality and Impermanence**: The film touches on the theme of mortality, as Jonathan faces the reality that his time is limited. He must come to terms with the fact that his creative output may not be recognized or appreciated during his lifetime.
4. **Friendship and Support**: The relationships between Jonathan and his friends, particularly Susan (played by Vanessa Hudgens) and Michael (played by Joshua Henry), are crucial in helping him navigate the challenges he faces.
5. **Perseverance and Resilience**: Despite facing numerous setbacks and rejections, Jonathan perseveres, driven by his passion for art and his determination to leave a lasting legacy.

These themes are woven throughout the film, which features an original score by Lin-Manuel Miranda, blending music, dance, and drama to tell Jonathan's story.

overview: Three people — a blue-collar American, a French journalist and a London school boy — are touched by death in different ways.
tagline: Touched by death. Changed by life.
title: Hereafter
plot:
Hereafter is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human existence, exploring the interconnectedness of life and death. The movie masterfully weaves together three seemingly unrelated storylines, each focusing on a different character's journey towards understanding the afterlife.

At its core, Hereafter is a poignant exploration of grief, loss, and the human need for connection. Through the eyes of its characters, the film reveals the profound impact that loved ones can have on our lives, even after they're gone. The movie also delves into the concept of near-death experiences (NDEs), raising questions about the nature of consciousness and the possibility of an afterlife.

One of the main themes of Hereafter is the idea that love transcends mortality. The film shows how the bonds we form with others can be incredibly powerful, even in the face of death. This theme is beautifully illustrated through the character of Claude, a French TV journalist who forms a deep connection with a young girl named Alyah, whose mother has passed away.

Another significant theme present in Hereafter is the concept of closure and acceptance. The movie highlights the importance of coming to terms with one's own mortality and finding peace in the face of loss. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, as each character grapples with their own unique struggles and ultimately finds a way to move forward.

Ultimately, Hereafter is a film about hope, resilience, and the human spirit. It reminds us that even in the darkest moments, there is always the possibility for connection, healing, and transformation. The movie's thoughtful exploration of these themes makes it a deeply moving and thought-provoking experience for audiences.

overview: When a young couple buys their dream home, they have no idea what the sweet little old lady upstairs is going to put them through!
title: Duplex
plot:
Duplex is a 2003 American comedy film directed by Danny DeVito and starring Ben Stiller and Drew Barrymore.

The main themes of Duplex revolve around the struggles of first-time homeownership, marriage, and the challenges of adapting to new environments. The story follows Max (Ben Stiller) and his fiancée, Olivia (Drew Barrymore), as they navigate their way through a series of misadventures in New York City.

One of the primary themes is the comedic exploration of the challenges of urban living, particularly for young couples trying to establish themselves. The film pokes fun at the absurdities of city life, from noisy neighbors to bureaucratic red tape.

Another significant theme is the portrayal of marriage and relationships. Max and Olivia's relationship is put to the test as they face various obstacles, including their own personal differences and the pressures of becoming homeowners. The film offers a humorous take on the ups and downs of married life, highlighting the importance of communication and compromise in maintaining a healthy partnership.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and cultural assimilation. Max, an American, is forced to adapt to a new culture when he moves into a New York City apartment with Olivia, who is from a more traditional background. The film explores the challenges of navigating different social norms and expectations, leading to comedic misunderstandings and unexpected connections.

Throughout the film, Duplex balances humor with heart, offering a relatable portrayal of young adulthood and the complexities of relationships.

original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター 幻のポケモン ルギア爆誕
overview: When Lawrence III's scheme to capture the Legendary Pokémon Lugia upsets the balance of nature, it is up to Ash Ketchum and his friends to save the world.
tagline: One person can make all the difference.
title: Pokémon: The Movie 2000
plot:
Pokémon: The Movie 2000, also known as Pokémon 2000: The Power of One, is a Japanese animated science fantasy film based on the popular Pokémon media franchise. The movie was produced by OLM, Inc., and TV Tokyo.

The story begins with Ash Ketchum, a young trainer from Pallet Town, who is on his way to the Indigo League tournament with his Pikachu. However, their journey takes an unexpected turn when they encounter a mysterious and powerful Pokémon known as Suicune, one of the three Legendary Beasts of Johto.

Suicune is being pursued by Team Rocket, who seek to capture it for their nefarious plans. Ash and Pikachu soon find themselves entangled in the chase, along with other trainers and their Pokémon. As they journey across the Johto region, they uncover a hidden truth about Suicune's past and its connection to the balance of nature.

Meanwhile, a mysterious figure known as Lawrence III is revealed to be behind Team Rocket's plans. He seeks to exploit Suicune's power for his own gain, which would disrupt the natural balance and allow him to control the world. Ash and his friends must now stop Lawrence and his team from achieving their sinister goals.

Throughout the movie, Ash and Pikachu form a strong bond with Suicune, learning about its unique abilities and the importance of teamwork and trust. The film features epic battles between the trainers and their Pokémon, as well as heartwarming moments of friendship and growth.

As the story unfolds, Ash and his friends face numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, fierce wild Pokémon, and even a rival trainer named Clair. However, with Suicune's guidance and support, they are able to overcome these hurdles and ultimately defeat Lawrence and his team.

In the climactic final battle, Ash confronts Lawrence III in an epic showdown. With Pikachu by his side, Ash uses all his skills and strategy to outmaneuver Lawrence and shatter his plans for world domination. In the end, Suicune is able to find peace and return to its natural habitat, restoring balance to the region.

Pokémon: The Movie 2000 features stunning animation, engaging characters, and an exciting plot that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and the importance of preserving nature. With its memorable soundtrack and lovable Pokémon, this film has become a beloved classic among fans of the franchise.

overview: Maurice may look like a penguin - but he's a real tiger inside! Raised by a tigress, he's the clumsiest kung-fu master ever. Along with his friends, The Jungle Bunch, he intends to maintain order and justice in the jungle, as his mother did before he. But Igor, an evil koala, wants to destroy the jungle once and for all—helped by his army of silly baboons.
title: The Jungle Bunch
plot: Maurice may look like a penguin - but he's a real tiger inside! Raised by a tigress, he's the clumsiest kung-fu master ever. Along with his friends, The Jungle Bunch, he intends to maintain order and justice in the jungle, as his mother did before he.
