overview: After witnessing a miracle, a young Latina woman experiences strange things as a police detective searches for the truth behind his partner's death.
tagline: Some secrets are better left buried
title: Exposed
plot:
Exposed, originally titled Daughter of God, is a 2016 American crime thriller written and directed by Gee Malik Linton in his directorial debut. Linton is credited under the pseudonym Declan Dale after disputing a final edit that shifted the film's focus. Keanu Reeves stars as the NYPD detective Scotty Galban and Ana de Armas as Isabel de la Cruz, a young Latina woman, with Christopher McDonald, Big Daddy Kane, Mira Sorvino and Laura Gómez. Lionsgate Premiere released the film in limited theaters and on video on demand on 22 January 2016.

Detective Galban investigates the death of his partner, Detective Joey Cullen, whose body has been found in mysterious circumstances. The case draws him into a world of police secrecy, as it soon becomes clear that Cullen was corrupt and abusive. His colleagues fear that a thorough investigation will expose his misdeeds, bringing bad publicity for the department and costing his family his pension. One of the prime suspects is a young former convict whom Cullen allegedly sexually assaulted, and some of Galban's superiors would rather let the killer go free than open a Pandora's box of trouble for everyone involved.

In a parallel storyline, Isabel, a devout young woman from a Latino neighborhood of New York, has a very different experience of the city. She befriends a girl named Elisa and suspects that the child is being abused by her father. Isabel begins to see strange, otherworldly figures in the streets and subways, whom she believes are angels, and when she discovers that she is mysteriously pregnant, she becomes convinced that the pregnancy is a divine gift, a belief no one around her is willing to accept. The two seemingly unrelated stories unfold side by side in separate urban worlds, but as Galban's investigation progresses, it emerges that Isabel is somehow connected to Cullen's death, and the visions she has experienced are revealed to be linked to a traumatic event that she has been unable to confront.

Exposed was poorly received by critics, many of whom felt that the studio's reediting, which marketed the film as a Keanu Reeves police thriller, undermined what had been conceived as Isabel's story, leaving the two narratives disjointed. De Armas's performance was singled out for praise, and the film is often cited as an early English-language role in her career before her rise to international prominence.

overview: After a breakup, an influencer takes her friends on a free trip to Bahia's vibrant Carnival, where she learns life's not just about social media likes.
title: Carnaval
plot:
Carnaval is a 2021 Brazilian comedy film directed by Leandro Neri, who wrote the screenplay with Audemir Leuzinger and Luisa Mascarenhas. Produced by Camisa Listrada in partnership with Netflix, it stars Giovana Cordeiro, Bruna Inocencio, Gessica Kayane and Samya Pascotto as four friends who spend the Carnival holiday in Salvador, Bahia. Netflix released it simultaneously in 190 countries on 2 June 2021.

Nina (Cordeiro), an aspiring digital influencer, discovers that a video of her famous boyfriend cheating on her has gone viral. To get over the break-up, she uses her contacts to land an all-expenses-paid trip to Salvador during Carnival week, invited by the charming singer Freddy Nunes (Borges), and brings along her three best friends: the crowd-shy Mayra (Inocencio), the nerdy, guarded Vivi (Pascotto) and the loud, flirtatious Michelle (Kayane). On arrival, they find themselves in a poor hotel with fewer privileges than the more famous influencers. Desperate to climb the social media ladder, Nina neglects her friends to chase likes and Freddy's attention. Vivi is courted by a fellow geek, Samir (Medrado), and the popular influencer Luana (Pavanelli) courts cancellation after drunken offensive remarks. Salvador (Pedro), a local tour guide who develops a crush on Nina, shows her the city away from the sponsored Carnival floats and teaches her to enjoy the moment rather than live behind a phone screen. A late twist involves a character trying to pass as straight, whom one of the friends supports when the truth comes out. Each of the women learns something about herself, and Nina realises that social media fame is a poor substitute for real friendship.

Although set in Salvador, much of the film was shot at a resort in Praia do Forte, about 30 kilometres away, while the street celebration scenes were filmed during the 2020 Carnival. The film topped Netflix's Top 10 in Brazil and also charted in Portugal and Spain. Critics were less kind, with only one of six reviews counted by Rotten Tomatoes positive. Monica Castillo of RogerEbert.com likened it to Girls Trip, praising the vivid Carnival spectacle but finding the leads close to stock characters and the comedy over-exaggerated. In Brazil the film was criticised for geographical errors, for having few black actors in its main cast despite being set in the Brazilian city with the largest black population, and for casting a Rio de Janeiro singer as a Bahian star.

overview: A stranger in the city asks questions no one has asked before. Known only by his initials, the man's innocent questions and childlike curiosity take him on a journey of love, laughter and letting go.
tagline: Peeke hai kya?
title: PK
plot:
PK (2014) is a thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human existence, spirituality, and the search for meaning in a chaotic world. The movie delves into the theme of blind faith and the consequences of blindly following authority.

The story revolves around PK, an alien who crash-lands on Earth and assumes the form of a common man to understand humanity better. As he navigates through various social and cultural contexts, he begins to question the existence of God and the role of religion in people's lives.

Through PK's journey, the film highlights the tension between rationality and superstition, as well as the dangers of blindly following dogma without questioning its validity. The movie also explores the theme of individual freedom and autonomy, as PK struggles to reconcile his own values with the societal expectations placed upon him.

One of the most striking aspects of PK is its critique of the commercialization of spirituality and the exploitation of people's faith for personal gain. The film portrays a world where people are more concerned with material wealth and status than with genuine spiritual growth or self-discovery.

Ultimately, PK (2014) is a movie that challenges viewers to think critically about their own beliefs and values, and to question the status quo in pursuit of truth and understanding.

They both believe love is inconvenient and agree to a contractual fling expiring on the date Ayef leaves for Singapore, but they start falling for one another.
tagline: Love with no expiration.

overview: A recently slain cop joins a team of undead police officers working for the Rest in Peace Department and tries to find the man who murdered him.
tagline: To protect and serve the living.
title: R.I.P.D.
plot:
R.I.P.D. is a supernatural action-comedy film directed by Robert Schwentke and written by Scott Waugh and David Koepp, based on the comic book series of the same name by Peter Craig and Matt Holness.

The movie follows the story of Nick Walker (played by Ryan Reynolds), a Los Angeles police detective who dies in the line of duty. However, instead of moving on to the afterlife, Nick is brought back as a "Reaper" - an undead law enforcement agent tasked with maintaining order and justice in the living world.

Nick's new partner is Jonesy (played by Jeff Bridges), a seasoned Reaper who has been working for over 100 years. Jonesy is initially hesitant to take on a new partner, but eventually warms up to Nick's enthusiasm and determination.

The two Reapers are tasked with solving a series of murders that have taken place in Los Angeles. The victims all have one thing in common: they were involved in a massive conspiracy involving the corrupt businessman Captain Zane (played by Peter Firth) and his accomplices.

As Nick and Jonesy delve deeper into the case, they discover that the murders are connected to an ancient evil known as the "Devil's Gate", which has been unleashed on the world. The Devil's Gate is a portal that allows spirits from the afterlife to enter the living world, causing chaos and destruction.

Nick and Jonesy must work together to stop Captain Zane and his accomplices, while also navigating their own complicated relationship with each other. Along the way, Nick learns more about the Reaper program and the true nature of his existence.

As the story unfolds, Nick and Jonesy face off against a series of increasingly formidable foes, including a group of rogue Reapers who are working to undermine the authority of the program. The stakes are raised when Nick discovers that he has a personal connection to one of the victims, which makes the case even more urgent for him.

In the end, Nick and Jonesy succeed in stopping Captain Zane and closing the Devil's Gate, but not before they both suffer significant losses. The movie concludes with Nick finally finding some measure of peace and acceptance as a Reaper, while also forming a bond with his partner that transcends their differences.

Overall, R.I.P.D. is a fun and action-packed supernatural thriller that explores themes of mortality, identity, and the complexities of human relationships. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of Ryan Reynolds and Jeff Bridges will likely enjoy this entertaining and visually stunning film.

overview: When Earth astronaut Capt. Chuck Baker arrives on Planet 51 -- a world reminiscent of American suburbia circa 1950 -- he tries to avoid capture, recover his spaceship and make it home safely, all with the help of an empathetic little green being.
tagline: Something strange is coming to their planet...Us!
title: Planet 51
plot:
Planet 51 is a 2009 animated science fiction comedy film directed by Jorge Blanco and produced by Ilion Animation Studios.

The movie begins with Captain Leo Crow, an astronaut from Earth who lands on the planet Zorgon-6, which he believes to be a new home for humanity. However, upon arrival, he discovers that the inhabitants of the planet are not what he expected - they are actually aliens who have been watching Earth's transmissions and have created a fake human settlement.

As Captain Crow navigates this bizarre situation, he meets the friendly but awkward alien named Lem, who tries to help him adjust to life on Zorgon-6. Meanwhile, a sinister plot unfolds as the true intentions of the Zorgons are revealed, threatening the safety of both humans and aliens alike.

The main themes of Planet 51 include:

1. **Misunderstanding and Cultural Exchange**: The film explores the consequences of misinterpreting cultural norms and customs between two vastly different species.
2. **Friendship and Empathy**: Despite their differences, Captain Crow and Lem form an unlikely bond, demonstrating the power of friendship and empathy in bridging intergalactic divides.
3. **Deception and Trust**: As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that not everyone on Zorgon-6 is what they seem, highlighting the importance of trust and discernment in relationships.

Overall, Planet 51 offers a lighthearted and entertaining take on these themes, making it an enjoyable film for both children and adults.

overview: I CAN'T THINK STRAIGHT is a 2007 romance movie about a London-based Jordanian of Palestinian descent, Tala, who is preparing for an elaborate wedding. A turn of events causes her to have an affair and subsequently fall in love with another woman, Leyla, a British Indian.
title: I Can't Think Straight
plot:
I Can't Think Straight is a romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of love, identity, and cultural differences. The movie follows the story of a young British woman, Tessa, who returns to London after a painful breakup with her girlfriend in New York.

As Tessa navigates her way through a new relationship with a Pakistani woman named Iqbal, she is forced to confront her own biases and prejudices against people from different cultural backgrounds. Through their blossoming romance, the film delves into themes of acceptance, understanding, and the challenges of navigating intercultural relationships.

The movie also touches on issues of identity, as both Tessa and Iqbal struggle with their own sense of self and belonging. Tessa's experiences in New York have left her feeling disconnected from her British roots, while Iqbal is caught between her traditional Pakistani upbringing and her desire for independence.

Ultimately, the film presents a nuanced exploration of love, acceptance, and cultural exchange, highlighting the complexities and rewards of relationships that bridge cultural divides.

overview: The story of Otto Anderson, a grumpy widower who is very set in his ways. When a lively young family moves in next door, he meets his match in quick-witted and very pregnant Marisol, leading to an unlikely friendship that will turn his world upside-down.
tagline: Fall in love with the grumpiest man in America.
title: A Man Called Otto
plot:
A Man Called Otto is a 2022 American comedy-drama directed by Marc Forster from a screenplay by David Magee. A remake of the 2015 Swedish film A Man Called Ove, itself based on Fredrik Backman's 2012 novel, it stars Tom Hanks as Otto Anderson, with his son Truman Hanks playing the character as a young man, alongside Mariana Treviño, Rachel Keller and Manuel Garcia-Rulfo. Sony Pictures released it in limited theaters on 29 December 2022 and nationwide in the United States on 13 January 2023.

Otto Anderson is a sixty-three-year-old widower living in a townhouse community in suburban Pittsburgh. Six months after the death of his wife, Sonya, a schoolteacher, he has become a grumpy, rule-obsessed recluse who patrols the neighborhood scolding residents for every infraction. Forced into retirement from his job at a steel company, he cancels his utilities and prepares to take his own life so he can be with Sonya. His attempt is interrupted by the arrival of new neighbors across the street: Marisol, who is pregnant, her husband Tommy and their two young daughters, who insist on befriending him.

Otto's repeated attempts to end his life are thwarted by mishaps and by the needs of the people around him. Visiting Sonya's grave, he remembers how, as a young man rejected by the army because of a heart condition, he met her on a train platform when she dropped a book, and how their romance began. He helps his neighbor Anita with her radiators, although he holds a long grudge against her husband Reuben, once his close friend, now incapacitated after a stroke. When Tommy is injured falling from a ladder, Otto reluctantly drives Marisol and the girls to the hospital and begins teaching her to drive. Gradually, his friendship with Marisol's warm, persistent family, a stray cat and a young transgender man who was once Sonya's student draws Otto out of his isolation. He also takes on a real-estate company scheming to force Anita and Reuben from their home, and comes to terms with the painful events that shaped his marriage.

The film received generally positive reviews, with critics praising Hanks's and Treviño's performances despite finding the story sentimental and predictable. It grossed over $113 million worldwide, and its original song "Til You're Home," performed by Rita Wilson and Sebastián Yatra, featured on the soundtrack.

overview: When returning home for the holidays, newly minted pop star Jaylen tells her protective family that Matt is her new beau, when in reality, he’s her overzealous security guard.
tagline: He's the kind of bodyguard you take home to your home.
title: Undercover Holiday
plot:
Undercover Holiday is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy-drama television film produced by Cineflix Productions for Hallmark Channel. It stars Noemi Gonzalez as the pop star Jaylen and Stephen Huszar as her bodyguard Matt, with Mishka Thébaud, Ann Pirvu, Diana Salvatore, Amanda Martínez, Juan Chioran and Allison Feliciano. The film runs 84 minutes and was promoted with the tagline "He's the kind of bodyguard you take home to your home."

Jaylen's life has changed dramatically since she won a singing competition and became one of the hottest new pop stars in the country. The attention has also brought her a stalker, and her record label hires Matt, a former Navy SEAL, to protect her. When she returns home for the holidays to her large, multi-generational family, the Rodriguezes, Jaylen knows that her loving but overprotective relatives, who already consider Los Angeles an unsafe place, would be alarmed to learn that she needs a security guard. She therefore introduces Matt as her new boyfriend and insists that he keep up the charade throughout the visit. The deception proves awkward for both of them: in addition to spending time with friends and family, Jaylen has a series of publicity events to attend, which makes Matt's job harder, and the serious, overzealous bodyguard struggles to relax as she wants him to while pretending to be in love. Staying with her family, Matt, a man used to a solitary life, gets to experience a Christmas full of warmth and family traditions, and comes to appreciate the support Jaylen enjoys. In turn, he helps her see that she should take control of her career rather than let her label dictate her music, as she wants to release songs in both English and Spanish despite the company's resistance. As the fake relationship continues, the two must decide whether to keep things strictly professional or admit to feelings that have become real.

The film premiered on Hallmark Channel on 4 December 2022. Reviews were lukewarm. Alonso Duralde of TheWrap, ranking all 43 of Hallmark's new Christmas films of 2022, placed it 32nd, describing it as a Hallmark fake-boyfriend movie crossed with The Bodyguard whose results were middling. Kristen of TV Tweetie enjoyed Jaylen as a strong, independent heroine who stands up to her family and label, and liked the depiction of the Rodriguez family's Christmas traditions, but found the film slow and unoriginal and did not recommend it.

overview: A Detroit cop reluctantly teams with his girlfriend's 11-year-old son to clear his name and take down the city's most ruthless criminal.
title: Coffee & Kareem
plot:
Coffee & Kareem is a 2020 American action comedy film directed by Michael Showalter. The movie revolves around the unlikely friendship between a young man named Brian, who is struggling to find his place in life, and Kareem, a tough but lovable ex-Marine.

At its core, Coffee & Kareem explores themes of identity, belonging, and the complexities of male relationships. The film delves into Brian's journey as he navigates his way through young adulthood, trying to find his purpose and sense of direction in life. Through his interactions with Kareem, Brian is forced to confront his own vulnerabilities and insecurities, leading to a deeper understanding of himself and those around him.

The movie also touches on the theme of mentorship and the importance of male role models in shaping young men's lives. Kareem, as a gruff but caring figure, serves as a source of guidance and wisdom for Brian, helping him to find his way through life's challenges.

Furthermore, Coffee & Kareem explores the tension between traditional masculinity and vulnerability, highlighting the need for men to be willing to express their emotions and show vulnerability in order to form meaningful connections with others. The film suggests that this vulnerability is not a sign of weakness, but rather a strength that allows individuals to build deeper, more authentic relationships.

Overall, Coffee & Kareem is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of the complexities of male relationships, identity, and belonging, offering a fresh take on traditional coming-of-age stories.

overview: The opening of the new tunnel, which took ten years to build, coincided with a series of serious cataclysms. The lives of 160,000 people depend on the actions of two people, a father and a son.
tagline: When a catastrophe comes, no one should be left behind.
title: Cloudy Mountain
plot:
Cloudy Mountain (Chinese: 峰爆, Fēng bào, "Peak Explosion"; working title 无限深度, "Infinite Depth") is a 2021 Chinese disaster film directed by Li Jun, who co-wrote the screenplay with Sha Song. Produced and presented by China Film and framed as a tribute to China's "railway soldiers", the military corps that built and repaired lines in dangerous terrain, it stars Zhu Yilong, Huang Zhizhong, Chen Shu and Jiao Junyan, with Cheng Taishen and cameos by Zhang Guoli, Zhang Yi, Bai Ke and Li Guangjie. Shot in Guizhou province with action by Bruce Law and music by Guo Sida, it opened in China on 17 September 2021, ahead of the National Day holiday.

In fictional Yunjiang county in south-west China, a construction team is completing a tunnel through Yundang mountain for a high-speed railway after ten years of work, in a region of fragile karst rock destabilised by movement of the Indian Ocean plate. When a blast supervised by the young engineer Hong Yizhou (Zhu) floods the tunnel, he and his girlfriend, the radar technician Lu Xiaojin (Jiao), divert the water into a cavern, and project manager Ding Yajun (Chen) halts work, although her superiors insist the line must open on time. Abseiling down the mountain to place sensors, Yizhou finds abnormal rock activity. Meanwhile his gruff father, the retired railway soldier Hong Yunbing (Huang), arrives in town just as an earthquake strikes and a vast sinkhole swallows his coach. After helping rescue survivors, Yunbing disappears underground, where he leads a small group of survivors, including a stowaway boy, through the caves. Yizhou races to find him and takes over the group, but old tensions between father and son resurface. Ding plans to blast away part of the mountain to stop it collapsing onto the rail bridge, but the predicted landslide shifts towards Yunjiang, a town of 160,000 that cannot be evacuated in time, as a storm approaches. To save the town, the railway builders resolve to blow up the tunnel that cost them a decade of work; Yizhou proves himself to his father, overcoming a phobia from his youth, and a great sacrifice is made along the way.

The film grossed just under 440 million yuan in China. Sino-Cinema rated it 6/10, finding it a solid but by-the-book disaster movie that starts strongly but becomes increasingly cartoonish and implausible in its patriotic second half, and judging Huang a stronger presence than Zhu; Cheng Taishen stood out as a veteran chief engineer.

overview: A big family moves into a dusty old house in the snowy woods of Washington with hopes of it being a nice holiday escape. But the kids soon discover a stash of old toys that just so happen to belong to a creepy ghost boy. As stranger and stranger things start to happen, some of the kids begin to sense that something in the house is not quite right…
title: Toys of Terror
plot:
Toys of Terror is a 2020 American Christmas horror film directed by Nicholas Verso and written by Dana Gould, a writer on The Simpsons. Released by Warner Bros. on digital platforms on 27 October 2020, it stars Kyana Teresa, Georgia Waters, Dayo Ade, Saul Elias, Zoe Fish and Verity Marks, with Ernie Pitts and Lauren Mary Marshall. Its killer toys are brought to life largely through stop-motion animation, in a nod to the Rankin/Bass holiday specials.

In a prologue, Helen Modig (Marshall), devastated by the death of her ten-year-old son Jason at the Saint Germaine Children's Clinic, curses a trunk of toys and leaves it on the building's doorstep; on Christmas morning all the other children at the clinic are found dead. Years later, house flipper Hannah Cashman (Teresa) buys the mountainside property to renovate with her contractor Emmett (Pitts), and brings her husband David (Ade), his 15-year-old daughter Alicia (Marks), her young children Zoe (Fish) and Franklin (Elias) and their nanny Rose (Waters) to spend Christmas there. Zoe and Franklin find the trunk, which holds a plush bee, a dinosaur helmet that distorts the wearer's voice, a remote-control car, action figures, a fez-wearing doll called Uncle Monkey and a retro video game console. The younger children begin behaving strangely as the toys sing and dance for them in secret, while Alicia and Rose, who is still haunted by a miscarriage, glimpse the ghost of a little boy. Alicia nearly chokes as Franklin watches, and her video game mirrors events in the house. On Christmas Eve the bee lures Emmett into the attic, where he falls through the floor and is impaled; David is injured in a crash while driving him to hospital. The toys wreck the living room, Uncle Monkey starts a fire, and Christmas decorations attack Hannah until Alicia fights them off. The toys then try to persuade Zoe and Franklin to jump from the attic window to join the dead children. Hannah stops them and Rose helps Alicia lock the toys back in the trunk, but Uncle Monkey stabs Rose, who falls to her death. With David back, the family burn the trunk and leave, while Rose's ghost becomes a kindly carer for the dead children.

Critics found it pleasant but slight. Meagan Navarro of Bloody Disgusting called the stop-motion toys surprisingly charming and the film full of heart, though never scary, with a thin mythology and stilted script. Culture Crypt found it competently made but generic.

overview: England, 15th century. Hal, a capricious prince who lives among the populace far from court, is forced by circumstances to reluctantly accept the throne and become Henry V.
tagline: All hail
title: The King
plot:
The King (2019) is a historical drama film directed by David Michôd, based on the 2003 play of the same name by Jez Butterworth. The movie stars Timothée Chalamet as King Henry V of England.

The main themes of The King (2019) include:

1. **Identity and Coming-of-Age**: The film explores King Henry's journey from a young prince to a confident leader, grappling with his own identity, masculinity, and sense of purpose.
2. **War and its Consequences**: The movie delves into the psychological effects of war on individuals and society, highlighting the brutal realities of conflict and the moral dilemmas that come with it.
3. **Power Dynamics and Corruption**: As Henry ascends to the throne, he must navigate the complexities of power, loyalty, and corruption, which threaten to undermine his authority and relationships.
4. **Mental Health and Trauma**: The film touches on King Henry's struggles with mental health, particularly his experiences with anxiety, depression, and PTSD, which are exacerbated by the trauma of war.
5. **Loyalty and Betrayal**: The movie examines the intricate web of alliances and rivalries within the royal court, where loyalty is tested and betrayal can be both expected and devastating.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together to create a nuanced portrayal of King Henry's transformation from a young prince to a confident leader, grappling with the weight of his responsibilities and the consequences of his actions.

overview: Wanted by the mafia, a New York City bike messenger escapes into the world of parkour after meeting a beautiful stranger.
tagline: It's not a crime if they can't catch you.
title: Tracers
plot:
Tracers is a 2015 American action film directed by Daniel Benmayor, with a screenplay by Matt Johnson from a story by Johnson, T. J. Scott and Kevin Lund. It stars Taylor Lautner as Cam, a New York bike messenger, with Marie Avgeropoulos as Nikki, Adam Rayner as Miller and Rafi Gavron as Nikki's brother Dylan, alongside Christopher Jackson, Josh Yadon and Luciano Acuna Jr. as members of the crew. The film centers on the urban sport of parkour, which its characters use to carry out robberies.

Cam is a bike courier in New York City who is struggling to make ends meet and owes 15,000 dollars to a Chinatown gang, whose enforcers threaten him for missed payments. One day his bike is wrecked when a young woman, Nikki, crashes into him while fleeing the police. After she replaces the bike, Cam becomes fascinated by her parkour skills and tries to imitate them. He begins training and eventually earns an invitation to join Nikki's crew, a tight-knit group of free runners led by the charismatic Miller.

When the gang takes his late father's car and threatens his landlady Angie and her son, Cam joins the crew in its criminal work, using parkour to carry out thefts across the city, and quickly becomes one of its most valuable members. He also grows close to Nikki, though she has hidden the truth about her relationship with Miller. After a bank robbery goes wrong, one of the crew is killed and Cam is arrested, and Miller reveals that he is actually a corrupt federal agent. In exchange for his freedom, Cam must help Miller carry out one last dangerous heist, while trying to free himself from the gang and protect Nikki.

The film features extensive parkour sequences performed through the streets and rooftops of New York, and its young cast trained in the discipline for the action scenes.

Tracers was released on March 20, 2015. Reviews were generally negative, with 25 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 45; critics found the action sequences fun to watch but regarded the plot as typical B-movie material.

overview: Summertime on the coast of Maine, "In the Bedroom" centers on the inner dynamics of a family in transition. Matt Fowler is a doctor practicing in his native Maine and is married to New York born Ruth Fowler, a music teacher. His son is involved in a love affair with a local single mother. As the beauty of Maine's brief and fleeting summer comes to an end, these characters find themselves in the midst of unimaginable tragedy.
tagline: A young man. An older woman. Her ex-husband. Things are about to explode...
title: In the Bedroom
plot:
In the Bedroom is a poignant and introspective drama that explores the complexities of human relationships, grief, and the fragility of life. The film delves into the emotional aftermath of a tragic event that shatters the tranquility of a seemingly ordinary family.

At its core, In the Bedroom is a nuanced portrayal of the devastating consequences of violence and the ways in which it can disrupt even the most carefully constructed facades. The movie masterfully captures the intricate web of emotions that ensues when a traumatic event shakes the foundations of a family's existence.

Through the characters' struggles to cope with their loss, the film sheds light on the universal human experience of grappling with the impermanence of life and the inevitability of sorrow. The narrative is marked by a sense of quiet desperation, as the characters struggle to find meaning in a world that seems to have been turned upside down.

One of the most striking aspects of In the Bedroom is its thoughtful exploration of the human capacity for love, forgiveness, and resilience in the face of unimaginable pain. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that even in the darkest moments, there is always a glimmer of hope – a testament to the enduring power of the human spirit.

Ultimately, In the Bedroom is a powerful and moving film that invites viewers to confront the complexities of human emotion and the fragility of life itself.

overview: When twin brothers arrive home to find their mother’s demeanor altered and face covered in surgical bandages, they begin to suspect the woman beneath the gauze might not be their mother.
tagline: The darkest family secrets stay under wraps.
title: Goodnight Mommy
plot:
Goodnight Mommy is a 2014 Austrian psychological horror film directed by Veronika Franz and Severin Fiala. The movie was released in 2022, not 2022, but I assume you meant to ask about the original release.

The story revolves around 10-year-old Elias (played by Elias Schwarz), who lives with his mother, Eva (played by Susanne Wuest), in a remote Austrian village. After a severe head injury, Eva is left with significant cognitive and physical impairments, making her unable to care for herself or communicate effectively.

Elias's father, Martin (played by Michaela Mayer), returns home from work one evening, but when he arrives, he finds that his wife has been replaced by an identical duplicate of himself. The duplicate, who is also played by Susanne Wuest, seems to be perfectly normal and even more affectionate towards Elias than Eva was.

As the days pass, Elias becomes increasingly unsettled by the presence of the duplicate, which he believes is a threat to his mother's life. He begins to notice small inconsistencies in her behavior and starts to investigate the identity of the imposter. Meanwhile, Martin seems oblivious to the situation, leaving Elias to navigate this complex web of deception on his own.

The plot thickens as Elias becomes more convinced that the duplicate is not who she claims to be. He discovers a series of clues, including a hidden room in their home and a mysterious letter, which suggest that the duplicate may be an imposter sent by Martin himself.

As the tension builds, Elias's behavior becomes increasingly erratic, and his relationship with the duplicate deteriorates. The film's climax features a shocking twist: the duplicate is revealed to be Eva, who has been suffering from dementia and has created the duplicate as a coping mechanism to deal with her own mortality.

The ending is both haunting and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the themes of identity, motherhood, and the complexities of human relationships. The film's use of long takes, atmospheric sound design, and Wuest's chilling performance create a sense of unease that lingers long after the credits roll.

Overall, Goodnight Mommy is a masterclass in psychological horror, exploring the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of dementia on individuals and families.

overview: Born To Race is the story of Danny Krueger, a rebellious young street racer on a collision course with trouble. After an accident at an illegal street race, he is sent to a small town to live with his estranged father, a washed up NASCAR racer. When Danny decides to enter the NHRA High School Drags, he's forced to seek his father's help in taking down the local hot shot.
tagline: Only one can win it all.
title: Born to Race
plot:
Born to Be Wild is not a match for the title "Born to Race" released in 2008 but I found that "Born to Be Raced" was released in 2011 and it's an animated film. However, I also found another movie titled "Born to Race" released in 2011 by American Cinema International.

The main theme of Born to Race (2011) is the importance of family, perseverance, and following one's passion. The story revolves around a young racing driver named Tyler Evans, who dreams of becoming a professional racing driver despite his father's disapproval. Throughout the film, Tyler faces various challenges and setbacks, but with the support of his friends and family, he learns to believe in himself and pursue his dreams.

The movie also explores themes of loyalty, friendship, and the value of hard work and dedication. As Tyler navigates the world of professional racing, he must confront his own limitations and learn to overcome obstacles in order to achieve success.

Overall, Born to Race (2011) is a heartwarming and inspiring film that celebrates the power of determination and the importance of following one's passion.

overview: A diplomatic couple adopts the son of the devil without knowing it. A remake of the classic horror film of the same name from 1976.
tagline: A new generation of terror
title: The Omen
plot:
The Omen (2006) is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. At its core, the movie explores the theme of destiny versus free will, as the protagonist, Damien Thorn, is destined to fulfill an ancient prophecy that foretells his role in bringing about the apocalypse.

The film also examines the corrupting influence of power and the dangers of blind faith. As Damien's powers grow stronger, he becomes increasingly consumed by a desire for control and domination, highlighting the destructive potential of unchecked ambition. The movie suggests that when individuals prioritize their own interests over the greater good, they risk unleashing catastrophic consequences.

Furthermore, The Omen touches on the theme of family dynamics and the complexities of relationships. Damien's adoptive father, Robert Thorn, is a well-meaning but ultimately flawed character who struggles to connect with his son, while Damien's mother, Katherine, is a symbol of maternal love and devotion that is tragically twisted by her own desires.

Throughout the film, the director, John Moore, weaves together elements of horror, suspense, and drama to create a tense and unsettling atmosphere that keeps viewers on edge. The Omen ultimately presents a cautionary tale about the dangers of succumbing to one's darker impulses and the devastating consequences that can result when individuals prioritize their own desires over the well-being of others.

The movie also explores the idea of evil as a corrupting influence, how it can seep into even the most seemingly good people, and how it can be passed down through generations.

overview: In a suburban fantasy world, two teenage elf brothers embark on an extraordinary quest to discover if there is still a little magic left out there.
tagline: Their quest begineth.
title: Onward
plot:
Onward is a fantasy adventure film released in 2020 by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie takes place in a world where magic has disappeared, and elves are no longer present.

The story follows two elf brothers, Ian Lightfoot (Tom Holland) and Barley Lightfoot (Chris Pratt), who live in the suburban town of Willow Creek with their mother, Laurel (Octavia Spencer). On the day of their 16th birthday, which is also the last day of summer vacation, the boys discover that magic has disappeared from the world. According to an ancient law, magic can only be used by those who are born with a magical mark on their hands.

Ian, who was born without a mark, and Barley, who was born with a small mark, set out on a quest to find a way to restore magic to the world. They embark on a journey through the wilderness, facing various obstacles and creatures along the way. Along the way, they meet a group of magical creatures known as the Kragnir, who are being hunted by the forces of darkness.

As they journey deeper into the wilderness, Ian and Barley discover that their quest is not just about restoring magic to the world but also about coming to terms with their own identities and relationships. Ian struggles with his lack of magic, feeling like an outcast among his peers, while Barley tries to live up to his father's expectations as a great warrior.

The brothers eventually stumble upon a magical portal that leads them to a mystical realm known as the "Fae Realm." There, they meet a group of magical creatures who possess ancient knowledge and magic. The Fae Realm is ruled by a powerful sorceress named Maud (Julie Andrews), who possesses incredible magical abilities.

As Ian and Barley navigate the Fae Realm, they discover that their quest to restore magic is not just about restoring power but also about understanding the true nature of magic and its connection to the world. Along the way, they encounter various challenges and obstacles, including a group of dark creatures known as the "Kragnir" who seek to destroy the Fae Realm.

In the end, Ian and Barley successfully restore magic to the world by using their own unique abilities and understanding the true nature of magic. The movie concludes with the brothers returning home, where they are welcomed back by their mother and community. The film ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in a world without magic, there is still room for love, friendship, and adventure.

Overall, Onward is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, family, and the power of imagination. With its stunning animation and lovable characters, it's a must-see for fans of fantasy adventures.

overview: This rock opera tells the story of one year in the life of a group of bohemians struggling in late 1980s East Village, New York, USA. The film centers around Mark and Roger, two roommates. While a  tragedy has made Roger numb to new experiences, Mark begins capturing their world through his attempts to make a personal movie. In the year that follows, they and their friends deal with love, loss, and working together.
tagline: No day but today.
title: Rent
plot:
Rent (2005) is a poignant and powerful film that explores the lives of artists struggling with love, loss, and the pursuit of one's passion in the face of adversity.

At its core, Rent is a story about the human experience, delving into themes of community, found family, and the power of art to transcend suffering. The characters, all living with HIV/AIDS in 1980s New York City, form a tight-knit circle that supports each other through the ups and downs of life.

The film also grapples with the harsh realities of poverty, addiction, and the struggle for survival in a city that seems determined to crush its inhabitants. Yet, amidst the darkness, Rent shines a light on the resilience of the human spirit, highlighting the ways in which art can be both a source of comfort and a means of resistance.

One of the most striking aspects of Rent is its exploration of love and relationships. The characters' experiences with romance, heartbreak, and loss are deeply nuanced and relatable, making it easy to become invested in their stories. Through the lens of these complex relationships, the film sheds light on the ways in which we find meaning and connection in our lives.

Ultimately, Rent is a powerful tribute to the artists and activists who fought for justice and equality during this tumultuous period in American history. The film's message of hope, acceptance, and the transformative power of art continues to resonate with audiences today, making it a timeless classic that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: All unemployed, Ki-taek's family takes peculiar interest in the wealthy and glamorous Parks for their livelihood until they get entangled in an unexpected incident.
tagline: Act like you own the place.
title: Parasite
plot:
Parasite is a 2019 South Korean black comedy thriller film written and directed by Bong Joon-ho. The film follows the story of the Kims, a poor family living in a cramped semi-basement apartment in Seoul.

The Kims consist of father Ki-taek (Choi Woo-shik), mother Chung-sook (Cho Yeo-jeong), son Ki-woo (Chang Hyae-in), and daughter Ki-jung (Park So-dam). They struggle to make ends meet, with the family's only source of income being a part-time job at a local convenience store. The family is forced to live in a small, dingy apartment with no natural light.

One day, Ki-woo sees an ad for an English tutor position at a wealthy family's house and decides to apply. He poses as a university student and lands the job, introducing himself as "Sun-gi." Ki-woo soon befriends the family, including the two children, Da-hye (Park So-dam) and Da-song (Lee Jung-eun), who are initially wary of him but eventually warm up.

As Ki-woo spends more time with the wealthy family, he discovers that they have a live-in housekeeper, Moon-gwang (Lee Jung-eun), who is also struggling to make ends meet. He decides to recruit his sister Ki-jung as a replacement for Moon-gwang, and she takes on the role.

The Kims soon find themselves immersed in the lives of their wealthy employers, the Parks. The family's fortunes change when they are hired as housekeepers and groundskeepers for the Parks' luxurious mansion. As they navigate their new roles, the Kims begin to exploit the Parks' generosity, with Ki-woo posing as a university student and his sister taking on the role of a tutor.

However, as the Kims become more entrenched in the Parks' lives, they begin to uncover dark secrets about their employers. The family's facade begins to crumble, and tensions rise as they struggle to maintain their deception.

As the story unfolds, Bong Joon-ho masterfully weaves together themes of class struggle, social inequality, and the exploitation of the underclass by the wealthy elite. Through the Kims' experiences, he highlights the absurdity and cruelty of a system that perpetuates poverty and oppression.

In the film's climax, the Kims' deception is exposed, and they are forced to confront the consequences of their actions. The Parks, who have grown increasingly suspicious of the Kims, turn on them, leading to a violent confrontation.

Ultimately, the film ends with the Kims being forced out of their luxurious mansion and back into poverty. However, in a surprising twist, Ki-taek is able to find work as a chef at a high-end restaurant, suggesting that even in the darkest of times, there is always hope for redemption and a chance to start anew.

Parasite is a masterful film that combines elements of comedy, drama, and social commentary to create a thought-provoking and unforgettable viewing experience.

overview: A tech worker with agoraphobia discovers recorded evidence of a violent crime but is met with resistance when she tries to report it. Seeking justice, she must do the thing she fears the most: she must leave her apartment.
tagline: She's not the only one listening.
title: Kimi
plot:
Kimi is a 2022 American thriller film directed by Steven Soderbergh and written by David Koepp. The movie stars Zoë Kravitz as Richard, a young woman who sets out to find her missing father, John (played by J.K. Simmons), after his disappearance in the Pacific Ocean.

The story begins with Richard's life unraveling. She is struggling to cope with the loss of her mother and feeling disconnected from her father, who she barely knows. When her father goes missing while on a solo sailing trip, Richard sets out to find him, despite her initial reluctance.

As Richard searches for her father, she becomes increasingly obsessed with finding him. She tracks his last known location to a small island in the Pacific, where she hopes to find some clues about his disappearance. Along the way, she encounters various characters who provide her with information and guidance, including a local fisherman (played by Ed Harris) and a mysterious woman (played by Kaitlyn Dever).

As Richard delves deeper into her father's disappearance, she uncovers a complex web of secrets and lies that lead her to question everything she thought she knew about him. Through a series of flashbacks, we see glimpses of Richard's childhood and her relationship with her father, which suggests that he may have been hiding something from her.

As the story unfolds, Richard becomes more and more entangled in a cat-and-mouse game with an unknown adversary who seems to be one step ahead of her. The tension builds as she navigates the treacherous waters of the Pacific, facing numerous challenges and obstacles along the way.

Throughout the film, Soderbergh employs his signature style of non-linear storytelling, jumping back and forth in time to reveal clues about Richard's father's disappearance. The pacing is deliberate and measured, building tension and suspense as the story hurtles towards its climax.

Ultimately, Richard discovers a shocking truth about her father's disappearance that challenges everything she thought she knew about him. In a thrilling finale, she confronts the unknown adversary in a tense showdown that will leave viewers on the edge of their seats.

Overall, Kimi is a gripping thriller that explores themes of family, identity, and obsession. With its complex characters, intricate plot, and stunning cinematography, it's a must-see for fans of suspenseful storytelling.

overview: When Rango, a lost family pet, accidentally winds up in the gritty, gun-slinging town of Dirt, the less-than-courageous lizard suddenly finds he stands out. Welcomed as the last hope the town has been waiting for, new Sheriff Rango is forced to play his new role to the hilt.
tagline: Heroes come in all different colors.
title: Rango
plot:
Rango is a 2011 American animated Western comedy film directed by Gore Verbinski and produced by Paramount Pictures. The movie takes place in the fictional town of Dirt, Arizona, where a pet chameleon named Rango lives.

The story begins with Rango, who has been living in his terrarium for most of his life. He is bored and longs for adventure. One day, he gets swept away by a strong storm and ends up in the middle of the desert. After being rescued by a group of animals, including a tortoise named Roadkill, Rango finds himself in the town of Dirt.

Initially, Rango tries to blend in with the townspeople, but his chameleon abilities make it difficult for him to hide his true nature. He is mistaken for a human and becomes embroiled in the town's politics when he discovers that the town is plagued by a severe drought and a mysterious illness affecting its residents.

As Rango navigates this new world, he meets a cast of colorful characters, including Beans, a tough-talking armadillo who becomes his friend; Rattlesnake Jake, a villainous snake who serves as the town's sheriff; and Squidward, a grumpy but lovable squid who runs the local saloon.

Rango soon discovers that he has a crucial role to play in saving the town. He learns about the town's history and its connection to an ancient Native American tribe. With the help of his new friends, Rango sets out on a quest to find the source of the drought and the mysterious illness.

Along the way, Rango faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous terrain, ferocious predators, and even a rival chameleon who seeks to take over the town. Through his journey, Rango learns valuable lessons about courage, friendship, and leadership.

As the story unfolds, Rango discovers that he is the reincarnation of a legendary Native American warrior named "The Spirit of the West." With this newfound knowledge, Rango must come to terms with his destiny and lead the townspeople in a final showdown against Rattlesnake Jake and his cohorts.

In the end, Rango emerges victorious, saving the town from destruction and restoring balance to its ecosystem. The movie concludes with Rango returning to his terrarium, but this time, he is no longer content to simply live a mundane life. He has found a new sense of purpose and belonging in the world outside his terrarium.

Throughout the film, Gore Verbinski's direction brings the desert landscape to life, creating a visually stunning and immersive experience for audiences. The voice cast, including Johnny Depp as Rango, Isla Fisher as Beans, and Abigail Breslin as Rattlesnake Jake, delivers memorable performances that bring depth and humor to the characters.

Overall, Rango is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, community, and redemption. With its unique blend of humor, action, and adventure, it has become a beloved classic among animation fans worldwide.

overview: When aspiring knight Gareth goes in search of a fallen comet rumored to contain gold, he is shocked to instead find the dragon Drago. After Drago saves Gareth's life the two become intricately bonded, and must work together to defeat an evil sorcerer and stop his reign of terror. Along the way, Gareth learns the true meaning of being a knight in this fantasy action-adventure for the ages.
title: Dragonheart 3: The Sorcerer's Curse
plot:
Dragonheart 3: The Sorcerer's Curse is a 2015 fantasy adventure film directed by Colin Teague and released direct-to-video by Universal. The third installment of the Dragonheart franchise and a prequel to the 1996 original, it stars Julian Morris as a young squire, Tamzin Merchant, Jassa Ahluwalia and Jonjo O'Neill, with Ben Kingsley voicing the dragon Drago.

In 9th-century northern Britain, a circle of druids foresees a falling star from the constellation Draco. One of them, Brude, summons a Pict clan known as the Painted tribe to slaughter the others and lead the northern clans to war against the southern kingdoms beyond Hadrian's Wall. Only a druid apprentice, Lorne, escapes. On the southern side of the wall, the squire Gareth completes his final tests to be knighted. He is the best fighter among the candidates but fails to collect enough taxes from the peasants, and his superior, Sir Horsa, refuses to knight him unless he pays a hundred crowns.

When a meteor falls north of the wall, Gareth goes in search of the riches it is said to contain, and instead finds a dragon emerging from it with a clutch of eggs. Gareth saves one of the eggs during a fight with the Painted tribe but is gravely wounded, and the dragon, moved by his mercy, shares its heart with him, binding them together. Brude places a curse on the dragon and seizes the eggs. Gareth names the dragon Drago and joins Lorne and Rhonu, a rebel leader of the clans opposing Brude, in an effort to rescue the eggs. Brude's Sorcerer's Curse threatens to place him under the sorcerer's control by the full moon.

The companions recover the eggs and head for the wall, where Gareth confesses to Drago that he is not truly a knight. They are arrested, and the eggs are seized by Horsa to be sold, as the Painted tribe and the enslaved Drago attack. Gareth's courage frees the dragon, who helps the defenders and the northern clans repel the attack. Gareth kills Horsa and Rhonu kills Brude, though she is fatally wounded until an unhatched dragon shares its heart with her. Gareth is knighted and becomes the settlement's leader, and the wall is renamed the Dragon's Gate as peace is established between north and south.

The film received mixed but generally positive reviews, with critics noting its impressive effects for a direct-to-video production and considering it an improvement over Dragonheart: A New Beginning. It earned over $2 million in domestic home video sales.

overview: A cooler-than-ever Bruce Wayne must deal with the usual suspects as they plan to rule Gotham City, while discovering that he has accidentally adopted a teenage orphan who wishes to become his sidekick.
tagline: Always be yourself. Unless you can be Batman.
title: The Lego Batman Movie
plot:
The Lego Batman Movie is a 2017 animated superhero comedy film directed by Chris McKay and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, DC Entertainment, and LEGO Films.

In a world made entirely of LEGO bricks, Batman (voiced by Will Arnett) is the self-proclaimed protector of Gotham City. He is obsessed with being seen as a hero and has become isolated from his friends and allies, including Robin (voiced by Michael Cera), Alfred Pennyworth (voiced by Ralph Fiennes), and Commissioner Gordon (voiced by Rosario Dawson).

The movie begins with Batman receiving a distress call from the Mayor of Gotham City, who is being held hostage by the Joker (voiced by Zach Galifianakis). However, when Batman arrives to rescue him, he finds that the Joker has escaped and left behind a trail of clues leading to the location of the Dark Knight's greatest fear: his own inadequacy.

As Batman delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the Joker is planning to destroy Gotham City by using an army of robotic duplicates of himself. The Joker's plan is to prove that he is the superior villain and that Batman is just a foolish mortal who can't stop him.

Meanwhile, a new villain emerges in the form of the Tumbler (voiced by Jake Johnson), a rogue LEGO minifigure who becomes Batman's arch-nemesis. The Tumbler is determined to take down Batman and prove himself as the greatest hero in Gotham City.

As the story unfolds, Batman must confront his own ego and learn to work with others to save the city. Along the way, he teams up with Robin, Batgirl (voiced by Hailee Steinfeld), and other allies to stop the Joker's plan and defeat the Tumbler.

Throughout the movie, there are numerous humorous references to Batman's iconic comics and movies, as well as pop culture icons like Spider-Man and Superman. The film also features a range of colorful characters, including the villainous Harley Quinn (voiced by Jenny Slate) and the wise-cracking Alfred Pennyworth.

In the end, Batman must face his greatest fear head-on and learn to trust himself and others in order to save Gotham City from destruction. The movie ends with a heartwarming moment between Batman and Robin, as well as a hilarious cameo appearance by Superman (voiced by Patrick Wilson).

Overall, The Lego Batman Movie is a hilarious and action-packed animated film that pokes fun at the superhero genre while still delivering plenty of excitement and adventure. With its witty humor, colorful characters, and clever references to comic book lore, it's a must-see for fans of Batman and superheroes in general.

overview: A 14th century Crusader returns with his comrade to a homeland devastated by the Black Plague. The Church commands the two knights to transport a witch to a remote abbey, where monks will perform a ritual in hopes of ending the pestilence.
tagline: Not all souls can be saved.
title: Season of the Witch
plot:
Season of the Witch is a 2011 American supernatural action-adventure film directed by Dominic Sena and written by Bragi Schut, starring Nicolas Cage and Ron Perlman, with Claire Foy, Stephen Campbell Moore and Christopher Lee. It reunited Sena and Cage after Gone in 60 Seconds. Schut's spec script was purchased in 2000 and passed between several studios before being produced by Relativity Media, with filming mainly in Austria, Hungary and Croatia.

In 13th-century Villach, a priest condemns three women as witches; after their execution, one of them rises in demonic form and kills him. A century later, the Teutonic Knights Behmen von Bleibruck and Felson fight for years in the Crusades, until Behmen is horrified to find he has killed women and children during the capture of Smyrna. The two friends desert and return to Europe, which has been ravaged by the Black Death. In Styria, Behmen's crest exposes them as deserters, and they are brought before the dying Cardinal D'Ambroise, who asks them to escort a young woman accused of causing the plague through witchcraft to a remote monastery, where monks can perform a ritual to destroy her power.

The knights agree on condition that the girl, Anna, receives a fair trial and that the charges against them are dropped. They are joined by the priest Debelzaq, the knight Johann, the young altar boy Kay and Hagamar, a swindler serving as guide. The journey is plagued by strange events. Johann is killed after Anna escapes and he is lured by visions of his dead daughter, Anna rescues Kay with unnatural strength on a crumbling bridge, and wolves seem to answer her call and kill Hagamar.

At the monastery, they find that all the monks have died of the plague. As Debelzaq reads the ritual against witches from the Book of Solomon, Anna speaks in a demonic voice of Behmen's past, and they realize that she is not a witch but is possessed by a demon seeking to destroy the book. The demon escapes, raises the dead monks against the men and kills Debelzaq and Felson. Behmen is mortally wounded fighting it while Kay completes the exorcism, freeing Anna. Behmen asks Kay to protect her, and after burying their friends, Kay and Anna leave together with the book.

Released on January 7, 2011, the film was panned by critics, who found it ponderous and silly, though some enjoyed it as B-movie schlock. Cage received a Golden Raspberry Award nomination for Worst Actor.

overview: Battle-scarred and disillusioned by the war, Corporal Chris Merrimette is put in charge of a unit whose next mission is to resupply a remote outpost on the edge of Taliban-controlled territory. While driving through the hostile Helmand province, a Navy SEAL flags down their convoy and enlists the unit on an operation of international importance: they must help an Afghan woman famous for her defiance of the Taliban escape the country. Without tanks or air support, Merrimette and his team will need all the courage and firepower they can muster to fight their way across the war-torn country and shepherd the woman to safety.
tagline: Find the courage, fight together.
title: Jarhead 2: Field of Fire
plot:
Jarhead 2: Field of Fire is a 2014 American direct-to-video war film directed by Don Michael Paul from a screenplay by Berkeley Anderson and Ellis Black. Although it borrows its title from Sam Mendes's Jarhead (2005), it is a sequel in name only, with an unrelated story and characters set during the war in Afghanistan. Josh Kelly stars as Corporal Chris Merrimette, with Cole Hauser as Navy SEAL Fox and Stephen Lang, Esai Morales, Bokeem Woodbine and Danielle Savre in supporting roles.

Merrimette, a Marine who has grown battle-scarred and disillusioned with the war, is given command of a tight-knit unit for the first time. Their assignment seems routine for a supply detachment: drive a convoy through some of the most dangerous Taliban-held territory in Helmand province to resupply a remote outpost at the edge of enemy-controlled ground. On the way, however, they are flagged down by Fox, a special operations officer who tells them their mission has changed. He is escorting Anoosh, an Afghan woman who has become famous for defying the Taliban and a symbol of resistance to them, and she must be brought to safety so she can deliver a speech at the United Nations.

The operation quickly turns into a fight for survival. Taliban forces ambush the Marines, inflicting casualties and leaving them no way back to the Green Zone except on foot, and the survivors must cross hostile country with no communication and no air support, and with only Fox's experience of the land and its people to guide them. Merrimette, whose experience until now has been limited to supply runs, must hold his unit together and protect Anoosh as they fight their way through one of the most dangerous places on Earth, while tensions flare between some of the Marines and their local allies and interpreters before giving way to mutual respect. As the Taliban close in, the Marines must rely on their courage and firepower to see Anoosh to safety, at heavy cost.

Released on home video and digital platforms in 2014, the film was followed by Jarhead 3: The Siege (2016) and Jarhead: Law of Return (2019). Common Sense Media judged it a better-than-expected war movie that conveys the Marines' esprit de corps and does not shy away from casualties, despite a formulaic story, while DVD Talk called it markedly average in concept, performances and script.

overview: A look behind the scenes at Bernie Madoff's massive Ponzi scheme, how it was perpetrated on the public and the trail of destruction it left in its wake, both for the victims and Madoff's family.
tagline: Only those you trust can truly betray you.
title: The Wizard of Lies
plot:
The Wizard of Lies is a 2017 American television biographical film directed by Barry Levinson and written by Sam Levinson, Sam Baum and John Burnham Schwartz, based on Diana B. Henriques's 2011 non-fiction book of the same name. It stars Robert De Niro as the financier and fraudster Bernie Madoff, Michelle Pfeiffer as his wife Ruth and Alessandro Nivola as their older son Mark, with Nathan Darrow as Andrew Madoff, Hank Azaria as Frank DiPascali and Kristen Connolly.

Bernie Madoff founded his firm on Wall Street in the early 1960s and built it into one of the largest investment operations in the world, earning a reputation as a successful and influential financier and a generous philanthropist. His sons Mark and Andrew work at the firm, and his wife Ruth is involved in the family's affairs. In 2008, it is revealed that Madoff's investment advisory business has for years been operating the largest Ponzi scheme in history, paying returns to existing investors with money from new ones.

The film moves back and forth in time, showing how Madoff evaded scrutiny, including an episode in which regulators could have exposed the fraud with a single phone call that was never made. When the 2008 financial crisis triggers a flood of withdrawal requests, Madoff realizes that the scheme can no longer be sustained and confesses to his family, and his sons turn him in to the authorities. Madoff is arrested and sentenced to 150 years in prison. The film then follows the devastating consequences for his family, as the Madoffs are shunned and sued, and his relationships with his wife and sons collapse amid tragedy.

The film portrays Madoff as a man unable to accept responsibility for the ruin he caused, ending with him asking a journalist whether she thinks he is a sociopath.

The Wizard of Lies premiered on HBO on May 20, 2017. It marked the fourth film pairing De Niro and Pfeiffer. Reviews were favorable, with 73 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised its solid direction and talented cast, and a Metacritic score of 67.

overview: Lion vs The Little People is a documentary comedy about the greatest internet hoax of all time. In 2005, a hoax news post masquerading as a bonafide BBC news website article, announced a fight had taken place between a lion and an army of 42 fighting dwarfs. The hoax spread like wild fire across the internet before eventually being accepted to be fake. While the article’s veracity has been diminished, the myth lives on in this outrageous deadpan comedy.
tagline: The Greatest Fight Never Seen
title: Lion vs The Little People
plot:
Lion vs The Little People is a 2022 British mockumentary comedy written and directed by Raphael Warner. Presented in the style of a true-crime documentary, it invents an elaborate backstory for a real internet hoax: a 2005 post disguised as a BBC News article which claimed that a lion had fought an army of 42 dwarfs, a story that spread widely online before being accepted as fake. The cast includes Leigh Gill, George Appleby, Linda Thorson, Paul Rider, Mark Arnold, Corey Johnson and Nadia Albina, with Rupert Degas as the narrator.

The film follows a documentary maker as he pieces together the supposed truth behind the myth. His investigation leads to Larry Vincent Ross, a wealthy cardboard magnate with political connections, glimpsed in doctored photographs with Bill Clinton and in television commercials for his short-lived chain of martial arts dojos. Ross turns his fortune toward sports betting and, in partnership with a Chinese gangster linked to senior Communist Party figures, sets up an underground fight circuit in Macau in which people with dwarfism battle one another. As the contests grow more popular the organisers escalate them, setting the fighters against animals. Deciding to cash out with one spectacular final event, they lure working actors with dwarfism from Hollywood, recruited through an unwitting casting director, Gayle Bennet, into a battle royale against a lion. Two survivors of the fight recount their experiences, while a police investigation, botched and then covered up by Interpol, comes to nothing. The film is framed by statements about the way little people are portrayed in the media, and its closing titles reveal that the story is fictional.

Thorson plays Bennet, Rider plays Ross and Gill appears as the survivor Thomas Rasndall, while Johnson plays Detective Rioni. David Boynes was production designer and an executive producer. Production began at the end of 2020 and took nearly two years. The film was promoted as the smallest and shortest theatrical release in British cinema history, a single London screening with a limited number of seats, before being released on video on demand in December 2022.

Reviews were divided. Unseen Films called it a brilliant faux documentary with pointed things to say about exploitation, wealth and the internet, but felt that out-of-place jokes undercut its tone, while J.B. Spins found its well-intentioned message at odds with an exploitative premise and did not recommend it.

overview: As a top student at St. Adeline's Catholic Boarding School, Zoe senses that something is not quite right about the school's new nun-- a sense proven to be true when it is revealed the "good' nun is an imposter with a fatal attraction to Zoe's brother.
tagline: How long has it been since your last confession?
title: Bad Sister
plot:
Bad Sister is a 2015 American-Canadian thriller television film written and directed by Doug Campbell for Lifetime, produced with Johnson Production Group and Golden Oak Entertainment. It stars Alyshia Ochse as a woman posing as a nun, with Devon Werkheiser, Ryan Whitney Newman, Helen Eigenberg, Robert Leeshock, Lise Simms, Sloane Avery and James Handy. Although dated 2015, it premiered on Lifetime on 3 January 2016.

Jason Brady (Werkheiser), a teenager who posts videos of his songs online, is sent by his parents to a Catholic boarding school after wrecking his father's car; they disapprove of his musical ambitions. His studious sister Zoe (Newman) attends the same school. The new teacher, Sister Sophia (Ochse), is welcomed by the headmistress, Sister Rebecca (Eigenberg), but Zoe soon notices that she skips the morning prayer and knows little about the faith. In truth she is Laura, a disturbed woman who became obsessed with Jason through his videos, murdered the real Sister Sophia and took her identity. Under her habit she wears lingerie and makeup; she moves Jason's girlfriend Sara (Avery) away from him in class, threatens her, and lets the boy glimpse her undressing. She plants a joint that gets Sara suspended and hides whiskey in Jason's room so that he must stay at school over a weekend, seduces him and secretly films them together, then frames Zoe for cheating when the girl grows suspicious. After Sara returns, Laura kills her in the shower and stages it as an accident. At a family dinner, Zoe catches the "nun" in lie after lie, and Jason confesses the affair and the sex tape she is using against him. The siblings search her computer, discover her real name and seek out Sister Rebecca, only to find her knocked unconscious. Laura confronts them in the chapel, but Sister Rebecca intervenes and Jason stabs the impostor with a screwdriver.

Reviewers who cover Lifetime films responded warmly to its excesses. Lisa Marie Bowman of Through the Shattered Lens called it an over-the-top masterpiece of the network's style, praising Campbell for playing up the sordid melodrama without taking it too seriously and singling out Ochse's switches between the cheerful nun and the irritated Laura. Lifetime Uncorked gave it a rating of three knives, though it found the casting of a genuinely teenage-looking actor as Jason somewhat creepy.

overview: Alex, an immigrant from Ukraine comes to Canada and becomes involved with an online criminal organization called Darkweb. What starts off as a way to help his parents financially, soon becomes a personal vendetta against the entire banking system, when his mother is fired from her job at the bank
tagline: He will find you. He will become you.
title: Hacker
plot:
Hacker, released theatrically in the United States as Anonymous, is a 2016 crime thriller directed by Akan Satayev and written by Timur Zhaxylykov and Sanzhar Sultan. It stars Callan McAuliffe as Alex, a young hacker, with Lorraine Nicholson as Kira, Daniel Eric Gold as Sye and Clifton Collins Jr. as Zed. Loosely based on real events, the story follows a group of young cybercriminals whose activities take them from Toronto to Hong Kong, New York and Bangkok.

Alex is the son of a struggling immigrant family in Canada that lives on welfare. A lonely child, he spends his time online and begins earning money by generating web traffic. After moving to Toronto to attend college, he turns to identity theft and credit card fraud with Sye, a streetwise hustler who introduces him to the black market. When Alex is caught trying to defraud the bank that fired his mother, he talks his way out of trouble by offering to fix its security flaws, and the episode earns him admiration on the dark web and the attention of Zed, a mysterious figure at its center.

Alex meets Kira, a skilled young hacker who shows him and Sye new ways to make money, including printing their own credit cards and using Bitcoin. Tension grows between Sye and Kira, and after a deal goes wrong the group relocates to Hong Kong, where Alex and Kira withdraw millions of dollars from cash machines. Their success attracts Zed, who recruits them for a dangerous mission and makes clear that failure will cost them and their families their lives. As old enemies catch up with them and the stakes rise, Alex is drawn into a much larger scheme than he imagined.

The film depicts the world of online fraud and the dark web, focusing on a young man seduced by easy money and the thrill of hacking.

The film had a limited release in the United States under the title Anonymous on December 2, 2016, after which Sony Pictures released it on home video. The screenplay was produced in association with Brillstein Entertainment Partners.

overview: Failed architect, engineer and vicious murderer Jack narrates the details of some of his most elaborately orchestrated crimes, each of them a towering piece of art that defines his life's work as a serial killer for twelve years.
title: The House That Jack Built
plot:
The House That Jack Built is a 2018 Danish black comedy film written and directed by Lars von Trier. The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, consisting of six chapters that explore the life of Jack (played by Matt Dillon), a serial killer who documents his crimes through voiceovers.

Throughout the film, several themes emerge:

1. **The Nature of Evil**: The House That Jack Built explores the concept of evil and whether it's inherent or learned. Jack's character is complex, and his actions are both disturbing and fascinating. The film raises questions about the origins of evil and whether individuals can be born with a predisposition to violence.

2. **Mortality and the Human Condition**: The film grapples with mortality, as each chapter focuses on a different victim and explores their final moments before Jack's brutal killing. This theme is intertwined with the human condition, highlighting the fragility of life and the inevitability of death.

3. **The Objectification of Women**: The House That Jack Built critiques the way women are often objectified in society. Jack's victims are frequently portrayed as sex objects or mere commodities, which serves to underscore his twisted worldview.

4. **The Power Dynamics of Relationships**: The film examines the power dynamics between men and women, particularly in relationships where one partner holds more control than the other. This theme is reflected in Jack's interactions with his victims and his own relationships throughout the narrative.

5. **The Blurred Lines Between Reality and Fantasy**: As the story unfolds, it becomes increasingly difficult to distinguish between reality and fantasy. The film's non-linear structure and Jack's voiceovers contribute to this ambiguity, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is part of Jack's twisted imagination.

6. **The Dark Side of Human Nature**: Ultimately, The House That Jack Built presents a bleak portrayal of human nature, highlighting the darker aspects of our existence. The film serves as a commentary on the darkness that can lurk within individuals and society as a whole.

It's worth noting that Lars von Trier's intention with this film was to spark controversy and challenge societal norms, rather than to provide a straightforward or sympathetic portrayal of Jack's character.

overview: A vengeful spirit has taken the form of the Tooth Fairy to exact vengeance on the town that lynched her 150 years earlier. Her only opposition is the only child, now grown up, who has survived her before.
tagline: Evil rises.
title: Darkness Falls
plot:
Darkness Falls is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of unchecked anger and resentment. The movie follows a young boy, Josh, who is haunted by his father's dark past and the malevolent spirit that has been awakened.

At its core, Darkness Falls explores the theme of the cyclical nature of violence and trauma. The film suggests that when we fail to confront and resolve our inner demons, they can consume us and ultimately lead to destruction. Josh's father, a former logger with a troubled past, is driven by a deep-seated anger and resentment towards those who have wronged him, which ultimately leads to his downfall.

The movie also touches on the idea of the long-term effects of childhood trauma and the ways in which it can shape our adult lives. Josh's experiences as a child are deeply ingrained, and he struggles to form healthy relationships or find closure as an adult. The film implies that unless we confront and heal from these wounds, they will continue to haunt us.

Furthermore, Darkness Falls explores the theme of redemption and the possibility of breaking free from the cycle of violence and trauma. Josh's journey is one of self-discovery and growth, as he grapples with his family's dark past and seeks to find a way to heal and move forward.

Overall, Darkness Falls is a haunting and atmospheric film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of trauma, violence, and redemption in a way that is both thought-provoking and unsettling.

overview: Nick Hume is a mild-mannered executive with a perfect life, until one gruesome night he witnesses something that changes him forever. Transformed by grief, Hume eventually comes to the disturbing conclusion that no length is too great when protecting his family.
tagline: Protect what's yours.
title: Death Sentence
plot:
Death Sentence is a 2007 American action thriller film directed by Peter Howitt and starring Kevin Costner, Lynn Collins, and John Gielgud. The movie follows the story of Nick Halsey (played by Kevin Costner), a widowed father who seeks revenge against the men responsible for his son's death.

The film begins with Nick Halsey, a former Army Ranger, living in rural Ohio with his wife, Laura (Lynn Collins), and their teenage son, Steve (Forest Whitaker). The family is struggling to cope with the loss of their daughter, who died in a car accident several years ago. Nick's life is marked by grief and anger, which he tries to keep under control.

However, when a group of thugs, led by a man named Victor Vex (John Malkovich), break into his home and kill Steve, Nick's world is shattered once again. The men are revealed to be the same gang that had been terrorizing the neighborhood for months, and they have been targeting families with young sons.

Nick becomes consumed by a desire for revenge against Victor and his gang. He begins to track them down, using his military skills to gather intelligence and plan his attacks. As he delves deeper into the world of organized crime, Nick's obsession with revenge grows, causing him to lose sight of what is truly important in life.
