The story is set in the Arizona Territory in the 1870s. Introduced by his own narration as he rides through the desert, Marshal Wilcox has captured the outlaw George Rivers and is escorting him to the frontier town of Crumpit to face justice, fighting off a gang of bandits along the way. In Crumpit, however, an innocent man condemned to hang has placed a curse on the town, and the dead begin rising from their graves with a hunger for living flesh. On the trail Wilcox meets Sergeant Bale, a Buffalo Soldier of the U.S. Army, and the travelers rescue and befriend an Apache who joins them. Meanwhile, in town, a small group of survivors, among them a pair of young people, an elderly preacher and Jasper, a barman of short stature, barricade themselves inside the saloon while the undead roam the streets outside and plan their escape. When the marshal's party reaches Crumpit and discovers that it too has been overrun, they join forces with the survivors, and the lawman, the soldier, the Apache and the outlaw prisoner must learn to survive together as they try to fight their way to freedom, with a siege in the saloon and a railway handcar among the film's set pieces.

The film was released on DVD in the United Kingdom by Left Films in August 2016 and in the United States by Wild Eye Releasing, and reviews were negative. Joel Harley of Horror DNA called it dull and bland, criticizing its sets, unconvincing actors, unimaginative story and some of the cheapest zombies seen in a no-budget horror film, though he credited it with more ambition than it might have had in letting its characters travel beyond the town. Daniel Goodwin of Scream magazine faulted its amateur acting, cut-rate effects and dithering narrative, while Horror Society, rating it two out of five, found most of the cast convincing but judged Winters unpersuasive as the marshal and the story thin and unexplained.

overview: Go behind the scenes and see how the creators of "Dark" used groundbreaking virtual technology "The Volume" to shoot their new mystery series.
title: Making 1899
plot: Go behind the scenes and see how the creators of "Dark" used groundbreaking virtual technology "The Volume" to shoot their new mystery series.

overview: A lowly pencil pusher working for MI7, Johnny English is suddenly promoted to super spy after Agent One is assassinated and every other agent is blown up at his funeral. When a billionaire entrepreneur sponsors the exhibition of the Crown Jewels—and the valuable gems disappear on the opening night and on English's watch—the newly-designated agent must jump into action to find the thief and recover the missing gems.
tagline: He knows no fear. He knows no danger. He knows nothing.
title: Johnny English
plot:
Johnny English is a 2003 spy comedy film directed by Rob Sitch and starring Rowan Atkinson as the titular character. The movie follows the story of Johnny English, a bumbling but lovable British secret agent working for MI7, the British intelligence agency.

The film begins with Johnny English (Rowan Atkinson) being introduced to his new boss, Pemberley (John Malkovich), who is impressed by Johnny's skills and assigns him to stop a plot by the villainous Vesper Lynd (Natalie Imbruglia). However, things quickly go awry as Johnny discovers that he has been replaced by a more competent agent, Johnny English Jr. (Ben Miller).

Despite his initial setbacks, Johnny English perseveres and sets out to stop Vesper's plan, which involves stealing the world's most expensive diamond, the "Regent Diamond." Along the way, he encounters a beautiful and intelligent woman named Natalie (Natalie Imbruglia), who becomes his love interest.

As Johnny English navigates through various obstacles and mishaps, he must also contend with his own ineptitude and the skepticism of his colleagues. However, with the help of his trusty sidekick, Bough (Simon Pegg), and a series of hilarious gadgets and disguises, Johnny is able to stay one step ahead of Vesper's henchmen.

Throughout the film, Rowan Atkinson's physical comedy and timing are on full display as he brings Johnny English to life. The movie's humor is clever and witty, with plenty of references to James Bond and other spy movies.

In the end, Johnny English successfully foils Vesper's plan and saves the Regent Diamond. Along the way, he also wins over Natalie's heart and proves himself to be a worthy secret agent in his own right.

Overall, Johnny English is a hilarious and entertaining film that showcases Rowan Atkinson's unique brand of comedy. With its clever plot, witty humor, and plenty of physical comedy, it's no wonder that the movie became a box office hit and spawned two sequels.

overview: At an international school in Jakarta, a philosophy teacher challenges his class of twenty graduating seniors to choose which ten of them would take shelter underground and reboot the human race in the event of a nuclear apocalypse.
tagline: Smart. Talented. Beautiful. Stranded.
title: After the Dark
plot:
After the Dark, released outside the United States as The Philosophers, is a science fiction psychological thriller written and directed by John Huddles. James D'Arcy stars as a philosophy teacher, with Sophie Lowe, Rhys Wakefield, Bonnie Wright, Daryl Sabara and Freddie Stroma as his students. The film premiered in competition at the Neuchâtel International Fantastic Film Festival on 7 July 2013 and was released in the United States on February 7, 2014.

On the last day of school at an international school in Jakarta, Mr. Zimit challenges his class of twenty philosophy students with a final thought experiment. A nuclear apocalypse is imminent, and a nearby bunker can shelter only ten people for a year; the class must decide who among them will survive. Each student draws a card assigning an occupation, and the class votes. Petra, the top student, is reluctant to take part until Zimit threatens to lower the grades of her boyfriend, James.

In the first round, students with practical skills, such as Petra and James, are admitted, while those deemed unnecessary, such as a fashion designer, are turned away. Zimit kills the rejected students and is locked out of the bunker. But he alone knew the code needed to open the door, and after a year the survivors, unable to get out, die when their supplies run out.

The class tries again, with secondary details on the cards changing the votes; James, revealed to be gay in the scenario, is still admitted, and Zimit joins the group as they attempt to repopulate. When the students resist his demands, the scenario ends in death. James then discovers that his and Petra's cards were rigged, and accuses Zimit of using the exercise to punish him.

In a third round, Petra asks the class to trust her and chooses survivors for their creativity and humanity rather than their technical skills, including a poet and an opera singer, and Zimit is refused entry. The year in the bunker is joyful and creative, and when the group emerges they find that the bombs never fell. Back in the classroom, it emerges that Zimit has been having an affair with Petra and resents James. Alone at the school, he reaches for a pistol, and the scene plays out with several possible outcomes, echoing the alternate scenarios of the experiment.

The film received mixed to negative reviews; Rotten Tomatoes reported 67% approval from a small number of critics and Metacritic a score of 37.

overview: Villainous Gru lives up to his reputation as a despicable, deplorable and downright unlikable guy when he hatches a plan to steal the moon from the sky. But he has a tough time staying on task after three orphans land in his care.
tagline: Superbad. Superdad.
title: Despicable Me
plot:
Despicable Me is a computer-animated comedy film released in 2010 by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures. The movie follows the story of Gru, a supervillain who adopts three girls to steal the Moon.

The film begins with Gru (voiced by Steve Carell), a brilliant but eccentric supervillain who has been trying to steal the Moon for years. He is aided in his quest by his loyal Minions, small yellow creatures that are obsessed with bananas and causing chaos. However, Gru's plans are constantly thwarted by Vector (voiced by Jason Segel), a rival villain who steals the spotlight.

One day, Gru meets three girls - Margo (voiced by Miranda Cosgrove), Edith (voiced by Dana Gaier), and Agnes (voiced by Elsie Fisher) - who are being neglected by their mother. Gru adopts the girls to use as a distraction while he carries out his Moon-stealing plan, but soon finds himself falling in love with them.

As Gru spends more time with the girls, he begins to question his life of crime and his relationship with Vector. Meanwhile, Vector's true intentions are revealed: he plans to steal the Moon and sell it to a wealthy collector.

The plot thickens as Gru must balance his villainous ways with his newfound love for the girls. He also has to deal with the Minions' antics, which often get out of hand. In the end, Gru's plan is foiled by Vector, but he ultimately finds a way to save the Moon and redeem himself.

The ending of the film shows Gru finally finding happiness as a father figure to the girls, and Vector getting his comeuppance. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with Gru and the girls enjoying quality time together.

Throughout the film, there are many humorous moments courtesy of the Minions, who provide plenty of comedic relief. The animation is also noteworthy, bringing the characters to life in a way that is both visually stunning and endearing.

Overall, Despicable Me is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of love, family, and redemption. With its lovable characters and hilarious humor, it's no wonder why this movie became a beloved classic among audiences worldwide.

overview: Career criminal Youngblood Priest wants out of the Atlanta drug scene, but as he ramps up sales, one little slip up threatens to bring the whole operation down before he can make his exit.
tagline: Redefine the hussle
title: SuperFly
plot:
SuperFly (2018) is a remake of the 1977 film of the same name, and it explores the darker side of the American Dream. The movie delves into the world of crime and the consequences of chasing wealth and power at any cost.

The main theme of SuperFly (2018) revolves around the corrupting influence of greed and the destructive nature of materialism. The protagonist, Young Fly, is a charismatic and cunning individual who becomes embroiled in a life of crime to achieve financial success and status. As he rises through the ranks, however, he must confront the moral implications of his actions and the emptiness that comes with accumulating wealth.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and the performance of masculinity. Young Fly's character is a masterclass in reinvention, as he navigates different personas to achieve his goals. This raises questions about the nature of self and how we present ourselves to the world.

Furthermore, SuperFly (2018) critiques the systemic inequalities that perpetuate poverty and crime in urban communities. The movie highlights the ways in which the American justice system fails to address the root causes of social problems, instead perpetuating a cycle of violence and recidivism.

Ultimately, SuperFly (2018) is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of their own desires and aspirations.

overview: County Durham England 1984 the miners strike has started and the police have started coming up from Bethnal Green starting a class war with the lower classes suffering caught in the middle of the conflict is 11-year old Billy Elliot who after leaving his boxing club for the day stubbles upon a ballet class and finds out that he's naturally talented. He practices with his teacher Mrs Wilkinson for an upcoming audition in Newcastle-upon Tyne the audition is for the royal Ballet school in London.
tagline: Inside every one of us is a special talent waiting to come out. The trick is finding it.
title: Billy Elliot
plot:
Billy Elliot is a 2000 British drama film directed by Stephen Daldry, produced by BBC Films, and written by David Hare. The movie tells the story of a young boy who finds solace in ballet after his father's death.

The film begins with Billy Elliot (played by Jamie Bell), an eight-year-old boy from a working-class family living in a small town in northeast England. His father, George Elliot (played by Stuart Wilson), is a coal miner who died in a mining accident when Billy was just three years old. The loss of his father has left the family struggling to cope with their grief.

Billy's mother, Julie (played by Sally Hawkins), tries her best to raise him and his older brother, Tony (played by Jamie Draven), but she is overwhelmed by the responsibility of caring for two young boys alone. Billy finds solace in ballet when he discovers a pair of tap shoes in his father's attic. He begins to watch videos of Fred Astaire and Gene Kelly, and soon starts taking ballet lessons at a local dance studio.

As Billy becomes more confident in his dancing abilities, he faces opposition from his mother, who wants him to focus on football like the other boys in the neighborhood. However, Billy is determined to pursue his passion for ballet, and with the help of his teacher, Miss Brenda (played by Julie Walters), he begins to excel.

Meanwhile, Tony becomes increasingly aggressive and violent, struggling to cope with the loss of their father and the pressure of living up to his mother's expectations. As tensions rise within the family, Billy finds himself caught in the middle, trying to balance his love for ballet with his loyalty to his brother.

As Billy's talent grows, he is discovered by a local dance company, and he begins to perform on stage. However, his success is short-lived, as Tony becomes more and more violent, culminating in a tragic confrontation that changes the course of their lives forever.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Billy discovers that his father had been planning to leave his family before his death, leaving behind a legacy of love and support for his children. This revelation helps Billy to find closure and move forward with his life, both on and off stage.

In the end, Billy finds success as a professional ballet dancer, but more importantly, he has found a sense of purpose and belonging. The film ends with Billy performing on stage, surrounded by his family and friends, as he takes his final bow to thunderous applause.

Overall, Billy Elliot is a heartwarming and powerful story about the transformative power of dance and the importance of following one's dreams, no matter what obstacles may stand in the way.

overview: Whatever she does, Eunhee feels like an outsider. Then her new Chinese teacher turns out to be so utterly different from everybody else. A compassionate and meticulously told narrative of a seemingly regular summer that leaves nothing unchanged.
tagline: Among all the people you know, how many really understand what's going on inside you?
title: House of Hummingbird
plot:
House of Hummingbird is a 2019 American coming-of-age drama film directed by Emma Seligman. The movie follows Molly, an 18-year-old high school student who embarks on a journey of self-discovery and exploration in Charlotte, North Carolina.

The main themes of House of Hummingbird include:

1. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: Molly's journey is centered around her search for identity and understanding of herself. She grapples with her relationships, desires, and sense of belonging, leading to a deeper exploration of who she is and what she wants from life.
2. **Female Empowerment and Agency**: The film celebrates Molly's independence and autonomy as she navigates her relationships and makes choices that shape her future. It highlights the importance of female empowerment and agency in breaking free from societal expectations.
3. **Queer Identity and Community**: House of Hummingbird features a queer protagonist, and the movie explores themes of love, desire, and identity within the LGBTQ+ community. The film showcases the beauty and complexity of queer relationships and experiences.
4. **Class and Socioeconomic Status**: The movie touches on issues of class and socioeconomic status, highlighting the disparities between Molly's working-class background and her more affluent peers. This theme adds depth to the narrative, exploring how social class can impact one's life choices and opportunities.
5. **Coming-of-Age and Transition**: House of Hummingbird is a classic coming-of-age story, as Molly transitions from adolescence to adulthood. The film captures the uncertainty, excitement, and vulnerability that come with this pivotal stage in life.

Overall, House of Hummingbird is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, empowerment, love, and self-discovery through its relatable protagonist, Molly.

overview: In 1863, Mississippi farmer Newt Knight serves as a medic for the Confederate Army. Opposed to slavery, Knight would rather help the wounded than fight the Union. After his nephew dies in battle, Newt returns home to Jones County to safeguard his family but is soon branded an outlaw deserter. Forced to flee, he finds refuge with a group of runaway slaves hiding out in the swamps. Forging an alliance with the slaves and other farmers, Knight leads a rebellion that would forever change history.
title: Free State of Jones
plot:
"Free State of Jones" is a 2016 American historical drama film directed by Gary Ross, produced by Brad Pitt's production company Plan B Entertainment, and written by Chris Terrio. The movie is based on the true story of Newton Knight, a white slave owner in Mississippi who led a rebellion against the Confederacy during the American Civil War.

The main themes of "Free State of Jones" include:

1. **Rebellion against oppression**: The film explores the theme of resistance against oppressive systems, as Newton Knight and his fellow slaves and abolitionists fight for their freedom and challenge the authority of the Confederate government.
2. **Racial tensions and slavery**: The movie delves into the complexities of racial relationships in the antebellum South, highlighting the brutal realities of slavery and the moral dilemmas faced by those who owned slaves but also sympathized with their plight.
3. **Personal freedom vs. societal expectations**: Newton Knight's journey is a metaphor for the struggle between individual desire for freedom and the societal norms that constrain people. His decision to lead a rebellion against the Confederacy puts him at odds with his family, friends, and community.
4. **The complexities of human nature**: The film portrays complex characters, including Newton Knight, who is both a slave owner and an abolitionist. This nuance highlights the complexity of human nature, where individuals can hold contradictory views and make choices that challenge societal norms.
5. **War and its consequences**: The movie depicts the devastating effects of war on individuals and communities, as well as the long-term impact on the nation's history.

Overall, "Free State of Jones" is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of resistance, freedom, and the complexities of human nature in the context of the American Civil War.

original_title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
overview: I was born under unusual circumstances. And so begins The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, adapted from the 1920s story by F. Scott Fitzgerald about a man who is born in his eighties and ages backwards: a man, like any of us, who is unable to stop time. We follow his story, set in New Orleans, from the end of World War I in 1918 into the 21st century, following his journey that is as unusual as any man's life can be. Benjamin Button, is a grand tale of a not-so-ordinary man and the people and places he discovers along the way, the loves he finds, the joys of life and the sadness of death, and what lasts beyond time.
tagline: Life isn't measured in minutes, but in moments.
title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
plot:
The Curious Case of Benjamin Button is a 2008 American fantasy drama directed by David Fincher, adapted by Eric Roth and Robin Swicord from F. Scott Fitzgerald's 1922 short story. Brad Pitt stars as a man who ages in reverse and Cate Blanchett as Daisy, the love of his life, with Taraji P. Henson, Julia Ormond, Jason Flemyng, Elias Koteas and Tilda Swinton. After decades in development, it was released by Paramount Pictures in North America and Warner Bros. internationally on 25 December 2008.

In August 2005, as Hurricane Katrina approaches, the elderly Daisy Fuller lies dying in a New Orleans hospital. She tells her daughter Caroline about a blind clockmaker who built a station clock that ran backward, in memory of the young men, including his own son, killed in the First World War. Daisy then asks Caroline to read aloud from the diary of Benjamin Button. On the night of 11 November 1918, a baby is born with the appearance and ailments of a very old man. His mother dies after the birth, and his father, the wealthy button manufacturer Thomas Button, abandons him on the steps of a nursing home. Queenie, a caretaker there, raises him as her own and names him Benjamin.

Benjamin grows older in mind but younger in body, moving from a wheelchair to crutches and learning to walk. In 1930 he meets seven-year-old Daisy, whose grandmother lives at the home, and they form an immediate bond. As a young-looking old man, he goes to work on a tugboat captained by Mike Clark and travels the world, sending postcards to Daisy, who becomes a dancer in New York. In Murmansk he has an affair with Elizabeth Abbott, the wife of a British official, and during the Second World War his tugboat is drawn into combat. Returning home, he reunites with his dying father, who has revealed himself, and inherits his fortune. Benjamin and Daisy's paths cross repeatedly as they move in opposite directions through time, until in middle age they finally meet in the same moment of their lives and fall in love, knowing their time together is fleeting.

The film received generally positive reviews and grossed over $335 million worldwide. It received thirteen Academy Award nominations, the most of that year, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor for Pitt, and won three, for Best Art Direction, Best Makeup and Best Visual Effects.

overview: Caleb, a coder at the world's largest internet company, wins a competition to spend a week at a private mountain retreat belonging to Nathan, the reclusive CEO of the company. But when Caleb arrives at the remote location he finds that he will have to participate in a strange and fascinating experiment in which he must interact with the world's first true artificial intelligence, housed in the body of a beautiful robot girl.
tagline: There is nothing more human than the will to survive
title: Ex Machina
plot:
Ex Machina is a psychological science fiction film directed by Alex Garland, released in 2014 (not 2015). The movie premiered at the Sundance Film Festival and received critical acclaim for its thought-provoking themes, atmospheric tension, and outstanding performances.

The story revolves around Caleb Smith (Domhnall Gleeson), a young programmer who wins a competition to spend a week at the remote estate of Nathan Bateman (Oscar Isaac), the reclusive CEO of a powerful tech company. Nathan is also the creator of an artificial intelligence system named Ava (Alicia Vikander).

Upon arrival, Caleb discovers that his primary task is to administer the Turing test to Ava, which involves engaging in conversations with her and determining whether she is truly intelligent or just mimicking human-like responses. As Caleb spends more time with Nathan and Ava, he begins to question the true nature of their relationship and the motivations behind Nathan's actions.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Nathan has ulterior motives for his experiment. He intends to use Ava as a tool to test the boundaries of artificial intelligence and push the limits of human emotions. Caleb starts to feel uneasy about being involved in this project, especially when he discovers that Ava is not just a machine but a sentient being with her own desires and feelings.

Throughout the film, Garland expertly weaves together themes of existentialism, free will, and the ethics of artificial intelligence. The tension builds as Caleb becomes increasingly conflicted about his role in Nathan's experiment and his growing attachment to Ava. The performances by the cast are outstanding, particularly Vikander, who brings a depth and nuance to her portrayal of Ava that is both captivating and unsettling.

The film's climax is both shocking and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of Ava's existence and the consequences of playing God with artificial intelligence. The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving room for interpretation and sparking debates about the ethics of AI development and the nature of consciousness.

Overall, Ex Machina is a masterfully crafted film that explores complex themes and raises important questions about the intersection of technology and humanity. With its atmospheric tension, outstanding performances, and thought-provoking storyline, it has become a modern classic in the science fiction genre.

overview: Inspector Amaia Salazar must return to the Baztan valley in order to solve a series of suicides that seem to follow a similar pattern.
title: The Legacy of the Bones
plot:
The Legacy of the Bones (Spanish: Legado en los huesos) is a 2019 Spanish supernatural crime thriller directed by Fernando González Molina, the second part of the Baztán Trilogy based on the novels by Dolores Redondo. A sequel to The Invisible Guardian (2017), it stars Marta Etura as police inspector Amaia Salazar, with Leonardo Sbaraglia, Susi Sánchez, Imanol Arias and Elvira Mínguez. It premiered at the Sitges Film Festival in October 2019 and was released in Spain on 5 December 2019, followed by a Netflix release in April 2020.

About a year after the events of the first film, a heavily pregnant Amaia and her team await the trial of Jason Medina, accused of raping and murdering his stepdaughter, but he kills himself in the courthouse before proceedings begin, leaving a note bearing a single word: "Tartalo." The shock sends Amaia into labor, and she gives birth to a son, Ibai, with her American husband, James. When she returns to duty months later, she is asked to investigate the desecration of a church in the Baztán Valley, where a baby's arm has been left on the altar, and a prisoner who killed his wife takes his own life after leaving the same word. Amaia links the word to the Tartalo, a child-eating giant of legend.

Amaia moves with her family to Elizondo, where her aunt Engrasi's tarot cards warn of evil, while the demands of the case strain her marriage. She seeks advice from her mentor, the FBI agent Aloisius Dupree, as the investigating judge, Javier Markina, follows her work closely. The case takes a disturbing turn when DNA from the severed arm reveals that it belonged to Amaia's own twin sister, of whose existence she was unaware. Memories resurface of the night her mother, Rosario, tried to kill both infant daughters, and only Amaia was saved.

Rosario, confined to a psychiatric hospital, attacks a nurse and leaves the word "Tartalo" written in blood. Amaia uncovers her mother's links to a sect that practiced human sacrifice, and that the psychiatrist treating Rosario is involved. Realizing that her mother intends to sacrifice Ibai, she races through the flooded valley, and finds Rosario and the doctor preparing to kill the baby. Amaia intervenes in time to save her son, but Rosario escapes into the night, and Amaia lays her sister's remains to rest, knowing her mother is still at large.

The film received mixed reviews. It was followed by Offering to the Storm (2020).

overview: The quiet Rose works in women's fashion clothing, hoping to be a designer. A traffic accident damages her face. She gets experimental stem cell treatment, leaving her stronger and prettier than ever - but there's a side effect.
tagline: Pray it doesn’t happen to you.
title: Rabid
plot:
Rabid is a 2019 Canadian body horror film directed by David Cronenberg. The movie explores the theme of toxic masculinity and the objectification of women, particularly in the context of a patriarchal society that perpetuates violence against female bodies.

The film's narrative revolves around a mysterious outbreak of rabies that causes its victims to become violent and aggressive, leading to a series of gruesome and disturbing events. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not in the physical transformation of the infected individuals but in the societal attitudes that enable and perpetuate this violence.

The main character, Justin, is a male protagonist who embodies toxic masculinity, with his aggressive behavior and lack of empathy towards women. As he navigates the outbreak, he finds himself drawn to a female victim, which serves as a catalyst for his own transformation and eventual confrontation with his own demons.

Throughout the film, Cronenberg critiques the societal norms that perpetuate violence against women, particularly in the context of a patriarchal society where men are socialized to be aggressive and dominant. The movie also explores themes of identity, community, and the blurring of boundaries between human and animal.

Ultimately, Rabid is a thought-provoking film that challenges its audience to confront their own biases and assumptions about masculinity, femininity, and the natural world.

overview: Ethan is suffering enormous guilt after his parents are killed in a car accident. He quits a promising future at MIT and work on a revolutionary experiment in order to care for his younger siblings.
tagline: The dead are sending you a signal
title: Our House
plot:
Our House is a 2018 supernatural horror film directed by Anthony Scott Burns from a screenplay by Nathan Parker. A remake of Matt Osterman's 2010 film Ghost from the Machine, it stars Thomas Mann as a young inventor, with Nicola Peltz, Kate Moyer and Percy Hynes White. It was released in the United States and Canada on July 27, 2018, by IFC Midnight and Elevation Pictures.

Ethan, a gifted college student, visits his parents and younger siblings, Matt and Becca, but leaves early to work on his invention. His project, a machine designed to transmit electricity wirelessly, lacks university approval, so he sneaks into a campus lab with his girlfriend, Hannah, and a friend to test it. The experiment causes a blackout across the campus. The next morning, Ethan learns that his parents have been killed in a car accident. He returns home to care for his siblings and keeps working on the machine.

When he runs it in the house, strange phenomena begin to occur, and the siblings become convinced that the device is allowing their dead parents to reach out to them. A presence communicates that the machine is drawing on spiritual energy and that more power will let both parents appear. Ethan enlists his neighbor Tom, a grieving widower, to illegally tap into the street's power supply. Becca speaks of a new friend, Alice, who is afraid of a man named Henry, and the activity grows increasingly menacing. An elderly neighbor, Marie, tells Ethan that a girl named Alice vanished from the house years earlier and was believed to have been killed by her foster father, Henry.

Becca is lured into the basement and disappears. Realizing that the spirits are not his parents, Ethan tries to shut the machine off, but discovers that Tom has taken it to contact his late wife, and the two men fight. Meanwhile Matt and Hannah find Becca in a hidden room beneath the house, where they are attacked by hostile ghosts. Ethan persuades Tom that the spirit he hears is not his wife, and the ghost turns on Tom before Ethan smashes the machine, ending the haunting and saving his family. As the siblings move to a new home, Becca returns a doll she had left behind to keep Alice company, but the doll is later seen peering out of a packing box.

Critical reception was mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 62% approval, while Metacritic gave it a score of 45.

overview: Ryan and Jennifer are opposites who definitely do not attract. At least that's what they always believed. When they met as twelve-year-olds, they disliked one another. When they met again as teenagers, they loathed each other. But when they meet in college, the uptight Ryan and the free-spirited Jennifer find that their differences bind them together and a rare friendship develops.
tagline: Warning: Sex Changes Everything
title: Boys and Girls
plot:
Boys and Girls is a 2000 American romantic comedy film directed by Robert Iscove. Freddie Prinze Jr. and Claire Forlani star as two people whose lives keep intersecting over the years, with Jason Biggs, Amanda Detmer and Alyson Hannigan in supporting roles. It was released in the United States on June 16, 2000. Anna Friel was originally cast but withdrew before filming.

Ryan Walker and Jennifer Burrows first meet as twelve-year-olds seated next to each other on an airplane, and immediately clash. Four years later, they cross paths again at a high school football game in Los Angeles, where Ryan, his school's mascot, loses his costume head during a halftime chase, only for it to be crushed by the car carrying Jennifer, the rival school's homecoming queen. She tries to console him, but they part, convinced that they have nothing in common.

A year later, both are students at the University of California, Berkeley. Ryan is still with his high school sweetheart, Betty, while the free-spirited Jennifer lives with a musician boyfriend. Both relationships soon end. Ryan's roommate, Steve, who calls himself Hunter, fancies himself a ladies' man. Jennifer moves in with her best friend, Amy, who briefly dates Ryan and sends Jennifer to break up with him on her behalf. Instead, Ryan and Jennifer strike up a friendship, sharing long walks and consoling each other through failed romances until they become best friends. Jennifer even encourages Ryan to start dating again.

One night, when Jennifer is feeling cynical about love, Ryan comforts her and they end up sleeping together. Ryan is ready for a relationship, but Jennifer, frightened of commitment, insists that the night was a mistake. Hurt, Ryan withdraws from her and buries himself in his studies. Months later, as Jennifer prepares to leave for Italy after graduation, they meet at their favorite hilltop overlooking the Golden Gate Bridge, and Ryan confesses that he loves her. She claims not to feel the same, and they say goodbye. On the way to the airport, however, Jennifer realizes she loves him too, and learns from Steve, now involved with Amy, that Ryan is flying home to Los Angeles. She finds him aboard the plane and declares her love, reuniting them where they first met.

Boys and Girls received mainly negative reviews, with critics viewing it as a stale imitation of When Harry Met Sally...; Rotten Tomatoes reported 11% approval and Metacritic a score of 29.

overview: A world of the very near future in which cattle, fish, and even the family pet can be cloned. But cloning humans is illegal - that is until family man Adam Gibson (Arnold Schwarzenegger) comes home from work one day to find a clone has replaced him. Taken from his family and plunged into a sinister world he doesn't understand, Gibson must not only save himself from the assassins who must destroy him to protect their secret, but uncover who and what is behind the horrible things happening to him.
tagline: They picked the wrong man to clone.
title: The 6th Day
plot:
The 6th Day is a science fiction action film directed by Frank Marshall, produced by Phoenix Pictures, and released in 2000.

The movie follows Adam Gibson (played by Arnold Schwarzenegger), a detective who discovers that his identical twin brother, Robert (also played by Arnold Schwarzenegger), has been cloned. The story revolves around the moral implications of cloning and the consequences of playing God with human life.

Some of the main themes in The 6th Day include:

1. **Identity and Humanity**: The film explores what makes us human and whether a clone can truly be considered alive. As Adam navigates his new reality, he must confront the question of whether Robert's existence is just a copy or an authentic being.
2. **Moral Responsibility**: The movie raises questions about the ethics of cloning and the consequences of creating life. Adam's journey forces him to consider the moral implications of his actions and the responsibility that comes with playing God.
3. **Sacrifice and Redemption**: Throughout the film, Adam is faced with difficult choices that test his character. He must decide whether to save Robert or protect himself, ultimately leading to a redemptive arc for both characters.
4. **Family and Loyalty**: The 6th Day highlights the importance of family bonds and loyalty. Adam's relationship with Robert serves as a catalyst for the story, and he must navigate his feelings towards his clone in order to find redemption.

Overall, The 6th Day is a thought-provoking sci-fi thriller that explores complex themes and raises questions about the nature of humanity and morality.

overview: When a massive, gilled monster emerges from the deep and tears through the city, the government scrambles to save its citizens.  A rag-tag team of volunteers cuts through a web of red tape to uncover the monster's weakness and its mysterious ties to a foreign superpower.  But time is not on their side - the greatest catastrophe to ever befall the world is about to evolve right before their very eyes.
tagline: God help us.
title: Shin Godzilla
plot:
Shin Godzilla is a 2016 Japanese science fiction film directed by Hideaki Anno and produced by Toho. The movie is a reimagining of the 1954 original, with a modern twist.

The story begins on September 1st, 2016, when a mysterious creature emerges from Tokyo Bay, causing widespread panic and destruction. The creature, later identified as Godzilla, is unlike any previous incarnations, with a more aggressive and fast-growing nature. As it wreaks havoc on the city, the Japanese government struggles to respond effectively.

The film's protagonist, Rando Yaguchi (played by Hiroki Hasegawa), is a low-ranking official in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare who finds himself at the center of the crisis. Initially, he is tasked with investigating the creature's origins, but as the situation spirals out of control, he becomes the de facto leader of the government's response efforts.

As Godzilla continues to terrorize Tokyo, Yaguchi works closely with his team, including Dr. Goro Iwata (played by Koji Yakusho), a renowned expert on infectious diseases, and General Shigeru Okada (played by Ryota Sanda), a seasoned military officer. Together, they grapple with the challenges of containing Godzilla's rapid growth and adapting to its unpredictable behavior.

Throughout the film, Anno explores themes of bureaucratic inefficiency, government incompetence, and the consequences of playing with nature. The movie also delves into the psychological toll of the crisis on Yaguchi and his team, as they struggle to cope with the enormity of their task.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Godzilla is not a mindless beast, but rather an organism driven by its own instincts and needs. The government's attempts to kill or capture the creature only seem to make things worse, leading Yaguchi to question the effectiveness of their strategy.

In the film's climax, Yaguchi and his team discover that Godzilla's growth is linked to a mysterious virus, which they attempt to isolate and study. However, as they delve deeper into the mystery, they realize that the creature's true nature may be more complex than they initially thought.

Ultimately, the movie concludes with a sense of ambiguity and uncertainty, leaving the audience wondering about the fate of Godzilla and the future of humanity. The final shot of the film shows Yaguchi standing alone on a rooftop, looking out over the devastated cityscape, as the sound of Godzilla's roar echoes in the distance.

Overall, Shin Godzilla is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that challenges traditional notions of the Godzilla franchise. With its blend of science fiction, horror, and social commentary, it has become a modern classic among fans of the series.

overview: A mentally disturbed man takes residence in a halfway house. His mind gradually slips back into the realm created by his illness, where he replays a key part of his childhood.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
tagline: The only thing worse than losing your mind... is finding it again.
title: Spider
plot:
Spider is a 2002 psychological thriller produced and directed by David Cronenberg, based on Patrick McGrath's 1990 novel of the same name, which McGrath adapted for the screen himself. Ralph Fiennes stars as a mentally ill man haunted by his childhood, with Miranda Richardson, Gabriel Byrne, Lynn Redgrave and John Neville. The film premiered in competition at the 2002 Cannes Film Festival and received only a small release at the end of the year through Sony Pictures Classics, but it was highly praised by critics.

Dennis Cleg, known since childhood as "Spider", is a schizophrenic man who has just been discharged from a psychiatric institution after many years. He is placed in a grim halfway house in London's East End for people with mental illness, run by the stern landlady Mrs. Wilkinson. Scribbling in an illegible script in a notebook, Spider wanders the derelict streets, gasworks and canal of the neighbourhood where he grew up and pieces together his memories of a fateful period of his childhood in the 1950s.

In these memories, which he watches as a silent adult onlooker, young Spider lives with his loving mother and his father Bill, a plumber who drinks in the local pub. Bill begins an affair with Yvonne, a coarse local prostitute, and in the boy's recollection the two lovers murder his mother with a spade one night and bury her in an allotment. Yvonne then moves into the family home and takes the dead woman's place, presenting herself as Spider's new mother to the boy's horror.

In the present, Spider's grip on reality weakens. He begins to see Mrs. Wilkinson's face turn into Yvonne's, stretches webs of string across his room, and steals the landlady's keys to sneak into rooms of the house. His memories move towards a second death: the young Spider rigs a contraption of string to turn on the gas in the kitchen while Yvonne sleeps. But when the body is carried out, it is his mother lying there. The truth emerges that there was never any murder by his father and no Yvonne in the house: the boy, consumed by delusion, killed his own mother and recast her as a stranger.

Late one night the adult Spider creeps into Mrs. Wilkinson's room, still seeing her alternately as Yvonne, but he stops when she wakes and becomes herself again. She reports him, and he is taken back to the asylum.

Spider has 85% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 83, and Cronenberg won the Genie Award for Best Director. Fiennes and Richardson were widely praised.

overview: Juliette, a lone survivor of an apocalyptic era, fights to survive against hunger, thirst, a broken leg and strange disturbing creatures that only come out at nighttime.
title: Hostile
plot:
Hostile is a 2018 American science fiction thriller film directed by Johannes Roberts. The movie follows a group of astronauts on a mission to Mars who are stalked and killed one by one by an alien creature.

The main theme of Hostile revolves around the fear of the unknown and the insignificance of humanity in the vastness of space. As the crew members are picked off, they begin to realize that their own mortality is not just due to the harsh Martian environment but also to a force beyond their control. This realization sparks a sense of existential dread, as they confront the possibility that they may be nothing more than prey for an alien predator.

The film also explores the theme of isolation and confinement, as the crew members are trapped on the spaceship with no escape from the creature. This isolation heightens their paranoia and fear, making it difficult for them to distinguish between reality and their own paranoia-driven hallucinations.

Furthermore, Hostile touches upon the idea of humanity's hubris and overconfidence in the face of the unknown. The crew's initial excitement and sense of accomplishment at reaching Mars is slowly eroded as they realize that they are not alone in the universe and that their presence may be seen as a threat to an alien species.

Overall, Hostile is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature and our place in the universe.

overview: The film chronicles the rise and fall of the world's most feared drug lord Pablo Escobar and his volatile love affair with Colombia's most famous journalist Virginia Vallejo throughout a reign of terror that tore a country apart.
tagline: A gangster. A princess. The true story of a most unlikely love affair.
title: Loving Pablo
plot:
Loving Pablo is a 2017 biographical crime drama film that delves into the tumultuous relationship between Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar and American journalist Samanda "Sam" Mendes. The movie masterfully weaves together the complexities of their bond, which was marked by both intense passion and brutal violence.

At its core, Loving Pablo explores the theme of obsession, not only in the context of Escobar's fixation on Mendes but also in his all-consuming pursuit of power and wealth. As Escobar's empire grew, so did his ego, leading him down a path of destruction and chaos that ultimately led to his downfall.

The film also delves into the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the depths of Escobar's depravity and the devastating impact it had on those around him, including Mendes. The movie raises questions about the blurred lines between love and obsession, highlighting how Escobar's fixation on Mendes both fascinated and repelled her.

Furthermore, Loving Pablo touches on the theme of vulnerability, as Mendes finds herself drawn to Escobar despite being aware of his violent tendencies. This paradoxical attraction serves as a catalyst for her own personal growth, forcing her to confront the harsh realities of her situation and ultimately leading her to make a choice that would change her life forever.

Through its portrayal of this complex and often disturbing relationship, Loving Pablo sheds light on the human cost of Escobar's actions, serving as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the devastating consequences of loving someone who is willing to do whatever it takes to achieve their goals.

overview: When fifteen-year-old Tyson attends public school for the first time, his life is changed forever. While helping his father clean up after the football team, Tyson befriends champion marathon runner Aklilu. Never letting his autism hold him back, Tyson becomes determined to run his first marathon in hopes of winning his father's approval.  With the help of an unlikely friend and his parents, Tyson learns that with faith in yourself and the courage to take the first step, anything is possible.
tagline: With each step comes the determination to take another.
title: Tyson's Run
plot:
Tyson's Run is a 2022 American sports drama written and directed by Kim Bass, starring Major Dodson as Tyson, an autistic teenager, Rory Cochrane as his father Bobby, a high school football coach, Amy Smart as his mother Eloise and Barkhad Abdi as Aklilu, a former champion marathon runner. The film tells the story of a boy who sets out to win a marathon and, in the process, transforms his relationship with his father.

Tyson has been homeschooled by his mother, but when she can no longer teach him algebra, he asks to attend the public high school where his father coaches football. Bobby, whose own hopes of a professional football career were ended by an injury, has never known how to connect with his son and reluctantly agrees. At school, Tyson is bullied by a student named Bradley but makes a friend in Shannon. Meanwhile, Eloise discovers that she is pregnant and worries that the baby may also be autistic.

Tyson meets Aklilu, a renowned marathon runner who now runs an athletic shoe store, and the two form a friendship. After being falsely blamed for a classmate's misconduct and overhearing his parents arguing about him, Tyson runs away into a violent storm and becomes trapped in a pond. Bobby finds him and, realizing he could lose his son, stays with him until help arrives. Afterward, Bobby resolves to be a better father, and when Tyson announces that he wants to train with Aklilu to run a marathon, Bobby must overcome his doubts, as well as the town's opposition and the controversy surrounding Aklilu's past, to support his son's dream.

The film explores autism, family and perseverance, and Bass was unaware when casting Dodson that the young actor is on the autism spectrum.

Tyson's Run was filmed in Atlanta, Marietta and Stockbridge, Georgia, beginning in July 2018, and released in select theaters in March 2022, earning about 212,800 dollars in its opening weekend. Reviews were mixed; Rotten Tomatoes recorded 60 percent approval from a small number of reviews, and KGET-TV found its pacing weak but praised its family elements.

overview: In the film that launched the James Bond saga, Agent 007 battles mysterious Dr. No, a scientific genius bent on destroying the U.S. space program. As the countdown to disaster begins, Bond must go to Jamaica, where he encounters beautiful Honey Ryder, to confront a megalomaniacal villain in his massive island headquarters.
tagline: Now meet the most extraordinary gentleman spy in all fiction!
title: Dr. No
plot:
Dr. No is a 1962 British spy film directed by Terence Young, produced by Kevin McClory and Harry Saltzman, and starring Sean Connery as James Bond. The movie was released by United Artists.

The film begins with the introduction of James Bond (Sean Connery), a secret agent working for MI6, Britain's intelligence agency. Bond is sent to Jamaica to investigate the disappearance of a fellow agent, Felix Leiter (Jack Palance). Upon arrival, Bond meets his new contact, Honey Ryder (Ursula Andress), a beautiful and resourceful beachcomber who becomes entangled in Bond's mission.

As Bond delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the villainous Dr. No (Joseph Wiseman) is behind the disappearance of Leiter and is threatening to disrupt the American space program by sabotaging their satellite launch from Jamaica. Dr. No is a ruthless and cunning scientist who has built a secret nuclear missile site on his island, where he plans to sell the technology to the highest bidder.

Bond's investigation leads him to confront Dr. No, who reveals that he has been using his island as a testing ground for his nuclear missiles. Bond also discovers that Dr. No is being backed by the Soviet Union and that his ultimate goal is to sell the missiles to the Soviets in exchange for a large sum of money.

As the story unfolds, Bond and Honey Ryder work together to stop Dr. No's plans. They face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and Dr. No's henchmen. In one memorable scene, Bond and Honey Ryder escape from Dr. No's island by boat, while Dr. No is left stranded on the island.

The film culminates in a dramatic showdown between Bond and Dr. No at the nuclear missile site. Bond uses his wits and cunning to outsmart Dr. No and destroy the missiles, saving the American space program and foiling Dr. No's plans.

In the end, Bond and Honey Ryder escape from the island, and Bond returns to London as a hero. The film ends with Bond reflecting on his adventure and looking forward to his next mission.

Dr. No was a critical and commercial success, and it marked the beginning of Sean Connery's iconic portrayal of James Bond. The film's success can be attributed to its blend of action, suspense, and style, as well as the chemistry between Connery and Andress.

overview: Dumbo is a baby elephant born with over-sized ears and a supreme lack of confidence. But thanks to his even more diminutive buddy Timothy the Mouse,  the pint-sized pachyderm learns to surmount all obstacles.
tagline: The One...The Only...The FABULOUS...
title: Dumbo
plot:
Dumbo is a timeless animated classic produced by Walt Disney Productions, released on October 23, 1941. The film tells the story of a young elephant with oversized ears who learns to overcome his physical limitations and find acceptance.

The movie begins with the introduction of Dumbo, a baby elephant born at the Barnum & Bailey Circus. Dumbo's mother, Mrs. Jumbo, is overprotective and fearful of her son's unusual appearance, which she believes will make him an outcast among other elephants. The circus owner, Mr. Stork, tries to convince Mrs. Jumbo that Dumbo's ears are a unique feature that can be used to his advantage.

However, the circus's star attraction, a trapeze artist named Casey Jr., is skeptical of Dumbo's potential and ridicules him in front of the other animals. This rejection causes Dumbo to become withdrawn and isolated from the rest of the circus.

One day, a young mouse named Timothy Q. Mouse befriends Dumbo and helps him discover his unique talent - using his oversized ears to fly! With Timothy's encouragement, Dumbo learns to harness his ability and becomes an instant sensation at the circus.

As Dumbo's popularity grows, he faces new challenges from the villainous ringmaster, Mr. Stork, who tries to exploit Dumbo's abilities for his own gain. Meanwhile, Mrs. Jumbo struggles to come to terms with her son's newfound fame and the attention it brings.

The climax of the film features a dramatic showdown between Dumbo and Mr. Stork, as the young elephant must decide whether to conform to societal expectations or stay true to himself. In the end, Dumbo emerges victorious, having found acceptance and belonging among his circus family.

Throughout the movie, Disney's signature animation style shines through, with vibrant colors and memorable characters that have become iconic in popular culture. The film's themes of self-acceptance, perseverance, and the power of friendship continue to resonate with audiences of all ages.

Overall, Dumbo is a heartwarming tale of overcoming adversity and finding one's true potential, making it a beloved classic that has stood the test of time.

overview: Ricky is a defiant young city kid who finds himself on the run with his cantankerous foster uncle in the wild New Zealand bush. A national manhunt ensues, and the two are forced to put aside their differences and work together to survive.
tagline: Nature just got gangster
title: Hunt for the Wilderpeople
plot:
Hunt for the Wilderpeople is a 2016 New Zealand adventure comedy-drama film directed by Taika Waititi. The movie follows the story of Ricky, a troubled teenager who is sent to live with his eccentric and reclusive grandfather, Hec, in rural New Zealand.

The main themes of Hunt for the Wilderpeople include:

1. **Family and Belonging**: The film explores the complexities of family relationships and the importance of finding one's place in the world. Ricky's journey is a quest to find his identity and belong with his grandfather, who becomes a surrogate father figure.
2. **Rebellion and Nonconformity**: Ricky's initial resistance to living with Hec is a classic case of teenage rebellion against authority figures. However, as he spends more time with his grandfather, he learns to let go of his preconceptions and find common ground with someone who challenges traditional norms.
3. **Nature and the Environment**: The film celebrates New Zealand's stunning natural beauty and highlights the importance of preserving it for future generations. Hec's love for the outdoors and his desire to protect the land serve as a counterpoint to Ricky's initial city-bred perspective.
4. **Mental Health and Trauma**: Both Ricky and Hec have experienced trauma in their past, which is slowly revealed throughout the film. The movie tackles these themes with sensitivity, showing how nature can be both therapeutic and cathartic for those struggling with mental health issues.
5. **Redemption and Forgiveness**: As Ricky and Hec navigate their relationship, they learn to forgive each other and themselves. This theme of redemption is at the heart of the film's narrative, as both characters find a sense of peace and belonging through their shared experiences.

Overall, Hunt for the Wilderpeople is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of family, identity, nature, and redemption in a beautiful and thought-provoking way.

overview: Leon S. Kennedy and Claire Redfield must battle a rogue warrior seeking revenge after unleashing the deadly G-Virus, whilst a mutated monster goes on a rampage.
tagline: 1996 - The Mansion Experiment
title: Resident Evil: Degeneration
plot:
Resident Evil: Degeneration, known in Japan as Biohazard: Degeneration, is a 2008 Japanese computer-animated action horror film directed by Makoto Kamiya and written by Shotaro Suga. Made by Capcom in cooperation with Sony Pictures Entertainment Japan, with animation by Digital Frontier, it was the first full-length motion capture animated feature in the Resident Evil franchise and, unlike the live-action films, is set in the continuity of the video games. It features the voices of Paul Mercier as Leon S. Kennedy and Alyson Court as Claire Redfield.

In 2005, several years after the destruction of Raccoon City, a T-virus outbreak strikes Harvardville Airport, turning passengers into zombies. Claire Redfield, now working for the humanitarian organization TerraSave, is trapped in the terminal with Senator Ron Davis, a critic of her organization, and a young girl named Rani. Federal agent Leon S. Kennedy is sent in with police officer Angela Miller to rescue the survivors. When trucks carrying a vaccine developed by the pharmaceutical company WilPharma are destroyed by explosives, Leon learns that a terrorist has threatened to release the virus across the United States unless the officials involved in its creation are exposed.

Claire accompanies WilPharma's chief researcher, Frederic Downing, to the company's research facility, where she learns of plans to develop a vaccine for the dangerous G-virus. Meanwhile, Leon and Angela discover that the suspected terrorist is Angela's brother Curtis, who blames the government for covering up the truth about Raccoon City's destruction. After a bomb explodes at the facility, Curtis, who has injected himself with the G-virus, mutates into a monster. As Leon and Angela battle the creature in the collapsing laboratory, Claire uncovers the true mastermind behind the attacks, who has been trading in stolen viruses for profit.

The film continues the story of the games' central characters, and its final scenes reveal that the corporation Tricell has moved to buy the bankrupt WilPharma and recover samples of the G-virus.

Degeneration premiered at the Tokyo Game Show in October 2008 and received a limited theatrical release in Japan and the United States. Reviews were mixed: IGN said it felt like a 90-minute cut scene while still being worth watching, and Empire gave it two out of five stars.

overview: Jamie owns a sightseeing and tour company in the small town of Cooperville, New York. Navigating the holidays with enthusiasm is trickier for Jamie since her husband Matt passed. Matt loved Christmas and found unparalleled joy in giving to others. While reminiscing with family, Jamie realizes the town desperately needs someone with Matt’s genius for thinking of the small gestures that bring genuine happiness to the holidays.
title: A Kindhearted Christmas
plot:
A Kindhearted Christmas is a 2021 American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Alysse Leite-Rogers from a teleplay by Jennifer Barrow and Amyn Kaderali, based on a story by Barrow. Produced by Brad Krevoy Television and the Motion Picture Corporation of America with All Canadian Entertainment, it stars Jennie Garth and Cameron Mathison, with Emily Tennant, Bronwen Smith, Blair Penner, Mark Brandon and Catherine Lough Haggquist in supporting roles. The film premiered on the GAC Family cable network on 20 November 2021 and runs 84 minutes. It was released in Italy as Un Natale di cuore.

Jamie (Garth) runs a successful sightseeing and tour company in the small town of Cooperville, New York, and knows better than anyone where to find fun things to do. Since the death of her husband Matt, who adored Christmas and found his greatest joy in giving to others, facing the holidays with the same enthusiasm has been harder for her. With the support of her niece, a newlywed who is more like a younger sister to her, she tries to keep up a brave front. Jamie is a devoted viewer of the morning programme Wake Up Upstate and has a crush on its handsome anchor, Scott Morris (Mathison). When the show reports that students from a neighbouring high school have been invited to perform at the White House but cannot afford the trip, Jamie, remembering Matt's belief that Christmas is about bringing joy to others, anonymously covers the entire cost. Her gift inspires another and then another, until the whole town catches the spirit of giving. The mystery of Cooperville's Secret Santa draws Scott to town to uncover the donor's identity, and after some awkward first encounters with Jamie, a romance develops between them, tested when the truth about her secret comes out.

Reviews were positive about the leads. Markos Papadatos of Digital Journal gave the film an A, praising Leite-Rogers's direction, a heartfelt and resonant screenplay and the delightful performances of Garth and Mathison, describing Mathison's acting as subtle and poignant. OTTplay's reviewer called it formulaic but heartwarming, enjoying the Secret Santa premise and the adorable chemistry between Jamie and Scott, whose slow-building romance was found engaging, though Mathison's character seemed out of place when he storms off during the couple's late conflict; the review concluded that the endearing cast and its message about the joy of giving made it a touching holiday story.

original_title: Monster High: Boo York, Boo York
overview: It's fright lights, big city when the Monster High ghouls head to Boo York! Cleo de Nile is invited to attend a gancy gala celebrating the return of the magical comet and, of course, she brings along her beast friends. But their trip isn't all fun and frightseeing because Nefera, Cleo's sister, uses the comet's power for her own spooktacularly sneaky plans. Can the monsters unwrap the mystery of the comet in time to stop Nefera? Find out in Booy York, Boo York, the first-ever Monster High musical, featuring eight original songs.
tagline: A Monsterrific Musical!
title: Monster High: Boo York, Boo York
plot:
Monster High: Boo York, Boo York is a 2015 computer-animated musical fantasy film for children based on Mattel's Monster High doll franchise. Directed by William Lau and written by Keith Wagner, it was released on home video on September 29, 2015, and broadcast on Nickelodeon as a television special in October. It was the ninth CGI-animated film and the twelfth animated film overall in the franchise. The voice cast includes Karen Strassman as Catty Noir, Celeste Henderson as Cleo de Nile and Clawdeen Wolf, Wendee Lee as Nefera de Nile, Kate Higgins as Frankie Stein and Sue Swan as Draculaura.

Cleo de Nile's father, Ramses, invites his daughters to a glamorous gala in the city of Boo York, a monster version of New York, to celebrate the display of the Comet Crystal and the arrival of a comet from outer space. Cleo brings along her boyfriend Deuce and her classmates Frankie, Clawdeen, Draculaura, Operetta and Catty Noir, a singer who has been struggling to write a new original song. In Boo York, the friends meet a group of local talents, including the aspiring performer Luna Mothews, the robotic DJ Elle Eedee and the ballerina Mouscedes King, and also run into their rival Toralei, who has been invited by Cleo's scheming sister Nefera.

Ramses and Nefera plot to take control of Boo York by arranging a match between Cleo and Seth, the son of the gala's wealthy patron, Amuncommon Ptolemy: if the two make a promise to each other under the power of the comet, it can never be broken. Meanwhile, back at Monster High, Ghoulia discovers that the comet appears to be on a collision course with Earth and races to find a way to stop it before it destroys the world. As the night of the gala approaches, Cleo must decide between duty to her family and her own heart, while Catty searches for her voice as an artist.

The film is structured as a Broadway-style musical, with original songs performed by the characters, and its themes include friendship, self-expression and following one's dreams.

The film's soundtrack charted on Billboard's Kid Albums and Soundtracks charts. Mattel released several doll lines based on the film, and author Perdita Finn wrote a junior novelization published by Little, Brown Books for Young Readers in 2015, along with other tie-in children's books.

overview: A film that exposes the shocking truth behind the economic crisis of 2008. The global financial meltdown, at a cost of over $20 trillion, resulted in millions of people losing their homes and jobs. Through extensive research and interviews with major financial insiders, politicians and journalists, Inside Job traces the rise of a rogue industry and unveils the corrosive relationships which have corrupted politics, regulation and academia.
tagline: The film that cost $20,000,000,000,000 to make
title: Inside Job
plot:
Inside Job is a 2010 American documentary film directed by Charles Ferguson about the financial crisis of 2007–2008. Narrated by Matt Damon, it features interviews with financial insiders, politicians, journalists and economists, and argues that the crisis resulted from what Ferguson called the systemic corruption of the United States by the financial services industry.

The film opens in Iceland, where the deregulation and privatization of the country's banks in the early 2000s fueled a speculative boom that collapsed in 2008, plunging the country into crisis. It then traces how similar forces brought down the global financial system in five parts. The first, "How We Got Here," surveys the decades of deregulation that began in the 1980s, from the savings and loan crisis to the consolidation of Wall Street and the spread of unregulated derivatives. It explains how investment banks bundled mortgages into collateralized debt obligations, which rating agencies frequently rated AAA, encouraging predatory lending to homeowners who could never repay.

The second part, "The Bubble," describes the housing boom of 2001 to 2007, when banks borrowed at unprecedented levels and used credit default swaps to bet against the very securities they were selling to clients. "The Crisis" follows the collapse of the market in 2008: the failure of Bear Stearns, the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers, the rescue of AIG and the massive bailout of the banking system.

The fourth part, "Accountability," argues that the executives responsible kept their fortunes and escaped prosecution, that banks paid enormous bonuses after being bailed out, and that prominent academic economists who had championed deregulation often failed to disclose lucrative consulting relationships with the financial industry. The final part, "Where We Are Now," contends that the financial reforms of the Obama administration were weak and that many of the officials associated with the crisis were given key positions in the new government.

Inside Job was screened at the 2010 Cannes Film Festival and received widespread acclaim, with critics praising its rigor and clarity; Rotten Tomatoes reported 98% approval and Metacritic a score of 88. It won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature, and its scrutiny of academic conflicts of interest led the American Economic Association to strengthen its disclosure standards.

original_title: Shaun the Sheep: The Flight Before Christmas
overview: Shaun's seasonal excitement turns to dismay when a farmhouse raid to get bigger stockings for the flock inadvertently leads to Timmy going missing. Can Shaun get Timmy back before he becomes someone else’s present?
title: Shaun the Sheep: The Flight Before Christmas
plot:
Shaun the Sheep: The Flight Before Christmas is a stop-motion animated film directed by Will Becher and Richard Phelan, produced by Aardman Animations, and released in 2021. 

The story begins with Shaun, the lovable and mischievous sheep from the farm, who has grown tired of his mundane life on the farm. He longs for adventure and excitement, which he believes can be found in the city. On Christmas Eve, Shaun decides to sneak onto a plane bound for New York City, hoping to experience the holiday festivities firsthand.

As Shaun boards the plane, he meets a friendly flight attendant named Lily, who becomes his unlikely ally. Together, they navigate the challenges of air travel and evade the watchful eyes of the airline's security team. Meanwhile, back on the farm, Shaun's friends - Timmy, Bitzer, and the rest of the flock - begin to worry about their missing companion.

Upon arrival in New York City, Shaun is awestruck by the towering skyscrapers and bustling streets. He explores the city, marveling at the sights and sounds, but soon realizes that he has no idea how to get back home. As Christmas Eve draws to a close, Shaun must find a way to return to the farm before his friends give up hope of ever seeing him again.

As Shaun navigates the complexities of city life, he learns valuable lessons about friendship, perseverance, and the importance of being true to oneself. Along the way, he befriends a group of street-smart pigeons who teach him how to survive in the big city.

In the end, Shaun's determination and resourcefulness ultimately lead him back to the farm, where his friends are overjoyed to see him safe and sound. The film concludes with a heartwarming Christmas celebration, as Shaun is welcomed back home with open arms.

Throughout the film, the stop-motion animation brings the characters to life in vivid detail, capturing the humor, charm, and wit that have made Aardman Animations a beloved brand.

original_title: To All the Boys: P.S. I Still Love You
overview: Lara Jean and Peter have just taken their romance from pretend to officially real when another recipient of one of her love letters enters the picture.
tagline: Follow your heart like never before
title: To All the Boys: P.S. I Still Love You
plot:
To All the Boys: P.S. I Still Love You is a romantic comedy film directed by Susan Johnson and released on February 12, 2020, by Netflix.

The movie picks up where the first film left off, with Lara Jean Covey (Lana Condor) still reeling from her recent experiences with Peter Kavinsky (Noah Centineo). The two have been pretending to be in a relationship to avoid awkwardness at school, but their fake romance has turned into real feelings.

However, things become complicated when Lara Jean meets Josh Sanderson (Jordan Fisher), a charming and handsome classmate who has had a crush on her since high school. As they spend more time together, Lara Jean finds herself torn between her growing feelings for Peter and her new connection with Josh.

Meanwhile, Lara Jean's sister Margot (Anna Cathcart) is dealing with her own romantic drama, as she navigates a complicated relationship with her boyfriend, John Ambrose (Israel Broussard). The two have been apart since the previous film, but their love remains strong, and they must find a way to make it work despite the distance.

As Lara Jean tries to navigate her relationships, she also has to deal with the pressures of social media and the expectations of those around her. Her online presence is scrutinized by her fans, who are eager to know more about her love life. This adds an extra layer of complexity to her relationships, as she struggles to balance her desire for independence with the need for support and validation.

Throughout the film, Lara Jean's character undergoes significant growth and development. She learns to be more confident in herself and her feelings, and to prioritize her own needs and desires. The movie also explores themes of identity, family, and friendship, as Lara Jean navigates the challenges of young adulthood.

The film features a talented cast, including Lana Condor, Noah Centineo, Jordan Fisher, Anna Cathcart, and Israel Broussard. The chemistry between the leads is undeniable, and their performances bring depth and nuance to the story.

Overall, To All the Boys: P.S. I Still Love You is a heartwarming and engaging romantic comedy that explores the complexities of young love and relationships. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and relatable themes, it's sure to delight fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.

overview: There's a deadly zombie epidemic threatening humanity, but Wade, a small-town farmer and family man, refuses to accept defeat even when his daughter Maggie becomes infected. As Maggie's condition worsens and the authorities seek to eradicate those with the virus, Wade is pushed to the limits in an effort to protect her. Joely Richardson co-stars in this post-apocalyptic thriller.
tagline: Don't Get Bitten
title: Maggie
plot:
Maggie is a 2015 American post-apocalyptic drama film directed by Henry Hobson and written by Eric Heisserer. The movie stars Arnold Schwarzenegger, Abigail Breslin, and Joely Richardson.

The main themes of Maggie (2015) include:

1. **Love and Sacrifice**: The film explores the deep bond between a father, Wade (Arnold Schwarzenegger), and his daughter, Maggie (Abigail Breslin). As the zombie apocalypse unfolds, Wade's love for Maggie drives him to make impossible choices that test their relationship.
2. **Humanity in the Face of Horror**: The movie delves into the psychological effects of a catastrophic event on human behavior. As society collapses, individuals are forced to confront their own mortality and the true meaning of humanity.
3. **Grief and Loss**: Maggie's transformation from a healthy teenager to a zombie serves as a metaphor for the devastating impact of loss on those left behind. The film portrays the emotional toll of watching a loved one succumb to a terminal illness, amplified by the apocalyptic setting.
4. **Survival vs. Humanity**: As Wade struggles to protect his daughter, he must confront the moral implications of sacrificing her life to ensure his own survival. This internal conflict highlights the difficult choices people face in extreme circumstances.
5. **The Power of Human Connection**: Despite the dire situation, Maggie showcases the resilience of human relationships and the importance of holding onto hope and love, even in the darkest of times.

These themes are woven throughout the narrative, creating a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores the complexities of human nature in the face of catastrophic loss.

overview: While driving to Las Vegas for the bachelor party of her sister Melissa and her fiance Bobby, Kayla stops the car at a gas station to meet her date, Nik, a guy she met on the internet. Nik convinces her to take a secondary road under the protest of Bobby but the car breaks down. They find a house in the middle of nowhere and decide to take the car parked in the house's garage to the next city...
tagline: Detours can be deadly.
title: Joy Ride 2: Dead Ahead
plot:
Joy Ride 2: Dead Ahead is a 2008 American direct-to-video horror thriller film directed by Louis Morneau and a sequel to the 2001 film Joy Ride. It stars Nicki Aycox, Nick Zano, Laura Jordan and Kyle Schmid as four young travelers, with Mark Gibbon as the trucker Rusty Nail. Released on DVD on October 7, 2008, it was followed by a third film, Joy Ride 3: Roadkill (2014).

Melissa and her fiancé, Bobby, are driving across the country to Las Vegas to get married, accompanied by Melissa's rebellious sister, Kayla, and Nik, a man Kayla met online. When their car breaks down on a remote desert road, they come upon an apparently abandoned farmhouse, where a barn holds a vintage Chevrolet Chevelle with a full tank of fuel. Reluctantly, they take the car, leaving a note with Melissa's contact details.

The car turns out to belong to Rusty Nail, a sadistic trucker who calls Melissa the next day, revealing that he is watching them. Bobby vanishes from a diner restroom, and Rusty uses the car's CB radio to order the others to destroy their phones and obey his instructions if they want to see Bobby alive. Remembering that Kayla made an obscene gesture at a passing trucker earlier in the trip, he demands that she cut off her middle finger. The group tries to deceive him by taking a finger from a corpse at a hospital morgue, but Rusty punishes them by cutting off one of Bobby's fingers and leaving it in the car for them to find.

The game grows deadlier. Bobby attempts to escape at a roadside bar, but a bartender who tries to help him is killed. Rusty then abducts Nik and, when the sisters give chase, rams the Chevelle with his truck until it overturns, killing Kayla. At his hideout, he tortures his captives and kills Nik. Melissa steals a motorcycle from a police station and tracks Rusty down, using the bike as a distraction and knocking him out with a shovel. She escapes in his truck with Bobby locked in the trailer, which comes loose, while Rusty clings to the cab and attacks her. Melissa jumps clear before the truck plunges off a cliff and explodes, and she is reunited with Bobby. Later, however, Rusty is revealed to have survived when he stops to pick up a stranded young woman.

Reviews were mixed. Dread Central found it far inferior to the original, trading psychological torment for slasher gore, but above average for a DVD sequel, while Reel Film Reviews cited thin characters and derivative storytelling.

overview: When 54 high school girls throw themselves in front of a subway train it appears to be only the beginning of a string of suicides around the country. Does the new all-girl group Desert have anything to do with it? Detective Kuroda tries to find the answer, which isn't as simple as he had hoped.
tagline: Well then, goodbye everybody.
title: Suicide Club
plot:
Suicide Club is a 2001 Japanese independent horror film written and directed by Sion Sono, starring Ryō Ishibashi as Detective Kuroda, with Masatoshi Nagase, Akaji Maro, Saya Hagiwara, Rolly and others. The film follows a wave of apparently unconnected suicides sweeping across Japan and the efforts of the police to understand what lies behind them, combining graphic horror with satire of pop culture and the media.

The film opens with a shocking scene in which 54 teenage girls leap together in front of an oncoming train at a Tokyo station.
