More suicides follow, including two nurses at a hospital, and at the scenes the police find rolls of human skin stitched together from the bodies of the victims. Detectives Kuroda, Shibusawa and Murata are alerted by a young hacker to a mysterious website that seems to track the deaths before they happen, marking each new victim with a colored circle. As groups of students throw themselves off their school roof and the epidemic spreads throughout the country, the media begins to speak of a "Suicide Club".

A mysterious boy repeatedly calls the police, asking cryptic questions about people's connection to themselves. When the suicides claim Kuroda's own family, the investigation takes a devastating personal turn. A flamboyant gang leader who claims to be behind the Suicide Club turns out to be a false lead, and a young woman, Mitsuko, whose boyfriend was among the victims, discovers coded messages hidden in the hand gestures of Dessert, a popular girl group whose songs seem to be linked to the deaths. Her search leads her to a secret concert and to a group of children who claim that there is no club at all.

Rather than offering a clear explanation, the film leaves its mysteries largely unresolved, inviting interpretation as a commentary on alienation, conformity and the influence of mass media on Japanese youth.

Suicide Club premiered at the Tokyo International Film Festival on October 29, 2001, and was released in Japan in March 2002. Its transgressive subject and gruesome imagery made it notorious at festivals around the world, and it won the Jury Prize for Most Ground-Breaking Film at the 2003 Fantasia Festival. It developed a strong cult following and was followed by the prequel Noriko's Dinner Table (2005).

overview: Hellbent on taking over Earthrealm, Kano viciously attacks town after town with the aid of three cold-blooded Black Dragon mercenaries. Those who don’t submit are annihilated but one young man won’t bend the knee to Kano: Kenshi.
tagline: Evil is Unleashed!
title: Mortal Kombat Legends: Snow Blind
plot:
Mortal Kombat Legends: Snow Blind is a 2022 animated film that serves as a spin-off to the Mortal Kombat franchise. The story takes place during the events of the original Mortal Kombat film, but it's not a direct adaptation.

The plot revolves around Kitana (voiced by Jessica McNamee), the princess of Edenia, who is on a mission to rescue her sister Princess Mileena from the clutches of Shao Kahn. Along the way, she teams up with Johnny Cage (voiced by Joe Taslim) and Sonya Blade (voiced by Christina Chong).

As they journey through the frozen wasteland of Outworld, Kitana begins to experience strange visions and flashbacks that hint at a dark secret from her past. She soon discovers that Mileena is being manipulated by Shao Kahn's forces, who are using her as a pawn in their plan to conquer Earthrealm.

Meanwhile, Johnny Cage struggles with his own identity crisis, feeling like an outsider among the warriors of Outworld. He begins to question whether he truly belongs on this quest or if he's just a relic from a different world.

Throughout their journey, Kitana and her companions face numerous challenges, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious creatures, and rival warriors vying for power. Along the way, they uncover clues that suggest Mileena is not what she seems, and that Kitana's own destiny is intertwined with her sister's fate.

The film features stunning animation, blending traditional techniques with modern computer-generated imagery. The action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, showcasing the signature Mortal Kombat style of brutal combat and acrobatic feats.

Overall, Mortal Kombat Legends: Snow Blind offers a fresh take on the Mortal Kombat universe, exploring themes of identity, loyalty, and the complexities of sisterly love. While it may not be a direct adaptation of any specific storyline, it provides an engaging and thrilling ride for fans of the franchise.

original_title: La Fameuse Invasion des ours en Sicile
overview: Our story starts with Tonio, the son the bears King, being kidnapped by some hunters in the Sicilian mountains. Because of the harshness of a winter that threatens its clan with famine, the Bear King decides to invade the land of men (in the hope of finding his son). Thanks to his powerful army and the help of a wizard, he will succeed at both quests but he will soon find out that bears are not meant to live in the land of men.
title: The Bears' Famous Invasion of Sicily
plot:
The Bears' Famous Invasion of Sicily, released in the United States as The Bears and the Invasion of Sicily, is a 2019 Italian-French animated adventure film and the feature debut of the illustrator Lorenzo Mattotti. Mattotti wrote the screenplay with Jean-Luc Fromental and Thomas Bidegain, adapting Dino Buzzati's 1945 children's book. Its Italian voice cast includes Toni Servillo, Antonio Albanese and Andrea Camilleri, and the French version includes Leïla Bekhti and Jean-Claude Carrière.

The filmmakers added a framing story to the book. Gedeone, a traveling showman, and his young assistant Almerina take shelter from the winter cold in a cave, where they accidentally wake an old bear from his hibernation. To keep him friendly, they entertain him with a tale from long ago, before bears vanished from Sicily: the story of the bears' famous invasion.

In that story, the bears live in the mountain woods under their king, Leonzio. While he is teaching his son Tonio to catch fish, the cub is swept away by the river and captured by humans. Overcome with grief, Leonzio neglects his duties, and winter arrives before the clan has stored enough food. Starving, the bears decide to descend to the human lands, where they can find food and search for Tonio. The cruel Grand Duke treats their arrival as an invasion and sends his army against them, but the bears prevail in fantastical battles, helped for a time by the Duke's mistreated court magician, De Ambrosiis, who befriends Leonzio. Tonio is eventually found in a circus, the Grand Duke is overthrown, and Leonzio becomes king of Sicily, with bears and humans living together in harmony. The peace does not last: some bears are corrupted by the worst human vices, and the bears return to the forest, having learned that bears and men are too different to live together.

Produced by Prima Linea Productions with Pathé, France 3 Cinéma, Indigo Film and Rai Cinema, the film drew its visual style from Buzzati's own illustrations. It premiered in the Un Certain Regard section at the 2019 Cannes Film Festival and was released in France by Pathé on 9 October 2019 and in Italy by BIM Distribuzione on 7 November 2019. Critics acclaimed it, giving it a 100% Rotten Tomatoes rating; Variety's Jay Weissberg called its bold, colorful hand-drawn style classic animation at its best, though he found the pace hurried and the ending's message open to unfortunate readings.

overview: A family of four fractures under the weight of unmet expectations, unexpected tragedy, and uncompromising pride.
title: A Sun
plot:
A Sun (Chinese: 陽光普照) is a 2019 Taiwanese drama film directed by Chung Mong-hong, who co-wrote it with Chang Yao-sheng. Chen Yi-wen and Samantha Ko star as the parents of two very different sons, played by Wu Chien-ho and Greg Hsu, with Liu Kuan-ting as a dangerous friend. Exploring juvenile delinquency, suicide and the pressures placed on children, the film also reflects socioeconomic inequality in Taiwan.

In Taipei in 2013, the teenage Chen Jian-ho, known as A-Ho, accompanies his friend Radish to confront a young man in a restaurant, where Radish suddenly cuts off the victim's hand with a machete. A-Ho is sentenced to juvenile detention, while Radish receives a longer term. Their father, A-Wen, a driving instructor whose motto is "Seize the day, decide your path," effectively disowns his younger son and focuses all his hopes on A-Hao, the gentle and studious elder son preparing for medical school. Their mother, Qin, continues to visit A-Ho, and soon learns that A-Ho's fifteen-year-old girlfriend, Yu, is pregnant with his child. Meanwhile the victim's father harasses A-Wen for compensation.

The family is shattered when A-Hao, outwardly the perfect son, takes his own life. A girl he was close to later tells Qin that he felt overwhelmed by the constant attention and had nowhere to hide from it. After his release, A-Ho marries Yu and works at a car wash to support his family while A-Wen continues to ignore him, though father and son begin to reconcile after a quiet late-night conversation about A-Hao.

Years later, Radish is released and begins pulling A-Ho back into crime, coercing him into firing a gun at a politician's office and later into helping with a mysterious delivery. When A-Wen's offer of money to stay away from his son is refused, Radish disappears, and his associates abduct and beat A-Ho. A-Wen later confesses to Qin that he had been following the pair and killed Radish himself, believing it was the only way to protect his one remaining son. Afterward, Qin and A-Ho find the notebooks A-Wen once gave A-Hao, inscribed with his motto and left blank, and mother and son ride a bicycle together through a sunlit park.

A Sun premiered at the 2019 Toronto International Film Festival and was widely acclaimed. It won Best Feature Film and Best Director at the Golden Horse Awards, and as Taiwan's Oscar submission it made the shortlist.

overview: Chris, a wealthy divorcee, lives in a high-tech house of his own design in Montana. His life changes when he meets Sky, a mysterious young woman who draws him out of his shell and moves in after Chris is injured.
tagline: She'll love him to death.
title: Shattered
plot:
Shattered is a 2022 American psychological thriller directed by Luis Prieto and written by David Loughery. Cameron Monaghan stars as Chris, a wealthy, recently separated tech entrepreneur, with Lilly Krug as Sky, the young woman who enters his life, Frank Grillo, Sasha Luss as Chris's estranged wife Jamie, and John Malkovich as Ronald, a motel landlord. It was released in January 2022.

Chris, who made his fortune creating Watchdog, a home security system, lives alone in his isolated, high-tech mansion and has been putting off signing the divorce papers sent by his wife, Jamie, who felt that his work always came first. During a late-night trip to a grocery store he meets Sky, and when her ride is canceled he offers to drive her home. At the run-down motel where she is staying, she hesitates to go inside, explaining that her roommate, Lisa, is unpredictable because of her drug use. Chris invites her back to his house to wait, they spend the night together, and she returns to the motel in the morning to find Lisa furious.

Soon after, Chris visits Sky at her workplace and, returning to his car, interrupts someone trying to break into it. In the ensuing struggle he is badly injured and left with a broken leg in a cast. With his mobility limited, Sky offers to look after him, and he gives her the access codes to his house, which is entirely controlled by Watchdog. When Sky goes back to the motel to collect her belongings, Lisa hints that she knows things about her and that Sky cannot simply leave. The motel's landlord, Ronald, fed up with excuses about overdue rent, lets himself into their rooms and makes a horrifying discovery. As Sky settles into Chris's home, her behavior grows increasingly sinister, and Chris, trapped by his injury inside his own fortress, gradually realizes that the woman caring for him has a hidden agenda involving his money, his security system and his estranged family.

Shattered received negative reviews, holding a 19 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 27. Angela Dawson of Forbes was more positive, describing it as a simmering thriller reminiscent of classic femme fatale films with a modern sensibility, while most critics found it derivative and implausible.

overview: The young wizard Marek is forced to lead her band of would-be heroes on a mission for the corrupt Thieves Guild, which has taken her friend hostage. Their journey will take them straight into the wicked clutches of Szorlok, their greatest enemy.
title: Mythica: The Necromancer
plot:
Mythica: The Necromancer is an action-adventure fantasy film that delves into the realms of magic, power, and self-discovery. At its core, the movie explores the theme of identity and the struggle to find one's place in a world where ancient powers and modern society coexist.

The story follows Eira, a young woman with a mysterious past, as she navigates her newfound abilities as a necromancer. As she delves deeper into the world of magic, Eira must confront the darkness within herself and the consequences of wielding such immense power. The film masterfully weaves together elements of mythology, folklore, and fantasy to create a rich tapestry of themes that resonate with audiences.

One of the primary concerns of Mythica: The Necromancer is the corrupting influence of power. Eira's journey serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of humility in the face of great power. As she grapples with her newfound abilities, Eira must confront the temptation to use her powers for personal gain or to dominate others.

The film also explores the theme of belonging and finding one's place in the world. Eira's struggles to understand her past and her connection to the magical realm serve as a metaphor for the human experience of searching for identity and purpose. Through Eira's journey, the movie highlights the importance of embracing one's uniqueness and finding a sense of community and acceptance.

Furthermore, Mythica: The Necromancer touches on the theme of redemption and personal growth. As Eira navigates the complexities of her powers and her past, she is forced to confront the darkness within herself and make amends for past mistakes. This narrative thread serves as a powerful reminder that individuals have the capacity for change and growth, and that it's never too late to seek forgiveness and redemption.

Overall, Mythica: The Necromancer is a captivating tale of self-discovery, power, and redemption, set against a richly imagined world of magic and mythology.

overview: The attempted assassination of the American president is told and re-told from several different perspectives.
tagline: 8 Strangers. 8 points of view.  1 Truth.
title: Vantage Point
plot:
Vantage Point is a 2008 thriller film directed by Pete Travis, starring Dennis Quaid, Forest Whitaker, and Sigourney Weaver.

The movie's central theme revolves around the concept of perspective and how it can shape our understanding of reality. The story follows a series of events that unfold from multiple viewpoints, showcasing different characters' experiences on the same day. This narrative structure allows the audience to piece together the puzzle alongside the protagonist, creating a sense of tension and suspense.

As the film progresses, it becomes clear that the main character's perception of the world is not always accurate, and that his understanding is influenced by his own biases and limitations. The movie highlights how our individual perspectives can be skewed by personal experiences, emotions, and motivations, leading to a distorted view of reality.

The film also explores the theme of fate versus free will, leaving the audience questioning whether the events that unfold are predetermined or if they can be changed through human action. This philosophical debate adds depth to the narrative, making it more thought-provoking and engaging.

Furthermore, Vantage Point touches on the idea of isolation and disconnection in a world where people are increasingly disconnected from one another. The characters' experiences serve as a commentary on how our individual lives can become isolated, even when we're surrounded by others.

Overall, Vantage Point is a gripping thriller that masterfully weaves together multiple storylines, exploring themes of perspective, fate, and human connection in a thought-provoking and suspenseful narrative.

overview: Expecting the usual tedium that accompanies a summer in the Catskills with her family, 17-year-old Frances 'Baby' Houseman is surprised to find herself stepping into the shoes of a professional hoofer—and unexpectedly falling in love.
tagline: Have the time of your life.
title: Dirty Dancing
plot:
Dirty Dancing is a classic romantic drama film released in 1987, directed by Emile Ardolino and produced by Elizabeth A. Kaye, Linda Gottfried, and Jerry Bruckheimer.

The story takes place in the summer of 1963 at Kellerman's, a resort in the Catskill Mountains, New York. Frances "Baby" Houseman (played by Jennifer Grey), a sheltered young woman from a wealthy family, falls in love with dance instructor Johnny Castle (played by Patrick Swayze) and his partner, Penny Johnson (played by Cynthia Rhodes).

Baby, who has grown up watching her father's old dance records, is drawn to the resort's working-class staff and their passion for dance. She begins to sneak into the staff quarters to watch them practice and eventually meets Johnny, a charismatic and talented dancer who teaches her how to dance.

As Baby spends more time with Johnny and Penny, she learns about their struggles and the harsh realities of life at Kellerman's. The resort is run by the strict and uptight manager, Max Kellerman (played by Jerry Orbach), who disapproves of the staff's dancing and considers it to be "dirty" or "unrefined."

Baby and Johnny develop a romance, but their social differences and the fact that Penny is pregnant pose obstacles to their relationship. Baby also learns about the tragic circumstances surrounding Penny's pregnancy and her decision to give up her baby for adoption.

As the summer progresses, Baby and Johnny's relationship deepens, and they perform a memorable dance routine at the resort's annual summer ball. However, their love is threatened when Max discovers that Penny is pregnant and orders Johnny to leave Kellerman's with her.

In a dramatic turn of events, Baby decides to take matters into her own hands and convinces Johnny to stay with Penny and raise their child together. The film ends with Baby and Johnny performing a romantic dance at the resort's closing night, surrounded by the staff and guests who have come to accept them.

Throughout the film, the director Emile Ardolino uses the setting of Kellerman's as a metaphor for social class divisions and the struggle for identity. The film's iconic soundtrack, featuring hits like "(I've Had) The Time of My Life" and "Hungry Eyes," adds to the movie's nostalgic charm.

Overall, Dirty Dancing is a timeless romance that explores themes of love, social class, and self-discovery in a beautiful and memorable way.

overview: Playing around while aboard a cruise ship, the Chipmunks and Chipettes accidentally go overboard and end up marooned in a tropical paradise. They discover their new turf is not as deserted as it seems.
tagline: Sun, Sea and Squeaks.
title: Alvin and the Chipmunks: Chipwrecked
plot:
Alvin and the Chipmunks: Chipwrecked is a 2011 American musical comedy film directed by Mike Mitchell. The movie is the third installment in the Alvin and the Chipmunks film series, following The Squeakquel (2009) and Alvin and the Chipmunks (2007).

The story begins with Alvin, Simon, and Theodore, the three main chipmunk characters, preparing for their Christmas concert tour. However, things take a turn when they are invited to perform at a luxurious cruise ship called the "Sea-Dog." The ship is owned by Dave Seville's (Jason Lee) friend, Ian Hawke (David Cross), who has recently become wealthy.

Upon arrival, the chipmunks meet their new friends, including Brittany and Jeanette, two human girls who are also on the cruise. However, things quickly take a turn for the worse when the ship is attacked by a group of pirates led by the infamous Captain Sykes (Jedward). The pirates steal the ship's treasure, which includes a valuable diamond necklace.

The chipmunks and their new friends must work together to outsmart the pirates and retrieve the stolen treasure. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous sea routes, wild animals, and even a rival group of singing chipmunks led by the villainous Alby (Zachary Gordon).

As the story unfolds, the characters learn valuable lessons about teamwork, friendship, and believing in themselves. The movie features a range of catchy musical numbers, including "The Chipmunk Song (Christmas Don't Be Late)," "I'm Right Here," and "We Can Make It Happen."

In the end, the chipmunks and their friends successfully defeat the pirates and recover the stolen treasure. The movie concludes with a heartwarming performance by the chipmunks at the Sea-Dog's Christmas concert, which is attended by a large audience of fans.

Overall, Alvin and the Chipmunks: Chipwrecked is a fun and entertaining film that combines music, adventure, and humor. While it may not be as memorable as some of its predecessors, it remains a enjoyable addition to the franchise.

overview: Two childhood friends are recruited for a suicide bombing in Tel Aviv.
tagline: From the most unexpected place, come a  new call for peace
title: Paradise Now
plot:
Paradise Now is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that delves into the complexities of terrorism, faith, and the human condition. The movie follows two young Palestinian men, Said and Khaled, who are recruited to carry out a suicide bombing in Israel.

At its core, Paradise Now explores the themes of identity, belonging, and the search for meaning in a world torn apart by conflict and extremism. Through the characters' struggles with their faith and their desire to do good, the film raises questions about the nature of terrorism and whether it can ever be justified as a means to an end.

The movie also delves into the psychological effects of violence on individuals and society, highlighting the ways in which trauma and fear can shape people's perceptions of themselves and the world around them. As Said and Khaled grapple with their own demons, they begin to question the true nature of their mission and the motivations of those who sent them.

Ultimately, Paradise Now is a powerful exploration of the human cost of violence and the search for redemption in a world marked by conflict and uncertainty. The film's nuanced portrayal of complex characters and its thought-provoking themes make it a haunting and unforgettable viewing experience.

overview: A group of archaeology students awaken an ancient mummy. After being trapped in a time loop, the only way they can escape, is to defeat the mummy. As the body count rises, it seems the Mummy has to collect the souls of those who woke him to be able to walk the earth - for good.
tagline: Evil has been unearthed.
title: Rise of the Mummy
plot:
Rise of the Mummy, also known as Mummy Resurgence, is a 2021 British low-budget horror film directed by Antonia Johnstone from a screenplay by Shannon Holiday. A sequel to The Mummy Reborn (2019), it was made by Jagged Edge Productions, one of the companies of the prolific producer Scott Jeffrey, and stars Abi Casson Thompson, Megan Purvis, Stephanie Lodge, Amanda-Jade Tyler, Arthur Boan, Mya Brown, Barbara Dabson and Johnstone herself. Johnstone, who had previously appeared as an actress in the producer's The Leprechaun's Game, also handled make-up and costumes. The film was released on video on demand in the United States in early 2021, followed by a British release on 3 April 2021, and runs about 90 minutes.

A prologue shows a group of people being chased through a forest by the mummy before performing a ritual that stops the creature and the "time loop" its awakening has created; the soldiers involved kill everyone connected with the incident. Some months later the British military hands the now dormant mummy to a university, where a group of archaeology students and their lecturer study it and learn about mummification and the creature's mysterious origins. When someone tries to steal the mummy's necklace, it rises again and begins stalking and killing those trapped inside the building. Its victims return as possessed servants who hunt down the survivors, and no one can escape, because time has frozen and anyone leaving one room finds themselves back where they started. The mummy needs to collect the souls of those who woke it in order to walk the earth for good, but the heroine discovers that it has only 24 hours to do so, and the survivors must stay alive until sunrise.

Phil Wheat of Nerdly found that the camp humour of the first film had been toned down in favour of a more traditional British mummy picture, but felt the film ended with a whimper as the survivors simply run out the clock, while leaving room for a third instalment. Don Anelli of Don's World of Horror and Exploitation called it enjoyable if flawed, praising the time-loop conceit, the practical, jerky-moving mummy and the creepy possessed followers, but finding the first half, dominated by classroom lessons on mummification, sluggish. One commenter also noted that the supposed university was evidently filmed in a secondary school.

overview: A young boy finds himself pursued by two assassins in the Montana wilderness, with a survival expert determined to protect him, and a forest fire threatening to consume them all.
tagline: Nature finds a way.
title: Those Who Wish Me Dead
plot:
Those Who Wish Me Dead is a 2021 American thriller film directed by Taylor Sheridan and starring Angelina Jolie, Aidan Gillen, and Nicholas Hoult. The movie follows the story of Hannah Faber, a smokejumper who lives off the grid with her son, Connor.

The plot begins with Hannah's life being turned upside down when she is forced to leave her isolated home in Montana after her estranged husband, Connor's father, dies under mysterious circumstances. As they try to rebuild their lives, they are pursued by a group of ruthless mercenaries who will stop at nothing to get what they want.

The mercenaries, led by the cunning and deadly Victor (Aidan Gillen), have been hired by a wealthy client to capture Hannah and her son. The stakes are raised when Connor is kidnapped, and Hannah must use her skills as a smokejumper to track down the kidnappers and rescue her son.

As Hannah navigates the treacherous terrain of the Montana wilderness, she faces numerous challenges, including harsh weather conditions, treacherous terrain, and the mercenaries who will stop at nothing to capture her. Along the way, she meets Matt (Nicholas Hoult), a young boy who has also been kidnapped by the mercenaries.

As Hannah and Matt form an unlikely bond, they work together to evade their captors and find a way to escape. Meanwhile, Victor's true intentions are revealed, and Hannah must confront her own demons in order to save herself and her son.

Throughout the movie, Sheridan explores themes of motherhood, survival, and redemption. Hannah is a complex character who has been forced to grow up too quickly due to her circumstances. Her relationship with Connor is particularly poignant, as she struggles to balance her desire to protect him with her need for independence.

The action sequences in the film are intense and suspenseful, with Sheridan using the stunning natural beauty of Montana to create a sense of unease and tension. The cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the vast expanses of wilderness and the tiny moments of intimacy between Hannah and Connor.

Ultimately, Those Who Wish Me Dead is a gripping thriller that explores the complexities of human relationships and the resilience of the human spirit. With its stunning visuals, pulse-pounding action sequences, and powerful performances from its cast, this movie is sure to keep audiences on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: A widowed new dad copes with doubts, fears, heartache and dirty diapers as he sets out to raise his daughter on his own. Inspired by a true story.
tagline: In it, together.
title: Fatherhood
plot:
Fatherhood is a 2021 American comedy-drama film directed by Paul Weitz, who wrote the screenplay with Dana Stevens, based on Matthew Logelin's 2011 memoir Two Kisses for Maddy: A Memoir of Loss and Love. Kevin Hart stars as a young widower raising his daughter alone, with Alfre Woodard, Frankie Faison, Lil Rel Howery, DeWanda Wise, Anthony Carrigan, Melody Hurd and Paul Reiser. Originally intended for theatrical release by Sony Pictures, it was sold to Netflix during the COVID-19 pandemic and released on June 18, 2021.

Matt Logelin and his wife, Liz, childhood sweethearts, eagerly prepare for the birth of their first child. Just after their daughter, Maddy, is born, Liz suffers a pulmonary embolism and dies. Devastated, Matt resolves to raise Maddy on his own, despite the doubts of friends and family. Liz's mother, Marion, with whom he has a strained relationship, is the most concerned. When Matt turns down her offer to stay for months to help, and refuses to move back to Minnesota where both families live, she warns him that Maddy will need family and female role models.

Matt struggles at first to balance his grief, a demanding full-time job and the endless demands of an infant, while facing condescension from people who assume a father cannot be the primary parent. With help from friends and other parents, he finds his footing. Years later, Maddy is a confident, tomboyish schoolgirl. Matt is set up with a woman, played by Wise, whose name echoes his late wife's, and they begin dating. Maddy soon grows fond of her, but when Maddy is hurt at school and Matt misses the calls because he is with her, he blames himself and ends the relationship, upsetting his daughter.

On a trip to Minnesota for Marion's birthday, Maddy delights in staying in her mother's childhood room and learning about Liz, and asks to remain with her grandparents. Convinced that he has failed to understand what she needs, Matt reluctantly leaves her there. Back at work, on the verge of a promotion and about to leave on a business trip abroad, he is overwhelmed by thoughts of his daughter and returns to Minnesota. He reconciles with Maddy and, with Marion's blessing, brings her home, where he also rekindles his romance.

Fatherhood received mixed reviews. Rotten Tomatoes reported 67% approval, its consensus crediting the strong cast with giving the fact-based story real emotional resonance, and Metacritic gave it a score of 53.

original_title: Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story
overview: Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story is a movie based on the life story of world-renowned neurosurgeon Ben Carson from 1961 to 1987.
title: Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story
plot:
Gifted Hands: The Ben Carson Story is a 2009 American biographical television film directed by Thomas Carter and written by John Pielmeier, based on the 1990 autobiography of the neurosurgeon Ben Carson, written with Cecil Murphey. Cuba Gooding Jr. stars as Carson, with Kimberly Elise as his mother, Sonya, and Aunjanue Ellis as his wife, Candy. Presented as a Johnson & Johnson Spotlight Presentation, it premiered on TNT on February 7, 2009.

In 1987, Dr. Ben Carson, director of pediatric neurosurgery at Johns Hopkins Hospital, travels to Ulm, West Germany, to meet Peter and Augusta Rausch, whose twin baby boys are joined at the back of the head. He believes the boys could be separated, but warns that the operation risks the lives of one or both. As Carson spends months searching for a way to perform the surgery, the film turns back to his childhood.

In Detroit in 1961, ten-year-old Ben is failing at school and taunted by classmates. His mother, Sonya, a single parent with only a third-grade education, refuses to let her sons fail. She makes Ben and his older brother, Curtis, learn their multiplication tables, limits them to two television programs a week, and requires them to read library books and write reports on them, concealing from the boys that she herself cannot read. Ben discovers a love of books, and within a year he rises from the bottom of his class to the top. As a teenager, however, he struggles with a violent temper, until an incident in which he nearly stabs a friend, whose belt buckle stops the blade. Horrified, Ben prays for forgiveness and finds in his faith the strength to master his anger.

Ben earns a scholarship to Yale University, where he meets his future wife, Candy, and goes on to study medicine. As a neurosurgery resident at Johns Hopkins, he risks his career by operating without supervision to save a dying patient and is rewarded with promotion. In 1985, while Candy suffers the loss of twins in a miscarriage, he performs a hemispherectomy on a young girl suffering from constant seizures, removing half of her brain, and her recovery brings him to public attention.

Back in Germany, Carson finally devises a plan and leads a team through a twenty-two-hour operation that successfully separates the twins, saving both boys' lives, and he faces the press afterward. Gooding was nominated for the Screen Actors Guild Award for his performance, and Carter for a Directors Guild of America Award for his direction.

overview: Danny Krueger is a twenty-year old drag racer who plays by his own rules. After winning a scholarship to the prestigious Fast Lane Racing Academy, Danny finds himself competing against some of the fiercest young drivers in the world. Tension soars on and off the track, and a terrible incident leaves Danny without a racing partner. Facing dismissal from the academy, Danny is forced to team up with an old rival. The pair must learn to set aside their differences as they vie for rookie spots on a professional racing team.
tagline: Survival of the fastest
title: Born to Race: Fast Track
plot:
Born to Be Wild is not a match for the title "Born to Race: Fast Track" and release date "2014". However, I found that the movie "Born to Be Wild" was released in 2007.

However, I did find information on "Born to Be Raced" (not "Fast Track") which is a 2008 film. But it seems like you are referring to "Born to Race: Fast Track", but I couldn't verify any information about this movie.

However, I found that the movie "Born in East L.A." was released in 2022 and produced by American Cinema International, however, I also found another movie titled "Born to Be Raced" (2008) which is a family drama film directed by Chris Corbett.

overview: Minnesota, 1990. Detective Bruce Kenner investigates the case of young Angela, who accuses her father, John Gray, of an unspeakable crime. When John unexpectedly and without recollection admits guilt, renowned psychologist Dr. Raines is brought in to help him relive his memories and what they discover unmasks a horrifying nationwide mystery.
tagline: Fear always finds its victim
title: Regression
plot:
Regression is a 2015 psychological thriller film directed by James Marsh, starring Colin Firth, Anne Hathaway, and Jeremy Irvine.

The main themes of Regression revolve around the complexities of human psychology, trauma, and the unreliability of memory. The story follows a detective, Cathal (Colin Firth), who is tasked with investigating a series of child abductions in Ireland. As he delves deeper into the case, he becomes obsessed with uncovering the truth behind one particular abduction, which leads him to re-examine his own past and confront his own dark memories.

One of the primary themes of Regression is the exploration of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Cathal's investigation is motivated by a personal connection to the abducted child, and as he digs deeper, he uncovers disturbing secrets about his own past that have been repressed or hidden from him. The film suggests that traumatic experiences can shape our perceptions of reality and lead us down a path of self-destruction.

Another significant theme in Regression is the concept of memory and its fragility. As Cathal's investigation unfolds, it becomes clear that memories are not always reliable or trustworthy. The film blurs the lines between truth and fiction, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is imagined. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Tanya (Anne Hathaway), who is struggling to come to terms with her own traumatic experiences.

The film also explores the idea of obsession and its destructive power. Cathal's fixation on uncovering the truth behind the abduction leads him down a dark path, causing him to lose sight of reality and his relationships with others. This theme serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of becoming too consumed by our own obsessions.

Finally, Regression touches on the theme of redemption and the possibility of healing. As Cathal confronts his past and works to uncover the truth, he begins to find a sense of closure and redemption. The film suggests that it may be possible to overcome traumatic experiences and find a way forward, even if the wounds are deep-seated.

Overall, Regression is a complex and thought-provoking film that explores the darker aspects of human psychology and the power of trauma to shape our lives.

overview: Four talented alien musicians are kidnapped by a record producer who disguises them as humans. Shep, a space pilot in love with bass player Stella, follows them to Earth. Reprogrammed to forget their real identities and renamed The Crescendolls, the group quickly becomes a huge success playing soulless corporate pop. At a concert, Shep manages to free all the musicians except Stella, and the band sets out to rediscover who they really are -- and to rescue Stella.
tagline: The animated House musical.
title: Interstella 5555
plot:
Interstella 5555: The 5tory of the 5ecret 5tar 5ystem is a 2003 Japanese-French animated musical science fiction film produced by Toei Animation and directed by Kazuhisa Takenouchi under the supervision of Leiji Matsumoto. It was written by the French electronic duo Daft Punk, Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, with Cédric Hervet. Conceived as a visual companion to Daft Punk's second album, Discovery, it has no dialogue and is set entirely to the album's tracks.

On a distant planet inhabited by blue-skinned humanoids, a four-piece band made up of keyboardist Octave, guitarist Arpegius, drummer Baryl and bassist Stella plays a joyful concert to a packed stadium. An armed force from Earth invades the venue and abducts the musicians. Shep, a young space pilot who idolises Stella, receives a distress call and pursues the kidnappers' ship through a wormhole, crash-landing on Earth.

On Earth, the band is taken to an underground facility where their memories are extracted onto discs, replaced with false ones, and their skin is altered so that they look human. Fitted with mind-controlling sunglasses, they are relaunched by their captor, the sinister manager Earl de Darkwood, as a pop group called the Crescendolls, and quickly become huge stars while being worked to exhaustion.

Shep tracks them down and bursts into a concert with a jetpack, using a ray to free three of the members from mind control; Stella remains under Darkwood's power, and Shep is fatally wounded during the escape. Stella is later rescued at an awards ceremony where the Crescendolls win a coveted Gold Record. Before dying, Shep reveals the band's true identity and his love for Stella, and his comrades bury him.

Using a card that Stella had taken, the band reaches Darkwood's mansion and discovers his journal: he has been kidnapping musicians from other worlds to amass 5,555 Gold Records, which will grant him power over the universe. Captured during a ritual in which Darkwood plans to sacrifice Stella, the band fights back, and the final record is thrown into a lava pit, with Darkwood plunging after it. The musicians recover their memories with the help of Earth's authorities, and they return home through the wormhole, aided by Shep's spirit, to a triumphant welcome. The ending suggests that the whole story may have been the dream of a young Daft Punk fan.

It has 80% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and the BBC awarded it four stars.

overview: Thirteen-year-old Kayla endures the tidal wave of contemporary suburban adolescence as she makes her way through the last week of middle school — the end of her thus far disastrous eighth grade year — before she begins high school.
tagline: Based on the most awkward year of your life
title: Eighth Grade
plot:
Eighth Grade is a 2018 American coming-of-age comedy-drama film directed by Bo Burnham. The movie was produced by Scott Rudin Productions, but I couldn't find any information on it being released under that production company.

The main themes of Eighth Grade revolve around the struggles and challenges faced by eighth-grade students during this pivotal stage in their lives. Some of the key themes include:

1. Social anxiety and self-doubt: The protagonist, Kayla, struggles with feelings of inadequacy and insecurity as she navigates her relationships with peers and tries to find her place in the world.
2. Body image and self-acceptance: Kayla grapples with body image issues and societal expectations around beauty, leading to a deeper exploration of self-acceptance and individuality.
3. Friendship and loyalty: The film highlights the complexities of friendships during adolescence, particularly when it comes to navigating social hierarchies and cliques.
4. Identity formation: As Kayla approaches the end of eighth grade, she begins to question her interests, values, and sense of self, leading to a journey of self-discovery.

The movie features a nuanced portrayal of adolescent struggles, tackling topics like online harassment, peer pressure, and the challenges of growing up in a rapidly changing world.

overview: Adèle's life is changed when she meets Emma, a young woman with blue hair, who will allow her to discover desire, to assert herself as a woman and as an adult. In front of others, Adele grows, seeks herself, loses herself, finds herself.
title: Blue Is the Warmest Color
plot:
Blue Is the Warmest Color is a poignant and introspective coming-of-age drama that explores the complexities of first love, identity, and vulnerability. The film delves into the tumultuous relationship between Adèle, a shy and introverted teenager, and Emma, an older woman who becomes her lover.

At its core, Blue Is the Warmest Color is a nuanced portrayal of adolescent desire, self-discovery, and the struggle to reconcile one's emotions with societal expectations. The film masterfully captures the intensity and uncertainty of Adèle's first experiences with love, as she navigates the blurred lines between passion, intimacy, and identity.

Through Adèle's journey, the film sheds light on the fragility of young hearts, the weight of unrequited love, and the resilience of the human spirit. The movie also explores themes of vulnerability, consent, and the complexities of adult relationships, raising important questions about the nature of desire, intimacy, and the passage from adolescence to adulthood.

The film's title, Blue Is the Warmest Color, is a metaphor for the intensity and depth of Adèle's emotions, as well as the transformative power of love. The movie's use of vibrant colors and sensual imagery serves to underscore the beauty and complexity of human experience, inviting the viewer to immerse themselves in the world of its protagonist.

Ultimately, Blue Is the Warmest Color is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that celebrates the messy, beautiful, and often painful nature of love, identity, and self-discovery.

overview: Two romantically-engaged corporate spies team up to manipulate a corporate race to corner the market on a medical innovation that will reap huge profits and enable them to lead an extravagant lifestyle together.
tagline: Outwit. Outspy. Outsmart. Outplay. Then get out.
title: Duplicity
plot:
Duplicity is a 2009 romantic comedy-thriller film that explores the complexities of love, deception, and loyalty. The movie follows the story of two corporate spies, Claire Stenwick (Claire Danes) and Richard Greer (Tony Shalhoub), who engage in a cat-and-mouse game of espionage and seduction.

At its core, Duplicity is a film about the blurred lines between love and deception. The characters are expert manipulators, using their charm and wit to get what they want from each other. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that both Claire and Richard have ulterior motives for their actions, and that their true feelings for each other are tangled in a web of lies.

The film also explores the theme of identity and how people present themselves to others. Both Claire and Richard are skilled at hiding their true selves behind masks of confidence and sophistication. As they navigate their complicated relationship, they must confront the fact that their identities are not as fixed as they thought.

Furthermore, Duplicity touches on the idea of loyalty and commitment. The characters' actions are driven by a desire for security and stability, but this comes at a cost to their personal relationships and sense of self. As the story progresses, Claire and Richard must confront the consequences of their choices and decide what is truly important to them.

Overall, Duplicity is a film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the ways in which we present ourselves to others. It's a witty and engaging movie that keeps viewers guessing until the very end.

overview: A group of high school outcasts get revenge on the students that torment them.
tagline: This lesson can't be learned in the classroom.
title: The Final
plot:
The Final is a 2010 American independent psychological horror thriller film directed by Joey Stewart and written by Jason Kabolati. It stars Marc Donato, Jascha Washington, Justin S. Arnold, Lindsay Seidel, Julin, Laura Ashley Samuels, Ryan Hayden and Travis Tedford, and was released as part of the After Dark Horrorfest series.

A disfigured teenage girl walks into a diner, drawing stares from the customers, and begins to cry as the story unfolds in flashback. At a high school, a group of outcasts suffers relentless cruelty from the popular students: Ravi is bullied by Bradley and Bernard, Emily is tormented by Heather, Bridget and Kelli, and the quiet Dane, who has inherited a secluded house in the woods from his late uncle, is also a target. The only popular student who treats them decently is Kurtis, an aspiring actor who stands up to Bradley after the bullies break Ravi's camera at a video shoot.

Emily, Jack, Ravi, Andy and Dane decide to take revenge and send a message to their community, inspired by horror films and historical torture methods. They intend to spare Kurtis. They host a costume party at Dane's house, invite their tormentors and drug the punch, and the guests wake to find themselves chained together. The outcasts announce that rather than killing them, they will make them suffer a fate worse than death by disfiguring them so they will live with the scars for the rest of their lives.

The torture begins as Bernard is pierced with needles and Emily burns Heather's face with a corrosive compound. Bridget, forced to choose between mutilating Bradley and suffering herself, loses two fingers and half her face. Ravi, uneasy with the violence, secretly frees Kurtis and is stabbed to death by the increasingly unhinged Dane. Kurtis seeks help, but a deputy who comes to his aid is shot, and an elderly war veteran living nearby investigates alone, triggering a trap but killing two of the outcasts' accomplices. Dane paralyzes Bradley with a switchblade. Kurtis returns to the house, kills Andy and is wounded by Dane before Emily kills Dane. Emily then has Jack shoot her, and as police storm the house, Jack takes his own life after warning that there are more like them.

In the aftermath, news reports describe the torture of the popular students as an attack without reason, and the disfigured girl in the diner is revealed to be Bridget. The film received largely negative reviews, holding a 13% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from a small sample of critics.

overview: A mother fights to save her ailing daughter after a global pandemic worse than any seen before ravaged the planet, leaving resources so scarce you must pay for them with your life.
tagline: Are you ready to die?
title: The Deal
plot:
The Deal is a 2022 American dystopian science fiction thriller film directed by Orsi Nagypál. It was created by Sumalee Montano, who also co-produced it and plays one of the lead roles, and was made by Dean Devlin's Electric Entertainment together with actor-producer Lisa Brenner and LinLay Productions, with Balkanic Media also credited. Alongside Montano, the cast includes Emma Fischer, Alastair Mackenzie, Taz Skylar, Lisa Brenner and Pearl Mackie. The film, which runs about 91 minutes, was released in the autumn of 2022 as an exclusive on The Roku Channel; in Germany it was distributed as The Deal – Der verwüstete Planet.

The story is set in a future devastated by a global pandemic worse than any before it and by climate change, where overpopulation and global warming have left resources desperately scarce and food shortages afflict the survivors. A totalitarian government known as the Bureau has introduced the "Deal" as its answer to the crisis: anyone who accepts it by their twentieth birthday is guaranteed work, shelter and everything they need to survive, but only for twenty more years, after which they are put to death to make room for others. Tala Bayani (Montano), a mother who took the Deal, is approaching the end of her term before she has managed to secure the survival of her daughter Analyn (Fischer), who suffers from kidney disease. With her time running out, Tala begins to fight back against the regime to save her child, and the two women find themselves trapped and racing to find a way out.

In an interview with the magazine Positively Filipino, Montano said that she modelled Tala on her own Filipina mother, Linda Montano, and the sacrifices she made in raising her as a single parent; the article described the mother-daughter relationship as the emotional centre of the film, taking precedence over its computer-generated cityscapes. Reviewing it for Week99er, Becky found that the premise of a pandemic followed by food shortages felt uncomfortably close to contemporary reality, but said the film held the attention with an interesting story and a couple of unexpected twists, and was relieved that its ending was less dark than she had anticipated, though some threads were left open. The German film magazine Filmdienst was less impressed, judging that the film failed to exploit the dramatic potential of its premise and settled into a thriller plot rendered rather pale, partly because of its low budget.

overview: A young girl discovers an idealized parallel universe behind a secret door in her new home, unaware that it contains a sinister secret.
tagline: Be careful what you wish for.
title: Coraline
plot:
Coraline is a 2009 American stop-motion animated dark fantasy film written and directed by Henry Selick, based on Neil Gaiman's 2002 novella. Produced by Laika, it features the voices of Dakota Fanning as Coraline Jones, Teri Hatcher as her mother and the sinister Other Mother, Jennifer Saunders and Dawn French as the eccentric neighbors April Spink and Miriam Forcible, Keith David as the Cat, John Hodgman as Coraline's father and Ian McShane as Mr. Bobinsky. Gaiman invited Selick to adapt the story while he was finishing the book.

Eleven-year-old Coraline Jones moves with her busy, distracted parents from Michigan into the Pink Palace Apartments, an old house in Oregon divided into flats. Bored and neglected, she explores the house and meets Wybie, the landlady's grandson, who gives her a rag doll that looks just like her, and her eccentric neighbors, a former circus performer and two retired actresses who warn her of danger. She discovers a small door in the living room that is bricked up, but at night it opens onto a tunnel leading to an Other World.

There she finds a more colorful version of her own home, where her Other Mother and Other Father, identical to her parents but with buttons for eyes, shower her with delicious food, attention and wonders. The Other World seems perfect, until the Other Mother offers to let Coraline stay forever if she agrees to have buttons sewn into her eyes. Horrified, Coraline tries to return home but finds herself trapped, and she learns from the ghosts of three children that the Other Mother is an evil creature, the Beldam, who lured them in the same way and consumed their lives. When the Beldam kidnaps her real parents, Coraline must challenge her to a game to rescue them and free the souls of the ghost children.

The film is a story about the dangers of wishing for a perfect life and about courage and appreciating one's family, told through elaborate handmade sets and puppets.

Coraline was released by Focus Features on February 6, 2009, and grossed 126 million dollars on its initial release, later rising to about 188 million with re-releases. It received widespread acclaim, with 91 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, won three Annie Awards and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

overview: Twenty-two years after the events of Jurassic Park, Isla Nublar now features a fully functioning dinosaur theme park, Jurassic World, as originally envisioned by John Hammond.
tagline: The park is open.
title: Jurassic World
plot:
Jurassic World is a science fiction adventure film directed by Colin Trevorrow and written by Trevorrow and Derek Connolly. The movie takes place 22 years after the events of the original Jurassic Park.

The story begins with a prologue that shows a young Owen Grady (Chris Pratt), a Velociraptor trainer, visiting his mother's grave on Isla Nublar, where he had grown up. He is shown to be an expert in raptor behavior and has a deep connection with the animals.

In 2015, Simon Masrani (Irrfan Khan) buys the rights to Jurassic Park from John Hammond's estate and decides to reopen the park as a theme park called Jurassic World. The park's new CEO, Claire Dearing (Bryce Dallas Howard), is tasked with overseeing the park's operations and ensuring its success.

Claire arrives on Isla Nublar to meet with Owen Grady, who has been hired to train the park's Velociraptors. She also meets the park's founder, Simon Masrani, and his team of scientists and engineers. The park is now a fully functioning theme park, with attractions such as the Indominus Rex exhibit.

However, things take a turn for the worse when a power outage caused by a cyber attack allows the Indominus Rex to escape from its enclosure. The creature is a genetically engineered hybrid of a Tyrannosaurus rex and a Velociraptor, designed to be more intelligent and aggressive than its predecessors.

As the park descends into chaos, Claire and Owen team up with the park's operations manager, Vic Hoskins (Vincent D'Onofrio), to stop the Indominus Rex. Along the way, they encounter other characters, including a young girl named Zach Mitchell (Ty Simpkins) who is visiting the park with his parents.

The movie's plot development involves Claire and Owen trying to outsmart the Indominus Rex and prevent it from escaping the park. They also uncover a conspiracy involving Vic Hoskins, who has been secretly working with the park's investors to create a new theme park attraction that will make them rich.

As the story unfolds, Claire and Owen face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, malfunctioning park systems, and the Indominus Rex itself. The creature is a formidable foe, using its intelligence and strength to outmaneuver its pursuers.

In the end, Claire and Owen manage to defeat the Indominus Rex by using a combination of strategy and quick thinking. They also uncover the truth about Vic Hoskins' conspiracy and bring him to justice.

The movie concludes with Claire reflecting on the events that have transpired and realizing that she has grown as a person. She also begins to see the park in a new light, recognizing its potential for education and conservation rather than just entertainment.

Overall, Jurassic World is an action-packed adventure film that explores themes of science, technology, and responsibility. The movie features stunning visual effects, thrilling sequences, and memorable characters, making it a must-see for fans of the Jurassic Park franchise.

overview: The story of Michael Berg, a German lawyer who, as a teenager in the late 1950s, had an affair with an older woman, Hanna, who then disappeared only to resurface years later as one of the defendants in a war crimes trial stemming from her actions as a concentration camp guard late in the war. He alone realizes that Hanna is illiterate and may be concealing that fact at the expense of her freedom.
tagline: Behind the mystery lies a truth that will make you question everything you know.
title: The Reader
plot:
The Reader is a 2008 drama film directed by Stephen Daldry, based on the novel of the same name by Bernhard Schlink. The movie stars Kate Winslet, David Kross, and Ralph Fiennes.

The story takes place in post-war Germany in 1956. We meet our protagonist, Michael Berg (played by David Kross), a young man who is struggling to come to terms with his past. He was a teenager when he had an affair with an older woman, Hanna Schmitz (played by Kate Winslet), who was a former Nazi guard at a concentration camp.

The film begins with Michael's life in 1956, where he is working as a photographer and struggling to find meaning in his life. One day, while on a train ride, he meets Hanna again, now an older woman. They rekindle their past affair, which had ended abruptly when Michael was just a teenager.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Michael's teenage years, where he is introduced to Hanna, who is 36 at the time. Despite their age difference and her occupation as a Nazi guard, they begin an illicit affair. However, their relationship is cut short when Michael's parents discover them together, leading to a painful separation.

The present-day storyline follows Michael's reunion with Hanna, which sparks a series of events that force him to confront his past and the trauma he experienced during World War II. Through their conversations, we learn more about Hanna's experiences as a Nazi guard at Auschwitz, where she was responsible for sending thousands of people to their deaths.

As the story progresses, Michael becomes increasingly drawn into Hanna's world, which is marked by darkness and tragedy. He begins to see the world through her eyes, and his own moral compass is challenged. Through their conversations, we also learn more about Hanna's backstory, including how she became a Nazi guard and the trauma she experienced during the war.

The film's climax revolves around Michael's discovery of a dark secret from Hanna's past, which forces him to confront the reality of her actions as a Nazi guard. The revelation is both shocking and heartbreaking, and it ultimately leads to a tragic conclusion.

Throughout the film, Ralph Fiennes plays the role of Dr. Werner von Berg, a psychiatrist who becomes Michael's therapist. Through their sessions, we see Michael grapple with his feelings about Hanna and his past, as well as his own guilt and shame.

The Reader is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores themes of trauma, guilt, and redemption. The performances by Kate Winslet and David Kross are outstanding, and the direction by Stephen Daldry is masterful. The film's use of flashbacks and non-linear storytelling adds to its complexity and emotional impact.

Overall, The Reader is a haunting and thought-provoking film that will leave viewers moved and disturbed. It is a powerful exploration of the human condition, and it serves as a reminder of the devastating consequences of war and the importance of confronting our past.

overview: Cobb, a skilled thief who commits corporate espionage by infiltrating the subconscious of his targets is offered a chance to regain his old life as payment for a task considered to be impossible: "inception", the implantation of another person's idea into a target's subconscious.
tagline: Your mind is the scene of the crime.
title: Inception
plot:
Inception is a 2010 science fiction action film written, directed, and produced by Christopher Nolan. The movie follows Cobb, a skilled thief who specializes in entering people's dreams and stealing their secrets.

The story begins with Cobb (Leonardo DiCaprio), a former soldier who lost his wife, Mal (Marion Cotillard), in a tragic accident. Cobb is haunted by the guilt of not being able to save her and is unable to return to the United States to see his children due to a past mistake that led to her death.

Cobb is approached by a wealthy businessman named Saito (Ken Watanabe) who offers him a chance to redeem himself and clear his name. Saito wants Cobb to perform a task known as "inception" - planting an idea in someone's mind instead of stealing one. The target is Robert Fischer (Cillian Murphy), the son of a dying business magnate, who needs to be convinced to dissolve his father's company.

To accomplish this, Cobb assembles a team of experts: Arthur (Joseph Gordon-Levitt), a point man; Ariadne (Ellen Page), an architect who designs the dreamscapes; Eames (Tom Hardy), a forger who can impersonate people in the dreams; and Saito, who joins the team as a consultant.

The team plans to perform "inception" by entering Fischer's dreams and convincing him to break up his father's company. However, things become complicated when Cobb's subconscious, fueled by guilt and anger, begins to sabotage the mission. Mal appears in Cobb's dreams, causing tension among the team.

As the team navigates multiple levels of dreams within dreams, they face various obstacles and challenges. The dream world becomes increasingly unstable, and the team must work together to stay one step ahead of their projections and maintain control over the dream state.

The climax of the movie features a thrilling sequence where Cobb's team performs a complex "inception" on Fischer, planting an idea in his mind that ultimately leads to the dissolution of the company. However, just as they think they've succeeded, Cobb is forced to confront his own guilt and emotions, which threaten to destroy the entire operation.

In the end, Cobb returns to the United States to see his children, but not before he performs a final " extraction" from his subconscious, allowing him to move on from his past and find closure. The movie ends with Cobb reunited with his children, but the audience is left wondering whether he's truly in a dream state or if he's finally found peace.

Throughout the film, Nolan explores themes of reality, identity, and the power of the human mind. The movie's complex plot and multiple layers of dreams create a sense of tension and uncertainty, keeping the audience engaged until the very end.

overview: A hiker finds shelter in a mountain lodge inhabited by two strange women.
title: Megan
plot: A hiker finds shelter in a mountain lodge inhabited by two strange women.

overview: After his family is kidnapped during their sailing trip in Spain, a young Wall Street trader is confronted by the people responsible: intelligence agents looking to recover a mysterious briefcase.
tagline: Instinct is his greatest weapon.
title: The Cold Light of Day
plot:
The Cold Light of Day is an action-thriller film that revolves around the story of Harry Shaw, a former CIA operative who finds himself caught in the middle of a global conspiracy. 

At its core, the movie explores themes of loyalty, duty, and redemption. The protagonist's journey is driven by his desire to protect his family and uncover the truth about his past, which has been shrouded in secrecy for years.

The film also delves into the complexities of human relationships, particularly the bond between a father and son. As Harry navigates the treacherous landscape of espionage and counter-terrorism, he must confront his own demons and make difficult choices that test his moral compass.

Furthermore, The Cold Light of Day touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. Harry's experiences force him to re-evaluate his sense of purpose and belonging, leading him down a path of self-discovery and ultimately, redemption.

The movie's tense atmosphere and high-stakes action sequences serve as a backdrop for exploring these themes, creating a gripping narrative that keeps the audience on the edge of their seats.

overview: Once upon a time... in the far away kingdom of Dor... lived a brave and virtuous mouse with comically oversized ears who dreamt of becoming a knight. Banished from his home for having such lofty ambitions, Despereaux sets off on an amazing adventure with his good-hearted rat friend Roscuro, who leads him, at long last, on a very noble quest to rescue an endangered princess and save an entire kingdom from darkness.
tagline: Small Mouse. Big Dreams
title: The Tale of Despereaux
plot:
The Tale of Despereaux is a 2008 animated fantasy adventure comedy film loosely based on Kate DiCamillo's 2003 Newbery Medal-winning novel. Directed by Sam Fell and Robert Stevenhagen and written by Gary Ross from a story by Will McRobb and Chris Viscardi, it features the voices of Matthew Broderick as the title character, with Emma Watson, Dustin Hoffman, Tracey Ullman, Kevin Kline and Robbie Coltrane, and Sigourney Weaver as narrator. Universal Pictures released it on December 19, 2008.

The rat Roscuro and his sailor companion arrive in the kingdom of Dor, famous for its soups, on the annual Royal Soup Day. Roscuro accidentally falls into the queen's soup, and the shock kills her. The grieving king bans soup and outlaws rats, and Dor falls into a gray gloom; the royal chef, Andre, loses his magical companion, Boldo, a spirit made of vegetables, and Princess Pea mourns her mother. Abandoned by his sailor, Roscuro takes refuge in the dungeon below, ruled by the cruel rat leader Botticelli.

In a mouse community hidden in the castle, Despereaux Tilling is born with oversized ears and an unusual lack of fear. Rather than chewing books, he reads them. When he befriends Princess Pea, breaking mouse law by speaking to a human, his family turns him over to the mouse council, which banishes him to the dungeon. There he is thrown into the rats' arena with a cat, until Roscuro saves him by claiming him as food. The two become friends, as Despereaux tells him stories of the princess. When Roscuro tries to apologize to Pea for her mother's death and is rejected, he vows revenge and persuades Mig, a simple-minded servant girl who dreams of being a princess, to help him kidnap Pea, then betrays Mig and takes the princess to the rats.

Despereaux seeks help, but the king is too depressed to listen and the mice fear him as a ghost. Andre, inspired by the sound of the castle bell, defies the ban and begins making soup again, bringing back Boldo, who sacrifices himself to help Despereaux reach the arena. As the rats prepare to devour Pea, Roscuro realizes Pea is sorry for her harshness and regrets his betrayal. Sunlight breaking through the clouds blinds the rats, and Roscuro helps defeat Botticelli, who is cornered by the cat. The king lifts his bans, and Despereaux sets out to see the world.

The film received mixed reviews, with critics praising its striking visuals but finding its story familiar; Rotten Tomatoes reported 57% approval and Metacritic a score of 53.

overview: Minions Stuart, Kevin and Bob are recruited by Scarlet Overkill, a super-villain who, alongside her inventor husband Herb, hatches a plot to take over the world.
tagline: Before Gru, they had a history of bad bosses
title: Minions
plot:
Minions is a 2015 computer-animated comedy film produced by Illumination Entertainment and distributed by Universal Pictures. The movie follows the origin story of the Minions, small yellow creatures that have been serving various villains throughout history.

The film begins with the Minions living in an island paradise, where they spend their days playing and causing chaos. However, as the years go by, the island becomes uninhabitable due to pollution and overpopulation. The Minions are forced to leave their home and search for a new one.

During their journey, the Minions meet a young girl named Scarlet Overkill (voiced by Sandra Bullock), who is on a mission to find a powerful artifact known as the "Golden Ticket." The Minions become obsessed with the ticket and decide to help Scarlet achieve her goal. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles and villains, including a group of ruthless pirates.

As the story unfolds, we see the Minions' interactions with other famous movie characters, such as Gru (voiced by Steve Carell), a supervillain who becomes their leader. The Minions are initially drawn to Gru's lair due to his impressive collection of bananas, but they soon realize that he is not the villain they expected.

Throughout the film, we see flashbacks of the Minions' past adventures with various villains, including Napoleon (voiced by Pierre Coffin), a short-lived dictator who becomes their first leader. The Minions also encounter other famous movie characters, such as Vincent Price and Boris Karloff.

As the story progresses, Scarlet Overkill's true intentions are revealed: she plans to use the Golden Ticket to become the world's first female supervillain. However, her plan is foiled by Gru, who outsmarts her and claims the ticket for himself.

In the end, Gru adopts the Minions as his own and takes them on a new adventure with him. The film concludes with the Minions finding a new home in Gru's lair, surrounded by bananas and other treasures.

Throughout the movie, the Minions' antics and interactions with other characters provide plenty of comedic moments. The film's colorful animation and catchy soundtrack add to its charm, making it a fun and entertaining ride for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Minions is a heartwarming story about friendship and belonging, as the Minions find their place in the world with Gru by their side.

overview: While visiting his hometown during Christmas, a man comes face-to-face with his old high school crush whom he was best friends with – a woman whose rejection of him turned him into a ferocious womanizer.
tagline: He loves her. She loves him not.
title: Just Friends
plot:
Just Friends is a 2005 American Christmas romantic comedy directed by Roger Kumble from a screenplay by Adam "Tex" Davis. Ryan Reynolds stars as a former overweight teenager trying to escape the "friend zone" with his high school crush, played by Amy Smart, alongside Anna Faris, Chris Klein and Christopher Marquette. The film plays on the comedy of platonic relationships and was released in the United States on November 23, 2005, the day before Thanksgiving.

In 1995, overweight New Jersey high school senior Chris Brander is secretly in love with his best friend Jamie Palamino. He writes a confession of his feelings in her yearbook, but at a graduation party it falls into the hands of Jamie's ex-boyfriend, who reads it aloud to the crowd. Jamie kisses Chris on the cheek but tells him she sees him only as a friend. Humiliated, he leaves town, vowing to become more successful than everyone who mocked him.

Ten years later, Chris has lost the weight and become a handsome, womanising record executive in Los Angeles. Shortly before Christmas, his boss sends him to escort Samantha James, a self-absorbed and unstable pop singer, to Paris so that she will sign with their label; she is infatuated with Chris, who wants nothing to do with her. When Samantha accidentally sets their private jet on fire, the plane makes an emergency landing in New Jersey, near Chris's hometown.

Staying with his mother and his younger brother Mike, a devoted fan of Samantha, Chris runs into Jamie, now working as a bartender while studying to become a teacher, and his old feelings return. He schemes to win her by keeping Samantha occupied with Mike, but finds himself slipping back into the role of the dependable friend. On a skating outing he is injured during a hockey game and carted away by paramedics, one of whom is Dusty Dinkleman, a former nerdy classmate who also loved Jamie and is now a smooth-talking rival.

Convinced Dusty only wants to use Jamie to settle old scores, Chris attacks him in front of her, and a drunken argument at the bar ends with Chris insulting Jamie and being thrown out. Back in Los Angeles, after rebuffing Samantha once more, he realises that he truly loves Jamie. He returns to New Jersey, apologises, and confesses his feelings, and the two finally kiss.

Just Friends received mixed reviews, with 43% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and grossed about 51 million dollars worldwide.

overview: After 20 years abroad, Mark Renton returns to Scotland and reunites with his old friends Sick Boy, Spud and Begbie.
tagline: Face your past. Choose your future.
title: T2 Trainspotting
plot:
T2 Trainspotting is a 2017 British comedy-drama film directed by Danny Boyle, produced by Daniel Corbett, and written by John Hodge. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1996 film of the same name.

The main themes of T2 Trainspotting revolve around:

1. Redemption: The story follows Mark Renton (Ewan McGregor), who has left Scotland and is trying to rebuild his life in London. He must confront his past mistakes and make amends with those he hurt, including his former friends and family.

2. Friendship and loyalty: Despite the characters' troubled pasts, their bond remains strong. The film explores how these relationships have evolved over time and whether they can withstand the test of adulthood.

3. Addiction and recovery: The movie delves into the ongoing struggles with addiction that many of the characters face. Mark's journey is particularly poignant as he tries to overcome his dependence on heroin and find a new sense of purpose.

4. Class and social status: Trainspotting explores the complexities of Scotland's class system, particularly in Edinburgh's Leith district. The film highlights the stark contrasts between wealth and poverty, as well as the difficulties faced by those trying to escape their circumstances.

5. Identity and self-discovery: Mark Renton's character arc is a central theme, as he grapples with his own identity and tries to find a sense of belonging in the world. This journey is mirrored in the experiences of other characters, who are also searching for meaning and purpose.

The film features a talented ensemble cast, including Jonny Lee Miller, Robert Carlyle, and Ewen Bremner, all reprising their iconic roles from the original. T2 Trainspotting received widespread critical acclaim for its witty dialogue, engaging storyline, and outstanding performances.

overview: In high school, Schmidt was a dork and Jenko was the popular jock. After graduation, both of them joined the police force and ended up as partners riding bicycles in the city park. Since they are young and look like high school students, they are assigned to an undercover unit to infiltrate a drug ring that is supplying high school students synthetic drugs.
tagline: They thought the streets were mean. Then they went back to high school.
title: 21 Jump Street
plot: [No information found]

overview: American tourist Frank meets mysterious British woman Elsie on the train to Venice. Romance seems to bud, but there's more to her than meets the eye. Remake of the 2005 French film "Anthony Zimmer", written and directed by Jérôme Salle.
tagline: It all started when he met a woman.
title: The Tourist
plot:
The Tourist is a 2010 romantic thriller film directed by Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck and starring Angelina Jolie, Johnny Depp, and Paul Bettany.

The movie begins with Frank Taylor (Johnny Depp), a widowed father who travels to Venice, Italy for his daughter's wedding. He meets Elise Sellas (Angelina Jolie), a beautiful and charming woman who is also attending the wedding. The two strike up a conversation, and despite their initial awkwardness, they find themselves drawn to each other.

As Frank and Elise spend more time together, they begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their budding romance is complicated by the presence of Elise's husband, Alexander (Paul Bettany), who is revealed to be a ruthless and cunning man with a dark past.

Unbeknownst to Frank, Elise is being pursued by her ex-husband, who has been trying to kill her. As Frank gets closer to Elise, he becomes entangled in her life and begins to uncover the truth about her past. Meanwhile, Alexander's true intentions are revealed, and Frank finds himself in a desperate bid to protect Elise from harm.

As the story unfolds, Frank and Elise's relationship deepens, but they are also forced to confront their own personal demons. Frank is haunted by his wife's death, while Elise struggles with her complicated past and her feelings for Alexander.

The plot takes a dramatic turn when Frank discovers that Elise is in grave danger, and he must use all his wits and resourcefulness to protect her. In the process, he uncovers a web of deceit and betrayal that threatens to destroy everything he holds dear.

In the end, Frank and Elise's love for each other prevails, but not without great cost. The movie ends on a bittersweet note, with Frank and Elise parting ways, but forever changed by their experience together.

Throughout the film, the cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty of Venice and its canals. The performances from Depp and Jolie are also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to their characters. While some critics have panned the movie's plot as predictable, many have praised its atmospheric setting and the chemistry between the leads.

Overall, The Tourist is a romantic thriller that explores themes of love, loss, and redemption. With its stunning visuals and strong performances, it is a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: A psychiatrist's adulterous past continues to haunt her and her husband after they move to India.
title: Brownian Movement
plot:
Brownian Movement is a 2010 Dutch drama written and directed by Nanouk Leopold, a Dutch–German–Belgian co-production made by Serendipity Films, Circe Films and Coin Film with Bella Cohen Films and the broadcaster VPRO. It stars Sandra Hüller as Charlotte, a German doctor working in Brussels, and Dragan Bakema as her husband Max. The title alludes to Brownian motion, the seemingly random movement of particles suspended in a gas or liquid, though the film itself never explains it.

Charlotte appears to have a perfect life with Max, an attentive and handsome architect, and their young son Benjamin, to whom she reads the Brothers Grimm tale "The Girl Without Hands" at bedtime. Her marriage is affectionate and the couple's intimacy is warm and trusting. Yet she secretly rents a bare apartment where she meets men she picks from among her patients, most of them physically unprepossessing, for impulsive sexual encounters. When she unexpectedly runs into one of these men again and he tries to get close to her, she breaks down, attacks him and collapses.

Her affairs come to light, she is struck off the medical register and her marriage nearly falls apart.
