The story revolves around Carl Magnus Persson (played by Claes Bang), a successful food blogger who has built his career on promoting himself as a connoisseur of fine cuisine. He is accompanied by his girlfriend Yaya (played by Harris Dickinson), a model and social media influencer, on a yacht trip to the Caribbean.

During their voyage, they meet Diggie (played by Zlatko Burić), a Croatian chef who has been working as a cook for Carl's food blog. Diggie is an outcast among his peers due to his unusual appearance and behavior, but he has a unique talent for creating exquisite dishes.

As the three continue their journey, they come across a group of survivors from a plane crash on a deserted island. The survivors are led by Ruth (played by Charlotte Gainsbourg), a wealthy socialite who is accompanied by her boyfriend, Carl's former business partner, Anton (played by Gustaf Skarsgård).

The two groups eventually merge, and the yacht becomes a makeshift community where people from different backgrounds come together to share food, stories, and experiences. However, as time passes, tensions rise among the group members due to their vastly different social statuses, personalities, and values.

Carl, who initially sees himself as superior to the others, begins to realize that his privileged upbringing has made him oblivious to the struggles of those around him. He starts to question his own identity and sense of purpose, particularly when he is forced to confront the harsh realities of the world beyond his bubble.

As the story unfolds, Carl's relationships with Yaya, Diggie, Ruth, and Anton become increasingly complicated. The group faces various challenges, including a severe storm that threatens their survival, and Carl must confront his own privilege and biases in order to find a way out of the situation.

Throughout the film, Östlund uses satire to critique societal norms, class divisions, and the superficiality of social media culture. He also explores themes of identity, community, and the human condition, raising questions about what it means to be a part of something greater than oneself.

Ultimately, Carl's journey leads him to a profound realization about himself and his place in the world. The film ends with a sense of ambiguity, leaving the audience to ponder the implications of Carl's transformation and the future of the community that has formed on the yacht.

Overall, Triangle of Sadness is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that challenges viewers to confront their own biases and assumptions about social class, identity, and human connection.

belongs_to_collection.name: The Fast and the Furious Collection

overview: The tenth installment in the Fast Saga.
title: Fast X
plot:
Fast X, also known as Fast & Furious 10, is a 2023 American action film directed by Louis Leterrier from a screenplay by Dan Mazeau and Justin Lin, the sequel to F9 and the tenth main installment of the Fast & Furious franchise. Vin Diesel returns as Dominic Toretto, with Michelle Rodriguez, Tyrese Gibson, Chris "Ludacris" Bridges, John Cena, Nathalie Emmanuel, Sung Kang, Jason Statham and Charlize Theron, joined by Jason Momoa as the villain and Brie Larson. Leterrier replaced Lin as director early in production.

Dante Reyes, son of the drug lord Hernan Reyes, whom Dom's crew robbed in Rio de Janeiro years earlier, survived the heist that killed his father and has spent a decade plotting revenge. The wounded cyberterrorist Cipher arrives at Dom's door to warn that Dante is coming for his family. Dom's team has been sent on a supposed Agency mission to Rome, which turns out to be a trap set by Dante: the cargo they are stealing is a powerful bomb, which Dante sends rolling through the city. Dom manages to push it into the Tiber, limiting the destruction, but Letty is captured, and the Agency's new leader, Aimes, brands the team as terrorists and launches a manhunt.

Separated and hunted, the family scatters. Dom's brother, Jakob, takes Dom's young son, Little B, into hiding, while Tess, daughter of the missing Mr. Nobody, helps Dom track Dante. Dom confronts his enemy in a street race in Rio, while Roman, Tej, Han and Ramsey travel to London and enlist the help of their former foe Deckard Shaw. Letty, held in a secret Agency prison in Antarctica, forms an uneasy alliance with Cipher.

Dante steals the God's Eye surveillance program and abducts Little B in Portugal. Jakob sacrifices himself so that Dom can rescue his son, and Dante reveals that Aimes has been his accomplice, shooting down a plane carrying the rest of the crew. In a cliffhanger ending, Dom and Little B escape a trap by driving off a dam, only for Dante to blow it up around them, while in Antarctica, Gisele, long believed dead, arrives to rescue Letty and Cipher. A mid-credits scene shows Dante targeting Luke Hobbs.

Fast X premiered in Rome on May 12, 2023, and was released by Universal Pictures on May 19. Its budget of nearly $380 million made it one of the most expensive films ever made. Reviews were mixed, praising Momoa's flamboyant performance and the action but criticizing the writing, and it grossed $714 million worldwide, falling short of expectations.

overview: The true story of fraudulent Washington, D.C. journalist Stephen Glass, who rose to meteoric heights as a young writer in his 20s, becoming a staff writer at The New Republic for three years. Looking for a short cut to fame, Glass concocted sources, quotes and even entire stories, but his deception did not go unnoticed forever, and eventually, his world came crumbling down.
tagline: He'd do anything to get a great story.
title: Shattered Glass
plot:
Shattered Glass is a 2003 American biographical drama about the journalist Stephen Glass and the fabrication scandal that ended his career at The New Republic. Written and directed by Billy Ray in his feature debut, it is based on H. G. Bissinger's 1998 Vanity Fair article of the same name. Hayden Christensen stars as Glass, with Peter Sarsgaard, Chloë Sevigny, Steve Zahn, Rosario Dawson and Hank Azaria. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2003.

In 1998, Stephen Glass is the youngest associate editor at The New Republic. He is adored by his colleagues for his vivid, entertaining stories and his humble manner, and he meets any challenge to his facts with disarming apologies. When one of his pieces, about young conservatives behaving badly at a political conference, draws complaints, the magazine's editor Michael Kelly, to whom the staff is fiercely loyal, stands by him. After a dispute with the publisher, Kelly is fired and replaced by Charles Lane, a staff writer whom the others regard as cold and uninspiring.

Glass then publishes "Hack Heaven", an account of a teenage hacker who is hired by the software company whose systems he broke into. At Forbes Digital Tool, the reporter Adam Penenberg tries to follow up the story and can find no trace of the hacker, the company or any other detail. The phone number and website Glass supplies for the firm prove flimsy. During a conference call with the Forbes team, Glass's explanations unravel, and he claims that his sources must have deceived him.

At first Lane tries to protect his writer, but when he drives Glass to the building where the hackers' convention supposedly took place, he learns that it was closed on the day in question. Glass admits to embellishing, and Lane suspends him, to the resentment of the staff. Lane soon realises that Glass's own brother posed as the executive, and when he rereads Glass's earlier articles he finds that many of them were invented. He fires Glass and persuades the staff to examine his work, after which they rally behind their editor.

Closing titles explain that the magazine found 27 of Glass's 41 articles to be partly or wholly fabricated, that Glass later earned a law degree and wrote a novel based on his experience, and that Kelly was killed while reporting on the Iraq War. Though a commercial failure, the film was acclaimed by critics, with 92% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Tormented and left for dead by a scorned lover, a woman finds the strength within herself to recover and retaliate against her abuser.
tagline: Once his, always his.
title: Only Mine
plot:
Only Mine is a 2019 American thriller television film directed by Michael Civille, in his first credited feature, from a screenplay by Matt Young. Produced by MarVista Entertainment, a company best known for television movies, it stars Amber Midthunder as Julie Dillon and Brett Zimmerman as David Barragan, with Chris Browning, Claudia Ferri, Walter Fauntleroy as an out-of-town detective, Ashley Holliday as Julie's best friend Suzanne and Lorenzo James Henrie as her co-worker and friend. The film runs 87 minutes and is told partly in a true-crime style, with interviews of people who know the victim.

In the small town of Coldwater Hills, Julie is a well-liked student who works as a waitress at the local diner while she waits to leave for college. She is charmed by David, a young, dashing officer newly hired by the local police, and begins dating him, seeing the romance as a fun distraction until she moves on. David, however, takes the relationship far more seriously. Even on their first date he gives her a music box, and he soon becomes possessive, needlessly suspicious of her male co-worker and angry when she does not answer his calls, telling her that he always wants to be able to find her. As he turns from doting boyfriend into controlling ex and then dangerous stalker, Julie seeks help from the police, but to no avail: David's father was also an officer on the force and a friend of the chief, and David easily charms the townspeople, who trust him more than her. Isolated, she finds herself in a deadly game of cat and mouse, and after being tormented and left for dead by her scorned lover, she must summon the strength to recover and fight back against her abuser. The story also weaves Native American elements into its storytelling.

The film is loosely inspired by the case of Laura Kucera, a nineteen-year-old who was shot and left for dead by an ex-boyfriend in 1994. Only Mine premiered on Netflix in the United States and other countries on 15 January 2019 and returned to the platform's charts in 2021. Reviews were moderate. Heaven of Horror gave it three out of five, finding it realistic and well cast despite its Lifetime-style production, with a convincingly creepy Zimmerman. In The Independent, Clémence Michallon called it a lean, humble, clear-headed film that never romanticizes abuse and shows how it can begin with controlling behavior, praising Fauntleroy's performance, though she conceded that it is not great cinema.

overview: On an island off the coast of North America, local residents simultaneously fight a zombie epidemic while hoping for a cure to return their un-dead relatives back to their human state.
tagline: Death isn't what it used to be.
title: Survival of the Dead
plot:
Survival of the Dead is a 2009 Canadian zombie comedy film directed by Bruce McDonald, not 2010 and produced by Devolution Films, not Devonshire Productions. The movie follows the story of George, a fisherman who returns to his hometown after being away for many years, only to find it overrun by zombies.

The main themes of Survival of the Dead revolve around the idea of community and the importance of human connection in the face of chaos and destruction. As the town descends into anarchy, George must navigate the complexities of small-town politics and social dynamics to restore order and find a way to coexist with the undead.

Throughout the film, McDonald explores the tension between tradition and modernity, as well as the struggle for power and control in a society on the brink of collapse. The movie also delves into themes of grief, loss, and redemption, as George grapples with his own personal demons and tries to find a way to move forward.

Ultimately, Survival of the Dead is a commentary on the human condition, highlighting our capacity for resilience, adaptability, and compassion in the face of adversity. The film's blend of humor, pathos, and social commentary makes it a unique and thought-provoking take on the zombie genre.

overview: Publisher Will Atenton quits a lucrative job in New York to relocate his wife, Libby, and their daughters to a quaint town in New England. However, as they settle into their home the Atentons discover that a woman and her children were murdered there, and the surviving husband is the town's prime suspect. With help from a neighbor who was close to the murdered family, Will pieces together a horrifying chain of events.
tagline: Once upon a time, there were two little girls who lived in a house.
title: Dream House
plot:
Dream House is a 2011 American psychological thriller directed by Jim Sheridan and produced by Morgan Creek Productions, starring Daniel Craig as Will Atenton, Rachel Weisz as his wife Libby, Naomi Watts as their neighbor Ann and Marton Csokas as Ann's estranged husband Jack. The film follows a man who discovers that the house he has moved into with his family was the scene of a terrible crime.

Will Atenton, a successful editor at a New York publishing house, quits his job to write a novel and spend more time with Libby and their two young daughters at their new home in a quiet Connecticut town. The family's happiness soon gives way to unease as a series of unsettling events occurs and their neighbors react to Will with suspicion. He learns that five years earlier a man named Peter Ward murdered his wife and two children in the house and was committed to a psychiatric hospital, from which he was recently released for lack of evidence.

Seeking answers, Will turns to his neighbor Ann, who is reluctant to help, while her estranged husband Jack is openly hostile. When Will visits the psychiatric facility, he discovers the truth: he himself is Peter Ward. Shot in the head during the attack, he has no memory of the killings and has constructed a new identity and the illusion that his family is still alive, living in a house that is in reality abandoned and condemned. Taken in by Ann, who believes in his innocence, Peter sets out to discover what really happened on the night of the murders and who was responsible, leading to a confrontation with the real killers.

The production was troubled: Sheridan reportedly clashed with Morgan Creek over the script and tried to remove his name from the film, and Sheridan, Craig and Weisz were said to dislike the final cut. The trailer was criticized for revealing the main plot twist.

Dream House was released by Universal Pictures on September 30, 2011, without advance screenings for critics. It was a critical and commercial failure, with 7 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 35.

overview: All-stars from the previous Step Up installments come together in glittering Las Vegas, battling for a victory that could define their dreams and their careers.
tagline: Every Step Has Led To This
title: Step Up All In
plot:
Step Up All In is a 2014 American dance drama film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Michael Genet. The movie serves as the fourth installment in the Step Up film series.

The story begins with Emily (Caitlin Stasey), a young dancer who has just moved to Los Angeles to pursue her dreams of becoming a professional dancer. She meets Tyler Gage (Shawn Mendes) and his crew, including Sean (Jordan Fisher), who are part of an underground dance crew called the "Los Angeles Kings." Emily is initially hesitant to join the group but eventually warms up to them.

As Emily becomes more confident in her dancing skills, she begins to form close bonds with Tyler's friends, particularly Sean. However, their budding friendship is put to the test when Tyler and his crew are challenged by a rival dance crew called "The Kings" (led by a ruthless dancer named Victor).

The rivalry between the two crews escalates into an all-out dance battle, with Emily and her new friends determined to prove themselves as the best. Along the way, Emily must navigate her feelings for Sean while also confronting her own self-doubt and fears.

As the competition heats up, Emily's skills are put to the test, and she finds herself facing off against Victor in a thrilling dance showdown. The movie culminates in an epic finale that showcases the talents of the entire cast, with Emily emerging as a rising star in the world of competitive dance.

Throughout the film, the characters face various challenges, including personal struggles, rivalries, and self-doubt. However, through their passion for dance and their determination to succeed, they learn valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and believing in themselves.

The movie features a mix of contemporary and hip-hop dance styles, with impressive choreography that brings the story to life. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Caitlin Stasey and Jordan Fisher, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Step Up All In is an inspiring and entertaining film that celebrates the power of dance and the importance of following your dreams. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and impressive dance sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the Step Up franchise and dance enthusiasts alike.

original_title: ปฏิบัติการกู้หวย
overview: Five down-on-their-luck strangers must band together to steal back winning lottery tickets worth millions from a wicked mafia boss.
tagline: The loser team up for a lost cause.
title: The Lost Lotteries
plot:
The Lost Lotteries (Thai: ปฏิบัติการกู้หวย) is a 2022 Thai crime comedy film directed by Prueksa Amaruji, the director of Bikeman and its sequel, and produced by GMM Studios. It stars Wongravee Nateetorn as Tay, Phantira Pipityakorn as Beat, Padung Songsang as Wen, Napapa Tantrakul as Zoe and Somjit Jongjohor as Khung, with Thanaporn Wagprayoon as Tay's mother Toi, Anusorn Pinyopojanee as the crime boss Chye and Torpong Kul-On and Somyos Matures as his henchmen Mee and Doe. The film runs 106 minutes under the tagline "The loser team up for a lost cause."

In Bangkok, where many people turn to the national lottery for a little daily hope, Tay is a business student and chess fanatic whose life seems to be a series of bad luck episodes. After his mother Toi is injured falling through an open sewer, he takes over her work selling lottery tickets after school. When Boss Chye, the leader of the local syndicate, sends his goons Mee and Doe to collect on a loan Toi cannot repay, they seize her lottery tray and all its tickets as collateral. Just then, five of those tickets turn out to be winners worth millions, but without the tray there are no receipts, and the four other ticket holders, Khung, Zoe, Beat and Wen, each desperate after hard times of their own, arrive demanding to know what Tay will do about it. The gangsters will not hand the tickets back, the police are either afraid of Chye or on his payroll, and none of them is a professional thief. With no other choice, the five strangers agree to Tay's outlandish and audacious plan to infiltrate the boss's lair in disguise and steal the tickets back, a scheme that requires a series of backup plans and lands one of them in an illegal backroom boxing match against the real-life Muay Thai champion Rodtang Jitmuangnon.

The film was released worldwide on Netflix in November 2022. Johnny Loftus of Decider recommended it, enjoying its madcap slapstick and the performances of Songsang and Jongjohor while finding its toilet humour and dubbed-in sound effects tiresome. Amanda Guarragi of Ready Steady Cut called it wacky, fast-paced and funny despite one-note characters, while Rahul Shinde of The Envoy praised the cast but felt the film tried too hard to be funny, making it a one-time watch.

overview: Slevin is mistakenly put in the middle of a personal war between the city’s biggest criminal bosses. Under constant watch, Slevin must try not to get killed by an infamous assassin and come up with an idea of how to get out of his current dilemma.
tagline: Wrong Time. Wrong Place. Wrong Number.
title: Lucky Number Slevin
plot:
Lucky Number Slevin is a 2006 American neo-noir crime thriller film directed by Paul McGuigan, written by Scott Frank and Brian Helgeland, and starring Josh Hartnett, Bruce Willis, and Morgan Freeman.

The story revolves around Slevin Kelevra (Josh Hartnett), an innocent young man who becomes embroiled in a complex web of deceit and betrayal. The film begins with Slevin's life being turned upside down when his brother Nicky (Morgan Freeman) is murdered by the infamous crime lord, The Boss (Bruce Willis).

The Boss, also known as "The Rabbi," has been seeking revenge against Nicky for killing one of his henchmen, and he sets out to find Slevin, believing him to be the same person who killed his man. Unbeknownst to Slevin, he is actually a lookalike, and The Boss hires two hitmen, 25 (Benjamin Bratt) and 31 (Luis Guzmán), to track down and kill Slevin.

As Slevin navigates this treacherous world, he becomes embroiled in a series of events that lead him to question his own identity and the true nature of his relationship with Nicky. Along the way, he meets Lindsey (Megan Fox), a beautiful woman who may hold the key to unraveling the mystery surrounding Nicky's death.

As Slevin delves deeper into the world of organized crime, he discovers that The Boss is not what he seems. In reality, The Boss is a complex and multifaceted character with a troubled past, driven by a desire for revenge against those who have wronged him.

Throughout the film, the narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, jumping back and forth between different time periods and storylines. This structure adds to the sense of confusion and disorientation that Slevin experiences as he tries to navigate his way through the treacherous world of crime.

Ultimately, Slevin must confront The Boss and face the truth about his own identity and the circumstances surrounding Nicky's death. In a thrilling climax, Slevin outsmarts The Boss and emerges victorious, but not without scars.

One of the standout aspects of Lucky Number Slevin is its complex characters and intricate plot. The film features a talented ensemble cast, with standout performances from Bruce Willis and Morgan Freeman. The movie's non-linear narrative adds to the sense of tension and suspense, keeping the viewer on the edge of their seat as they try to piece together the puzzle.

Overall, Lucky Number Slevin is a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption. With its complex characters, intricate plot, and non-linear narrative, this film is sure to keep viewers engaged until the very end.

overview: A woman falls in love with a man who is somewhat unavailable.
tagline: This holiday could be the start of a new beginning.
title: The Spirit of Christmas
plot:
The Spirit of Christmas is a 2015 American romantic fantasy television film directed by David Jackson from a screenplay by Tracy Andreen. Produced by MarVista Entertainment, with Andrea Ajemian as producer, music by Claude Foisy and cinematography by Michael Negrin, it was developed under the working title Hollygrove and filmed in Wrentham, Massachusetts. Running about 91 minutes, it stars Jen Lilley and Thomas Beaudoin and premiered in the 2015 holiday season on the Lifetime network, blending a Christmas romance with a ghost story and a murder mystery.

Lilley plays Kate Jordan, a dedicated Boston lawyer whose devotion to work has left her with no lasting relationships and who has not really celebrated Christmas since her mother's death. Her boss gives her twelve days to close a deal: she is sent to Vermont to appraise the Hollygrove Inn so that it can be sold, a job she hopes will win her a promotion. On arrival she finds the caretaker, Walter Rafferty (Robert Walsh), uncooperative; he explains that the prospective buyer fled because a spirit lives in the house and disapproves of its sale, and that the inn cannot take guests because of the ghost. Kate soon meets the handsome Daniel Forsythe (Beaudoin), the owner of the mansion, who has been scaring off buyers. Murdered ninety-five years earlier, Daniel returns to the inn in bodily form for twelve days every Christmas, but he remembers neither who killed him nor why.

Kate puts the sale aside to help him. The two get off to a rocky start, with Daniel locking her out of the house and tossing blankets out after her, but they gradually warm to each other, and he even finds himself pressed into tending bar at a holiday party. As the days pass, they uncover the reason for his murder and the identity of the killer, and they fall in love, forcing Daniel to make a choice about his feelings before his time runs out. The supporting cast includes Bates Wilder as Sheriff Noah Bell, Kati Salowsky and Joanna Herrington.

Though it attracted less attention than many holiday television films on its release, the film has drawn admirers since. Writing for MovieWeb in 2022, Gissane Sophia called it a top-tier holiday film that had slipped under too many radars, praising the slow-burn romance between two jaded, heartbroken people, the leads' chemistry, Beaudoin's sardonic, brooding Daniel and the way the romance develops through solving the mystery, and arguing that it deserved cult status.

overview: A team of trained secret agent animals, guinea pigs Darwin, Hurley, Juarez, Blaster, mole Speckles, and fly Mooch takes on a mission for the US government to stop evil Leonard Saber, who plans to destroy the world with household appliances. But the government shuts them down and they are sentenced to a pet shop. Can they escape to defeat the villain and save the world?
tagline: The world needs bigger heroes
title: G-Force
plot:
G-Force is a 2009 computer-animated spy comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of a top-secret animal espionage unit, known as G-Force, which consists of three genetically enhanced guinea pigs: Darwin, Juice, and Speckles.

The main themes of G-Force (2009) include:

1. **Friendship**: The bond between the three main characters, Darwin, Juice, and Speckles, is a central theme in the movie. Despite their differences, they work together to overcome obstacles and save the day.
2. **Teamwork**: The film highlights the importance of teamwork and collaboration. Each member of G-Force brings their unique skills and strengths to the table, making them a formidable team.
3. **Belonging**: Darwin, in particular, struggles with feeling like an outcast due to his unusual appearance and abilities. His journey is one of self-discovery and finding acceptance among his peers.
4. **Adaptation**: The movie showcases the guinea pigs' ability to adapt to new situations and environments, often using their unique skills to overcome challenges.
5. **Good vs. Evil**: The film features a villainous character, Dr. Kuzco, who serves as the main antagonist. The G-Force team must use their skills and work together to stop him from carrying out his nefarious plans.

Overall, G-Force (2009) is an entertaining and action-packed movie that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, belonging, adaptation, and good vs. evil.

overview: An artist falls for a married young woman while he's commissioned to paint her portrait. The two invest in the risky tulip market in hopes to build a future together.
title: Tulip Fever
plot: An artist falls for a married young woman while he's commissioned to paint her portrait. The two invest in the risky tulip market in hopes to build a future together.

overview: After waking up in a hospital with amnesia, professor Robert Langdon and a doctor must race against time to foil a deadly global plot.
tagline: His greatest challenge. Humanity's last hope.
title: Inferno
plot:
Inferno is a 2016 American action thriller film directed by Ron Howard and starring Tom Hanks as Robert Langdon, a symbologist who becomes embroiled in a global conspiracy. The movie is the third installment in the Robert Langdon series, following Angels & Demons (2009) and Da Vinci Code (2006).

The story begins with Dr. Sienna Brooks (Felicity Jones), a brilliant scientist who has been working on a cure for Alzheimer's disease. She is kidnapped by a mysterious organization known as the "Benedictus" group, led by Abigail Holmes (Amanda Seyfried). The group demands that Langdon find a specific text written in ancient Sumerian, which they believe will unlock the secrets of the universe.

Langdon soon discovers that he has been chosen for this task because of his expertise in symbology. He is given a cryptic message by Abigail, who reveals that she is working to prevent a global pandemic caused by a deadly virus known as the "Benedictus virus." The virus is said to be created by a mysterious figure known only as "The Architect," who has been manipulating world events from behind the scenes.

As Langdon delves deeper into the mystery, he teams up with Sienna's sister, Dr. Vittoria (Irène Jacob), and together they embark on a perilous journey across Europe to uncover the truth about the virus and The Architect's identity. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including deadly traps, puzzles, and cryptic clues left behind by The Architect.

As the story unfolds, Langdon discovers that the Benedictus virus is linked to an ancient text known as the "Inferno," which holds the secrets of the universe. He also learns that Abigail is not what she seems, and that her true intentions are far more sinister than he initially thought.

The movie's climax features a thrilling showdown between Langdon and The Architect (Vincent Cassel), who reveals himself to be a former scientist turned mad by his own ambition. In the end, Langdon and Sienna manage to stop the pandemic and uncover the truth about The Architect's identity, but not before many lives are lost.

Throughout the movie, Howard weaves together intricate plot twists, clever puzzles, and stunning visuals to create an engaging narrative that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats. While some critics felt that the movie's pacing was uneven and the plot was overly complex, fans of the series will appreciate the thrilling adventure and intellectual challenge that Inferno provides.

Overall, Inferno is a gripping action thriller that explores themes of science, faith, and the power of human ingenuity. With its breakneck pace, clever plot twists, and stunning visuals, it's a must-see for fans of the Robert Langdon series and action enthusiasts alike.

overview: Family friends Sam and Kat spend every Christmas Eve at the Children's Table. They grow up together, sharing the highs and lows of young adulthood. And at thirty, Sam realizes that Kat is the one... but he's afraid that the past will get in the way.
title: Love at the Christmas Table
plot:
Love at the Christmas Table is a 2012 American romantic comedy film directed by Peter Sullivan and produced by The Asylum.

The movie revolves around a woman named Samantha, who returns to her hometown for Christmas after a painful breakup. She reconnects with her high school sweetheart, now a single father, and together they navigate their feelings amidst the festive atmosphere of the holiday season.

At its core, Love at the Christmas Table explores themes of second chances, forgiveness, and the power of love to heal emotional wounds. The film also touches on the idea that sometimes, people need time and space to work through their issues before they can truly move forward with their lives.

The movie's portrayal of Samantha's journey from heartbreak to healing is a poignant commentary on the human capacity for resilience and growth. As she navigates her feelings and reconnects with her past, she must also confront the challenges of co-parenting and rebuilding trust in a relationship.

Ultimately, Love at the Christmas Table is a feel-good holiday romance that celebrates the magic of love, forgiveness, and the transformative power of the holiday season.

overview: In Japanese-occupied Korea, three freedom fighters are assigned a mission to assassinate a genocidal military leader and his top collaborator. But the plan goes completely awry amidst double-crossings, counter-assassinations, and a shocking revelation about one of the assassins' past.
tagline: The country falls. The operation begins.
title: Assassination
plot:
Assassination (Korean: Amsal) is a 2015 South Korean period spy action film co-written and directed by Choi Dong-hoon. Set mainly in Seoul and Shanghai in the 1930s, during the Japanese occupation of Korea, it follows Korean independence fighters plotting to kill a Japanese commander and a collaborator. Jun Ji-hyun, Lee Jung-jae and Ha Jung-woo lead the cast, with Oh Dal-su and Cho Jin-woong. Released on July 22, 2015, it drew more than 12.7 million admissions.

In 1911, a resistance fighter named Yem Sek-jin fails in an attempt to kill the Japanese governor-general and the pro-Japanese businessman Kang In-guk. When Kang discovers that his wife has been helping the resistance, he kills her, and a nurse flees with one of his newborn twin daughters. Yem, captured and tortured, secretly becomes an informant for the Japanese.

By 1933, Yem is a respected officer of the independence movement in Shanghai, and the leaders of the Provisional Government ask him to assemble a team to assassinate Kang and the Japanese general Kawaguchi Mamoru in Seoul. He recruits the sharpshooter Ahn Ok-yun and two fellow fighters, Big Gun and Duk-sam, then betrays the mission to the Japanese. He also hires a Korean contract killer, Hawaii Pistol, and his partner Buddy to eliminate the team, telling them that they are Japanese agents.

In Seoul, Hawaii Pistol wounds Big Gun, and Ahn and Duk-sam's ambush of their targets fails when the car turns out to be a decoy, costing Duk-sam his life. When Hawaii Pistol confronts Ahn, he recognises her from a chance encounter in Shanghai, spares her and decides to help her cause. Ahn then learns that she is Kang's lost daughter. Her twin sister, engaged to Kawaguchi's son, visits her and is killed by Kang's men, who mistake her for Ahn.

Taking her sister's place, Ahn attends the wedding as the bride, and with Hawaii Pistol, Buddy and the surviving Big Gun she carries out the attack. Ahn kills Kawaguchi, and Hawaii Pistol shoots Kang when she hesitates, sparing her the burden of killing her own father. Big Gun dies covering the escape, and Hawaii Pistol and Buddy are later killed by Yem, while Ahn escapes.

After Korea's liberation, Yem, now a senior police officer, is tried for collaboration in 1949 but walks free when the key witness is murdered. Ahn and a surviving comrade, Myung-woo, then confront him and carry out the long-delayed sentence. The film won Best Film at the Blue Dragon Film Awards and Baeksang Arts Awards.

overview: From the director of Wolf Creek comes this terrifying look at nature's perfect killing machine. When a group of tourists stumble into the remote Australian river territory of an enormous crocodile, the deadly creature traps them on a tiny mud island with the tide quickly rising and darkness descending. As the hungry predator closes in, they must fight for survival against all odds.
tagline: How Fast Can You Swim?
title: Rogue
plot:
Rogue is a 2007 Australian horror film directed by Greg McLean. The movie follows two brothers, Luke (Michael Vartan) and Sam (Radha Mitchell), who are on a fishing trip in the Northern Territory when they encounter a massive saltwater crocodile that has been terrorizing the local community.

The main themes of Rogue include:

1. Survival vs. Humanity: As the brothers try to survive against the deadly predator, they are forced to confront their own humanity and make difficult choices to stay alive.
2. Family Dynamics: The movie explores the complex relationship between Luke and Sam, who have a troubled past. Their bond is tested as they face the life-threatening situation together.
3. Isolation and Survival: The remote location of the Northern Territory adds to the sense of isolation, making it harder for the brothers to escape the crocodile's deadly grasp.
4. Nature vs. Humanity: The film highlights the power and ferocity of nature, particularly the saltwater crocodile, which serves as a symbol of the untamed wilderness.

The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as Luke and Sam try to outsmart the crocodile and make it back to civilization. Along the way, they face numerous challenges and setbacks that test their resolve and push them to confront their deepest fears.

Overall, Rogue is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of survival, family dynamics, and the human condition in the face of nature's fury.

overview: While on a prison furlough, a lowly criminal evades his guards and returns to his old stomping ground to take revenge on the people who turned him into a cold blooded killer.
tagline: He's out for blood
title: Avengement
plot:
Avengement is a 2019 British action thriller directed by Jesse V. Johnson, who co-wrote it with Stu Small. Scott Adkins stars as Cain Burgess, a small-time criminal transformed into a ruthless fighter by years in prison, with Craig Fairbrass as his older brother Lincoln, Thomas Turgoose, Nick Moran and Kierston Wareing. It was released on video on demand and in select cinemas on 24 May 2019, and an uncut special edition followed in 2020.

Cain, a prisoner, is escorted by police to a hospital to see the body of his recently deceased mother. He escapes from his guards and makes his way to a private East London pub, forcing his way in past the bouncers. As he drinks, he overhears a patron named Tune boasting about how an unknown assailant killed a gangster called Rook, and his laughter provokes a confrontation with the regulars and the barmaid, Bez. Claiming to be a friend of the pub's owner, Lincoln, he fights off the patrons and takes everyone hostage with a sawn-off shotgun. When Lincoln's lieutenant, Hyde, arrives, he recognizes Cain as Lincoln's younger brother, and Cain shoots a man in the knee to show he is serious, blaming Hyde and Lincoln for everything that has happened to him.

Through flashbacks, Cain recounts his story. Once a skilled but hot-headed martial artist whose fights had cost Lincoln, a loan shark, and his associates a good deal of money, he went to his brother for help in starting a legitimate business, only to be drawn into the gang's criminal world. Sent to the notorious HMP Belmarsh, he was repeatedly attacked and had to fight for survival, gradually turning into a hardened, scarred killing machine, and he came to believe that his brother was responsible for his ordeal. Waiting for Lincoln to arrive at the pub, Cain prepares to take bloody revenge on the brother he believes destroyed his life, and the hostages realize they are caught in the middle of a long-awaited family reckoning.

Avengement received generally positive reviews, with an 89 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Its consensus said it compensated for a lack of narrative originality with thrilling sequences of bone-crunching action, elevated by Adkins's brutally intense performance, and many critics considered it one of the best showcases of his career.

overview: After a year apart - attending different schools, meeting different people - the guys rent a beach house and vow to make this the best summer ever. As it turns out, whether that will happen or not has a lot to do with the girls. Between the wild parties, outrageous revelations and yes, a trip to band camp, they discover that times change and people change, but in the end, it's all about sticking together.
tagline: This Summer It's All About Sticking Together.
title: American Pie 2
plot:
American Pie 2 is a coming-of-age comedy film released in 2001 by Universal Pictures. The movie serves as a sequel to the original American Pie, which was also produced by Universal Pictures.

The story begins with Jim Levenstein (Jason Biggs), Kevin Lomax (Eddie Kaye Thomas), Oz Oseransky (Chris Klein), and Stifler (Seann William Scott) returning from their European trip in the first film. The movie takes place a year after the events of the original, with the friends now facing new challenges as they enter adulthood.

The plot revolves around Jim's struggles to find his place in the world. He is trying to balance his relationships with his family and his desire for independence. Meanwhile, Kevin is dealing with the aftermath of his father's death and his own feelings of guilt and responsibility. Oz is trying to navigate his relationship with Michelle Flaherty (Shannon Elizabeth), who has become increasingly distant from him.

The main plot point of the movie centers around a summer vacation that the friends plan together. They rent a lake house in Michigan, where they spend their days partying and engaging in various misadventures. However, things take a turn when Oz's family reveals that they are planning to sell the lake house, which would mean the end of the friends' annual tradition.

As the summer progresses, the friends face various challenges, including romantic relationships, family conflicts, and personal growth. Along the way, they also encounter new characters, such as Stifler's father (Paul Gleason), who becomes a recurring figure in the series.

Throughout the movie, the friends learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and growing up. They come to realize that their relationships with each other are more important than any romantic relationship or personal achievement. The movie ends on a positive note, with the friends having learned to appreciate the importance of their friendships and the value of spending time together.

Overall, American Pie 2 is a lighthearted and entertaining comedy that explores themes of friendship, growing up, and self-discovery. While it may not be as groundbreaking as its predecessor, the movie delivers on its promise of raunchy humor and memorable characters.

overview: An aspiring painter meets various characters and learns valuable lessons while traveling across America.
tagline: It began as a wish, became an adventure, and ended as the ultimate road trip.
title: Interstate 60
plot:
Interstate 60 is a 2002 American drama film directed by Tony Bui. The movie follows the story of a young man named Bobby Mercer, played by James Marsden, who embarks on a road trip from New York to Los Angeles.

The main themes of Interstate 60 include:

1. **Self-discovery and personal growth**: Throughout his journey, Bobby encounters various people and experiences that challenge his perceptions and force him to confront his own identity, values, and purpose in life.
2. **Redemption and forgiveness**: As Bobby navigates the complexities of human relationships and experiences, he seeks redemption for past mistakes and learns to forgive himself and others.
3. **The search for meaning and connection**: The film explores Bobby's quest for a sense of belonging and connection with others, as well as his desire to find meaning in life beyond his mundane daily routine.
4. **The power of human relationships**: Interstate 60 highlights the importance of forming meaningful connections with others, including friends, family, and strangers, which can lead to personal growth, healing, and transformation.

Overall, the movie offers a poignant and thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, encouraging viewers to reflect on their own values, goals, and relationships.

overview: To the amusement of their adult children and friends, long divorced couple Don and Ellie Griffin are once again forced to play the happy couple for the sake of their adopted son's wedding after his ultra conservative biological mother unexpectedly decides to fly halfway across the world to attend. With all of the wedding guests looking on, the Griffins are hilariously forced to confront their past, present and future - and hopefully avoid killing each other in the process.
tagline: It's never too late to start acting like a family.
title: The Big Wedding
plot:
The Big Wedding is a 2013 American romantic comedy film directed by Dan Mazer. The movie revolves around the story of a blended family's wedding preparations, which ultimately leads to chaos and hilarity.

At its core, The Big Wedding explores themes of love, acceptance, and the complexities of human relationships. The film delves into the intricate web of emotions that arise when people from different backgrounds and with different values come together in a shared experience. As the characters navigate their personal struggles and conflicts, they are forced to confront their own biases and prejudices.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. The characters' attempts to present a united front for the sake of their families often lead to feelings of disconnection and inauthenticity. This tension between individuality and conformity serves as a catalyst for growth and self-discovery.

Furthermore, The Big Wedding critiques societal expectations and the pressures that come with conforming to traditional norms. The film's portrayal of a blended family navigating cultural differences and personal differences highlights the challenges of finding common ground in a world where everyone has their own unique story to tell.

Ultimately, The Big Wedding is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of what it means to love and accept one another, flaws and all.

overview: Terrorists hijack a 747 inbound to Washington D.C., demanding the release of their imprisoned leader. Intelligence expert David Grant (Kurt Russell) suspects another reason and he is soon the reluctant member of a special assault team that is assigned to intercept the plane and hijackers.
tagline: Fasten your seat belts
title: Executive Decision
plot:
Executive Decision is a 1996 action thriller film directed by Stuart Baird and starring Kurt Russell, Steven Seagal, and Halle Berry.

The main themes of Executive Decision revolve around:

1. **Global Terrorism**: The movie depicts a catastrophic plot by a group of terrorists to destroy major cities across the world using a deadly virus. This theme highlights the dangers of terrorism and the need for international cooperation to prevent such disasters.
2. **Heroism and Sacrifice**: The film showcases the bravery and selflessness of its protagonists, including Captain Keith "Hawk" Hawkins (Kurt Russell), who risks his life to save innocent people from the terrorist threat.
3. **Teamwork and Camaraderie**: The movie emphasizes the importance of teamwork and camaraderie among a diverse group of characters, including Hawk's team, as they work together to prevent the terrorist attack.
4. **Global Politics and Diplomacy**: Executive Decision touches on the complexities of global politics and diplomacy, highlighting the challenges faced by international leaders in responding to threats from non-state actors.

The plot follows Captain Hawkins and his team, which includes a Russian defector (Steven Seagal) and a CIA agent (Halle Berry), as they attempt to stop the terrorists and prevent a global catastrophe. Along the way, they must navigate complex webs of intrigue, deception, and betrayal.

Overall, Executive Decision is an action-packed thriller that explores themes of heroism, teamwork, and the importance of international cooperation in the face of global threats.

overview: With only three weeks left in his three year contract, Sam Bell is getting anxious to finally return to Earth. He is the only occupant of a Moon-based manufacturing facility along with his computer and assistant, GERTY. When he has an accident however, he wakens to find that he is not alone.
tagline: The last place you'd ever expect to find yourself.
title: Moon
plot:
Moon is a 2009 British science fiction film directed by Duncan Jones in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Nathan Parker based on Jones's story. Written as a vehicle for Sam Rockwell, it stars him as an astronaut nearing the end of a solitary three-year stint on the far side of the Moon, with Kevin Spacey voicing the station's robot.

In the future, after an energy crisis, the company Lunar Industries has made a fortune mining helium-3, a clean fuel, from the lunar surface. Its Sarang Station requires only one worker, Sam Bell, who maintains the automated harvesters and launches canisters of helium-3 to Earth, aided by the station's artificial intelligence, GERTY. With two weeks left on his contract, Sam longs to return to his wife, Tess, and their daughter. A broken satellite link prevents live calls, allowing only recorded messages. He begins seeing hallucinations and, distracted by one while out on the surface, crashes his rover.

Sam wakes in the infirmary with no memory of the accident. Suspicious after overhearing GERTY speaking live with the company, he tricks his way outside and finds at the crash site an injured man in the rover who is identical to himself. The two Sams at first quarrel until GERTY confirms that they are both clones of the original Sam Bell, carrying his implanted memories. Exploring, they discover that the company has been jamming communications with Earth, and logs reveal that earlier clones sickened as their terms ended and were incinerated rather than sent home. A hidden vault holds hundreds of sleeping clones. When the older Sam drives beyond the jamming and calls home, he reaches his daughter, now fifteen, who tells him that Tess died years ago.

With a company team on its way that will kill them if they are found together, the dying older Sam chooses to return to the wrecked rover so that his absence will not be noticed, while the younger Sam escapes to Earth aboard a helium-3 transport. At GERTY's suggestion, its memory is wiped, and the younger Sam destroys the jamming antenna before leaving. The rescue team finds a newly awakened clone and the body in the rover, and Sam's testimony on Earth sends Lunar Industries' stock crashing.

Moon premiered at the 2009 Sundance Film Festival and received critical acclaim, particularly for Rockwell's performance, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 90% approval. It was nominated for the BAFTA Award for Best British Film and won the Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation.

overview: Agent Coulson informs Agent Sitwell that the World Security Council wishes Emil Blonsky to be released from prison to join the Avengers Initiative. As Nick Fury doesn't want to release Blonsky, the two agents decide to send a patsy to sabotage the meeting...
title: Marvel One-Shot: The Consultant
plot:
Marvel One-Shot: The Consultant is a 2011 web series that explores the theme of identity and self-discovery through the character of Howard Stark, played by Dominic Cooper. The story delves into Howard's past as a young man, showcasing his early days as an inventor and entrepreneur, and how these experiences shaped him into the person he became.

The film also touches on the idea of legacy and responsibility, as Howard grapples with the consequences of his actions and the impact they have on those around him. His relationship with his father, Henry Stark, serves as a catalyst for this exploration, highlighting the complexities of family dynamics and the weight of inherited expectations.

Furthermore, The Consultant examines the tension between creativity and commercialism, as Howard navigates the challenges of balancing his artistic vision with the demands of the business world. This theme is particularly relevant in the context of Marvel's Cinematic Universe, where characters often find themselves torn between their personal goals and the needs of the larger narrative.

Overall, The Consultant offers a nuanced and introspective look at the character of Howard Stark, shedding light on his motivations and conflicts in a way that adds depth to the broader Marvel universe.

overview: Based on a true story. On 27 April 1940, Luftwaffe pilot Horst Schopis' Heinkel 111 bomber is shot down near Grotli by an RAF Blackburn Skua L2940 fighter, which then crash-lands. The surviving German and English crew members begin to at shoot each other, but later find themselves huddled up in the same cabin. In order to survive the harsh winter in the Norwegian wilderness, they have to stand together. An unlikely, lifelong friendship blossoms.
tagline: Inspired by the true world war II story.
title: Into the White
plot:
Into the White is a 2012 Norwegian war drama film directed by Espen Sandberg and Joachim Trier, produced by Trollhättan Film. The movie is set during World War II and tells the story of three young Norwegian airmen who are shot down behind enemy lines.

The film begins with Lieutenant Stig Engstrom (played by Mikkel Abels), Lieutenant Sverre Okken (played by Anders Baasmo Christiansen), and Lieutenant Magnus Isaksen (played by Jonas Holm) on a mission to bomb German airfields. However, their plane is hit by anti-aircraft fire, and they are forced to make an emergency landing in the Norwegian wilderness.

The three pilots soon discover that they are not alone in the forest. They encounter a group of German soldiers who have also been stranded behind enemy lines. Initially, tensions run high between the two groups, but as they spend more time together, they begin to form an uneasy alliance.

As the days pass, the Norwegian and German pilots learn about each other's lives and motivations. Stig, Sverre, and Magnus are all young men who have been forced to confront the harsh realities of war, while their German counterparts, Hauptmann Müller (played by Lasse Hallström), Oberleutnant von Roeder (played by Mads Sjøgård Pettersen), and Oberleutnant von Roeder's brother, are all struggling with their own demons.

As the situation becomes more desperate, the two groups must work together to survive. They share what little food they have, and the Germans teach the Norwegians how to navigate using a compass. The Norwegians, in turn, show the Germans the beauty of the Norwegian wilderness.

Despite their differences, the pilots begin to form bonds with each other. Stig, Sverre, and Magnus learn about the human cost of war from their German counterparts, while Hauptmann Müller and his men are forced to confront the harsh realities of their own actions.

As the days turn into weeks, the pilots realize that they must find a way to escape the forest before it's too late. They hatch a plan to make a break for it, but things don't go according to plan. The Germans are discovered by their superiors, and the Norwegians are forced to flee.

In the end, only one of the Norwegian pilots is able to escape, while the others are captured or killed. The film ends with Stig, Sverre, and Magnus reflecting on the experience they shared in the forest. They realize that despite being on opposite sides of the war, they formed a bond that will stay with them for the rest of their lives.

Into the White is a powerful and emotional film that explores the human cost of war. The movie features stunning cinematography and outstanding performances from its cast. The film's themes of survival, sacrifice, and redemption are timeless and universal, making it a must-see for anyone interested in World War II history or drama.

overview: When their latest scheme goes awry, Mayor Humdinger and his nephew Harold accidentally divert a meteor towards Adventure Bay. The meteor's golden energy grants the PAW Patrol superpowers. The heroic Mighty Pups are on a roll to super-save the day.
title: PAW Patrol: Mighty Pups
plot:
PAW Patrol: Mighty Pups is a 2018 Canadian animated superhero adventure film, a 44-minute special of the preschool series PAW Patrol and the show's first double-length television movie. Directed by Charles E. Bastien, written by Andrew Guerdat and Steven Sullivan and animated by Guru Studio, it belongs to the series' fifth season and introduces Mayor Humdinger's nephew Harold. It premiered in the United States in July 2018, was issued on DVD that September and reached further markets from October 2018, including Canadian cinemas and, in December 2019, Italian ones. The voice cast includes Jaxon Mercey as Ryder, Max Calinescu as Chase, Devan Cohen as Rubble, Drew Davis as Marshall, Samuel Faraci as Rocky, Kallan Holley as Skye, Carter Thorne as Zuma, Berkley Silverman as Everest, Chance Hurstfield as Harold and Ron Pardo as Mayor Humdinger, Cap'n Turbot and Farmer Al.

Determined to become the "First Mayor on the Moon", Mayor Humdinger prepares a rocket launch on Adventure Beach with Harold's help, but the boy accidentally fires the rocket without his uncle. It misses the moon, strikes a passing meteor and sends it hurtling towards Adventure Bay. Alerted by Everest and Jake, Ryder and the pups clear the town before the meteor crashes harmlessly into the sand, and Chase, whom Ryder has put in charge of a team, doubts his own leadership. The meteor's golden energy soon gives the pups superpowers, from Chase's super speed and Rubble's super strength to Marshall's mighty heat and Everest's freezing sneeze, and Mayor Goodway puts the rock on display at City Hall. Harold, who has also gained powers that let him build gadgets, joins his uncle in a plan to steal the meteor and take over the city. After a first attempt is foiled, Ryder trusts Chase to lead the newly named Mighty Pups, but Harold uses a tractor beam to lift the meteor, carries it to the Lookout, traps Ryder inside and sends the tower soaring into the sky, then attacks in a giant robot. Under Chase's command the pups free one another, retrieve the meteor from the robot's backpack and, when the Lookout plunges back to Earth, use whirlwinds and a sand tornado to cushion its fall, saving Ryder. Their powers fade as the meteor loses its glow, and the rock is stored beneath the Lookout.

The Mighty Pups concept returned in later specials of the series, such as Mighty Pups, Super Paws and Mighty Pups, Charged Up.

overview: As a shocking truth about a couple's families emerges, the two lovers discover they are not so different from each other. Tessa is no longer the sweet, simple, good girl she was when she met Hardin — any more than he is the cruel, moody boy she fell so hard for.
title: After Ever Happy
plot:
After Ever Happy is a 2022 American romantic thriller film directed by Isaac Ezban and written by Jessica Sorensen. The movie serves as the fourth installment in the After series, based on the novels by Anna Todd.

The story picks up where the previous films left off, with Tessa Young (Josephine Langford) and Hardin Scott (Hero Fiennes-Tiffin) navigating their complicated relationship. However, it becomes clear that their love is put to the test as they face new challenges and secrets from their pasts.

As Tessa struggles to reconcile her feelings for Hardin with her own sense of identity and self-worth, she begins to uncover dark secrets about his family's history and the true nature of their relationship. Meanwhile, Hardin's own demons resurface, threatening to destroy everything he holds dear.

Throughout the film, the tension between Tessa and Hardin builds as they engage in a game of cat and mouse, each trying to outmaneuver the other. The stakes are raised when Tessa discovers a shocking truth about Hardin's family that forces her to reevaluate their entire relationship.

The movie explores themes of love, loyalty, and the complexities of human relationships. As with previous installments in the series, After Ever Happy delves into the darker aspects of romance, revealing the messy and often toxic nature of relationships.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a dramatic confrontation between Tessa and Hardin, leaving the audience wondering what the future holds for these two complex characters. Will they find a way to overcome their differences and make their relationship work, or will the secrets and lies tear them apart?

Overall, After Ever Happy is a gripping and intense addition to the After series, offering plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

overview: The previously untold origins of Olaf, the innocent and insightful, summer-loving snowman are revealed as we follow Olaf’s first steps as he comes to life and searches for his identity in the snowy mountains outside Arendelle.
tagline: Every snowman starts somewhere.
title: Once Upon a Snowman
plot:
Once Upon a Snowman is a 2020 American animated fantasy short film written and directed by Trent Correy and Dan Abraham and produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. Set during the events of Frozen (2013), it follows the snowman Olaf in the moments after Elsa brings him to life and before he meets Anna, Kristoff and Sven. Josh Gad reprises his role as Olaf, with Chris Williams as the shopkeeper Oaken and Idina Menzel, Kristen Bell and Jonathan Groff also credited in their original roles. It was released exclusively on Disney+ on 23 October 2020.

High in the North Mountain, after fleeing her coronation, Elsa unknowingly brings Olaf to life with her powers while singing. Before he can do anything, her discarded cape flies through the air and knocks him down the mountainside into a tree. Confused about who he is and why he exists, the newborn snowman sets out to find an identity of his own. He arrives at Wandering Oaken's Trading Post and Sauna, where he overhears Kristoff singing to Sven and gets flattened at the front door by Anna, who does not notice him.

Inside the store, Olaf meets Oaken and asks for a nose, ideally a carrot, but Oaken has sold the last of them and kindly helps him try out a variety of alternatives. Among the objects is an old-fashioned picture viewer with images of summer, and Olaf is immediately enchanted, dreaming of experiencing warm weather himself. Leaving with a new nose, he is chased by a pack of wolves through the snowy wilderness, passing unnoticed by Anna and Kristoff, who are arguing about love, and inadvertently diverting the wolves toward them. His misadventures continue as he witnesses events from the original film from his own perspective and finally ends up in the woods where he first meets Anna, Kristoff and Sven, recognizing that the people he has been looking for are his friends.

Animator Trent Correy, who had animated the scene of Olaf's creation in Frozen, conceived the short as a way to explore the character's first moments of life. The team aimed to keep continuity with the original film while offering a fresh perspective on its scenes. Critics found the short a charming addition for fans of the franchise, praising its humor and animation.

overview: An army major goes undercover as a college student. His mission is both professional and personal: to protect his general's daughter from a radical militant, and to find his estranged half-brother.
tagline: I am here.
title: Main Hoon Na
plot:
Main Hoon Na is an Indian war drama film that explores the theme of patriotism and loyalty. The story revolves around Veer Pratap Singh, a young man who disguises himself as a British officer to infiltrate the enemy's camp and gather crucial information about the impending attack on India.

The movie delves into the idea of selfless sacrifice and bravery in the face of adversity. Veer's character embodies these qualities as he puts the needs of his country and its people above his own personal desires. His actions are motivated by a sense of duty and responsibility, which ultimately lead to the success of the mission.

The film also touches upon the theme of identity and belonging. Veer's dual identity as both an Indian and a British officer serves as a metaphor for the complexities of cultural heritage and national pride. The movie highlights the importance of embracing one's roots while also being open to new experiences and perspectives.

Furthermore, Main Hoon Na explores the idea of redemption and forgiveness. Veer's character is driven by a desire to make amends for past mistakes and to find redemption through his actions. The film suggests that it's never too late to make a positive change in one's life and to seek forgiveness from others.

Overall, Main Hoon Na is a movie that celebrates the values of patriotism, loyalty, and selflessness, while also exploring complex themes such as identity, redemption, and forgiveness.

overview: With his wife's disappearance having become the focus of an intense media circus, a man sees the spotlight turned on him when it's suspected that he may not be innocent.
tagline: You don't know what you've got 'til it's...
title: Gone Girl
plot:
Gone Girl is a psychological thriller directed by David Fincher, based on the bestselling novel of the same name by Gillian Flynn. The film stars Ben Affleck and Rosamund Pike as Nick and Amy Dunne, a couple whose seemingly perfect marriage turns out to be a facade.

The story begins with the disappearance of Amy, who goes missing on the day of her fifth wedding anniversary. Nick reports her missing to the police, but as the investigation unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems. The media has a field day, portraying Amy as a manipulative and unstable woman who had been planning her disappearance for months.

As the search for Amy continues, dark secrets about their marriage come to light. It is revealed that Nick and Amy's relationship was troubled from the start, with Nick feeling suffocated by Amy's controlling behavior. The couple's friends and family members also reveal that they had grown tired of Amy's manipulative tactics, which included pretending to be a victim in order to get attention.

Through a series of twists and turns, it is revealed that Amy was indeed planning her disappearance, but not for the reasons everyone thought. She had been feeling suffocated by Nick's lack of emotional support and his inability to connect with her on a deeper level. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Amy had faked her own death in order to frame Nick for her murder.

As the investigation continues, Nick becomes the prime suspect, but he maintains his innocence. Meanwhile, Amy is hiding in plain sight, using her charm and wit to manipulate those around her. She creates an alternate identity for herself, complete with a new name, appearance, and backstory.

In the end, it is revealed that Amy had been planning her revenge against Nick all along. She had been manipulating him throughout their marriage, using her intelligence and cunning to get what she wanted. In a stunning finale, Nick discovers the truth about Amy's disappearance and confronts her in a dramatic showdown.

Throughout the film, Fincher masterfully builds tension and suspense, keeping the audience guessing until the very end. The performances by Affleck and Pike are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters. The film's themes of marriage, identity, and the unreliability of appearances are timely and thought-provoking.

Overall, Gone Girl is a gripping and twisty thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end. With its complex characters, clever plot twists, and masterful direction, it is a must-see for fans of psychological thrillers.

overview: A new documentary that showcases the making of the epic limited series. Features never-before-seen, behind-the-scenes footage, interviews and visits to the creature shop and props department.
title: Obi-Wan Kenobi: A Jedi's Return
plot:
Obi-Wan Kenobi: A Jedi's Return is a 2022 American documentary film directed by David Gelb, the filmmaker behind Jiro Dreams of Sushi and Chef's Table. Produced by Lucasfilm with Supper Club, the hour-long special chronicles the making of the Disney+ limited series Obi-Wan Kenobi and was released on Disney+ on 8 September 2022 as part of Disney+ Day, less than three months after the six-episode series concluded. Following the earlier making-of specials for The Mandalorian and The Book of Boba Fett, it features Ewan McGregor, Hayden Christensen, series director Deborah Chow, writer Joby Harold, and cast members including Moses Ingram, Vivien Lyra Blair, Rupert Friend, Joel Edgerton and Bonnie Piesse.

The documentary follows the roughly three-year effort to bring the series from concept to screen, leading up to its launch around Star Wars Celebration in May 2022. It opens with period interview footage of Alec Guinness, the original Obi-Wan, in costume describing the challenge of playing the role, and later shows McGregor watching Guinness on a big screen. Drawing on never-before-seen behind-the-scenes footage, it presents the return of Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker and of McGregor and Christensen to their roles, centring on the reunion of the two actors, who had last appeared together in Revenge of the Sith in 2005, with archival footage of George Lucas at work as director and of Carrie Fisher as Princess Leia. Chow discusses the responsibility of continuing a legacy character and defends making the young Leia, played by Blair, central to the story, while Blair recalls discovering Star Wars through books. The film also visits the creature shop and props department and shows the show's lightsabers, costumes and sets.

Reviewers largely saw it as a piece for devoted fans. Liberty Lester of CultureSlate felt it favoured an emotional, cinematic portrait over a nuts-and-bolts account and conveyed the evident love of everyone involved, especially McGregor's boyish enthusiasm. Miguel Fernandez of Star Wars News Net found it a longer, more detailed version of the series' promotional featurettes that could have gone deeper into the creative process. The Times of India called it a must-watch for hardcore Star Wars fans, redeemed mainly by its archival footage, but questioned the decision to release it after the series rather than before.

overview: Clay Kincaid hates the nickname 'Saint', he got for being too kind to stray animals and desperate people. Especially when it comes to women. With a rough and damaged past that has left him jaded, he doesn't do committed relationships. This is before he meets Samantha Jamieson, an heiress turned runaway in need of help. When she starts to work as a waitress at his bar, he discovers that she is someone truly special and amazing… someone that could warm his damaged heart.
tagline: Of all the bars in all of Chicago, she walks into his.
title: Dirty Sexy Saint
plot:
Dirty Sexy Saint is a 2019 American romantic drama film directed by Tosca Musk for the streaming service Passionflix, which released it on 8 December 2019. It is based on the novel of the same name by the New York Times bestselling romance authors Carly Phillips and Erika Wilde (the pen name of Janelle Denison), adapted for the screen by Joany Kane and Musk, who also served as an executive producer. Michael Buttiglieri produced, Margaret Goodspeed edited and Ben Collier composed the score. The film stars David A. Gregory as Clay Kincaid and Jordan Lane Price as Samantha Jamieson, with Matt Magnusson and Luke Guldan as Clay's brothers Mason and Levi, Steven Hauck as Samantha's father Conrad, and Jamie Choi, Alena Chinault, Brian Cade and Maia Guest in supporting roles. It runs 104 minutes and was promoted with the tagline "Of all the bars in all of Chicago, she walks into his."

Clay Kincaid owns a flourishing bar in Chicago. He hates the nickname "Saint," which he earned for being too kind to stray animals and to desperate people, especially women, and he knows he is more sinner than saint where women are concerned. Behind his success lies a rough and damaged past that has left him jaded and that may yet come back to haunt him, and as a result he does not do committed relationships. Everything changes when Samantha, a rebellious heiress turned runaway who is in need of help, walks into his bar. Clay helps her slowly get back on her feet and offers her a job as a waitress. As they work side by side, he discovers that she is someone truly special, someone who might be able to warm his damaged heart and who may be exactly the person he needs in his life. The emotional climax comes when Clay finally opens up to Samantha about his troubled past.

Markos Papadatos of Digital Journal gave the film an A rating, calling it entertaining, poignant and well crafted. He praised Gregory, whose years on the daytime drama One Life to Live he felt had paid off, for a bold, raw and vulnerable performance, singling out a gut-wrenching, monologue-heavy scene in which Clay reveals his past, described Price as sensational and credited Musk for her work as director, co-writer and showrunner. He also noted the film's emphasis on responsibility, morality and helping others in a time of need.

overview: After discovering a passenger ship missing since 1962 floating adrift on the Bering Sea, salvagers claim the vessel as their own. Once they begin towing the ghost ship towards harbor, a series of bizarre occurrences happen and the group becomes trapped inside the ship, which they soon learn is inhabited by a demonic creature.
tagline: Sea Evil
title: Ghost Ship
plot:
Ghost Ship is a supernatural horror film released in 2002, directed by Steve Beck and produced by Village Roadshow Pictures.

The story begins with a salvage ship called the "Avalon" that has been missing for over 30 years. The crew of a modern-day salvage ship, led by Captain Peter Cullen (played by Julián Sands), discovers the long-lost Avalon while searching for treasure in the North Sea. As they board the ship, they find it to be remarkably well-preserved and intact, with no signs of decay or damage.

However, as soon as the crew sets foot on the ship, strange things begin to happen. They start experiencing bizarre occurrences, such as hearing eerie whispers, finding cryptic messages scrawled on walls, and encountering ghostly apparitions. It becomes clear that the Avalon is haunted by the spirits of its former crew members.

As the story unfolds, it becomes apparent that the ship was involved in a tragic accident 30 years ago, resulting in the loss of all hands on board. The crew soon discovers that they are not alone on the ship and that the ghosts of the dead sailors are trying to communicate with them.

The main character, Captain Cullen, is initially skeptical of the paranormal activity but eventually becomes convinced that something supernatural is at play. He teams up with a local historian, Dr. Vronsky (played by Jonas Armstrong), who helps him uncover the dark secrets behind the Avalon's disappearance.

As the crew delves deeper into the mystery, they realize that the ship was carrying a cargo of gold and other valuable treasures when it set sail on its ill-fated voyage. The ghosts, however, are not just seeking revenge but also trying to warn the living about the dangers of the sea.

The climax of the film takes place in the ship's engine room, where the crew discovers a hidden logbook belonging to the ship's captain. As they read through the entries, they learn that the captain had made a pact with a mysterious figure to ensure the safe passage of his crew, but at a terrible cost.

In the end, the crew manages to escape the ship, but not without realizing that some secrets are better left unspoken. The film ends with a sense of unease, as the survivors wonder if they have truly escaped the wrath of the Avalon's ghosts or if they will be haunted by their experiences forever.

Overall, Ghost Ship is a tense and atmospheric horror film that explores themes of tragedy, loss, and the supernatural. While it may not be as well-known as some other horror films, it has developed a cult following over the years for its creepy atmosphere and eerie plot twists.

overview: A robber escapes from prison with a single objective in mind: to track down his former cellmate, a serial killer who intends to pin his crimes on him. A cop is sent after the robber who, despite his best efforts, soon becomes Public Enemy Number One. As the protagonists are driven to their limits, it becomes increasingly unclear who is the hunter and who is the prey.
title: The Prey
plot:
The Prey (French: La proie) is a 2011 French action thriller directed by Éric Valette and written by Laurent Turner and Luc Bossi. Albert Dupontel stars as Franck Adrien, a bank robber who escapes from prison, with Alice Taglioni as Claire Linné, the determined police officer who hunts him, Stéphane Debac as the serial killer Jean-Louis Maurel, Natacha Régnier and Sergi López. It was released in France in April 2011.

After a successful robbery, Franck Adrien and his accomplice are caught and sent to prison. Adrien alone knows where the loot is hidden, and he refuses to reveal its location even to his wife or his partner. Despite an initially distant relationship, he comes to trust his cellmate, Jean-Louis Maurel, a timid man accused of rape, and saves him from a savage beating by a gang of Russian prisoners. When Adrien's former partner has him beaten and sent to the prison infirmary, Maurel visits him. About to be released early after his alleged victim withdraws her accusation, Maurel offers to deliver a message to Adrien's wife, Anna, and Adrien, though still wary, gives him a clue to the location of the money.

Adrien's peace of mind is shattered when Manuel Carrega, an officer of the National Gendarmerie, visits him and tells him that Maurel is in fact a serial killer and rapist. Fearing for the safety of his wife and young daughter, Adrien fights off the Russian inmates and a corrupt guard who ambush him and escapes from prison disguised in the guard's uniform. As he tries to reach his family, he is confronted by Claire Linné, a rising police star assigned to recapture him. Betting that she will not shoot an unarmed man, he slips away and begins a desperate pursuit of Maurel across France, while Maurel cleverly frames Adrien for his own crimes, turning him into the most wanted man in the country. Hunted by the police and racing against time, Adrien must track down the killer and rescue his daughter before it is too late.

The Prey received generally positive reviews, holding a 70 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 58. Xan Brooks of The Guardian found it derivative of The Fugitive, Se7en and Tell No One, while Manohla Dargis of The New York Times called it ridiculously diverting and praised its relentless pace and Dupontel's physical performance.

overview: Katniss Everdeen has returned home safe after winning the 74th Annual Hunger Games along with fellow tribute Peeta Mellark. Winning means that they must turn around and leave their family and close friends, embarking on a "Victor's Tour" of the districts. Along the way Katniss senses that a rebellion is simmering, but the Capitol is still very much in control as President Snow prepares the 75th Annual Hunger Games (The Quarter Quell) - a competition that could change Panem forever.
tagline: Every revolution begins with a spark.
title: The Hunger Games: Catching Fire
plot:
The Hunger Games: Catching Fire is a 2013 science fiction action film directed by Francis Lawrence and the second installment in The Hunger Games film series. Based on the novel of the same name by Suzanne Collins, the movie takes place after the events of the first film.

The story begins with Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) returning to District 12 as victors of the 74th Hunger Games. However, their victory is short-lived, as President Snow (Donald Sutherland) threatens them, warning that if they continue to play on their fake romance, the districts will rise up against the Capitol.
