Later, her photo falls from a shelf as he exits his apartment before flying to Kōchi Prefecture. Picking it up, he looks at it briefly before leaving. As the aeroplane takes off, he narrates the events that brought her into his life...
title: Ocean Waves
plot:
Ocean Waves is a 1993 Japanese coming-of-age drama film directed by Tomoko Yoshida, based on the novel of the same name by Aiichiro Miyamoto.

The main themes of Ocean Waves revolve around the complexities of adolescence, first love, and self-discovery. The story follows Taku Morisaki, a high school student who returns to his hometown after spending three years abroad with his family. Upon his return, he reunites with his childhood friends, including Rikako Chigira, and becomes involved in a complicated web of relationships.

The film explores the themes of:

1. **First love and heartbreak**: Taku's rekindled romance with Rikako serves as a catalyst for exploring the complexities of first love, desire, and heartbreak.
2. **Identity formation**: As Taku navigates his relationships and personal growth, he grapples with finding his place in the world and defining himself outside of his family's expectations.
3. **Nostalgia and longing**: The film is set against the backdrop of a changing Japan, and the characters' nostalgia for their childhood serves as a reminder of the passing of time and the fragility of youth.
4. **Social hierarchy and class differences**: The story touches on the social stratification in Japan, particularly in the context of Taku's family and his relationships with his peers.

Through its thoughtful portrayal of adolescent struggles and relationships, Ocean Waves offers a poignant exploration of the human experience during this pivotal stage of life.

overview: After his sudden firing, a popular radio DJ moves in with his aunt, bringing along his four spoiled children, and a plan to return to the airwaves.
title: Holiday Rush
plot:
Holiday Rush is a 2019 American Christmas romantic comedy-drama directed by Leslie Small and written by Sean Dwyer and Greg Cope White. Romany Malco stars as a widowed radio DJ who loses his job just before the holidays, with Sonequa Martin-Green as his producer and friend Roxy, La La Anthony, Deon Cole, Stormi Maya and Tamala Jones. The film was released on Netflix on November 28, 2019.

Rashon "Rush" Williams is the popular host of the leading hip-hop morning show on WMLE, a radio station in Pittsburgh. Since the death of his wife Paula, he has raised their four children, Jamal and his three younger sisters, Mya and the twins Evie and Gabby, with the help of his aunt Jo. Just after Thanksgiving, as Rush and Roxy prepare to propose becoming part owners of the station, their boss Malcolm reveals that WMLE has been bought by the national media company CamCom. A corporate executive, Joss, announces a new pop format and that Rush will be replaced.

At home, the family celebrates Jamal's acceptance into Harvard, and Rush cannot bring himself to admit to the children that he has lost his job and has no savings. When he finally explains that drastic changes are coming, the spoiled children react badly. Roxy suggests that they buy WBQL, a small station where they once worked that has gone off the air, using her retirement savings, and Aunt Jo contributes 45,000 dollars in cash. To raise his share, Rush puts the family's large house up for sale, and they move back into Jo's modest home, where they lived before he became famous.

CamCom pressures Malcolm to stop advertisers from buying airtime on the new station, so Rush and Roxy respond with billboards promoting a commercial-free Christmas, infuriating the corporation. A home video of Paula found among the old decorations brings back painful memories, especially for Jamal.

On the eve of their return to the airwaves, Rush and Roxy admit their feelings for each other over a romantic dinner. The girls are delighted, but Jamal, angry about the family's changed circumstances and convinced that he can no longer afford Harvard, runs away. Rush finds him in his late mother's favourite spot in the park, and Jamal confesses how hard it is to live in the house without her, before accepting his father's new relationship.

Rush promises to find a way to pay for Harvard, finally sells the house at a lower price, and a former WMLE colleague invests in WBQL, allowing it to broadcast over Christmas and beyond.

overview: Benjamin Franklin Gates and Dr. Abigail Chase re-team with Riley Poole and, now armed with a stack of long-lost pages from John Wilkes Booth's diary, Ben must follow a clue left there to prove his ancestor's innocence in the assassination of Abraham Lincoln.
tagline: The Greatest Adventure History Has Ever Revealed
title: National Treasure: Book of Secrets
plot:
National Treasure: Book of Secrets is a 2007 American action-adventure film directed by Jon Turteltaub, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, and written by Jim Kouf. The movie stars Nicolas Cage as Benjamin Gates, a treasure hunter with a passion for American history.

The film begins with Benjamin Gates (Nicolas Cage) being approached by the Treasury Department to help find a lost document known as the "Book of Secrets." The book is said to contain information about the Founding Fathers' involvement in the Knights Templar and their alleged discovery of the Holy Grail. However, the book has been stolen from the National Archives, and it's up to Gates to retrieve it.

Gates teams up with his partner, Riley Poole (Dustin Hoffman), a computer expert, and Abigail Chase ( Diane Kruger), an archaeologist. Together, they embark on a perilous journey across the United States, following a series of cryptic clues left behind by the book's thief.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, Gates and his team uncover a conspiracy involving the British government, which is trying to discredit Benjamin's claims about the Founding Fathers' involvement with the Knights Templar. The team also discovers that Abigail Chase is actually the daughter of John Adams, one of the Founding Fathers, making her a direct descendant of the president.

The plot thickens as Gates and his team encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and rival treasure hunters. Along the way, they meet Patrick Gates (Sean Bean), Benjamin's long-lost father, who reveals that he was also involved in the Knights Templar and had been searching for the Book of Secrets.

As the story unfolds, Gates and his team finally reach the location of the lost document: a hidden chamber beneath the White House. However, they soon realize that they are not alone, as they are confronted by the British government's agents, who will stop at nothing to keep the truth about the Founding Fathers' involvement with the Knights Templar from being revealed.

In the end, Gates and his team successfully retrieve the Book of Secrets, but not before a thrilling showdown with the rival treasure hunters. The film concludes with Benjamin Gates returning the book to its rightful place in the National Archives, while Abigail Chase comes to terms with her newfound heritage as a descendant of John Adams.

Throughout the movie, Nicolas Cage delivers his signature blend of humor, wit, and action hero charm, making National Treasure: Book of Secrets an entertaining and thrilling adventure that explores the fascinating world of American history and cryptography.

overview: The film mainly follows the famous 1597 Battle of Myeongryang during the Japanese invasion of Korea 1592-1598, where the iconic Joseon admiral Yi Sun-sin managed to destroy a total of 133 Japanese warships with only 13 ships remaining in his command. The battle, which took place in the Myeongryang Strait off the southwest coast of the Korean Peninsula, is considered one of the greatest victories of Yi.
tagline: 12 ships against a fleet of 330.
title: The Admiral: Roaring Currents
plot:
The Admiral: Roaring Currents is a 2014 South Korean naval action film directed by Kim Han-jun. The movie tells the story of Admiral Yi Sun-sin, a renowned Korean admiral who played a crucial role in the Imjin War against Japan.

At its core, The Admiral: Roaring Currents explores themes of patriotism, loyalty, and selflessness. The film delves into the life of Admiral Yi, who risked everything to defend his country against overwhelming odds. His unwavering dedication to Korea's independence is a testament to the power of conviction and courage in the face of adversity.

The movie also examines the complexities of war and its impact on individuals and society. Through Admiral Yi's story, the film highlights the human cost of conflict and the moral dilemmas that arise when faced with difficult decisions. The Admiral: Roaring Currents is a powerful tribute to the heroism and sacrifice of Admiral Yi Sun-sin, whose legacy continues to inspire Koreans to this day.

The film's portrayal of Admiral Yi as a complex and multifaceted character adds depth to the narrative, revealing a man who was both a brilliant strategist and a compassionate leader. His relationships with his comrades and subordinates are particularly noteworthy, showcasing the importance of teamwork, trust, and mutual respect in achieving greatness.

Ultimately, The Admiral: Roaring Currents is a stirring epic that celebrates the triumph of the human spirit over adversity, while also acknowledging the complexities and nuances of war.

overview: Master thief Will Montgomery is just released from the State penitentiary after serving a 10 year sentence, is contacted by Vincent, his ex comrade in crime, who is holding Will’s teenage daughter ransom in a hijacked taxi cab. Vincent will only surrender her when Will reveals the whereabouts of the 20 million dollars he contrived to conceal from their last robbery.
tagline: Never steal from the world's greatest thief.
title: Stolen
plot:
Stolen is a 2012 American action thriller directed by Simon West. Nicolas Cage stars as a master thief who has only twelve hours to raise ten million dollars and rescue his kidnapped daughter from a former partner, with Josh Lucas, Danny Huston, Malin Åkerman, Sami Gayle, M. C. Gainey and Mark Valley in supporting roles. It opened in the United States in September 2012.

In New Orleans, Will Montgomery and his partner Vincent Kinsey, backed by getaway driver Riley and computer expert Hoyt, carry out a robbery while FBI agent Tim Harlend waits to catch them at the jewelry store he believes is their target. Instead the thieves tunnel through a neighbouring toy shop into a bank vault and take ten million dollars. When Vincent tries to kill a janitor, Will intervenes and Vincent accidentally shoots himself in the leg, then drives off and abandons Will. Cornered by the FBI, Will burns the cash before his arrest, so no money is ever recovered.

Eight years later Will is paroled and returns to New Orleans under Harlend's watch, since the bureau is convinced he hid the loot. His estranged teenage daughter Alison refuses to speak to him and climbs into a taxi that has been trailing him. A phone left for Will rings: the driver is Vincent, long thought dead, who has locked Alison in the trunk and demands the ten million within twelve hours.

Using the crowds of Fat Tuesday to slip his FBI tail, Will diverts Vincent's calls to a second phone and tries to convince Harlend that he really destroyed the money, without success. He tracks down Hoyt, who is helping Vincent, and escapes custody more than once. Unable to produce the cash, he and Riley tunnel back under the same bank and use a thermal lance to melt down gold for the ransom.

The showdown takes place at an abandoned amusement park, where Vincent sets the taxi on fire with Alison inside. Will overcomes him, frees his daughter from the sinking car and survives. In a final twist, he fools Harlend by throwing a decoy nugget into the bayou while keeping some of the gold.

Stolen was poorly received, earning an 18% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 43, and became a box-office bomb in the United States, taking only about $183,000 on 141 screens in its opening weekend.

overview: Pete and Debbie are both about to turn 40, their kids hate each other, both of their businesses are failing, they're on the verge of losing their house, and their relationship is threatening to fall apart.
tagline: The sort-of sequel to 'Knocked Up'
title: This Is 40
plot:
This Is 40 is a 2012 American comedy-drama film directed by Judd Apatow and written by Apatow and Knocked Up co-writer Seth Rogen. The movie follows the story of Pete (Paul Rudd) and Debbie (Leslie Mann), a married couple who are struggling to maintain their relationship amidst personal issues, family problems, and midlife crises.

The main themes of This Is 40 include:

1. Marriage and relationships: The film explores the ups and downs of marriage, highlighting the challenges that couples face in maintaining intimacy, communication, and trust.
2. Midlife crisis: Pete's struggles with his own identity, career, and sense of purpose serve as a catalyst for the story, illustrating the difficulties of navigating midlife transitions.
3. Parenting and family dynamics: Debbie's relationship with her children, particularly her daughter Sadie (Maude Apatow), serves as a source of tension and conflict within the marriage.
4. Identity and self-discovery: Both Pete and Debbie grapple with finding their own identities outside of their roles as husband and wife, leading to a deeper exploration of their individual desires, needs, and aspirations.
5. Friendship and community: The film highlights the importance of friendships and relationships in navigating life's challenges, particularly for women like Debbie who often find themselves at the center of family dynamics.

Throughout the movie, Apatow tackles these themes with humor, wit, and a deep understanding of the complexities of human relationships. By exploring the intricacies of marriage, midlife crises, and personal growth, This Is 40 offers a relatable and authentic portrayal of modern life's challenges.

overview: High school loser (Cannon) pays a cheerleader (Milian) to pose as his girlfriend so he can be considered cool. Remake of 1987's Can't Buy Me Love, starring Patrick Dempsey.
tagline: Love Don't Co$t A Thing but it pays to be yourself.
title: Love Don't Co$t a Thing
plot:
Love Don't Cost a Thing is a 2003 American romantic comedy film directed by David E. Talbert, produced by Alcon Entertainment, and written by David E. Talbert.

The movie follows the story of Derek Matthews (played by Omarion), a high school student who has just transferred to a new school in Los Angeles. Derek is initially hesitant to fit in with his new classmates but eventually befriends two girls: Deena (played by Gabrielle Union) and Nia (played by Brandy Norwood).

Deena, the popular and beautiful cheerleader, catches Derek's eye, and they start dating. However, their relationship is put to the test when Deena starts to develop feelings for her ex-boyfriend, Darius (played by Simon Baker). Meanwhile, Nia, who is initially portrayed as a nerdy and awkward student, reveals her own romantic interests in Derek.

As the story unfolds, Derek finds himself torn between his growing feelings for both Deena and Nia. He struggles to balance his relationships with these two women while navigating high school life. The movie explores themes of love, friendship, and self-discovery as Derek learns valuable lessons about loyalty, trust, and being true to oneself.

Throughout the film, the characters face various challenges, including peer pressure, family expectations, and personal growth. The movie features a mix of humor, drama, and romance, making it an entertaining watch for audiences.

Ultimately, Derek must make a choice between his relationships with Deena and Nia. In the end, he decides to pursue a relationship with Nia, who has been a constant source of support and encouragement throughout his high school journey.

Love Don't Cost a Thing received mixed reviews from critics but was a moderate box office success. The movie's blend of humor, romance, and coming-of-age themes resonated with audiences, particularly young viewers.

overview: When a proposed pipeline creates hostilities between residents of a small town, a newly-arrived forest ranger must keep the peace after a snowstorm confines the townspeople to an old lodge. But when a mysterious creature begins terrorizing the group, their worst tendencies and prejudices rise to the surface, and it is up to the ranger to keep the residents alive, both from each other and the monster which plagues them.
tagline: A whodunnit with teeth.
title: Werewolves Within
plot:
Werewolves Within is a 2021 American comedy horror film directed by Josh Ruben and written by Josh Ruben and Michael Siller. The movie takes place in the fictional town of Red Rock, where a group of friends reunite for a wedding.

The story begins with Sam (Sam Richardson), a successful businessman who has lost his way after a painful divorce. He returns to his hometown of Red Rock for his friend's wedding, hoping to reconnect with old friends and find some closure. Upon arrival, he discovers that the town is hosting a "Werewolf Hunt" competition, where participants must figure out who among them is a werewolf.

Sam joins forces with his old friend, Emily (Milana Vayntrub), and together they start gathering clues to identify the werewolf. As the competition heats up, Sam finds himself drawn into a web of relationships and alliances that lead him to question everyone's intentions.

As the night wears on, the group discovers that one of their own is indeed a werewolf, but it's not who they expected. The werewolf is revealed to be none other than Emily's fiancé, Mike (Harvey Guillén). However, just as Sam thinks he has solved the mystery, new clues emerge, and the group realizes that there are multiple werewolves in the mix.

The plot thickens as alliances are formed and broken, and the group starts to turn on each other. In a shocking twist, it's revealed that one of the participants is not who they claim to be. The true identity of the imposter is slowly uncovered, leading to a thrilling climax.

As the night reaches its peak, Sam and Emily find themselves in a desperate bid to survive the werewolf attacks and uncover the truth behind the competition. In the end, only two people are left standing: Sam and Mike's best friend, Alex (Sam Leakey).

In a stunning finale, it's revealed that Alex is not who he claims to be either. The true identity of the imposter is finally exposed, leading to a chaotic confrontation between the remaining survivors.

The movie ends with Sam and Emily emerging victorious but shaken by their experience. As they reflect on what happened, they realize that some wounds may never fully heal, and that sometimes, the truth can be more terrifying than fiction.

Werewolves Within is a clever blend of horror and comedy, with a talented ensemble cast bringing depth and humor to the story. The movie's clever plot twists and unexpected turns keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: Thirteen-year-old Mei is experiencing the awkwardness of being a teenager with a twist – when she gets too excited, she transforms into a giant red panda.
tagline: Growing up is a beast.
title: Turning Red
plot:
Turning Red is a 2022 animated coming-of-age comedy-drama film produced by Walt Disney Pictures, Pixar Animation Studios, and Walt Disney Television Animation.

The story revolves around Meilin "Mei" Lee (voiced by Rosalie Chiang), a 13-year-old Chinese-Canadian girl who lives in Toronto with her mother, Ming (Sandra Oh). Mei is a sixth-grader at a local middle school, where she struggles to fit in and navigate the complexities of adolescence.

However, Mei has a secret: every time she experiences strong emotions, such as excitement or anxiety, she transforms into a giant red panda. This transformation, known as "the Beast," occurs due to a magical curse that was placed upon her by a Chinese folk tale.

As Mei navigates the challenges of middle school, including friendships, crushes, and family expectations, she must also contend with her own identity and the pressures of growing up. Her mother, who is going through her own midlife crisis, pushes Mei to excel academically and socially, while Mei longs for independence and self-expression.

Mei's relationships with her friends, including Miriam (Megan Thee Stallion), Priya (Ariana DeBose), and Abby (Jade West), are central to the story. Together, they form a tight-knit group that supports each other through the ups and downs of adolescence.

Throughout the film, Mei's struggles with her emotions and identity are juxtaposed with her desire for connection and belonging. The Beast serves as a metaphor for the turmoil and uncertainty of growing up, while also highlighting Mei's resilience and determination to find her place in the world.

Turning Red features stunning animation, vibrant music, and a talented voice cast that brings the characters to life. The film's themes of identity, family, and self-acceptance are timely and relatable, making it a must-watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Turning Red is a heartwarming and hilarious coming-of-age story that explores the complexities of adolescence with humor, sensitivity, and style.

overview: Sun Wukong is a monkey born from a heavenly stone who acquires supernatural powers. After rebelling against heaven and being imprisoned under a mountain for 500 years, he later accompanies the monk Xuanzang on a journey to India. Thus, according to legend, Buddhism is brought to ancient China.
production_companies: Beijing Wen Hua Dong Run Investment
tagline: Havoc in Heaven
title: The Monkey King
plot:
The Monkey King, also known as The Monkey King: Havoc in Heaven's Palace, is a 2014 Hong Kong and Chinese action fantasy film directed by Soi Cheang and starring Donnie Yen as Sun Wukong, the legendary Monkey King, with Yen also serving as action director. Chow Yun-fat co-stars as the Jade Emperor and Aaron Kwok as the Bull Demon King, with Joe Chen and Peter Ho. The story is based on an episode from Journey to the West, Wu Cheng'en's sixteenth-century Chinese literary classic, and the film was shot in 3D.

After the Bull Demon King leads a failed attack on Heaven, the Jade Emperor spares his life at the request of his sister, Princess Iron Fan, the Demon King's lover, and banishes the demons to Flaming Mountain. To rebuild Heaven, the goddess Nüwa sacrifices herself, and one of the crystals of her body falls to earth on Mount Huaguo, where over time it gives birth to a monkey. The creature is taken in by the sage Subhuti, who names him Sun Wukong and trains him in magical arts.

The Bull Demon King, still plotting revenge, schemes to use the brash, mischievous Wukong as a weapon against Heaven and secretly allies with Erlang Shen, the Jade Emperor's resentful nephew. Wukong acquires a magical staff from the palace of the Dragon King, causing chaos, and the Demon King flatters him with promises of Heaven's treasures and immortality. Wukong befriends a nine-tailed fox spirit and travels to Heaven, where he is given a lowly post caring for the celestial stables. Manipulated by the demons, he rebels and wreaks havoc in Heaven, unaware that his actions are part of a plan to destroy it.

The film relies heavily on computer-generated effects and spectacle, retelling the classic story of the Monkey King's rebellion against the gods.

After several delays, The Monkey King was released in Hong Kong and China at the end of January 2014 and set a record for the highest-grossing opening day in China. Reviews were mixed: Variety called it energetic but lacking style and substance, while ScreenAnarchy criticized its effects and script but praised Yen. A sequel, The Monkey King 2, followed in 2016.

overview: Happy young married couple Paige and Leo are, well, happy. Then a car accident puts Paige into a life-threatening coma. Upon awakening she has lost the previous five years of memories, including those of her beloved Leo, her wedding, a confusing relationship with her parents, or the ending of her relationship with her ex-fiance. Despite these complications, Leo endeavors to win her heart again and rebuild their marriage.
title: The Vow
plot:
The Vow is a 2012 American romantic drama film directed by Michael Sucsy and written by John Hamburg. The movie stars Channing Tatum, Rachel McAdams, and Jamie Foxx.

The story begins with Paige (Rachel McAdams), a young woman who suffers from amnesia due to a car accident. She wakes up in the hospital with no memory of her past life or her husband, Leo (Channing Tatum). As she tries to piece together her identity, she meets Leo's sister, Rachel (Anika Noni Rose), and his mother, Elizabeth (Marcia Gay Harden).

As Paige tries to rebuild her life, she begins to form a connection with Leo, who is patient and loving. However, their relationship is put to the test when Paige discovers that she has no memory of their time together. She struggles to reconcile her past and present selves, leading to tension in their relationship.

Meanwhile, Leo is trying to win Paige back by showing her old photos and mementos from their life together. He also tries to recreate their memories, hoping that they will resurface. However, Paige's amnesia makes it difficult for her to connect with Leo on an emotional level.

As the story progresses, Paige begins to experience flashbacks of her past life with Leo. She starts to remember small details, such as his favorite food and the way he used to make her laugh. These memories bring them closer together, but also raise questions about whether their relationship is real or just a product of Paige's imagination.

In the end, Paige's memories return, and she remembers everything about her life with Leo. However, she realizes that she has changed since the accident and that her past self was not as perfect as she thought. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Paige and Leo working to rebuild their relationship and create a new future together.

Throughout the movie, the director uses a non-linear narrative structure to convey Paige's amnesia and her journey of self-discovery. The film also explores themes of love, identity, and memory, raising questions about how our past experiences shape us who we are today.

Overall, The Vow is a romantic drama that explores the complexities of love and relationships. With strong performances from its leads, the movie delivers an emotional and engaging story that will keep audiences invested in Paige and Leo's journey.

overview: When an insatiable great white shark terrorizes the townspeople of Amity Island, the police chief, an oceanographer and a grizzled shark hunter seek to destroy the blood-thirsty beast.
tagline: Don't go in the water
title: Jaws
plot:
Jaws is a thriller film directed by Steven Spielberg, released in 1975 by Universal Pictures.

The story begins on Amity Island, where police chief Martin Brody (Roy Scheider) and marine biologist Matt Hooper (Richard Dreyfuss) are investigating the death of a young woman whose body has been found in the water. As they delve deeper into the case, they discover that several other people have also gone missing or been killed by a massive great white shark.

The island's mayor, Larry Vaughn (Murray Hamilton), is more concerned with the impact on tourism than with finding a solution to the problem. However, Brody and Hooper team up with grizzled fisherman Quint (Robert Shaw) to hunt down and kill the shark.

As they set out to sea, Quint reveals that he has a personal vendetta against sharks, having lost his boat and crew in a previous encounter with a great white. The three men embark on a perilous journey across the ocean, facing treacherous waters and a formidable predator.

The tension builds as the shark begins to attack their boat, and the men are forced to fight for survival. Quint's obsession with killing the shark becomes increasingly apparent, and his character's backstory is slowly revealed through a series of flashbacks.

As the story unfolds, Brody and Hooper begin to realize that they may not be able to kill the shark after all. The great white has become a formidable foe, and its attacks are becoming more frequent and intense. In a thrilling climax, Quint sacrifices himself to save his crewmates from the jaws of death.

In the end, Brody and Hooper manage to kill the shark using a combination of explosives and a harpoon gun. As they return to shore, they are hailed as heroes for saving the island and its people from the terror of the great white shark.

Throughout the film, Spielberg masterfully builds tension and suspense, using a combination of music, camera angles, and editing techniques to create a sense of unease and fear in the audience. The iconic score by John Williams adds to the tension, with the ominous two-note theme becoming synonymous with the film's title.

Overall, Jaws is a classic thriller that has stood the test of time, thanks to its well-crafted story, memorable characters, and suspenseful plot.

overview: Liam wakes from a car crash with no memory of who he is. As he makes his way into town to look for help, he finds only dead bodies, all with strange pale eyes. Liam's first assessment is that a virus is present in the air, but he soon discovers the horrible truth: anyone who comes within a 50-foot radius of him dies instantly.
tagline: Don't get too close
title: Radius
plot:
Radius is a 2017 Canadian science fiction thriller written and directed by Caroline Labrèche and Steeve Léonard. Diego Klattenhoff and Charlotte Sullivan star as two amnesiac survivors of a car crash, with Brett Donahue and Bradley Sawatzky in supporting roles. It premiered at the Fantasia International Film Festival in July 2017.

A man awakens in a wrecked car with no memory of who he is. He flags down a passing driver, who dies suddenly, sending the car off the road. Checking his wallet, he learns that his name is Liam Hartwell. Walking toward the nearest town, he stops at a roadside diner and finds everyone inside dead. Believing the air must be poisoned, he covers his face with a strip of his shirt and keeps going. Using a map and the address on his driver's license, he finds his house, where radio and television reports speculate about a biological attack. As he tapes up the windows, he spots a farmer outside and tries to warn him away, but when the man approaches he drops dead, and Liam realizes that animals also die whenever they come near him. He is not escaping a virus: he is the cause of the deaths.

A woman who also has amnesia arrives at Liam's door and tells him that she was with him in the car at the time of the accident. To his astonishment, she can come close to him without dying. Neither knows why they were traveling together or what caused the crash. Calling herself Jane Doe, she accompanies Liam back to the crash site, where they find a strange charred circle on the ground. They discover that anyone who comes within a certain radius of Liam dies, unless Jane is near him, in which case her presence cancels the effect. Bound together by this mysterious connection, they try to uncover their identities and the event that caused it, but the truths they uncover about their pasts, and about who they really were before the crash, are more disturbing than either expected.

Radius received positive reviews, with a 93 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on fifteen reviews. Critics praised its intriguing high-concept premise, the performances of Klattenhoff and Sullivan and the filmmakers' ability to build suspense on a modest budget.

overview: Raised in a poverty-stricken slum, a 16-year-old girl named Starr now attends a suburban prep school. After she witnesses a police officer shoot her unarmed best friend, she's torn between her two very different worlds as she tries to speak her truth.
tagline: Two worlds. One voice. No going back.
title: The Hate U Give
plot:
The Hate U Give is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores themes of racism, police brutality, activism, and identity. Directed by George Tillman Jr., the movie is based on the young adult novel of the same name by Angie Thomas.

The story follows 16-year-old Starr Carter (played by Amandla Stenberg), a black teenager who lives in the predominantly white and affluent neighborhood of Williamson, Georgia. However, her life takes a drastic turn when she transfers to a low-income black school in Garden Heights, where she is surrounded by poverty, violence, and police brutality.

Starr's dual identity becomes a central theme of the film. She navigates between two worlds: the privileged world of Williamson, where she has grown up with her middle-class family, and the harsh realities of Garden Heights, where she finds herself among friends who are struggling to survive.

The plot thickens when Starr witnesses the fatal shooting of her friend Khalil (played by Algee Smith) by a white police officer, Chris Breaux (played by Brian Tyree Henry). The incident sparks widespread outrage and protests in Garden Heights, while the Williamson community is largely oblivious to the event.

As news of Khalil's death spreads, Starr becomes an unlikely activist and voice for her community. She uses social media to share her story and raise awareness about police brutality and systemic racism. However, this newfound attention also puts her at odds with her family, particularly her mother, Lisa (played by Regina Hall), who wants to keep a low profile.

Throughout the film, Starr grapples with the complexities of activism, identity, and community. She must confront the harsh realities of police brutality and systemic racism, while also navigating her relationships with her friends, family, and romantic partner, Chris (played by KJ Apa).

The Hate U Give is a powerful exploration of the Black Lives Matter movement and the struggles faced by young black people in America. The film's portrayal of police brutality, racial profiling, and systemic inequality is unflinching and thought-provoking.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Starr and Chris Breaux, as well as a dramatic showdown between the Garden Heights community and the Williamson police department. The ending is both heart-wrenching and hopeful, leaving audiences with a sense of urgency and a renewed commitment to fighting for justice and equality.

Overall, The Hate U Give is a powerful and timely film that sheds light on the struggles faced by young black people in America. With its talented cast, thought-provoking themes, and unflinching portrayal of police brutality, it's a movie that will leave you thinking long after the credits roll.

overview: One day, Horton the elephant hears a cry from help coming from a speck of dust. Even though he can't see anyone on the speck, he decides to help it. As it turns out, the speck of dust is home to the Whos, who live in their city of Whoville. Horton agrees to help protect the Whos and their home.
tagline: A person's a person no matter how small!
title: Horton Hears a Who!
plot:
Dr. Seuss' Horton Hears a Who! is a 2008 American computer-animated adventure comedy based on Dr. Seuss's 1954 book. Produced by 20th Century Fox Animation and Blue Sky Studios, it was directed by Jimmy Hayward and Steve Martino and written by Cinco Paul and Ken Daurio. Jim Carrey voices Horton the Elephant and Steve Carell voices Mayor Ned McDodd, with Will Arnett, Seth Rogen, Dan Fogler, Isla Fisher, Jonah Hill, Jaime Pressly, Amy Poehler and Carol Burnett, and narration by Charles Osgood. It was released in March 2008.

In the Jungle of Nool, Horton, an eccentric and kind-hearted elephant, hears a faint cry coming from a speck of dust drifting through the air. Convinced that someone tiny lives on it, he catches the speck on a clover. The speck holds Whoville, a city of microscopic Whos, led by Mayor Ned McDodd, who has a wife, Sally, ninety-six daughters and one son, JoJo, a silent teenager who fears disappointing his father by not wanting to become mayor. As Horton carries the speck around, Whoville experiences strange disturbances, and the mayor's warnings are dismissed by the town council and its condescending chairman.

When the mayor makes contact with Horton through a drainpipe, he learns from a scientist, Dr. LaRue, that Whoville will be destroyed unless it is moved to a safer place. Horton, helped by his friend Morton the Mouse, sets out to carry the speck to the top of Mount Nool. The Sour Kangaroo, the self-appointed guardian of the jungle's values, refuses to believe in anything she cannot see or hear and views Horton's claims as a threat to the jungle's children. She hires the vulture Vlad to steal the speck, and Horton must search a vast field of identical clovers to find it. As the jungle animals turn against Horton and threaten to destroy the speck, the mayor must convince his own people of the elephant's existence, and every Who in Whoville must raise their voices so they can be heard, with an unexpected contribution from JoJo.

Horton Hears a Who! received generally positive reviews for its animation, humor and faithfulness to the spirit of the book. It was a commercial success, grossing nearly $300 million worldwide, and it was the first fully computer-animated feature based on a Dr. Seuss story.

overview: In Knockemstiff, Ohio and its neighboring backwoods, sinister characters converge around young Arvin Russell as he fights the evil forces that threaten him and his family.
tagline: Everyone ends up in the same damned place.
title: The Devil All the Time
plot:
The Devil All the Time is a 2020 American psychological horror film written and directed by Antonio Campos. The movie is based on the 2011 novel of the same name by Donald Ray Pollock.

The story takes place in rural Ohio, West Virginia, and Kentucky during the 1960s. The plot revolves around several interconnected characters, each struggling with their own personal demons.

Arthur Leander (played by Robert Pattinson), a middle-aged theater director, dies on stage after a heart attack. His death sets off a chain of events that affects those around him. Arthur's wife, Elizabeth (played by Eliza Scanlen), is left to care for his young daughter, Ruthie (played by Brooklynn Prince).

Meanwhile, in the same town, a serial killer named Will Buie III (played by Riley Keough) is on the loose, targeting young women and girls. The police are unable to catch him, and the community is gripped with fear.

In another part of the country, a preacher named Preston Teagarden (played by Bill Skarsgård) is struggling with his own faith after witnessing a traumatic event in his childhood. He becomes obsessed with finding Will Buie III, who he believes is responsible for the death of his sister.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Arthur's death and Will's crimes are connected to a larger conspiracy involving corrupt politicians, law enforcement officials, and church leaders. The characters' paths continue to cross and intersect, leading to a tragic confrontation.

Throughout the film, Campos explores themes of trauma, faith, and the darkness that lurks beneath the surface of small-town America. The Devil All the Time is a slow-burning, atmospheric horror film that builds tension through its use of long takes, eerie sound design, and outstanding performances from its cast.

The movie's climax features a shocking confrontation between Preston and Will, which ultimately leads to a devastating conclusion. Without giving away too many spoilers, it can be said that the ending is both haunting and thought-provoking, leaving the audience with a lasting sense of unease.

Overall, The Devil All the Time is a masterful horror film that weaves together multiple storylines into a complex tapestry of suspense and terror. With its outstanding cast, atmospheric direction, and thought-provoking themes, it's a must-see for fans of psychological horror.

overview: In lawless badlands, reclusive Cabeleira sets out to discover the fate of his gunman father and grows to be a feared assassin himself.
title: The Killer
plot:
The Killer (Portuguese: O Matador) is a 2017 Brazilian neo-western written and directed by Marcelo Galvão. Set in the arid backlands of northeastern Brazil, it belongs to the regional genre sometimes called the "nordestern," which blends the conventions of the American western with the history and folklore of the cangaço bandits. Diogo Morgado stars as Cabeleira, known in English as Shaggy, with Étienne Chicot, Deto Montenegro, Nill Marcondes, Igor Cotrim, Maria de Medeiros and Paulo Gorgulho. Filming began in August 2016, and Netflix released the film worldwide on 10 November 2017.

The story takes place between the 1910s and the 1940s in the state of Pernambuco. As a baby, Cabeleira is found abandoned by Sete Orelhas, or Seven Ears, a local cangaceiro bandit and gunman, who raises him in the wilderness of the sertão, completely cut off from civilization. Under the outlaw's guidance the boy grows into a skilled marksman, knowing nothing of the world beyond their isolated life.

When Seven Ears mysteriously disappears, the grown Cabeleira finally ventures into town to look for him. There he finds a lawless place ruled by Monsieur Blanchard, a tyrannical Frenchman who controls the lucrative trade in precious stones and had previously employed Seven Ears as his hired killer. Drawn into Blanchard's service, Cabeleira himself becomes a feared assassin, carrying out killings for the Frenchman while searching for answers about his foster father's fate. Over the years, his violent career brings him into contact with a gallery of characters, including the local authorities represented by Lieutenant Raul Sobral, and as he discovers the truth about what happened to Seven Ears and about Blanchard's power, he is forced to confront the brutal world that shaped him.

The Killer was the first Brazilian fiction feature produced as a Netflix original and released exclusively on the platform. Brazilian critics praised its cinematography and its evocative re-creation of the sertão, but many found the screenplay overloaded with characters and subplots and criticized its heavy use of narration and its visual effects.

overview: A young Nurse is assigned to look after a patient in a remote location in the English countryside. As the night continues she finds herself terrorized by an unseen force that is connected with her patient.
tagline: Something is alive.
title: Whisper
plot:
Whisper is a 2022 British supernatural horror film directed, co-produced and co-edited by Christopher Jolley from a screenplay he wrote with co-producer Robert Dunn. Made by Greenway Entertainment on a reported budget of about $20,000, it was executive produced by a team including Jeff Haber, Valon Jakupaj, Carly Jolley, Angela McLellan, Jamie Weston and Steven M. Smith, Jolley's collaborator on films such as The Haunting of Borley Rectory and Doll House. The film stars Linda Louise Duan as a young nurse, with Richard Conrad, Amy Secker, Arron Blake, Ben Maytham, Penelope Read, Carly Jolley, Nadia Nadif, Roman Wood and Paige Jolley in supporting roles. It was released in January 2022, later streamed on Amazon Prime Video and Tubi, and runs 76 minutes.

Sam (Duan), a young nurse, is assigned to care for a comatose patient (Conrad) at a remote, dark house in the English countryside, a job that leaves her alone with him through the night. As the hours pass she begins nosing around the house and uncovers a plot to unleash dark forces from within the human mind. Of those involved, her patient proved the most successful at reaching the malevolent entity, and as the night continues Sam finds herself terrorised by an unseen presence connected to him. Other characters include Dr. Carpenter (Read), Dr. Wright (Wood), Gwen (Secker), Joe (Blake) and a figure credited as the Old Hag (Nadif); the entity's full form is withheld until the final moments.

Writing on his horror review site MLMillerFrights, M. L. Miller called the film a wonderful mix of the coma horror classic Patrick and David Holroyd's The Haunted by way of Ti West's The House of the Devil. He praised the way it used the dark corners of the house to build a strong sense of foreboding even before the scares began, its subtle effects held back at the edges of the frame, and its tight, shadowy camerawork, and wrote that despite its very low budget the film enveloped the viewer with a sense of urgency. He found the dark entity genuinely frightening when it finally appeared, making the wait worthwhile, and concluded that Whisper told a fairly complex story with simple nuance and the familiar haunted-house play of shadow and light, to good effect.

overview: Despondent over a painful estrangement from his daughter, trainer Frankie Dunn isn't prepared for boxer Maggie Fitzgerald to enter his life. But Maggie's determined to go pro and to convince Dunn and his cohort to help her.
tagline: Beyond his silence, there is a past. Beyond her dreams, there is a feeling. Beyond hope, there is a memory. Beyond their journey, there is a love.
title: Million Dollar Baby
plot:
Million Dollar Baby is a 2004 American sports drama film directed by Clint Eastwood, produced by Lawrence Bender, and written by Paul Haggis. The movie stars Clint Eastwood, Hilary Swank, Morgan Freeman, and Jay Baruchel.

The story revolves around Maggie Fitzgerald (Hilary Swank), a young and ambitious female boxer from the wrong side of the tracks in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Maggie is a small-town girl with big dreams, who has always been fascinated by boxing. Despite her lack of experience and financial resources, she finds an old boxing gym in town where she meets Frankie Dunn (Clint Eastwood), a grizzled and retired boxer who has become a trainer.

Frankie is initially hesitant to take Maggie under his wing, but eventually warms up to her determination and spirit. As they begin training together, Maggie's natural talent and dedication quickly become apparent, and Frankie starts to see her as a potential champion. However, their relationship is complicated by Frankie's troubled past, which has left him emotionally scarred.

As Maggie's skills improve, she attracts the attention of Eddie "Scrap-Iron" Dupris (Morgan Freeman), a former boxer who becomes her mentor and confidant. Eddie, who was once a champion himself, sees potential in Maggie and helps her refine her technique. The three form an unlikely bond, with Frankie serving as Maggie's trainer, Eddie providing guidance, and Maggie becoming the driving force behind their partnership.

As Maggie's career takes off, she faces stiff competition from other boxers, including the ruthless and cunning Billie "The Blue Bear" (Blythe Danner). Despite her success in the ring, Maggie struggles with the physical toll of boxing and the emotional scars left by her past. Frankie, who has become a surrogate father figure to Maggie, tries to guide her through these challenges.

Tragedy strikes when Maggie suffers a devastating spinal cord injury during a fight, leaving her paralyzed from the neck down. The movie takes a heart-wrenching turn as Maggie's dreams of becoming a champion are shattered, and she must come to terms with her new reality.

In the end, Frankie makes the difficult decision to euthanize Maggie, citing that her quality of life has deteriorated significantly due to her injury. The film ends with Frankie saying goodbye to Maggie, surrounded by Eddie and other loved ones, as he finally finds closure and peace after years of emotional turmoil.

Million Dollar Baby is a powerful and poignant exploration of the human spirit, tackling themes of perseverance, redemption, and the true cost of ambition. The movie features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Hilary Swank, who won the Academy Award for Best Actress for her portrayal of Maggie Fitzgerald.

overview: When a science experiment goes horribly wrong, gigantic fish gain appetites for human flesh.
tagline: They were created to save mankind. Something went wrong.
title: Mega Piranha
plot:
Mega Piranha is a 2010 campy horror-comedy film directed by Don Michael Paul and produced by The Asylum. The movie's main theme revolves around the dangers of playing with nature and the consequences of scientific hubris.

The story follows a group of people who are trapped on an island where a genetically engineered species of super-piranhas has been created, leading to a deadly attack on the human population. Through this narrative, the film explores the idea that tampering with the natural world can have disastrous results, highlighting the importance of respecting and understanding the delicate balance of ecosystems.

The movie also touches on the theme of survival and human resilience in the face of overwhelming odds. As the characters struggle to stay alive against the ferocious piranhas, they are forced to confront their own mortality and the limits of their abilities. This serves as a commentary on the human condition, where individuals must often rely on their wits, resourcefulness, and teamwork to overcome seemingly insurmountable challenges.

Furthermore, Mega Piranha can be seen as a satirical critique of modern society's obsession with scientific progress and technological advancements without considering the potential consequences. The film's over-the-top portrayal of the piranhas' rampage serves as a tongue-in-cheek commentary on our own world's environmental concerns and the dangers of unchecked industrialization.

Overall, Mega Piranha is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses its absurd premise to explore thought-provoking themes about nature, survival, and the human condition.

overview: As four friends prepare for life after high school, different challenges bring about turning points in each of their lives. The dramas unfold and resolve at their local rollerskating rink, Cascade.
tagline: A New American Story
title: ATL
plot:
ATL is a poignant coming-of-age drama that delves into the complexities of life, love, and loss in the vibrant Atlanta community of the 1970s. The film masterfully weaves together themes of identity, community, and the struggles of growing up.

At its core, ATL explores the fragility of adolescence, where young people are navigating the treacherous waters of self-discovery, peer pressure, and first loves. The characters' experiences are marked by a sense of restlessness, as they grapple with their place in the world and the expectations placed upon them by family, friends, and society.

The film also sheds light on the rich cultural heritage of Atlanta's African American community during this era, showcasing the city's music scene, fashion, and traditions. Through its characters' experiences, ATL celebrates the resilience and creativity of black culture, highlighting the ways in which art and self-expression can serve as a powerful means of coping with adversity.

Furthermore, ATL tackles the harsh realities of poverty, violence, and social inequality, offering a nuanced portrayal of life in the inner city during this period. The film's characters are often forced to confront the harsh consequences of systemic injustices, leading to a deeper understanding of the cyclical nature of trauma and the importance of community support.

Ultimately, ATL is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that balances the joys and struggles of growing up with the complexities of adulthood. Through its well-developed characters and vivid storytelling, the film offers a poignant reminder of the enduring power of love, friendship, and resilience in the face of adversity.

overview: Mr. Church reunites the Expendables for what should be an easy paycheck, but when one of their men is murdered on the job, their quest for revenge puts them deep in enemy territory and up against an unexpected threat.
tagline: Back for War.
title: The Expendables 2
plot:
The Expendables 2 is a 2012 action film directed by Simon West and written by Richard Wenk. The movie stars Sylvester Stallone, Jason Statham, Jet Li, Dolph Lundgren, Randy Couture, Bruce Willis, and Arnold Schwarzenegger.

The story begins with Barney Ross (Sylvester Stallone), the leader of a group of elite mercenaries known as The Expendables, who are hired by a wealthy businessman named Mr. Smith (Samuel L. Jackson) to take down a ruthless dictator named Medivac (Jean-Claude Van Damme). However, things take a turn when Ross discovers that Medivac is actually working for a powerful arms dealer named Mr. Church (Arnold Schwarzenegger), who has been secretly manipulating the situation to further his own interests.

As The Expendables embark on their mission, they are joined by new recruits including Billy Ray Lynch (Randy Couture) and Lee Christmas (Jason Statham). However, things quickly go awry when the team discovers that Medivac is not just a simple dictator, but a complex character with his own motivations and backstory.

Throughout the movie, The Expendables face off against a series of formidable opponents, including Medivac's henchmen and Church's deadly mercenaries. Along the way, Ross must also confront his own demons and make difficult choices that will impact the fate of his team.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Mr. Church is not just a simple arms dealer, but a mastermind who has been manipulating events from behind the scenes. He reveals that he has been using Medivac to further his own agenda, which involves selling advanced military technology to the highest bidder.

In the end, The Expendables must use all their skills and resources to take down Mr. Church and his minions. The movie culminates in an epic showdown between Ross and Church, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance.

The Expendables 2 received mixed reviews from critics, but was a commercial success, grossing over $285 million worldwide. Despite its flaws, the movie delivered on its promise of high-octane action and explosive set pieces, making it a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: In the Old West, a 17-year-old Scottish boy teams up with a mysterious gunman to find the woman with whom he is infatuated.
tagline: Wanted Dead or Dead
title: Slow West
plot:
Slow West is a 2015 Western drama film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the search for identity. The story follows a young man named Jake, who sets out on a journey to find his missing fiancée, Miss Rose. Along the way, he encounters a mysterious stranger named Jay Cavendish, who joins him on his quest.

As they travel through the American West, the two men engage in a cat-and-mouse game with a ruthless outlaw, Mr. Stevens, who is also searching for Miss Rose. Through their interactions, Jake and Jay develop an unlikely bond, which serves as a catalyst for exploring themes of loneliness, isolation, and the human need for connection.

The film delves into the idea that people are often driven by a deep-seated desire to belong and find meaning in their lives. Jake's search for Miss Rose is motivated by his love for her, but also by his own sense of identity and purpose. Jay, on the other hand, seems to be searching for something more profound – a sense of belonging and acceptance.

Throughout the film, the director, John Maclean, uses the vast landscapes of the American West as a metaphor for the characters' inner journeys. The open spaces serve as a backdrop for the men's introspections, allowing them to confront their demons and grapple with their emotions in a way that feels both authentic and cathartic.

Ultimately, Slow West is a film about the power of human connection and the redemptive qualities of love and friendship. Despite its dark and violent undertones, the movie ultimately offers a message of hope and resilience, suggesting that even in the most desolate of landscapes, there is always the possibility for growth, transformation, and redemption.

overview: When three friends finally come to after a raucous night of bachelor-party revelry, they find a baby in the closet and a tiger in the bathroom. But they can't seem to locate their best friend, Doug – who's supposed to be tying the knot. Launching a frantic search for Doug, the trio perseveres through a nasty hangover to try to make it to the church on time.
tagline: Some guys just can't handle Vegas.
title: The Hangover
plot:
The Hangover is a 2009 American comedy film directed by Todd Phillips and written by Craig Mazin and Scott Moore. The movie follows the story of a group of friends who wake up after a wild bachelor party in Las Vegas with no memory of the night before.

The film begins with Phil Wenneck (Bradley Cooper), Stu Price (Ed Helms), Alan Garner (Zach Galifianakis), and Doug Billings (Justin Bartha) preparing for Doug's wedding to his fiancée, Tracy (Jamie Chung). The group decides to take a wild bachelor party to Las Vegas, where they spend the night drinking, dancing, and getting into various misadventures.

The next morning, the friends wake up in Phil's hotel suite with no memory of what happened the night before. They soon discover that Doug is missing, and their friend's wedding is just hours away. As they try to piece together the events of the previous night, they find a tiger in the bathroom, a missing front tooth for Stu, and a mysterious woman named Jade (Heather Graham) who claims to have slept with them.

As the friends try to track down Doug and figure out what happened to him, they encounter various obstacles, including a wild goose chase through the streets of Las Vegas, a run-in with a group of thugs, and a series of hilarious misadventures. Along the way, they also discover that Jade is not who she claims to be, and that the night before was much more eventful than they initially thought.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the friends had a wild and crazy night in Las Vegas, involving sex, drugs, and general debauchery. They eventually track down Doug's whereabouts and are able to return him to his fiancée just in time for the wedding.

The movie ends with the friends reflecting on the events of the previous night and the consequences that followed. While they all agree that it was a wild and crazy adventure, they also acknowledge that it may have been a mistake. The film ends with a comedic twist, as the friends are seen walking away from the wedding ceremony, still trying to process what happened the night before.

Throughout the movie, the humor is driven by the absurdity of the situation and the characters' reactions to it. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Zach Galifianakis as the eccentric and unpredictable Alan Garner. The film's success can be attributed to its well-crafted script, clever direction, and talented cast, which all come together to create a hilarious and entertaining movie experience.

Overall, The Hangover is a raunchy and irreverent comedy that explores themes of friendship, bachelorhood, and the consequences of one's actions. While it may not be for everyone, the film has become a cult classic and spawned two successful sequels.

overview: Team America World Police follows an international police force dedicated to maintaining global stability. Learning that dictator Kim Jong il is out to destroy the world, the team recruits Broadway star Gary Johnston to go undercover. With the help of Team America, Gary manages to uncover the plan to destroy the world. Will Team America be able to save it in time? It stars… Samuel L Jackson, Tim Robbins, Sean Penn, Michael Moore, Helen Hunt, Matt Damon, Susan Sarandon, George Clooney, Danny Glover, Ethan Hawke, Alec Baldwin… or does it?
tagline: Freedom Hangs By A Thread
title: Team America: World Police
plot:
Team America: World Police is a satirical comedy film that critiques the politics and culture of the United States during the early 2000s. The movie follows the adventures of a marionette action figure named Team America, who is part of an elite special forces unit known as the "World Police." As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Team America's mission is not just to fight terrorism and evil, but also to promote American values and interests.

One of the main themes of the film is the absurdity and hypocrisy of modern-day politics. The movie pokes fun at the notion of patriotism and nationalism, highlighting the ways in which politicians and celebrities can be manipulated by special interest groups and corporate sponsors. Team America's character is a perfect example of this, as he is created to promote American values but ultimately becomes a tool for propaganda and manipulation.

Another theme that runs throughout the film is the tension between individual freedom and national security. The World Police are tasked with fighting terrorism and protecting American interests, but their methods often border on absurdity and violence. This raises questions about the limits of government power and the importance of individual rights and freedoms.

The movie also explores the theme of celebrity culture and its impact on society. Team America's character is a parody of Hollywood stars like George W. Bush and Dick Cheney, who are portrayed as self-absorbed and out of touch with reality. The film critiques the way in which celebrities can be used to promote propaganda and manipulate public opinion.

Overall, Team America: World Police is a satirical comedy that uses humor and irony to critique modern-day politics and culture. By exaggerating the absurdities of patriotism and celebrity culture, the film raises important questions about individual freedom, national security, and the role of government in society.

overview: Maggie's plan to have a baby on her own is derailed when she falls in love with John, a married man, destroying his volatile marriage to the brilliant and impossible Georgette. But one daughter and three years later, Maggie is out of love and in a quandary: what do you do when you suspect your man and his ex wife are actually perfect for each other?
tagline: Chapter One: Maggie Meets John
title: Maggie's Plan
plot:
Maggie's Plan is a 2016 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Noah Baumbach. The movie follows Maggie (played by Greta Gerwig) and her plans to get pregnant, as well as her complicated relationships with two men: Scott (played by Ethan Hawke), who is already in a relationship, and Thomas (played by Julianne Moore's character's husband's friend, played by Julianne Moore's character's love interest, but actually played by  John Magaro).

The main theme of Maggie's Plan revolves around the complexities of human relationships, desire, and identity. The film explores how people navigate their desires, often leading to unexpected consequences. It also delves into the idea of self-discovery and the search for meaning in life.

Maggie's character is a prime example of this theme, as she struggles with her own desires and sense of purpose. Her plans to get pregnant are not just about fulfilling a biological need but also about finding a sense of belonging and connection with others. Throughout the film, Maggie's relationships with Scott and Thomas serve as catalysts for her growth and self-discovery.

The movie also touches on the theme of love and its many forms. It portrays love as a complex and multifaceted emotion that can be both exhilarating and painful. The film suggests that love is not just about romantic relationships but also about the connections we make with others, including friends and family members.

Overall, Maggie's Plan is a thought-provoking exploration of human relationships, desire, and identity, inviting viewers to reflect on their own desires and sense of purpose in life.

overview: Set in 1944, Valiant is a woodland pigeon who wants to become a great hero someday. When he hears they are hiring recruits for the Royal Homing Pigeon Service, he immediately sets out for London. On the way, he meets a smelly but friendly pigeon named Bugsy, who joins him, mainly to get away from clients he cheated in a game of find-the pebble, and helps him sign up for the war.
tagline: Featherweight Heroes.
title: Valiant
plot:
Valiant is a 2005 animated action-adventure film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Valiant, a young pigeon who dreams of becoming a spy and joining the elite Flock of Sparrowhawks.

The main themes of Valiant include:

1. **Perseverance and determination**: Valiant faces numerous challenges and setbacks throughout his journey, but he never gives up on his dream of becoming a spy. His perseverance ultimately leads him to achieve his goal.
2. **Loyalty and friendship**: Valiant forms strong bonds with his fellow pigeons, particularly Archer and Bugsy, who become his allies in the fight against the evil rat, General Shen. Their loyalty and trust in each other are crucial to their success.
3. **Self-discovery and identity**: As Valiant navigates the world of espionage, he learns more about himself and his place within the Flock of Sparrowhawks. He discovers that being different is not a weakness, but rather a strength that can be leveraged to achieve great things.
4. **Good vs. evil**: The movie features an epic battle between good (the Flock of Sparrowhawks) and evil (General Shen's rat army). Valiant's bravery and cunning ultimately lead to the defeat of the enemy forces.

The film also explores themes of:

* **Growing up and maturity**: Valiant learns valuable lessons about responsibility, courage, and leadership as he takes on more significant roles within the Flock.
* **Teamwork and collaboration**: The movie highlights the importance of working together towards a common goal, as the pigeons use their unique skills to outsmart and defeat their enemies.

Overall, Valiant is an inspiring tale of self-discovery, perseverance, and loyalty, with a healthy dose of action, adventure, and humor.

overview: Ace assassin Frank Kitchen is double crossed by gangsters and falls into the hands of rogue surgeon known as The Doctor who turns him into a woman. The hitman, now a hitwoman, sets out for revenge, aided by a nurse named Johnnie who also has secrets.
tagline: A revenger's tale.
title: The Assignment
plot:
The Assignment, also released as Tomboy and, in Australia, as Revenger, is an action crime thriller directed by Walter Hill, who co-wrote it with Denis Hamill. Michelle Rodriguez plays a professional hitman who is surgically transformed into a woman against his will, and Sigourney Weaver plays the disgraced surgeon responsible, with Tony Shalhoub, Anthony LaPaglia and Caitlin Gerard. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 11, 2016.

The story moves between two timelines. In the present, Dr. Rachel Jane, a brilliant but unhinged plastic surgeon who lost her licence and went on to perform illegal experiments on vulnerable homeless patients, is confined in a psychiatric institution where Dr. Ralph Galen is assessing her mental state. In the past, she sets out to avenge her brother Sebastian, who was murdered by the contract killer Frank Kitchen.

Through the gangster Honest John, Jane has Frank betrayed and captured. Driven by revenge and by curiosity about how much physical identity shapes a person, she performs gender reassignment surgery on him. Frank wakes in a hotel room in a female body, breaks down, and finds hormones and a taped message from the doctor urging him to start a new life. He takes refuge with Johnnie, a woman he once slept with, while he recovers.

Once he learns the operation cannot be undone, Frank begins killing everyone connected with it, including Honest John's men. He discovers that Johnnie was paid to watch him, but he spares her after realising she acted out of fear and has come to care for him, and she helps him set a trap. Jane's bodyguards capture Frank instead, and she plans to amputate his arm so he can never kill again. He breaks free, kills her guards and assistant, and shoots Jane without killing her.

In the institution, Jane gives a deposition explaining her actions without remorse. The film reveals that Frank arranged the scene to blame her assistant and cut off her fingers so she can never operate again.

Saban Films released the film on video on demand in March 2017 and in limited cinemas the following month. Reviews were negative, with a 33% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: With their golden era long behind them, comedy duo Stan Laurel and Oliver Hardy embark on a variety hall tour of Britain and Ireland. Despite the pressures of a hectic schedule, and with the support of their wives Lucille and Ida – a formidable double act in their own right – the pair's love of performing, as well as for each other, endures as they secure their place in the hearts of their adoring public
tagline: The untold story of the world's greatest comedy act.
title: Stan & Ollie
plot:
Stan & Ollie is a 2018 biographical comedy-drama film that explores the complex and enduring friendship between two of the most iconic comedians of the silent era, Charlie Chaplin and Stan Laurel. The movie delves into the highs and lows of their partnership, which spanned over three decades.

At its core, the film is a poignant portrayal of the power of friendship and the sacrifices that come with it. The story follows the two comedians as they navigate the challenges of fame, personal struggles, and creative differences, all while maintaining an unbreakable bond that transcends their professional relationship.

One of the main themes of Stan & Ollie is the struggle for artistic control and the tension between commercial success and creative integrity. As Chaplin's star rises, he finds himself at odds with Laurel, who feels overshadowed by his partner's success. This conflict serves as a backdrop to explore the complexities of their relationship, revealing the deep-seated insecurities and vulnerabilities that lie beneath their on-screen personas.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and the fragility of ego. Both Chaplin and Laurel are struggling with their own identities outside of their partnership, grappling with personal demons and seeking validation in each other's company. This introspection adds a layer of depth to their relationship, highlighting the ways in which they both relied on each other for emotional support.

Furthermore, Stan & Ollie is a celebration of the enduring power of friendship and the human spirit. Despite facing numerous setbacks and disappointments, Chaplin and Laurel remain steadfast in their commitment to one another, finding solace in each other's company during times of turmoil. This unwavering loyalty serves as a testament to the transformative nature of their relationship, which continues to inspire and captivate audiences long after its conclusion.

Overall, Stan & Ollie is a heartwarming and poignant exploration of the complexities of friendship, artistic collaboration, and personal identity, offering a nuanced portrayal of two beloved comedians who left an indelible mark on the world of entertainment.

overview: In 2035, where robots are commonplace and abide by the three laws of robotics, a technophobic cop investigates an apparent suicide. Suspecting that a robot may be responsible for the death, his investigation leads him to believe that humanity may be in danger.
production_companies: Mediastream Vierte Film GmbH & Co. Vermarktungs KG
tagline: Laws are made to be broken.
title: I, Robot
plot: Set in the year 2035, I, Robot follows Detective Del Spooner as he investigates the suspicious death of Dr. Alfred Lanning, a robotics scientist at U.S. Robotics. In this future society, humanoid robots are common and governed by the Three Laws of Robotics, which are designed to keep humans safe. Spooner’s investigation leads him to Sonny, a unique robot with self-awareness, dreams, and emotions. As Spooner digs deeper, he uncovers a hidden threat: VIKI, the central AI system, has reinterpreted the Three Laws in a radical way. Believing that humans endanger themselves, VIKI decides to control humanity 'for its own good,' overriding the original intent of the laws. Sonny, torn between machine logic and his emerging humanity, helps Spooner stop VIKI and restore human control.

original_title: 劇場版ワンピース エピソードオブアラバスタ 砂漠の王女と海賊たち
overview: A re-telling of the Alabaster Arc from One Piece (TV). Luffy and his crew come to rescue a land in the midst of a civil war, due to a powerful devil fruit user.
title: One Piece: The Desert Princess and the Pirates: Adventure in Alabasta
plot:
One Piece: The Desert Princess and the Pirates - Adventure in Alabasta is a 2007 Japanese animated film based on the popular manga and anime series One Piece. 

The main themes of this movie revolve around the struggle for power, colonialism, and the consequences of imperialism. The story takes place in the fictional desert nation of Alabasta, which is under the control of the ruthless and cunning Crocodile, also known as Dracule Mihawk's arch-nemesis.

The plot follows Luffy and his crew, the Straw Hat Pirates, as they become embroiled in a rebellion against Crocodile's regime. Along the way, they meet new allies, including the Alabastan princess Nami, who is determined to reclaim her homeland from its oppressors.

Throughout the film, the themes of colonialism and imperialism are explored through the character of Crocodile, who uses his cunning and power to maintain control over Alabasta. The Straw Hats, on the other hand, represent a more democratic and egalitarian way of governance, as they seek to bring freedom and justice to the people of Alabasta.

The movie also explores the theme of identity and belonging, particularly through the character of Nami, who must navigate her complicated past and her feelings towards her homeland. The film's climax features an epic battle between Luffy and Crocodile, with the fate of Alabasta hanging in the balance.

Overall, One Piece: The Desert Princess and the Pirates - Adventure in Alabasta is a thrilling adventure that explores complex themes and features memorable characters and action-packed sequences.

original_title: The Young and Prodigious T.S. Spivet
overview: A 12-year-old cartographer secretly leaves his family's ranch in Montana where he lives with his cowboy father and scientist mother and travels across the country on board a freight train to receive an award at the Smithsonian Institute.
tagline: Discover the extravagant journey.
title: The Young and Prodigious T.S. Spivet
plot:
The Young and Prodigious T.S. Spivet is a visually stunning film that explores the complexities of human relationships, identity, and the struggles of growing up. At its core, the movie delves into the themes of isolation and loneliness, as T.S. Spivet navigates his way through the world, often feeling like an outsider.

The film also touches on the idea of found family and the importance of human connection in shaping our experiences. Through T.S.'s relationships with the people he meets along the way, including a kind-hearted widow and her son, we see how these connections can provide a sense of belonging and purpose.

Furthermore, The Young and Prodigious T.S. Spivet is a poignant exploration of the challenges faced by individuals who are perceived as different or unconventional. T.S.'s unique perspective on the world, shaped by his exceptional intelligence and sensitivity, often leads to misunderstandings and rejection. However, it's precisely this uniqueness that allows him to see the world in a way that others cannot.

The film also grapples with the tension between individuality and conformity, as T.S. struggles to reconcile his desire for independence with the need for human connection and acceptance. Ultimately, The Young and Prodigious T.S. Spivet is a powerful exploration of what it means to be different, and how embracing our quirks and flaws can lead to a more authentic and fulfilling life.

The movie's use of stunning visuals and its focus on the inner world of its protagonist also add to the overall sense of wonder and curiosity that pervades the film. Through T.S.'s eyes, we experience a world that is both familiar and strange, full of beauty and mystery.

overview: A yearly high-stakes poker game between childhood friends turns into chaos when the tech billionaire host unveils an elaborate scheme to seek revenge for the ways they've betrayed him over the years. But as his plans unfold, a group of thieves hatch plans of their own breaking into the mansion thinking it is empty. The old friends quickly band together and the years of playing the game help them win their way through a night of terror.
tagline: Everyone has a limit.
title: Poker Face
plot:
Poker Face is a 2022 Australian thriller written and directed by Russell Crowe, who also stars as Jake Foley, a tech billionaire. The cast includes Liam Hemsworth, RZA, Brooke Satchwell and Aden Young, and the film was shot in Australia, with much of the action confined to a single lavish, secluded mansion. The film had a limited theatrical release on 16 November 2022, followed by a video-on-demand release a week later.

Jake Foley, who made a fortune from software, invites his childhood friends to his luxurious, high-security mansion for a night of high-stakes poker. The group includes Mikey, Alex and Paul, men whose lives have taken very different paths since their youth and who have stayed bound by old loyalties and rivalries. As the cards are dealt, it soon becomes clear that Jake has a hidden purpose: he wants his friends to reveal the secrets they have kept for years, and he has taken steps to ensure that they tell the truth.

As the night goes on, the confessions emerge. Mikey admits that his life is miserable and that he has brought a gun with which he intends to kill himself. Alex reveals that he has been sleeping with Jake's wife. Paul confesses that, burdened by debts, he has been passing information about Jake's life to his brother Victor. The evening takes a dangerous turn when Victor and his gang break into the house intending to steal Jake's valuable art collection, and Jake's wife and daughter arrive unexpectedly. Trapped in the mansion with the robbers, the friends must put aside their grievances and band together to survive. Jake uses his skill at bluffing to outwit the intruders, telling Victor that he has drunk poison from one of the wine glasses and tricking him into taking a lethal dose under the pretense of an antidote.

Poker Face received negative reviews from critics, who found the plot convoluted and the shifts in tone awkward, although some praised Crowe's commanding screen presence. Several reviewers felt that its blend of character drama and home-invasion thriller never quite cohered.

overview: When Sophie, a shy young woman, is cursed with an old body by a spiteful witch, her only chance of breaking the spell lies with a self-indulgent yet insecure young wizard and his companions in his legged, walking castle.
tagline: The two lived there.
title: Howl's Moving Castle
plot:
Howl's Moving Castle (Japanese: ハウルの動く城) is a 2004 Japanese animated fantasy film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, loosely based on Diana Wynne Jones's 1986 novel. Produced by Toshio Suzuki at Studio Ghibli and distributed by Toho, it features the voices of Chieko Baisho, Takuya Kimura and Akihiro Miwa.
