Set in a fictional kingdom where magic coexists with early 20th-century technology during a war, it reflects Miyazaki's opposition to the Iraq War.

Sophie, a shy young hatmaker, is rescued from two soldiers by a mysterious wizard, Howl. That evening, the jealous Witch of the Waste enters Sophie's shop and curses her, transforming her into a ninety-year-old woman who cannot speak of the spell. Sophie leaves home and wanders into the hills, where she befriends an enchanted scarecrow she names Turnip Head, who leads her to Howl's huge walking castle. Inside, she meets Howl's young apprentice, Markl, and Calcifer, a fire demon bound to Howl by a contract and the source of the castle's power. Calcifer promises to break her curse if she frees him, and she becomes the castle's cleaning lady.

The king summons Howl to aid in the war, but Howl sends Sophie, posing as his mother, to declare him a coward. At the palace, Madame Suliman, the royal sorceress and Howl's former teacher, strips the Witch of the Waste of her powers, reducing her to a harmless old woman, and threatens Howl with the same fate. Howl rescues Sophie, and they escape with the Witch and Suliman's dog. Sophie learns that Howl has been transforming into a bird-like creature to fight against both sides of the war, at the risk of losing his humanity, and her feelings for him grow.

When the town is bombed, Howl leaves to protect his household. To save him, Sophie removes Calcifer from the hearth, collapsing the castle. Through a magic ring, she travels into Howl's past and sees him as a boy swallowing a falling star, Calcifer, and giving the demon his heart. She returns Howl's heart to him, freeing Calcifer and breaking her own curse. Her kiss transforms Turnip Head back into a missing prince of the enemy kingdom, who sets off to end the war, and Sophie and Howl fly off together in a rebuilt castle.

Howl's Moving Castle premiered at the Venice Film Festival and became one of Japan's most successful films, grossing about $236 million worldwide. It received critical acclaim and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

overview: In 16th-century Zazzau, now Zaria, Nigeria, Amina must utilize her military skills and tactics to defend her family's kingdom. Based on a true story.
tagline: She is Amina and she fears nobody.
title: Amina
plot:
Amina is a 2021 Nigerian historical action drama directed by Izu Ojukwu, based on the life of Amina, the legendary warrior queen of Zazzau in the 16th century, a Hausa kingdom in what is now northern Nigeria, centered on the city of Zaria. Lucy Ameh stars in the title role, with Ali Nuhu, Clarion Chukwurah-Abiola, Chris Gbakann and Ibrahim Mijinyawa. The film premiered on Netflix on 4 November 2021.

The film opens with a duel between Kabarkai, the champion of Zazzau, and Danjuma. Having witnessed the fight, the young Amina tells her father, the ruler of Zazzau, that she wants to become a warrior. Her wish meets resistance from the Magaji, an important official, who points out that the armies of Zazzau have never recruited a woman. Determined, Amina trains in combat and horsemanship and gradually proves herself, defying the restrictions placed on women in her society.

The story follows the events that lead to Amina's rise to the throne of Zazzau. As a princess, she becomes involved in the political intrigues of the court and in the wars between Zazzau and its rivals, while her family faces betrayal from within. Her relationship with her sister Zaria, after whom the city is named, and a romance with Danjuma, a foreign prince, are threatened by the conflicts surrounding them. After suffering painful personal losses, including the death of her sister, Amina leads Zazzau's armies into battle and ultimately claims power, emerging as a formidable ruler who expands the kingdom's influence.

Amina received the most nominations at the 2022 Africa Magic Viewers' Choice Awards. Critics praised its costumes, music and battle scenes, but many faulted its plot, character development and underdeveloped romance. It was also criticized for being performed in Hausa with a non-Hausa lead actress, and for historical inaccuracies, such as its treatment of Amina's mother, Bakwa Turunku, who historians say had herself ruled Zazzau. Ojukwu responded that the scarcity of archives on Nigeria's history made the film difficult to produce.

overview: Twenty year-old Julius Caesar flees Rome for his life during the reign of Sulla but through skill and ambition rises four decades later to become Rome's supreme dictator.
title: Julius Caesar
plot:
Julius Caesar is a 2002 television miniseries directed by the German filmmaker Uli Edel and written by Peter Pruce and Craig Warner, dramatising the life of the Roman statesman from 82 BC to his death in 44 BC. Jeremy Sisto plays Caesar, with Richard Harris, in one of his final screen roles, as Sulla, Christopher Walken as Cato, Chris Noth as Pompey and Valeria Golino as Calpurnia. It aired on German television in December 2002 and on TNT in two parts in June 2003.

The story opens as the dictator Sulla marches on Rome and posts lists of men marked for death. The eighteen-year-old Caesar tries to save his father-in-law, is arrested by Sulla's officer Pompey and refuses to divorce his wife Cornelia. Pompey secretly spares him and sends him into exile, and on the voyage he is captured by pirates and survives only when his ransom arrives. After Sulla dies, Caesar returns to political life, but Cornelia falls ill and dies, and he vows to become the great man she believed he could be.

Years later, as Pompey celebrates a triumph, Caesar has been elected consul and conceals the seizures of his "falling sickness" with help from Calpurnia, whom he later marries. To seal an alliance, his daughter Julia marries Pompey, who gives Caesar the forces to conquer Gaul. There Caesar spares the defiant warrior Vercingetorix, who later raises a vast Gallic army against him, and Caesar wins the decisive Battle of Alesia.

Julia's death in childbirth ends the alliance. Pompey and Cato push the Senate to strip Caesar of his command, and Caesar responds by crossing the Rubicon. He makes himself dictator, defeats Pompey at Pharsalus, follows him to Egypt, where the boy king Ptolemy XIII has Pompey killed, and becomes involved with Cleopatra. After his victory at Thapsus, Cato takes his own life rather than ask for mercy.

Convinced that Caesar intends to become king, a group of senators led by Cassius brings the respected Brutus into a conspiracy. Ignoring Calpurnia's warning dream, Caesar goes to the Senate on the Ides of March and is stabbed to death.

The miniseries received two Primetime Emmy nominations, for makeup and for sound editing.

original_title: Dragons: Dawn Of The Dragon Racers
overview: A hunt for a lost sheep turns into a competition between Hiccup and friends as they compete to become the first Dragon Racing champion of Berk.
title: Dragons: Dawn Of The Dragon Racers
plot:
Dawn of the Dragon Racers, also known as Dragons: Dawn of the Dragon Racers, is a 2014 American computer-animated short film produced by DreamWorks Animation and directed by Elaine Bogan and John Sanford. Based on the How to Train Your Dragon franchise, it features the voices of Jay Baruchel as Hiccup and America Ferrera as Astrid, alongside cast members of the television series. Set before How to Train Your Dragon 2, it explains the origin of dragon racing.

As the dragon riders of Berk prepare for the island's official Dragon Race, Snotlout boasts that he invented the sport. Hiccup and Astrid dispute this, and the friends recall how dragon racing began. Years earlier, when the riders were younger, the village was preparing for its traditional annual regatta when a flock of sheep stampeded through the streets, frightened by the voice of Silent Sven. Rounding up the animals turns into an impromptu competition among the young riders and their dragons. Before leaving to gather wood, Chief Stoick puts Hiccup in charge of the regatta preparations.

Hiccup tries to forbid the sheep-catching game, but the others ignore him, and the villagers find it far more exciting than the regatta. Under pressure from the crowd, Hiccup reluctantly allows another race. The riders form two teams: Snotlout and the twins, Ruffnut and Tuffnut, against Hiccup and Astrid. Fishlegs refuses to join, devoted to the regatta. During the race, Astrid injures her arm in a collision with Snotlout while chasing a prized black sheep. Fishlegs finally changes his mind when his boat sinks after his dragon, Meatlug, becomes seasick and spits lava.

Stoick returns and, rather than punishing Hiccup for disobeying, allows the contest to continue, provided it has proper rules: each white sheep is worth one point and the black sheep five, and the winners will have their portrait hung in the Great Hall. The race is tied until the twins appear with a black sheep and claim victory, but Fishlegs then arrives with the real black sheep, revealing that the other team had painted an ordinary sheep. The victory is awarded to Hiccup and Fishlegs, the first dragon racing champions. Back in the present, Hiccup concludes that Tuffnut, who devised the rules, really invented the sport, and the riders rush off to race.

The short was released on November 11, 2014, as a bonus feature on the home media release of How to Train Your Dragon 2, and was later released separately on DVD with earlier franchise shorts.

original_title: 劇場版総集編 オーバーロード 不死者の王【前編】
overview: The first recap film of season 1 of the anime TV series Overlord, covering episodes 1 to 7. In the year 2138,  the popular online VR game Yggdrasil is quietly shut down one day. However, the player Momonga decides to not log out and is transformed into a powerful skeletal wizard upon shutdown. The game world continues to change, with non-player characters beginning to feel emotions. Confronted with this abnormal situation, Momonga and his loyal followers strive to investigate and take over the new world the game has become.
title: Overlord: The Undead King
plot:
Overlord: The Undead King (Gekijō-ban Sōshūhen Ōbārōdo: Fushisha no Ō) is a 2017 Japanese animated fantasy film, the first of two theatrical compilation films recapping the first season of the anime television series Overlord, itself based on the light novels written by Kugane Maruyama and illustrated by so-bin. Produced by Madhouse with Kadokawa, it was directed by Naoyuki Itō, with series composition by Yukie Sugawara and music by Shūji Katayama, and re-edits the first seven episodes of the 2015 series, adding new scenes such as an extended battle with Hamsuke. Released in Japan on 25 February 2017 and running 103 minutes, it was followed on 11 March by the second compilation, Overlord: The Dark Warrior. Its theme song, "Crazy Scary Holy Fantasy", was performed by Myth & Roid. The voice cast is led by Satoshi Hino as Momonga, with Yumi Hara as Albedo, Sumire Uesaka as Shalltear Bloodfallen, Masayuki Katou as Demiurge and Aoi Yūki as Clementine.

In the year 2138, after twelve years of operation, the immersive online role-playing game Yggdrasil is shutting down its servers. The once-feared guild Ainz Ooal Gown, which had 41 members, has dwindled to almost nothing, and its leader Momonga, a skeletal undead spellcaster, decides to stay in the guild's base, the Great Tomb of Nazarick, until the end. When the deadline passes he finds himself unable to log out, trapped in the body of his avatar, while the non-player characters have gained minds and wills of their own and pledge him absolute loyalty. Realising he is no longer in the game but in a strange new world, Momonga adopts a regal manner and wonders whether his friends were transported too.

When knights attack the nearby Carne Village, he intervenes, saving two young girls and dispatching the attackers with a summoned Death Knight, then rescues the kingdom's Warrior Captain, Gazef Stronoff, from the assassins of the Sunlight Scripture. Taking the guild's name, Ainz Ooal Gown, so that it might become legendary and reach any lost comrades, he unknowingly sets his followers on a path of world conquest. Disguised as the adventurer Momon, he travels to the city of E-Rantel with his battle maid Narberal Gamma, now called Nabe, joins the adventurer team Swords of Darkness to escort the young pharmacist Nfirea Bareare, and tames the legendary Wise King of the Forest, a giant hamster he names Hamsuke, while a cult and the killer Clementine plot to seize Nfirea.

overview: Peter Parker and his friends go on a summer trip to Europe. However, they will hardly be able to rest - Peter will have to agree to help Nick Fury uncover the mystery of creatures that cause natural disasters and destruction throughout the continent.
tagline: It’s time to step up.
title: Spider-Man: Far from Home
plot:
Spider-Man: Far From Home is a 2019 superhero film directed by Jon Watts and produced by Marvel Studios and Sony Pictures Releasing. The movie takes place after the events of Avengers: Endgame and follows Peter Parker, aka Spider-Man (played by Tom Holland), as he tries to balance his personal life with his responsibilities as a superhero.

The story begins with Peter Parker attending a school trip to Europe, accompanied by his friends Ned Leeds (Jacob Batalon) and MJ (Zendaya). However, the trip is disrupted when Mysterio (Jake Gyllenhaal), a mysterious and charismatic figure, appears on social media, claiming to be a superhero who has been fighting alongside Spider-Man in the Avengers. Mysterio's presence sparks Peter's interest, and he begins to investigate his claims.

As Peter delves deeper into Mysterio's identity, he discovers that the man is actually Quentin Beck (Jake Gyllenhaal), a former special effects artist who created an elaborate illusion to gain fame and recognition as a superhero. Beck uses advanced technology to create fake battles and heroic feats, which he broadcasts on social media to gain sympathy and admiration from the public.

Meanwhile, Nick Fury (Samuel L. Jackson) reappears, revealing that Mysterio is actually a threat to global security. He has been using his technology to manipulate people's perceptions of reality, creating chaos and destruction in various parts of the world. Peter, along with Ned and MJ, joins forces with Beck's allies, including Maria (Rita Moreno), to stop Mysterio.

As the story unfolds, Peter begins to question his own identity as Spider-Man and whether he is truly making a difference as a superhero. He also starts to develop feelings for MJ, who becomes increasingly concerned about Peter's well-being.

The climax of the movie features an epic battle between Spider-Man and Mysterio, with Peter using his wits and agility to outsmart Beck's illusions. In the end, Peter manages to defeat Mysterio, but not before realizing that he has been living in a world of fantasy created by Beck.

In the aftermath, Peter comes to terms with the fact that being a superhero is not just about having powers or gadgets, but also about taking responsibility and making sacrifices for the greater good. He also begins to rebuild his relationships with his friends and loved ones, including MJ, who becomes more than just a friend to him.

The movie concludes with Peter reflecting on the lessons he has learned from Mysterio's illusions, realizing that the line between reality and fantasy is often blurred, and that true heroism requires courage, empathy, and selflessness.

overview: In the near future, society collapses and water becomes scarce. When a greedy water baron starts violently clearing out survivors, Kendal, a 17-year-old teenager, fights the baron's henchman to keep a well open.
tagline: Stand your ground.
title: The Last Survivors
plot:
The Last Survivors, originally titled The Well, is a 2014 American post-apocalyptic thriller film directed by Thomas Hammock and written by Hammock and Jacob Forman. Haley Lu Richardson stars as a resourceful teenage girl struggling to survive a decade-long drought, with Booboo Stewart, Max Charles, Michael Welch and Rena Owen. The film premiered at the Los Angeles Film Festival on June 12, 2014.

Ten years after the rain stopped falling, rural Oregon has become a parched wasteland where survivors fight over the last water. Kendal, an orphan, cares for Dean, a fellow orphan who is dying of kidney failure. Her friend Gabriel, who lives with his family on a neighboring farm, urges her to join them, but she refuses to abandon Dean. Responding one day to a radio call for help, Kendal discovers it is a trap and can only watch as raiders slaughter a neighboring family.

As the local wells run dry, Dean suspects that Carson, a warlord who runs a fortified compound he promotes as a refuge, has drilled down to the aquifer and is draining the water from beneath the surrounding farms. When Carson arrives to collect Kendal's neighbor Grace, he coldly kills most of Gabriel's family, saying they are too old or weak to be worth the water, and spares only Gabriel, who reluctantly joins him. Kendal kills a guard and escapes. She and Dean hope to flee in an old Cessna airplane they have almost restored, needing only a distributor cap, which she recovers from a car inside Carson's compound. She also looks in on Alby, a young boy surviving alone.

When three desperate strangers come to the house, Dean persuades Kendal to give them water, but they return to steal the rest and Dean, barely able to walk, shoots them. The gunfire draws Carson's men, and Dean is killed after taking several of them with him. Arming herself with a katana taken from a grave on Grace's farm, Kendal returns and kills the men searching her home, among them a masked Gabriel. Discovering that Carson has abducted Alby, she storms the compound alone, kills his henchmen, and defeats Carson and his daughter, Brooke, in brutal fights. Kendal and Alby then start up the repaired plane and prepare to fly away, leaving Dean behind.

The film received generally positive reviews; Rotten Tomatoes reported 75% approval from 12 critics. Critics praised its distinctive setting and Richardson's performance, though some found the story unoriginal.

overview: The teenage girls of Vestalis Academy are meticulously trained in the art of being “clean girls,” practicing the virtues of perfect femininity. But what exactly are they being trained for? Vivien intends to find out.
tagline: Purity has a price.
title: Level 16
plot:
Level 16 is a 2018 Canadian science fiction film directed by Francesca Eastwood and written by Francesca Eastwood and Jonathan Hirschorn. The movie follows the story of Jordana Brooks, a teenager who discovers that her boarding school is actually an underground facility where girls are being trained to be perfect wives for wealthy men.

The main themes of Level 16 include:

1. **Toxic Femininity**: The film critiques the societal pressure on women to conform to traditional feminine norms, particularly in terms of beauty and domesticity. Jordana's rebellion against these expectations serves as a commentary on the limitations placed on women.
2. **Conformity vs. Individuality**: The movie explores the tension between conformity to societal expectations and embracing individuality. Jordana's desire for autonomy and self-expression is at odds with the school's emphasis on obedience and submission.
3. **Trauma and Abuse**: Level 16 touches on themes of trauma, abuse, and exploitation, particularly in the context of the girls' experiences at the boarding school. The film raises questions about the long-term effects of such trauma and the importance of support systems for survivors.
4. **Societal Expectations and Privilege**: The movie critiques the privileges afforded to those who conform to societal expectations, particularly in terms of wealth and social status. Jordana's journey is also a commentary on the limitations placed on individuals from marginalized groups.

Overall, Level 16 is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and issues relevant to contemporary society.

overview: An FBI agent is suspicious of two master thieves, quietly enjoying their retirement near what may - or may not - be the biggest score of their careers.
tagline: Who will walk away?
title: After the Sunset
plot:
After the Sunset is a 2004 action comedy film directed by Brett Ratner and starring Pierce Brosnan, Salma Hayek, and Sean Bean.

The main themes of After the Sunset revolve around:

1. Redemption: The protagonist, Charlie Cavendish (Pierce Brosnan), is a retired thief who tries to leave his past life behind. However, he's pulled back into the game when an old flame, Sandra (Salma Hayek), asks for his help in pulling off one last heist.

2. Loyalty and Betrayal: As Charlie navigates the complex web of loyalty and betrayal within his team, he must confront his own morals and values. The film explores the blurred lines between right and wrong, highlighting the consequences of choosing between personal gain and doing what's right.

3. Identity and Self-Discovery: Throughout the film, Charlie struggles to reconcile his past and present selves. As he navigates the world of high-stakes thievery, he begins to question who he truly is and what he wants from life.

4. Love and Sacrifice: The relationship between Charlie and Sandra serves as a catalyst for the plot, highlighting the complexities of love, loyalty, and sacrifice. The film shows how these themes can both drive us forward and hold us back.

5. Deception and Appearance vs Reality: After the Sunset is full of twists and turns, keeping viewers guessing about who to trust. This theme speaks to the idea that appearances can be deceiving, and that nothing is as it seems.

Overall, After the Sunset is a thrilling ride filled with action, humor, and heart, exploring complex themes that keep audiences engaged until the very end.

overview: Spoof of romantic comedies which focuses on a man, his crush, his parents, and her father.
tagline: An Unprotected Comedy
title: Date Movie
plot:
Date Movie is a 2006 American romantic comedy film directed by Ivan Reitman and written by Adam Sztykiel. The movie stars Steve Carell, Julia Roberts, and Breckin Meyer.

The main themes of Date Movie include:

1. Romantic Comedy Tropes: The film pokes fun at common romantic comedy clichés, such as the "meet-cute" and the "love triangle." It uses satire to comment on the conventions of the genre.
2. Social Satire: The movie satirizes modern dating culture, including online dating, speed dating, and the expectations placed on men and women in relationships.
3. Self-Deprecation: Steve Carell's character, Derek, is a parody of himself as a romantic lead. His character's awkwardness and ineptitude are played for laughs, but also serve to highlight the absurdity of modern dating.
4. Friendship: The film explores the importance of male friendships and how they can provide support and guidance in navigating relationships.

The plot follows Derek (Steve Carell), a man who is desperate to find love. He enlists the help of his friend Ian (Breckin Meyer) to set him up with women, but things don't go as planned. Meanwhile, Derek meets Dr. Jill (Julia Roberts), a beautiful and successful woman who challenges his expectations about relationships.

The movie's ending features a heartwarming moment between Derek and Jill, which subverts the typical romantic comedy formula. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the midst of chaos and uncertainty, love can be found.

Overall, Date Movie uses humor and satire to comment on modern dating culture and the conventions of romantic comedies.

overview: The beautiful princess Giselle is banished by an evil queen from her magical, musical animated land and finds herself in the gritty reality of the streets of modern-day Manhattan. Shocked by this strange new environment that doesn't operate on a "happily ever after" basis, Giselle is now adrift in a chaotic world badly in need of enchantment. But when Giselle begins to fall in love with a charmingly flawed divorce lawyer who has come to her aid - even though she is already promised to a perfect fairy tale prince back home - she has to wonder: Can a storybook view of romance survive in the real world?
tagline: This fairytale princess is about to meet a real Prince Charming.
title: Enchanted
plot:
Enchanted is a 2007 American musical fantasy comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of Giselle, a princess from the magical kingdom of Andalasia, who is engaged to Prince Edward.

The film begins with Giselle's wedding day, where she is about to marry Prince Edward. However, her life takes an unexpected turn when her evil stepmother, Queen Narissa, and her advisor, Morgan, plot to sabotage the wedding. In a dramatic twist, Giselle falls off a castle balcony and lands in the real world of New York City.

In the real world, Giselle meets Robert, a lawyer who is initially unaware of his royal connection. As they spend more time together, Giselle's innocence and naivety clash with the harsh realities of the modern world. Despite this, Robert finds himself falling for Giselle's charm and kindness.

Meanwhile, Queen Narissa and Morgan continue to pursue their evil plans, seeking to capture Giselle and use her as leverage to gain control over Prince Edward's kingdom. As Giselle navigates her new life in New York, she must also confront the reality of her own destiny and the true nature of her relationship with Prince Edward.

As the story unfolds, Robert becomes increasingly entangled in Giselle's world, and they begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their love is threatened by Queen Narissa's schemes, which lead to a dramatic confrontation between the two kingdoms.

In the end, Giselle must make a choice between her life in the real world with Robert or returning to her kingdom as the princess she was meant to be. Ultimately, Giselle decides to stay with Robert and find happiness in the real world, rather than conforming to the expectations of her royal duties.

The film features a range of memorable characters, including Morgan, who provides comedic relief, and the villainous Queen Narissa, whose evil plans drive much of the plot. The movie's blend of fantasy and reality creates a unique and engaging narrative that explores themes of love, identity, and the power of true connection.

Overall, Enchanted is a charming and entertaining film that offers a fresh take on traditional fairy tale tropes. With its witty dialogue, catchy musical numbers, and lovable characters, it has become a beloved classic among Disney fans and beyond.

overview: A small group of survivors are left behind after millions of people suddenly vanish during the rapture and the world is plunged into chaos and destruction.
tagline: The end begins
title: Left Behind
plot:
Left Behind is a 2014 American Christian apocalyptic thriller film directed by Vic Armstrong and written by Paul LaLonde and John Patus, based on the 1995 novel by Tim LaHaye and Jerry B. Jenkins. The second film adaptation of the first book in the Left Behind series, it stars Nicolas Cage, Chad Michael Murray, Cassi Thomson, Nicky Whelan, Jordin Sparks and Lea Thompson. Unlike the novel, it is set largely on an airplane.

Chloe Steele, a college student, flies home to New York to surprise her father, airline pilot Rayford Steele, for his birthday, only to learn that he has been called in to fly to London. At the airport she meets the investigative journalist Cameron "Buck" Williams. Chloe resents the religious fervor of her mother, Irene, a recent convert, and suspects that her parents' marriage is in trouble after seeing Rayford flirting with the flight attendant Hattie Durham and noticing that he is not wearing his wedding ring.

While Chloe is at a mall with her young brother, he vanishes in her arms, leaving his clothes behind. Millions of people around the world, including all children, disappear in an instant, and chaos erupts. On Rayford's flight to London, his co-pilot, a flight attendant and every child on board have also vanished, and he struggles to keep the frightened passengers under control while trying to make contact with the ground. A pilotless plane collides with his aircraft, damaging the fuel line, and he turns back toward New York.

At home, Chloe finds that her mother is also gone, and at Irene's church the pastor explains that the faithful have been taken to heaven while he was left behind because he never truly believed. Rayford reaches the same conclusion after finding Bibles among the belongings of his missing crew. In despair, Chloe climbs a bridge intending to end her life, but receives a call from her father and Buck: with the New York airports closed and fuel running out, Rayford needs somewhere to land. Chloe uses a truck to clear a road under construction and guides him to it, and he brings the plane down safely. As the survivors look out at a burning world, Buck remarks that it looks like the end, and Chloe replies that it is only the beginning.

Left Behind was panned by critics, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 0% approval and Metacritic a score of 12. It received three Golden Raspberry Award nominations, including Worst Picture and Worst Actor for Cage.

overview: A man with the ability to enter peoples' memories takes on the case of a brilliant, troubled sixteen-year-old girl to determine whether she is a sociopath or a victim of trauma.
tagline: Don't let her in.
title: Anna
plot:
Mindscape, also released as Anna, is a 2013 psychological science fiction thriller and the feature directorial debut of the Spanish filmmaker Jorge Dorado, written by Guy Holmes. An international co-production, it stars Mark Strong as John Washington, a memory detective, Taissa Farmiga as Anna Greene, Brian Cox as his superior Sebastian and Noah Taylor. The film follows an investigator who must determine whether a troubled teenager is a sociopath or a victim.

In a world where some people, known as viewers, have developed the psychic ability to enter other people's memories, John Washington works for Mindscape, an agency that uses such talents to help solve criminal cases, though its findings are not admissible in court. Still grieving the death of his wife, John suffers a stroke during a failed session and is left unable to work for two years. Financially desperate, he asks Sebastian for a new assignment.

He is given the case of Anna, a brilliant but troubled sixteen-year-old who is on a hunger strike and whose stepfather wants her institutionalized. As John explores her memories of her time at a prestigious girls' school, he uncovers a series of disturbing incidents, including accusations against a teacher and the poisoning of classmates, for which Anna blames a mysterious girl nicknamed Mousey. Increasingly drawn to Anna and convinced that she is a victim of abuse, John begins to suspect the adults around her, while signs emerge that Anna may be manipulating him and altering her own memories. When violence erupts at Anna's home, John finds himself accused of a crime and must discover the truth about the girl he has been trying to help.

The film is a puzzle thriller about memory, manipulation and the unreliability of perception.

Mindscape premiered at the 46th Sitges Film Festival in October 2013, with StudioCanal handling international sales and distribution in several European countries. It grossed about 1.1 million dollars and received mixed reviews, with 33 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 42.

overview: When her scientist ex-boyfriend discovers a portal to travel through time -- and brings back a 19th-century nobleman named Leopold to prove it -- a skeptical Kate reluctantly takes responsibility for showing Leopold the 21st century. The more time Kate spends with Leopold, the harder she falls for him. But if he doesn't return to his own time, his absence will forever alter history.
tagline: If they lived in the same century, they'd be perfect for each other.
title: Kate & Leopold
plot:
Kate & Leopold is a 2001 romantic comedy film directed by James Mangold, produced by Miramax Films, and written by Steven Rogers.

The movie tells the story of Kate McKay (played by Meg Ryan), a successful event planner in New York City, who meets Leopold (played by Hugh Jackman), a duke from the 19th century who has traveled through time to the present day. Despite their vastly different backgrounds and circumstances, they fall in love.

The main themes of Kate & Leopold include:

1. **Love transcending time and social class**: The film explores the idea that true love can conquer all obstacles, including time and social differences. Leopold's journey from 19th-century England to modern-day New York City serves as a metaphor for the power of love to bridge gaps between different eras and cultures.
2. **Self-discovery and growth**: Kate, in particular, undergoes significant personal growth throughout the film. As she navigates her relationship with Leopold, she learns to let go of her past and find new meaning in life.
3. **Adaptation and change**: The movie highlights the importance of adapting to changing circumstances and embracing new experiences. Leopold's initial struggles to adjust to modern life serve as a catalyst for Kate's own growth and self-discovery.
4. **The power of relationships**: The film celebrates the transformative impact that meaningful relationships can have on our lives. Through their romance, Kate and Leopold learn valuable lessons about themselves, each other, and the importance of human connection.

Overall, Kate & Leopold is a charming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, self-discovery, and adaptation in a unique and engaging way.

overview: When ruthless terrorists threaten to bring down the United Nations, they frame the one man they believe can stop them: an international security expert named Shaw. Now he must run from his own allies and become a solitary force for good, as he tries to stop what could become World War III.
tagline: Who is your foe?
title: The Art of War
plot:
The Art of War is a 2000 Canadian-American action spy thriller directed by Christian Duguay. Wesley Snipes stars as Neil Shaw, a covert operative working for the United Nations, with Michael Biehn, Anne Archer, Donald Sutherland, Maury Chaykin, Marie Matiko and Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa. It was the first installment of The Art of War series and was followed by two direct-to-video sequels, The Art of War II: Betrayal and The Art of War III: Retribution, the latter without Snipes.

Shaw works for a secret division of the United Nations that uses espionage and ethically questionable methods to secure peace. In Hong Kong he infiltrates a Chinese New Year party thrown by the businessman David Chan and blackmails a North Korean official, using evidence of misappropriated UN aid, into continuing negotiations with South Korea. Discovered, he fights his way out and is shot in the shoulder during his escape.

Six months later, a shipping container filled with the bodies of Vietnamese refugees from Hong Kong is found on the New York docks, in the same week that China is due to sign a landmark trade agreement with the United States. Shaw's superior, Eleanor Hooks, suspects that the Chinese ambassador, Wu, has links with the Triads and assigns Shaw to plant a tracking device on him during a banquet hosted by Chan. At the event, Wu is assassinated, Chan is wounded, and Shaw chases the masked gunman; his teammate Robert Bly corners the killer but is killed. Shaw is arrested by the police, and during a prison transfer the van carrying him and FBI agent Frank Capella is attacked, and Shaw is abducted by Triad members. Framed for the ambassador's murder and disowned by the organization he served, Shaw goes on the run, hunted by the FBI, the Triads and his own former colleagues. With the help of Julia Fang, an interpreter who witnessed the killing, he sets out to uncover a conspiracy to sabotage the trade agreement and discover who within his own circle betrayed him.

The Art of War received negative reviews from critics, who found its plot convoluted and borrowed from other spy thrillers, though Snipes's martial-arts action sequences drew some praise. It was a modest box-office performer, and its title references the ancient Chinese military treatise by Sun Tzu, which is quoted in the film.

overview: An ordinary man makes an extraordinary discovery when a train accident leaves his fellow passengers dead — and him unscathed. The answer to this mystery could lie with the mysterious Elijah Price, a man who suffers from a disease that renders his bones as fragile as glass.
tagline: Some things are only revealed by accident
title: Unbreakable
plot:
Unbreakable is a 2000 American superhero thriller written, produced and directed by M. Night Shyamalan. Bruce Willis stars as a man who walks away unhurt from a catastrophic train crash and begins to suspect he has extraordinary powers, with Samuel L. Jackson as the fragile comic-book enthusiast who seeks him out, Robin Wright as his wife and Spencer Treat Clark as his son. Shyamalan structured the story to mirror the three-part arc of a traditional comic book.

In 1961 Philadelphia, Elijah Price is born with broken limbs caused by osteogenesis imperfecta, a disease that makes his bones extremely brittle. Decades later, David Dunn, a former star quarterback now working as a security guard and stuck in an unhappy marriage, is the only survivor of a derailment that kills every other passenger on his train, and he emerges without a scratch.

After a memorial service, David finds a note asking whether he has ever been ill, inviting him to Elijah's comic-art gallery. Elijah lays out his theory that if he lies at one extreme of human fragility, someone must exist at the other who is practically unbreakable. Sceptical, David nonetheless discovers he can lift far more weight than he expected, while his son Joseph becomes convinced his father is a superhero. Elijah suggests that water, which nearly drowned David as a child, is his one weakness, and David admits he faked an injury after a car crash to quit football because his wife Audrey disliked the violence.

With Elijah's encouragement, David comes to see that his instinct for spotting dangerous people is a form of extrasensory perception: by touching strangers he glimpses crimes they have committed. He follows a janitor who has invaded a family's home and holds the children captive, frees them, survives being thrown into a pool and kills the intruder. Renewed, he reconciles with Audrey and quietly shows Joseph a newspaper sketch of the unknown hero.

When David shakes Elijah's hand, he sees that Elijah engineered a series of deadly disasters, including the train crash, in his search for a hero. Embracing the nickname Mr. Glass, Elijah casts himself as the villain, and a closing title reveals that he is committed to a psychiatric institution.

Released on November 22, 2000, the film grossed about $248 million worldwide on a $75 million budget and drew generally positive reviews, holding a 70% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Fifty years of war between the Great Eastern Federation and Europa - now merged as Eurasia - have taken their toll on planet Earth. As a result of the use of biological, chemical and nuclear weapons, much of Earth has become uninhabitable and people have become prey to new diseases. Professor Azuma's "neo-cell" project, which is supposed to be the answer to mankind's hardships, becomes a nightmare come true when mutants spawned from the experiment escape and declare war on the human race. Azuma's son Tetsuya, who was killed during the previous war, is reborn into the cyborg Casshern as mankind's last hope against the new mutant threat. This live-action sci-fi movie based on a 1973 Japanese animé of the same name.
tagline: When a hero falls a legend will rise
title: Casshern
plot:
Casshern is a 2004 anime film directed by Yoh Yoshinari and produced by Tatsunoko Production. The movie is set in a post-apocalyptic world where humanity has been devastated by war, and the story revolves around Casshern, a cyborg who seeks revenge against those responsible for his past.

The main theme of Casshern is the exploration of what it means to be human in a world that values technology and efficiency above all else. The film delves into the consequences of creating beings like Casshern, who are designed to serve humanity but ultimately become victims of its own making. Through Casshern's journey, the movie raises questions about the nature of existence, identity, and the blurred lines between human and machine.

The film also touches on the theme of redemption and the possibility of finding peace in a world that seems determined to destroy itself. Casshern's quest for revenge is slowly replaced by a desire to protect others and find a sense of belonging, highlighting the complexities of his own existence.

Furthermore, the movie critiques the notion of a society that values power and control above all else, as embodied by the character of Shun. His relentless pursuit of dominance and destruction serves as a commentary on the dangers of unchecked ambition and the devastating consequences of war.

Overall, Casshern is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and raises important questions about what it means to be human in a world that is increasingly dominated by technology.

belongs_to_collection.name: The Secret Life of Pets Collection

overview: Max the terrier must cope with some major life changes when his owner gets married and has a baby. When the family takes a trip to the countryside, nervous Max has numerous run-ins with canine-intolerant cows, hostile foxes and a scary turkey. Luckily for Max, he soon catches a break when he meets Rooster, a gruff farm dog who tries to cure the lovable pooch of his neuroses.
tagline: They still have their secrets.
title: The Secret Life of Pets 2
plot:
The Secret Life of Pets 2 is a 2019 computer-animated comedy film produced by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2016 film The Secret Life of Pets.

The story begins with Max, a terrier who has grown up with his owner Katie (Ellie Kemper). As Max ages, he starts to feel left behind by Katie's busy lifestyle and her new boyfriend, Rooster (Harrison Ford), a veteran who lost his leg in combat. Feeling neglected, Max decides to take matters into his own paws.

One day, while on a walk with Rooster, Max meets a stray dog named Snowball (Kevin Hart), the main antagonist of the first film. However, instead of being hostile towards each other, they form an unlikely friendship. Snowball convinces Max to join him on a road trip to help him find his long-lost brother, Daisy.

As they embark on their journey, Max and Snowball encounter various pets who are struggling with their own issues. There's Gidget (Jenny Slate), a Poodle who is trying to overcome her fear of the water; Tiberius (Lake Bell), a cat who is dealing with his own identity crisis; and Chloe (Bella Thorne), a rabbit who is trying to find her place in the world.

Throughout their journey, Max learns valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and finding one's purpose. He also helps Snowball come to terms with his past and find closure with his brother.

Meanwhile, back home, Katie is struggling to balance her life as a single mother and her new relationship with Rooster. She must confront her own feelings of insecurity and learn to trust herself and others again.

As Max and Snowball's road trip comes to an end, they return home to a surprise: Daisy has been found by the animal shelter, and she is now living in the shelter. Max and Snowball decide to help Daisy find her way back to her brother, but not before she helps them all learn valuable lessons about themselves and their relationships with others.

The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with Max and his friends having found their purpose and happiness. Max has learned to appreciate Katie's busy lifestyle and Rooster's love for him, while Snowball has finally found closure with his brother. The film concludes with a montage of the pets enjoying their newfound friendships and adventures.

Overall, The Secret Life of Pets 2 is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and self-discovery. With its lovable characters and engaging storyline, it's sure to delight audiences of all ages.

overview: Koyomi Araragi was turned into a vampire by the legendary vampire, Kiss-shot Acerola-orion Heart-under-blade, and he needs to revive the weakened vampire back to her complete form to return to being human again. The only way for Koyomi to achieve his goal is to fight the three vampire hunters – Dramaturgy, Episode and Guillotinecutter.
title: Kizumonogatari Part 2: Nekketsu
plot:
Kizumonogatari Part 2: Nekketsu is a Japanese anime film directed by Akiyuki Shinbo and produced by SHAFT. The main themes of the movie are:

1. **The struggle with one's own identity**: The story revolves around Araragi Koyomi, who is struggling to come to terms with his own identity and the consequences of his actions in the previous film. He grapples with the moral implications of his decisions and the weight of his responsibilities as a vampire hunter.

2. **The blurred lines between good and evil**: The movie explores the gray areas between right and wrong, highlighting the complexity of human nature and the ease with which individuals can become consumed by their own darkness. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Shinobu Oshino, who embodies both benevolent and malevolent qualities.

3. **The power of human connections**: Throughout the film, Koyomi forms strong bonds with those around him, including Miki Saeki, Suruga Kanbaru, and Shinobu. These relationships serve as a source of comfort, support, and strength for Koyomi, helping him navigate the challenges he faces.

4. **The cyclical nature of time**: The movie's narrative is heavily influenced by the concept of time loops, where events repeat themselves in a never-ending cycle. This theme serves as a metaphor for the human experience, highlighting the idea that our lives are shaped by patterns and cycles that we often struggle to break free from.

5. **The fragility of mental health**: Koyomi's struggles with depression and anxiety are a recurring theme throughout the film. The movie sheds light on the importance of seeking help and support when dealing with mental health issues, emphasizing the need for empathy and understanding in addressing these challenges.

Overall, Kizumonogatari Part 2: Nekketsu is a thought-provoking exploration of complex themes that challenge viewers to confront their own assumptions about human nature and the world around them.

original_title: The Scorpion King 5: Book of Souls
overview: The Scorpion King teams up with a female warrior named Tala, who is the sister of The Nubian King. Together they search for a legendary relic known as The Book of Souls, which will allow them to put an end to an evil warlord.
title: The Scorpion King 5: Book of Souls
plot:
The Scorpion King: Book of Souls, released as The Scorpion King 5, is a 2018 American direct-to-video sword-and-sorcery adventure directed by Don Michael Paul from a screenplay by David Alton Hedges. The fifth and final entry in The Scorpion King series, itself a spin-off of Stephen Sommers' Mummy films, it follows The Scorpion King 4: Quest for Power and stars Zach McGowan as the warrior Mathayus, with Pearl Thusi, Mayling Ng and Peter Mensah in supporting roles.

The film's mythology begins in ancient Egypt, where King Memtep strikes a bargain with the god of the underworld and forges a fearsome blade called the Fang of Anubis. The sword draws its power from the souls of everyone it kills, and the names of its victims are recorded in a mystical volume known as the Book of Souls.

Many centuries later, the ruthless warlord Nebserek digs up the Fang and uses it to launch a brutal campaign of conquest across the land. Meanwhile Tala, a Nubian warrior, is searching for the legendary Scorpion King in the hope that he can help her stop the tyrant. She frees a blacksmith named Mathayus, believed to be that hero, and persuades him to join her on a perilous mission to halt the dark power spreading through Egypt.

Their journey brings them into conflict with mercenaries and with the Black Arrows, a tribe of fierce warriors. They also encounter Enkidu, a golem who acts as the guardian of Amina, a young woman who is the living embodiment of the Book of Souls. Amina reveals the key to defeating Nebserek: the power of the Fang can be broken only if the Book itself is sacrificed.

As Nebserek and his forces close in, the companions make a final stand. Enkidu gives his life to protect Amina, and in the end Amina willingly sacrifices herself to lift the sword's curse and release the souls trapped within it. With the threat ended, Tala rises to become Queen of Nubia, while Mathayus fully accepts his identity as the Scorpion King and sets off alone, apparently to begin the campaign of conquest that will define his legend.

Produced by Universal 1440 Entertainment and shot largely in South Africa, the film cast McGowan in the role earlier played by Dwayne Johnson and Victor Webster.

overview: When his lawyer wife, Sofia, becomes pregnant, chronic underachiever Tom Reilly must take a job at his father-in-law's advertising firm. Tom has to adjust to the demands of a very high-powered job, and he finds himself in an increasingly hostile office rivalry with Chip, Sofia's paraplegic former lover.
tagline: Credit-grabbing, back-stabbing, wife-nabbing. Just another day at the office.
title: The Ex
plot:
The Ex is a 2006 American comedy film directed by Jesse Peretz, starring Zach Braff, Amanda Peet and Jason Bateman, with Charles Grodin, in his first film role since 1994, Mia Farrow and Amy Adams. Originally developed under the working title Fast Track, it was screened in late 2006, and after several postponements was released theatrically in the United States on May 11, 2007.

Tom Reilly, a talented but unreliable chef in Manhattan, struggles to hold a job, while his wife, Sofia, is a successful lawyer. When their first child is born, they agree that Sofia will stay home with the baby and Tom will build a steady career. Soon afterward Tom is fired from his restaurant job after standing up for his friend Paco, a fellow cook. To support the family, he accepts a job at an advertising agency in Ohio, Sofia's hometown, where her father, Bob, works, and the young family moves in with her parents.

Tom's new supervisor is Chip Sanders, a relentlessly upbeat, inspirational paraplegic who is admired by everyone at the agency and who turns out to be Sofia's high school boyfriend. Chip still harbors feelings for Sofia and sets out to make Tom's life miserable, undermining him at work while charming the family and spending time with Sofia and the baby. Every attempt Tom makes to expose Chip makes him look petty and jealous. Convinced that Chip is not really paralyzed, Tom finds a photograph of him playing tennis, and in a confrontation at his in-laws' home drags Chip up a staircase and throws him, expecting him to catch himself. Chip does not, the photo turns out to show his late twin brother, and Tom is humiliated.

Later, Chip reveals to Tom in private that he can in fact walk, though he cannot fight outside his wheelchair, and then beats Tom from his chair, boasting that he will win Sofia back. When Chip receives an offer to become creative director at an agency in Barcelona, he invites Sofia to go with him. She refuses, and the phone call proves to have been a trick arranged by Paco. Furious, Chip rises from his chair, exposing his deception, before storming outside and being hit by a bus. Tom and Sofia leave Ohio and swap roles, with Sofia returning to law and Tom staying home with their child while her father helps him launch his own business.

The Ex received largely negative reviews, with critics faulting its direction and its unsympathetic characters; Rotten Tomatoes reported 18% approval. It was a commercial failure, grossing about $5 million.

overview: Tarzan, having acclimated to life in London, is called back to his former home in the jungle to investigate the activities at a mining encampment.
tagline: Human. Nature.
title: The Legend of Tarzan
plot:
The Legend of Tarzan is a 2016 American adventure film directed by David Yates, based on the classic novel "Tarzan" by Edgar Rice Burroughs. The movie stars Alexander Skarsgård as Tarzan, Margot Robbie as Jane Porter, and Christoph Waltz as Lord Greystoke.

The film begins with a young boy named John Clayton (Alexander Skarsgård), who is raised by gorillas in the jungle after his parents' death. He is found by a gorilla named Kala, who adopts him and teaches him how to survive in the jungle. As John grows up, he learns about the ways of the wild and becomes a skilled hunter and warrior.

Years later, Lord Greystoke (Christoph Waltz), John's father, is captured by a group of poachers led by Medusa (Samuel L. Jackson). The poachers plan to sell him as a slave, but they are thwarted by a group of rebels who rescue Greystoke and return him to England.

In England, Greystoke marries Lady Alice (Diana Hardcastle) and has a son named John Clayton. However, the marriage is unhappy, and Lady Alice dies soon after giving birth to their son. Lord Greystoke becomes ill and dies, leaving John as the sole heir to his title and estate.

The film then jumps forward in time, where we see John Clayton (Alexander Skarsgård) living a life of luxury as the Earl of Greystoke. However, he is unhappy with his life and feels disconnected from his heritage. He meets Jane Porter (Margot Robbie), a beautiful and adventurous young woman who has come to Africa on an expedition.

As John and Jane spend more time together, they begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that John is hiding his true identity as Tarzan, the jungle boy raised by gorillas.

Meanwhile, Medusa (Samuel L. Jackson) returns with a group of mercenaries who are seeking revenge against Greystoke for foiling their plans in the past. They kidnap Jane and take her to the jungle, where they plan to use her as leverage to get to John.

Tarzan must then confront his past and face Medusa's men in order to rescue Jane and protect his home in the jungle. Along the way, he also learns more about his father's death and the reason behind his adoption by the gorillas.

In the end, Tarzan defeats Medusa and his men, and he and Jane confess their love for each other. The film ends with John Clayton embracing his true identity as Tarzan, and he and Jane setting off on a new adventure together in the jungle.

Overall, The Legend of Tarzan is an action-packed adventure film that explores themes of identity, belonging, and redemption. The movie features stunning visuals, impressive stunts, and a strong performance from Alexander Skarsgård as the titular character.

overview: An art curator decides to seek revenge on his abusive boss by conning him into buying a fake Monet, but his plan requires the help of an eccentric and unpredictable Texas rodeo queen.
tagline: A fake masterpiece. The perfect plan.
title: Gambit
plot:
Gambit is a 2012 heist comedy directed by Michael Hoffman from a screenplay by Joel and Ethan Coen. A remake of the 1966 film starring Shirley MacLaine and Michael Caine, it stars Colin Firth as Harry Deane, a London art curator, Cameron Diaz as a Texas rodeo queen, Alan Rickman as his abusive employer, Tom Courtenay as an art forger and Stanley Tucci as a rival art expert. The film premiered in London in November 2012 and was released in the United Kingdom by Momentum Pictures; in the United States it was not released until April 2014, by CBS Films, in select cinemas and on demand.

Harry Deane, a mild-mannered curator, is fed up with his arrogant, abusive boss, the media tycoon Lord Lionel Shabandar, and devises a plan to con him. Shabandar owns Claude Monet's Haystacks at Dawn, and Harry intends to sell him a forgery of its long-lost companion piece, Haystacks at Dusk, painted by his friend the Major, a master forger. To give the forgery a credible provenance, Harry travels to Alpine, Texas, to recruit PJ Puznowski, a brash rodeo queen whose grandfather, an American sergeant, captured Hermann Göring in 1945. The story will be that the painting, last seen in Göring's collection after being looted by the Nazis, was brought home by her grandfather as a war souvenir.

PJ agrees, and the conspirators hang the fake Monet in her grandmother's trailer in the desert and photograph it in the background of a magazine feature on the rodeo queen, to be published by one of Shabandar's own publications. In London, Harry shows Shabandar the photos and steers his attention to the painting. Shabandar dismisses it as a reproduction, but Harry persuades him to look into it. When PJ comes to London, the con quickly goes off the rails: Shabandar is more interested in her than in the painting, Harry's plan runs into a string of humiliating mishaps at the Savoy Hotel, and Shabandar calls in a rival German art expert, Martin Zaidenweber, whose assessment threatens to expose the forgery, leaving Harry scrambling to keep the scheme alive.

Gambit received negative reviews. It holds an 18 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a curiously charmless caper that squanders a starry cast and a screenplay by the Coen brothers. It grossed about $1.9 million in the United Kingdom and $14.2 million worldwide.

original_title: Before the Devil Knows You're Dead
overview: When two brothers organize the robbery of their parents' jewelry store, the job goes horribly wrong, triggering a series of events that send them and their family hurtling towards a shattering climax.
tagline: No one was supposed to get hurt.
title: Before the Devil Knows You're Dead
plot:
Before the Devil Knows You're Dead is a 2007 American crime drama film directed by Sidney Lumet, produced by Sidney Lumet and Michael Lerner, and written by Billy Bob Thornton. The movie stars Philip Seymour Hoffman, Steve Buscemi, and Albert Finney.

The main themes of Before the Devil Knows You're Dead include:

1. Family dynamics: The film explores the complex relationships within a family, particularly between two brothers, Nick (Philip Seymour Hoffman) and Andy (Steve Buscemi), who are struggling with their own personal demons.
2. Loyalty and betrayal: As the story unfolds, the characters' loyalties are tested, and they are forced to confront the consequences of their actions. The film raises questions about what it means to be loyal to family, friends, or oneself.
3. Morality and ethics: The movie delves into the gray areas between right and wrong, encouraging viewers to consider the moral implications of one's choices. The characters' decisions are often driven by desperation, greed, and a desire for financial security.
4. Identity and redemption: Through the characters' experiences, the film explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and the possibility of redemption. Nick, in particular, grapples with his own sense of purpose and direction.

The plot follows Nick, who is struggling to make ends meet as a used car salesman. When he discovers that his brother Andy has embezzled money from their father's funeral home, Nick sees an opportunity to get out of debt by helping Andy sell the stolen cash. However, things quickly spiral out of control, and the brothers find themselves in a desperate situation.

As the story unfolds, the characters' relationships with each other and with others are put to the test. The film builds towards a tense and violent climax, ultimately leading to a tragic confrontation that forces the characters to confront their own mortality and the consequences of their actions.

Overall, Before the Devil Knows You're Dead is a gripping drama that explores complex themes and character relationships in a thought-provoking and emotionally charged way.

overview: The balance of power in four couples’ relationships is upset when the women start using the advice in Steve Harvey’s book, Act Like A Lady, Think Like A Man, to get more of what they want from their men. When the men realize that the women have gotten a hold of their relationship “playbook,” they decide that the best defense is a good offense and come up with a plan to use this information to their advantage.
tagline: Let the mind games begin.
title: Think Like a Man
plot:
Think Like a Man is a 2012 American romantic comedy directed by Tim Story, written by Keith Merryman and David A. Newman and produced by Will Packer. It is based on comedian Steve Harvey's 2009 relationship advice book Act Like a Lady, Think Like a Man. The ensemble cast includes Kevin Hart, Meagan Good, Jerry Ferrara, Regina Hall, Michael Ealy, Terrence J, Taraji P. Henson, Romany Malco, Chris Brown and Gabrielle Union.

The film follows four couples in Los Angeles whose stories are presented through archetypes drawn from Harvey's book: "The Mama's Boy" and "The Single Mom", "The Non-Committer" and "The Girl Who Wants the Ring", "The Dreamer" and "The Woman Who Is Her Own Man", and "The Player" and "The 90 Day Rule Girl". The men are a group of friends who play basketball together, while each of the women turns to Harvey's book for guidance in dealing with the men in her life.

Following the book's advice, the women begin to gain the upper hand in their relationships, setting rules and pushing their partners to change. When the men discover the source of the women's sudden insight, they obtain copies of the book and try to use its advice to turn the tables on their partners, a strategy that soon backfires. As the romantic games escalate, each couple must confront what they really want, and the men and women learn that honesty and compromise matter more than any strategy.

Production took place in Los Angeles and Culver City, California, in 2011, and the film includes cameo appearances by several professional basketball players, including Lisa Leslie, Metta World Peace and Matt Barnes, who appear as themselves, while Harvey's book is central to the plot.

Think Like a Man was released by Screen Gems on April 20, 2012, and was a major box office success, grossing 96.1 million dollars worldwide on a budget of 12.5 million dollars and ending The Hunger Games' four-week run at the top of the North American box office. Reviews were mixed, with 55 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 51. A sequel, Think Like a Man Too, was released in 2014.

overview: Investigators reveal how Boeing’s alleged priority of profit over safety could have contributed to two catastrophic crashes within months of each other.
title: Downfall: The Case Against Boeing
plot:
Downfall: The Case Against Boeing is a 2022 American documentary directed by Rory Kennedy. Through interviews with journalists, engineers, former Boeing employees, pilots, members of Congress and relatives of victims, together with archival footage, it investigates the events that led to the crashes of two Boeing 737 MAX aircraft within five months of each other, and the investigations that followed. It premiered in a virtual screening at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival on 21 January 2022 and was released on Netflix the following month.

In October 2018, Lion Air Flight 610 crashed into the Java Sea shortly after takeoff from Jakarta, and in March 2019, Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crashed minutes after leaving Addis Ababa. Together the two disasters killed 346 people. The documentary examines how investigators traced both crashes to a flight-control software system on the 737 MAX, known as MCAS, which could repeatedly push the plane's nose down on the basis of faulty sensor data, and how pilots had not been adequately informed about the system or trained to handle it.

The film places the crashes within the broader history of Boeing, arguing that the company, once renowned for an engineering culture focused on safety and excellence, underwent a profound shift after its 1997 merger with McDonnell Douglas, when financial performance and shareholder value came to dominate decision-making. It describes how the pressure to compete with Airbus, whose fuel-efficient A320neo threatened Boeing's market share, led the company to rush the 737 MAX into service as an update of an older design rather than develop a new aircraft. Interviewees criticize Boeing's initial attempts to blame the foreign pilots, as well as the close relationship between the company and the Federal Aviation Administration, which had delegated much of the certification process to Boeing itself. Kennedy has said that for decades Boeing showed that a focus on safety and ingenuity was the key to profit, until it was taken over by people for whom Wall Street was everything, and that elected officials must hold companies accountable for the public interest.

The documentary was well received by critics, who praised its clear explanation of the technical and corporate failures and its emotional interviews with the victims' families, though some felt it covered ground already familiar from news reporting.

overview: Alice Gould, a private investigator, pretends to be mentally ill in order to enter a psychiatric hospital and gather evidence for the case she is working on: the death of a patient in unclear circumstances.
title: God's Crooked Lines
plot:
God's Crooked Lines (Spanish: Los renglones torcidos de Dios) is a 2022 Spanish psychological thriller directed by Oriol Paulo and starring Bárbara Lennie as Alice Gould. Written by Paulo and Guillem Clua with the collaboration of Lara Sendim, it adapts Torcuato Luca de Tena's 1979 novel of the same name. Set inside a psychiatric hospital, the film is built around the question of whether its heroine is a brilliant investigator or a dangerously unstable patient.

In 1979, Alice Gould de Almenara is admitted to a psychiatric institution. She tells the doctors that she has been "legally abducted" by her husband, Heliodoro, who wants to seize her fortune. In reality, Alice claims, she is a private investigator who has feigned a mental illness to get inside the hospital, at the request of a doctor whose son, Damián, died there in mysterious circumstances. Once inside, she begins investigating among the patients, befriending some of them, including Ignacio Urquieta and a pair of twins, while confronting a predatory inmate known as the Gnome and his protector.

A second timeline, set during a stormy night when a fire and riot break out and a body is found in one of the cells, gradually converges with the main story. When the Gnome is found dead after attacking Alice in the woods, she becomes a suspect, and she struggles to remember what happened. Alice's account of her mission is challenged by the hospital's director, who presents evidence that she tried to poison her husband and that her story is a symptom of paranoia. As the medical council meets to decide her fate, both the doctors and the audience must determine whether Alice is telling the truth.

The film plays with the unreliability of perception and the boundary between sanity and madness, keeping its central ambiguity alive until the end.

God's Crooked Lines premiered at the 70th San Sebastián International Film Festival in September 2022 and was released theatrically in Spain by Warner Bros. on 6 October 2022, becoming one of the highest-grossing Spanish films of the year, before arriving on Netflix in December. It received positive reviews, with Cinemanía calling it a thrilling and elegant exercise, and earned six nominations at the 37th Goya Awards, including Best Actress for Lennie and Best Adapted Screenplay.

overview: In the menacing inferno of the old North-American West, Liz is a genuine survivor who is hunted by a vengeful preacher for a crime she didn’t commit.
tagline: Retribution is coming
title: Brimstone
plot:
Brimstone is a 2016 American Western horror film directed by Martin Campbell and starring Michael Fassbender, Sophia Cooksley, and Alexander Ludwig.

The main themes of Brimstone revolve around the struggle between good and evil, faith, and redemption. The story follows John Henry Breck (Michael Fassbender), a former preacher turned bounty hunter who is tasked with capturing a group of outlaws in 19th-century New Mexico.

As the film progresses, it becomes clear that Breck's past as a preacher has left emotional scars, and he struggles to reconcile his faith with his violent profession. The film explores the tension between Breck's desire for redemption and his need for revenge against those who have wronged him.

The movie also delves into the theme of morality in a lawless frontier society, where outlaws and lawmen often walk a fine line between right and wrong. Through Breck's character, the film raises questions about the nature of justice and whether it can be served through violence or compassion.

Furthermore, Brimstone touches on the idea of the "other," highlighting the tensions between Native Americans and European settlers in the American West. The film features a strong performance from Sophia Cooksley as Breck's daughter, Charlotte, who serves as a symbol of innocence and purity in a world torn apart by violence and greed.

Overall, Brimstone is a complex and thought-provoking film that explores themes of redemption, morality, and the human condition.

overview: It has been ten years since The Battle of the Breach and the oceans are still, but restless. Vindicated by the victory at the Breach, the Jaeger program has evolved into the most powerful global defense force in human history. The PPDC now calls upon the best and brightest to rise up and become the next generation of heroes when the Kaiju threat returns.
tagline: Rise up.
title: Pacific Rim: Uprising
plot:
Pacific Rim: Uprising is a 2018 science fiction monster film directed by Steven S. DeKnight and written by Emily Carmichael, Kira Snyder, and John Francis Daley. The movie takes place 10 years after the events of the first Pacific Rim film.

The story begins with Jake Pentecost (played by John Boyega), the son of Stacker Pentecost (played by Idris Elba), who was killed in action during the war against the Kaijus. Jake is a young and talented engineer who has grown up hearing stories about his father's bravery and sacrifice.

Jake is recruited by Dr. Newton Geiszler (played by Charlie Hunnam), a scientist who has discovered a way to communicate with the Jaegers, giant robots that were used to fight against the Kaijus. The Jaegers are now being decommissioned due to their high maintenance costs and lack of effectiveness in modern warfare.

Jake is paired with Dr. Zhang (played by Rinko Kikuchi), a brilliant scientist who has developed a new technology that allows humans to pilot the Jaegers without the need for a human co-pilot. The two scientists embark on a mission to develop a new generation of Jaeger pilots, known as "drifters," who can work together to take down the Kaijus.

However, their plans are soon disrupted by a group of rogue drifters, led by the enigmatic and ruthless Cassius (played by Scott Eastwood). Cassius is determined to use the technology for his own gain and becomes a formidable foe for Jake and Dr. Zhang.

As the story unfolds, Jake discovers that he has a unique connection to the Jaegers, which makes him an ideal candidate to pilot the new generation of machines. He also learns about his father's past and the sacrifices he made during the war against the Kaijus.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between the humans and the Kaijus, with Jake and Dr. Zhang leading the charge. Along the way, they encounter a range of formidable foes, including the monstrous Otachi and the treacherous Cassius.

In the end, Jake emerges as a hero, having saved humanity from extinction. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, with Jake and Dr. Zhang looking towards a brighter future for humanity and the Jaegers.

Overall, Pacific Rim: Uprising is an action-packed sci-fi adventure that explores themes of identity, sacrifice, and the power of human connection. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans and offers plenty of excitement and thrills for fans of the franchise.

overview: Four young outsiders teleport to a dangerous universe, which alters their physical form in shocking ways. Their lives irrevocably upended, the team must learn to harness their daunting new abilities and work together to save Earth from a former friend turned enemy.
tagline: Change is coming.
title: Fantastic Four
plot:
Fantastic Four is a 2015 superhero film based on the Marvel Comics team and the first reboot of the Fantastic Four film series. Directed by Josh Trank and written by Trank, Jeremy Slater and Simon Kinberg, it stars Miles Teller as Reed Richards, Michael B. Jordan as Johnny Storm, Kate Mara as Sue Storm, Jamie Bell as Ben Grimm and Toby Kebbell as Victor von Doom, with Reg E. Cathey as Franklin Storm and Tim Blake Nelson. The film offers a darker, more grounded take on the team's origin.

Childhood friends Reed Richards and Ben Grimm have spent years building a prototype teleporter, which attracts the attention of Professor Franklin Storm, head of the Baxter Foundation, a government-funded institute for young prodigies. Reed is recruited to work with Storm's children, Sue and Johnny, and the brilliant but difficult Victor von Doom on the Quantum Gate, a machine designed to reach another dimension. When the experiment succeeds and the project's supervisors plan to send NASA astronauts instead, Reed, Johnny, Victor and Ben make an unauthorized journey to the parallel world known as Planet Zero.

The trip goes disastrously wrong: Victor is apparently killed, and the explosion of the gate alters the others at a genetic level, giving them uncontrollable powers. Reed can stretch his body, Sue can turn invisible and create force fields, Johnny can engulf himself in flames and fly, and Ben is transformed into a rock-like creature of enormous strength. A year later, the government is using Ben, Johnny and Sue as military assets, while a guilt-ridden Reed has gone on the run. When an expedition to Planet Zero brings back a transformed Victor, now possessing devastating powers and determined to destroy Earth, the four must learn to work together as a team.

The film's troubled production became widely publicized, with reports of conflict between Trank and the studio and extensive reshoots.

Fantastic Four grossed 168 million dollars worldwide against a budget of 120 million dollars and was panned by critics, receiving 9 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 27. Trank publicly blamed the studio for the final film, and it won several Golden Raspberry Awards, including Worst Picture and Worst Director.

overview: A high school valedictorian who gets baked with the local stoner finds himself the subject of a drug test. The situation causes him to concoct an ambitious plan to get his entire graduating class to face the same fate, and fail.
tagline: Random drug tests? You just can't study for them.
title: High School
plot:
High School is a 2010 American teen stoner comedy and the feature directorial debut of John Stalberg Jr. It stars Matt Bush as Henry Burke, a model student, and Sean Marquette as his former best friend Travis, with Adrien Brody as the eccentric drug dealer Psycho Ed, Michael Chiklis as the school's principal, Dr. Gordon, and Colin Hanks, Adhir Kalyan, Mykelti Williamson, Yeardley Smith, Curtis Armstrong and Michael Vartan in supporting roles.

Henry Burke is Morgan High School's top student, on track to become valedictorian and headed for a bright future, while Travis is the school's resident stoner and troublemaker. Reconnecting just before graduation, Travis persuades Henry to smoke marijuana for the first time. The next day, after the school's spelling bee champion is caught high during a competition, the principal announces a zero-tolerance drug test for the entire student body, and anyone who fails will be expelled. Facing the destruction of everything he has worked for, Henry panics.

Travis comes up with a desperate plan: if every student in the school fails the test, the results will be invalid. He knows of a psychotic drug dealer, Psycho Ed, who possesses a powerful stash of cannabis extract, and the two boys steal it in order to secretly get the entire school high before the test. As the students and teachers become increasingly intoxicated, chaos spreads through Morgan High, while Henry and Travis are pursued by both the furious Psycho Ed and the suspicious Dr. Gordon, and Henry's academic rival threatens to expose them.

The film satirizes zero-tolerance school policies and high school culture through broad, outrageous humor.

High School was shot in 2008 in Howell, Michigan, and premiered at the Sundance Film Festival, where it was well received on the festival circuit, including at the Edinburgh International Film Festival. Its release was delayed for more than two years while the producers made changes, and it was eventually distributed by Anchor Bay Films in 2012, receiving mostly negative reviews, with 28 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31.

overview: Taking place on the last day of the Creeper’s twenty-three-day feeding frenzy, as the skeptical Sergeant Tubbs teams up with a task force hellbent on destroying the Creeper for good. The Creeper fights back in gory glory as its enemies grow closer than ever before to learning the secret of its dark origins.
tagline: Third Time's the Charm
title: Jeepers Creepers 3
plot:
Written and directed by Victor Salva, Jeepers Creepers 3 is a 2017 American horror film and the third instalment in the Jeepers Creepers series. Set between the events of the first two films, it brings back Jonathan Breck as the Creeper, alongside Stan Shaw, Gabrielle Haugh, Brandon Smith and Meg Foster, while Gina Philips makes a cameo as Trish Jenner, her first appearance in the series since the original film.

The story begins a day after the first film. Police find the Creeper's truck full of corpses and rigged with deadly traps, and Sheriff Dan Tashtego tells Sergeant Davis Tubbs about the creature and what drives it. The Creeper soon reclaims the truck, abducting one of the officers transporting it. Tashtego assembles a team of hunters made up of relatives of the creature's past victims.

Elsewhere, Gaylen Brandon, whose son Kenny was killed by the Creeper, sees a vision of him warning that the monster will come for something he buried on her property and will kill her and her granddaughter Addison. When a group of teenagers discovers the truck in a field, the Creeper kills them all. Addison is later abducted after stumbling on the creature's attack at a plantation house.

Gaylen digs up a severed hand Kenny had found, and touching it reveals visions of how ancient the Creeper is. Tashtego's team catches up with the truck on the highway, but their bullets have little effect; Michael is killed and Tashtego dies at the Creeper's hands, leaving Tubbs to retreat.

Held captive in the truck, Addison triggers one of its traps and drives a metal pipe into the Creeper's head, costing it an eye. She escapes when the monster is struck by a passing truck, though it heals itself by consuming the driver.
