Ultimately, Son of Rambow is a poignant coming-of-age story that explores the complexities of childhood and the challenges of growing up. The film's nuanced portrayal of its characters and themes makes it a relatable and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

original_title: The Odd Life of Timothy Green
overview: A childless couple bury a box in their backyard, containing all of their wishes for an infant. Soon, a child is born, though Timothy Green is not all that he appears.
tagline: He's a force of nature.
title: The Odd Life of Timothy Green
plot:
The Odd Life of Timothy Green is a heartwarming and poignant film that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, loss, and the transformative power of imagination. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of grief and how it can shape us in profound ways.

The story follows a widowed mother, Susan, who struggles to connect with her son, Josh, after the sudden loss of his father. As she navigates this difficult time, she begins to see the world through the eyes of her son's imaginary friend, Timothy Green, a magical and endearing character who embodies the innocence and wonder of childhood.

Through Timothy's presence, Susan is forced to confront her own emotional baggage and learn to let go of her grief. The film beautifully captures the bittersweet nature of loss and the ways in which it can both break us and ultimately set us free.

The movie also explores the theme of love and its many forms. Susan's relationship with Josh is tender and loving, but also fraught with tension and uncertainty. As she navigates her new role as a single mother, she must find a way to balance her own needs with those of her son, all while learning to trust herself and her abilities.

One of the most striking aspects of The Odd Life of Timothy Green is its use of fantasy and imagination as a means of healing and transformation. Through Timothy's magical presence, Susan is able to tap into a sense of wonder and possibility that she had lost in her grief. This serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of holding onto hope and finding joy in the midst of sorrow.

Overall, The Odd Life of Timothy Green is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, loss, and the transformative power of imagination. With its poignant performances, stunning visuals, and thoughtful storytelling, it is a movie that will leave audiences moved and inspired long after the credits roll.

overview: The Boat That Rocked is an ensemble comedy, where the romance is between the young people of the 60s, and pop music. It's about a band of DJs that captivate Britain, playing the music that defines a generation and standing up to a government that  wanted control of popular culture via the British Broadcasting Corporation. Loosely based on the events in Britain in the 60's when the Labour government of Harold Wilson, wanted to bring the pirate radio stations under control, enough to see the passage of the Marine Broadcasting Offences Act on 15 August 1967. Also known as "Pirate Radio".
tagline: On air. Off shore. Out of control.
title: The Boat That Rocked
plot:
The Boat That Rocked, released in North America as Pirate Radio, is a 2009 British comedy-drama film written and directed by Richard Curtis about pirate radio in the United Kingdom in the 1960s. Its ensemble cast includes Philip Seymour Hoffman, Bill Nighy, Rhys Ifans, Nick Frost, Kenneth Branagh, Tom Sturridge and Emma Thompson. It was produced by Working Title Films for Universal Pictures.

In 1966, while the BBC plays almost no rock and pop music, pirate stations broadcast it to millions of listeners from ships in international waters. Seventeen-year-old Carl, recently expelled from school, is sent by his mother to spend time with his godfather, Quentin, who runs Radio Rock from an old ship anchored in the North Sea. There Carl joins an eccentric community of disc jockeys and crew, led by the brash American DJ known as the Count.

In London, the government minister Sir Alistair Dormandy is determined to shut the pirate stations down, and instructs his aide, Twatt, to find a legal means of doing so. When the government forbids British companies from advertising on unlicensed stations, Quentin responds by bringing back the legendary DJ Gavin Kavanagh, whose popularity draws advertisers back but sparks a rivalry with the Count. Carl falls for Quentin's niece, Marianne, but she is seduced by the DJ Doctor Dave; the gentle DJ Simple Simon marries a glamorous fan who soon leaves him for Gavin, prompting a dangerous duel between Gavin and the Count on the ship's mast. When his mother visits at Christmas, Carl learns that the reclusive late-night DJ Bob Silver is his father, and Marianne later returns to him.

Dormandy finally gets his law when a fishing boat's distress call is blocked by Radio Rock's signal, and the Marine Broadcasting Offences Act makes the pirate stations illegal from August 1967. The crew defy the law and keep broadcasting, starting the ship's engine to evade arrest, but the old vessel's engine explodes and it begins to sink. Dormandy refuses to send help, but as the DJs keep broadcasting their position, dozens of fans sail out in small boats to rescue them, Carl being pulled from the water by Marianne.

The film premiered in London in March 2009 and was released in the United Kingdom on 1 April. It received mixed reviews, with criticism of its length, and performed poorly at the British box office; for North America it was cut by about twenty minutes. It grossed about $36.6 million worldwide against a $50 million budget.

original_title: 西遊記之孫悟空三打白骨精
overview: Taking place 500 years after the Havoc in Heaven, the Tang Priest is appointed by Buddha to go to the West to fetch the sacred scriptures, only to accidentally free the Monkey King. With Lady White aiming to break up the team assembled to defeat her, the Monkey King must fight in order to save his world!
title: The Monkey King 2
plot:
The Monkey King 2 is a 2016 Chinese fantasy adventure film directed by Yuen Woo-ping and produced by Filmko Pictures.

The movie is based on the classic Chinese novel "Journey to the West" and serves as a sequel to The Monkey King (2014). The story follows the adventures of Sun Wukong, also known as the Monkey King, who has been imprisoned by the Jade Emperor for 500 years. After his release, he sets out to find his true identity and reunite with his friends, including Tang Sanzang.

The main themes of The Monkey King 2 include:

1. Identity: Sun Wukong's journey is a metaphor for self-discovery and finding one's true purpose in life. As he navigates the world, he encounters various challenges that force him to confront his own identity and sense of belonging.
2. Friendship: The movie highlights the strong bond between Sun Wukong and Tang Sanzang, as well as their relationships with other characters, such as Zhu Bajie and Sha Wujing. These friendships are tested throughout the story, but ultimately prove to be essential in overcoming adversity.
3. Power and responsibility: As a powerful being, Sun Wukong must learn to wield his abilities wisely and use them for the greater good. This theme is explored through his interactions with other characters, particularly the Jade Emperor, who serves as a symbol of authority and wisdom.
4. Balance between good and evil: The Monkey King 2 explores the gray areas between good and evil, as Sun Wukong struggles to reconcile his own nature with his desire to do good. This theme is reflected in his relationships with other characters, particularly Zhu Bajie, who represents a more straightforward approach to morality.
5. Self-sacrifice: Throughout the story, Sun Wukong faces numerous challenges that require him to make difficult choices and put the needs of others before his own. These sacrifices ultimately lead to his growth as a character and his development into a true hero.

Overall, The Monkey King 2 is a rich and complex film that explores themes of identity, friendship, power, balance, and self-sacrifice, set against the backdrop of Chinese mythology and folklore.

overview: Elsa and Clive, two young rebellious scientists, defy legal and ethical boundaries and forge ahead with a dangerous experiment: splicing together human and animal DNA to create a new organism. Named "Dren", the creature rapidly develops from a deformed female infant into a beautiful but dangerous winged human-chimera, who forges a bond with both of her creators - only to have that bond turn deadly.
tagline: Science's newest miracle...is a mistake.
title: Splice
plot:
Splice is a 2009 science fiction horror film directed by Vincenzo Natali and written by Tyler Labine and Vincenzo Natali. The movie stars Adrien Brody, Sarah Polley, and David Hewlett.

The story begins with two scientists, Dreyfuss (David Hewlett) and Werner (Adrien Brody), who work at a biotech company called Medtech Industries. They are part of a team led by Dr. Emma Cullen (Sarah Polley), who is working on a top-secret project to create life from DNA samples.

The team has been experimenting with the genetic material of various animals, including monkeys and pigs, in an attempt to create a new species that can be used for medical research. However, their experiments have been unsuccessful, and they are about to give up when Emma discovers a unique DNA sample that she believes holds the key to creating life.

Emma decides to use this DNA sample to create a new organism, which she names "Dren." As Dren begins to grow and develop, the team is amazed by its rapid progress and potential. However, as Dren grows in size and strength, it becomes clear that something is not quite right.

Dren's behavior becomes increasingly erratic and violent, and the team realizes that they have created a being with a twisted sense of self-preservation. As tensions rise, Emma begins to question whether she has made a terrible mistake by creating life.

As Dren continues to evolve, it becomes clear that it is not just a simple organism, but a being with its own desires and motivations. The team is forced to confront the consequences of their actions and the ethics of playing God.

The movie builds towards a tense and suspenseful climax as Emma and her colleagues try to understand and control Dren's behavior. In the end, they are faced with a horrific choice: to destroy Dren or risk everything to save it.

Throughout the movie, Natali explores themes of scientific hubris, the ethics of genetic engineering, and the dangers of playing God. The film is also notable for its graphic and disturbing content, which includes scenes of violence, gore, and body horror.

Overall, Splice is a thought-provoking and unsettling sci-fi horror film that challenges viewers to consider the consequences of scientific progress without moral responsibility.

overview: Archive is a 2020 science fiction thriller directed by Gavin Rothery. Set in 2038, it follows George Almore, a scientist working in a remote facility on developing a true human-equivalent artificial intelligence. George’s goal is deeply personal: to recreate his deceased wife through advanced AI and robotics technology.George has created several prototypes of androids designed to house his wife’s consciousness. He is in the final stages of perfecting the latest model, which is almost indistinguishable from a real human. Throughout the film, George struggles with the ethical and emotional challenges of his project, as well as the risks involved in pushing the boundaries of technology.As George interacts with the android, named J3, it becomes clear that the line between human and machine is blurring. J3 shows moments of self-awareness and emotional responses, raising questions about consciousness and identity.Meanwhile, George is hiding his true motive—his desperate desire to reunite with his wife, who passed away years earlier. His work is secretive, and the risks of his experiment extend beyond technical difficulties to psychological and moral dilemmas.The film explores themes such as grief, love, loss, the nature of consciousness, and the ethical implications of artificial intelligence. It probes the question of whether recreating a loved one digitally can truly replace the original person or if it’s a haunting illusion.
tagline: Death is not the end
title: Archive
plot:
Archive is a 2020 British science fiction film written and directed by Gavin Rothery in his directorial debut. Set in 2038, it stars Theo James as George Almore, a robotics engineer, with Stacy Martin, Rhona Mitra, Peter Ferdinando, Lia Williams and Toby Jones. Its planned premiere at South by Southwest in March 2020 was canceled because of the COVID-19 pandemic, and it was instead released digitally and in limited theaters in the United States on 10 July 2020.

George's wife, Jules, has been killed in a car accident, but her consciousness has been preserved by a company called Archive, whose technology lets George speak with her by video for a limited total of about 200 hours. Working alone at a remote, snowbound research facility in Japan on a project for his employer, George secretly pursues a personal goal: building a robot body capable of holding Jules's consciousness permanently. He has already made two prototypes. J1 is a crude, childlike machine, while J2 has the mind of a teenager and grows jealous of George's work on the third, nearly complete model, J3, increasingly behaving unpredictably.

Representatives from Archive come to inspect the device storing Jules's mind, notice that it has been tampered with and suspect that George is stealing their intellectual property. George finishes the J3 robot, which is strikingly humanlike. Confronted with the realization that she will never become anything more than she is, J2 destroys herself by walking into a lake, and Archive retrieves the robot and threatens to sue George's employer. When his boss discovers his secret project, she fires him. In a final call with Jules, George ends by saying he will see her soon, and J3, overhearing, realizes that he intends to overwrite her consciousness with Jules's. As George races to complete the transfer before he loses access to the facility, the film builds toward a revelation that reframes everything he believes about his situation and his wife's death.

Archive received generally favorable reviews. It holds a 78 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus says it executes its fairly basic program efficiently while offering an engaging meditation on love and human nature, and a Metacritic score of 67. Critics particularly praised its production design and atmosphere on a modest budget.

overview: Sara and Brian live an idyllic life with their young son and daughter. But their family is rocked by sudden, heartbreaking news that forces them to make a difficult and unorthodox choice in order to save their baby girl's life. The parents' desperate decision raises both ethical and moral questions and rips away at the foundation of their relationship. Their actions ultimately set off a court case that threatens to tear the family apart, while revealing surprising truths that challenge everyone's perceptions of love and loyalty and give new meaning to the definition of healing.
tagline: A tale of life, love, and letting go.
title: My Sister's Keeper
plot:
My Sister's Keeper is a 2009 American drama film directed by Nick Cassavetes, based on the novel of the same name by Jodi Picoult.

The movie revolves around the complex relationship between two sisters, Kate Fitzgerald (Sofia Vassilieva) and Anna Fitzgerald (Abigail Breslin), who are genetically identical twins. The story begins with a heart-wrenching scene where Anna is diagnosed with leukemia, which prompts her parents, Brian (Cameron Diaz) and Sara (Aubrey Plaza), to seek a second opinion from a geneticist.

The geneticist, Dr. Leslie Burke (Sandra Bullock), informs the family that Anna's identical twin sister, Kate, has a rare genetic mutation that makes her a perfect bone marrow donor for Anna. The parents decide to use this genetic material without Anna's consent, which leads to a court battle and a dramatic confrontation between the sisters.

The main themes of My Sister's Keeper include:

1. **Family dynamics**: The movie explores the intricate relationships within the Fitzgerald family, particularly the bond between Kate and Anna, who are genetically identical but have distinct personalities.
2. **Medical ethics**: The film raises questions about the morality of using a child's genetic material for medical purposes without their consent. It highlights the complexities of medical decision-making and the need for informed consent.
3. **Identity and autonomy**: As Anna grows older, she begins to assert her independence and individuality, which puts her at odds with her parents' wishes. The movie explores the tension between a child's desire for autonomy and the responsibilities that come with being a family member.
4. **Grief and loss**: The story is marked by tragedy, as Anna's leukemia diagnosis sets off a chain of events that lead to devastating consequences. The film handles these themes with sensitivity, exploring the emotional toll on the characters and their loved ones.

Overall, My Sister's Keeper is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of family relationships, medical ethics, and personal identity.

overview: Docu-drama based on the life of Ted Bundy, a serial killer who killed at least 19 young women during the 1970's (though some sources say as many as 30 to 35 were murdered). Set from his college student years, to his first victims, his capture, escape from prison (twice), his final killing spree to his trial, conviction and execution.
tagline: Not every serial killer fits the profile.
title: Ted Bundy
plot:
Ted Bundy is a 2002 independent biographical crime thriller directed by Matthew Bright, who wrote it with Stephen Johnston. A sardonic dramatisation of the crimes of the American serial killer who raped and murdered numerous young women during the 1970s, it stars Michael Reilly Burke as Bundy and Boti Bliss as his girlfriend Lee, with Tracey Walter, Deborah Offner and Tom Savini in supporting roles.

In 1974 Ted Bundy is a law student in Seattle with a long-term girlfriend and a part-time job at a crisis hotline. Hidden from those around him is a sadistic personality given to stalking, voyeurism and theft. He commits his first murder, killing a woman who called the hotline, and soon develops a pattern: breaking into the homes of young women or luring them to his car by pretending to be injured or posing as a police officer, then abducting, assaulting and killing them. His knowledge of police methods helps him avoid suspicion, although investigators have composite sketches and have learned his name from witnesses.

In Utah in 1975 a young woman escapes from his moving car, and her description of the vehicle later leads to his arrest, when officers find his kit of restraints and tools in the trunk. Convicted of kidnapping, he becomes the prime suspect in a series of murders. When he assures Lee that the authorities can never prove the killings, she realises he is guilty and leaves him.

Acting as his own lawyer in Colorado in 1977, Ted escapes by jumping from a courthouse library window, is recaptured days later, and then escapes again, landing on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted list. Settling in Tallahassee, Florida, he attacks four women in a Florida State University sorority house, killing two, and then murders a young girl before being caught. Sentenced to die in the electric chair, he spends a decade filing appeals that all fail. In 1989 guards drag him to the execution chamber, and later Lee, watching the news with her husband, wonders who Ted Bundy really was.

The film had a limited theatrical run in American cities including New York and Los Angeles in September 2002 and grossed under $70,000 worldwide. It holds a 41% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: With a team of the world's foremost historic and marine experts as well as friend Bill Paxton, James Cameron embarks on an unscripted adventure back to the wreck of the Titanic where nearly 1,500 souls lost their lives almost a century ago.
tagline: The legend no one can forget has become the greatest adventure ever filmed.
title: Ghosts of the Abyss
plot:
Ghosts of the Abyss is a documentary film directed by James Cameron, not produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The film is a sequel to the 1995 film Titanic and explores the wreckage of the Titanic.

The main theme of Ghosts of the Abyss revolves around the exploration of the Titanic's final resting place, and it delves into the mysteries surrounding the ship's tragic fate. The documentary also touches on the emotional connection people have with the Titanic, as well as the sense of loss and tragedy that still lingers long after the event.

The film is not just a factual account but also an introspective journey for James Cameron, who revisits the site where his previous film was set. It's a poignant exploration of human curiosity, the power of storytelling, and the enduring impact of historical events on our collective psyche.

As for Walt Disney Pictures, they were not involved in the production of Ghosts of the Abyss.

overview: A cop turns vigilante after his family is murdered, exacting vengeance on the killers - and then on all criminals who have slipped through the system.
tagline: They each have a score to settle.
title: Recoil
plot:
Recoil is a 2011 Canadian-American action film directed by Terry Miles, starring Steve Austin as a vigilante hunting the men who murdered his family. Danny Trejo, Serinda Swan, Keith Jardine, Lochlyn Munro and Noel Gugliemi co-star. It premiered in the United States on March 6, 2012.

In 2009 Ryan Varrett, a police officer in Dallas, survived an attack by a gang that killed his wife and nine-year-old son, killing three of the attackers himself. He has since left the force and taken to the road, tracking down and executing everyone involved, while FBI Special Agent Frank Sutton of the Seattle office investigates the string of dead criminals.

After killing a rapist, Ryan arrives in the small town of Hope, Washington, where a gas station owner, Kirby, points him to a little hotel run by a woman named Darcy. There he finds Rex Santiago, one of the gang members who attacked his family. Hope is controlled by the Circle, a drug- and gun-running biker gang led by Rex's brother Drayke, a fugitive wanted by the ATF, and the local sheriff, Cole, is in his pocket. When Ryan kills Rex, Drayke declares war on him and the town becomes a battlefield.

Ryan learns that Drayke planned the attack on his family as part of a campaign of revenge against the police officers who had sent him to a prison where he was brutalised. After Drayke's right-hand man Crab murders Kirby, Ryan burns Crab to death. Sutton arrives in Hope, and while Cole tries to pass off Rex's death as an accident, the sheriff's son, Deputy Hedge, who is not on the gang's payroll, explains how the Circle went from protecting the town to dealing guns and methamphetamine.

The bikers seize Darcy and beat Ryan, taking them both to an abandoned ferry that serves as Drayke's headquarters. Ryan breaks free, defeats Drayke's men and rescues Darcy. Cole, meanwhile, takes his own life, and Hedge and Sutton set out after Drayke. Ryan confronts the gang leader, whom he remembers from the night of the attack, and their fight ends when Sutton shoots Drayke dead.

Sutton chooses not to arrest Ryan, Hedge becomes sheriff, and Darcy decides to stay in Hope as Ryan leaves town, promising to send her a postcard. The film drew moderately positive reviews, with some critics appreciating its return to a plainer style of action filmmaking.

overview: Texan Charles Farmer left the Air Force as a young man to save the family ranch when his dad died. Like most American ranchers, he owes his bank. Unlike most, he's an astrophysicist with a rocket in his barn - one he's built and wants to take into space. It's his dream. The FBI puts him under surveillance when he tries to buy rocket fuel, and the FAA stalls him when he files a flight plan – but Charles is undeterred.
title: The Astronaut Farmer
plot:
The Astronaut Farmer is a 2006 American family drama film that explores the complexities of family relationships and the sacrifices made for the greater good. The movie revolves around Michael Collins, a former astronaut who returns to his rural Texas farm after being grounded due to a heart condition. As he struggles to adjust to life on Earth, he must also confront the consequences of his past actions and the expectations placed upon him by his family.

The film delves into themes of identity, duty, and redemption, as Michael navigates his relationships with his wife, his children, and his estranged father. Through his character's journey, the movie highlights the importance of finding one's place in the world and making amends for past mistakes.

One of the primary themes of The Astronaut Farmer is the struggle to balance personal ambition with family responsibilities. Michael's experiences as an astronaut have left him feeling disconnected from his loved ones, and he must confront the reality that his career choices have come at a great cost to those around him.

The film also explores the theme of forgiveness and understanding, particularly in the context of intergenerational relationships. As Michael reconciles with his father, played by Sam Elliott, he comes to terms with the complexities of their past and the ways in which they have hurt each other.

Ultimately, The Astronaut Farmer is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that celebrates the power of family love and redemption. Through its exploration of complex themes and characters, the movie offers a nuanced portrayal of what it means to be human and to find one's place in the world.

overview: A reimagining of the classic horror tale about Carrie White, a shy girl outcast by her peers and sheltered by her deeply religious mother, who unleashes telekinetic terror on her small town after being pushed too far at her senior prom.
tagline: Know her name. Fear her power.
title: Carrie
plot:
Carrie is a 2013 American supernatural horror film directed by Kimberly Peirce, the third screen adaptation of Stephen King's 1974 novel and a remake of the 1976 film. Written by Lawrence D. Cohen and Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa and produced by Kevin Misher, it stars Chloë Grace Moretz as Carrie White and Julianne Moore as her mother, Margaret, with Judy Greer, Portia Doubleday and Alex Russell.

Carrie is a shy, friendless student at a high school in Maine. When she gets her first period in the gym showers and, not knowing what is happening, believes she is bleeding to death, the other girls mock her and pelt her with tampons, and the bully Chris Hargensen films the scene and posts it online. The gym teacher, Miss Desjardin, comforts her, but at home her fanatically religious mother treats menstruation as a sin and locks her in a prayer closet. A crack appears in the door, and Carrie soon begins exploring and learning to control telekinetic powers.

Desjardin punishes the girls involved, and Chris, refusing detention, is barred from the prom. Remorseful, Sue Snell asks her boyfriend Tommy Ross to take Carrie to the dance. Carrie accepts, sews her own dress and, when Margaret tries to stop her, uses her powers to shut her mother in the closet.

At the prom, Chris and her boyfriend Billy rig the vote so that Carrie and Tommy are crowned queen and king. Sue rushes to warn someone after a taunting text from Chris, but Desjardin, suspecting her, keeps her out. A bucket of blood is dumped on Carrie and the shower video plays on screens around the hall. Humiliated, and after the falling bucket kills Tommy, Carrie unleashes her powers on the crowd, sparing only Desjardin, as fire engulfs the school. She then kills Billy and Chris as they try to run her down.

At home, Margaret reveals that Carrie was conceived through rape and stabs her, and Carrie kills her mother. As stones rain down on the house, Sue arrives; Carrie senses that she is pregnant, throws her clear and is buried as the house collapses.

The film grossed $84 million worldwide. It holds a 51% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with critics praising its cast and modern updates but finding little new in the story.

overview: In 1984, a Russian research team goes below the surface to find out what secret the world's deepest borehole is hiding. On their expedition, something unexpectedly gruesome awaits the researchers.
tagline: No light. No salvation.
title: The Superdeep
plot:
The Superdeep (Russian: Kol'skaya sverkhglubokaya) is a 2020 Russian horror film directed by Arseny Syuhin, inspired by the real Kola Superdeep Borehole, the deep scientific drilling project on the Kola Peninsula in the Soviet Arctic. Set in the Soviet Union in 1984, it follows a small team of researchers and soldiers sent to investigate a mysterious outbreak at a secret laboratory built kilometers beneath the Arctic surface.

Anna Fedorova, a Soviet epidemiologist, is haunted by the death of a colleague who tested an experimental vaccine on himself after she agreed to skip safety trials to meet state deadlines. On New Year's Eve, she is summoned by Colonel Morozov of military intelligence for a clandestine mission to the Kola borehole near Murmansk. Officially a drilling site, it secretly houses an underground laboratory where strange sounds were recorded deep below the surface, after which twenty people went missing. Anna's task is to collect samples from a suspected disease outbreak concealed by the site's director, Dr. Grigoriev.

Accompanied by a squad of soldiers led by Major Mikheev, Anna arrives at the frozen facility, where a man in a lab coat survives several gunshots before killing himself with a grenade. Evacuating staff warn that the lower levels are hell. Descending into the facility, the team discovers that a parasitic fungal organism has been infecting the workers, mutating their bodies and fusing them into monstrous forms. As the team searches for survivors and pursues Grigoriev, they face the organism's growing threat and Anna realizes that the infection must never be allowed to reach the surface.

The film draws on the legends surrounding the Kola borehole and combines Cold War paranoia with body horror reminiscent of science fiction classics about isolated research stations.

The Superdeep was released in 2020 and received mixed to negative reviews, holding 29 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, with an average rating of 4.1 out of 10. Its premise draws on popular myths about sounds recorded at the bottom of the real borehole.

original_title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows
overview: After supervillain Shredder escapes custody, he joins forces with mad scientist Baxter Stockman and two dimwitted henchmen, Bebop and Rocksteady, to unleash a diabolical plan to take over the world. As the Turtles prepare to take on Shredder and his new crew, they find themselves facing an even greater evil with similar intentions: the notorious Krang.
title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows
plot:
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows is a 2016 American superhero comedy film directed by Dave Green and written by Josh Appignanesi, Art Marcum, Matt Holloway, and Seth Grahame-Smith. The movie is the sequel to the 2014 film Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.

The story begins with the Turtles (Leonardo, Donatello, Michelangelo, and Raphael) living in New York City, where they have formed a strong bond with April O'Neil (Megan Fox), a journalist who has become like a sister to them. The Turtles are still fighting against the evil Shredder (Tohoru Masamune), the leader of the Foot Clan, but they also face new threats from other villains.

The movie introduces two new characters: Krang (voiced by Fred Armisen), an alien warlord who seeks to conquer Earth and its inhabitants; and Baxter Stockman (Tyler Perry), a scientist who works for Shredder and is obsessed with creating the perfect Foot Clan soldier. The Turtles soon discover that Krang has taken over Baxter's body, using his technology to control him.

As the story unfolds, the Turtles must face their new enemies while also dealing with personal struggles. Leonardo (Jellystone) is struggling with leadership, feeling overwhelmed by the responsibility of being the leader of the group. Donatello (Beezle) is trying to find a way to defeat Krang and Baxter, who are using advanced technology to wreak havoc on New York City.

Meanwhile, Michelangelo (Raph's brother) is dealing with his own demons, feeling like he doesn't fit in with the rest of the group. Raphael (Michelangelo's brother) is struggling with anger issues, which puts him at odds with Leonardo and Donatello.

The Turtles also have to navigate their relationships with April and Casey Jones (Stephen Amell), a hockey-masked vigilante who becomes an ally in their fight against Shredder and Krang. The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, including battles between the Turtles and the Foot Clan, as well as showdowns between the heroes and the villains.

In the end, the Turtles are able to defeat Shredder and Baxter, but not before they realize that their greatest enemy is within themselves. The movie ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as the Turtles come together to support each other and face whatever challenges come their way.

Overall, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows is an entertaining and action-packed sequel that expands on the characters and world introduced in the first film. While it may not be as strong as its predecessor, it still delivers plenty of laughs, excitement, and heart.

original_title: Mune, le gardien de la lune
overview: When a faun named Mune becomes the Guardian of the Moon, little did he had unprepared experience with the Moon and an accident that could put both the Moon and the Sun in danger, including a corrupt titan named Necross who wants the Sun for himself and placing the balance of night and day in great peril. Now with the help of a wax-child named Glim and the warrior, Sohone who also became the Sun Guardian, they go out on an exciting journey to get the Sun back and restore the Moon to their rightful place in the sky.
title: Mune: Guardian of the Moon
plot:
Mune: Guardian of the Moon is a 2015 French-Belgian animated musical fantasy film directed by Pascal Pinon, produced by Onyx Films, and Studio Mir. The movie follows the story of Mune, a young boy who lives on the moon with his adoptive family.

The main themes of Mune: Guardian of the Moon include:

1. **Identity**: Mune struggles to find his place in the world, feeling like an outsider among his lunar family. His journey is about self-discovery and embracing his true identity.
2. **Belonging**: The film explores the theme of belonging, as Mune searches for a sense of home and connection with others. He eventually finds acceptance and love on Earth, but also learns to appreciate his roots on the moon.
3. **Friendship**: The movie highlights the importance of friendship and loyalty, particularly between Mune and his friends, including Cendrillon and Lao Ma.
4. **Growing up**: Mune's journey is also a metaphor for growing up and transitioning from childhood to adulthood. He faces challenges and learns valuable lessons about responsibility, courage, and sacrifice.

The film features a richly detailed world with a unique blend of fantasy and science fiction elements, making it a visually stunning and engaging watch. The story is full of memorable characters, catchy musical numbers, and exciting action sequences, all of which contribute to its enduring appeal.

Overall, Mune: Guardian of the Moon is a heartwarming and imaginative film that explores universal themes in a way that's both entertaining and accessible to audiences of all ages.

overview: To inherit her father's company, socialite Ellen must first visit his small hometown, where she learns the value of hard work and helping others.
title: Christmas Inheritance
plot:
Christmas Inheritance is a 2017 Canadian Christmas romantic comedy-drama film directed by Ernie Barbarash and written by Dinah Eng. Eliza Taylor stars as a pampered New York heiress sent to a small town to prove herself, with Jake Lacy as the local innkeeper and Andie MacDowell as the owner of the town diner. Netflix released it on December 15, 2017.

Jim Langford, a Manhattan business executive, wants to retire, but worries that his carefree daughter, Ellen, is not ready to succeed him as chief executive. Every Christmas, Jim and his former business partner, Zeke, exchange letters in person in Snow Falls, the small New England town where they founded the company. This year, as a test, Jim sends Ellen to deliver his letter in a box holding their past letters to her "Uncle Zeke." Wanting her to learn to rely on herself rather than the family's money and name, he gives her only a hundred dollars in cash and asks her to travel without revealing who she is.

In Snow Falls, Ellen befriends Jake, who manages the town's inn, and learns that Zeke has just left for his cabin. She takes a room to wait for him and dines with Jake at the diner run by his aunt, Debbie. When Zeke still has not appeared the next day, Ellen's fiancé, Gray, urges her to leave the letters and come home, but she insists on fulfilling her father's request. Out of money, she works at the inn to pay her way, and later helps at the diner, where Debbie recognizes her but keeps her secret and teaches her to bake.

When a snowstorm knocks out power, Jake shelters townspeople at the inn, and Ellen, inspired by him, gives her bed to a mother and her children. Ellen and Jake open up to each other and they grow close. Gray arrives to collect Ellen and, after dismissing the town, reveals her identity to Jake, who feels betrayed. On the drive back to the city, Ellen realizes how little Gray values her father's traditions, returns her engagement ring and takes a bus back to Snow Falls.

At the town's Christmas Eve celebration, Ellen apologizes to Jake. Zeke, dressed as Santa Claus, reads Jim's letter aloud, revealing that the journey was meant to teach Ellen the value of tradition, friendship and love, and that she will become the company's new CEO. Jim himself arrives and reunites with Debbie, his high school sweetheart, while Jake asks Ellen to dance. Reviews were mixed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 50% approval from a small number of critics.

overview: As the deceased soul Ja-hong and his three afterlife guardians prepare for their remaining trials for reincarnation, the guardians soon come face to face with the truth of their tragic time on Earth 1,000 years earlier.
tagline: Unveiling millennium-old secrets.
title: Along with the Gods: The Last 49 Days
plot:
Along with the Gods: The Last 49 Days is a 2018 South Korean fantasy adventure film directed by Kim Sung-su and written by Lee Seung-jun. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Park Chang-pil.

The story follows Han-seo (played by Ha Jung-woo), a young man who dies in a car accident at the age of 18. However, he soon finds himself transported to the afterlife, where he meets three gods: Hae-soo (played by Kim Hyang-gi), a goddess of love and beauty; Jang-seo (played by Park Seo-joon), a god of war; and Mu-seo (played by Ma Dong-seok), a god of death.

The three gods inform Han-seo that he has been chosen to participate in the "Great Competition" - a test of worthiness to ascend to heaven. The competition is a 49-day trial, during which Han-seo must complete various tasks and prove his worth to the gods.

As the story progresses, Han-seo embarks on a journey through different realms, each representing a different aspect of human life. He encounters various characters, including a young woman named Ji-hyun (played by Kim Mi-so), who becomes his love interest. Along the way, he also faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including fierce battles with monsters and rival contestants.

Throughout the movie, Han-seo's character undergoes significant development as he learns to confront his own flaws and weaknesses. He begins to understand the true nature of the afterlife and the gods' intentions, which ultimately leads him to question their motives.

As the 49-day trial nears its end, Han-seo faces off against the main antagonist, a powerful being known as the "God of Darkness." In a climactic battle, Han-seo uses his newfound skills and knowledge to defeat the God of Darkness and prove himself worthy to ascend to heaven.

In the end, Han-seo is granted his wish to return to earth, but with a twist - he is given a second chance at life, albeit in a different form. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, as Han-seo sets out to make the most of his new life and find happiness with Ji-hyun.

Overall, Along with the Gods: The Last 49 Days is a visually stunning and action-packed film that explores themes of mortality, redemption, and the human condition. With its unique blend of fantasy and adventure elements, it has become a beloved classic among Korean cinema fans.

overview: When the three pigs find a tiny wolf cub on their doorstep, they decide to raise him as their own, unaware that they've played right into the plan of a special-ops team of wolves. As the newest addition to their family, Lucky grows into his teens not knowing his history, his role in the wolves' plan or the difficult choice he will have to make about the family that raised him.
title: Unstable Fables: 3 Pigs & a Baby
plot:
Unstable Fables: 3 Pigs & a Baby is a 2008 American computer-animated comedy, the first of three direct-to-DVD Unstable Fables features produced by The Jim Henson Company with Flame Ventures, Prana Studios and The Weinstein Company, and distributed by Genius Products. Directed by Howard E. Baker and Arish Fyzee from a script by Craig Bartlett and Joseph Purdy, with music by Jim Lang, it irreverently reimagines "The Three Little Pigs" with a modern, pop-culture twist. It was released on DVD on 4 March 2008.

The story is told largely in flashback by the three pigs as they hang upside down over a cooking pot, recalling what happened after the familiar tale ended. Having failed to huff and puff their way into the pigs' impenetrable brick house, and regrouping after the loss of the Big Bad Wolf, a militaristic special-ops team of wolves hatches a patient scheme: they leave a tiny wolf cub in a basket on the pigs' doorstep, planning to use him one day as an inside operative. The surfer-style straw builder Sandy, the neurotic stick builder and the burly bricklayer Mason take the baby in, name him Lucky and raise him lovingly as their son, so devoted to him that they overlook the fact that they are bringing up a natural predator.

Lucky grows into his teens knowing nothing of his origins, but his claws and sharp teeth become harder to ignore, and his adolescent rebellion arrives complete with dyed blue hair, a motorbike and heavy metal songs about eating pigs. The wolves seize the moment, courting him with promises of belonging and status, including the attentions of a teenage she-wolf, and Lucky is forced to choose between the wolf pack he was born into and the family that raised him.

The voice cast features Brad Garrett as Mason, Jon Cryer as the stick-building pig, Steve Zahn as Sandy and Jesse McCartney as the teenage Lucky, with his brother Timothy McCartney voicing Lucky as a child. Tom Kenny, Nolan North, Tara Strong, Steve Wilcox and Audrey Wasilewski voice a range of wolves and townsfolk. Reception was mixed: Video Librarian called it a fresh and funny update and an Editor's Choice, Common Sense Media praised its smarts and compelling plot, while other reviewers found its humour, pacing and animation merely average next to major studio fairy-tale parodies.

overview: After his girlfriend, Julie, and two best friends are killed in a tragic auto accident, Nick struggles to cope with his loss and grief. Suffering from migraine-like seizures, Nick soon discovers that he has the power to change the past via his memories. However, his time-traveling attempts to alter the past and save his one true love have unexpected and dire consequences.
tagline: Can you change your past without destroying your future?
title: The Butterfly Effect 2
plot:
The Butterfly Effect 2 is a 2006 American science fiction psychological thriller film directed by John R. Leonetti and written by Mike Werb. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2004 film The Butterfly Effect.

The main themes of The Butterfly Effect 2 revolve around the consequences of altering one's past, the fragility of reality, and the devastating effects of playing with time. The story follows Evan Treborn (played by Ashton Kutcher), who is still struggling to cope with his traumatic childhood experiences.

As the movie progresses, it becomes clear that Evan's actions in the first film have created a ripple effect, causing chaos and destruction throughout his life. The film explores the idea of how even small changes can have significant and far-reaching consequences, leading to a downward spiral of events that are difficult to control or predict.

The Butterfly Effect 2 also delves into the theme of guilt and responsibility, as Evan grapples with the repercussions of his actions and tries to make amends for the harm he has caused. The film raises questions about the nature of free will and whether our choices truly determine our destiny.

Throughout the movie, the narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, mirroring the time-travel elements of the story. This structure adds to the sense of disorientation and confusion, reflecting Evan's own struggles to navigate the complexities of his altered reality.

Ultimately, The Butterfly Effect 2 presents a cautionary tale about the dangers of meddling with the timeline and the importance of accepting one's past experiences as a part of who they are.

overview: When his best friend and podcast co-host goes missing in the backwoods of Canada, a young guy joins forces with his friend's girlfriend to search for him.
tagline: Let me tell you a story...
title: Tusk
plot:
Tusk is a 2014 Canadian black comedy horror film directed by Kevin Smith and written by Smith and Joseph Keery. The film stars Michael Parks, Justin Long, Haley Joel Osment, and Genesis Rodriguez.

The story begins with Wallace Bryton (Justin Long), a podcaster who hosts a popular show called "The Tusk That Took My Tush" where he interviews guests about their unusual experiences. On his latest episode, Wallace meets Howard Howe (Michael Parks), an eccentric old man who claims to have undergone a transformation into a walrus-like creature after being attacked by a whale.

Wallace is skeptical of the story but agrees to meet with Howard in person. However, when Wallace arrives at Howard's remote cabin, he finds himself in a desperate situation. Howard has indeed transformed into a walrus, and Wallace soon discovers that he too has undergone a similar transformation, turning him into a human-walrus hybrid.

As the days pass, Wallace struggles to cope with his new form, which is both physically and emotionally challenging. He tries to find a way to reverse the transformation but realizes that Howard's cabin is surrounded by a group of ruthless poachers who are hunting walruses for their tusks.

The plot thickens as Wallace forms an unlikely alliance with Howard, who has become increasingly unstable and violent in his human-walrus form. As they navigate the treacherous wilderness together, Wallace begins to question his own identity and humanity.

Throughout the film, Kevin Smith explores themes of identity, masculinity, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The film's tone is darkly comedic, with a touch of absurdity that adds to its offbeat charm.

As the story unfolds, Wallace and Howard face numerous challenges, including the poachers, treacherous terrain, and their own internal struggles. In the end, Wallace manages to escape from the cabin and find his way back to civilization, but not before confronting the darker aspects of himself and the true nature of his transformation.

The film's climax features a tense showdown between Wallace and Howard, who has become increasingly unhinged in his human-walrus form. The outcome is both shocking and unsettling, leaving the audience with a lasting sense of unease.

Overall, Tusk is a unique and unsettling film that explores themes of identity and humanity through a darkly comedic lens. With its blend of horror, comedy, and drama, it has become a cult classic among fans of offbeat cinema.

overview: Former Gotham City District Attorney Harvey Dent, one side of his face scarred by acid, goes on a crime spree based on the number '2'. All of his actions are decided by the flip of a defaced, two-headed silver dollar.
tagline: Everyone must face their demons.
title: Batman vs. Two-Face
plot:
Batman vs. Two-Face is a 2017 American animated superhero film produced by Warner Bros. Animation and a direct sequel to Batman: Return of the Caped Crusaders (2016). Based on the 1960s Batman television series, it features Adam West, Burt Ward and Julie Newmar reprising their roles as Batman, Robin and Catwoman, with William Shatner voicing District Attorney Harvey Dent, who becomes Two-Face. It premiered at New York Comic Con in October 2017 before its digital and home-video release later that month. It was West's final performance as Batman and was released after his death in June 2017.

Batman and Robin join Gotham's district attorney, Harvey Dent, at a secret demonstration by Professor Hugo Strange and Dr. Harleen Quinzel of the "Evil Extractor," a machine designed to drain the evil from captured criminals and store it in a vat. When the vat explodes, Dent is drenched in liquefied evil, which scars half of his face and splits his personality, turning him into the coin-flipping criminal Two-Face. After a series of clashes with the Dynamic Duo, Dent undergoes reconstructive surgery that appears to erase his evil side, and he returns to fighting crime as an assistant to the district attorney.

Six months later, Batman and Robin capture King Tut and his henchmen after they steal a biplane. Commissioner Gordon and Chief O'Hara interrogate Tut's alter ego, the mild-mannered Professor William McElroy, with O'Hara repeatedly tapping him on the head to switch his personality. After the trial, Dent and Bruce Wayne share a drink before Dent leaves for a charity event for underprivileged twins at the Winning Pair casino. Soon a mysterious package arrives at Gordon's office, signaling the return of Two-Face, whose crimes revolve around duality and the number two. Batman and Robin must determine whether Dent has relapsed, and as Catwoman reappears and the threat escalates, the heroes face death traps, disguises and a scheme that endangers Gotham City itself.

Batman vs. Two-Face received positive reviews, holding a 100 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on eight reviews. IGN gave it 8.4 out of 10, calling it a worthy entry in the 1966 canon and a fine send-off for West, and Nick Blackshaw of Starburst described it as a very entertaining piece of animation. Critics singled out Shatner's dual performance and the film's affectionate recreation of the series' campy humor.

overview: A reclusive English teacher suffering from severe obesity attempts to reconnect with his estranged teenage daughter for one last chance at redemption.
title: The Whale
plot:
The Whale is a 2022 American drama film directed by Darren Aronofsky, written by Samuel D. Hunter, and starring Brendan Fraser, Sadie Sink, Hong Chau, and Ty Simpkins.

The story revolves around Charlie (Brendan Fraser), a reclusive English teacher in his late 40s who weighs over 600 pounds. He lives alone in a small apartment with his cat, Patrick. Charlie's life is marked by loneliness, isolation, and a deep sense of regret for past mistakes.

Charlie's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Eleanor (Hong Chau), the school nurse, who becomes his love interest. Despite their physical differences, they form a connection that helps Charlie to confront his inner demons and re-evaluate his life.

As Charlie navigates his relationships with Eleanor and his estranged daughter, Liz (Sadie Sink), he begins to see the world in a different light. He starts attending support groups for people struggling with obesity and addiction, where he meets others who are fighting similar battles.

Through his interactions with these individuals, Charlie gains a new perspective on life and begins to make amends for past mistakes. He also starts to reconnect with Liz, who is struggling with her own personal demons.

Throughout the film, Aronofsky employs a unique visual style, using close-ups and long takes to emphasize Charlie's physical transformation as he loses weight. The Whale is a powerful exploration of themes such as loneliness, redemption, and the human condition.

The film received widespread critical acclaim for its performances, direction, and screenplay. Brendan Fraser's performance as Charlie earned him numerous awards and nominations, including an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor.

Overall, The Whale is a poignant and powerful drama that explores the complexities of the human experience. With its outstanding performances, thought-provoking themes, and visually stunning cinematography, it is a must-see film for anyone interested in character-driven dramas.

original_title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
overview: Siblings Lucy, Edmund, Susan and Peter step through a magical wardrobe and find the land of Narnia. There, they discover a charming, once peaceful kingdom that has been plunged into eternal winter by the evil White Witch, Jadis. Aided by the wise and magnificent lion, Aslan, the children lead Narnia into a spectacular, climactic battle to be free of the Witch's glacial powers forever.
tagline: Evil Has Reigned For 100 Years...
title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
plot:
The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe is a 2005 high fantasy film directed by Andrew Adamson, based on C. S. Lewis's 1950 novel. The first installment of The Chronicles of Narnia film series, it was produced by Walt Disney Pictures and Walden Media. William Moseley, Anna Popplewell, Skandar Keynes and Georgie Henley star as the four Pevensie children, with Tilda Swinton as the White Witch and Liam Neeson as the voice of Aslan.

In 1940, to escape the Blitz, Peter, Susan, Edmund and Lucy Pevensie are evacuated to the countryside home of Professor Kirke. During a game of hide-and-seek, Lucy hides in a wardrobe and finds herself in a snowy forest in the land of Narnia, where she meets a faun, Mr. Tumnus. He confesses that he meant to hand her over to the White Witch, Jadis, who has cursed Narnia with endless winter and no Christmas, but instead he helps her return home. When Lucy returns to Narnia, Edmund follows her and meets the Witch, who tempts him with Turkish delight and a promise to make him a prince if he brings his siblings to her.

Fleeing the housekeeper, all four children escape through the wardrobe into Narnia, where they find that Tumnus has been arrested. Mr. and Mrs. Beaver tell them that Aslan, the true king, has returned and of a prophecy that four humans will end the Witch's reign. Edmund slips away to the Witch, who imprisons him and sends her wolves after the others. As her power weakens, Father Christmas gives the children gifts, including a sword for Peter, a bow for Susan and a healing cordial for Lucy. They reach Aslan, a great lion, and his army, and Edmund is rescued.

The Witch claims Edmund's life as a traitor under the Deep Magic, and Aslan secretly agrees to die in his place. Lucy and Susan watch as the Witch kills him on the Stone Table. The next morning, Aslan returns to life through a deeper magic and leads the sisters to free the creatures turned to stone in the Witch's castle. In the great battle, Edmund is gravely wounded while breaking the Witch's wand before Aslan arrives and kills her, and Lucy heals him. The four are crowned kings and queens of Narnia. Years later, as adults, they follow a white stag back through the wardrobe and return as children to the same moment they left.

The film premiered on 7 December 2005 and was a critical and commercial success. It grossed $745 million worldwide, won the Academy Award for Best Makeup, and was followed by Prince Caspian (2008).

overview: After watching their respective partners die, a cop and a hitman form an alliance in order to bring down their common enemy.
tagline: Revenge Never Gets Old.
title: Bullet to the Head
plot:
Bullet to the Head is a 2012 action thriller film directed by Santiago Cabrera and starring Sylvester Stallone, Sung Kang, and Sarah Shahi.

The movie follows the story of hitman Jimmy Bobo (Sylvester Stallone) who teams up with a private investigator named Keegan (Sung Kang) to take down a crime lord. The plot revolves around their quest for revenge against the men responsible for the murder of Keegan's wife, which also happens to be on the same day as Jimmy Bobo's hitman contract.

The main themes of Bullet to the Head include:

1. Revenge: The movie explores the theme of revenge and its consequences. Both Jimmy Bobo and Keegan are driven by a desire for revenge against those who have wronged them, which leads to a series of violent confrontations.
2. Loyalty: The film highlights the importance of loyalty and friendship. Despite their differences, Jimmy Bobo and Keegan form an unlikely alliance that helps them achieve their goals.
3. Redemption: Through his partnership with Keegan, Jimmy Bobo begins to question his own morality and seek redemption for past mistakes.
4. Violence: The movie is known for its graphic violence and dark humor, which serves as a commentary on the cyclical nature of violence in society.

Overall, Bullet to the Head is an action-packed thriller that explores themes of revenge, loyalty, and redemption through its violent and humorous take on the hitman genre.

overview: When a young Master Ip stops a kidnapping, he ignites a turf war with a ruthless human trafficking ring. In retaliation, the gang kidnaps one of Ip Man’s close friends, forcing him to face the group’s brutal boxing champion head-on.
title: Ip Man: The Awakening
plot:
Ip Man: The Awakening (Chinese: Ye Wen Zongshi Juexing) is a 2021 Chinese martial arts action film that serves as an origin story for the Wing Chun master Ip Man, the teacher of Bruce Lee and the subject of Donnie Yen's acclaimed Hong Kong film series. Running about 80 minutes, it stars Miu Tse, a former child star associated with Jet Li, as the young Ip Man, with Sergio De Ieso as the British villain Mr. Stark and Chen Guanying, Hou Tongjiang and Gu Lei in supporting roles. The film is in Cantonese, and its fights pit Ip Man's Wing Chun against bartitsu, a real but largely forgotten British martial art of the nineteenth century that blends Western boxing with Asian techniques and often makes use of a cane.

Apparently set in the 1930s, the story follows a young Ip Man, a gifted fighter who arrives in the big city for the first time with no idea of the corruption he will face. When he stops a kidnapping, he stumbles upon a large-scale human trafficking ring run by arrogant British colonialists led by Mr. Stark, who round up local women with the help of police officers on the take and Chinese collaborators more interested in money than in their compatriots. His intervention ignites a turf war with the gang. In retaliation, the traffickers kidnap one of Ip Man's close friends, and after suffering losses and setbacks, he sets out to rescue the captive women, defend Chinese pride against the colonial bullies and confront the group's brutal boxing champion and finally Stark himself.

Distributed in North America by Well Go USA, the film premiered on the Hi-Yah! streaming service on 20 May 2022 and was later released on Blu-ray; in the United Kingdom it reached the Icon Film Channel in April 2023 and cinemas in May. Reviews were mixed. Mark Glass of We Are Movie Geeks gave it three out of four stars, calling Tse a worthy successor in the role and a likely rising star, and noting that although the early fights suffered from close camerawork and choppy editing, the later ones were polished. He also highlighted the novelty of bartitsu. Phil Hoad of The Guardian was harsher, describing it as a clunky attempt to cash in on Yen's superior series with a laughably thin narrative and pantomime villains who speak oddly accented English, though he found Tse spry and convincing in the generally competent fight scenes.

overview: Youngsters called Kildren, who are destined to live eternally in their adolescence. The Kildren are conscious that every day could be the last, because they fight a war as entertainment, organized and operated by adults. But as they embrace the reality they are faced with, they live their day-to-day lives to the full.
title: The Sky Crawlers
plot:
The Sky Crawlers is a thought-provoking anime film that explores the human cost of war and the consequences of technological advancements on society. Set in an alternate history where humanity has colonized other planets, the story follows a young soldier named Shiro Amada as he navigates the complexities of war and grapples with the moral implications of his actions.

At its core, The Sky Crawlers is a film about the dehumanizing effects of war and the ways in which it can strip individuals of their humanity. Through Shiro's character, the film highlights the psychological toll that war takes on soldiers, who are often forced to confront the harsh realities of violence and mortality. As Shiro struggles to come to terms with his own role in the war, he begins to question the true nature of conflict and the motivations of those who wage it.

The film also explores the theme of technological advancement and its impact on society. The Sky Crawlers is set in a world where advanced technology has enabled humans to colonize other planets and engage in interplanetary warfare. However, this technology comes at a great cost, as it perpetuates a cycle of violence and destruction that threatens the very fabric of human existence.

One of the most striking aspects of The Sky Crawlers is its portrayal of the relationship between humanity and technology. Through Shiro's character, the film suggests that technology can be both a powerful tool for good and a destructive force that can dehumanize individuals and societies. As Shiro grapples with the moral implications of his actions, he begins to realize that true humanity lies not in our technological advancements, but in our capacity for empathy, compassion, and connection.

Ultimately, The Sky Crawlers is a film about the search for meaning and purpose in a world torn apart by conflict and destruction. Through its thought-provoking themes and complex characters, the film challenges viewers to confront the harsh realities of war and the consequences of technological advancement on society.

overview: A group of students investigates a series of mysterious bear killings, but learns that there are much more dangerous things going on. They start to follow a mysterious hunter, learning that he is actually a troll hunter.
tagline: You’ll believe it when you see it!
title: Troll Hunter
plot:
Troll Hunter is a Norwegian fantasy adventure film directed by André Øvredal and written by André Øvredal and Michael Fimognari. The movie was released in 2010.

The story begins with a young boy named Erik (Laurin Lundstrøm) who has always been fascinated by the supernatural creatures that are said to inhabit the forests of Norway. According to legend, trolls are real and can be found in the wilderness, but they are rarely seen by humans due to their ability to blend into their surroundings.

Erik's life is turned upside down when he meets a group of men who claim to be troll hunters. The group, led by Oskar (Stig Raetta), consists of experienced hunters who have dedicated their lives to tracking and killing the trolls that threaten human settlements.

As Erik joins the group, they embark on a mission to hunt down a particularly large and aggressive troll that has been terrorizing a nearby village. Along the way, Erik learns about the history and mythology behind the trolls, as well as the skills and techniques required to track and kill them.

Throughout their journey, the group faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and even other hunters who are not what they seem. As they get closer to their target, Erik begins to question whether the trolls are truly monstrous creatures or if there is more to them than meets the eye.

As the story unfolds, Erik discovers that the trolls are not just mindless beasts but rather complex beings with their own culture and society. The group's leader, Oskar, has a personal connection to the trolls that he keeps hidden from his team, adding an air of mystery to the narrative.

In the end, the group faces off against the troll in an epic battle that tests their skills and their resolve. As the dust settles, Erik is forced to confront the reality of what he has learned about the trolls and the world they inhabit.

The movie ends on a bittersweet note, with Erik reflecting on his experience as a troll hunter and the lessons he has learned about the importance of respecting and understanding the natural world. The final shot of the film shows Oskar walking away from the camera, leaving behind the life of a troll hunter and embracing a new path.

Overall, Troll Hunter is a thrilling adventure that combines elements of fantasy, action, and coming-of-age drama. With its richly detailed world-building and complex characters, the movie offers a unique take on the traditional troll mythology.

original_title: American Psycho II: All American Girl
overview: Rachel is a criminology student hoping to land a position as a teacher's assistant for professor Robert Starkman. She's sure this position will pave the way to an FBI career, and she's willing to do anything to obtain it -- including killing her classmates. The school psychiatrist, Dr. Daniels, becomes aware that Rachel is insane, but Rachel is skilled at her dangerous game of death and identity theft.
tagline: Angrier. Deadlier. Sexier.
title: American Psycho II: All American Girl
plot:
American Psycho 2, also known as American Psycho II: All American Girl, is a 2002 American black comedy slasher film directed by Morgan J. Freeman from a screenplay by Alex Sanger and Karen Craig. Mila Kunis stars as Rachael Newman, a criminology student, with William Shatner as her professor, Geraint Wyn Davies, Lindy Booth and Charles Officer. A stand-alone sequel to American Psycho (2000), it began as an unrelated script titled The Girl Who Wouldn't Die and was altered during production to connect it to the earlier film. It was released direct-to-video on 18 June 2002.

In 1988, a twelve-year-old girl accompanies her babysitter on a date with the serial killer Patrick Bateman. When Bateman murders the babysitter, the girl kills him with an ice pick. Five years later, the girl, Rachael Newman, is a college student studying criminology under Professor Robert Starkman, a former FBI agent famed for his work on serial killers. Determined to join the FBI, Rachael sets her sights on the coveted position of Starkman's teaching assistant, which would virtually guarantee her a place in the bureau's training program at Quantico.

When the department secretary dismisses Rachael's application because she is only a freshman, Rachael follows her home and beats her to death. She then sets out to eliminate every classmate who stands in her way, beginning with Brian, whom she drugs and kills during a planned sexual encounter. While continuing her killing spree, she starts seeing the campus psychiatrist, Dr. Eric Daniels, who realizes that she is a textbook sociopath obsessed with Starkman. Bound by confidentiality, Daniels tries to warn Starkman without naming her, but the professor mistakenly assumes the obsessed student is Cassandra Blaire, with whom he is having an affair. As the body count rises and the competition for the assistantship narrows, Rachael's methods become increasingly brazen, and Daniels, Starkman and her roommate gradually come to suspect the truth, while Rachael reveals the deeper motive behind her ambition.

American Psycho 2 was panned by critics, holding a 23 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it lackluster and ill-conceived, abandoning its predecessor's satire for shallow slasher tropes and unconvincing dark humor. Critics noted that the film's tenuous link to the original, added late in production, sat awkwardly with its campus-slasher story, although Kunis's energetic lead performance was occasionally singled out.

overview: When a Russian mobster sets up a real estate scam that generates millions of pounds, various members of London's criminal underworld pursue their share of the fortune. Various shady characters, including Mr One-Two, Stella the accountant, and Johnny Quid, a druggie rock-star, try to claim their slice.
tagline: A story of sex, thugs and rock 'n roll.
title: RocknRolla
plot:
RocknRolla is a 2008 British crime comedy film directed by Guy Ritchie. The movie follows the story of Johnny English's friend, One Two, played by Idris Elba, and his crew as they try to pull off an elaborate heist.

The main themes of RocknRolla include:

1. Loyalty: The film highlights the importance of loyalty among friends and family. One Two's crew is willing to risk their lives for each other, showcasing the strong bonds that tie them together.
2. Friendship: The movie celebrates the power of male friendships and the camaraderie that develops between characters like One Two, Turkish (Mark Strong), and Swallow (Tom Wilkinson).
3. Greed: The heist itself serves as a catalyst for exploring themes of greed and materialism. As the characters navigate the complexities of their plan, they must confront their own desires and motivations.
4. Identity: One Two's character struggles with his identity, caught between his loyalty to his crew and his desire to break free from his past. This internal conflict serves as a driving force for the plot.

The film features witty dialogue, clever plot twists, and a talented ensemble cast, making it an entertaining ride that explores these themes in a humorous and engaging way.

overview: The story of two sisters on a journey, where they try to get close to each other and approach the tough questions in life. Euphoria is a contemporary drama about responsibility and reconciliation, in a world where these concepts are gradually being lost.
tagline: It's never too late.
title: Euphoria
plot:
Euphoria is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged series that delves into the complexities of adolescence, identity, trauma, and the struggles of growing up in today's society. The show masterfully weaves together various narrative threads to explore themes such as mental health, addiction, social media's impact on self-perception, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

At its core, Euphoria is a poignant portrayal of the fragility and resilience of young lives, navigating the treacherous waters of adolescence with all its attendant emotions, desires, and vulnerabilities. The series sheds light on the crippling effects of trauma, particularly in the context of childhood abuse and neglect, which can have lasting consequences for individuals and their relationships.

The show also critiques the societal pressures that shape our perceptions of beauty, identity, and self-worth, often perpetuating unrealistic standards and expectations. Through its characters' struggles with body image, social media obsession, and the quest for validation, Euphoria highlights the performative nature of identity and the ways in which we present ourselves to the world.

Furthermore, Euphoria explores the complexities of human relationships, particularly those marked by codependency, toxic love, and the cyclical nature of abuse. The series delves into the darker aspects of human connection, revealing the ways in which our relationships can both heal and harm us.

Ultimately, Euphoria is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that acknowledges the messy, often painful realities of growing up while offering a message of hope and resilience in the face of adversity.

original_title: 劇場版 魔法科高校の劣等生 星を呼ぶ少女
overview: In the story, the seasons have changed and it will soon be the second spring. Tatsuya and Miyuki have finished their first year at First Magic High School and are on their spring break. The two go to their villa on the Ogasawara Island archipelago. After only a small moment of peace a lone young woman named Kokoa appears before them. She has abandoned the Naval base and she tells Tatsuya her one wish.
title: The Irregular at Magic High School: The Girl Who Summons the Stars
plot:
The Irregular at Magic High School: The Girl Who Summons the Stars is a Japanese anime film directed by 8-bit, based on the light novel series "Mahouka Koukou no Rettousei" by Tsutomu Satō.

The main themes of the movie can be summarized as follows:

1. **Self-discovery and empowerment**: The protagonist, Tatsuya Shiba, is a student with exceptional magical abilities who struggles to find his place in a prestigious magic academy. Throughout the story, he learns to accept himself and develop his unique strengths, ultimately becoming a confident and powerful individual.
2. **Friendship and camaraderie**: Despite initial difficulties, Tatsuya forms strong bonds with his classmates, particularly Mayumi Shiba (his sister) and Yuuhi Kaiba. These relationships help him navigate the challenges of magic school and grow as a person.
3. **Perseverance and determination**: The film highlights the importance of perseverance in overcoming obstacles. Tatsuya faces numerous setbacks, but he refuses to give up, using his intelligence and magical abilities to overcome each challenge.
4. **Social hierarchy and prejudice**: The movie explores the social stratification within the magic academy, where students are often judged based on their family background and magical abilities. This theme is particularly relevant in the context of Japanese society, where social class and status can be significant factors in determining one's opportunities and treatment.
5. **Personal growth and self-improvement**: Throughout the story, Tatsuya learns to balance his individual strengths with the need for teamwork and cooperation. He develops a more nuanced understanding of himself and his place within the world of magic.

Overall, The Irregular at Magic High School: The Girl Who Summons the Stars is a heartwarming and engaging film that explores themes of self-discovery, friendship, perseverance, social hierarchy, and personal growth.

overview: A love potion works its devious charms on fairies, elves and the swamp-dwelling Bog King as they all try to possess the potion for themselves.
tagline: Everyone Deserves to be Loved.
title: Strange Magic
plot:
Strange Magic is a 2015 animated fantasy musical film produced by Lucasfilm Ltd. The movie follows the story of three fairies - Merida, Poppy, and Arthur - who are brought together to save their magical kingdom from destruction.

The main themes of Strange Magic include:

1. Friendship: The film highlights the importance of friendship and unity among individuals with different backgrounds and personalities. Merida, Poppy, and Arthur put aside their differences to work together and save their kingdom.
2. Self-discovery: Each character in the movie undergoes a journey of self-discovery, learning to accept themselves and find their true purpose. Merida learns to let go of her independence, Poppy finds her own identity beyond being a princess, and Arthur discovers his own magical powers.
3. Love and acceptance: The film promotes love and acceptance, encouraging viewers to appreciate and celebrate individual differences. The characters learn to love and accept each other for who they are, flaws and all.
4. Empowerment: Strange Magic features strong female protagonists who take charge of their lives and make decisions that shape their futures. Merida, Poppy, and Arthur empower themselves and others, demonstrating the importance of female agency and leadership.

The movie's storyline is engaging, with a unique blend of music, humor, and adventure. The characters are well-developed and relatable, making it easy for audiences to become invested in their journeys. Overall, Strange Magic is a heartwarming film that celebrates friendship, self-discovery, love, and empowerment.

overview: Jake Kimble, the sole survivor of the Chicago massacre, is killed while in solitary confinement. His doctor begins investigating the claims he made about a long-haired woman in white, as a mysterious Japanese woman arrives at his old apartment building to help them get rid of the curse.
tagline: You can't escape the curse.
title: The Grudge 3
plot:
The Grudge 3 is a supernatural horror film directed by Toby Wilkins and written by Michael Nankin. The movie takes place in Chicago, Illinois, where a young woman named Karen Davis (played by Sarah Roemer) moves to with her sister, Claire (played by Amber Tamblyn).

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Karen is haunted by the vengeful spirit of Kayako Saeki, who was murdered by her husband, Takeo. The film explores themes of grief, trauma, and the cyclical nature of violence.

The main theme of The Grudge 3 revolves around the idea that the past can never be fully escaped, and that the traumas of the past can continue to haunt us in the present. Karen's character is particularly affected by her family's dark history, which is slowly revealed throughout the film.

Another significant theme in the movie is the concept of cultural heritage and the impact of colonialism on indigenous communities. The Saeki family's story is deeply rooted in Japanese culture, and the film explores the ways in which Westerners often misunderstand or exploit Asian cultures.

The Grudge 3 also touches on the idea of female empowerment and the struggle for independence. Karen's character is a strong and determined protagonist who must navigate her way through a complex web of supernatural forces to uncover the truth about her family's past.

Overall, The Grudge 3 is a horror film that explores themes of trauma, cultural heritage, and female empowerment, set against the backdrop of a haunted house in Chicago.

overview: When their only daughter Blair leaves the family nest, Luther and Nora Krank decide to book an island cruise to beat the yuletide blues and just skip the holidays. But their decision to boycott tradition has the whole neighborhood in an uproar, and when Blair call son Christmas Eve to announce a surprise visit with her new fiancée, the Kranks have just twelve hours to perform a miracle and pull themselves and their neighbors together to throw the best celebration ever!
tagline: Their Christmas will turn the town upside down!
title: Christmas with the Kranks
plot:
