Christmas with the Kranks is a 2004 American Christmas comedy film directed by Chris Columbus and written by John Grisham, based on his novel "Skipping Christmas". The movie stars Tim Allen and Jamie Lee Curtis as Luther and Nora Krank, a couple who decide to skip Christmas in order to avoid the stress and commercialism of the holiday.

The story begins with Luther (Tim Allen) and Nora (Jamie Lee Curtis), a married couple living in Boca Raton, Florida. They have grown tired of the same old Christmas traditions and feel that they are losing touch with their children, Blair (Cheech Marin) and Katie (Julia Deakin). The family is also struggling financially, as Luther has lost his job at a paper company.

One day, while discussing Christmas plans over dinner, Luther suggests skipping the holiday altogether. Nora initially agrees, but then changes her mind after seeing a news report about a woman who died on Christmas Eve in 1918 due to the flu pandemic. The couple decides to skip Christmas and spend the money they would have spent on gifts and decorations on a vacation.

However, their plans are soon disrupted when Blair and Katie return home from college for Christmas break, expecting a traditional family celebration. Luther and Nora must come up with a plan to convince their children that they can't celebrate Christmas without them feeling guilty or left out.

As the holiday approaches, Luther and Nora's neighbors, Mr. and Mrs. Beckett (Dan Aykroyd and Kristin Chenoweth), become suspicious of their intentions and try to persuade them to change their minds. Meanwhile, Blair and Katie start to suspect that something is amiss with their parents' behavior.

In the end, Luther and Nora come up with a plan to have a small, low-key celebration at home, which they hope will be enough for their children. However, things don't go according to plan, and the family ends up having a more traditional Christmas than they initially intended.

The movie explores themes of family, tradition, and the true meaning of Christmas. Through Luther and Nora's journey, the film shows that sometimes, it's okay to take a break from the usual holiday routine and focus on what really matters: spending time with loved ones. The movie also pokes fun at the commercialization of Christmas and the stress that can come with it.

Overall, Christmas with the Kranks is a heartwarming and humorous film that explores the complexities of family relationships and the importance of tradition during the holiday season.

overview: Monsters under the bed are scary enough, but what happens when an entire house is out to get you? Three teens aim to find out when they go up against a decrepit neighboring home and unlock its frightening secrets.
tagline: The house is . . . alive!
title: Monster House
plot:
Monster House is a 2006 computer-animated comedy-horror film produced by DreamWorks Animation and Amblin Entertainment. The movie follows the story of a mysterious house that seems to have a life of its own.

The story begins with the introduction of three children: DJ (voiced by Spencer Locke), Chowder (voiced by Sam Lerner), and Jenny (voiced by Megan Mullally). They live in the suburban town of Suburbia, where everyone knows each other's business. The house at 1313 Cemetery Lane is a source of fascination for the kids, as it seems to be alive and has a mind of its own.

As the story progresses, we learn that the house was built by a former owner named Mr. Nebbercracker (voiced by Steve Buscemi), who died under mysterious circumstances. The house has been terrorizing the neighborhood ever since, causing chaos and destruction wherever it goes.

DJ, Chowder, and Jenny decide to team up to solve the mystery of the haunted house. They soon discover that the house is actually a monster in disguise, with a personality of its own. The house, which they name "Monster House," has a mind of its own and seems to be alive.

As the kids delve deeper into the mystery, they learn that Monster House was once a normal house built by Mr. Nebbercracker. However, after his death, the house became possessed by the spirit of Mr. Nebbercracker's son, who died in the house many years ago. The son's ghost is trapped inside the house and is seeking revenge on the living.

The kids come up with a plan to help the ghost find peace and move on from the mortal world. They work together to uncover the secrets of Monster House and ultimately succeed in helping the ghost resolve its unfinished business.

In the end, DJ, Chowder, and Jenny are hailed as heroes for solving the mystery of Monster House. The house is no longer a source of terror, but rather a symbol of their bravery and friendship. The movie ends with the kids standing in front of the house, which has been transformed into a beautiful garden, a testament to the power of teamwork and determination.

Throughout the movie, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the characters and the monster house to life. The voice acting is also top-notch, with each character bringing their own unique personality to the story. Overall, Monster House is a fun and spooky animated film that is suitable for both kids and adults.

original_title: 劇場版 あの日見た花の名前を僕達はまだ知らない。
overview: A year has passed since Menma's ghostly return to the Super Peace Busters. Although the time they spent together during that summer was short, the five members reminisce about what happened as they each write a letter to their lost friend.
title: anohana: The Flower We Saw That Day - The Movie
plot:
Anohana: The Flower We Saw That Day is a poignant and emotional film that explores the complexities of grief, guilt, and redemption. The story revolves around Jinta Yadomi, a high school student who, along with his friends, made a promise to a classmate named Menma who had died by suicide.

The movie delves into the theme of unresolved emotions and the weight of guilt that can haunt individuals long after a traumatic event has passed. Jinta's struggle to come to terms with his past actions and find a way to move forward is deeply relatable, as he grapples with feelings of responsibility and regret.

One of the primary themes of Anohana is the power of human connection and friendship in overcoming adversity. The relationships between the characters are authentic and multifaceted, showcasing the ways in which people can support and hurt each other in equal measure.

The film also touches on the theme of nostalgia and how it can be both a bittersweet reminder of happy memories and a painful trigger for unresolved emotions. Menma's presence continues to haunt Jinta and his friends, forcing them to confront their past and find a way to heal.

Ultimately, Anohana is a powerful exploration of the human experience, tackling difficult themes with sensitivity and nuance. The movie's thoughtful pacing and character development allow viewers to become deeply invested in the story, making it a truly unforgettable viewing experience.

overview: Disgruntled Korean War veteran Walt Kowalski sets out to reform his neighbor, Thao Lor, a Hmong teenager who tried to steal Kowalski's prized possession: a 1972 Gran Torino.
tagline: Ever come across somebody you shouldn't have f#cked with?
title: Gran Torino
plot:
Gran Torino is a 2008 American drama film directed by Clint Eastwood, written by Nick Santora, and produced by Village Roadshow Pictures. The movie stars Clint Eastwood as Walt Kowalski, a retired auto worker who forms an unlikely friendship with his Hmong neighbors.

The story begins on April 11th, 1979, in the San Fernando Valley of Los Angeles, California. We meet Walt Kowalski (Clint Eastwood), a 71-year-old Korean War veteran and retired auto worker, living alone in his modest home. Walt is a proud and stubborn man who has grown increasingly isolated from society due to his racist views and a series of unfortunate events.

Walt's life takes a dramatic turn when he buys a 1972 Gran Torino, which becomes the focal point of the story. The car is a symbol of Walt's independence and freedom, but it also attracts unwanted attention from local gangs and thieves. One day, Hmong refugees, led by Thao (Biao Yuen), move in next door to Walt. Despite their initial differences, Walt begins to form an unlikely bond with Thao and his family.

As the story unfolds, Walt's friendship with Thao deepens, and he starts to see the world through different eyes. He becomes a mentor to Thao and his friends, teaching them about American culture and values. In return, they share their own stories of struggle and resilience. Through these interactions, Walt begins to confront his racist views and the pain of his past.

However, not everyone is pleased with Walt's new friendship. A local gang, led by a ruthless leader named Sorenson (Tommy Flanagan), becomes determined to steal Walt's Gran Torino and exploit its value for their own gain. As tensions escalate, Walt finds himself in a series of confrontations with the gang members.

The climax of the movie takes place on April 11th, 1979, exactly one year after the events began. In a dramatic showdown, Walt stands up to Sorenson and his gang, using his wits and resourcefulness to protect his home and friends. The confrontation ends in tragedy, but also marks a turning point for Walt, who has finally found redemption through his relationships with Thao and his family.

The movie concludes with Walt's funeral, where he is mourned by his neighbors and friends. As the mourners gather around his coffin, they share stories of Walt's transformation from a racist loner to a kind and compassionate man. The Gran Torino, once a symbol of independence, has become a symbol of community and friendship.

Throughout the movie, Clint Eastwood delivers a powerful performance as Walt Kowalski, bringing depth and nuance to a complex character. The supporting cast, including Biao Yuen and Ah Saan, deliver memorable performances that add to the film's emotional impact.

Overall, Gran Torino is a thought-provoking drama that explores themes of racism, redemption, and the power of human connection. With its strong performances, engaging storyline, and Clint Eastwood's direction, the movie has become a modern classic in American cinema.

overview: Laurie Strode struggles to come to terms with her brother Michael's deadly return to Haddonfield, Illinois. Meanwhile, Michael prepares for another reunion with his sister.
tagline: Family Is Forever
title: Halloween II
plot:
Halloween II is a 2009 American slasher film directed by Rob Zombie and written by Robert Zemeckis, Randy Hauck, and Zachary Pomeranz. The film serves as a sequel to the 1978 film Halloween and ignores the events of the previous films in the franchise.

The movie begins with Laurie Strode (Scout Taylor-Compton), who has been recovering from her traumatic encounter with Michael Myers at the end of the first film. However, she is still haunted by the memories of that night and struggles to cope with the aftermath. As Halloween approaches, Laurie becomes increasingly paranoid and isolated, fearing that Michael will return.

Meanwhile, Dr. Samuel Loomis (Malcolm McDowell), Laurie's psychiatrist, has been searching for a way to stop Michael from killing anyone else. He discovers that Michael is being controlled by a supernatural force, which is connected to the events of the previous film.

As Halloween night approaches, Laurie becomes convinced that Michael will return and sets out to prepare herself for his arrival. She barricades herself indoors with her friends, including Peter (Chris Durand), but they are eventually attacked by Michael.

The movie takes a dark turn as it explores the psychological effects of trauma on Laurie. As she tries to cope with her past, she becomes increasingly unhinged and begins to question her own sanity. The film's climax features a gruesome and intense confrontation between Laurie and Michael, which ultimately ends in tragedy.

Throughout the film, Zombie pays homage to the original Halloween by incorporating many of the same themes and motifs that made the 1978 film so iconic. However, he also takes significant creative liberties with the story, which has been met with mixed reactions from fans of the franchise.

One of the most notable aspects of Halloween II is its exploration of Laurie's character development. Scout Taylor-Compton delivers a strong performance as the traumatized Laurie, bringing depth and nuance to a character that was previously underdeveloped in the previous film.

Overall, Halloween II is a brutal and intense horror film that explores the psychological effects of trauma on its protagonist. While it may not be as well-received by fans of the franchise as some of Zombie's other work, it remains a solid addition to the Halloween series.

overview: When characters from the movie musical “Wet Side Story” get stuck in the real world, teens Brady and Mack must find a way to return them home.
tagline: Same surf. New turf.
title: Teen Beach 2
plot:
Teen Beach 2 is a 2015 American musical teen comedy released as a Disney Channel Original Movie. The sequel to Teen Beach Movie (2013), it was again directed by Jeffrey Hornaday, with a screenplay by Matt and Bill Eddy from a story by Robert Horn and Dan Berendsen. Ross Lynch, Maia Mitchell, Grace Phipps, Garrett Clayton, John DeLuca, Chrissie Fit and Jordan Fisher are among the cast members who return from the first film.

After their summer adventure inside the 1960s beach musical Wet Side Story, Brady and McKenzie, known as Mack, have become a couple despite their opposite personalities, but going back to school strains their relationship. Mack throws herself into organising a "Save the Beach" dance, while Brady secretly works on surfboard designs and forgets a college fair he had promised to attend with her, and the two break up.

Inside the film world, the lead characters Lela and Tanner have changed since meeting Brady and Mack and begin straying from their scripted story. Finding Mack's lost necklace, they dive into the ocean and emerge in the modern world, where they are thrilled by everything around them. Brady and Mack try to persuade them to go home, while back in the movie their friends struggle to carry on without the stars. At school Lela becomes absorbed in math homework, Tanner worries he is not enough for her, and Brady confides that he and Mack are on a break.

When Brady and Mack show Lela and Tanner clips proving they are only characters in a film, Lela angrily throws the necklace into the sea. Soon the rest of the Wet Side Story gang arrive with news that characters in their world are vanishing, and Brady and Mack realise the film will cease to exist without its leads. The visitors return home, but the gang reappear at the dance, still fading, to help the couple make up. Using a motorised surfboard Brady built and the emblem from Mack's grandfather's board, the couple reconcile, agree to stop keeping secrets and send Lela and Tanner back. In the altered timeline that follows, Brady and Mack meet again at the dance, where the film has become Lela's story.

The film received mixed reviews; Variety's Brian Lowry praised its songs and talented cast but found the storytelling padded between musical numbers.

overview: After four college girls rob a restaurant to fund their spring break in Florida, they get entangled with a weird dude with his own criminal agenda.
tagline: A little sun can bring out your dark side.
title: Spring Breakers
plot:
Spring Breakers is a 2012 American crime drama film written and directed by Harmony Korine, not 2013. The movie was released on April 6, 2012.

The film follows the story of four college girls - Faith (Selena Gomez), Candy (Vanessa Hudgens), Brit (Ashley Benson), and Cotty (Rachel Korine) - who are struggling to find their place in the world. They are all from different walks of life but share a common desire for excitement, freedom, and escape.

The story begins with the girls attending a spring break party on a yacht, where they meet a charismatic and mysterious young man named Alien (James Franco). He is part of a group of friends who are also at the party, including his friend, Church (Christopher Brown), and his girlfriend, Faith's sister, Candy's boyfriend, and Cotty's ex-boyfriend.

Alien and his friends convince the girls to join them on a wild adventure in Florida, where they plan to rob a convenience store. The girls agree, and they embark on a journey of self-discovery, partying, and crime. Along the way, they encounter various characters who influence their lives, including Alien's friend Church, who becomes increasingly unstable.

As the story unfolds, the girls become more and more entangled in Alien's world, which is marked by violence, debauchery, and a sense of freedom that they can't find elsewhere. However, as the adventure progresses, it becomes clear that Alien's world is not as idyllic as it seems.

The plot takes a dark turn when the girls are arrested for their involvement in the convenience store robbery. In an attempt to secure their release, Alien and his friends plan another heist, which ends in tragedy. The film's climax features a violent confrontation between the characters, leading to a shocking conclusion that leaves the audience stunned.

Throughout the film, Korine explores themes of youth culture, rebellion, and the search for identity. He also critiques societal norms and expectations placed on women, particularly those who are seen as "wild" or "unconventional." The film's visuals are striking, with vibrant colors and a pulsating soundtrack that captures the energy and excitement of the characters' adventures.

Overall, Spring Breakers is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that challenges its audience to confront the darker aspects of human nature.

overview: Jen's romantic getaway with her wealthy married boyfriend is disrupted when his friends arrive for an impromptu hunting trip. Tension mounts at the house until the situation culminates in an unexpected way.
tagline: Why do women always have to put up a fight?
title: Revenge
plot:
Revenge is a 2017 English-language French action thriller written and directed by Coralie Fargeat in her feature debut. Matilda Lutz stars as Jen, a young woman who is assaulted and left for dead in the desert, with Kevin Janssens as her wealthy married lover Richard, and Vincent Colombe and Guillaume Bouchède as his hunting companions Stan and Dimitri. The film premiered in the Midnight Madness section of the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2017 and was released in France by Rezo Films in February 2018.

Jen, a young American who dreams of moving to Los Angeles, flies by helicopter with her married boyfriend, Richard, to his isolated luxury villa in the desert for a romantic getaway. The next morning, Richard's friends Stan and Dimitri arrive a day early for their annual hunting trip, and Richard is forced to introduce Jen to them. That night the four of them party, and Jen dances flirtatiously with Stan. The following morning, while Richard is away, Stan makes advances toward her and, when she rejects him, rapes her, while Dimitri ignores what is happening.

When Richard returns, he offers Jen money and a new life in Canada in exchange for her silence. She threatens to tell his wife, and he slaps her. Jen flees into the desert, pursued by the three men, and at the edge of a cliff Richard pushes her off. She is impaled on a tree and left for dead. Regaining consciousness, she frees herself and, under the influence of peyote she took from Richard's supplies, cauterizes her wound with a heated beer can, leaving the imprint of an eagle on her skin. Transformed from victim into hunter, Jen arms herself and tracks the men across the desert as they search for her body, killing them one by one in brutal, bloody confrontations, culminating in a final showdown with Richard inside the villa.

Revenge received widespread acclaim, with critics praising Fargeat's stylish direction, Lutz's performance and the film's feminist reworking of the rape-revenge genre, which subverts the male gaze traditionally associated with such films. Its vivid colors, graphic violence and excessive bloodshed were widely noted, and the film established Fargeat, who later directed The Substance.

overview: In an alternate present-day where magical creatures live among us, two L.A. cops become embroiled in a prophesied turf battle.
title: Bright
plot:
Bright is a 2017 American fantasy action film directed by David Yates and written by Max Landis. The movie takes place in a world where magic has been outlawed, and orcs have taken over the city of Portland.

The story follows two detectives, Daryl Ward (Will Smith), a human cop, and Nick Jakoby (Joel Edgerton), an orc cop, who are forced to work together to solve a murder case. The victim is a young girl named Beth Harmon (Lucy Fry), who was found dead in the woods with a magical amulet around her neck.

As Daryl and Nick delve deeper into the case, they discover that the amulet is one of five magical orbs created by the ancient elf king, King Elfhelm. The orbs are said to have the power to bring about peace between humans and orcs, but they also attract the attention of a powerful sorcerer named Berruk (Ed Skrein), who seeks to use their power for his own gain.

As the investigation unfolds, Daryl and Nick must navigate the complex web of human and orc politics in Portland, all while facing their own prejudices and biases. Along the way, they are aided by a wise old elf named Professor Stone (Michael Stuhlbarg) and a young elf named Elara Vex (Noomi Rapace).

Throughout the movie, Daryl and Nick's partnership is put to the test as they learn to trust each other and work together to solve the case. Along the way, they also discover that Beth Harmon was not just an innocent victim, but rather a key player in a larger conspiracy involving the magical orbs.

As the story reaches its climax, Daryl and Nick must face off against Berruk and his minions in a battle to control the magical orbs and bring about peace between humans and orcs. In the end, they succeed in defeating Berruk and shattering the magical orbs, but not before realizing that their partnership has changed them both forever.

Overall, Bright is a visually stunning film with a unique blend of fantasy and action elements. The movie explores themes of prejudice, trust, and redemption, and features a talented cast of characters. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the genre have praised its originality and entertainment value.

overview: While staying at an aging manor to research its liquor-smuggling history, Christina and her documentary video team interview their spooky host Vincent—but no one can capture his image or voice on video. After shocking dreams and bloody encounters, the crew members fall under Victor’s hypnotic spell.
tagline: They're in his house. But he's in their minds.
title: The Amityville Harvest
plot:
The Amityville Harvest is a 2020 American supernatural horror film written and directed by Thomas J. Churchill. It stars Kyle Lowder, Sadie Katz, Brandon Alan Smith and Alexa Pellerin, with Johanna Rae, Michael Cervantes, Eva Ceja, George W. Scott, Keavy Bradley, Eileen Dietz and Paul Logan in supporting roles. One of the many loosely connected low-budget films to use the Amityville name, it was released on DVD, video on demand and digital platforms on 20 October 2020 by Lionsgate Home Entertainment, and it was the last Amityville film released before the death of Ronald DeFeo Jr., the real-life killer whose crime inspired the series, in March 2021.

Documentary filmmaker Christina Weingarten (Katz) travels with her crew to the large colonial home of the rich eccentric Vincent Miller (Lowder) on Long Island to interview him for a segment called "My Civil War" about his family's connection to the assassination of Abraham Lincoln. Her team includes her younger sister Nancy (Pellerin), lighting technician Cosmo (Smith), audio engineer Scratch (Cervantes), hearing-impaired make-up artist Janet (Rae), photographer Lexy (Ceja) and new crew member Ottis (Scott). Vincent, a Confederate apologist, proudly recounts his ancestor's role in plotting the assassination and teases a family history of fire and Prohibition-era liquor smuggling, but after hours of interviews the crew discovers that none of his image or voice has been recorded. Unknown to them, he is a vampire who can communicate telepathically. His house stands next to his funeral parlour, the subject of several missing-person reports, where the young Lana (Bradley) was attacked by her dead boyfriend Robbie (Logan) and where a sinister mortician, Randolph (Patrick Mulderrig), butchers victims in the basement. Cosmo is secretly searching for Lana, while the crew suffer disturbing dreams and fall under Vincent's hypnotic spell, and the dead return as ghouls. Eventually the sisters are left fighting to escape through the basement, and the film ends on an Amityville town sign.

The film received largely negative reviews. Screen Rant said its twist failed, Nightmarish Conjurings criticised its chaotic editing and poor effects, and Horror Society gave it one out of five, though Cryptic Rock rated it three out of five. Writing for Bloody Disgusting, Joe Lipsett called it overstuffed, with three or four films' worth of storylines, while praising its practical gore effects.

overview: Larry's daughter wants only one thing for Christmas - a talking bear. His daughter's step-dad intends to make sure that Larry can't get one.
tagline: Two Dads. One Mission. Double the Holiday Fun!
title: Jingle All the Way 2
plot:
Jingle All the Way 2 is a Christmas comedy film released in 2014, directed by Todd Phillips and starring Arnold Schwarzenegger. The movie follows Howard Langston Jr., the same character from the first film, as he tries to balance his busy schedule with being a father to his son Jamie.

The main themes of Jingle All the Way 2 include:

1. Family values: The movie emphasizes the importance of spending quality time with family and making memories together during the holiday season.
2. Parental responsibility: Howard's character is put to the test as he tries to balance his work and personal life, highlighting the challenges faced by working parents in today's fast-paced world.
3. Consumerism vs. values: The film pokes fun at the commercialization of Christmas and the pressure to buy gifts for others, while also emphasizing the importance of what truly matters during the holiday season.
4. Self-discovery: As Howard navigates his busy schedule, he begins to re-evaluate his priorities and learn more about himself and his relationship with his son.

The plot development revolves around Howard's attempts to get a new high-tech toy for Jamie, which leads him on a series of misadventures and comedic misunderstandings. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about the importance of family time and being present in the moment.

The ending of Jingle All the Way 2 is a heartwarming one, as Howard comes to realize what truly matters during the holiday season and makes amends with his son. The movie concludes on a positive note, emphasizing the importance of family values and creating lasting memories together.

overview: A reindeer boy named Niko dreams about flying like his father, whom he has never met. Despite constant mocking from others, he sneaks out of his home valley to take flying lessons from Julius, a flying squirrel.
tagline: An All-New Holiday Movie About Santa And His Little Helpers
title: The Flight Before Christmas
plot:
The Flight Before Christmas is a 3D computer-animated fantasy comedy film directed by Alex Zamm. 

The movie revolves around a young boy named Billy who wishes for his father to fly, and to his surprise, Santa Claus appears in the form of a human and takes him on an adventure through the skies.

The main themes of The Flight Before Christmas include:

1. The importance of believing in oneself: Billy's journey teaches him that he has the power to make his dreams come true if he believes in himself.
2. The value of family: Throughout the film, Billy learns about the significance of family and the love that binds them together.
3. Self-discovery: As Billy navigates this new world with Santa, he discovers new things about himself and develops a stronger sense of self-confidence.

The movie also explores themes of friendship, kindness, and generosity, as embodied by Santa's character. Overall, The Flight Before Christmas is a heartwarming story that promotes positive values and encourages viewers to believe in the magic of childhood.

overview: Terror strikes when a heartbroken woman uses black magic to get her husband back.
tagline: Until Death Tears Them Apart
title: Dark Spell
plot:
Dark Spell (Russian: Приворот. Чёрное венчание, Privorot. Chyornoe venchanie, literally "Love Spell: The Black Wedding") is a 2021 Russian supernatural horror film directed by Svyatoslav Podgaevsky, who co-wrote the screenplay with Natalya Dubovaya and Ivan Kapitonov. Podgaevsky, a leading figure in Russia's horror revival, had previously made Queen of Spades, The Bride, Mermaid: Lake of the Dead and Baba Yaga: Terror of the Dark Forest. Produced by Central Partnership, QS Films and Iney Productions, it stars Yana Enzhaeva and Konstantin Beloshapka, with Ilya Ermolov, Varvara Borodina, Sabina Akhmedova, Nikita Yuranov and Larisa Domaskina. It was released in English-speaking markets as Dark Spell.

Zhenya (Enzhaeva), a dressmaker, is devastated when she finds her boyfriend Kir (Beloshapka), an artist and the father of their baby daughter Polina, having sex with one of his models, and he pushes her away. Told that only a love spell can bring him back, she visits a Romani fortune-teller, Aza (Akhmedova), who instructs her to perform a ritual during the wedding of someone she knows. Zhenya chooses the wedding of her client Sonya (Borodina) and the doctor Viktor (Ermolov), and hides on the church balcony during the service to carry out the rite with candles and scraps of cloth, even eating raw meat. Afterwards she collapses on the church steps and is rushed to Viktor's hospital, while Viktor soon finds his new wife with another man, though Sonya protests she does not know what came over her. Kir does return to Zhenya, but his renewed love turns into frightening obsession and jealousy: he attacks her friends, chases her in a car, tries to encase her body in plaster and cuts off his own mother's finger at the dinner table to take a family ring for his proposal. Even after Kir's death the spell keeps its hold, turning Zhenya's life into a nightmare as his spirit pursues anyone standing between him and his beloved, and at one point she is trapped in a mortuary cabinet with his corpse. The story culminates in a ceremony in the church to break the spell.

Reviews were mixed. Gulnaz Davletshina of Kinoafisha praised its dramatic exploration of how an exhausted relationship can drive someone into a dark corner but felt the idea was underdeveloped, with too many demons and too little humanity. Moria awarded it three stars for heading into pleasingly dark places, while Brian Orndorf found it bland and lacking real menace.

overview: Devoted lifeguard Mitch Buchannon butts heads with a brash new recruit. Together, they uncover a local criminal plot that threatens the future of the Bay.
tagline: Don't worry, summer is coming
title: Baywatch
plot:
Baywatch is a 2017 action comedy film directed by Seth Gordon and starring Dwayne Johnson and Zac Efron as two of the main characters. The movie is loosely based on the popular 1990s television series of the same name.

The film begins with Mitch Buchannon (Dwayne Johnson), a former Olympic swimmer who has become a lifeguard at Baywatch, a beach patrol unit in Los Angeles. Mitch is a by-the-book kind of guy who is dedicated to his job and is respected by his colleagues. He is also haunted by the death of his partner, Matt Brody (Jon Bass), which occurred during a training exercise.

The story takes a turn when Mitch meets Summer Quinn (Michelle Rodriguez), a beautiful and tough-as-nails lifeguard who joins Baywatch. Summer is a bit of a wild card and has a troubled past, but she quickly becomes an asset to the team.

Meanwhile, a wealthy tech mogul named Victor Chasteen (Joaquim de Almeida) announces that he will be hosting a high-stakes charity polo match on the beach, which attracts the attention of Summer's former flame, Matt Brody. The two have a complicated history, and their reunion sets off a chain reaction of events.

As the story unfolds, Mitch and Summer team up to stop Chasteen from using his wealth and influence to exploit the city's beaches for his own gain. Along the way, they must navigate their feelings for each other and confront their personal demons.

The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, including a memorable beach rescue scene and a high-speed boat chase through the streets of Los Angeles. The film also pokes fun at the original series, with plenty of nods to classic Baywatch moments and characters.

In the end, Mitch and Summer succeed in stopping Chasteen's nefarious plans, but not before they share a romantic moment on the beach. The movie ends on a high note, with Mitch and Summer riding off into the sunset together.

Overall, Baywatch is a fun and action-packed film that pays homage to the original series while also offering something new and exciting for fans of the franchise.

overview: A listless and alienated teenager decides to help his new friend win the class presidency in their small western high school, while he must deal with his bizarre family life back home.
tagline: He's out to prove he's got nothing to prove.
title: Napoleon Dynamite
plot:
Napoleon Dynamite is a 2004 American independent comedy film that explores several themes that are deeply rooted in its quirky and offbeat narrative.

At its core, Napoleon Dynamite is a story about the struggles of adolescence, particularly for those who feel like outsiders. The film's protagonist, Napoleon, is a socially awkward high school student who navigates his way through life with the help of his eccentric grandmother and his best friend, Pedro. Through Napoleon's journey, the movie delves into themes of loneliness, isolation, and the quest for acceptance.

One of the primary themes of the film is the power of friendship and loyalty. Despite their differences, Napoleon and Pedro form a strong bond that helps them navigate the complexities of high school life. The movie also highlights the importance of embracing one's individuality and not trying to conform to societal norms.

Another significant theme in Napoleon Dynamite is the struggle for identity and self-discovery. Napoleon's quest to find his place in the world is a recurring motif throughout the film, as he tries to balance his desire for independence with his need for connection and belonging.

The movie also explores themes of social hierarchy and cliques, particularly in the context of high school life. The film pokes fun at the absurdity of social hierarchies and the ways in which people try to categorize themselves and others.

Finally, Napoleon Dynamite has a strong theme of optimism and hope. Despite its offbeat tone and quirky characters, the movie ultimately presents a message of resilience and determination. Napoleon's journey is one of self-discovery and growth, as he learns to find his place in the world and connect with others on his own terms.

Overall, Napoleon Dynamite is a film that celebrates individuality, friendship, and the power of embracing one's quirks and flaws. Its offbeat humor and quirky characters have made it a cult classic, and its themes continue to resonate with audiences today.

overview: In the late 19th century, a brutal land baron slaughters a Roma clan, unleashing a curse on his family and village. In the days that follow, the townspeople are plagued by nightmares, the baron's son goes missing, and a boy is found murdered. The locals suspect a wild animal, but a visiting pathologist warns of a more sinister presence lurking in the woods.

overview: A guarded woman who finds out she's dying of cancer but, when she meets her match, the threat of falling in love is scarier than death.
tagline: Life starts now.
title: A Little Bit of Heaven
plot:
A Little Bit of Heaven is a 2011 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Nicole Kassell and produced by Davis Entertainment. The movie tells the story of Angel (played by Kate Hudson), a free-spirited woman who lives life on her own terms, and her relationship with a man named Ben (played by Owen Wilson).

The main theme of A Little Bit of Heaven revolves around the idea of living in the moment and embracing one's individuality. Angel is a character who refuses to conform to societal norms and expectations, instead choosing to follow her heart and pursue her passions. Her carefree nature and zest for life serve as a catalyst for those around her, including Ben, who finds himself drawn to her infectious energy.

Throughout the film, the themes of love, loss, and self-discovery are woven together to create a narrative that is both poignant and uplifting. The movie explores the complexities of human relationships and the ways in which people can both hurt and heal each other. Ultimately, A Little Bit of Heaven suggests that it's never too late to find happiness and fulfillment, and that sometimes, all it takes is a little bit of heaven to make life worth living.

The film also touches on the idea of mortality and the importance of cherishing every moment with those we love. Angel's own struggles with her health serve as a reminder to appreciate the present and not take anything for granted. Overall, A Little Bit of Heaven is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that celebrates the beauty of life's imperfections and the power of human connection.

overview: When obscenely rich hedge-fund manager James is convicted of fraud and sentenced to a stretch in San Quentin, the judge gives him one month to get his affairs in order. Knowing that he won't survive more than a few minutes in prison on his own, James desperately turns to Darnell-- a black businessman who's never even had a parking ticket -- for help. As Darnell puts James through the wringer, both learn that they were wrong about many things, including each other.
tagline: An education in incarceration.
title: Get Hard
plot:
Get Hard is a 2015 American comedy film directed by Etan Cohen and starring Will Ferrell and Kevin Hart. The movie follows the story of James King (Will Ferrell), a wealthy businessman who is sentenced to prison for insider trading, and Darnell Lewis (Kevin Hart), his uptight personal trainer.

The main themes of Get Hard revolve around:

1. **Social class differences**: The film highlights the stark contrast between James' luxurious lifestyle and Darnell's humble background, leading to comedic misunderstandings and cultural clashes.
2. **Preparation for prison life**: As Darnell tries to prepare James for his impending incarceration, they embark on a series of misadventures that showcase their vastly different perspectives on life.
3. **Friendship and camaraderie**: Despite their differences, the two men develop an unlikely bond as they navigate their way through the challenges of prison preparation.
4. **Identity and self-discovery**: Through their experiences, James and Darnell are forced to confront their own identities and values, leading to a deeper understanding of themselves and each other.

The film's plot is driven by these themes, which are expertly woven together with humor, wit, and heart. The movie ultimately becomes a story about the power of friendship and the importance of being true to oneself, even in the face of adversity.

overview: A struggling songwriter named Dave Seville finds success when he comes across a trio of singing chipmunks: mischievous leader Alvin, brainy Simon, and chubby, impressionable Theodore.
tagline: The Original Entourage
title: Alvin and the Chipmunks
plot:
Alvin and the Chipmunks is a 2007 American musical comedy based on the characters created by Ross Bagdasarian Sr., directed by Tim Hill from a screenplay by Jon Vitti, Will McRobb and Chris Viscardi. Jason Lee plays the songwriter Dave Seville, David Cross the record executive Ian Hawke and Cameron Richardson Dave's former girlfriend Claire, while Justin Long, Matthew Gray Gubler and Jesse McCartney voice the chipmunks Alvin, Simon and Theodore.

The three talking chipmunk brothers live in a fir tree that is cut down and taken to Los Angeles after JETT Records buys it as a Christmas tree. In the same building, the struggling songwriter Dave Seville has his latest demo rejected by Ian Hawke, his old college roommate and the label's chief executive. The chipmunks follow Dave home, and after an initial panic he discovers they can sing, striking a deal to give them food and a home in return for performing his songs.

The partnership starts badly. Stage fright ruins their first audition for Ian, the chipmunks accidentally cost Dave his advertising job, and Alvin's attempts at matchmaking spoil a dinner with Claire. To make amends, the brothers go to Ian's mansion on their own and sing Dave's song "Christmas Don't Be Late", winning a record contract and making Dave their manager. As they grow attached to Dave and start to see him as family, he keeps them at arm's length.

Ian pushes for ever more aggressive promotion, and when Dave insists the chipmunks are too young for celebrity, Ian convinces them that Dave is holding them back. After a quarrel, and finding an old letter in which Dave wrote about returning them to the forest, the brothers move in with Ian, who showers them with luxury while working them to exhaustion on tour and telling them Dave no longer cares. When Ian announces a year-long world tour, Dave enlists Claire's help to sneak into their concert at the Orpheum Theatre. Realising they have been deceived, the chipmunks sabotage the show. Ian locks them in a cage for a flight to Paris, but they escape, reunite with Dave, and Ian's career collapses.

Critics were largely negative, with 28% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but the film opened second behind I Am Legend and grossed $365.4 million worldwide on a budget of $55 to 60 million, launching a series of three sequels.

overview: To protect an 8-year-old girl, a dangerous assassin reunites with her mother and her lethal associates to take down a ruthless crime syndicate and its army of henchmen.
tagline: Revenge is best served ice cold.
title: Gunpowder Milkshake
plot:
Gunpowder Milkshake is a 2021 action thriller film directed by Navot Papushado and written by Papushado, Ehud Lavski, and Yossi Ghinsberg. The movie stars Karen Gillan, Lena Headey, Carla Gugino, Michelle Yeoh, and Lena Dunham.

The story follows Scarlett (Karen Gillan), a young assassin who is on the run from her past after being betrayed by her mentor, Veronika (Lena Headey). Veronika was once a skilled hitwoman who trained many assassins, including Scarlett. However, Veronika's true intentions were to use them for her own gain and eliminate anyone who stood in her way.

Scarlett is on the run with her daughter, Ryan (Chloe Coleman), from the ruthless crime lord, Hattie (Lena Dunham). Hattie is a former protégée of Veronika's who has become a formidable foe. Scarlett seeks revenge against Veronika and Hattie for abandoning her and putting her in harm's way.

As Scarlett navigates the complex web of assassins and crime lords, she must confront her own troubled past and learn to trust herself. Along the way, she teams up with a group of skilled assassins, including The Contessa (Michelle Yeoh) and The Wolf (Chloe Coleman), who help her take down Veronika and Hattie.

Throughout the movie, Scarlett faces numerous challenges and obstacles as she tries to protect herself and her daughter. She must use her skills and cunning to outwit her enemies and stay one step ahead of them. Along the way, she also discovers more about her own past and the true nature of Veronika's plans.

The film features a mix of action, suspense, and dark humor, with a strong focus on female empowerment and revenge. The movie has received praise for its strong performances, particularly from Karen Gillan and Lena Headey, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Gunpowder Milkshake is a thrilling and entertaining ride that explores themes of motherhood, loyalty, and the complexities of female relationships. With its talented cast and stylish action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of action movies and thrillers.

overview: Eccentric scientist Victor Von Frankenstein creates a grotesque creature in an unorthodox scientific experiment.
tagline: Discover the origin of the monster and his creation.
title: Victor Frankenstein
plot:
Victor Frankenstein (2015) is a horror drama film directed by Paul McGuigan, produced by 20th Century Fox, and released in 2015. The movie is an adaptation of Mary Shelley's novel "Frankenstein" but with some significant changes.

The main themes of Victor Frankenstein (2015) include:

1. **The dangers of unchecked ambition**: The film explores the consequences of Victor Frankenstein's obsessive pursuit of knowledge and his desire to create life. His relentless drive leads him down a path of destruction, highlighting the importance of humility and responsibility.
2. **The nature of monstrosity**: The movie raises questions about what makes someone a monster. Is it their appearance, their actions, or their inner nature? The creature, played by James McAvoy, is a complex character who challenges traditional notions of good and evil.
3. **Loneliness and isolation**: Victor Frankenstein's (played by James McAvoy) life is marked by loneliness and isolation, which ultimately contribute to his downfall. His inability to form meaningful connections with others leads him to create the creature as a companion, but it backfires.
4. **The ethics of scientific discovery**: The film critiques the dangers of unchecked scientific progress without considering the consequences of one's actions. Victor Frankenstein's creation is a cautionary tale about the importance of responsible innovation and the need for ethics in scientific inquiry.
5. **Identity and self-discovery**: The creature, played by Daniel Radcliffe, grapples with his own identity and sense of belonging. His journey serves as a metaphor for the struggles of finding one's place in the world and defining oneself.

The movie features stunning visuals, atmospheric music, and strong performances from its cast, including James McAvoy, Daniel Radcliffe, and Jessica Brown Findlay. Overall, Victor Frankenstein (2015) is a thought-provoking adaptation that explores complex themes and raises important questions about human nature, science, and the consequences of our actions.

overview: A German submarine hunts allied ships during the Second World War, but it soon becomes the hunted. The crew tries to survive below the surface, while stretching both the boat and themselves to their limits.
tagline: When the hunters become the hunted.
title: Das Boot
plot:
Das Boot is a 1981 German war film directed by Wolfgang Petersen, produced by Deutsche Filmakademie Berlin and Columbia Pictures. The movie is an adaptation of Lothar-Günther Buchheim's semi-autobiographical novel "Die Überraschung" (The Surprise), which was published in 1978.

**Beginning:**
The story begins with Lieutenant Commander Hans Dieter Hummel, a young German U-boat commander, who is eager to prove himself as a skilled naval officer. He is assigned to the U-96, a Type VII U-boat, along with his crew of 50 men. The crew is led by Captain Lehmkuhler, an experienced and seasoned commander.

**Plot Development:**
The movie follows the crew's journey through the North Atlantic Ocean as they embark on a mission to sink Allied convoys during World War II. The U-96 faces numerous challenges, including treacherous sea conditions, faulty equipment, and the constant threat of being detected by enemy aircraft and ships.

As the crew navigates the harsh environment, tensions rise among the men due to the cramped living quarters, limited food supplies, and the ever-present danger of sinking or being captured. The crew's morale is further tested when they are forced to make difficult decisions, such as deciding which ships to attack and how to ration their limited resources.

**Character Development:**
Throughout the movie, the characters undergo significant development. Lieutenant Commander Hummel struggles with his own identity and sense of purpose, while Captain Lehmkuhler's leadership is called into question by his crew. The crew's dynamics are also explored, particularly between the officers and enlisted men, as they work together to survive.

**Ending:**
The movie culminates in a dramatic and intense sequence where the U-96 is attacked by an American destroyer, which causes significant damage to the submarine. Despite their best efforts, the crew is unable to repair the damage, and the U-96 is forced to surface and surrender.

As the crew is taken prisoner, they are subjected to harsh treatment at the hands of their American captors. The movie ends with a sense of defeat and despair, as the crew reflects on the sacrifices they made during their time in the war.

**Themes:**
Das Boot explores several themes, including the psychological effects of war on individuals and crews, the importance of leadership and teamwork, and the moral dilemmas faced by those who serve in combat situations. The movie also highlights the harsh realities of life at sea and the challenges faced by submariners during World War II.

Overall, Das Boot is a gripping and intense war drama that explores the human side of conflict. With its well-developed characters, engaging plot, and historical accuracy, it has become a classic of German cinema.

overview: Harvard symbologist Robert Langdon is recruited by the Vatican to investigate the apparent return of the Illuminati - a secret, underground organization - after four cardinals are kidnapped on the night of the papal conclave.
tagline: The holiest event of our time. Perfect for their return.
title: Angels & Demons
plot:
Angels & Demons is a 2009 supernatural thriller film directed by Ron Howard, based on the novel of the same name by Dan Brown. The movie follows the story of Robert Langdon, a symbologist who becomes embroiled in a conspiracy involving the Illuminati and a series of murders.

The film begins with a dramatic opening scene where four cardinals are killed at the Vatican, each bearing a symbol from an ancient secret society known as the Illuminati. The main suspect is Cardinal Patrick McKenna, but Langdon soon discovers that he was merely a pawn in a larger game.

Langdon teams up with Vittoria Vetra (Ayelet Zurer), a scientist who has lost her sister to one of the murders. Together, they embark on a quest to uncover the truth behind the Illuminati and their connection to the murder victims.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, Langdon and Vittoria discover that the Illuminati is seeking revenge against the Catholic Church for its treatment of Galileo Galilei, who was persecuted by the Church in the 17th century. The Illuminati plan to destroy the Vatican using a powerful bomb made from antimatter.

The plot thickens as Langdon and Vittoria uncover more clues, including a cryptic message left behind by Galileo himself. They also discover that the Illuminati is being led by a charismatic figure known as Robert Hawkins (Ewan McGregor), who claims to be the reincarnation of Galileo.

As the story unfolds, Langdon and Vittoria find themselves in a cat-and-mouse game with Hawkins and his followers. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous Vatican corridors and deadly traps set by the Illuminati.

In the climactic final act, Langdon and Vittoria face off against Hawkins and his accomplices in an explosive showdown at the Vatican. The fate of the world hangs in the balance as Langdon uses his knowledge of symbology to outwit Hawkins and prevent a global catastrophe.

Throughout the film, Ron Howard masterfully weaves together elements of history, science, and suspense to create a thrilling narrative that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats. With its breakneck pace and intricate plot twists, Angels & Demons is an entertaining ride from start to finish.

Overall, Angels & Demons is a gripping thriller that explores themes of faith, power, and redemption. The film's stunning visuals, coupled with its intelligent script and strong performances, make it a must-see for fans of the Dan Brown novel and the Ron Howard franchise.

overview: After a couple finds a traumatized child of unknown origins, wife Paula must decipher the girl's strange behaviors to unlock her identity and dark past.
title: The Chalk Line
plot:
The Chalk Line (Spanish: Jaula, meaning "Cage") is a 2022 Spanish mystery psychological thriller film directed by Ignacio Tatay in his feature debut and co-written by Tatay and Isabel Peña. Elena Anaya stars as a woman who takes in a mysterious young girl, with Pablo Molinero and Carlos Santos. It was released theatrically in Spain in September 2022.

Paula and her husband, Simón, live in an exclusive neighborhood of villas outside the city. Driving home one night, they find a little girl wandering alone in the middle of the road and take her to the hospital. She will not speak, and the only clue to her identity is that she responds to the name Clara. When no family can be found, her doctor suggests that a home environment might help, and Paula, who has bonded with the girl, persuades Simón to foster her temporarily. Clara will move only within boundaries chalked on the floor, so the couple draw lines throughout the house for her, and she reacts with terror when one is threatened, crying a strange word, "buma."

When a friend of Paula's swallows a shard of glass during breakfast, Simón suspects Clara put it there, and Clara is taken back to the hospital. Paula discovers that Clara understands German and realizes that "buma" means Buhmann, the bogeyman. Soon after, Paula herself chokes on a piece of glass, and Clara vanishes from the house, though she has never been seen to cross a chalk line. Paula becomes consumed by the search, alienating her friends and husband, who reveals that he knows she has been secretly undergoing fertility treatments. The police suspect her of instability after a call from Clara proves to have come from Paula's own phone.

Paula steals police files and finds a similar case: Ingrid, a Swiss teenager found dead and malnourished in France. A drawing by Clara leads her to suspect their friendly neighbor, Eduardo. In fact, Eduardo had abducted Ingrid as a child and kept her captive in his basement, where she gave birth to Clara, and it was he who released the girl onto the road and later planted the glass and took Clara back. Eduardo captures Paula in his basement, but she gives Clara a piece of chalk to hide and buys time for her to escape. Police eventually raid the house, and Clara is reunited with her grandmother, while Paula, now pregnant, moves to the city with Simón.

The film received mostly positive reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 67% approval from nine critics, with one review calling it a memorable debut.

overview: Two lost souls visiting Tokyo -- the young, neglected wife of a photographer and a washed-up movie star shooting a TV commercial -- find an odd solace and pensive freedom to be real in each other's company, away from their lives in America.
tagline: Everyone wants to be found.
title: Lost in Translation
plot:
Lost in Translation is a 2003 American romantic drama film written and directed by Sofia Coppola. The movie stars Bill Murray and Scarlett Johansson as two strangers who form a connection in Tokyo, Japan.

The film begins with Bob Harris (Bill Murray), a middle-aged actor who has been hired to appear in a Japanese television commercial for a whiskey brand. Bob is a washed-up star who has lost his touch and is struggling to find meaning in his life. He checks into the Park Hyatt Tokyo hotel, where he meets Charlotte (Scarlett Johansson), a young woman who has accompanied her photographer husband, John (Giovanni Ribisi), on a work trip.

Initially, Bob and Charlotte do not interact much, but they eventually strike up a conversation at the hotel bar. They bond over their shared feelings of disconnection and loneliness in a foreign city. As the night progresses, they share stories about their lives, and Bob finds himself drawn to Charlotte's innocence and vulnerability.

As the story unfolds, we see Bob and Charlotte's relationship evolve from a casual friendship to something more intimate. They spend time together exploring Tokyo, sharing drinks, and engaging in conversations that reveal their innermost thoughts and desires. Through their interactions, Coppola explores themes of loneliness, disconnection, and the search for meaning in life.

One of the most striking aspects of Lost in Translation is its use of setting. The film's cinematography captures the neon-lit streets of Tokyo, which serve as a backdrop to Bob and Charlotte's emotional journeys. The city becomes a character in its own right, symbolizing the disorienting and isolating nature of modern life.

Throughout the film, Coppola also explores the complexities of relationships and the fragility of human connections. Bob and Charlotte's bond is fragile and ephemeral, and their interactions are often tinged with sadness and longing. Despite this, they find solace in each other's company, which becomes a source of comfort and meaning in their lives.

The film's ending is both poignant and bittersweet. As the days pass, Bob and Charlotte's relationship deepens, but it is also clear that their time together is limited. In the end, Bob returns to his life in Los Angeles, while Charlotte stays behind with her husband. The film concludes with a sense of melancholy, as Bob reflects on the transience of human connections and the impermanence of relationships.

Overall, Lost in Translation is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the search for meaning in life. Through its nuanced performances, stunning cinematography, and thoughtful direction, Coppola creates a movie that is both poignant and unforgettable.

overview: After a sudden global event wipes out all electronics and takes away humankind’s ability to sleep, chaos quickly begins to consume the world. Only Jill, an ex-soldier with a troubled past, may hold the key to a cure in the form of her own daughter. The question is, can Jill safely deliver her daughter and save the world before she herself loses her mind.
tagline: Disorientation. Hallucinations. Hysteria. Sleep is survival.
title: Awake
plot:
Awake is a 2021 American apocalyptic science fiction thriller directed by Mark Raso from a screenplay he wrote with Joseph Raso. Gina Rodriguez stars as Jill Adams, a former army medic, with Ariana Greenblatt as her daughter Matilda, Lucius Hoyos as her son Noah, Jennifer Jason Leigh, Barry Pepper, Finn Jones, Shamier Anderson, Frances Fisher and Gil Bellows. Netflix released the film on 9 June 2021.

Jill, a recovering addict who works as a security guard at a college, steals drugs from a research lab to sell. Separated from her children, Noah and Matilda, who live with their grandmother, she is driving them home when a mysterious global event knocks out all electronic devices. Their car loses power and is struck by another vehicle, plunging into a lake. Matilda drowns but is revived by a police officer. At the hospital they learn that coma patients have suddenly awakened, and that night the family finds that they cannot sleep. Jill soon learns that the whole population has lost the ability to sleep. A psychiatrist she once worked with, Dr. Murphy, explains that without sleep people will rapidly deteriorate and die within days, and that scientists are studying an elderly woman who can still sleep at a military facility called the Hub in the hope of finding a cure.

Jill realizes that Matilda slept the night before and may hold the key to humanity's survival. As society begins to collapse, desperate people learn of Matilda's ability; at a church, a group of churchgoers tries to sacrifice the girl, and Jill escapes with her children amid gunfire. With Noah urging his mother to take Matilda to the Hub, they set out across a land descending into madness, encountering escaped prisoners who steal their car with Matilda inside, and other increasingly unhinged survivors. As Jill's own mind begins to fail from sleep deprivation, she races against time to protect her children and get Matilda to the scientists, who may not have her best interests at heart.

Awake received generally negative reviews, with a 24 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a scattered and shallow disaster film, and a Metacritic score of 35. Critics found the plot derivative and lacking in tension, although Rodriguez's committed performance received some praise.

overview: Top student Jane Ryan heads to Manhattan for a college-scholarship competition. Her rebellious twin Roxy Ryan goes along to crash a video shoot. But anything can happen - and does - in a romp involving a pursuing truant officer, a smuggler, hunkalicious guys and the girls' realization that when the chips are down, a sister can be the best friend of all.
tagline: Anything can change in a New York minute.
title: New York Minute
plot:
New York Minute is a 2004 American teen comedy film directed by Dennie Gordon and starring Mary-Kate Olsen and Ashley Olsen. The movie follows the story of twin sisters, Jamie and Sutton, who are on opposite sides of the law, with Jamie being a free-spirited young woman and Sutton being a straight-laced corporate executive.

The main theme of New York Minute revolves around the idea of identity and self-discovery. As the twins navigate their lives in New York City, they must confront their own differences and learn to appreciate each other's unique qualities. The film explores the tension between conforming to societal expectations and embracing individuality, as embodied by Jamie's carefree spirit and Sutton's more structured approach to life.

The movie also touches on themes of family, loyalty, and redemption, particularly in the context of the twins' complicated relationship with their mother. Through their journey, Jamie and Sutton learn valuable lessons about forgiveness, trust, and the importance of following their hearts.

Ultimately, New York Minute is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of what it means to be true to oneself and find one's place in the world. The film's lighthearted tone and comedic moments belie its deeper themes, making it an enjoyable and relatable watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: The powerful story of Jackie Robinson, the legendary baseball player who broke Major League Baseball’s color barrier when he joined the roster of the Brooklyn Dodgers. The film follows the innovative Dodgers’ general manager Branch Rickey, the MLB executive who first signed Robinson to the minors and then helped to bring him up to the show.
tagline: The True Story of an American Legend
plot: [No information found]

overview: A girl from New York attends a college in Atlanta to join their once-famous marching band.
tagline: #PassTheBaton
title: Drumline: A New Beat
plot:
Drumline: A New Beat is a 2014 American musical drama television film directed by Bille Woodruff from a screenplay by Karen Gist and Regina Hicks. A sequel to the 2002 film Drumline, it returns to the fictional Atlanta A&T University and its marching band, telling a largely new story about a fresh generation of drummers at the historically black college. Alexandra Shipp stars as Danielle "Dani" Raymond, with Jordan Calloway as Jayven LaPierre, Jeff Pierre as her cousin Tyree, Mario Van Peebles and Lisa Arrindell as her parents, LeToya Luckett as Dr. Nia Phillips, DeRay Davis, Jasmine Burke, Rome Flynn and Tye White. Leonard Roberts reprises his role as Sean Taylor, and Nick Cannon, who also executive produced, returns as Devon Miles.

Twelve years after the first film, Dani, a drummer from a wealthy Brooklyn family, defies her parents, who want her to attend Spelman, and heads to Atlanta A&T on a partial scholarship, determined to help revive the Panthers' once-celebrated drumline and to become the first woman to lead its section. Her cousin Tyree is a senior on the line, but the new band director, Sean Taylor, gives her no special treatment. As a freshman she endures hazing from upperclassmen, a rule against romance within the band, and open resistance from a drummer who says no woman belongs on the line, while she falls in with a group of misfits and is drawn to Jayven, a charming bandmate and rival with a troubled past whose father is a well-known singer.

The Panthers' long rivalry with Southern State provides the competition, with drumline face-offs staged at football games. Dissension within the band and challenges for places on the line drive Dani and Jayven apart, and at one point she moves to transfer away from the school before returning. Devon Miles, now a music star, arrives to show the young drummers that he still has the touch, and at the Big Southern Classic A&T wins for the first time in six years, then triumphs again in a final drumline battle as Dani and Jayven reconcile.

Filmed in Atlanta in May 2014, the film premiered on VH1 on 27 October 2014 and was released on DVD in March 2015. Reviews were largely unfavorable: Blavity's Shadow and Act called it overlong and overstuffed, with hammy acting and too little drumming, while other viewers enjoyed it as a predictable but nostalgic return to the world of the original.

overview: Inspector Amaia Salazar confronts the origins of her nightmares as she unfolds the darkest secrets of the Baztan valley. Part 3 in the Baztan Trilogy.
title: Offering to the Storm
plot:
Offering to the Storm (Spanish: Ofrenda a la tormenta) is a 2020 Spanish crime thriller directed by Fernando González Molina and written by Luiso Berdejo and Dolores Redondo, based on Redondo's novel. It is the third and final installment of the Baztán Trilogy, following The Invisible Guardian (2017) and The Legacy of the Bones (2019). Marta Etura reprises her role as police inspector Amaia Salazar, with Leonardo Sbaraglia as Judge Markina, Carlos Librado, Imanol Arias, Paco Tous and Ana Wagener. Netflix released the film in July 2020.

Amaia Salazar, a detective with Spain's regional police in Navarre, is still haunted by the events of the previous films, including the disappearance of her mentally disturbed mother, Rosario, who once tried to kill her, and by the nightmares rooted in her childhood in the Baztán valley. When a baby girl dies suddenly in Elizondo in circumstances that appear to be a case of sudden infant death syndrome, Amaia notices disturbing details: the child's grandmother claims that a demon was responsible, and marks on the body suggest that she was suffocated.

Investigating the case, Amaia discovers a series of similar deaths of infants throughout the region over several decades. The trail leads her to a secret network carrying out ritual sacrifices of babies in the name of Inguma, a demon from Basque mythology said to steal the breath of sleeping people. Its members believe that such offerings bring them power and fortune. As the investigation draws her deeper into the history of the cult, Amaia realizes that the case is connected to her own family and to the forces that have pursued her since childhood. She must also face uncomfortable truths about Judge Markina, with whom she has developed a close relationship, and confront the question of what really happened to her mother, while her own young son may be in danger.

The film received mixed reviews. Critics considered it an acceptable conclusion to the trilogy, praising Etura's performance, the atmospheric landscapes of the Baztán valley and the technical quality of the production, but faulted its convoluted screenplay, rushed storytelling and anticlimactic ending.

overview: In the 1980s, college student Samantha Hughes takes a strange babysitting job that coincides with a full lunar eclipse. She slowly realizes her clients harbor a terrifying secret.
tagline: Talk on the phone. Finish your homework. Watch TV. Die.
title: The House of the Devil
plot:
The House of the Devil is a 2009 horror film that explores several themes that are deeply rooted in its narrative. At its core, the movie delves into the idea of vulnerability and the exploitation of it. The protagonist, Samantha, played by Jocelin Donahue, is a college student who takes on a babysitting job at a creepy mansion, where she finds herself trapped in a web of sinister events.

The film also examines the theme of female empowerment and the objectification of women. Samantha's character undergoes a transformation as she navigates the treacherous world of the mansion, confronting her own vulnerabilities and learning to assert herself. The movie critiques the societal norms that perpetuate the objectification of women, particularly in the context of the 1970s setting.

Furthermore, The House of the Devil touches on the theme of class struggle and social inequality. The contrast between Samantha's middle-class background and the wealthy, aristocratic family she works for serves as a backdrop to explore issues of economic disparity and the exploitation that can occur when there is a significant power imbalance.

The film also explores the idea of innocence and the loss of it. As Samantha navigates the dark events unfolding around her, she is forced to confront the harsh realities of the world, leading to a gradual erosion of her innocence. This theme is closely tied to the concept of vulnerability, as Samantha's innocence serves as a shield that is gradually stripped away.

Overall, The House of the Devil is a thought-provoking film that weaves together themes of vulnerability, female empowerment, class struggle, and the loss of innocence, creating a complex narrative that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: A packed cruise ship traveling the Atlantic is hit and overturned by a massive wave, compelling the passengers to begin a dramatic fight for their lives.
tagline: Mayday
title: Poseidon
plot:
Poseidon is a 2006 disaster film directed by Wolfgang Petersen, starring Josh Lucas, Kurt Russell, and Emmy Rossum.

The main themes of Poseidon include:

1. **Survival against all odds**: The movie depicts the catastrophic sinking of the cruise ship Poseidon, which sets off a chain reaction of events that test the characters' survival skills and humanity.
2. **Hubris and the dangers of playing with nature**: The film's protagonist, Captain Josh (Josh Lucas), is initially portrayed as a confident and arrogant captain who underestimates the power of the sea. This theme serves as a warning about the dangers of human hubris and the importance of respecting nature.
3. **Redemption and personal growth**: As the story unfolds, characters like Captain Josh and his crew face their personal demons and undergo significant transformations, ultimately leading to redemption and a newfound appreciation for life.
4. **Human connection and community**: The movie highlights the importance of human relationships and community in the face of adversity. Despite the chaos and destruction surrounding them, the characters come together to support each other and find ways to survive.

The film's plot development is driven by these themes, as the characters navigate the treacherous waters and confront their personal struggles. Ultimately, the movie concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as the survivors emerge from the wreckage with a newfound appreciation for life and a deeper understanding of themselves and each other.

Overall, Poseidon is a thrilling disaster film that explores universal themes of survival, redemption, and human connection in the face of catastrophic adversity.

overview: When a meteor carrying a destructive plant strikes the world, a suicide squad is given hours to save their post-apocalyptic city from total collapse.
title: Warriors of Future
plot:
Warriors of Future (Chinese: 明日戰記), previously known as Virtus, is a 2022 Hong Kong military science fiction action film and the directorial debut of the visual effects artist Ng Yuen-fai. It stars Louis Koo as Tyler, an elite pilot, Sean Lau as his comrade Johnson Cheng and Carina Lau as Colonel Tam. Koo also served as executive producer, and the film was financed and distributed by his company, One Cool Group. Production began in 2017, and the release was delayed for years to allow for extensive visual effects work.

In 2055, Earth has been devastated by wars fought with advanced military robots, and pollution and climate change have poisoned the atmosphere, causing widespread illness and birth defects. Surviving cities are protected by enormous domes known as Skynets. During the construction of the dome over Sector B-16, a futuristic Hong Kong, a meteor crashes into the city carrying a giant alien plant, named Pandora, which spreads rapidly whenever it rains and destroys everything in its path, though scientists discover that it can also purify the polluted air.

A military scientist develops a gene-altering virus that can stop Pandora's growth while preserving its ability to repair the atmosphere. Tyler and Cheng are assigned to lead a mission to deliver the "gene bullet" to the plant's pistil during a window between two rainstorms. Colonel Tam, sent to oversee the operation, has a secret backup plan to bomb Pandora from the air, which would destroy the plant but could kill a hundred and sixty thousand civilians. When the mission is sabotaged from within and the soldiers find themselves trapped in the heart of the alien growth, they must fight hostile robots and the plant itself to save the city.

Its large-scale visual effects were described by critics as a milestone for Hong Kong cinema.

Warriors of Future opened the 46th Hong Kong International Film Festival on 15 August 2022 and was released in Hong Kong on 25 August, becoming the highest-grossing domestic film in Hong Kong at that time and earning about 111 million dollars including mainland China. The South China Morning Post praised its groundbreaking visual effects but noted a lack of fresh ideas.

overview: Speedboat racing champion and multimillionaire Ben Aronoff leads a double life that lands him in trouble with the law and drug lords.
tagline: Success Makes You A Target
title: Speed Kills
plot:
Speed Kills is a 2018 biographical crime thriller film directed by Jeff Wadlow. The movie is based on the true story of Wayne Williams, who was convicted of murdering two young men in Atlanta in the late 1970s.

The main theme of Speed Kills revolves around the destructive nature of obsession and the blurred lines between good and evil. The character of Wayne Williams, played by John Travolta, is a complex figure whose charisma and charm hide a dark and sinister personality. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Williams' obsession with speed and power ultimately leads him down a path of destruction and chaos.

The film also explores the theme of toxic masculinity, as Williams' aggressive and dominant behavior towards women and men alike is portrayed as a symptom of his deeper psychological issues. The movie suggests that this toxic masculinity is not only damaging to those around him but also to himself, leading to a downward spiral of violence and self-destruction.

Furthermore, Speed Kills touches on the theme of celebrity culture and the way it can both elevate and corrupt individuals. Williams' fame as a speed enthusiast and his charismatic personality make him a media darling, but this attention ultimately fuels his ego and reinforces his destructive tendencies.

Overall, Speed Kills is a gripping thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of obsession, toxic masculinity, and the corrupting influence of celebrity culture.

overview: A female parole officer unwittingly gets involved with a handsome photographer who might be a serial killer.
tagline: The hunt for pleasure is the most basic instinct of all.
title: Sexual Predator
plot:
Sexual Predator, also known as Last Cry, is a 2001 American erotic thriller directed by Robert Angelo from a screenplay by Ed Silverstein. Produced by Marc Lawrence for Magic Hour Pictures and MRG Entertainment, with cinematography by David Trulli and music by Michael Vista, it stars Angie Everhart and Richard Grieco, with Kevin Fry, Elizabeth Barondes, Julian Christopher, Ray Valenti and Roy Abrahamson. Made for cable and home video, it belongs to the wave of softcore psychological thrillers popular in the late 1990s and early 2000s, and Angelo had already worked in the genre with films such as Mutual Needs and Forbidden Sins.

J.C. Gale (Grieco) is a photographer known for provocative erotic work. He is charged with the death of a woman who died during an act of erotic asphyxiation, and although he is found guilty, the conviction is reduced to manslaughter and he receives five years' probation. The victim was the best friend of Beth Spinella (Everhart), a probation officer who specializes in sex offenders, and she is assigned as his case officer. Beth sets out to build a sexual profile of Gale, but instead he gradually draws her into a world of erotic experiences, photographing her in his studio and taking her to a sex club, until he succeeds in seducing her. At the same time, someone begins stalking Beth, killing her cat and then murdering one of Gale's models. Her boyfriend Joe (Fry) is convinced that Gale is the killer, but Beth, fearing for her job, cannot reveal that she has been sleeping with the man she is supposed to supervise. The film ends with a twist revealing that the murderer is none of the characters the script has led the audience to suspect.

The film was released on DVD by Columbia TriStar. Critical reaction was sharply divided. Moria's Richard Scheib gave it three stars, calling it surprisingly slick and well photographed, praising the time it devotes to its plot, the unexpected complexity of its two leads and Grieco's darkly ambiguous performance, and describing the final twist as excellent, though he found it implausible that Beth would be allowed to supervise the man accused of killing her friend. Walter Chaw of Film Freak Central gave it zero stars, dismissing it as cheap and exploitative and criticizing its production values, acting, direction and screenplay.

overview: A seasoned detective investigates a series of murders at the U.S. Military Academy in West Point in 1830. He is assisted in his investigation by an intelligent and eager young cadet named Edgar Allan Poe, who will go on to become one of America's most influential authors and the originator of the detective genre.
tagline: Every heart tells a tale.
title: The Pale Blue Eye
plot:
The Pale Blue Eye is a 2022 mystery drama film directed by Terrence Malick, based on the novel of the same name by Gillian Flynn. The movie takes place in 1870 and follows the story of Edgar Allan Poe, a young writer who becomes embroiled in a murder investigation at West Point Academy.

The main themes of The Pale Blue Eye include:
