Arturo leads her to DiFranco, a corrupt attorney who launders the gang's money, and after she beats him she learns where Silas's girlfriend, Petra, will next collect cash. Erin follows Petra into a bank robbery staged by Silas's new crew, survives the shootout and captures Petra after a vicious fight. She also tries to reconnect with her teenage daughter, Shelby, who was raised by an adoptive father.

Flashbacks reveal what went wrong. While undercover, Erin and Chris fell in love and she became pregnant. At her urging, they decided to take part in the gang's robbery and keep their share before quitting the force. But a dye pack exploded, Silas killed a teller, and Chris was shot dead trying to intervene. Erin hid her share of the money and returned to police work, consumed by guilt. In the present, she retrieves the cash from a storage unit and finds most of it ruined by dye. When she meets Silas, she kills him, revealing that he was the dead man in the opening scene. Erin hands her partner evidence of her own guilt. Bleeding internally, she sits alone in her car, remembering a happier moment with her young daughter.

Destroyer received generally positive reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 74% approval; critics singled out Kidman's transformative performance, which earned a Golden Globe nomination, though the film grossed only $5.6 million.

overview: When the old-old-old-fashioned vampire Vlad arrives at the hotel for an impromptu family get-together, Hotel Transylvania is in for a collision of supernatural old-school and modern day cool.
tagline: They're back to raise a little terror
title: Hotel Transylvania 2
plot:
Hotel Transylvania 2 is a 2015 American animated comedy horror film produced by Sony Pictures Animation and directed by Genndy Tartakovsky. The movie takes place one year after the events of the first film, with Mavis (voiced by Selena Gomez) now 18 years old.

The story begins with Dracula (voiced by Adam Sandler), who is struggling to find a suitable bride for his daughter Mavis. He decides to hold a grand wedding ceremony at Hotel Transylvania, inviting all of the monsters from around the world. However, things take a turn when an American tourist named Jonathan (voiced by Andy Samberg) stumbles upon the hotel and falls in love with Mavis.

As the wedding preparations begin, Dracula's past comes back to haunt him. His long-lost brother, Vlad (voiced by David Spade), arrives at the hotel, revealing that he is a werewolf who has been living in the forest for centuries. Vlad's presence sparks a series of events that threaten the safety of Hotel Transylvania and its inhabitants.

Meanwhile, Mavis begins to develop feelings for Jonathan, but her father disapproves of their relationship due to his concerns about human-monster interactions. As the wedding day approaches, Dracula must confront his own biases and learn to accept Jonathan as a potential partner for his daughter.

The plot thickens when Vlad's werewolf curse is triggered, causing him to lose control and wreak havoc on the hotel. Mavis and Jonathan team up with their friends, including Frankenstein (voiced by Kevin James), the Invisible Man (voiced by David Koechner), and Murray (voiced by Steve Buscemi), to help Vlad overcome his curse.

In the end, Dracula comes to accept Jonathan as a worthy partner for Mavis, and the two share a romantic moment. The movie concludes with a grand wedding ceremony, where all of the monsters from around the world come together to celebrate the union of Mavis and Jonathan.

Throughout the film, the characters' personalities shine through, with Adam Sandler's Dracula providing comedic relief and Selena Gomez's Mavis showcasing her growth as a character. The movie features plenty of humor, action, and heart, making it a fun and entertaining ride for audiences of all ages.

overview: Office worker Truly Lin goes on a journey through her memories. 20 years ago, she had a crush on the most popular guy in school. Taiyu, a ruffian and a bully, is in love with the campus belle. Truly teams up with Taiyu to tear the golden couple apart and help each other to get the ones they love.
title: Our Times
plot:
Our Times (Chinese: 我的少女時代) is a 2015 Taiwanese teen romantic comedy-drama and the feature directorial debut of Frankie Chen, who had previously worked in television drama. It stars Vivian Sung as the schoolgirl Lin Truly, Darren Wang as Hsu Tai-yu, the school's notorious gang leader, Dino Lee as Ouyang Fei-fan, the most popular boy in school, and Dewi Chien as Tao Min-min, with Joe Chen and Jerry Yan as the adult Truly and Tai-yu. Set largely in the 1990s, the film is a nostalgic look at first love and adolescence.

In the present day, Lin Truly is an overworked office employee whose sincerity makes her the target of ridicule from younger colleagues. Listening to an old cassette of a song by Andy Lau, she recalls her high school years, when she was an ordinary girl who idolized Lau and had a crush on Ouyang. When she naively passes on a threatening chain letter to several people, including the school bully Hsu Tai-yu, who is then hit by a car, Tai-yu discovers she sent it and forces her to become his errand girl.

After discovering that Ouyang is secretly dating Min-min, the school's most popular girl, on whom Tai-yu has a crush, Truly forms an alliance with Tai-yu to break the couple up. She learns that Tai-yu and Ouyang were once close friends and that a tragedy turned Tai-yu into a gangster, and she persuades him to become his old self again. As the two study together, defend each other against an unfair school administrator and lead a student protest, their friendship slowly turns into love, but misunderstandings and Tai-yu's health problems separate them before they can confess their feelings. Years later, a chance encounter with Andy Lau leads the adult Truly back to the boy who once promised her that Lau would sing for her.

The film gained wide popularity across Asia, and its theme song, "A Little Happiness" by Hebe Tien, became the first video by a Chinese-language singer to reach 100 million views on YouTube.

Our Times grossed about 84.4 million dollars worldwide, with mainland China its largest market, making it a major commercial success across Asia. Critical response was lukewarm: the South China Morning Post found it excessively saccharine, while the Taipei Times praised Sung's performance and the film's period detail.

overview: A career officer and his wife work with a police detective to uncover the truth behind their son's disappearance following his return from a tour of duty in Iraq.
tagline: Sometimes finding the truth is easier than facing it.
title: In the Valley of Elah
plot:
In the Valley of Elah is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of war, identity, and redemption. The film tells the story of Hank DeVille (played by Russell Crowe), a U.S. Army National Guard sergeant who returns home from Iraq to find his son missing in action.

As Hank searches for answers about his son's disappearance, he becomes embroiled in a mystery surrounding a local teenager, Emmett (played by Joseph Gordon-Levitt), who is accused of murdering a young woman. Through this investigation, the film explores themes of patriotism, duty, and the moral complexities of war.

The movie also delves into the psychological toll that war takes on soldiers, particularly those who are forced to confront the harsh realities of combat. Hank's journey is marked by a deep sense of loss, anger, and disillusionment, as he struggles to reconcile his own identity with the expectations placed upon him as a soldier.

One of the most striking aspects of In the Valley of Elah is its portrayal of the human cost of war, particularly on those who are left behind. The film raises important questions about the nature of patriotism, duty, and responsibility, and challenges the viewer to consider the complexities of these themes in the context of modern warfare.

Ultimately, In the Valley of Elah is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that grapples with some of the most pressing issues of our time. Through its thought-provoking narrative and nuanced character development, the film offers a searing critique of the war on terror and its impact on American society.

overview: Poonam, a traditionally brought-up young woman, is to marry Prem, a groom chosen by her uncle. Poonam and Prem's faith and love are to be tested however, when an accident occurs and Poonam might be scarred for life.
tagline: Marriage isn't a game...
title: Vivah
plot:
Vivah is a 2006 Indian romantic drama film directed by Shimit Amin and produced by Rajshri Productions. The movie revolves around the story of Prem (played by Akshay Kumar), a young man who falls in love with Sanjana (played by Karisma Kapoor), but struggles to win her heart due to his own shortcomings.

The main theme of Vivah is the importance of self-improvement and personal growth. Prem's journey is a metaphor for the human struggle to overcome one's flaws and become a better version of oneself. Through his experiences, he learns to appreciate the value of hard work, dedication, and perseverance in achieving his goals.

Another significant theme present in Vivah is the significance of family values and relationships. The movie highlights the importance of respecting and valuing one's family, particularly parents, and the sacrifices they make for their children. Prem's relationship with his father, who is a strict but loving figure, serves as a catalyst for his personal growth.

The film also explores the theme of love and its various forms. Sanjana, despite her initial reluctance, comes to realize that she has fallen in love with Prem, and their bond becomes stronger through mutual understanding and respect. The movie showcases the beauty of unconditional love and acceptance, which is a central theme throughout the narrative.

Overall, Vivah is a heartwarming story that celebrates the power of self-improvement, family values, and the transformative nature of love.

overview: The hot-headed young D'Artagnan along with three former legendary but now down on their luck Musketeers must unite and defeat a beautiful double agent and her villainous employer from seizing the French throne and engulfing Europe in war.
tagline: Every legend has a new beginning.
title: The Three Musketeers
plot:
The Three Musketeers is a 2011 period action-adventure film directed by Paul W. S. Anderson, a loose adaptation of Alexandre Dumas's 1844 novel adding fantastical airships. Logan Lerman stars as D'Artagnan, with Matthew Macfadyen, Ray Stevenson and Luke Evans as the musketeers Athos, Porthos and Aramis, Milla Jovovich as Milady de Winter, Mads Mikkelsen as Rochefort, Orlando Bloom as the Duke of Buckingham and Christoph Waltz as Cardinal Richelieu.

In Venice, the musketeers Athos, Porthos and Aramis, aided by Milady de Winter, steal Leonardo da Vinci's designs for a flying warship, only for Milady to betray them and sell the plans to the Duke of Buckingham. A year later, the young D'Artagnan leaves Gascony for Paris, hoping to become a musketeer like his father, only to find that the regiment has been disbanded. After a humiliating encounter with Rochefort, the captain of Cardinal Richelieu's guard, he unwittingly offends Athos, Porthos and Aramis and arranges to duel each of them, but when Richelieu's guards interrupt, the four fight side by side. Summoned before the young King Louis XIII, they are honored rather than punished.

Richelieu, scheming to seize power, has Milady plant forged love letters among the queen's possessions and steal her diamond necklace, taking it to London to suggest an affair with Buckingham. If the queen cannot wear the necklace at an upcoming ball, the king will be forced to execute her and go to war with England. Learning of the plot from the queen's lady-in-waiting, Constance the musketeers travel to London. There they outwit Milady and Buckingham, steal Buckingham's airship and recover the necklace, while Milady leaps from the ship rather than face execution.

On their return to France, they are attacked by Rochefort aboard a larger airship built from Milady's copies of the plans, and the battle ends with both vessels crashing onto Notre-Dame Cathedral, where D'Artagnan kills Rochefort in a duel. The necklace is returned to the queen in time for the ball, and the musketeers cover up the affair using Milady's written authorization from Richelieu, who vows revenge after they refuse to serve him. Meanwhile, Buckingham rescues Milady and advances on France with an armada of ships and airships.

The film received negative reviews, with critics faulting its writing and characters; Rotten Tomatoes reported 27% approval. It grossed $132 million worldwide against a production budget of $75 million.

overview: Mulder and Scully, now taken off the FBI's X Files cases, must find a way to fight the shadowy elements of the government to find out the truth about a conspiracy that might mean the alien colonization of Earth.
tagline: Fight the Future
title: The X Files
plot:
The X-Files is a science fiction-supernatural television series created by Chris Carter that premiered in 1993, not 1998. It was produced by 20th Century Fox Television.

The main themes of The X-Files include:

1. Government conspiracy: The show explores the idea of a secret government agency, known as the Syndicate, that is hiding the truth about paranormal events and extraterrestrial life.
2. Paranoia and mistrust: The series follows FBI agents Fox Mulder (David Duchovny) and Dana Scully (Gillian Anderson) as they investigate cases involving the supernatural, often uncovering a web of deceit and conspiracy that threatens to destroy their lives.
3. Science vs. Faith: The show explores the tension between scientific rationalism and faith in the paranormal, with Mulder believing in the existence of extraterrestrial life and Scully initially skeptical but later becoming more open-minded.
4. Personal sacrifice: Throughout the series, both Mulder and Scully face personal sacrifices as they delve deeper into their cases, often putting their lives at risk to uncover the truth.

The show's themes are expertly woven throughout its nine seasons, with each episode exploring a new case while contributing to the overall mythology of the series.

overview: The Addams get tangled up in more wacky adventures and find themselves involved in hilarious run-ins with all sorts of unsuspecting characters.
tagline: Unhappy to see you again.
title: The Addams Family 2
plot:
The Addams Family 2, also titled The Addams Family 2: Road Trip, is a 2021 animated supernatural black comedy based on Charles Addams's characters and a sequel to The Addams Family (2019). Directed by Greg Tiernan and Conrad Vernon and written by Dan Hernandez, Benji Samit, Ben Queen and Susanna Fogel, it features the voices of Oscar Isaac, Charlize Theron, Chloë Grace Moretz, Nick Kroll, Javon Walton, Wallace Shawn, Snoop Dogg, Bette Midler and Bill Hader.

At a school science fair, Wednesday Addams demonstrates an experiment that uses the DNA of her pet squid Socrates to "improve" Uncle Fester, with the side effect that he slowly begins to mutate. Her work catches the eye of the scientist Cyrus Strange. At home, Gomez fears his children are growing away from him and Morticia and plans a cross-country family vacation. Before they leave, a lawyer named Mr. Mustela claims that Wednesday was switched at birth and may not be an Addams, a claim the parents dismiss.

Pursued by Mustela and a henchman named Pongo, the family travels across the United States, visiting Niagara Falls, Sleepy Hollow, Miami, where Cousin Itt joins them, San Antonio and the Grand Canyon. When Fester recalls juggling newborn babies in the delivery room on the day Wednesday was born, Gomez and Morticia's doubts grow, and Wednesday overhears them. She captures Mustela and learns he works for Cyrus, who suggests he is her real father and invites her to his home in Sausalito. A DNA test on Gomez's hair appears to confirm the claim, and she slips away from the family, followed by Lurch and then the others.

Cyrus reveals he has been trying to create human-animal hybrids and wants to use Wednesday's superior formula. When she refuses to test it on her family, Lurch and Pongo, who knew each other from an asylum, free the Addamses. Cyrus is transformed into a hybrid monster, admits he faked the DNA results, and dies after a fight with Fester, who has fully mutated. Wednesday restores Fester using a necklace containing the family's blood, and the family heads home together.

The film grossed $120 million worldwide but received poor reviews, with 28% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 37.

overview: Upon receiving a mysterious letter that her mother's grave has been vandalized, Marie travels to the desolate island town where she's buried. Just as she arrives, the island closes for the season, leaving Marie trapped in a nightmare.
tagline: Something is off on this island.
title: Offseason
plot:
Offseason is a 2021 American supernatural horror film written and directed by Mickey Keating. It stars Jocelin Donahue, Joe Swanberg, Richard Brake and Melora Walters, with Jeremy Gardner and April Linscott in supporting roles. Keating began developing the story in 2018 after reading William Faulkner's "A Rose for Emily" and Shirley Jackson's "The Summer People", and shot it with cinematographer Mac Fisken in and around New Smyrna Beach, Florida, wrapping in February 2020. The film premiered at South by Southwest on 17 March 2021, also played at Sitges, and was released by RLJE Films on video on demand and in limited theatres on 11 March 2022.

Marie Aldrich (Donahue) receives a mysterious letter from a cemetery caretaker urging her to come at once, because the grave of her famous, mentally troubled mother Ava (Walters) has been vandalised. With her boyfriend George (Swanberg) she drives to Lone Palm Beach, the remote island town where Ava grew up and is buried, even though her mother had insisted that not even her ashes should return there. The keeper of the island's only drawbridge (Brake) warns them that the town is closing for the off-season and that the bridge will soon be raised until spring, but lets them through. Marie finds Ava's headstone broken in half, while the fog-bound, nearly deserted town is populated by off-kilter locals, among them a florist, Miss Emily (Linscott), who studies her with glassy eyes, and a man known only as the Fisherman (Gardner). Roads seem to loop back on themselves, the couple are cut off once the bridge goes up, and white-eyed figures begin closing in. Divided into chapters by title cards, the story has Marie weighing her mother's ravings about a pact with an aquatic deity against the dangers around her, as she uncovers a generational curse and a Lovecraftian deity demanding sacrifices from the townspeople.

Critics praised the atmosphere more than the story. Rotten Tomatoes counted a 68% approval rating from 65 reviews, its consensus crediting strong performances by Donahue and Walters, while Metacritic's score of 55 indicated mixed reviews. Tomris Laffly of Variety found it thinly conceived but full of genuinely spine-tingling images and sounds, Slashfilm likened its subtle creeps to John Carpenter's The Fog, and Dread Central singled out Brake's unhinged performance, whereas RogerEbert.com and The A.V. Club found it derivative and aimless.

overview: As a deadly virus ravages the world, Dr. Martin Lowery embarks on a mission to reach test site ATU327A, a research hub deep in the Arboreal Forest. The arduous journey, guided by park scout Alma, is set back by a nighttime attack that leaves the two bruised and shoeless. When they run into Zach, a man living off the grid, they gratefully accept his help. Zach’s intentions aren’t exactly what they seem, however, and a path out of the forest and into safety quickly fades as the line between myth and science blurs.
tagline: Nature is a force of evil.
title: In the Earth
plot:
In the Earth is a 2021 British science fiction horror film directed by Ben Wheatley. The movie follows a geologist, Dr. Amelia Gray (Joanna Scanlan), who returns to her childhood home in the Yorkshire moors after a personal tragedy.

The main themes of In the Earth include:

1. Grief and Trauma: The film explores Dr. Gray's emotional state as she grapples with the loss of her daughter. Her journey is a metaphor for the healing process, but also highlights the complexity and intensity of grief.
2. Nature vs. Humanity: The movie portrays the Yorkshire moors as a powerful, almost sentient force that threatens humanity. This dichotomy serves as a commentary on our relationship with nature and the consequences of exploiting it.
3. Isolation and Loneliness: Dr. Gray's isolation in the remote moors mirrors her emotional state, emphasizing the crushing loneliness that can result from trauma and loss.
4. The Unknowable: The film's use of an ancient, prehistoric creature as a threat serves as a metaphor for the unknowable, uncontrollable forces that exist beyond human understanding.

Throughout the movie, Ben Wheatley masterfully weaves these themes together to create a tense, unsettling narrative that explores the complexities of human emotion and our place in the natural world.

overview: After her grandfather's death, 20-year-old Alma decides to go back to her childhood home - a little island in the heart of the majestic Canadian forest. Whilst there, she rescues two helpless cubs: a wolf and a lion. They forge an inseparable bond, but their world soon collapses as the forest ranger discovers the animals and takes them away. The two cub brothers must now embark on a treacherous journey across Canada to be reunited with one another and Alma once more.
tagline: An unlikely friendship. An incredible adventure.
title: The Wolf and the Lion
plot:
The Wolf and the Lion (French: Le Loup et le Lion) is a 2021 family adventure film directed by Gilles de Maistre, who wrote the screenplay with his wife, Prune de Maistre. Molly Kunz stars as Alma, a young pianist, with Graham Greene, Charlie Carrick, Derek Johns and Rebecca Croll. Shot in the Canadian wilderness with real animals rather than computer-generated imagery, the film premiered at the Zurich Film Festival in September 2021, where it won the award for best children's film, and was released in France in October.

After the death of her grandfather, Alma Deranquel returns to his cabin in the Canadian wilderness, where she grew up. In the forest she discovers the wreckage of a small plane that was carrying a lion cub, captured in Africa and destined for a circus. The cub survives, and Alma decides not to hand it over to the forest rangers, remembering that her grandfather campaigned against the mistreatment of animals in circuses. At the same time, a she-wolf who had befriended her grandfather, and whose den once lay where his cabin now stands, takes refuge in the house with her pup while being pursued by two scientists.

The lion cub and the wolf pup grow up together like brothers, playing and feeding side by side under the care of the she-wolf. While Alma is away for two days at an audition for the Los Angeles Philharmonic, the mother wolf disappears, captured with a tranquilizer dart by the scientists, who want to transfer her to a breeding program for an endangered wolf species. Alma is left to raise the two young animals alone, and as they grow, the bond between the wolf and the lion deepens. Their unusual friendship eventually attracts outside attention, and Alma, torn between her musical career and her responsibility to the animals, must fight to keep the two brothers together and secure their future in the wild.

The Wolf and the Lion received generally negative reviews from critics, with a 29 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Reviewers praised the picturesque scenery, Serge Desrosiers's cinematography and the remarkable scenes with the animals, but criticized the plot, the human performances and the film's length, while Richard Whittaker of the Austin Chronicle found much to enjoy in its old-fashioned charm.

overview: Following the loss of their son, a retired sheriff and his wife leave their Montana ranch to rescue their young grandson from the clutches of a dangerous family living off the grid in the Dakotas.
tagline: Fight for family.
title: Let Him Go
plot:
Let Him Go is a 2020 American Western drama film directed by Thomas Bezucha, based on the 2009 novel of the same name by Larry Watson.

The movie follows George Blackwell (played by Kevin Costner) and his wife Margaret (played by Diane Lane), who live in rural Montana. When their daughter dies, they are left alone to care for each other. However, when Margaret falls ill, George is forced to take her on a road trip to visit her estranged sister in Utah.

During the journey, they encounter a mysterious and sinister figure named Lorne Malvo (played by Will Oldham), who seems to be manipulating events from behind the scenes. As they travel through the American West, George becomes increasingly obsessed with finding out what happened to his daughter and confronting the dark forces that have been at work in their lives.

The main themes of Let Him Go include:

1. **Grief and Loss**: The movie explores the devastating effects of loss on a family, particularly when it comes to the death of a child. George's grief is palpable, and his journey is driven by a desire to understand what happened to his daughter.
2. **The American West as a Character**: The film portrays the vast, isolated landscapes of Montana and Utah as a character in its own right, with the natural world serving as a backdrop for the characters' emotional struggles.
3. **Mortality and the Human Condition**: As George and Margaret face their own mortality, they are forced to confront the meaninglessness and uncertainty of life. The film raises questions about the human condition, the nature of existence, and what lies beyond death.
4. **The Corrupting Influence of Power**: Lorne Malvo is a master manipulator who uses his charm and intelligence to exploit those around him. His presence serves as a catalyst for George's transformation, highlighting the dangers of unchecked power and the corrupting influence it can have on individuals.

Overall, Let Him Go is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores the complexities of human relationships, the fragility of life, and the darkness that lurks beneath the surface of even the most idyllic communities.

overview: Video game bad guy Ralph and fellow misfit Vanellope von Schweetz must risk it all by traveling to the World Wide Web in search of a replacement part to save Vanellope's video game, Sugar Rush. In way over their heads, Ralph and Vanellope rely on the citizens of the internet — the netizens — to help navigate their way, including an entrepreneur named Yesss, who is the head algorithm and the heart and soul of trend-making site BuzzzTube.
tagline: Who Broke the Internet?
title: Ralph Breaks the Internet
plot:
Ralph Breaks the Internet is a 2018 American animated comedy-adventure film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie serves as a sequel to Wreck-It Ralph, released in 2012.

The story begins with Ralph (voiced by John C. Reilly), the lovable but destructive villain from the classic arcade game Fix-It Felix, who has become an unlikely hero after saving the arcade from an evil virus known as "Sugar Rush." To celebrate his victory, Ralph and his new friend Vanellope von Schweetz (voiced by Sarah Silverman) are invited to a high-tech gaming convention called Slaughter Race.

However, things take a turn when Ralph becomes fascinated with the world of online gaming and decides to explore the internet. He and Vanellope embark on a journey through various websites, including YouTube, eBay, and Amazon. Along the way, they encounter new characters, such as Shank (voiced by Gal Gadot), a tough-as-nails driver from the racing game Crash Bandicoot.

As Ralph delves deeper into the internet, he becomes increasingly obsessed with his online persona and the validation it provides. He starts to neglect his friendship with Vanellope and his responsibilities in the arcade. Meanwhile, Shank's true intentions are revealed, and she is determined to take down Ralph and claim the championship title for Crash Bandicoot.

As Ralph struggles to balance his online life with his real-life relationships, he must also confront the darker side of the internet. He discovers that the world of online gaming can be cruel and unforgiving, where players are often pitted against each other in a never-ending cycle of competition.

In the end, Ralph realizes that true friendship and connection cannot be found online but rather through shared experiences and genuine relationships. With Vanellope's help, he finds a way to reconcile his online persona with his real-life identity and saves the arcade from Shank's evil plans.

The movie features stunning animation, witty humor, and a talented voice cast. The film's exploration of the internet's impact on society is both thought-provoking and entertaining, making it a must-see for audiences of all ages. Overall, Ralph Breaks the Internet is a heartwarming and hilarious adventure that celebrates the power of friendship and the importance of staying true to oneself.

overview: Restless and ready for an adventure, four suburban bikers leave the safety of their subdivision and head out on the open road. But complications ensue when they cross paths with an intimidating band of New Mexico bikers known as the Del Fuegos.
tagline: A lot can happen on the road to nowhere.
title: Wild Hogs
plot:
Wild Hogs is a 2007 American comedy film directed by Walt Becker and starring John Travolta, Tim Allen, Martin Lawrence, and William H. Macy.

The movie follows four middle-aged friends - Steve (John Travolta), Bubba (Tim Allen), Ralph (Martin Lawrence), and Doug (William H. Macy) - who embark on a road trip together to find meaning in their lives after a series of personal crises. Along the way, they encounter various challenges, including run-ins with bikers, eccentric characters, and themselves.

The main themes of Wild Hogs include:

1. Friendship: The film explores the importance of male friendships and how these relationships can provide support, comfort, and a sense of belonging.
2. Midlife Crisis: The movie pokes fun at the common phenomenon of men experiencing a midlife crisis, where they question their purpose and identity in life.
3. Self-discovery: As the characters navigate their journey, they are forced to confront their own insecurities, fears, and desires, leading to a deeper understanding of themselves and their place in the world.
4. Camaraderie: The film celebrates the joy of shared experiences and the bonds that form between people who come from different walks of life.
5. Embracing change: Wild Hogs encourages viewers to be open to new experiences and to find happiness in the journey, rather than just focusing on the destination.

Overall, Wild Hogs is a heartwarming comedy that explores themes of friendship, self-discovery, and embracing change, all set against the backdrop of an epic road trip adventure.

overview: Fifteen directors and an all-star cast created this twisted comedy that follows three teens on the hunt for the world's most banned film.
tagline: The biggest cast ever assembled for the most outrageous comedy ever made.
title: Movie 43
plot:
Movie 43 is a 2013 American anthology comedy film directed by Peter Segal, written by Jake Kasdan, Jason Segel, and Nicholas Stoller, and starring an ensemble cast including Emma Stone, Hugh Jackman, Kate Winslet, and Stephen Merchant.

The film consists of six separate stories, each with its own unique tone and style. The first story, "The Catch," stars Halle Berry as a woman who is trying to get revenge on her cheating ex-boyfriend (played by Chris Parnell). However, things take a dark turn when she discovers that he has been replaced by a lookalike.

The second story, "The Getaway," stars Kate Winslet and Hugh Jackman as a couple who are on the run from the law after a botched heist. As they try to escape, they realize that their relationship is not as strong as they thought it was.

The third story, "The Catch: Part Two," serves as a sequel to the first story and follows the same characters as they try to take revenge on the lookalike who replaced Berry's character.

The fourth story, "Milk," stars Seth MacFarlane as a man who is trying to get his girlfriend (played by Emma Stone) to lose weight. However, things take a dark turn when he discovers that she has been hiding a shocking secret.

The fifth story, "Pedestal," stars Stephen Merchant and Johnny Knoxville as two men who are trying to make it big in the world of adult entertainment. However, their plans are foiled when they discover that their rival is not what he seems.

The sixth and final story, "The Catch: Part Three," serves as a conclusion to the first story and follows Berry's character as she tries to take revenge on her ex-boyfriend once again.

Throughout the film, the tone shifts from dark comedy to slapstick humor, making it a challenging watch for some viewers. However, fans of the genre will likely find it entertaining and hilarious.

Overall, Movie 43 is a unique and unpredictable film that explores themes of love, relationships, and revenge. While it may not be to everyone's taste, it is certainly an interesting and thought-provoking watch.

overview: The passing of a beloved old neighbor reunites six friends for a hometown holiday treasure hunt, where sparks fly once again between brand strategist Austin and his former best friend Everett.
title: A Christmas to Treasure
plot:
A Christmas to Treasure is a 2022 American Christmas romantic comedy television film written and directed by Jake Helgren and produced by The Ninth House. It stars Taylor Frey and Kyle Dean Massey, with Katie Walder, Mary-Margaret Humes, Roberto Aguire, Nikki McKenzie, Cort McCown, Norman Towns and Autumn Federici in supporting roles. The film premiered on Lifetime on 16 December 2022 and runs about 90 minutes.

Austin Craig (Frey), a quick-witted brand strategist, works with his childhood friend Tipper Tisdale (Walder), and the pair are close to landing an event that could take their business to the next level when each receives a mysterious letter from Mrs. Marley, a beloved old neighbour who has recently died. Growing up, Mrs. Marley and her husband opened their large house to the neighbourhood children, hosting an annual Candy Cane Carnival and a Christmas treasure hunt every year, and in her letter she invites the six childhood friends to reunite in their hometown of Belleville for one last hunt. Her death has hit Everett Matthews (Massey), Austin's former best friend, especially hard, since he cared for her in her final years. While he is decorating her old house for Christmas on his own, their friend Ricky Treviño (Aguire) brings the bad news that the house will be sold to a land developer and turned into a ski resort unless Everett can raise $200,000. Everett is determined to find Mrs. Marley's buried treasure to save it, while Austin hopes to use part of the money to build his company. As the friends, including Michelle Wu (McKenzie) and the professional basketball player Clay King (Towns), follow her clues and contend with a scheming estate agent, Rochelle Raimo (Federici), Austin and Everett revisit their complicated history, including Everett's painful coming out, and the old sparks between them reignite.

Decider recommended the film, calling it "a lot of movie", with a larger lead cast and bigger premise than most holiday television films, but praising the multi-faceted, lived-in characterisations of the principal characters, Frey's snarky yet cuddly Austin, and a memorable fast-talking bluffing scene for Walder. The reviewer found the elaborate Marley backstory distracting and felt that two of the friends were underused, but concluded that the film understood that the most important parts were its small, intimate details.

overview: When young dockworker Jude leaves Liverpool to find his estranged father in the United States, he is swept up by the waves of change that are re-shaping the nation. Jude falls in love with Lucy, who joins the growing anti-war movement. As the body count in Vietnam rises, political tensions at home spiral out of control and the star-crossed lovers find themselves in a psychedelic world gone mad.
tagline: All you need is love.
title: Across the Universe
plot:
Across the Universe is a 2007 musical romantic drama film that weaves together the music of The Beatles with a narrative that explores the tumultuous 1960s in Liverpool, England. At its core, the movie delves into themes of love, loss, and social upheaval during a pivotal moment in history.

The story revolves around Lucy (played by Evan Rachel Wood), a young woman who becomes entangled in a complicated web of relationships with Jude (played by Jim Sturgess), a working-class Liverpudlian struggling to find his place in the world. As their romance blossoms, they must navigate the challenges of social class differences and the constraints of societal expectations.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with the disillusionment and frustration that characterized the late 1960s, as the Vietnam War raged on and the civil rights movement gained momentum. The movie captures the sense of restlessness and rebellion that defined this era, as young people sought to challenge the status quo and forge their own paths.

The film also explores the complexities of identity and belonging, particularly for those who felt like outsiders or misfits. Jude's struggles to reconcile his working-class roots with his aspirations for a better life serve as a powerful metaphor for the tensions between tradition and innovation that defined this period in history.

Ultimately, Across the Universe is a poignant and visually stunning tribute to the music of The Beatles, which serves as a soundtrack for the characters' emotional journeys. Through its exploration of love, loss, and social change, the film offers a nuanced and thought-provoking portrayal of a pivotal moment in modern history.

overview: A tale of friendship between two unlikely pen pals: Mary, a lonely, eight-year-old girl living in the suburbs of Melbourne, and Max, a forty-four-year old, severely obese man living in New York.
tagline: Sometimes perfect strangers make the best friends.
title: Mary and Max
plot:
Mary and Max is a 2009 animated black comedy-drama film directed by Adam Elliot. The movie tells the story of an unlikely friendship between two individuals from different walks of life: Mary, a young girl living in Australia, and Max, a middle-aged man living in New York.

The main themes of Mary and Max include:

1. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Both Mary and Max are outsiders who feel disconnected from society. Mary lives on a remote farm with her abusive father, while Max is a lonely office worker who struggles to connect with others.
2. **Friendship and Connection**: Despite their differences, Mary and Max form an unlikely bond through letters, which becomes the heart of the story. Their friendship helps them both find meaning and purpose in their lives.
3. **Mental Health**: The film explores themes of depression, anxiety, and loneliness, particularly in Max's character. His struggles with mental health are portrayed as a source of vulnerability and strength.
4. **Childhood Innocence vs. Adult Reality**: Mary represents childhood innocence and naivety, while Max embodies adult cynicism and disillusionment. As their friendship evolves, they learn to appreciate each other's perspectives and find common ground.
5. **The Power of Imagination**: The film celebrates the power of imagination and creativity, as embodied by Mary's artistic talents and Max's love of fantasy.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together to create a poignant and humorous exploration of human connection in a world that often feels isolating and lonely.

overview: For years, old wood carver Mr. Meacham has delighted local children with his tales of the fierce dragon that resides deep in the woods of the Pacific Northwest. To his daughter, Grace, who works as a forest ranger, these stories are little more than tall tales... until she meets Pete, a mysterious 10-year-old with no family and no home who claims to live in the woods with a giant, green dragon named Elliott. And from Pete's descriptions, Elliott seems remarkably similar to the dragon from Mr. Meacham's stories. With the help of Natalie, an 11-year-old girl whose father Jack owns the local lumber mill, Grace sets out to determine where Pete came from, where he belongs, and the truth about this dragon.
tagline: Some secrets are too big to keep.
title: Pete's Dragon
plot:
Pete's Dragon (2016) is a fantasy adventure film directed by David Lowery, produced by Walt Disney Pictures and Whitaker Entertainment.

The main themes of Pete's Dragon (2016) include:

1. **Friendship**: The movie revolves around the unbreakable bond between Pete and Elliot, a dragon who becomes his best friend. Their friendship is put to the test when they face various challenges and dangers.
2. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Pete, an orphaned boy, lives in isolation with Elliot on a remote island. As the story progresses, he longs for human connection and acceptance, highlighting the importance of relationships in our lives.
3. **Growing Up and Self-Discovery**: Throughout the film, Pete learns to navigate his emotions, confront his fears, and develop a sense of self-worth. His journey is marked by significant growth and self-discovery.
4. **Protection and Sacrifice**: Elliot's protective nature towards Pete drives many of the plot developments. The movie showcases the lengths to which one would go to safeguard those they care about, highlighting the value of sacrifice in relationships.
5. **Embracing Differences**: The film celebrates the unique bond between a human and an animal, promoting acceptance and understanding of differences.

The story begins with Pete's life on the island, where he befriends Elliot, a dragon who becomes his companion. When a logging company threatens their home, they embark on a journey to find safety and acceptance in the outside world. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including the villainous Dr. Terminus, who seeks to exploit Elliot's powers.

As Pete navigates this new world, he faces challenges that test his courage, loyalty, and sense of self. Ultimately, the film concludes with a heartwarming moment of acceptance and belonging for both Pete and Elliot, as they find a new home where they can be themselves without fear of judgment or rejection.

Overall, Pete's Dragon (2016) is a beautifully crafted story that explores themes of friendship, growth, protection, and self-acceptance, making it a delightful and engaging film for audiences of all ages.

overview: Two strangers strike up a conversation on a long journey. One is a suspect in an unsolved missing person’s case and the other an undercover operative on his trail. Their uneasy friendship becomes the core of this tightly wrought thriller, which is based on the true story of one of the largest investigations and undercover operations in Australia.
tagline: The closer you get...
title: The Stranger
plot:
The Stranger is a 2022 Australian psychological crime thriller film written and directed by Thomas M. Wright, starring Joel Edgerton and Sean Harris. Based on Kate Kyriacou's nonfiction book The Sting: The Undercover Operation That Caught Daniel Morcombe's Killer, it was inspired by the investigation into the 2003 murder of the Queensland schoolboy Daniel Morcombe, with names changed. The film premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2022 Cannes Film Festival and was released on Netflix in October 2022.

Police are convinced that Henry Teague, a loner with a violent past, abducted and murdered a young boy years earlier, but they have no proof. They launch an elaborate undercover sting known as a "Mr. Big" operation. An undercover officer befriends Teague on a long bus journey and introduces him to his associate, Mark Frame, who appears to be part of a powerful criminal organization but is also an undercover detective. Frame offers Teague small jobs, stressing that the organization values loyalty and honesty above all and can solve any problem for its members as long as nothing is kept from it. Teague admits to time in prison for assault, but insists his record is otherwise clean.

Over many months, Frame becomes Teague's mentor and closest companion, drawing him deeper into the fake organization and introducing him to increasingly senior figures, all of whom are police officers. The role takes a heavy toll on Frame. Teague grows dependent on Frame, at one point making a sexual advance toward him. Meanwhile, Detective Kate Rylett pursues every lead Frame supplies, and discovers that Teague had been convicted under another name of an earlier attack on a child, strengthening her certainty of his guilt.

When police fear that Teague may be growing suspicious, they arrange for a supposedly corrupt officer to warn him that he is about to be charged. Frame brings him to meet John, the organization's boss, who promises that his problems can disappear as long as he reveals every detail of the crime. Despite tense moments, Teague confesses and leads the officers to the scene in the woods, where he is arrested. After an exhaustive search, police find physical evidence. Frame, however, remains haunted by the case, unable to sleep and fearfully overprotective of his young son.

The Stranger received critical acclaim, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 92% approval, with praise for its tension and its two lead performances.

overview: Fact-based war drama about an American battalion of over 500 men which gets trapped behind enemy lines in the Argonne Forest in October 1918 France during the closing weeks of World War I.
tagline: Caught between two lines of fire, the Germans gave them two options: surrender or die. They chose a third.
title: The Lost Battalion
plot: Fact-based war drama about an American battalion of over 500 men which gets trapped behind enemy lines in the Argonne Forest in October 1918 France during the closing weeks of World War I.

overview: A newly-released prison gangster is forced by the leaders of his gang to orchestrate a major crime with a brutal rival gang on the streets of Southern California.
tagline: Some criminals are made in prison
title: Shot Caller
plot:
Shot Caller is a 2017 American drama film directed by Albert Hughes and written by Nick Sandow. The movie stars Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, Lake Bell, and Jeffrey Donovan.

The story revolves around Jacob Harford (played by Nikolaj Coster-Waldau), a successful businessman who is sentenced to five years in prison for a white-collar crime he committed. Initially, Jacob struggles to adapt to the harsh realities of prison life, where he faces violence, corruption, and exploitation from the inmates and guards.

As Jacob navigates the prison system, he meets a group of inmates who become his allies, including a tough-as-nails inmate named Frank (played by Jeffrey Donovan). Frank takes Jacob under his wing and teaches him how to survive in the prison. However, their friendship is put to the test when Jacob becomes embroiled in a violent gang war between rival factions.

Despite the dangers, Jacob begins to transform himself, both physically and mentally. He starts working out with the inmates, particularly Frank, and learns new skills that help him cope with the harsh environment. Jacob also forms a bond with a fellow inmate named Emily (played by Lake Bell), who becomes his love interest.

As Jacob's transformation progresses, he faces challenges from within and outside the prison walls. He must confront his own demons and make difficult choices to protect himself and those around him. The movie takes a dramatic turn when Jacob is forced to participate in a violent gang fight that puts his life at risk.

Throughout the film, the director uses vivid imagery and cinematography to convey the harsh realities of prison life. The performances by the cast are also noteworthy, particularly Coster-Waldau's portrayal of Jacob Harford, who undergoes a remarkable transformation from a privileged businessman to a hardened inmate.

The ending of Shot Caller is intense and emotional, as Jacob faces a difficult decision that will determine his future. Without giving away too much, I can say that the movie concludes on a hopeful note, with Jacob having undergone a profound transformation that sets him up for a chance at redemption.

Overall, Shot Caller is a gripping drama that explores themes of survival, redemption, and personal growth in the harsh environment of prison. The film features strong performances from its cast, particularly Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, who delivers a powerful performance as Jacob Harford.

overview: France, 1940. In the first days of occupation, beautiful Lucile Angellier is trapped in a stifled existence with her controlling mother-in-law as they both await news of her husband: a prisoner of war. Parisian refugees start to pour into their small town, soon followed by a regiment of German soldiers who take up residence in the villagers' own homes. Lucile initially tries to ignore Bruno von Falk, the handsome and refined German officer staying with them. But soon, a powerful love draws them together and leads them into the tragedy of war.
tagline: Forced to host the enemy. Tormented by intruders. Tempted by desire.
title: Suite Française
plot:
Suite Française is a 2015 war romance directed by Saul Dibb, who co-wrote the screenplay with Matt Charman, based on the second part of Irène Némirovsky's novel, written in the early 1940s and published posthumously in 2004. Michelle Williams stars as Lucile Angellier, with Kristin Scott Thomas as her mother-in-law, Matthias Schoenaerts as the German officer Bruno von Falk, Sam Riley, Ruth Wilson, Lambert Wilson and Margot Robbie. Filmed in France and Belgium, it was released in the United Kingdom in March 2015 and premiered in the United States on the Lifetime network in 2017.

In 1940, in the small French town of Bussy, Lucile lives with her domineering mother-in-law, Madame Angellier, while awaiting news of her husband, Gaston, who is serving in the French army. After surviving an air raid by German dive bombers while collecting rents from the family's tenants, the women learn of France's surrender, and soon a German regiment arrives and billets its soldiers in the villagers' homes. Oberleutnant Bruno von Falk, a cultured aristocrat and composer, is quartered at the Angellier house. Lucile tries to ignore him, but she is gradually drawn to his courteous manner and the music he plays on the piano.

Lucile learns that Gaston is being held in a German prisoner-of-war camp. Meanwhile the farmer Benoît, who was unable to fight because of a leg injury, and his wife Madeleine suffer under the harassment of another German officer, Kurt Bonnet, and Benoît secretly hides a rifle. When Lucile discovers that one of the tenants is sleeping with a German soldier, the woman reveals that Gaston had been having an affair and fathered a daughter. Angry that her mother-in-law kept the secret, Lucile grows closer to Bruno. As tensions rise between villagers and occupiers, with informers denouncing their neighbors, Benoît's resistance leads to violence, and Lucile is forced to choose between her feelings for Bruno and loyalty to her community, risking her life to help Benoît escape.

The film received mixed reviews, with praise for Williams's performance and its period detail but criticism that it reduced Némirovsky's sweeping novel to a conventional romance. Némirovsky, a Jewish writer, was deported and died at Auschwitz in 1942, and her manuscript was preserved by her daughters for decades.

overview: Journey into the extraordinary world of "The Witcher" — from casting the roles to Jaskier's catchy song — in this behind-the-scenes look at the series. Go behind the monsters, the ballads and every bit of magic that went into bringing The Witcher's Continent to life.
title: Making The Witcher
plot:
Making The Witcher is a 2020 British behind-the-scenes documentary special about the first season of the Netflix fantasy series The Witcher, adapted from the novels and stories of the Polish author Andrzej Sapkowski. Produced by The Workhouse Picture Company and running about 32 minutes, it was released on Netflix on 26 August 2020. It features interviews with showrunner Lauren Schmidt Hissrich, executive producer Tomek Bagiński and cast members including Henry Cavill, Anya Chalotra, Freya Allan, Joey Batey, Eamon Farren, Adam Levy, Mimi Ndiweni and MyAnna Buring.

The special was released during the long gap between the first and second seasons, when production of the second season had been halted by the COVID-19 pandemic, and it revisits the making of the first. Netflix promoted it as a journey into the world of the show, from the casting of the main roles to the bard Jaskier's catchy song "Toss a Coin to Your Witcher", and as a look behind the monsters, the ballads and the magic that went into bringing the Continent to the screen. Across its half-hour running time it touches on the history of the Continent and the first season's non-linear timeline, the relationships between Geralt of Rivia, Yennefer and Ciri, the show's magic system, the importance of the property in Poland, and the series' portrayal of women, with Chalotra praising Sapkowski's complex female characters. It also covers the design of the creatures, built through a combination of practical effects and computer-generated imagery, as well as costume and set design and their architectural influences, the fight choreography, and the experiences of the episode writers, among them Declan de Barra, who wrote the fourth episode, "Of Banquets, Bastards and Burials". The actors also discuss how they approached their characters, frequently complimenting one another's work.

Reception was mixed. Writing for FilmObserver, a self-described devoted fan of the franchise found the special rushed and more like an extended commercial than a documentary, arguing that it tried to cram far too many subjects into 30 minutes and lingered on familiar backstory at the expense of genuine behind-the-scenes material. The reviewer nonetheless enjoyed the too-brief segments on monster creation, costume and set design, which offered real production footage rather than clips from the show, as well as de Barra's insights and the actors' interviews.

overview: A tragic car accident puts a woman in a two year coma. She wakes up to find her fiance' is dead and her friends have abandoned her. So she calls on an evil spirit to raise her fiance' from the dead and exact revenge. But revenge always comes with a price.
tagline: Who will miss you when you're gone?
title: Undying
plot: A tragic car accident puts a woman in a two year coma. She wakes up to find her fiance' is dead and her friends have abandoned her. So she calls on an evil spirit to raise her fiance' from the dead and exact revenge. But revenge always comes with a price.

overview: After a catastrophic crash on an unknown planet, pilot Mills quickly discovers he's actually stranded on Earth…65 million years ago. Now, with only one chance at rescue, Mills and the only other survivor, Koa, must make their way across an unknown terrain riddled with dangerous prehistoric creatures in an epic fight to survive.
tagline: 65 million years ago, prehistoric Earth had a visitor.
plot:
65 is a 2023 American science fiction thriller film written and directed by Scott Beck and Bryan Woods. Adam Driver stars as a space pilot stranded on prehistoric Earth, with Ariana Greenblatt as the young girl he struggles to keep alive. Beck and Woods produced the film with Sam Raimi, Deborah Liebling and Zainab Azizi, and Sony Pictures released it under its Columbia Pictures label on March 10, 2023.

Sixty-five million years ago, Mills, a pilot from the planet Somaris, reluctantly accepts a two-year deep-space expedition to pay for treatment for his seriously ill daughter, Nevine. During the voyage, his ship is struck by an asteroid field and crashes on an uncharted planet, which is Earth. Mills finds that the passengers in cryosleep have been killed, and is on the verge of taking his own life when he discovers one survivor, a young girl named Koa. With no common language and a broken translator, they can barely communicate.

Mills learns that the ship's escape shuttle has landed on a mountain about fifteen kilometers away, and to persuade Koa to come with him, he falsely tells her that her family is waiting there. As they make their way through the jungle, they discover that the planet is inhabited by dinosaurs and other predators. They free a small creature from a tar pit, only to see it killed; they are separated when a rockfall blocks a cave in which they shelter from a huge carnivore that Mills blinds in one eye; and each saves the other from attacks and from quicksand. Along the way, Koa watches video messages from Nevine, and the two slowly form a bond. Mills also discovers that a much larger asteroid will strike the planet within hours.

When they reach the shuttle, Koa learns that Mills lied about her family, and he confesses that Nevine died while he was away, promising to protect Koa. As they prepare to leave, falling debris knocks the shuttle down the mountain. They fight off a pair of Tyrannosaurus rex, with Koa distracting them using a projection of Nevine, and finally kill the carnivore Mills wounded earlier. They launch the shuttle just as the asteroid strikes, triggering the mass extinction that ends the age of the dinosaurs.

65 received mixed to negative reviews; Rotten Tomatoes reported 36% approval, with a consensus describing it as sodden science fiction. It grossed about $60 million worldwide against a $45 million budget.

overview: Andy, at the urging of his former mentor and Magic Camp owner Roy Preston, returns to the camp of his youth hoping to reignite his career. Instead, he finds inspiration in his ragtag bunch of rookie magicians.
title: Magic Camp
plot:
Magic Camp is a heartwarming and nostalgic film that explores the universal theme of self-discovery and growth through the lens of summer camp experiences. The movie delves into the complexities of adolescence, where young characters are navigating their identities, forming friendships, and learning to find their place in the world.

At its core, Magic Camp is a story about embracing one's individuality and finding confidence in the face of uncertainty. The film celebrates the beauty of imperfection and the power of creativity, as the campers learn to express themselves authentically and support each other in their unique journeys.

The movie also touches on the theme of letting go and moving forward, as the characters confront the challenges of growing up and saying goodbye to a carefree summer. Through its portrayal of these themes, Magic Camp offers a poignant reminder that it's okay to be different and that true magic lies in embracing our quirks and imperfections.

Overall, Magic Camp is a charming film that will resonate with audiences of all ages, particularly those who have experienced the joys and challenges of summer camp or are navigating the complexities of adolescence.

overview: A woman is forced to go on the run after her husband betrays his partners, sending her and her baby on a dangerous journey.
tagline: No one survives alone.
title: I'm Your Woman
plot:
I'm Your Woman is a 2020 American comedy-drama film directed by Maria Pulera. The movie revolves around Marisa Wemstead, a suburban mom who pretends to be her husband's girlfriend in order to impress his wealthy and influential family.

The main theme of I'm Your Woman explores the complexities of identity, class, and social status. Marisa, as she navigates this new persona, must confront her own insecurities and desires, which are deeply rooted in her suburban upbringing. As she becomes more entrenched in this role, she begins to question what it truly means to be a woman, a partner, and an individual.

Throughout the film, the tension between Marisa's authentic self and her fabricated persona serves as a metaphor for the societal expectations placed on women, particularly those from lower socioeconomic backgrounds who are expected to conform to certain standards of behavior. The movie also touches on themes of loneliness, intimacy, and the performance of relationships in order to achieve social acceptance.

Ultimately, I'm Your Woman is a nuanced exploration of the human desire for connection and belonging, as well as the difficulties that arise when we try to fit into predetermined roles or expectations.

overview: In 1976, four hijackers take over an Air France airplane en route from Tel Aviv to Paris and force it to land in Entebbe, Uganda. With 248 passengers on board, one of the most daring rescue missions ever is set in motion.
tagline: 248 passengers were held hostage. For seven days, the world was held captive.
title: 7 Days in Entebbe
plot:
"7 Days in Entebbe" is a gripping and intense thriller that delves into the complexities of terrorism, politics, and human resilience. The film masterfully weaves together the true story of Operation Thunderbolt, a daring rescue mission conducted by Israeli commandos to free hostages taken by Palestinian terrorists at Entebbe Airport in Uganda in 1976.

At its core, "7 Days in Entebbe" is a powerful exploration of the intricate web of international politics and terrorism that defined the Cold War era. The film sheds light on the cat-and-mouse game played between Israeli intelligence and Palestinian militants, highlighting the moral dilemmas faced by those caught in the middle.

The movie also delves into the personal stories of its characters, particularly the hostages and their families, whose lives were forever changed by this traumatic event. Through their experiences, the film conveys a sense of hope and resilience in the face of unimaginable horror.

Furthermore, "7 Days in Entebbe" touches on the theme of identity and belonging, as the Israeli commandos grapple with their own roles and loyalties in the midst of the operation. The film raises questions about the nature of heroism and the true cost of sacrifice, leaving the audience to ponder the complexities of human behavior under extreme circumstances.

Overall, "7 Days in Entebbe" is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged thriller that masterfully balances action, suspense, and character-driven drama to create a cinematic experience that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: The savage murders of three young children sparks a controversial trial of three teenagers accused of killing the kids as part of a satanic ritual.
tagline: They say the crimes were satanic. The truth may be scarier.
title: Devil's Knot
plot:
Devil's Knot is a 2013 American biographical crime drama directed by Atom Egoyan, adapted by Paul Harris Boardman and Scott Derrickson from Mara Leveritt's 2002 book of the same name. Reese Witherspoon stars as Pam Hobbs, the mother of one of the murdered children, and Colin Firth as Ron Lax, a private investigator, with Dane DeHaan, Mireille Enos, Bruce Greenwood, Elias Koteas, Stephen Moyer and Alessandro Nivola. The film dramatizes the case of the West Memphis Three, three teenagers convicted of murdering three young boys amid the Satanic panic of the early 1990s.

In 1993, in the working-class, deeply religious community of West Memphis, Arkansas, three eight-year-old boys, Stevie Branch, Christopher Byers and Michael Moore, disappear. Their bound and beaten bodies are found the following day. Because of the brutal nature of the crime, the community and the police quickly become convinced that the killings were the work of a satanic cult.

A month later, three teenagers, Damien Echols, Jason Baldwin and Jessie Misskelley Jr., are arrested after Misskelley confesses following twelve hours of police interrogation. Ron Lax, a private investigator who comes to work with the defense, uncovers inconsistencies in the evidence, mishandled clues and alternative suspects, while Pam Hobbs, grieving for her son Stevie, begins to have doubts about the guilt of the accused. Despite the weakness of the case and the defendants' insistence on their innocence, Baldwin and Misskelley are sentenced to life in prison and Echols to death. The film ends by noting that the three men were released in 2011 after nearly two decades in prison by entering Alford pleas, under which they remain convicted felons, and that questions about the case remain unanswered.

The case had previously been the subject of the acclaimed Paradise Lost documentary series and the documentary West of Memphis, which the film's critics frequently cited.

Devil's Knot was filmed in Georgia in 2012 and premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 8, 2013. It received mostly negative reviews, with 26 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus noted that the story had already been covered by more compelling documentaries, and a Metacritic score of 42.

original_title: Justin and the Knights of Valour
overview: A heart-warming tale about friendship, honor & courage, which sees a young boy become a man as he embarks on a quest to become a knight.
production_companies: Gobierno de Cantabria, Consejería de Cultura, Turismo y Deporte
title: Justin and the Knights of Valour
plot:
Justin and the Knights of Valour is an animated adventure film that tells the story of a young nobleman named Justin who sets out on a quest to save his kingdom from the evil forces of darkness. The movie explores themes of courage, honor, and self-discovery as Justin navigates treacherous landscapes, battles fearsome enemies, and confronts his own doubts and fears.

At its core, the film is a classic tale of good vs. evil, with Justin embodying the virtues of chivalry and bravery in the face of overwhelming odds. However, the movie also delves deeper into the complexities of human nature, revealing the inner struggles and vulnerabilities that even the most heroic characters must confront.

Through Justin's journey, the film highlights the importance of perseverance, loyalty, and the power of friendship and camaraderie. The Knights of Valour, a group of noble warriors who join Justin on his quest, serve as a symbol of unity and solidarity in the face of adversity.

Ultimately, the movie suggests that true heroism is not about grand acts of bravery, but about the small, everyday choices we make to stand up for what is right, even when it's difficult or unpopular. The film's themes are timeless and universal, making it a compelling and inspiring watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: In 1561, Mary Stuart, widow of the King of France, returns to Scotland, reclaims her rightful throne and menaces the future of Queen Elizabeth I as ruler of England, because she has a legitimate claim to the English throne. Betrayals, rebellions, conspiracies and their own life choices imperil both Queens. They experience the bitter cost of power, until their tragic fate is finally fulfilled.
tagline: Bow to No One
title: Mary Queen of Scots
plot:
Mary Queen of Scots is a 2018 historical drama film that delves into the complexities of power, identity, and the consequences of one's actions. The movie revolves around the tumultuous life of Mary Stuart, who finds herself entangled in a web of politics, romance, and betrayal.

At its core, the film explores the theme of female empowerment and the constraints placed on women in positions of power during the 16th century. Mary, as a queen, is expected to embody traditional feminine virtues, but her desire for autonomy, independence, and self-determination sets her apart from the expectations of those around her.

The movie also examines the destructive nature of ambition and the consequences of seeking power at any cost. Mary's quest for the throne of Scotland leads her down a path of deceit, manipulation, and ultimately, tragedy. The film highlights the devastating impact of these actions on not only Mary but also those around her, including her husband, Lord Darnley, and her cousin, Queen Elizabeth I.

Furthermore, the film touches upon the theme of identity and the performance of self. Mary's struggles to reconcile her Catholic faith with her royal duties serve as a metaphor for the tensions between personal conviction and public expectation. Her relationships with those around her, particularly her husband and her cousin, are also fraught with tension, as she navigates the complexities of love, loyalty, and duty.

Ultimately, Mary Queen of Scots is a film about the human cost of power and the devastating consequences of allowing ambition to consume us. The movie raises important questions about the nature of leadership, the constraints placed on women, and the enduring power of personal conviction in the face of adversity.

overview: Aviation disaster-prone Joe Patroni must contend with nuclear missiles, the French Air Force and the threat of the plane splitting in two over the Alps.
tagline: At twice the speed of sound, can the Concorde evade attack?
title: The Concorde... Airport '79
plot:
The Concorde... Airport '79 is an action-thriller film that revolves around a catastrophic event at Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport, where a commercial airliner carrying the Concorde supersonic jet crashes. The movie's main themes revolve around the consequences of human error, technological hubris, and the devastating impact of tragedy on individuals and society.

At its core, the film explores the theme of hubris and the dangers of unchecked ambition. The characters' obsession with pushing the boundaries of technology and innovation ultimately leads to a catastrophic failure, highlighting the importance of humility and responsible decision-making in the face of complex systems.

The movie also delves into the human cost of tragedy, as the characters grapple with the aftermath of the disaster and its effects on their lives. The film's portrayal of grief, guilt, and redemption serves as a poignant reminder of the devastating consequences of human error and the importance of accountability.

Furthermore, the Concorde... Airport '79 touches on themes of paranoia and mistrust, as the characters begin to suspect that the crash may not have been an accident. This sense of unease and uncertainty adds to the film's tension and suspense, creating a sense of claustrophobia and desperation among the characters.

Overall, The Concorde... Airport '79 is a gripping thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of playing with forces beyond our control.

original_title: H.G. Wells' War of the Worlds
overview: In this modern retelling of H.G. Wells' classic sci-fi horror, civilization is laid to ruin when a super race of aliens invades Earth. In a blink of an eye, massive "walkers" cover the planet, annihilating all in their path. As cities crumble and human flesh is ripped from the bone, one man struggles to find the one weapon that will turn the tide for mankind.
title: H.G. Wells' War of the Worlds
plot:
War of the Worlds (2005) is a science fiction horror film directed by Steven Spielberg and produced by DreamWorks Pictures, not The Asylum. However, I can provide information on the movie.

The main themes of H.G. Wells' War of the Worlds (2005) revolve around the destruction of human civilization and the insignificance of humanity in the face of an alien invasion. The film explores the idea that even with advanced technology and military might, humans are vulnerable to the unknown and the uncontrollable forces of nature.

The movie also delves into the theme of survival and the human condition, highlighting the resilience and resourcefulness of individuals in the face of catastrophic events. The characters' struggles to cope with the invasion and its aftermath serve as a commentary on the fragility of human existence and our place in the universe.

Furthermore, the film touches upon the idea of xenophobia and the fear of the unknown, as the humans' initial response to the alien threat is rooted in superstition and prejudice. As the story unfolds, however, the characters are forced to confront their own biases and limitations, leading to a more nuanced understanding of the true nature of the enemy.

Overall, War of the Worlds (2005) is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and ideas through its narrative, leaving audiences with a sense of unease and introspection.

overview: A woman adjusting to life after a loss contends with a feisty bird that's taken over her garden — and a husband who's struggling to find a way forward.
tagline: Hope Starts Small
title: The Starling
plot:
The Starling is a 2021 American drama film directed by Joe Wright, starring Sam Claflin and Sally Hawkins.

The main themes of The Starling revolve around loneliness, isolation, and the complexities of human relationships. The story follows William "Will" Evans (Sam Claflin), a widowed father who moves to a rural area with his young daughter, Rose (Abigail Whelan). Will's life is marked by grief and loneliness after the loss of his wife, and he struggles to connect with his daughter.

The film explores the theme of isolation through Will's character, as he navigates his new life in the countryside. He finds solace in hunting and becomes increasingly withdrawn from society. The arrival of a mysterious woman, Rose (Sally Hawkins), who is also an outsider, sets off a chain of events that challenges Will's perceptions of loneliness and human connection.

The film delves into the complexities of relationships, particularly between parents and children. Will's relationship with his daughter is strained due to his grief and emotional unavailability. However, as he forms a bond with Rose, he begins to confront his emotions and learn to connect with her on a deeper level.

Throughout the film, Wright explores the idea that loneliness can be both a source of pain and a catalyst for growth. Will's journey is marked by moments of vulnerability, self-discovery, and ultimately, healing. The Starling is a poignant exploration of the human condition, highlighting the importance of connection, empathy, and understanding in overcoming loneliness.

The film received critical acclaim for its nuanced performances, atmospheric cinematography, and Wright's sensitive direction.

overview: A demoted police officer assigned to a call dispatch desk is conflicted when he receives an emergency phone call from a kidnapped woman.
tagline: Listen carefully.
title: The Guilty
plot:
The Guilty is a 2021 American thriller film directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by Tony Fadell and Nicholas Jarecki. The movie stars Jake Gyllenhaal as Joe Baylor, a 911 operator who must navigate a life-or-death situation when he's put on the line to handle an emergency call.

The story begins with Joe Baylor (Jake Gyllenhaal), a 911 operator working late-night shifts at the Emergency Services Dispatch Center in Los Angeles. He's a bit of a loner, struggling to connect with his colleagues and feeling disconnected from the world outside his cubicle. On this particular night, Joe is on duty when he receives an emergency call from a woman claiming to be kidnapped by her boyfriend.

As Joe tries to stay calm and focus on the situation, he realizes that the caller's story seems suspiciously rehearsed, and she keeps asking for help with something called "the package." Despite his initial reservations, Joe becomes increasingly invested in helping the woman, who claims to be in grave danger. He starts to piece together a narrative of her kidnapping, but as the conversation unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems.

As the story progresses, Joe's investigation leads him down a rabbit hole of deceit and manipulation. The caller, whose name is Emily (Patti Harrison), seems to be playing a cat-and-mouse game with Joe, feeding him clues while keeping her true intentions hidden. Meanwhile, Joe's colleagues at the dispatch center are skeptical of his involvement in the case, and he starts to feel like an outsider.

As the tension builds, Joe becomes more and more entangled in Emily's web of lies. He starts to question his own perceptions of reality, wondering if he's just a pawn in a larger game. The film's climax features a heart-pumping confrontation between Joe and Emily, which raises more questions than it answers.

Ultimately, the truth behind Emily's situation is revealed, and Joe must confront the consequences of his actions. The movie ends with a sense of ambiguity, leaving the audience to ponder the nature of reality and the blurred lines between good and evil.

Throughout the film, Jake Gyllenhaal delivers a standout performance as Joe Baylor, bringing depth and nuance to a character that could have easily been one-dimensional. The supporting cast, including Patti Harrison and Peter Sarsgaard, adds to the tension and complexity of the story.

Overall, The Guilty is a gripping thriller that explores themes of isolation, manipulation, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. With its tense atmosphere and unexpected twists, it's a must-see for fans of psychological suspense.

original_title: マルドゥック・スクランブル 燃焼
overview: Second film of the Mardock Scramble series. Balot and a severely injured Oeufcoque seem to be at the mercy of an obsessed Boiled. Dr. Easter comes to the rescue and the group escapes to "Paradise" where many secrets of Mardock lie and where Balot will need to come to a decision herself about what she will and can do.
title: Mardock Scramble: The Second Combustion
plot:
Mardock Scramble: The Second Combustion is an anime film that delves into the complex and often dark world of human relationships, particularly in the context of trauma, abuse, and the struggle for empowerment. At its core, the movie explores the theme of emotional manipulation and control, as embodied by the character of Shirogane.

The story follows Ram, a young woman who finds herself entangled in a web of psychological games with Shirogane, a charismatic and enigmatic figure from her past. As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that Shirogane's actions are rooted in a deep-seated need for control and validation, which he attempts to satisfy through his interactions with Ram.

Through Ram's character, the film also touches on themes of vulnerability, resilience, and the struggle to break free from toxic relationships. The movie raises important questions about the nature of consent, power dynamics, and the blurred lines between love and manipulation.

One of the most striking aspects of Mardock Scramble: The Second Combustion is its unflinching portrayal of the long-term effects of trauma and emotional abuse. The film's depiction of Ram's inner turmoil and her desperate attempts to escape Shirogane's grasp serves as a powerful commentary on the devastating consequences of such experiences.
