At Aladin's birthday party, organized by Kasim to humiliate him, Jasmine gives him an old lamp as a present, which turns out to be the very lamp his parents' killers were seeking.

When Aladin rubs the lamp, he releases Genius, a flamboyant, rock-star genie who is desperate to grant three wishes so that his contract with the lamp can end. Aladin is reluctant to make any wishes, but Genius cleverly extracts them, turning his life upside down. With Genius's help, Aladin stands up to Kasim and begins a relationship with Jasmine. Their happiness is threatened by Ringmaster, a former genie who wants to regain his lost powers. He tricks Aladin into turning against Genius and steals the lamp, setting in motion a scheme involving an approaching comet, and Aladin and Genius must join forces to rescue Jasmine and stop him.

The film combines fairy-tale fantasy with comedy, musical numbers and visual effects, and gives the classic story a contemporary setting.

Aladin was released in 2009 and was a commercial failure, grossing an estimated 10 crore rupees. Critics were largely negative: Bollywood Hungama gave it one star, calling it a terrible waste of a terrific opportunity, and the Hindustan Times criticized its hollow storytelling while acknowledging Bachchan's enduring appeal.

overview: The King's Speech tells the story of the man who became King George VI, the father of Queen Elizabeth II. After his brother abdicates, George ('Bertie') reluctantly assumes the throne. Plagued by a dreaded stutter and considered unfit to be king, Bertie engages the help of an unorthodox speech therapist named Lionel Logue. Through a set of unexpected techniques, and as a result of an unlikely friendship, Bertie is able to find his voice and boldly lead the country into war.
tagline: Find your voice.
title: The King's Speech
plot:
The King's Speech is a historical drama film directed by Tom Hooper, released in 2010 by The Weinstein Company. The movie tells the story of King George VI's struggle to overcome his stutter and lead the United Kingdom through World War II.

The film begins with King George VI (played by Colin Firth) as a young prince, struggling with a severe stutter. He is portrayed as an awkward and shy individual, unable to express himself effectively in public. The king's stutter becomes a source of embarrassment for him, particularly when he is expected to perform ceremonial duties.

In 1925, King George VI marries his wife, Elizabeth Bowes-Lyon (played by Helena Bonham Carter), who encourages him to seek help for his stutter. He meets Lionel Logue (played by Geoffrey Rush), an Australian speech therapist who specializes in treating stuttering patients. Initially, the king is hesitant to accept Logue's unconventional methods, but eventually warms up to his approach.

Logue uses a combination of techniques, including singing and speaking exercises, to help the king overcome his stutter. The two men form a strong bond, with Logue becoming a trusted confidant and advisor to the king. Through their sessions, the king gradually becomes more confident in his ability to speak clearly and effectively.

As World War II breaks out, King George VI is faced with the daunting task of leading the United Kingdom through its darkest hour. He must navigate the complexities of diplomacy and statecraft while struggling to overcome his stutter. Logue continues to provide support and guidance, helping the king to find his voice and assert himself as a leader.

The film's climax features the king's famous speech at the opening of the 1948 London Olympics, in which he delivers a powerful and eloquent address that marks a turning point in his life and career. The speech is a testament to the king's newfound confidence and ability to communicate effectively, thanks in large part to Logue's help.

Throughout the film, the relationship between King George VI and Lionel Logue is portrayed as a deep and abiding friendship. The two men form a strong bond, with Logue serving as a source of emotional support and guidance for the king. The film also explores the complexities of their relationship, including the power dynamics at play and the ways in which they navigate their differences.

Overall, The King's Speech is a powerful and moving drama that explores themes of identity, leadership, and the human spirit. The film features outstanding performances from Colin Firth and Geoffrey Rush, as well as strong supporting performances from Helena Bonham Carter and Guy Pearce.

overview: Jack Conrad is awaiting the death penalty in a corrupt Central American prison. He is "purchased" by a wealthy television producer and taken to a desolate island where he must fight to the death against nine other condemned killers from all corners of the world, with freedom going to the sole survivor.
tagline: 10 Will Fight, 9 Will Die. You Get To Watch.
title: The Condemned
plot:
The Condemned is a 2007 action thriller film directed by Pierre Morel and starring Stone Cold Steve Austin, Brian Cox, and Jeroen Krabbé.

The main themes of The Condemned revolve around the concept of redemption, survival, and the human condition. The story takes place in a maximum-security prison where death row inmates are forced to participate in a televised fight-to-the-death tournament, known as "The Condemned".

Throughout the film, the protagonist, Jack Conrad (played by Stone Cold Steve Austin), is driven by his desire for revenge against those who wronged him. As he navigates the treacherous world of the prison and the tournament, he must confront his own demons and make difficult choices to survive.

One of the primary themes explored in The Condemned is redemption. Jack Conrad's character arc is centered around finding a way to redeem himself after being wrongly convicted and sentenced to death. Through his experiences in the prison and the tournament, he begins to see that there is more to life than just revenge and survival.

The film also explores the theme of human nature, highlighting the darker aspects of human behavior when people are pushed to their limits. The prisoners in the film are forced to confront their own mortality and the true meaning of humanity, leading to a series of intense and violent confrontations.

Furthermore, The Condemned touches on the idea of entertainment and voyeurism. The film's premise is built around a televised fight-to-the-death tournament, which raises questions about the morality of exploiting human suffering for entertainment purposes.

Overall, The Condemned is a gripping action thriller that explores complex themes such as redemption, survival, and human nature, set against the backdrop of a deadly and intense prison environment.

overview: In the occupied Netherlands during World War II, banker Walraven van Hall is asked to use his financial contacts to help the Dutch resistance. With his brother Gijs, he comes up with a risky plan to take out huge loans and use the money to finance the Resistance.
tagline: The greatest concealed act of resistance
title: The Resistance Banker
plot:
The Resistance Banker (Dutch: Bankier van het Verzet) is a 2018 Dutch Second World War drama directed by Joram Lürsen. It tells the true story of Walraven van Hall, an Amsterdam banker who secretly financed the Dutch resistance during the German occupation, played by Barry Atsma, with Jacob Derwig as his brother Gijs and Fockeline Ouwerkerk as Walraven's wife, Tilly.

In 1941, soon after the occupation begins, the Nazi collaborator Rost van Tonningen is installed at the head of the Dutch central bank. Shaken by the suicide of a Jewish colleague and his family, who had been ordered to hand their home over to the Germans, Walraven, known as Wally, is approached by a resistance member using the name Van den Berg, who runs an illegal fund supporting escaped sailors and persuades him to set up a similar fund for the resistance. Wally enlists Gijs, and through their financial networks the brothers raise and distribute huge sums. Under the alias "Van Tuyl", Wally convinces resistance leaders to let him act as their banker, and the government-in-exile in London promises to repay the loans. Meanwhile Rost van Tonningen sets SS intelligence on the trail of the shadow bank.

By 1944 a captured courier and her boyfriend are pressured into helping the Germans, and arrests and betrayals thin the movement's ranks. When London calls a national railway strike, the money to support the striking workers runs short, so Wally devises an audacious fraud: stealing treasury bonds from the central bank and replacing them with forgeries. He narrowly escapes capture, goes into hiding and finally carries out the scheme. In January 1945 he is arrested without the Germans realising who he is, but an informant betrays his identity, and after defying Rost van Tonningen in an interrogation he is executed alongside other prisoners shortly before the liberation. A framing story shows Gijs after the war, accounting for every guilder to government ministers who ask him to keep the affair quiet.

The film became the most-watched Dutch film of 2018 and was the Netherlands' submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, although it was not nominated. At the Golden Calf awards it won Best Film, Best Actor for Derwig, Best Supporting Actress for Ouwerkerk and Best Production Design, as well as the audience award. Critics on Rotten Tomatoes reviewed it favorably.

overview: As the city is locked down under quarantine, Alice finds out that the people that died from the previous incident at the Umbrella Corporation have turned into zombies. She then joins a small band of elite soldiers, who are enlisted to rescue the missing daughter of the creator of the mutating T-virus.  Once lack of luck and resources happen, they begin to wage an exhilarating battle to survive and escape before the Umbrella Corporation erases its experiment from the face of the earth.
tagline: You're all going to die.
title: Resident Evil: Apocalypse
plot:
Resident Evil: Apocalypse is a 2004 science fiction horror film directed by Russell Mulcahy and starring Milla Jovovich, Sienna Guillory, Oded Fehr, and Colin Salmon. The movie is the second installment in the Resident Evil film series.

The story begins with Alice (Milla Jovovich), a special forces operative who has been infected with the T-virus, which slowly transforms her into a zombie-like creature known as a "Licker." Alice escapes from the Umbrella Corporation's secret facility on Isla de Muerta and finds herself in a desolate wasteland.

As she navigates through the barren landscape, Alice encounters other survivors, including Ana (Sienna Guillory), a skilled fighter who becomes her ally. The two women soon discover that they are being pursued by a group of Umbrella Corporation agents, led by Albert Wesker (Oded Fehr).

Wesker reveals that he has been searching for the T-virus, which he believes holds the key to immortality. He intends to use it to create an army of super-soldiers and conquer the world.

Alice and Ana join forces with a group of rebels, including Carlos Oliveira (Oded Fehr) and Rain Ocampo (Michelle Rodriguez), who are fighting against Umbrella's sinister plans. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to stop Wesker and his minions.

As they navigate through the treacherous landscape, Alice begins to experience strange visions and flashbacks, hinting at her connection to the T-virus and her own destiny. The group soon discovers that the only way to defeat Wesker is to find the "Eclipse," a powerful device capable of destroying the T-virus.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between Alice and Wesker's forces. In the end, Alice manages to destroy the Eclipse, but not before Wesker reveals his true intentions: to use the T-virus to create a new world order with himself as the ruler.

As the credits roll, Alice is seen walking away from the ruins of Isla de Muerta, forever changed by her experiences and determined to continue fighting against Umbrella's evil plans. The movie ends on a hopeful note, setting the stage for the next installment in the series.

Throughout the film, Mulcahy's direction and the cast's performances bring the Resident Evil universe to life, delivering plenty of action, suspense, and horror elements that fans of the franchise have come to expect.

belongs_to_collection.name: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs Collection

original_title: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs 2
overview: After the disastrous food storm in the first film, Flint and his friends are forced to leave the town. Flint accepts the invitation from his idol Chester V to join The Live Corp Company, which has been tasked to clean the island, and where the best inventors in the world create technologies for the betterment of mankind. When Flint discovers that his machine still operates and now creates mutant food beasts like living pickles, hungry tacodiles, shrimpanzees and apple pie-thons, he and his friends must return to save the world.
tagline: Something big was leftover.
title: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs 2
plot:
Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs 2 is a 2013 animated adventure comedy film produced by Sony Pictures Animation and directed by Kris Peverall. The movie takes place two years after the events of the first film.

The story begins with Flint Lockwood (voiced by Bill Hader), now working at Swallow Falls, a food-themed town where cheeseburgers fall from the sky instead of rain. Flint's invention, the FLDSMDFR (Flint Lockwood Diatonic Super Mutating Dynamic Food Replicator), has become a sensation and is used to create an endless supply of food for the town.

However, Flint soon discovers that his invention has attracted the attention of the evil Chef Cassius (voiced by Will Arnett), who seeks to steal the FLDSMDFR and use it to take over the world. Cassius's plan involves using the machine to create an army of Swallow Falls' food products, which he can then control and use for his own gain.

Flint teams up with his friends Steve (voiced by Neil Patrick Harris), Sam Sparks (voiced by Anna Faris), and Manny (voiced by Danny McBride) to stop Cassius and save the world. Along the way, they encounter a group of edible creatures known as the "Foodimals," which are the result of Flint's invention gone wrong.

As the story unfolds, Flint and his friends embark on a series of adventures to stop Chef Cassius and find a way to reverse the effects of the FLDSMDFR. They visit various Foodimal habitats, including the Flock of Seagulls (a flock of seagull-like creatures made of cheeseburgers), the T-Rexes (Tyrannosaurus Rexes made of pizza slices), and the Sharktopus (a shark-like creature made of sushi).

Throughout their journey, Flint learns valuable lessons about responsibility, friendship, and the importance of using his inventions for good. In the end, Flint and his friends successfully defeat Chef Cassius and find a way to reverse the effects of the FLDSMDFR.

The movie features stunning animation, witty humor, and lovable characters, making it a delightful sequel to the original Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs film. The story is full of action, adventure, and heart, making it a must-see for fans of animated movies and comedy.

overview: Brewster, an aging minor-league baseball player, stands to inherit 300 million dollars if he can successfully spend 30 million dollars in 30 days without anything to show for it, and without telling anyone what he's up to... A task that's a lot harder than it sounds!
tagline: An American excess story.
title: Brewster's Millions
plot:
Brewster's Millions is a 1985 American comedy film directed by Walter Hill and starring Richard Pryor as Montgomery "Monty" Brewster, a minor league baseball player who must spend $3 million in 30 days or give up his inheritance.

The movie begins with Monty, a struggling baseball player, being forced to take a job at a small insurance company. However, he soon discovers that his late uncle, James Brewster (played by John Rhys-Davies), has left him an unusual condition: if he wants to inherit the majority of his wealth, Monty must spend $3 million in 30 days, or else he'll be cut out of the will.

Monty is initially skeptical and disbelieving, but after consulting with a lawyer (played by John Candy), he realizes that this is indeed the only way to get his hands on the inheritance. The catch is that Monty must spend the money in a series of outrageous and extravagant ways, which are dictated by a set of rules.

The first rule states that Monty must spend $100,000 on a hot air balloon ride over the Grand Canyon. He then proceeds to hire a group of eccentric friends, including his lawyer (John Candy), his friend Spike Nolan (played by Dan Aykroyd), and a beautiful woman named Roxanne (played by Amy Madigan).

As Monty navigates the challenges of spending $3 million in 30 days, he must also contend with a series of obstacles, including a rival suitor for Roxanne's affections and a group of con artists who are trying to steal his money.

Throughout the movie, Monty uses his wit and cunning to outsmart his enemies and stay one step ahead of the game. Along the way, he also learns valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and the importance of living life to the fullest.

As the deadline for spending the money approaches, Monty must make a series of increasingly absurd and outrageous purchases, including a private island, a collection of rare cars, and a lavish party at a luxurious mansion. However, despite his best efforts, he still falls short of the $3 million mark by the end of the 30-day period.

In the end, Monty is forced to give up his inheritance, but he also gains something far more valuable: the knowledge that true wealth comes from living life on one's own terms and surrounding oneself with good friends. The movie ends with Monty and his friends celebrating their newfound appreciation for life, as they watch a sunset over the Grand Canyon.

Overall, Brewster's Millions is a hilarious and entertaining comedy that showcases Richard Pryor's signature wit and charm. With its lighthearted tone and absurd humor, it's a fun and feel-good movie that's sure to leave audiences smiling long after the credits roll.

overview: Sent to Mexico to help take care of aging Father Benito, young Father Amaro faces a moral challenge when he meets a 16-year-old girl who he starts an affair with. Likewise, the girl's mother had been having an affair with Father Benito. Father Amaro must choose between a holy or sinful life.
tagline: Lead us not into temptation
title: The Crime of Padre Amaro
plot:
The Crime of Padre Amaro is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human nature, morality, and the blurred lines between good and evil. Set in 19th-century Mexico, the movie tells the story of a young priest, Padre Amaro, who becomes embroiled in a web of corruption and deceit.

At its core, The Crime of Padre Amaro is a exploration of the human condition, examining the ways in which individuals are driven by their desires, weaknesses, and flaws. The film's protagonist, Padre Amaro, is a well-intentioned but ultimately flawed character, whose own moral compass is tested by the temptations and pressures of his situation.

The movie also grapples with themes of power, corruption, and the abuse of authority. The corrupt clergy and politicians who surround Padre Amaro serve as a commentary on the darker aspects of human nature, highlighting the ways in which those in positions of power can exploit and manipulate others for their own gain.

Furthermore, The Crime of Padre Amaro is a nuanced exploration of faith and spirituality, questioning the role of religion in shaping individual morality and behavior. The film's portrayal of a priest who becomes increasingly disillusioned with his own faith serves as a powerful commentary on the complexities of spiritual conviction and the human search for meaning.

Ultimately, The Crime of Padre Amaro is a complex, thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to confront their own moral assumptions and consider the gray areas between right and wrong.

overview: Henry is a player skilled at seducing women. But when this veterinarian meets Lucy, a girl with a quirky problem when it comes to total recall, he realizes it's possible to fall in love all over again…and again, and again. That's because the delightful Lucy has no short-term memory, so Henry must woo her day after day until he finally sweeps her off her feet.
tagline: Imagine having to win over the girl of your dreams... every friggin' day.
title: 50 First Dates
plot:
"50 First Dates" is a romantic comedy film released in 2004, directed by Peter Segal and produced by Adam Sandler Productions, Inc., in association with Columbia Pictures.

The movie tells the story of Henry Roth (played by Adam Sandler), a veterinarian who falls in love with Lucy Whitmore (played by Drew Barrymore) at a Hawaiian luau. However, their romance is short-lived as Lucy suffers from short-term memory loss due to a head injury she sustained in an accident. As a result, she wakes up every day thinking it's the day of her accident and doesn't remember Henry or their time together.

Henry tries to win Lucy over every day, but his efforts are met with confusion and frustration. Despite this, he continues to visit her every day, hoping that eventually she'll remember him. The situation becomes a daily routine for both Henry and Lucy, as Henry tries to make the most of each day they spend together.

As the days go by, Henry starts to notice small changes in Lucy's behavior, suggesting that she may be starting to develop some memories of their time together. However, these moments are fleeting, and Lucy still doesn't remember Henry consistently.

Henry decides to take matters into his own hands and comes up with a plan to win Lucy over once and for all. He enlists the help of his friend Ula (played by Sean Astin) and his brother Rob (played by Rob Schneider), who also have their own romantic misadventures.

As Henry tries to make Lucy fall in love with him, he must confront his own feelings and learn to accept that Lucy's condition may be permanent. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about love, loss, and the importance of living in the present moment.

The movie takes a heartwarming turn when Henry finally succeeds in making Lucy remember him, but not before she realizes that she has fallen in love with him. The film ends on a hopeful note, as Henry and Lucy look forward to building a life together, despite the challenges they face.

Overall, "50 First Dates" is a charming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, loss, and memory. With its witty dialogue, engaging characters, and beautiful Hawaiian setting, it's no wonder this movie has become a beloved classic among rom-com fans.

overview: British retirees travel to India to take up residence in what they believe is a newly restored hotel. Less luxurious than its advertisements, the Marigold Hotel nevertheless slowly begins to charm in unexpected ways as the residents find new purpose in their old age.
tagline: Share the journey. Share the laughter.
title: The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel
plot:
The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel is a heartwarming and poignant film that explores several universal themes. At its core, it's a story about self-discovery, love, and finding one's purpose in life.

One of the primary themes of the movie is the concept of "finding oneself" as people navigate midlife crises. The characters, all in their 60s, are forced to confront their own mortality and reevaluate their priorities. They embark on a journey of self-discovery, which leads them to question their past choices, relationships, and aspirations.

The film also delves into the theme of love and connection. Despite being from different walks of life, the characters form strong bonds with each other, often finding comfort and solace in their newfound friendships. The movie showcases how love can take many forms, including platonic, familial, and romantic relationships.

Another significant theme present in the film is the idea of embracing change and letting go of the past. As the characters navigate their new lives in India, they must adapt to unfamiliar surroundings, cultures, and ways of life. This process forces them to confront their fears, insecurities, and biases, ultimately leading to personal growth and transformation.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and cultural exchange. The characters' experiences as expats in India serve as a catalyst for exploring different perspectives, traditions, and values. Through their interactions with the local community, they learn to appreciate the beauty of cultural diversity and the importance of understanding and empathy.

Lastly, the film explores the idea of finding purpose and meaning in life, particularly during times of transition or uncertainty. The characters' journeys are marked by a sense of restlessness and discontent, but ultimately, they discover new passions, interests, and ways to contribute to society.

Overall, The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel is a rich tapestry of themes that celebrate the human spirit's capacity for growth, love, and self-discovery.
